title: saveAllDocuments crashes on IntelliJ Platform 2025.1 (write-intent lock assertion)
description: TransactionGuard.isWritingAllowed() asserts the write-intent lock is held (ApplicationImpl.assertWriteIntentLockAcquired) on platform 2025.1 when called from a raw EDT dispatch that hasn't acquired it, even though the call is only a check, not a write. Later platform versions (2025.2+) don't assert this. This broke the compat CI job's platformTest(2025.1) run for CommandStaleInterceptTest (4/4 tests failing deterministically, not the usual flaky LeakHunter retry) — surfaced while verifying CI health before pushing jj-idea-nuk0's fix. Not a regression from nuk0's change; pre-existing since the stale-workspace-recovery commit (jj-idea-b65g/27b4) that added the executeAsync() -> saveAllDocuments() call path.
close_reason: Fixed: moved the isWritingAllowed() check inside runWriteIntentReadAction in Tasks.kt's saveIfWritingAllowed(). Verified against platform 2025.1 locally (CommandStaleInterceptTest, SaveAllDocumentsTest); ./gradlew check green.

title: Ignore scan walks entire repo unpruned on every refresh (GitHub #35 regression)
description:
Regression after 0.6.12, reported in https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/35 (stack trace from SergejSalnikov pins it to JujutsuChangeProvider.reportIgnoredFiles).

Root cause: JujutsuStateModel calls dirDirtyRecursively(repo.directory) on every working-copy change (every jj op, every debounced save), which makes needsFullScan true in reportIgnoredFiles (JujutsuChangeProvider.kt:232-268). The full scan File.walk()s the entire repo from disk, pruning only .jj/.git — it descends into node_modules, build, .gradle etc. For each file, GitignoreCache.isIgnored re-checks every ancestor with regexes: O(depth^2 x patterns) per file. The walk is synchronous inside getChanges (blocks modified-file display) and has no checkCanceled (causes the 10s shutdown hang in the report).

Fix:
1. In walk onEnter, check if the directory is ignored: if so, report the directory itself via builder.processIgnoredFile and do NOT descend (git semantics: a file cannot be re-included if a parent dir is excluded, so pruning is correct).
2. Maintain a stack of applicable PatternLists while descending so each path is matched once (eliminates per-file ancestor re-derivation).
3. Call progress.checkCanceled() per directory.
4. Report only top-most ignored dirs + individually ignored files — the platform treats ignored dirs recursively, exhaustive enumeration is unnecessary.
acceptance_criteria: Full refresh on a repo with a large ignored tree (e.g. node_modules with 100k files) visits O(non-ignored entries): verified by an operation-count test with a counting walker. Ignored dirs reported as single entries. Scan aborts promptly on cancellation. Existing GitignoreCache semantics tests still pass (negation, anchoring, deepest-wins).
close_reason: Pruning scan added to GitignoreCache.collectIgnored; change provider updated; operation-count regression test GitignoreScanTest added

title: JujutsuVirtualFile.contentsToByteArray calls jj file show under ReadAction — threading violation
description: CliExecutor.show() (jj file show) is called synchronously while a ReadAction lock is held, violating the IntelliJ platform rule that blocking operations must not run under ReadAction. Triggered when the platform calls AbstractVcsVirtualFile.getLength() → JujutsuVirtualFile.contentsToByteArray() → fetch() → CliExecutor.show(). Stack: JujutsuVirtualFile.kt:27 (contentsToByteArray) → JujutsuVirtualFile.kt:34 (fetch) → JujutsuRepository.kt:202 (getContent) → CliExecutor.kt:203 (show). Fix: pre-fetch and cache file content on a background thread before the ReadAction scope needs it, or restructure the VirtualFile implementation to avoid blocking in contentsToByteArray. This manifests as a logged Throwable in the sandbox IDE when selecting commits with file content (observed on large-commit bookmark). May cause UI freezes in practice.
notes: User reports this is a regression from previous version. Triggered again when using the Edit action to navigate back to the wip commit — platform tries to load file content (large_commit/file_001.txt) under ReadAction during the transition. Same stack: JujutsuVirtualFile.contentsToByteArray → CliExecutor.show. This fires reliably whenever a commit with file content is involved in a navigation operation.
close_reason: Read-access guard in contentsToByteArray(): returns empty + kicks off background load when read lock is held (no blocking CLI). On load completion, fires VcsFileSystem.fireContentsChanged via invokeLater+runWriteAction so any open editor reloads automatically. Existing logRefresh invalidation kept unchanged (no TTL, no re-warm). Two injectable seams (isReadAccessAllowed, backgroundExecutor) allow unit testing without a real Application.

title: Error when removing current change
description: Some VCS operations can remove the current change - abandon is an obvious one, but this can also happen when creating changes that cause the current (empty) change to be discarded. When this happens, the commit detail pane tries to refresh itself, causing the JujutsuFullCommitDetails to reload, but this reloading fails because the underlying change has gone. We need to change this situation to be expected, and defensively paint the commit details pane as if no commit has been selected in that situation. Ideally, the operation would already have refreshed the 'current selection' but this may happen later. As part of this fix, investigate sequencing around that to see if there is a neater way - i.e. the table realises that its current selection has disappeared, then clears the detail pane. Or: the detail pane realises that the current change has disappeared and sends a message to select the working copy in the table instead.

title: Comprehensive testing of custom log UI
Allow to initialise a jj root
description:
## Problem

The plugin needs to gracefully handle the case where it's used in a directory that is not a Jujutsu repository (no .jj directory found).

## Current Behavior

- JujutsuVcs has a `root` property that auto-discovers .jj directory by searching upward
- Unclear what happens if no .jj directory is found in the project or any parent directories

## Expected Behavior

The plugin should:
1. Detect when no JJ repository is present
2. Either disable itself gracefully or show a helpful message
3. Not throw errors or crash
4. Not show the Jujutsu tool window if not applicable

## Testing Scenarios

- [ ] Open project without .jj directory
- [ ] Check if VCS is properly disabled
- [ ] Verify no errors in IDE logs
- [ ] Ensure Jujutsu tool window doesn't appear
- [ ] Test with project that has Git but not JJ

## Related Code

- `JujutsuVcs.root` property (auto-discovery logic)
- `JujutsuRootChecker` (currently disabled due to API changes)
- VCS detection and initialization

title: Marketplace builds ship without JJP1 signing key, so preview codes are rejected
description: Marketplace 0.8.19 jar lacks preview/code-key.bin (GitHub release jar has it). The publishPlugin step runs bare ./gradlew publishPlugin with no PREVIEW_CODE_KEY, so generatePreviewCodeKey re-runs and deletes the key before repackaging. Fix: pass the key + -PrequirePreviewCodeKey to publishPlugin and add a jar-contents assertion in CI.
close_reason: publishPlugin now gets PREVIEW_CODE_KEY + -PrequirePreviewCodeKey; CI asserts code-key.bin is in the built and published jars. Takes effect from the next release.

title: Log jumps to an unrelated row after Undo: requestSelection resolves against the stale model
description: Regression from mxwrvuwvvltt (jj-idea-3r7s). After an action then Undo, performUndo -> invalidate(select=WorkingCopy) fires logRefresh then changeSelection. requestSelection resolves @ against the stale model, selects/scrolls the old row and now clears pendingSelection, so the fresh setEntries treats the selection as carried (no scroll). With logOrder following jj order, @ moves rows after an op, so the viewport sits at an unrelated spot. Fix: mark refresh pending on logRefresh so requestSelection defers to the next setEntries, which selects and scrolls once.
close_reason: Fixed: requestSelection defers to the next setEntries while a refresh is pending

title: Bug: Reference filter dropdown freezes EDT for many bookmarks/tags - O(n^2) DefaultActionGroup.add (GitHub #136)
description: Reporter fan-tom (IU-262.10968.63, plugin 0.8.18): opening the log's Reference dropdown freezes the EDT for 17s. Root cause: JujutsuReferenceFilterComponent.createActionGroup() (ui/log/JujutsuReferenceFilterComponent.kt:173-195) calls group.add() once per bookmark/tag. Each DefaultActionGroup.addAction runs createActionIdResolver, which calls ActionManager.getId for every existing child (intellij-community DefaultActionGroup.java:156-173); addAll and the List constructor loop the same way. So building the menu is O(n^2) in the number of references, all on the EDT. Fix: return precomputed children from a lightweight ActionGroup.getChildren (no per-add resolver) so the build is O(n). Apply the same to JujutsuAuthorFilterComponent (:53), which has the same pattern. Consider a speed-search popup too: a flat menu of thousands of entries is hard to use anyway. Scale deliverable: operation-count test showing linear build cost in number of references. Ask reporter for bookmark/tag counts. Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/136
close_reason: Reference/Author popups built as precomputed ListActionGroup (O(n)); scale test added

title: Gutter change markers missing when file was added in an ancestor change (regression 0.8.14, GitHub #133)
description:
Reporter (emadpres, RustRover 2026.2.3, plugin 0.8.18): gutter indicators for updated lines are not shown when the file was added in an ancestor change. Example: parent 'aaa' adds foo.rs; at 'bbb'/@ adding a line to foo.rs shows no markers. Last good 0.8.13; bad 0.8.14-0.8.18. Reporter says it occurs regardless of the Diff Base option.

0.8.14 introduced the Diff Base setting (jj-idea-fwea, #43). Suspects: vcs/diffbase/DiffbaseContentLoader.kt - if the file does not exist at the resolved base, contentRevision.content is null -> loadContent returns null -> handleLoadingError -> dropBaseRevision() -> no markers at all (should be an empty base so every line shows as added). That does not obviously explain 'Working copy parent' mode (isTrackedFile is false there so the platform tracker is used) - verify; also check JujutsuChangeProvider before-revisions for a file added in an ancestor.

Acceptance: test for gutter base when file is absent at the diff base; test for the @- mode. Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/133
acceptance_criteria: Markers show for a file added in an ancestor under every Diff Base option; regression tests added

title: [bug] Restore hidden for a deleted-only selection: empty VIRTUAL_FILE_ARRAY defeats the restorePaths fallback
description:
toddjonker (GitHub #122, 2026-09-18): edited files offer Restore, but a deleted file in the working copy or log panel does not. kkkev committed publicly (2026-09-20) to fixing this 'as quickly as I can'.

Root cause (traced 2026-09-20, not a missing feature - restoring a deleted file works once invoked; only the enablement check is wrong):

- RestoreSelectionAction.update (actions/file/RestoreSelectionAction.kt:59) enables on e.singleRepoForRestore != null.
- singleRepoForRestore resolves via AnActionEvent.restorePaths (actions/ActionEventExtensions.kt:104):
      fileList?.map { it.filePath } ?: changes.flatMap { it.allPaths }.distinct()
  The ?: fallback to changes.allPaths is exactly the deleted/rename-source path (what jj-idea-g5nn fixed in June), but it only fires when fileList is NULL.
- JujutsuChangesTree.uiDataSnapshot (ui/common/JujutsuChangesTree.kt:203) publishes
      sink.lazy(CommonDataKeys.VIRTUAL_FILE_ARRAY) { selectedChangesSnapshot.mapNotNull { it.filePath.virtualFile }.toTypedArray() }
  A deleted file has no virtualFile, so this is an EMPTY BUT NON-NULL array.
- fileList (ActionEventExtensions.kt:59) is getData(...)?.toList() -> empty list, not null -> restorePaths empty -> singleRepoForRestore null -> action hides itself. The allPaths fallback is unreachable.

Second symptom, same cause, also in scope: a selection MIXING a deleted file with an edited one DOES show Restore, but the deleted file is silently dropped from the operation (fileList is non-empty and wins outright).
design:
Fix shape: treat an empty VIRTUAL_FILE_ARRAY as absent. Prefer scoping this to restorePaths rather than to fileList itself, so filePaths' documented precedence invariant (ActionEventExtensions.kt:62-78) is left alone - ActionEventExtensionsTest's 'fileList takes precedence over changes' test pins it.

Note the two are not equivalent for a mixed selection: falling back only when fileList is empty still drops the deleted file from a mixed selection. To fix both symptoms, restorePaths should union the fileList paths with changes.flatMap { it.allPaths } rather than choosing between them, since allPaths is authoritative for deletes and rename sources.

Tests: regression coverage for (1) deleted-only selection enables Restore and restores the file, (2) mixed deleted+edited selection restores BOTH, in RestoreSelectionAction and RestoreToChangeAction (the latter shares restorePaths at actions/filechange/RestoreToChangeAction.kt:42).

Manual: UI-affecting - report smoke steps for Restore on a deleted file from both the Working Copy panel and a log commit's changes list, plus the manual regression scope for the MT-* sections covering restore.

title: Intermittent VCS root deactivation race on project reopen
description: Reopening a project (close then open again in same IDE session) intermittently causes Jujutsu VCS to deactivate and roots to drop to 0 a few seconds after load, disappearing the UI. Confirmed via sandbox idea.log timeline: activate+1-root at open, then 'Workspace model updated: Add project root' followed by 'Jujutsu VCS deactivated' + 'Initialized roots changed to 0 roots' 5-15s later, on roughly half of reopens (not deterministic). Likely a race between our async VCS-root discovery (JujutsuStateModel's jujutsuVcsRoots/initialisedRepositories) and the platform's VcsRootScanner auto-detection re-scan triggered by a late content-root registration. This may be the real underlying cause the GitHub #113 reporter hit (the SlowOperations assertion may be a symptom of the same churn), per user feedback while verifying jj-idea-nuk0's fix. Investigating root cause now.
close_reason: Duplicate — this is jj-idea-3zk1, already root-caused in an earlier session (ModuleVcsDetector.kt:194-199 deletes the VCS directory mapping on workspace-model resync when colocated with another VCS; re-detection gated off by haveDefaultMapping()). See 3zk1 for the confirmed debug-log trace and design.

title: VFS mark-dirty runs on EDT after every mutating jj command
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
Run any mutating jj action in the plugin (e.g. New Change) against a repository large enough that a full VFS mark-dirty walk is noticeably slow; watch the IDE log.

## Analysis
Reporter's stack trace: com.intellij.util.SlowOperations.assertSlowOperationsAreAllowed fires from NewChangeAction, but this hits every mutating command.

JujutsuRepository.invalidate() (jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt:638) calls VfsUtil.markDirtyAndRefresh(true, true, true, directory). The async=true flag only makes the *refresh* async - the recursive markDirtyRecursively walk (and its symlink resolution, which hits FSRecordsImpl.update) happens synchronously on the caller's thread. Callers reach it from CommandExecutor$Command.handleResult -> runLater (util/Tasks.kt:110), i.e. the EDT, hence the SlowOperations assertion.

One fix at the single invalidate() call site covers every mutating action (edit/new/abandon/rebase/squash/split/fetch, UndoBalloon.kt:52, JujutsuWorkingCopySwitcher.kt:87,95, JujutsuMergeProvider.kt:29): do the mark-dirty work on a pooled thread, keeping only the state-model notifications on the EDT.

Scale note: the walk is O(files under the repo root), so this is exactly the loop that must not sit on the EDT - ship an operation-count test per contributing.md's Performance & Scale rule.
design: Do the VfsUtil.markDirtyAndRefresh walk on a pooled thread from JujutsuRepository.invalidate() (jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt:638); keep only the state-model notifications (logRefresh, changeSelection) on the EDT.
acceptance_criteria: markDirtyAndRefresh's synchronous walk no longer runs on the EDT for any mutating jj command; a large-repo operation-count test exists; the reporter's SlowOperations assertion no longer fires.
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/113
close_reason: Fixed: refreshVfsInBackground() moves the mark-dirty walk off the EDT via runInBackground. Verified with InvalidateVfsScaleTest (operation-count) and a new JujutsuStateModelPlatformTest case (real off-EDT dispatch); ./gradlew check green.

title: JJ VCS root mapping permanently lost after workspace-model cache resync
description:
On project open, when the workspace model is loaded from a cache and then IntelliJ resyncs it against real on-disk project state a moment later (ProjectSynchronizerUtilImpl: "Workspace model loaded from cache. Syncing real project state into workspace model in N ms"), the resync's content-root diff can remove the content root backing a JJ repo without ever re-adding it. ModuleVcsDetector.scheduleScanForNewContentRoots (ModuleVcsDetector.kt:194-199) unconditionally deletes the corresponding VcsDirectoryMapping the moment a content root disappears from the workspace model, regardless of whether the directory is re-added moments later.

Normally the platform's own re-detection (autoDetectForContentRoots, triggered on content roots *added*) would restore the mapping. But that path is gated behind `ProjectLevelVcsManagerImpl.haveDefaultMapping() == null` (ModuleVcsDetector.kt:179) and a single-common-VCS check (autoDetectForContentRoots, lines ~155-166). When a second VCS mapping already exists for the same project (e.g. a colocated .git alongside .jj — confirmed via the "Mixed VCS roots (JJ + other)" log line before the loss), haveDefaultMapping() returns non-null, so the re-detect-on-add path never runs. The removed JJ mapping is never restored, even though the .jj directory is still present on disk and the repo is fully valid.

Symptom: the JJ UI (tool windows, log tab, status bar widgets) briefly appears on project open, then permanently disappears a few seconds later, because JujutsuStateModel.jujutsuVcsRoots reads its value straight from ProjectLevelVcsManager's directory mappings, which the platform silently dropped.

## Repro
Open a project where the JJ repo is colocated with another VCS (e.g. git), sized large enough that project open takes a noticeable cache->real-state resync (jj-stress-test reproduces reliably). Confirmed via debug log category #com.intellij.openapi.vcs.impl.projectlevelman.NewMappings:

```
09:15:00,211  NewMappings: "roots removed [jj-stress-test]" - ModuleVcsDetector deletes the mapping
09:15:00,212  JujutsuVcsBase: "Jujutsu VCS deactivated for project"
09:15:00,213  jujutsuVcsRoots v5 loaded, changed=true   <- now empty
09:15:00,225  JpsProjectModelSynchronizer: "Attempt 1: Changes were successfully applied"
09:15:00,225  ProjectSynchronizerUtilImpl: "Workspace model loaded from cache. Syncing real
               project state into workspace model in 1443 ms"
   ...
09:15:05,382  JujutsuUiEnabler: "Mixed VCS roots (JJ + other), showing both logs"   <- stale replay
09:15:05,417  Initialized Repositories v3 loaded, changed=true   <- now reflects empty jujutsuVcsRoots
09:15:05,843  JujutsuStateModel: "Initialized roots changed to 0 roots"
09:15:05,843  JujutsuUiEnabler: "No VCS roots remaining, letting VCS system clean up"
```

## Root cause
Platform behavior (ModuleVcsDetector's removed-content-root handling has no debounce/retry, and its re-detection path is gated off whenever another VCS mapping coexists). Not fixable upstream from this plugin; must self-heal on our side.
design:
Do not treat ProjectLevelVcsManager's directory mappings as unconditionally authoritative for jujutsuVcsRoots. When initialisedRepositories collapses to empty (or jujutsuVcsRoots drops previously-known roots) as a result of a directory-mapping removal, self-heal:

1. In JujutsuStateModel, remember the last known-good set of JJ root paths (or re-derive from project content roots directly via WorkspaceModel/ModuleManager rather than solely from VCS directory mappings).
2. On VCS_CONFIGURATION_CHANGED (or when initialisedRepositories transitions to empty after having had roots), re-verify each previously-known root path on disk via JujutsuRootChecker.isJujutsuRoot. If still present, re-register the mapping ourselves via ProjectLevelVcsManager.setDirectoryMappings(...) instead of waiting on the platform's auto-detect (which we've shown can be permanently gated off by haveDefaultMapping() when a second VCS is colocated).
3. Guard against thrashing: only self-heal a genuine platform-dropped mapping (root still has .jj on disk), never fight a legitimate user-initiated mapping removal (e.g. via Settings > Version Control > Directory Mappings, or jj repo actually deleted).
4. Add a regression test simulating a directory-mapping removal via ProjectLevelVcsManager while the .jj directory still exists, asserting the plugin restores the mapping and the UI does not disable.

See conversation history / debug log excerpt in the description for the confirmed causal chain (JujutsuStateModel.kt, JujutsuUiEnabler.kt, platform ModuleVcsDetector.kt:194-199 and :179).
close_reason: Fixed: added JujutsuVcsRootRecovery to self-heal a JJ VcsDirectoryMapping dropped by the platform's workspace-model resync, in-session, without fighting deliberate user removal. Follow-up jj-idea-ccm3 filed for the across-restart persistence case.

title: [bug] "Write-unsafe context!" error from saveAllDocuments; documents never saved before jj commands (GitHub #106)
description:
GitHub #106 (filed 2026-09-04): fetching remote changes from the log toolbar sometimes produces an IDE error "Write-unsafe context! Model changes are allowed from write-safe contexts only" with FileDocumentManagerImpl.saveAllDocuments <- in.kkkev.jjidea.util.TasksKt.saveAllDocuments(Tasks.kt:38) <- TransactionGuardImpl$1.run(TransactionGuardImpl.java:211).

Regression introduced by the still-open jj-idea-c4tp fix (its hazard 1), which changed saveAllDocuments() to post with ModalityState.any(). Two compounding defects: the guard checks isWriteSafeModality(ModalityState.current()) while the platform assertion checks TransactionGuardImpl.myWritingAllowed, which wrapLaterInvocation only sets from the modality PASSED IN (any() is never write-safe) - so guard and assertion disagree. And ModalityState.any() is documented as forbidden for VFS/PSI/project-model work, so under it the save could never legally run at all: jj commands have been running against stale on-disk content since c4tp landed.

Severity P1: silent data-correctness issue (unsaved editor content not written before jj operates) plus a user-visible IDE error.
design:
# Fix GH #106 — "Write-unsafe context!" error from `saveAllDocuments()`

## Context

GitHub #106 (filed 2026-09-04): fetching remote changes from the log toolbar
*sometimes* produces an IDE error:

```
java.lang.Throwable: Write-unsafe context! Model changes are allowed from write-safe
contexts only. current modality=ModalityState.NON_MODAL
  at ...TransactionGuardImpl.assertWriteSafeEnvironment(TransactionGuardImpl.java:145)
  at ...FileDocumentManagerImpl.saveAllDocuments(FileDocumentManagerImpl.java:264)
  at in.kkkev.jjidea.util.TasksKt.saveAllDocuments$lambda$0$0(Tasks.kt:38)
  at ...TransactionGuardImpl$1.run(TransactionGuardImpl.java:211)
```

This is a **regression introduced by the still-open jj-idea-c4tp fix** (hazard 1 in that
bead), which changed `saveAllDocuments()` to post with `ModalityState.any()`. It is not
yet tracked in beads, and neither are 12 other open GitHub issues (see Appendix).

### Root cause (traced through `../intellij-community`)

`util/Tasks.kt:31-46` currently does:

```kotlin
app.invokeAndWait({
    if (TransactionGuard.getInstance().isWriteSafeModality(ModalityState.current())) {
        app.runWriteIntentReadAction<Unit, Nothing> {
            FileDocumentManager.getInstance().saveAllDocuments()
        }
    } else { log.info(...) }
}, ModalityState.any())
```

Two independent defects compound:

1. **The guard checks the wrong predicate.** Every `invokeLater`/`invokeAndWait` runnable
   is wrapped by `TransactionGuardImpl.wrapLaterInvocation` (`TransactionGuardImpl.java:203-213`),
   which enables writing (`myWritingAllowed = true`) **only if the modality the caller
   passed in** is write-safe. `myWriteSafeModalities` is populated solely by `nonModal()`
   at construction (`:34`) and by `enteredModality()` (`:200`) — `ModalityState.any()` is
   never in it, so `isWriteSafeModality(any())` is `false` and the `else` branch at `:210`
   runs the body with `myWritingAllowed` left at whatever the EDT's ambient value was
   (`false` for a queued runnable).

   Our guard instead asks `isWriteSafeModality(ModalityState.current())`. With no modal
   dialog showing, `current()` is `nonModal()`, which **is** registered write-safe → the
   guard passes. `assertWriteSafeEnvironment()` (`:137-149`) then checks `myWritingAllowed`
   — `false` → `LOG.error`. The guard and the assertion are checking different things and
   can disagree.

2. **`ModalityState.any()` is documented as forbidden for this.** `ModalityState.java:74-78`:
   *"Please don't use it unless absolutely needed. The code under this modality can only
   perform purely UI operations, it shouldn't access any PSI, VFS or project model."*
   `saveAllDocuments()` is a VFS write. Under `any()` the save can therefore **never**
   legally run — so even without the error, c4tp's change silently disabled document
   saving before every jj command, meaning jj can operate on stale on-disk content.

**Why "sometimes":** `gitFetchAction` (`actions/git/gitRemoteActions.kt:55-73`) reaches
`performFetch` on a pooled thread when there is exactly one remote (`:64`) but via
`runLater` on the EDT when the dialog is shown (`:67-71`). The EDT path is the one that
queues through `wrapLaterInvocation` and errors. `TransactionGuardImpl.myErrorReported`
(`:145`) also de-dupes repeats within an activity.

### Intended outcome

`saveAllDocuments()` actually saves documents again, never logs a write-unsafe error, and
still cannot park a pooled thread indefinitely behind a modal dialog (c4tp's original
concern).

## Design

Rewrite `saveAllDocuments()` in `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/util/Tasks.kt`:

1. **Post with `ModalityState.nonModal()`, not `any()`.** `nonModal()` is registered
   write-safe, so `wrapLaterInvocation` enables writing and the save is legal. This matches
   platform prior art — `VcsUpdateTask.kt:66-68` (`edtWriteAction { saveAllDocuments() }`)
   and `ChangeListManagerRefreshHelper.kt:109-112` (`withContext(Dispatchers.EDT)`) — neither
   of which uses `any()`.

2. **Replace the blocking `invokeAndWait` with `invokeLater` + a bounded `CountDownLatch`
   wait.** This keeps c4tp's property (a modal dialog can no longer park the calling
   pooled thread for the modal's lifetime) without borrowing `any()`. Pass `app.disposed`
   as the `invokeLater` expiry condition so shutdown doesn't leak the runnable. On timeout,
   log a warning and proceed — bounded staleness only in the rare modal case, instead of an
   indefinite park. Use a named constant (suggest 10s) for the timeout.

3. **Run inline when already on the EDT.** `performFetch` and several other call sites
   reach `saveAllDocuments()` from `runLater`, i.e. already on the EDT. Save directly there
   rather than re-queueing.

4. **Guard with `TransactionGuard.getInstance().isWritingAllowed()`**, not
   `isWriteSafeModality(ModalityState.current())`. `isWritingAllowed()` returns exactly the
   `myWritingAllowed` field that `assertWriteSafeEnvironment()` asserts on
   (`TransactionGuardImpl.java:126-134`), so the guard can no longer disagree with the
   assertion. It returns `true` unconditionally off-EDT, which is fine — we only evaluate it
   on the EDT. Keep the existing `log.info` skip message (it's the right "skip rather than
   save" fallback for an EDT caller inside a modal).

5. **Update the `## Modality (jj-idea-c4tp)` KDoc** (`Tasks.kt:21-29`) — it currently
   documents the `any()` rationale and asserts the guard "then no-ops the save", which is
   the incorrect reasoning above. Replace with the `nonModal()` + bounded-wait rationale
   and a pointer to GH #106.

No behavioural change is needed at the two call sites
(`jj/CommandExecutor.kt:659`, `:666`).

### Scale

No filesystem traversal or per-file/per-commit loop is added — `saveAllDocuments()` cost is
unchanged (it is the platform's own O(open documents) call). No operation-count test needed.

## Files

- `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/util/Tasks.kt` — the fix (lines 15-46).
- `src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/util/SaveAllDocumentsTest.kt` — new platform test.

## Beads

- `bd create` a bug for GH #106, referencing jj-idea-c4tp as the regression source.
- Update `jj-idea-c4tp`'s notes: hazard 1's fix was wrong and was corrected by the new bead.
  Leave c4tp in progress (its acceptance criterion — reproducing the hang with a thread
  dump — is still open).

## Verification

**Automated** — new `@Tag("platform") @TestApplication` test following the existing pattern
in `src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/util/TasksBackgroundErrorTest.kt`, using
`LoggedErrorProcessor` so a platform `LOG.error` fails the test:

1. *Regression guard:* call `saveAllDocuments()` from a pooled thread inside
   `LoggedErrorProcessor.executeWith` and assert nothing was logged as an error. This fails
   on the current code and passes after the fix.
2. *Same from the EDT* (the `gitFetchAction` dialog path that actually produced the report)
   — assert no logged error.
3. *It actually saves:* create a document with unsaved content via
   `FileDocumentManager`/an in-memory `LightVirtualFile`, call `saveAllDocuments()`, assert
   the document is no longer in `FileDocumentManager.getInstance().unsavedDocuments`. This
   is the check that catches c4tp's silent "never saves" outcome.

Run with `./gradlew platformTest --tests '*SaveAllDocuments*'`, then `./gradlew check`.

**Manual smoke** (jj repo with 2+ git remotes, so the dialog path is taken):

1. Open a tracked file, type an edit, do not save.
2. Log toolbar → Fetch → pick a remote → OK.
3. Expect: no "Write-unsafe context!" IDE error balloon; the edit is written to disk before
   `jj git fetch` runs; the log refreshes.
4. Repeat with a single-remote repo (pooled-thread path, no dialog) — same expectations.

**Manual regression scope:** MT sections covering git fetch/push and any action routed
through `CommandExecutor.executeAsync`/`executeWithProgress` — resolve the exact `MT-*` IDs
from `docs/manual-tests.md` during implementation. `docs/manual-tests.md` needs no new
section: this changes no manual-testable surface, it restores existing behaviour.

**CHANGELOG.md** — user-facing entry under `[Unreleased]`, e.g. *"Fixed an error reported
when fetching from a remote, and restored saving of modified files before jj commands run."*

## Appendix — untriaged GitHub issues (not part of this change)

13 open GitHub issues have no beads entry: **#48, #74, #76, #82, #88, #95, #101, #102,
#103, #104, #105, #106**, and **#100** (fixed in `b4036dc18` but still open upstream).
Seven were filed in the 48 hours before 2026-09-05. Worth a separate triage pass.
acceptance_criteria: saveAllDocuments() saves modified documents before every jj command again; no "Write-unsafe context!" error is logged from either the EDT (multi-remote fetch dialog) or pooled-thread (single-remote) fetch path; a modal dialog cannot park the calling pooled thread indefinitely (the property jj-idea-c4tp was protecting). Covered by a @Tag("platform") test that fails on the current code.
notes: GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/106. Regression source: jj-idea-c4tp (hazard 1). Traced against ../intellij-community: TransactionGuardImpl.java:34, :126-149, :200, :203-213; ModalityState.java:74-78. Platform prior art for the correct shape: VcsUpdateTask.kt:66-68, ChangeListManagerRefreshHelper.kt:109-112.
close_reason: Fixed: saveAllDocuments() now posts with ModalityState.nonModal() (write-safe) with a bounded 10s wait instead of the broken ModalityState.any(), and guards with TransactionGuard.isWritingAllowed(). New platform test SaveAllDocumentsTest covers pooled-thread/EDT no-error and actual-save-clears-unsaved-flag. CHANGELOG updated. ./gradlew check has 20 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (confirmed reproducing in isolation without this fix) — JujutsuEditorActionGroupTest, FileChangeActionGroupPlatformTest, HunkPickerDialogTest, JujutsuLogContextMenuActionsLiveSelectionTest, JujutsuLogTableEnterActionTest, plus a cascading LeakHunter failure; worth a separate bead.

title: [bug] Split dialog preview panes don't match their titles (GitHub #101)
description:
The right pane of the Split dialog's file preview is labelled "Child" but actually
shows the parent-remainder content, and both title strings are derived from that same
right-hand content. For a fully-ticked (fully-moved) file, the right pane content
equals the left pane content (the base), so the diff reads "The contents are
identical" under titles that claim "Parent (unchanged)" / "Child (all changes)" —
which looks like a bug because it is one.

Root cause: HunkPickPreviewController.render() (src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/common/HunkPickPreviewController.kt,
~line 122) always puts contents.before on the left and resolveContent(...) on the
right. For SplitDialog, resolveContent is computePreviewLeftContent
(ui/split/SplitDialog.kt:274), which computes the FIRST-COMMIT (parent) remainder —
so the "right"/"Child" pane is actually showing parent content. Both title strings
come from describeSplitState(content, ...) (SplitDialog.kt:663), evaluated on that
same wrong-side content.

SquashFilePreview.kt is NOT affected — its left title is a static "Before" so its
pane and title agree.
design:
Chosen fix: make the panes match the titles rather than relabel around the bug.

- left = first-commit (parent) remainder (today's computePreviewLeftContent result /
  override)
- right = second-commit (child) content = contents.after — the child always ends up
  with the full original file content
- titles continue to come from describeSplitState, now correctly describing each side

Resulting behaviour:
  ticked:   [Parent (unchanged)]  base      |  after      [Child (all changes)]
  unticked: [Parent (all changes)] after    |  after      [Child (no changes)]
  partial:  [Parent (partial)]    remainder |  after      [Child (partial)]

Files to touch:
- ui/common/HunkPickPreviewController.kt — render() hardcodes contents.before as the
  left side today. Needs a per-dialog seam for BOTH sides (Squash must keep `before`
  on the left) — e.g. widen resolveContent to return a (left, right) pair, or add
  separate resolveLeft/resolveRight lambdas.
- ui/split/SplitDialog.kt — rename computePreviewLeftContent (it feeds the RIGHT side
  today, will feed the LEFT side after the fix); supply contents.after as the right
  side; keep the newParent/parallel label swap at SplitDialog.kt:361-378 working.
- ui/squash/SquashIntoDialog.kt / SquashFilePreview.kt — adapt to the widened seam
  with no behaviour change.
- Tests: src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/split/SplitDialogTest.kt — add a case
  asserting the two preview sides differ for a fully-ticked file.

P1: the preview actively misleads about what a split will do, on a destructive-ish
operation.
close_reason: Fixed: HunkPickPreviewController now pairs each pane's text with its own title (previewPanes seam), so Split's right/Child pane shows contents.after instead of duplicating the parent-remainder. Added regression tests.

title: DnD core: payload/target model, y-aware hit-test, zones, indicator, guards
description: Foundational infrastructure for drag-and-drop graph operations (docs/design/jj-idea-6oeg-drag-and-drop-graph-ops.md, section 1). Introduce sealed DragPayload (Commit/BookmarkRef/TagRef/WorkingCopyRef/Files) and DropTarget (CommitRow/Gap/RefChip) types, and the single (payload, target) dispatch table that decides the operation - mirroring how LogClickTarget.resolve already centralizes click resolution. Extend JujutsuLogTable's hit-testing to be y-aware (clickTargetAt is x-only today) with the quarter/half zone split (band = min(JBUI.scale(6), rowHeight / 4)), bound per-row not per-gap (top band of row N always means -B N regardless of what's drawn above). Build on DnDSupport.createBuilder(...) directly (NOT RowsDnDSupport - it requires EditableModel/list-reorder semantics that don't fit a DAG-derived row order; see design doc section 5). Add hysteresis so zone assignment doesn't flicker. Paint feedback via DnDEvent.setHighlighting (FILLED_RECTANGLE for insert-boundary, RECTANGLE for onto), and surface every guard via setDropPossible(false, reason) with a real reason string (immutability via DuplicateImmutabilityGuard.invalidDestinationIds, cycles via RebaseSimulator.excludedDestinationIds, cross-repo via repo identity, self-drop).
design: See docs/design/jj-idea-6oeg-drag-and-drop-graph-ops.md sections 1, 2, 5, 6.
acceptance_criteria: DragPayload/DropTarget types exist with a single dispatch point. Log table hit-testing resolves a y-position to ONTO/BEFORE/AFTER using the specified zone geometry with a test covering the boundary math. Invalid drops show a reject cursor and a real reason string, verified for at least immutability and cross-repo cases. SmoothAutoScroller is wired for long logs.
notes: Blocks every other DnD gesture bead.
close_reason: DnD infra (payload/target model, y-aware zone hit-test, guards, dispatch, DnDSupport wiring) landed with full unit+platform test coverage; ./gradlew check passes. Local throwaway verification spike sits on top (not pushed) for manual runIde testing.

title: Undo our own jj operation via jj op revert + balloon action
description: Foundation of the undo mini-roadmap (docs/design/undo-support-roadmap.md, Stage 1). Add CommandExecutor.opLog(limit, template) and opRevert(id, what) plus pure arg builders in CliExecutor.kt. Identify our own operation by capturing the op-log head before running a command, then matching self.parents() among the most recent ops afterward - never jj undo (reverts the repo's last op, which may not be ours) or jj op restore (a reset that discards concurrent work). Withhold the undo affordance if the parent match is not unique. Pass --what repo (not the default repo remote-tracking) so undo doesn't desync push state. Wire the result into a balloon via the existing Notification.addExpiringAction helper (ui/services/JujutsuNotifications.kt) on the Jujutsu BALLOON group.
design: See docs/design/undo-support-roadmap.md Stage 1 for the full concurrency-safety analysis (jj op revert vs jj undo vs jj op restore).
acceptance_criteria: opLog and opRevert exist on CommandExecutor with unit-tested arg builders. A helper exists that captures/matches/reverts per the algorithm above, with a test proving it withholds undo on a non-unique parent match. At least one mutating action shows an undo balloon after completing.
notes: Blocks every immediate-apply drag-and-drop bead in jj-idea-6oeg's design doc (docs/design/jj-idea-6oeg-drag-and-drop-graph-ops.md).
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix New Change preview: pending-row rendering crash, radio/flash symptoms, multi-line description
description:
New Change... dialog (jj-idea-grc8) crashes: URISyntaxException building a jjc:// link from the synthetic 'pending' LogEntry's placeholder id (LogEntryText.kt appendSummary -> ChangeKey -> URI). Also: earlier placeholder 'zzzz...z' literally collided with jj's real root change id (see CommitGraphBuilderRepoScopingTest doc comment). Reported symptoms, likely all downstream of the paint-time exception: preview pane shows nothing, radio buttons visually desync (multi-selected or not updating), dialog flashes grey before displaying.

Fix: add LogEntry.pending: Boolean = false (matches existing isWorkingCopy/hasConflict/isEmpty/immutable idiom). Add a minimal pending-row paint path (e.g. appendPendingSummary) that skips ChangeKey/link, bookmarks, tags, and status badges entirely -- renderer dispatches on entry.pending at the LaidOutCell.forRow call site and in JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.buildTooltip. NewChangeDialog's synthetic entry sets pending=true and uses a short placeholder id distinct BY LENGTH from any real 32-char changeId/40-char commitId (no longer needs to look 'real' since no link is ever built from it).

Also: description field should be a multi-line JBTextArea (rows=4, lineWrap, wrapStyleWord) in a JBScrollPane, matching WorkingCopyControlsPanel.descriptionArea's styling -- currently a single-line JBTextField.

Depends on jj-idea-fjsg (DagNode refactor) landing first per user's request to land the refactor as a separate, verified-inert commit before behavior changes on top of it.
acceptance_criteria: ./gradlew check passes; opening New Change... for all 3 placement modes shows no exception in idea.log; preview's pending row renders without a clickable link; radio buttons respond correctly to clicks; no grey flash on dialog open; description field wraps multi-line text
close_reason: Fixed: added LogEntry.pending flag + a minimal appendPendingSummary render path (no ChangeKey/link, no bookmarks/tags/status badges), guarded at appendSummaryAndStatuses/LaidOutCell.forRow/JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.buildTooltip. Radio-button desync and grey flash confirmed resolved by the user as consequences of the paint-time exception. Bonus (user feedback during manual testing): the working-copy checkbox now toggles which row renders bold '@' in the preview, and the pending row shows the '(empty)' indicator. Description field is now a multi-line JBTextArea. ./gradlew check green; new PendingLogEntryRenderingTest + LaidOutCellTest cases cover the crash scenario directly.

title: File history table shows blank Date/Author/Committer (GitHub #88)
description:
GitHub #88: 'Show History' on a file shows Date/Author/Committer columns blank.

Root cause (verified): the platform history path (vcs/history/JujutsuHistoryProvider.kt:38) calls logService.getLogAndFileStatuses(...), which builds its request from logTemplates.fileStatusesFor(filePath) (jj/cli/CliLogService.kt:98-99, 416-422). fileStatusesFor composes on basicLogTemplate (buildBasicTemplate, ~CliLogService.kt:340-384), which never asks jj for author/committer fields — only buildFullTemplate (CliLogService.kt:386-396) fills authorTimestamp/committerTimestamp/author/committer. So LogEntry (jj/LogEntry.kt:22-25) keeps those fields at their null defaults, and JujutsuFileRevision (vcs/history/JujutsuFileRevision.kt) returns null for revisionDate/author/authorEmail/committerName/committerDate — the platform Date/Author columns and the plugin's own CommitterColumnInfo/CommitTimestampColumnInfo (vcs/history/JujutsuHistoryColumns.kt) render blank.

The plugin's own custom file-history panel (ui/history/JujutsuFileHistoryDataLoader.kt -> getLog) is unaffected since getLog already uses fullLogTemplate.

Fix shape: have fileStatusesFor take the base LogTemplate<LogEntry> as a parameter, and make getLogAndFileStatuses mirror the supportsPushedAncestor() branching that getLog already does at CliLogService.kt:60-72 (fullLogTemplate with fullLogTemplateWithoutPushedAncestor as fallback). Note getLogAndFileStatuses currently calls the private getLog(template, ...) overload with no fallbackTemplate, so that branching needs to be added, not just the template swapped.
acceptance_criteria: Platform 'Show History' tab populates Date, Author, Committer and Commit Time for every revision; a unit/contract test asserts the template used by getLogAndFileStatuses includes the author and committer signature fields; ./gradlew check passes.
close_reason: Fixed: getLogAndFileStatuses now routes through fullLogTemplate with pushed-ancestor fallback, same as getLog

title: CI: fail release workflow if Marketplace rejects the upload
description: Follow-up to jj-idea-ppqv (0.8.11 Marketplace compatibility rejection). publishPlugin succeeding only proves the upload was accepted -- Marketplace then runs its own async compatibility check and can still reject it, and a successful publishPlugin step looks identical in the Actions log either way. 0.8.11 was rejected silently and nobody noticed until the next release. Add a post-publish step to .github/workflows/build.yml that polls the public Marketplace API (https://plugins.jetbrains.com/api/plugins/30576/updates) for the just-released version to show up approved+listed, and fails the job loudly if it doesn't within a generous window.
design: Added 'Verify JetBrains Marketplace approval' step after 'Publish to JetBrains Marketplace' in the build job, gated on the same is_release/PUBLISH_TOKEN condition. Polls every 2 minutes for up to 50 minutes (observed real-world approval latency was ~40 min for 0.8.12). Response schema note: the endpoint returns a bare JSON array, and the approval field is literally named 'approve', not 'approved' -- verified against the live API. Writes the response to a file rather than a shell variable (command substitution was unreliable with the large embedded changelog HTML).
acceptance_criteria: Workflow step added and YAML validated; jq query manually verified against the live Marketplace API for both a matching version (0.8.12, confirmed match) and a non-matching version (confirmed no match / correct failure path).
close_reason: Added Verify JetBrains Marketplace approval step to .github/workflows/build.yml, polling the Marketplace API every 2 min for up to 50 min after publishPlugin and failing the job with an actionable message if the released version isn't approved+listed. Logic verified locally against the live API for both match and non-match cases.

title: Fix 0.8.11 marketplace compatibility rejection (override-only + internal API usage)
description: 0.8.11 was rejected by JetBrains Marketplace's automated compatibility check and never went live (marketplace API still shows 0.8.10 as latest), even though our own CI (verifyPlugin, compat matrix) passed. Root cause: WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt's stableAction wrapper called delegate().actionPerformed(e) directly, invoking AnAction.actionPerformed (an @ApiStatus.OverrideOnly method) outside the platform's own invocation machinery. Separately, JujutsuBookmarkStatusBarWidgetFactory.kt used ExperimentalUI/StatusBarWidgetSettings, both @ApiStatus.Internal. Our verifyPlugin task's failureLevel deliberately excludes INTERNAL_API_USAGES (for an unrelated, narrow, documented exemption) and never included OVERRIDE_ONLY_API_USAGES at all, so neither was caught locally.
design: Fix: replaced delegate().actionPerformed(e) with ActionManager.getInstance().tryToExecute(...) (stable public API for programmatic action invocation). Replaced ExperimentalUI.isNewUI() with the public NewUI.isEnabled() wrapper. Removed the redundant StatusBarWidgetSettings.isExplicitlyDisabled() pre-check since StatusBarWidgetsManager.updateWidget already checks it internally. Added OVERRIDE_ONLY_API_USAGES to verifyPlugin's failureLevel. Added IntelliJ 2026.1 (build 261) to the pluginVerification ides list, which was missing (unrelated gap, closed opportunistically).
acceptance_criteria: verifyPlugin passes with OVERRIDE_ONLY_API_USAGES in failureLevel; no ExperimentalUI/StatusBarWidgetSettings usage remains in src/main; 0.8.12 successfully appears on JetBrains Marketplace as latest version.
close_reason: Fixed: ActionManager.tryToExecute replaces direct AnAction.actionPerformed call; NewUI.isEnabled() replaces ExperimentalUI.isNewUI(); dropped internal StatusBarWidgetSettings pre-check. Added OVERRIDE_ONLY_API_USAGES to verifyPlugin failureLevel and 2026.1 to the verified IDE list. verifyPlugin and ./gradlew check both pass.

title: jj log fails with 'Change ID prefix is ambiguous' (GitHub #76)
description: SergejSalnikov (GitHub #76) reports background jj log crashes: 'Error from jj log: Error: Change ID prefix `q` is ambiguous' (and similarly for 'u', 'pp'), surfaced as an uncaught VcsException in CliLogService.getLog (CliLogService.kt:246), reached via RepoLogCache.fetch -> loadContext -> UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.loadExpanding. Likely root cause: LogCache.kt:128 builds its context-window revset by interpolating id.short directly (ancestors(${id.short}, $window) | ${id.short} | descendants(...)), and squashAction.kt:30 does the same (parents(${target.id.short})). ChangeId.short (ChangeId.kt:26) is a shortest-unique-prefix computed at the time a log entry was fetched/rendered; jj's actual shortest-unique-prefix length shifts as the repo grows or the working copy changes, so a short value cached from an earlier fetch can stop being unique by the time it's substituted into a later jj log/CLI call, and jj then rejects the ambiguous prefix outright.
design: Use id.full instead of id.short when building revset expressions for CLI calls — full change ids are always unambiguous. Audit both call sites (LogCache.kt:128, squashAction.kt:30) and any other Expression(...) construction that interpolates .short instead of .full. short should only be used for display, never for revset/CLI arguments.
acceptance_criteria: jj log/jj CLI calls built from ChangeId never interpolate .short into a revset expression; a regression test constructs a context-window/parents revset from a ChangeId and asserts it uses the full id; manual repro (large/busy repo where the same prefix stops being unique across two log fetches) no longer throws.
close_reason: Fixed: use ChangeId.full instead of .short in LogCache.loadContext and squashAction revsets. Regression test in RepoLogCacheTest.

title: Bookmark widget label stays blank (Bookmark: with no value)
description: closestBookmarks state is never invalidated on the normal repo-refresh paths (only on plugin-initiated JujutsuRepository.invalidate()), and JujutsuBookmarkWidget's subscriptions call plain repaint() instead of refreshPresentation(), so the value label keeps a stale zero width even when text is present. Net effect: the toolbar bookmark widget shows just 'Bookmark:' with no value on IDE start and after external jj operations, defeating the #62 'nearest bookmark' fallback.
close_reason: Fixed: invalidateRepositoryState() now loads closestBookmarks on every refresh path, and the widget uses refreshPresentation() to re-measure the value label.

title: Can't diff files with fileset meta-chars (parens/brackets) in path (GitHub #73)
description: jj CLI calls pass file paths as bare positional args, which jj parses as fileset expressions. Paths with ()[]~|& etc. fail (e.g. Next.js app-router paths). Wrap every path arg in cwd:"..." fileset literal. Also harden CliLogService template interpolation against apostrophes.
close_reason: Fixed by wrapping fileset-taking jj CLI path args in cwd:"..." (annotate excluded — takes a literal PATH, not a fileset). Verified via contract tests against real jj 0.44.

title: fileExistsAt in JujutsuFileAnnotation runs jj file show synchronously under ReadAction
description: AnnotatePreviousRevisionAction.update() (BGT action update) runs isEnabled()/getFileRevision() under an implicit ReadAction. JujutsuFileAnnotation.fileExistsAt() (jj-idea-o95r) calls repo.commandExecutor.show() synchronously, which blocks on OSProcessHandler.waitFor() and trips the platform's checkEdtAndReadAction() guard (java.lang.Throwable: Synchronous execution under ReadAction). Observed via AnnotatePreviousRevisionAction.getFileRevision -> JujutsuFileAnnotation$getPreviousFileRevisionProvider$1.getPreviousRevision -> fileExistsAt -> CliExecutor.show. Fix: use the same runInBackground + ProgressIndicatorUtils.awaitWithCheckCanceled(future) pattern already used by AnnotationFileRevision.loadContent and ParentFileRevision.loadContent in the same file (JujutsuFileAnnotation.kt:214-215, 249-250), instead of calling commandExecutor.show directly.
close_reason: fileExistsAt now runs repo.commandExecutor.show via runInBackground + ProgressIndicatorUtils.awaitWithCheckCanceled, matching the existing pattern used by AnnotationFileRevision/ParentFileRevision.loadContent in the same file, instead of blocking the ReadAction-holding thread directly.

title: 2025.1 compat leg fails compileTestKotlin on LineFragment shape change
description: LineFragment changed from a Java interface (getters) to a Kotlin interface (val properties) between 2025.1 and 2025.2. TranslateRangeTest's anonymous object implementation overrides nothing on 2025.1, breaking :compileTestKotlin in the compat CI matrix.
close_reason: Fixed TranslateRangeTest to use platform LineFragmentImpl instead of anonymous impl; also fixed workflow/contributing.md doc drift

title: Saving a file switches the editor to the diff preview tab (GitHub #67)
description: Root cause: JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview.handleSingleClick() re-opens the preview tab on any tree selection change, including the selection restore that happens when the changes tree model rebuilds after a save (or log refresh). Fix: guard the re-open to only apply on a real click.
close_reason: Fixed: guarded JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview.handleSingleClick() against tree-rebuild-driven selection events; see commit 09b35f78

title: Pushing doesn't always work
description: Often, when using the push dialog, the 'Push' button does nothing.
close_reason: Fixed: switching the remote/repo combo in the push/fetch dialogs desynced the Swing selection from the bound Kotlin property, and toNullableProperty()'s !! NPE'd on the resulting null selection inside doOKAction/applyFields, leaving the Push button inert. Also fixed a related stderr-only-success-message bug. See GitPushDialog.kt, GitFetchDialog.kt, ComboBoxModels.kt, gitRemoteActions.kt.

title: 2025.2/2025.3 compat build failure: CommitMode API renamed in 261 (2026.1)
description: CI compat (2025.2) job fails: intellij-community commit debbc20aea (2026-01-06) renamed CommitMode's members (useCommitToolWindow->isCommitTwEnabled etc.) and added a CommitMode param to AbstractVcs.getForcedCommitMode, shipping in build 261 (2026.1) onward. 2025.2 and 2025.3 (released 2025-12-08, before the commit) still have the old shape. No compat shim exists on either side. Fix: split JujutsuVcs's getForcedCommitMode override + JujutsuHiddenCommitMode into two Gradle-source-set-gated variants (kotlin-commitModeOld/New), keeping the rest of JujutsuVcs (renamed JujutsuVcsBase) shared.
close_reason: Split JujutsuVcs's getForcedCommitMode override + JujutsuHiddenCommitMode into kotlin-commitModeOld/kotlin-commitModeNew Gradle-source-set-gated variants, switched at build 261 (2026.1) - the exact commit intellij-community made the incompatible rename in (debbc20aea, 2026-01-06), verified via javap on real 2025.2/2026.2 platform jars. Rest of JujutsuVcs moved to shared JujutsuVcsBase. Verified: ./gradlew compileKotlin test -PplatformVersion=2025.2 and ./gradlew check (default 2026.2) both pass.

notes:
2026-09-06: New downstream evidence, same root cause (workspace stale/broken → repo dropped from `workingCopies`), this time surfacing as an uncaught VcsException in the platform's action-update path instead of a background-task warning:

com.intellij.openapi.vcs.VcsException: Working copy not found for Repository:
    at in.kkkev.jjidea.jj.JujutsuRepositoryImpl.getWorkingCopy(JujutsuRepository.kt:173)
    at in.kkkev.jjidea.ui.workingcopy.UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.uiDataSnapshot(UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt:375)
    at com.intellij.openapi.actionSystem.impl.MySink.uiDataSnapshot(PreCachedDataContext.kt:542)
    at com.intellij.openapi.actionSystem.DataSink$Companion.uiDataSnapshot(UiDataProvider.kt:223)
    at com.intellij.openapi.actionSystem.impl.PreCachedDataContextKt.cacheProviderData(PreCachedDataContext.kt:411)
    at com.intellij.openapi.actionSystem.impl.PreCachedDataContextKt.cacheComponentsData(PreCachedDataContext.kt:396)
    at com.intellij.openapi.actionSystem.impl.PreCachedDataContextKt.access$cacheComponentsData(PreCachedDataContext.kt:1)
    at com.intellij.openapi.actionSystem.impl.PreCachedDataContext.<init>(PreCachedDataContext.kt:127)
    at com.intellij.openapi.actionSystem.impl.Utils.createAsyncDataContext(Utils.kt:241)
    at com.intellij.openapi.fileEditor.impl.IdeUiServiceImpl.createUiDataContext(IdeUiServiceImpl.java:81)
    at com.intellij.ide.impl.DataManagerImpl.getDataContext(DataManagerImpl.kt:216)

Root-cause chain, traced this session:
- `loadWorkingCopies` (jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt:601-621) catches the stale-workspace VcsException from `repo.logCache[WorkingCopy]`, marks the root unreadable, and returns null for that repo — so the repo is silently dropped from `stateModel.workingCopies`.
- `JujutsuRepositoryImpl.workingCopy` (jj/JujutsuRepository.kt:171-173) throws `VcsException("Working copy not found for …")` for any repo missing from that map — this is the new trace, one layer downstream of the original stale-workspace failure this bead already tracks.
- `UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.uiDataSnapshot` (ui/workingcopy/UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt:375/385) and `.kt:273` (`controlsPanel.update(repo.workingCopy)`) both call the throwing getter unguarded, and `uiDataSnapshot` runs inside the platform's data-context caching path, so the exception can break action updates for the whole component (not just a background-task log warning).
- A null-safe pattern already exists to copy: `WorkingCopyControlsPanel.currentWorkingCopy()` (ui/workingcopy/WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt:305-315) reads `stateModel.workingCopies.value[...]` directly instead of the throwing `JujutsuRepository.workingCopy` getter.
- There is no workspace-aware code anywhere in the plugin (`grep -rn workspace src/main/kotlin` = no hits).
- ~20 other unguarded `repo.workingCopy` reads exist across JujutsuChangeProvider, JujutsuAnnotationProvider, advanceBookmarkAction, Split/SquashFilesAction, gitRemoteActions, VcsExtensions.kt:52 — all share this hazard while any repo's workspace is stale.

Suggested fix shape: add a `JujutsuRepository.workingCopyOrNull` (or route call sites through the `currentWorkingCopy()`-style direct map lookup) and route all UI-facing call sites through it, plus decide how the UI should present "this workspace is stale" rather than just suppressing the crash. Root-cause fix belongs with jj-idea-vwxu (Cope with stale workspaces) / jj-idea-2ol (Add workspace capability).

Raised priority P2 -> P1: this now escapes as an uncaught exception in the IntelliJ action system (breaks action updates for the Working Copy tool window), not just a background-task warning.
close_reason: Stale workspace and unreadable-repo failures now surface as a typed RepositoryHealth (Stale/Unreadable) and a specific WorkingCopyUnavailableException instead of an uncaught VcsException; a one-click 'Update Stale Workspace' remedy runs jj workspace update-stale and re-runs the interrupted action. Also fixed the co-reported 58s EDT freeze in JujutsuFilePathIconProvider. Full workspace management (create/list/delete, workspace-scoped config) remains in jj-idea-vwxu/jj-idea-2ol.

title: Closing conflict-resolution window discards a side (GitHub #63)
description:
Opening 'Resolve Conflicts...' -> selecting a conflicted file opens IntelliJ's three-way merge
tool. Closing that window WITHOUT resolving (the x button, or resolving only some hunks)
silently marks the whole file resolved by discarding one side - the conflict vanishes from the
working copy. Reported on RustRover 2026.2 (GitHub #63).

Root cause: IntelliJ's merge tool uses the real file's Document as the editable output pane and
resets it to the base side at init (MergeConflictModel.setInitialOutputContent), erasing jj's
conflict markers. IntelliJ 2026.2 defaults to the iterative merge flow
(Registry vcs.merge.conflict.iterative.resolution=true), where cancel no longer restores
original content (MergeUtil.shouldRestoreOriginalContentOnCancel returns false when the request
has iterative data), and MultipleFileMergeDialog saves the document unconditionally. For jj,
the working file IS the conflict record (re-parsed from markers on every snapshot), unlike git
where the index is authoritative and the file is disposable scratch.

Fix: stop handing the real file to the platform as merge output. Drive resolution via
DiffManager.showMerge with a scratch output document (the HunkDiffPicker pattern already used
for jj split), writing back to the real file only on a non-cancel result.

See plan: /Users/kevin/.claude/plans/look-at-https-github-com-kkkev-jj-idea-i-starry-taco.md
acceptance_criteria: Closing the merge tool without resolving (or after only partial resolution) leaves the file's on-disk conflict markers and conflicted status unchanged. Accept Yours/Accept Theirs/Apply inside the tool still work and clear the conflict.
close_reason: Implemented: JujutsuConflictResolver drives the merge tool with a scratch output document; the three Resolve Conflicts actions now use it instead of AbstractVcsHelper.showMergeDialog. Unit tests cover cancel/accept-yours/accept-theirs/already-resolved/multi-file-stop-on-cancel. ./gradlew check passes. CHANGELOG.md and docs/manual-tests.md updated.

This is a real NoSuchMethodError/NoSuchFieldError crash risk at runtime on those IDE versions, not a false positive. Needs either an isPre253-style runtime guard/reflection fallback, or bumping sinceBuild past 253 if these APIs are load-bearing and no older equivalent exists.

title: Unit test task silently crashed at JVM bootstrap on 2025.3+ (253+) platforms
description: Discovered while landing jj-idea-qa8i and jj-idea-vll4/m2wr on top of the jj-idea-gu9q groundwork: the plain 'test' Gradle task was crashing at JUnit5-launcher-session startup on 2025.3+ (253+) platforms (default is now 2026.2), before any test class ever ran. This was masked in every earlier ./gradlew check run this session because Gradle stopped at an earlier task failure (platformTest) before ever reaching :test, so 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL' was never actually validating unit tests against 2026.2 — including on the already-pushed gu9q groundwork commit. Three compounding root causes, all fixed in the same commit that lands qa8i/vll4/m2wr: (1) IJPGP's testFramework(JUnit5) declaration unconditionally adds a JDK25-compiled test-framework-junit5 jar to the test classpath, whose registered LauncherSessionListener the launcher eagerly loads regardless of tag filtering; (2) real platform classes 2026.2 unit tests legitimately reference (e.g. com.intellij.openapi.vcs.FilePath) are themselves JDK25-compiled, so the unit test task's launcher needed the same JDK21/JDK25 platform-version-conditional split already used for platformTest; (3) mockk 1.13.9's bundled ByteBuddy couldn't generate working proxies for JDK25-compiled classes, silently falling through to real (unmocked) implementations and throwing @NotNull/NPE errors instead of returning stubbed values — bumped to 1.14.11.
acceptance_criteria: ./gradlew check passes (including the plain 'test' task, not just platformTest) on both platformVersion=2026.2 and 2025.2.
close_reason: Fixed in the same commit landing jj-idea-qa8i and jj-idea-vll4/jj-idea-m2wr: excluded test-framework-junit5 from the unit test classpath, matched platformTest's JDK21/JDK25 conditional launcher selection, bumped mockk 1.13.9 -> 1.14.11. Verified ./gradlew check green on both 2026.2 and 2025.2.

title: Redesign Split dialog hunk picker as 2-pane accept-arrow diff
description:
The 3-way merge widget used for "Pick Hunks..." in the Split dialog is a metaphor mismatch:
it's built for merging two divergent branches, but we're using it to partition one linear
diff into two pieces (parent-remainder / child). This causes real confusion:

1. Reversed picking: depending on file tick state, live/clickable hunks appear on different
   sides, so "accept" sometimes means keep, sometimes means send away.
2. "Both changes show against the child" - not a bug (jj split's child always ends up with
   the source commit's full content by construction) but never explained by the UI.
3. Partial pick force-ticks the file (confirmed bug in onPickHunks()).
4. No persistence: reopening the picker always resets, discarding a prior partial selection
   (confirmed bug).

Redesign: replace the 3-way merge with a plain 2-content diff embedded via DiffRequestPanel
(same mechanism SplitDialog already uses for its own read-only preview) - editable "Parent"
pane + fixed read-only "Child" pane (always afterContent). Accept-arrows then always pull a
hunk from Child into Parent, same direction regardless of tick state. Fixes persistence
(seed from firstCommitOverrides) and the force-tick bug (don't call ensureFileIncluded for
genuinely-partial results) as part of the same change.

Related: jj-idea-twis (original tick/child regression fix, closed), jj-idea-v527 (subprocess
classpath crash, still open).

Full design in /Users/kevin/.claude/plans/fix-jj-idea-twis-zesty-clover.md (this session's plan file).
acceptance_criteria: Pick Hunks opens a 2-pane diff (editable Parent, read-only Child); accepting a hunk always pulls it from Child into Parent regardless of tick state; a partial pick does not force the file's tick; reopening the picker after a partial pick resumes the prior selection; ./gradlew check passes; docs/manual-tests.md updated.
notes: Second iteration: the initial 2-pane accept-arrow design (editable Parent + fixed read-only Child) had two real flaws reported by the user: (1) an unticked file showed an empty, unusable diff since Parent's starting content equalled the fixed Child reference exactly; (2) a ticked file's picks were one-directional with no way to reverse a hunk once accepted. Fixed by reverting to a 3-way merge widget but with FIXED left/right roles (Before / Child, never tick-dependent) instead of the earlier tick-flipped 'live side' — confirmed via platform source that both sides' accept actions are always simultaneously available per hunk, giving true bidirectional reversibility.
close_reason: Replaced 3-way merge picker with a 2-pane accept-arrow diff (editable Parent, fixed read-only Child); fixed force-tick and persistence bugs; shared title-mapping helper used by both the picker and main preview

title: HunkApplyMain subprocess crashes with NoClassDefFoundError: kotlin/jvm/internal/Intrinsics
description:
Splitting with individual hunks picked (via "Pick Hunks..." in the Split dialog) fails with:

  Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: kotlin/jvm/internal/Intrinsics
  at in.kkkev.jjidea.diffedit.HunkApplyMain.main(HunkApplyMain.kt)
  Error: Failed to edit diff
  Caused by: Tool exited with exit status: 1

Root cause: DiffEditTool.discoverClasspath() computed the -cp for the standalone
HunkApplyMain subprocess by reading UrlClassLoader.getFiles() on this plugin's own
PluginClassLoader. Under a real installed plugin, that only returns the plugin's own
jar(s), not kotlin-stdlib, which the subprocess also needs.

Fix applied: discoverClasspath() now unions classloader files from both DiffEditTool's
own class AND kotlin.jvm.internal.Intrinsics's own class, which should track wherever
the live JVM actually resolves kotlin-stdlib from, regardless of mechanism.

Open question (not yet resolved): investigation found the plugin's own distribution
zip does not bundle kotlin-stdlib at all (kotlin.stdlib.default.dependency=false,
set in 4c825e0d / jj-idea-ar7t / GitHub #41, on the premise the platform provides it).
Exhaustive search of a real installed IntelliJ IDEA CE 2025.2 found kotlin-stdlib
classes only inside the bundled Kotlin plugin's private compiler toolchain, not
generally reachable. How the plugin's own in-process Kotlin code resolves Intrinsics
normally is unconfirmed. User chose to ship the classloader-introspection fix first
and verify against a real rebuild before considering reverting kotlin.stdlib.default.dependency.
acceptance_criteria: Split with hunk-level picking completes without NoClassDefFoundError on a real (non-sandbox) plugin install.
close_reason: Verified via clean ./gradlew runIde: split a change with a partial hunk selection (some hunks to parent, some to child) via Pick Hunks -> Apply -> Split, completed successfully with no NoClassDefFoundError. Confirms discoverClasspath()'s union of DiffEditTool's and kotlin.jvm.internal.Intrinsics's own classloader files correctly resolves kotlin-stdlib under a real PluginClassLoader.

title: Decide fate of standard Commit tool window for jj repos (hide vs. keep partial)
description: GitHub #56 follow-up. The plugin disables the platform Commit dialog's actual commit step (JujutsuVcs.isCommitActionDisabled=true, JujutsuCheckinEnvironment.commit() always errors) but otherwise leaves the standard Commit/Local Changes tool window active with IntelliJ's generic action set (including the still-broken Rollback, jj-idea-ad5d). A reporter on #56 found having both the Commit panel and the plugin's own Working Copy panel — which look similar but only the latter is jj-aware (Restore/Split/Squash/Resolve wired to real jj commands, Describe/New Change workflow) — confusing, since they didn't realize Working Copy existed and instead used the half-functional Commit panel. Need to decide: hide/suppress the Commit tool window for jj-only projects (simplest, but complicated by mixed-VCS projects where a Git root should keep its own Commit panel — see JujutsuVcs.allowsNestedRoots and multi-root handling), or otherwise merge/limit it so it doesn't offer broken or misleading actions.
design: Must account for multi-VCS-root projects (jj + Git) where hiding the Commit window globally would break Git workflows; likely needs per-root or per-VCS-type suppression rather than a global toggle.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is made and implemented: either the Commit tool window is hidden/suppressed for jj-only projects (with Git-root projects unaffected), or its action set for jj files is curtailed so it no longer exposes non-functional actions like Rollback.
close_reason: Implemented: JujutsuVcs.getForcedCommitMode() hides the standard Commit tool window + Local Changes tab for jj-only projects, gated by a new settings toggle (default on). Mixed jj+Git projects unaffected. Fast-follow jj-idea-jqpe bumped to P2.

The Resolve actions call AbstractVcsHelper.showMergeDialog(files, JujutsuMergeProvider) (actions/file/ResolveConflictsAction.kt:30, ResolveSelectedConflictsAction.kt:28, actions/change/resolveConflictsAction.kt:55) backed by MergeProvider2/MergeSessionEx (vcs/merge/JujutsuMergeProvider.kt).
