Consider a CI matrix build against 262.
acceptance_criteria: Resolve opens the merge window on IDEA/RustRover 2026.2; root-cause API change identified and adapted; ideally a build/smoke against 262 added.
close_reason: Fixed: JujutsuMergeSession now returns 2 merge-info columns (Yours/Theirs), matching Git4Idea, so 2026.2's iterative merge dialog no longer throws IndexOutOfBoundsException on an empty column list.

title: 'Split into New Child' puts selected files in parent instead of child (regression)
description: GitHub #54. Regression from the split-dialog redesign (commit 1444ca2b1, jj-idea-jtpb). Right-clicking files and choosing 'Split into New Child' now keeps the selected files in the PARENT and moves the unselected files to the child — the opposite of Squash and of the pre-redesign behaviour. Root cause: SplitFilesAction passes right-clicked files as preSelectedFiles; SplitDialog seeds them as 'included' (ui/split/SplitDialog.kt:169-174) and doOKAction passes filePaths = includedPaths to jj split (:623-660), but 'jj split <paths>' keeps those paths in the first commit = parent. The old dual-tree dialog passed the complement (parent files), so selected files went to the child. Fix: invert the pre-selection/inclusion mapping so selected files land in the child. Also realign the now-inverted validation strings (SplitDialog.kt:598-618) and update SplitDialogTest first-commit assertion (:139-148). Add a regression test asserting selected files go to the child.
acceptance_criteria: Right-click file(s) -> Split into New Child moves the selected files into the new child commit and leaves the rest in the parent; validation messages match; regression test added.
close_reason: Inverted the Split dialog checkbox model: ticking a file now moves it to the child; nothing ticked by default; child description shown first; hunk picker follows suit

title: Annotate on merge fails with 'No such path' when file missing from one parent
description:
Annotating a merge commit (e.g. a criss-cross merge, per the jj-stress-test repo's criss_merge_1.txt scenario) failed with 'Error: No such path: <file>' whenever the file didn't exist at one of the merge's real parents (e.g. added on only one side of history). Both the MergeAnnotationReconciler path (annotateMerge) and its arbitrary-first-parent fallback (beforeRevisionFor) queried a parent lacking the file and threw, since the per-parent annotate calls were not resilient to individual failures.

Fix: JujutsuAnnotationProvider.annotateMerge now uses mapNotNull with per-parent try/catch (annotationLinesOrNull) instead of a plain .map, so a parent missing the file is skipped rather than aborting the whole reconciliation. Only returns null (triggering full fallback) if literally every parent fails to annotate.
acceptance_criteria: Annotating a merge commit where the file exists in only some parents succeeds, using blame from whichever parents do have the file.
close_reason: Fixed: JujutsuAnnotationProvider.annotateMerge now uses mapNotNull with per-parent try/catch (new annotationLinesOrNull helper) instead of a plain .map over parentIds, so a parent lacking the file (e.g. added on only one side of a criss-cross merge) is skipped rather than aborting the whole reconciliation with 'No such path'. Only falls back to null (first-parent fallback) if every parent fails. Covered by two new tests in JujutsuAnnotationProviderMergeTest: one confirming resilience when one parent is missing the file, one confirming the full fallback still triggers when every parent fails.

title: Annotate on merge commits shows line-count-mismatch warning
description:
Annotating a file whose working copy (or ancestor) is a merge commit with resolved conflicts triggers IntelliJ's platform warning: 'Number of lines annotated by Jujutsu is not equal to number of lines in the file. Check file encoding and line separators.'

Root cause: JujutsuAnnotationProvider.annotate(file) annotates a file's PARENT revision (not its own), relying on UpToDateLineNumberProvider to diff that against the live editor content. For a merge, the crash-fix fallback (beforeRevisionFor) uses an arbitrary first parent, which can differ hugely in line count from the real resolved file (which combines both parents plus conflict-resolution edits), tripping AnnotateWarningsService's abs(expected-actual)>1 check.

Fix: annotate every real parent, reconstruct jj's actual auto-merged tree (reusing JujutsuRepository.MergeParentContentRevision's reverse-diff logic from jj-idea-ayk7/pz4l), and align each parent's per-line blame against that reconstructed tree via com.intellij.util.diff.Diff. Unattributed lines (jj's conflict markers) are attributed to the merge commit itself. New MergeAnnotationReconciler (pure function, no mocking needed for tests). See full design in the approved plan from this session.
acceptance_criteria: Annotating a real two-parent merge with a resolved conflict shows no line-count-mismatch warning, and blame correctly attributes inherited lines to their original parent with conflict-resolution lines attributed to the merge commit.
close_reason: Implemented MergeAnnotationReconciler: annotates every real parent of a merge commit, reconstructs jj's auto-merged tree (reusing the existing reverse-diff logic from ayk7/pz4l, extracted into JujutsuRepository.reconstructMergeParentContent), and aligns each parent's blame against it via com.intellij.util.diff.Diff. Unattributed lines (conflict markers / resolution edits) are attributed to the merge commit itself. This matches LineStatusTracker's existing base for merges (pz4l), so line counts now agree and the platform warning no longer fires. Falls back to the prior arbitrary-first-parent behavior (beforeRevisionFor) if reconstruction or a parent annotate call fails. Covered by MergeAnnotationReconcilerTest (pure) and JujutsuAnnotationProviderMergeTest (platform test, incl. an operation-count test asserting exactly P annotate calls per P-parent merge).

title: Push button unresponsive when repo selected + default 'tracking bookmarks' scope
description:
User report: in the Git Push dialog, after selecting a repo (multi-repo project) and leaving the 'Tracking bookmarks (default)' scope radio selected, clicking Push produces no visible effect - no push, no error, no notification.

Reported alongside a second, confirmed-and-fixed bug (jj-idea-dt2k follow-up): the untracked-bookmark confirmation dialog showed a literal unsubstituted '{0}' due to an unescaped apostrophe breaking java.text.MessageFormat (fixed by rewording 'don't' -> 'do not' in action.git.push.untracked.message).

Investigation so far (could not reproduce interactively - no GUI automation available in this environment):
- GitPushDialog.kt (the dialog itself, OK button/doOKAction) is untouched by the recent push-flow changes: ruled out as the direct cause of a non-responding OK button per se.
- For default scope (spec.bookmark = null), the dry-run 'jj git push' command arguments are byte-identical before and after the recent allowNew removal (bookmark=null always bypassed the old allowNew logic too), so the dry-run call itself isn't a new risk.
- IF the current revision has an untracked/new bookmark, default scope now goes through the new checkAndPush -> parseRefusedNewBookmarks -> confirmUntrackedPush -> trackAndPush path (gitRemoteActions.kt). This is new code as of the --allow-new removal work. It's possible (not confirmed) this interacts with the bug#1 MessageFormat issue in a way that produced a non-rendering dialog before the fix, rather than just a garbled one - the fix might resolve this too.
- CommandExecutor.CommandResult.tellUser uses a modal Messages.showErrorDialog, so a normal dry-run/push failure would NOT be silent - this rules out plain CLI errors as the explanation.
- Found a real, pre-existing architectural risk that could fully explain 'silent no response': util/Tasks.kt's runInBackground wraps work in ApplicationManager.executeOnPooledThread<T>, returning a Future<T> that no caller ever calls .get() on. Any exception thrown inside a runInBackground block anywhere in the codebase is completely swallowed - no log entry, no user-visible sign. See jj-idea (new bead) for making this visible.

Next steps: ask reporter to retest after the MessageFormat fix lands (jj-idea-dt2k follow-up), and if it persists, get: (1) whether the working-copy revision has any bookmarks at all, (2) how many git remotes are configured, (3) an idea.log excerpt from around the time of the failed click.
acceptance_criteria: Push with default scope selected either succeeds, or shows a visible error/dialog to the user, in all repo/bookmark configurations.
close_reason: Root cause fixed: runInBackground now logs uncaught throwables instead of swallowing them silently via an unconsumed Future

title: Push fails on jj >= 0.42: --allow-new flag removed
description: jj 0.42.0 removed the --allow-new flag from 'jj git push' (deprecated since 0.36 in favour of auto-tracked bookmarks). The plugin's resolveAllowNew (actions/git/gitRemoteActions.kt) still unconditionally emits --allow-new for untracked/new bookmark pushes, so Push from the Jujutsu Log view fails on jj >= 0.42 (reported in GitHub issue #53 by atty303, jj 0.43.0). Fix must be version-gated since jj 0.37-0.41 still require/accept the flag (plugin minimum supported version is 0.37.0).
acceptance_criteria: resolveAllowNew never emits --allow-new when detected jj version >= 0.42.0; still emits it (when needed) on jj < 0.42.0; unit tests cover both branches; gh issue #53 verified fixed against a real jj >= 0.42 binary.
notes: Final approach differs from initial close reason: instead of version-gating --allow-new, the fix removes --allow-new entirely (dropped from CommandExecutor.gitPush/gitPushArgs). When jj refuses to create a new remote bookmark ('Refusing to create new remote bookmark X@Y', both the Error/exit-1 form for a specific bookmark and the Warning/exit-0 form for the default push scope), the plugin now parses the bookmark+remote from stderr, tracks it via 'jj bookmark track', then retries the push with no flag. Verified to work identically on jj 0.37 through 0.43 (no version check needed) via manual testing against real binaries. Bonus fix: the default push scope previously silently dropped new bookmarks with no feedback (Warning + exit 0 wasn't detected); now it's caught and offered for confirmation same as the specific-bookmark case.
close_reason: Fixed: resolveAllowNew is now version-gated on jj >= 0.42.0 (JjVersion.ALLOW_NEW_REMOVED). Verified against a real jj 0.43.0 binary: --allow-new reproduces the #53 error, while the new no-flag path succeeds and auto-tracks the bookmark.

title: Multi-repo log merge conflated repos' commits sharing a change id (root commit collision)
description:
Follow-up to jj-idea-6fxz: that fix addressed the single-repo cold-cache path, but the user
reported the bug persisting in a multi-repo project (jj-test), with no discernible
per-repo pattern.

Root cause: UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.topologicalSort merges ALL repos' entries into one
flat list and keys its entryById/childCount maps by bare ChangeId. jj's root commit has the
IDENTICAL change id ("zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz") in every repository, since it's
synthetic rather than content-derived (verified directly: `jj log -r 'root()' -T change_id`
in two freshly-initialized repos returns the same id). So different repos' root commits (and
in principle any other colliding id) collide in that map, corrupting the Kahn's-algorithm
child-count computation - silently breaking the sort for whichever repo's root loses the
collision, depending on flatten()/map-iteration order. That explains "no discernible
pattern": which repo is affected is nondeterministic across runs.

The codebase already has ChangeKey(repo, revision) for exactly this class of bug (per
contributing.md: "Selection matching requires both repo and revision to avoid cross-repo
collisions") - topologicalSort just never got that treatment.

Fix: keyed entryByKey/childCount in topologicalSort by ChangeKey(entry.repo, entry.id)
instead of bare ChangeId.

Files: src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/log/UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt (fix),
src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/log/TopologicalSortTest.kt (regression tests -
verified they fail without the fix and pass with it).
acceptance_criteria: topologicalSort keeps different repos' commits independent even when they share a change id (e.g. the root commit). Multi-repo projects show every repo's commits in correct order in both the main log window and dialog pickers, regardless of load order.
close_reason: Keyed topologicalSort's maps by ChangeKey(repo, id) instead of bare ChangeId; added regression tests

title: logCache.all returned unsorted entries on cold fetch (immutable root shown first)
description:
Reported by user: opening the Duplicate Onto... dialog in a repo with just a couple of
commits showed the immutable root commit FIRST in the destination picker, ahead of the
mutable commit — the reverse of the main log window's order (newest-first, root at
bottom).

Root cause: UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.loadCommits() explicitly topologically sorts
(children before parents, newest-first) before storing into repo.logCache — that's what
makes the main log window's order correct. But RepoLogCache.fetch() (LogCache.kt, used by
the logCache.all/get/loadContext cold-cache path) stored the RAW jj log CLI output with no
sort step. So logCache.all only "looked" sorted by accident, when the main log window had
already warmed the cache for that repo first. Any dialog that calls logCache.all before the
log window has loaded that repo (RebaseDialog, SquashIntoDialog, MoveBookmarkToChangeDialog,
DuplicateDialog, etc.) could see unsorted output — likely also breaking CommitGraphBuilder's
line rendering, since topologicalSort's docstring says the builder requires children-before-
parents input.

Fix: RepoLogCache.fetch() now runs the same topologicalSort (reused from
UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt, internal/module-visible) before storing/returning, so
logCache.all is guaranteed sorted regardless of whether the cache was warm or cold.

Files: src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/jj/LogCache.kt (fix),
src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/jj/RepoLogCacheTest.kt (regression test - verified it fails
without the fix and passes with it).
acceptance_criteria: logCache.all/get/loadContext returns topologically sorted (children-before-parents) entries even on a cold fetch with no prior main-log-window load. Covered by a unit test that reproduces the reported bug.
close_reason: Fixed in RepoLogCache.fetch() by applying the same topologicalSort the main log window already used; added regression test

title: Plugin throws 'Not a Jujutsu revision' on foreign-VCS changes (GitHub #50)
description:
GitHub issue #50 (https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/50): the plugin throws exceptions when the user works in a non-jj repo (reporter hit it in a Piper repo). Sample:

  com.intellij.openapi.vcs.VcsException: Not a Jujutsu revision: PiperContentRevision
    at VcsExtensionsKt.getLocator(VcsExtensions.kt:112)
    at FileAtVersionKt.getFileAtVersion(FileAtVersion.kt:18)
    at FileChange$Companion.from(FileChange.kt:92)
    at ActionEventExtensionsKt.getChanges(ActionEventExtensions.kt:84)
    at OpenChangeFileAction.update(OpenChangeFileAction.kt:53)

Root cause: AnActionEvent.changes (ActionEventExtensions.kt:79-84) eagerly maps EVERY selected Change (VcsDataKeys.SELECTED_CHANGES/CHANGES, a VCS-agnostic aggregate) through FileChange.from, which calls ContentRevision.locator (VcsExtensions.kt:106-114). That throws for any non-jj revision (Piper here; Git in colocated repos). Amplified because Jujutsu.OpenChangeFile carries a global $default F4 keyboard shortcut (plugin.xml:225-227), so its update() is evaluated by the platform even in pure non-jj contexts -> 'multiple exceptions'.
design:
Same bug CLASS as jj-idea-t0zo (closed, shipped v0.7.13, commit 78fbbd012, one day before #50 was filed). t0zo added Iterable<Change>.filterInJujutsuRepo(project) (VcsExtensions.kt:64) and applied it to the Working Copy panel + 3 resolve-conflict actions, but did NOT touch the shared action-event 'changes' extension, leaving ~10 filechange/file actions exposed. This bead closes that surface gap.

Fix: in AnActionEvent.changes (ActionEventExtensions.kt:79), filter the raw Change list through filterInJujutsuRepo(project) BEFORE .map { FileChange.from(it) }; return emptyList() when project is null. filterInJujutsuRepo resolves via change.filePath -> possibleJujutsuRepositoryFor and never touches .locator, so it is safe on foreign changes. The single fix covers filePaths/restorePaths and all downstream filechange actions since they funnel through this getter. Optional defense-in-depth: make .locator (VcsExtensions.kt:112) degrade instead of throw.

Tests: extend ActionEventExtensionsTest.kt (already touched by t0zo) to assert a mixed selection containing a non-JujutsuRevisionNumber Change is dropped and does not throw.
notes:
Reuse existing helper Iterable<Change>.filterInJujutsuRepo(project) at VcsExtensions.kt:64. Related: jj-idea-t0zo (closed). Manual repro: colocated jj+Git4Idea or any non-jj VCS project -> select a foreign change in the Changes view, press F4 / open context menu -> currently logs VcsException: Not a Jujutsu revision.

REGRESSION INTRODUCED IN v0.6.7 (2026-05-12), commit 8644ef638 (jj-idea-76uo, 'Jujutsu submenu for historical versions'). That commit changed AnActionEvent.changes from returning raw List<Change> to List<FileChange> by eagerly mapping every selected change through FileChange.from -> .locator, which throws on foreign revisions. Before v0.6.7 this path returned raw Change objects and never touched .locator, so update() did not crash on non-jj changes. The .locator throw and OpenChangeFileAction's global F4 shortcut both predate v0.6.7 but were only wired into the action-update path by this commit.
close_reason: Fixed: added ContentRevision.isJujutsuRevision / Change.isJujutsuChange (VcsExtensions.kt) and filtered AnActionEvent.changes on it before FileChange.from, so foreign-VCS changes are dropped instead of throwing. Closes the action-event surface left by jj-idea-t0zo.

title: Fix flaky CI: LeakHunter retained-Project failure in platformTest
description: CI failed on master commit ff8e4898 with a JUnit executionError / AssertionError at LeakHunter.java:109 during platformTest teardown. The exact same commit passed on a later workflow_dispatch run 15s after failing on push, and it passes locally on repeated runs -- confirming this is a flaky GC-timing leak-detection false positive, not a real regression. Root cause: JujutsuStateModel.init fires fire-and-forget pooled-thread invalidate() loaders (Messaging.kt / Tasks.kt runInBackground) that capture the platform test's fixture project; the affected tests (JujutsuStateModelPlatformTest, UnifiedWorkingCopyPanelScaleTest) only drain the EDT, not the pooled threads, so a loader can still be in flight when projectFixture disposes the project. Fix: make CI resilient by retrying the platformTest task and uploading test reports on failure, and reduce recurrence by draining background loaders before teardown in the affected tests.
acceptance_criteria: CI workflow retries platformTest on failure and uploads test reports; JujutsuStateModelPlatformTest and UnifiedWorkingCopyPanelScaleTest drain background loaders in @AfterEach before fixture teardown; ./gradlew check passes locally.
close_reason: CI hardened: platformTest retried 3x with test-report upload on failure; JujutsuStateModelPlatformTest and UnifiedWorkingCopyPanelScaleTest drain pooled-thread loaders in @AfterEach before fixture teardown to reduce LeakHunter flake recurrence. Verified ./gradlew check green locally, platformTest stable across 3 reruns.

title: Crash on tooltip when workspace path contains spaces
description:
GitHub #39: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/39
URISyntaxException 'Illegal character in path' from TextCanvas.append (TextCanvas.kt:124) building a jjc:// URI for a path like '.../untitled untitled'. The path segment isn't encoded. Fix: percent-encode the path when constructing the URI. Affects any repo whose path contains spaces.
close_reason: Percent-encode repo path in jjc:// and jjref:// link URIs (URLUtil.encodePath/unescapePercentSequences), matching the fix the reporter suggested in GitHub #39. Added regression tests.

title: Reprioritise backlog to win market share (protect rating > UX depth > defer scale)
description:
Re-triage the ~50 open issues against one rule: protect the 4.63 rating first, win share via jj-specific UX depth second, defer speculative large-repo perf. Rationale: the market (jj on JetBrains) is small but growing; being the best-rated, deepest reference implementation both wins share vs Selvejj and hedges against JetBrains shipping official jj support (IJPL-174543 — 'To be discussed', Normal priority, not roadmapped).

Apply via bd update --priority.

Tier 1 -> P1 (protect rating: correctness / broken core workflows):
 sm1s (cannot resolve inherited conflict), gpf5 (octopus merge wrong diff), 1ojh (graph tree-line corruption), spyi (annotate broken for merges), t0zo (WC window shows Git changes), 7jkr (graph layout not recomputed on filter), x283 (modify/delete conflict support). Also keep ignored-file-scan HANG fixes high (0xqp, ixju, 2570.3) — hardening, not speculative.

Tier 2 -> keep P2 (win share, jj UX depth): finish in-flight hunk-split/squash (epic 5isf, 4q7m — code already uncommitted in working tree), g05l (multi-parent merge support), uuy9 (squash preview), 10fo (issue links), lo7u (compare action), 3as8 (scaled-icon polish).

Tier 3 -> P3/P4 or park (defer/on-demand): speculative scale infra edjs.4/.5/.6 (keep only cheap PR-blocking regression guard edjs.2), extreme-scale perf a0wp/ix4v, internal refactors emff/flb0/ulg3/lrfn, bookmark icon polish fyxb/i6oz/rskx/kcgf/zhyy, test housekeeping j0hs/pcp8/2poe. Build heavy perf ONLY when a named large-repo user reports it.

Also: open a follow-up to capture reporter context (repo size, personal vs commercial) on large-repo bug reports — the signal that would later justify a commercial tier. Ask on existing open GitHub large-repo issues and/or add to the bug-report path.
acceptance_criteria: bd list --status=open reflects the new tier priorities; a reporter-context follow-up issue exists; no code/test regressions (metadata-only re-triage).
close_reason: Backlog re-triaged into tiers; reporter-context follow-up created (jj-idea-b2ny)

title: split: excluded files deleted instead of deferred to second commit
description: When using hunk-level split with firstCommitOverrides, HunkApplyMain's mirrorTree deletes any file absent from the staging dir. But $right starts as the full revision tree; excluded files should be restored from $left (the parent tree) so the first commit leaves them unchanged and the change lands in the second commit. Only files added in the revision (not present in $left) should be removed from $right.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix hunk-apply diff-editor launch: empty classpath + wrong main-class name
description: jj split --tool fails with ClassNotFoundException when Split is pressed. Three bugs in DiffEditTool classpath wiring: (1) discoverClasspath() returns '' because PluginClassLoader returns null for codeSource.location; (2) kotlin-stdlib missing from -cp (HunkApplyMain.kt uses kotlin.io.path.* etc.); (3) top-level fun main compiles to HunkApplyMainKt not HunkApplyMain. Fix: resource-URL classpath discovery (glob all *.jar in plugin lib/ dir), @file:JvmName on HunkApplyMain.kt.

title: Drop internal FilePathHolder API: report ignored files via ChangeProvider
description: Marketplace verifier rejects the plugin for using @ApiStatus.Internal FilePathHolder, which is an unavoidable transitive dependency of implementing VcsManagedFilesHolder. Fix: remove JujutsuVcsIgnoredFilesHolder (the sole FilePathHolder implementor), keep the async JujutsuIgnoredFilesService engine, and report ignored files via ChangelistBuilder.processIgnoredFile() in JujutsuChangeProvider. Add an IGNORE_REPORT_CAP to guard the new O(n) reporting step for large repos that scan fast but produce huge ignored sets.
close_reason: Removed JujutsuVcsIgnoredFilesHolder (the FilePathHolder implementor), moved ignored-file reporting into JujutsuChangeProvider.reportIgnoredFiles with IGNORE_REPORT_CAP guard. 5 scale tests added.

title: Ignore-scan watchdog never fires on flat/large directories
description: GitHub issue #35 (SergejSalnikov): the 5s ignore-scan watchdog is the checkCanceled closure passed into GitignoreCache.collectIgnored, but it is only called once per directory entered (GitignoreCache.kt:72 inside recurse()), never inside the per-child loop and never during File.listFiles(). A flat directory with millions of files (or a slow listFiles() call) blocks past 5s without the watchdog ever checking the clock, so the 'scan is slow, disable?' notification (JujutsuNotifications.notifyIgnoreScanSlow) never appears and the IDE hangs. Even when the watchdog does fire today, it only logs+notifies (JujutsuIgnoredFilesService.kt:167-180) — it never aborts the in-progress scan, so a huge repo still runs to completion regardless.
design: 1) In GitignoreCache.collectIgnored (lines 64-88), call checkCanceled() inside the per-child loop on a throttle gated on the existing 'visited' counter, e.g. 'if (visited % CHECK_INTERVAL == 0L) checkCanceled()', in addition to the existing entry-time check at line 72. This bounds work between checks to O(CHECK_INTERVAL) entries regardless of tree shape (flat or deep), so a flat million-file directory still trips the watchdog. Update the KDoc at lines 56-62 (currently states checkCanceled is 'called once per directory entered'). 2) Make the watchdog ABORT: in JujutsuIgnoredFilesService.kt's checkCanceled closure (lines 167-180), after calling JujutsuNotifications.notifyIgnoreScanSlow, throw com.intellij.openapi.progress.ProcessCanceledException (idiomatic platform cancellation) instead of just logging. 3) In scan() (JujutsuIgnoredFilesService.kt:164-188), catch ProcessCanceledException around the collectIgnored call so an aborted full scan leaves the repo's ignored set empty (RecursiveFilePathSet) and degrades gracefully without propagating an error — the notification already invites the user to disable scanning permanently for that repo (or globally, see jj-idea companion issue for the global toggle).
acceptance_criteria: - collectIgnored calls checkCanceled at least every CHECK_INTERVAL visited entries even within a single flat directory of many children (not just once per directory). - When checkCanceled throws (watchdog tripped), collectIgnored's walk stops partway (visited count < total entries) rather than running to completion. - scan() catches the thrown cancellation, leaves state.ignored empty, does not crash or propagate the exception, and the slow-scan notification still fires exactly once per repo per session. - Ship an operation-count test per CLAUDE.md scale rules: feed collectIgnored an in-memory IgnoreScanNode (see GitignoreScanTest.kt/GitignoreCacheTest.kt for the test pattern) with one directory containing many flat children and a counting checkCanceled; assert it is called >= floor(children / CHECK_INTERVAL) times, and that throwing from it aborts the walk before all children are visited.
close_reason: Watchdog now throttled inside the per-child loop and aborts the scan on trip; op-count tests added in GitignoreScanTest.kt

title: Read-access error: AnActionEvent data accessed on background thread in diff/file actions (GitHub #38)
description:
IntelliJ logs a RuntimeExceptionWithAttachments when showing diff from the History view (and from several related file actions). The diff still appears, but the error pollutes the log and can cause subtle failures on newer platform builds where the assertion becomes a hard throw.

Root cause: five actions read AnActionEvent data extensions (e.changes, e.files, e.file, e.jujutsuFiles) inside a runInBackground block (pooled thread). Accessing VIRTUAL_FILE_ARRAY lazily triggers PsiFileRule → FileManagerImpl.findFile, which requires a read action. The platform throws without one.

Affected actions:
- actions/filechange/ShowDiffAction.kt — e.changes, e.files (reported in #38)
- actions/filechange/CompareWithLocalAction.kt — e.changes, e.file
- actions/filechange/CompareBeforeWithLocalAction.kt — e.changes, e.file
- actions/filechange/OpenChangeFileAction.kt — e.files
- actions/file/CompareFileWithBranchAction.kt — e.jujutsuFiles

Fix: capture all AnActionEvent data reads as EDT-side locals in actionPerformed before entering runInBackground, then reference those locals inside the background block. This is the pattern already used correctly in ShowDiffInNewTabAction, SplitFilesAction, SquashFilesAction, and SquashIntoFilesAction.
design:
AnActionEvent.getData() for keys backed by PsiFileRule / VirtualFileArrayRule invokes FileManagerImpl.findFile, which calls ThreadingAssertions.softAssertReadAccess. That assertion throws RuntimeExceptionWithAttachments on any thread without a read action. The EDT always runs under an implicit read access; pooled threads do not.

The fix is purely mechanical: hoist AnActionEvent data reads to the EDT (top of actionPerformed), before runInBackground. No architectural change — just reorder 1-3 lines per action.

Stack trace from #38:
  FileManagerImpl.findFile (requires read action)
  PsiFileRule.getData
  VirtualFileArrayRule.getData
  PreCachedDataContext.getDataInner
  AnActionEvent.getData
  ActionEventExtensionsKt.getFiles (ActionEventExtensions.kt:27)
  ShowDiffAction.actionPerformed$lambda$2 (ShowDiffAction.kt:40)
  TasksKt.runInBackground$lambda$2 (Tasks.kt:28)
close_reason: Fixed in all 5 affected actions by hoisting AnActionEvent data reads to the EDT (before runInBackground). BUILD SUCCESSFUL, all tests pass.

title: Runtime escape hatches: ignore-scan watchdog + setting to disable scanning
description:
Safety net for scale cases the guardrails miss:
1. Watchdog: time-box the ignore scan; if it exceeds a budget (e.g. 5s), log WARN with the instrumentation counters (jj-idea-edjs.1) and show a one-time notification suggesting the user file an issue (with the counter stats to paste) — turning silent multi-minute hangs like GitHub #35 into actionable reports.
2. Setting (Settings > Version Control > Jujutsu): disable ignored-file scanning entirely, so affected users have an immediate workaround without waiting for a release. Follows the three-tier settings model — likely a project-tier default with per-repo override (RepositoryConfig nullable field).

Uses JujutsuNotifications for the balloon with action buttons per the error-handling philosophy (user-error UX, not silent failure).
acceptance_criteria: Scan exceeding budget logs WARN with counts and notifies once per session with a 'report issue' action. Setting exists, persists, and short-circuits the scan (and the async holder once jj-idea-2570.2 lands). Both covered by the manual smoke steps in the implementation summary.
close_reason: Implemented: per-repo 'disable ignored-file scanning' setting in RepositoryConfig + JujutsuSettings + JujutsuConfigurable (per-repo checkbox with persist/load/prune via isEmpty()); short-circuit in JujutsuChangeProvider.reportIgnoredFiles; mid-scan watchdog at 5s triggers JujutsuNotifications.notifyIgnoreScanSlow (once-per-session per repo) with Disable + Report Issue actions.

title: CLAUDE.md/contributing.md: Performance & Scale section (scale envelope, refresh-path rules, agent requirements)
description:
Add a 'Performance & Scale' section to CLAUDE.md (which doubles as agent instructions) and reference it from contributing.md.

Content:
1. Scale envelope the plugin must support: ~1M files, ~500k ignored files (node_modules-style trees), ~100k commits, ~1k-change working sets, multi-root projects.
2. Refresh-path rules:
   - Nothing O(repo-size) on the refresh path — only O(working-set).
   - Never traverse the file tree without pruning ignored/excluded directories.
   - Every loop over files/commits must be cancellable (checkCanceled per batch/directory).
   - Prefer delegating enumeration to jj/git CLI over reimplementing traversal in the JVM.
   - Listener callbacks (VFS, ChangeListListener) must do O(1)/debounced work.
3. Agent-directed requirement: any change adding a filesystem traversal or a per-file/per-commit loop must (a) state its complexity against the scale envelope in the implementation summary, and (b) ship with an operation-count test (see jj-idea-edjs.2 pattern). This makes scale analysis a deliverable, not a review afterthought.
4. PR checklist line: 'Does this change do work proportional to repo size? If yes, where is the scale test?'
acceptance_criteria: Section exists in CLAUDE.md, linked from contributing.md. Rules match what jj-idea-2570.1/.2 implement. Agent requirement phrased as an instruction, verified by a trial prompt producing the complexity statement.
close_reason: Performance & Scale section added to CLAUDE.md (scale envelope, refresh-path rules, non-colocation requirement, agent-directed complexity+test requirement, multi-dimension PR checklist question). Linked from contributing.md.

title: Perf instrumentation: timers + work counters on hot paths with WARN thresholds
description:
Extend the existing ad-hoc timing log (e.g. 'jj status took Xms' at JujutsuChangeProvider.kt:43) into a small reusable perf-logging helper wrapping the hot paths: getChanges total, ignore scan, log load/parse, graph layout, working-copy tree rebuild.

Log BOTH duration and work counts (entries visited, files matched, rows laid out). Counters are the point: 'ignore scan visited 1,843,201 entries in 41s' in idea.log would have made GitHub #35 self-diagnosing instead of requiring a contributor thread dump. Counts are hardware-independent red flags.

- INFO for normal operation; WARN above thresholds (e.g. >500ms or >50k entries) so it stands out in user-submitted logs.
- Zero/near-zero overhead when under threshold; no allocation-heavy formatting on the hot path.
- One helper, consistent format (operation, duration, counts, repo) so logs are greppable.
acceptance_criteria: Hot paths listed above emit duration+count log lines. Threshold breach logs WARN. Format documented in CLAUDE.md debugging section. No measurable overhead in normal-size repos.
close_reason: Implemented util/Perf.kt helper with measurePerf + PerfReport; wired 5 hot paths (getChanges, ignore-scan, log-load, graph-layout, wc-rebuild); GitignoreCache.collectIgnored now returns ScanStats(visited, ignored); tests added; CLAUDE.md + CHANGELOG.md updated.

title: Move ignored-file reporting to async VcsManagedFilesHolder (com.intellij.vcs.ignoredFilesHolder EP)
description:
Decouple ignored-file computation from JujutsuChangeProvider.getChanges so modified-file refresh latency is independent of repo size. This is how git4idea works: GitUntrackedFilesHolder + GitIgnoredFilesHolder registered at the com.intellij.vcs.ignoredFilesHolder extension point. Platform javadoc on VcsManagedFilesHolder: when registered, the ChangeProvider is no longer expected to report ignored files; the holder loads them autonomously and notifies via VcsManagedFilesHolder.TOPIC — the Commit toolwindow shows an updating state meanwhile (built-in perceived-speed mechanism).

Design (mirror git4idea/repo/GitUntrackedFilesHolder.kt in ../intellij-community):
- Per-repo holder with its own dirty-set (everything-dirty vs file list) — VcsDirtyScopeManager only serves ChangeProvider, so the holder tracks modifications itself (hook into existing JujutsuStateModel file-change events).
- Debounced background update (git uses 500ms SingleTaskRunner); publish VcsManagedFilesHolder.TOPIC and notifyUnchangedFileStatusChanged on completion.
- Store results in RecursiveFilePathSet; containsFile = hasAncestor, so top-most ignored dirs suffice.
- Remove reportIgnoredFiles from JujutsuChangeProvider; register holder Provider in plugin.xml.

Depends on the pruned walker from jj-idea-2570.1 — async does not excuse an O(repo) scan burning CPU on every save.
acceptance_criteria: JujutsuChangeProvider.getChanges no longer reports ignored files. Ignored status appears asynchronously with the platform updating indicator. Time-to-display for modified files after a save is independent of ignored-tree size. Incremental updates re-check only dirty paths.
close_reason: JujutsuIgnoredFilesService + JujutsuVcsIgnoredFilesHolder registered at com.intellij.vcs.ignoredFilesHolder EP. Ignored-file scan fully decoupled from ChangeProvider; JujutsuStateModel feeds markDirty/invalidate. Unlocks jj-idea-2570.3.

title: Change parser fails on parent<->child file move ({ => child} rename format)
description:
## Problem

GitHub issue #37: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/37

When a file is moved from a parent directory into a new child directory (or vice versa), jj emits a rename spec with an empty side, e.g.:

  src\components\pages\{ => blankExperience}\blankExperience.tsx

The change parser throws 'Invalid rename/copy format' and the entire change fails to load, so the affected revision shows no file changes in the IDE log.

## Root Cause

The rename/copy regex requires non-empty text on both sides of `=>`:

  ([^{)]*)\{([^}]+) => ([^}]+)}(.*)

`[^}]+` means one or more chars — empty left side doesn't match, so requireNotNull throws.

The identical regex exists in **two** places:
- CliLogService.kt:142 (the one producing the logged WARN; completely untested)
- JujutsuChangeProvider.kt:271

## Fix Direction

Change `[^}]+` → `[^}]*` for both before/after capture groups in both files. Add tests for the empty-side cases ({ => child} and {child => }). Consider deduplicating the two copies of this logic. Also check for secondary issue: Windows backslash path separators vs forward-slash expectations in getChildPath.
close_reason: Deduplicated rename/copy spec parsing into jj/FileSpec.kt#parseRenameSpec; fixed regex to allow empty-side moves; added joinPathParts to avoid double separators; added FileSpecTest and two integration tests in JujutsuChangeProviderTest

title: Revision selector hangs the EDT when searching (large repos)
description:
Reported on GitHub issue #34 by adam-talos as a follow-up after the v0.7.5 LogCache fix.

Symptom: typing in the revision selector search field (Compare with Commit / revision picker) freezes the UI on large repos. The AWT Event Thread is blocked for 5+ seconds.

Root cause per profiler trace from the reporter:
- RevisionChoicePanel.loadData (RevisionChoicePanel.kt:187) populates the list by calling DefaultListModel.addElement one item at a time on the EDT, each triggering a WideSelectionListUI re-layout.
- Re-layout calls WideSelectionListUI.getItemPreferredSize which builds a brand-new TextCanvasPanel (TextListCellRenderer.kt:15) per row — expensive JPanel init with UI lookups.
- Each TextCanvasPanel creation runs SVG applyColors regex on every icon, uses Kotlin reflection (ReflectJvmMapping.getJavaField), and pays a CellRendererPane ArrayList.indexOf linear scan (5s alone for large lists).

Profiler trace from reporter:
  java.awt.Container.add  30200ms
   → CellRendererPane.addImpl → Container.addImpl → JComponent.addNotify
   → Component.updateZOrder → Component.getSiblingIndexAbove  5000ms
     → ArrayList.indexOf  5000ms

Suggested fixes to evaluate:
1. Batch list-model updates on the EDT: build the full array off-EDT, then call listModel.clear() + a single bulk addAll (or replace with a fresh DefaultListModel) rather than per-element addElement (RevisionChoicePanel.kt:186-188).
2. Reuse a single component in TextListCellRenderer.getListCellRendererComponent (TextListCellRenderer.kt:15) instead of allocating a new TextCanvasPanel per cell — standard Swing renderer pattern.
3. Cache/precompute colored SVG icons so applyColors regex isn't re-run on every render.

References: GitHub issue #34 (adam-talos comment); adam-talos PR #28 for an alternative UI approach with search for git SHAs, git branches, jj bookmarks, and change IDs.
close_reason: Fixed all 4 perf issues: (1) reuse single renderer component in TextListCellRenderer, (2) batch listModel.addAll() instead of per-element addElement, (3) hoist IconSpec constants to avoid per-render javaField reflection, (4) precompute immutable tag name set off-EDT. Regression test added.

title: Out-of-limit log revisions loaded for annotation navigation show empty author/date columns
description:
Follow-up to GitHub issue #32. The v0.7.5 fix loads a target change plus ancestors/descendants (window=10) when it's outside the truncated log limit, so annotation-click navigation can select it. But these additionally-loaded revisions render with EMPTY Author and Date columns, while normal truncated revisions render fine (reported by 'ohle' with screenshot).

Root cause: RepoLogCache.loadContext() (jj/LogCache.kt:126-136) fetches via logService.getLogBasic(), which uses basicLogTemplate (jj/cli/CliLogService.kt:284-311) — this template omits the author/committer signature fields. The main log load uses getLog()/fullLogTemplate (CliLogService.kt:313-323), which populates author, committer, authorTimestamp, committerTimestamp. Expansion entries get merged into the same table model (UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:129-147), so only the expansion rows have blank Author/Date.

Fix direction: have loadContext (and the other getLogBasic-based point lookups in RepoLogCache.get(), LogCache.kt:106-124, if they can surface in the table) fetch with the full template so expansion entries carry author/date like main log entries.

GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/32
close_reason: Fixed by switching all RepoLogCache fetches from getLogBasic to getLog so every cached entry carries author/committer signatures

title: Error doing 'Show Diff' on a file in a historical diff
description:
When comparing with a previous revision, then selecting the right-hand editor and 'Show Diff', the following error occurs:

com.intellij.openapi.vcs.VcsException: com.intellij.diff.editor.ChainDiffVirtualFile@254adaea:{} is not within a Jujutsu VCS root
