title: Add integration tests using jj stub
description: Write integration tests that verify plugin behaviour (CliExecutor, CliLogService, ChangeProvider, AnnotationParser, etc.) against the jj stub. These tests exercise the full parsing pipeline end-to-end without needing a real jj installation or IntelliJ platform, giving fast deterministic feedback on plugin correctness.
design:
# Integration Tests Using jj Stub (jj-idea-sljq)

## Context

The project has contract tests that verify raw CLI output format (field counts, separators) against both real jj and the in-memory stub, and unit tests that test parsers with hand-crafted strings. The missing layer is **integration tests** that exercise the full parsing pipeline end-to-end: `JjStub` → `CommandExecutor` → `CliLogService`/`AnnotationParser` → parsed domain objects (`LogEntry`, `FileChange`, `BookmarkItem`, `AnnotationLine`). These catch mismatches between template generation and output parsing without needing a real jj installation or IntelliJ platform.

## Approach

### 1. Create `StubCommandExecutor` adapter

**New file**: `src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/contract/StubCommandExecutor.kt`

Wraps `JjStub` as a `CommandExecutor`, translating between the typed interface and raw `JjBackend.run()` calls. Only methods needed by `CliLogService` and annotation tests need real implementations; others throw `UnsupportedOperationException`.

Methods to implement:
- `log(revset, template, filePaths, limit)` → `stub.run("log", "-r", revset, "--no-graph", "-T", template)`
- `diffSummary(revision)` → `stub.run("diff", "--summary", "-r", revision)`
- `bookmarkList(template)` → `stub.run("bookmark", "list", "-T", template)`
- `annotate(file, revision, template)` → `stub.run("file", "annotate", "-r", revision, "-T", template, file.path)`
- `status()` → `stub.run("status")`
- All other methods: `TODO("Not needed for integration tests")`

Convert `JjBackend.Result` → `CommandExecutor.CommandResult` via simple mapping.

### 2. Update `JjStub.cmdBookmarkList()` for 3-field template

**Modify**: `src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/contract/JjStub.kt`

The actual `bookmarkListTemplate` in `CliLogService` generates a 3-field template (`present`, `nameWithRemote`, `qualifiedChangeId`), but the stub currently outputs only 2 fields. Update `cmdBookmarkList()` to detect the full template (contains `"present"`) and output 3 fields:
- `field("true")` (all stub bookmarks are present/local)
- `field(name)` (no remotes in stub, so `nameWithRemote` = name)
- `field(qualifiedChangeId(change))`

Keep backward compat with the 2-field template used by `BookmarkContractTest`.

### 3. Create integration test classes

**New file**: `src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/integration/LogServiceIntegrationTest.kt`

Tagged `@Tag("stub")` — runs in both `./gradlew test` and `./gradlew stubTest`, no jj required.

Setup pattern:
```kotlin
val stub = JjStub(tempDir)
val executor = StubCommandExecutor(stub)
val repo = mockk<JujutsuRepository> { every { commandExecutor } returns executor }
val logService = CliLogService(repo)
```

**Test cases for `getLogBasic()`:**
- Single entry with description → verify changeId, commitId, description, isWorkingCopy=true
- Multiple entries → verify count and ordering
- Entry with bookmarks → verify bookmarks list
- Multiline description → verify preserved correctly
- Empty working copy → verify isEmpty=true

**Test cases for `getLog()` (full):**
- Verify author name, email, and timestamps populated
- Verify committer fields populated

**Test cases for `getFileChanges()`:**
- Added file → ADDED status
- Modified file → MODIFIED status
- Deleted file → DELETED status
- Mixed changes → correct statuses for each

**Test cases for `getBookmarks()`:**
- Single bookmark → name and changeId
- Multiple bookmarks → all returned

**New file**: `src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/integration/AnnotationIntegrationTest.kt`

Tests the annotation pipeline: `CommandExecutor.annotate()` → `AnnotationParser.parse()`.

**Test cases:**
- Single-change file → all lines attributed to same change
- Multi-change file → lines attributed to different changes
- Verify parsed AnnotationLine fields: changeId, commitId, author, timestamp, description, lineContent, lineNumber

### Files to create/modify

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `src/test/kotlin/.../contract/StubCommandExecutor.kt` | Create |
| `src/test/kotlin/.../contract/JjStub.kt` | Modify (3-field bookmark template) |
| `src/test/kotlin/.../integration/LogServiceIntegrationTest.kt` | Create |
| `src/test/kotlin/.../integration/AnnotationIntegrationTest.kt` | Create |

### Key reuse points

- `CliLogService(repo)` — the class under test (`src/main/kotlin/.../jj/cli/CliLogService.kt`)
- `AnnotationParser.parse()` / `AnnotationParser.TEMPLATE` (`src/main/kotlin/.../jj/cli/AnnotationParser.kt`)
- `JjStub` (`src/test/kotlin/.../contract/JjStub.kt`) — the in-memory backend
- `JjBackend` (`src/test/kotlin/.../contract/JjBackend.kt`) — backend interface
- MockK for `JujutsuRepository` (already a test dependency)
- `@Tag("stub")` for test classification (existing pattern)

## Verification

```bash
./gradlew test          # Integration tests run here (tagged "stub", not excluded)
./gradlew stubTest      # Also runs here (includes "stub" tag)
./gradlew check         # Full check including tests
```

title: Add logRefresh notifier to decouple log from repositoryStates
description:
Currently `repositoryStates` is used as a proxy for 'any log change'. A proper 'log changed' state would be semantically correct and allow finer-grained refresh.

**Context**: The log panel listens to `repositoryStates` changes, but this is actually a working copy/repository state signal. When we want to refresh the log specifically (e.g., after operations that don't change working copy status), we don't have a proper semantic signal.

**Proposed solution**:
- Add a `logChanged` notifiable state to JujutsuStateModel
- JujutsuLogPanel subscribes to this instead of repositoryStates
- Operations that affect the log (new, edit, abandon, describe, etc.) invalidate logChanged
- Operations that only affect working copy files invalidate repositoryStates

**Benefits**:
- Cleaner separation of concerns
- Allows finer-grained refresh
- More semantic state model

**Related**: This emerged from jj-idea-850 during the workingCopies → repositoryStates rename.

title: Fix disposal error when opening native log pane in mixed VCS project
description:
When trying to open a native log pane in the VCS tool window for a mixed VCS root project, an IncorrectOperationException is thrown because the parent VcsLogUiImpl has already been disposed.

The root cause is in ToolWindowEnabler.kt:100 - the contentAdded listener removes content immediately, causing the VcsLogUiImpl to be disposed before VcsLogContentUtil.openLogTab finishes initializing it.

Stack trace shows:
1. OpenAnotherLogTabAction.actionPerformed triggers
2. VcsLogContentUtil.openLogTab adds content
3. ContentManagerImpl.fireContentAdded triggers our listener
4. ToolWindowEnabler.contentAdded removes the content (disposing VcsLogUiImpl)
5. VcsLogContentUtil.openLogTab tries to register a child disposable on the already-disposed parent
6. IncorrectOperationException is thrown

The default log tab suppressor is too aggressive - it removes content synchronously in the contentAdded callback, which interferes with the platform's initialization sequence.

Potential fix: Defer the removal with invokeLater, or check if the content is fully initialized before removing, or use a different approach to suppress default log tabs.

description:
Lines don't continue through intermediate cells when parent/child are separated

**Problem**: Major rendering bug - lines disappear when commits aren't in consecutive rows

**Current behavior**:
- Commit A (row 0, lane 0) has child
- Commit B (row 1, lane 1) - different branch  
- Commit C (row 2, lane 0) - parent of A

**Root cause**: 
Each cell only draws to immediately adjacent rows. Need to track which lanes are 'active' and draw pass-through lines in intermediate cells.

**Solution**:
Track active lanes at each row, draw continuation lines for lanes that pass through but don't have commits

**Complexity**: High - requires redesigning how graph data flows to renderer

title: Investigate VCS log internal API accessibility and alternatives
description:
## Investigation: Option B - Fully Custom Log UI

**Decision**: Build completely custom table/graph UI from scratch, no VcsLogUiEx dependency.

## Architecture: Standalone Custom Log UI

### Core Principle
Don't extend IntelliJ's VcsLogUi at all. Build our own UI that:
- Uses our JujutsuLogProvider data directly
- Has its own table component
- Renders its own commit graph
- Lives in our own tool window tab

### Components to Build

#### 1. Data Layer (Reuse existing)
✅ Already have:
- JujutsuLogProvider - provides commits
- LogService - gets log entries
- ChangeId, LogEntry - domain types

#### 2. Table Component (Build from scratch)
**JujutsuLogTable** - Custom JTable
- Extends JTable directly (not VcsLogGraphTable)
- Custom TableModel with our columns
- No dependency on GraphTableModel
- Columns:
  - Graph (visual commit graph)
  - Status (conflict/empty icons)
  - Change ID (formatted)
  - Description (with right-aligned refs)
  - Author
  - Date

#### 3. Graph Rendering (Build custom)
**JujutsuCommitGraphRenderer** - Custom cell renderer
- Draw commit graph using Graphics2D
- Circles for commits
- Lines for parent relationships
- Different colors for branches
- Similar to VcsLogGraphTable but simpler

#### 4. Column Renderers (Custom implementations)
- **GraphCellRenderer** - Draws commit graph
- **StatusCellRenderer** - Conflict/empty icons
- **ChangeIdCellRenderer** - Bold prefix + gray remainder
- **DescriptionCellRenderer** - Description + right-aligned bookmark icons
- **AuthorCellRenderer** - Author name
- **DateCellRenderer** - Relative dates

#### 5. Main Panel (Custom layout)
**JujutsuLogPanel** - Main UI component
- JujutsuLogTable in scroll pane
- Toolbar (refresh, filters)
- Details pane (commit info when selected)
- Status bar (commit count, etc.)

#### 6. Data Loading (Custom)
**JujutsuLogDataLoader** - Background loading
- Load commits from JujutsuLogProvider
- Build graph structure from parent relationships
- Update table model on EDT
- Handle pagination/incremental loading

### Integration Points

**Instead of VcsLogUi registration**:
- Add tab to our existing 'Working copy' tool window
- Or create new 'Jujutsu' tool window with multiple tabs
- Use ContentFactory to create tabs

**Data source**:
- JujutsuLogProvider (already works)
- Call logService.getLog() directly
- No dependency on VcsLogData/VcsLogManager

**Actions**:
- Right-click context menu with our own actions
- Double-click to show diff
- Keyboard shortcuts (F4, Enter, etc.)

## Advantages of This Approach

1. **No internal API dependencies** - Only use public IntelliJ SDK
2. **Complete control** - Every pixel is ours
3. **Simpler codebase** - No fighting with platform abstractions
4. **Jujutsu-native** - Design specifically for JJ concepts
5. **Easier to maintain** - No platform update breakage
6. **Faster iteration** - No reverse-engineering platform behavior

## Challenges

1. **Graph algorithm** - Need to implement commit graph layout
2. **Performance** - Optimize for large repos (1000+ commits)
3. **Polish** - Match platform look & feel
4. **Features** - Implement filtering, search, etc.
5. **Effort** - More code to write upfront

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Basic Table (jj-idea-9to, jj-idea-jbb, jj-idea-57u)
- JujutsuLogTable with basic columns (no graph yet)
- Simple TableModel loading from LogService
- Basic rendering (text only)
- Show in tool window tab
**Goal**: See commits in a table

### Phase 2: Graph Rendering (new task)
- Implement commit graph layout algorithm
- GraphCellRenderer with Graphics2D
- Parent relationship visualization
**Goal**: Visual commit graph

### Phase 3: Custom Renderers (jj-idea-53v, jj-idea-aq7)
- All column-specific renderers
- Icons, colors, formatting
- Right-aligned refs in description
**Goal**: Professional appearance

### Phase 4: Features (jj-idea-9y2, jj-idea-ncg, jj-idea-6gx)
- Details pane
- Filtering/search
- Context menu actions
**Goal**: Feature parity with needs

### Phase 5: Polish (jj-idea-qvf, jj-idea-035)
- Performance optimization
- Keyboard shortcuts
- Testing
**Goal**: Production ready

## References for Graph Algorithm

- Git log --graph implementation
- Gitk graph rendering
- IntelliJ's graph (for inspiration, not code reuse)

## Decision: Proceed with Option B

This is more work upfront but gives us a maintainable, Jujutsu-native solution.

title: Visual polish: themes, scaling, tooltips
description:
Visual polish pass for custom log UI to ensure professional appearance across themes, display scales, and with proper tooltips.

## Issues Found

### P0 - Critical (Must Fix)

1. **Hardcoded graph colors don't adapt to themes**
   - File: `JujutsuCommitGraph.kt:51-58`
   - Issue: Uses `Color(0x...)` instead of `JBColor`
   - Impact: Poor contrast in dark theme, unprofessional appearance
   - Fix: Replace with `JBColor(lightColor, darkColor)` pairs

   - Fix: Add HTML tooltips explaining each indicator

### P1 - High Priority (Should Fix)

   - File: `JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt:209`
   - Issue: `HORIZONTAL_PADDING = 4` doesn't scale

   - Issue: `GAP_BEFORE_ARROW`, `BORDER_SIZE`, `ARC_SIZE` are raw ints
   - Fix: Use `JBUI.scale()`

### P2 - Nice to Have

title: File history: Open in remote (GitLab/GitHub)
design:
## Design: Open in Remote (GitHub/GitLab)

### How IntelliJ's Git Plugin Does It

The Git plugin's \"Open on GitHub\" does NOT use RepositoryLocation or VcsFileRevision.getChangedRepositoryPath(). Instead it uses a dedicated infrastructure:

- `HostedGitRepositoriesManager` discovers remotes reactively via Kotlin flows
- `GlobalHostedGitRepositoryReferenceActionGroup` provides context-aware actions
- GitHub plugin implements these interfaces and registers via `Git.Hosting.Open.In.Browser.Group` action group
- Data sources: VCS_FILE_REVISION (file history), VCS_LOG_COMMIT_SELECTION (log), VIRTUAL_FILE+EDITOR (editor)

We can't reuse this because it requires GitRepository objects from GitRepositoryManager, which won't exist for jj-registered roots.

### Proposed Approach: Simple Custom Action

Since we're a standalone VCS plugin (not a Git hosting plugin), implement a simpler self-contained approach:

**1. URL Builder** — Pure function that constructs web URLs:
```kotlin
object RemoteUrlBuilder {
    fun commitUrl(remoteUrl: String, commitHash: String): String?
    fun fileUrl(remoteUrl: String, commitHash: String, filePath: String, lineRange: IntRange? = null): String?
}
```

Supports GitHub and GitLab URL patterns by parsing the remote URL:
- SSH: `git@github.com:user/repo.git` → `https://github.com/user/repo`
- HTTPS: `https://github.com/user/repo.git` → `https://github.com/user/repo`
- Commit: `<base>/commit/<hash>`
- File: `<base>/blob/<hash>/<path>` (GitHub) or `<base>/-/blob/<hash>/<path>` (GitLab)

**2. Remote Resolution** — Use existing `CommandExecutor.gitRemoteList()`:
- Parse `<name> <url>` lines
- Prefer `origin` remote
- Cache per repository (remotes rarely change)

**3. Action Integration** — Add to existing context menus:

a) **File history** (JujutsuHistoryProvider): Add \"Open on Remote\" to `getAdditionalActions()`. Get commit hash from `JujutsuRevisionNumber` → need to expose `CommitId` from `JujutsuFileRevision` or store it in `JujutsuRevisionNumber`.

b) **Custom log** (JujutsuLogContextMenuActions): Add action that reads selected `LogEntry.commitId`.

c) **Editor/file** (optional, future): Open current file at working copy's commit on remote.

**4. Data Available Today**:
- `LogEntry.commitId: CommitId` — the git commit hash (full + short), already parsed
- `JujutsuRepository.commandExecutor.gitRemoteList()` — already implemented
- `JujutsuRevisionNumber` wraps a `Revision` (ChangeId), but NOT CommitId — need to expose CommitId somehow

### Key Decision: How to Get CommitId in File History

`JujutsuFileRevision` has access to `LogEntry` (which has `commitId`), but the platform action only sees `VcsFileRevision`. Options:
1. Add a `commitId` property to `JujutsuFileRevision` (simplest — cast in action)
2. Store both ChangeId and CommitId in `JujutsuRevisionNumber`
3. Pass LogEntry reference through

Option 1 is simplest and follows the pattern Git uses (casting to GitFileRevision).

### Scope

- GitHub and GitLab support (covers most jj users)
- Commit view only initially (file view is nice-to-have)
- Opens in default browser via `BrowserUtil.browse()`
- Graceful handling: disabled when no recognized remote, no error dialogs

### Test Plan

- Unit test `RemoteUrlBuilder` with GitHub SSH, GitHub HTTPS, GitLab SSH, GitLab HTTPS, unknown hosts
- Unit test remote list parsing
- Manual: runIde with a repo that has GitHub/GitLab remotes, verify URLs open correctly from log and file history
close_reason: Implemented RemoteUrlBuilder (github.com/gitlab.com SSH+HTTPS parsing), openInRemoteGroup (dynamic per-remote actions with single/submenu behavior), OpenInRemoteFromHistoryGroup for file history toolbar. Unit tests pass.

* def5678 (feature-branch) Another commit

title: Real-time status updates (auto-refresh)
description:
**Priority**: MEDIUM (Phase 1 - Read-only features)
**Effort**: 1-2 days

## Description
Auto-refresh working copy status when files change on disk.

## User Experience
- File changes appear immediately in tool window
- Status colors update automatically
- No manual refresh needed

## Implementation
```kotlin
class JujutsuFileListener(private val project: Project) : VirtualFileListener {
    override fun contentsChanged(event: VirtualFileEvent) {
        VcsDirtyScopeManager.getInstance(project).fileDirty(event.file)
    }
}
```

## Registration
In `JujutsuVcs.activate()`:
```kotlin
override fun activate() {
    super.activate()
    VirtualFileManager.getInstance().addVirtualFileListener(fileListener, this)
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] File edits trigger automatic refresh
- [ ] File creation triggers refresh
- [ ] File deletion triggers refresh
- [ ] Listener registered in activate()
- [ ] No performance issues with large projects
- [ ] Optional: debouncing for rapid changes

## References
See ROADMAP.md Phase 1 - Read-only Features
See VCS_API_REFERENCE.md - Virtual File Listener

title: Annotation click doesn't select an old change in the Jujutsu log (GitHub #140)
description:
Reporter adam-talos: clicking the author in the annotation gutter does not take them to the change in the log; they suspect the 500-change limit. Suggests bisecting or just showing the change files instead.

Out-of-limit navigation already exists (JujutsuFileAnnotation.handleAnnotationClick -> changeSelection -> JujutsuLogTable.requestSelection -> loadExpanding/loadContext; see closed jj-idea-vuzp, jj-idea-fy2p), so the limit alone should not cause this. Hypotheses: (a) notify fires before activateLogTab so a not-yet-created log panel misses it; (b) change id hidden/rewritten so loadContext returns empty and onMissing silently clears the request (cf. jj-idea-wiz0 / #130); (c) interaction with paged loading (jj-idea-2570.4).

Status: needs repro - awaiting reporter info. Fallback idea (show change files directly) is close to jj-idea-7m8.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/140

title: Merge tool pane titles drop <...> text from change descriptions (GitHub #138)

Likely cause: ExtractedConflict.currentTitle/lastTitle (from jj conflict marker labels, include description) go unescaped into merge titles that the platform renders as HTML. Fix at JujutsuConflictResolver.kt (~:125-132) and JujutsuConflictDiffRequestProvider.kt (~:105-107); also check conflictBannerModel.kt. Add a unit test with a description containing <foo@bar>.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/138

title: Preview access code field: live feedback and clearer errors
description: Settings access-code field only re-evaluates on Apply + reopen, shows nothing when a code is accepted, and reports a JJP1 code on a build without the signing key as 'Not a valid access code' (misleading). Make status and feature list update as the text changes; add an Unverifiable grant state with its own message; show an accepted message.

title: Log viewport jumps back to selected commit on every page load after a requestSelection
description: After any requestSelection() that finds its target immediately (e.g. changeSelection on startup), pendingSelection stayed set and pendingSelectionIsExplicit stayed true, so every later setEntries() re-selected it WITH scrollIntoView, yanking the viewport back while the user scrolled and pages loaded. Fix: clear pendingSelection on immediate success; setEntries never scrolls to a carried-over selection. Test in JujutsuLogTableScrollPreservationTest.
close_reason: Fixed: append fast path now used (logOrder + multi-repo-only timestamp guard); scroll-jump fixed. 2570.7 not yet re-measured on r80k-git sandbox.

title: Status bar widget install() renders Swing off the EDT (assertIsDispatchThread failure)
description: Seen while smoke-testing jj-idea-n3u0 in runIde (unrelated to the Tasks handler). IdeStatusBarImpl.doInit calls StatusBarWidget.install on a DefaultDispatcher worker ('status bar widget creating'), and JujutsuStatusBarWidget.install (JujutsuStatusBarWidget.kt:~45) sets panel.statusBarWidth = component.width, whose setter calls renderTruncated() -> TextCanvasPanel.renderFrom (TruncatingLeftRightLayout.kt:45), which asserts EDT: RuntimeExceptionWithAttachments 'Access is allowed from Event Dispatch Thread (EDT) only'. Logged as an unhandled coroutine exception; the widget may not render its initial state. Fix: do the install-time Swing work (statusBarWidth set, addComponentListener, initial refresh) via invokeLater/EDT, or make the setter marshal to EDT. Add a regression test that install() from a non-EDT thread does not throw. Manual regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY (status bar widget).
close_reason: Closed

title: Graduate in-editor conflict gutter (CONFLICT_GUTTER) out of preview, on for everyone

title: [perf] GraphEdgeIndex.build runs on the EDT per graph update, O(sum of edge spans): 5-6s UI freezes at ~47k rows (git/git)
description: Measured 2026-10-03 on ~/workspace/jj-scale/r80k-git (85,912 commits, 7 heads), paged log, page size 500, sandbox IDE (2 GB heap). Four 'UI was frozen' reports of 5.3-6.4 s at 18:20:28-18:20:52 (rows ~46-49k); every freeze thread dump's AWT-EventQueue is in GraphEdgeIndex$Companion.build (GraphEdgeIndex.kt:260/317) <- JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.edgeIndex (:82) <- GraphAndDescriptionPanel.textStartX <- getTableCellRendererComponent, i.e. the index is built lazily INSIDE PAINT, on the EDT, once per renderer, and JujutsuLogTable.updateGraph installs a fresh renderer on every graph update - so every page that lands (every 1-7 s) re-triggers a full rebuild. build() does one place()/map put per (row x lane) an edge's span touches (for (r in row..parentRow)), so cost and memory are O(sum of edge spans) = rows x average active lanes. The layout's own operationCount shows ~557 cells/row on git/git at 49k rows (27.3M cumulative; 4.4M @10k, 11.2M @24k, 20.1M @39k) vs ~63/row on keycloak (2.25M @35.5k). Same freezes show as log-edt-wait of 0.6-3.1 s (EDT busy painting when a page lands) from ~39k rows. Directions: (a) build the index off-EDT in the same background pass as the layout and hand it over with the graph; (b) extend it incrementally in step with appendGraph; (c) store each edge as a [childRow,parentRow] interval with lane and look up per painted row, instead of materialising a map entry per (row,lane); (d) long-edge collapsing (jj-idea-66rr) bounds active lanes and so everything above. Needs an operation-count test (cells built per update) per contributing.md. Related: jj-idea-a0wp (closed; its premise predicted this, its fix removed the per-repaint rescans but kept the O(sum spans) build), jj-idea-jnqi, jj-idea-66rr.
close_reason: GraphEdgeIndex now stores each edge once as a row interval per lane (build O(rows+edges) instead of O(sum of edge spans)); equivalence-tested against the old per-cell build on 80 random graphs; operation-count tests on a 5k-row x 200-lane graph (bound 8n). Sandbox run on r80k-git to 81.5k rows: no UI freezes, log-edt-wait 0 ms (previously 4 freezes of 5.3-6.4 s at ~47k rows). Follow-ups: 2570.7 (full relayout per page, cost grows with depth).

title: [perf] Graph appendGraph cost per page grows with depth on wide graphs (git/git: 8 ms at 500 rows -> 3-8 s per 500-row page at 44-48k)
description: Measured 2026-10-03, r80k-git, paged log, page size 500 (perf: graph-layout lines in idea.log). Layout time per appended page: 8 ms @500 rows, 76 ms @5k, 180 ms @10k, 391 ms @15k, 890 ms @24k, 1.5 s @29k, 1.0 s @34k, 2.3 s @39k, 3.0 s @44k, 6.9 s @48k, 5.0 s @49k. Per-page operations stay ~200-350k (400-700 per appended row), so it is the cost PER OPERATION that climbs (maps/sets of ever larger size, cache misses, and GC pressure - the sandbox logged 'High memory usage (free 215-232 of 2048 MB)' from ~46k rows) rather than the algorithm doing more work per page; jj-idea-jnqi made the append O(delta + bounded window) but 'bounded' is in lanes, and git/git runs hundreds of concurrent lanes. keycloak (35.5k rows, ~63 cells/row) never exceeded ~0.5 s per page. Investigate: what the incremental engine retains per row (RowLayout/GraphNode.passthroughLanes maps are O(active lanes) per row), whether any per-append step touches all retained rows, and heap per row/cell. Likely resolved by the same representation change as the GraphEdgeIndex bead (store spans, not per-row cells) and by jj-idea-66rr (long-edge collapsing). Add a deep-append operation-count test on a wide synthetic graph.
notes: 2026-10-05 root cause: appendGuardHolds' 'delta newer than snapshot.minTimestamp' guard failed on ~every page past ~2.5k rows on git/git (non-monotonic author dates), forcing a full re-layout per page. Fix: logOrder keeps jj order within a repo (index-tiebreak Kahn) and interleaves repos by timestamp; timestamp guard now multi-repo only; guard decision logged at debug ('log merge: append|full (reason)'). Tests: LogMergeScaleTest deep wide-graph append, TopologicalSortTest log order. Still to verify in sandbox on r80k-git (expect graph-layout-append lines).

title: [bug] Push dry-run parsing uses old jj output format: force-push/delete confirmations silently skipped on jj 0.44
description:
FOUND while planning jj-idea-7n98 (Preview push) by running real jj 0.44.0 (not yet confirmed on other versions - step 1 of the design).

actions/git/gitRemoteActions.kt `checkAndPush` runs `jj git push --dry-run` and parses the text to decide whether to show the force-push / deletion confirmations before pushing:
- `FORCE_PUSH_MARKERS = ["Move sideways bookmark ", "Move backward bookmark "]` (gitRemoteActions.kt:264) -> `parseForcePushBookmarks`
- `DELETE_MARKER = "Delete bookmark "` (:274) -> `parseDeletedBookmarks`
- `REFUSING_NEW_BOOKMARK_MARKER = Regex("Refusing to create new remote bookmark (\S+)")` (:254) -> `parseRefusedNewBookmarks`
Unit tests (actions/git/GitPushActionTest.kt:86,106,169) use the OLD format "Move sideways bookmark main from abc1234 to def5678".

jj 0.44.0 actually prints (probed locally with a bare remote):
```
Changes to push to origin:
  bookmark: main [move forward from f34428f2095e to dcb29298f0e3]
  bookmark: main [move backward from f34428f2095e to 182a4033cf41]
  bookmark: main [delete from b582baa20a86]
  bookmark: brandnew [add to 8135a00429e9]
Dry-run requested, not pushing.
```
So on jj 0.44 none of the "Move backward/sideways"/"Delete bookmark" markers match: the safety confirmations (force push of non-fast-forward moves, pushing bookmark deletions) are silently skipped and the push proceeds unconfirmed. (A sideways move printed as "move forward" in my probe because the fixture wasn't actually a diverging move - re-check with a genuine sideways case; the format for sideways is probably "[move sideways from X to Y]".) New untracked bookmarks printed "[add to X]" with --bookmark, i.e. may no longer be "refused" at all in 0.44 - the untracked-bookmark confirm flow (trackAndPush) may be dead too.
design:
PLAN: make dry-run parsing format-tolerant, prove it per jj version, and add a drift canary so this can't be silent again. (jj-idea-7n98's preview must reuse this parser - land this first.)
Step 1 - characterise (1h): for each jj version the project supports (MINIMUM 0.37.0 .. current 0.44.0; contributing.md "Testing against multiple jj versions" describes how to run contract tests against several jj binaries) run `jj git push --dry-run` over a scripted fixture (bare remote) covering: add (tracked + untracked/new), move forward, move backward, move sideways (create a genuinely diverging move: push main, then `jj new main@origin`, `jj bookmark set main -r @ --allow-backwards` where @ is NOT a descendant AND not an ancestor of the remote target), delete, conflicted bookmark, tags (0.44), --all/--deleted scopes, the "Refusing to create new remote bookmark" warning/error (default scope vs --bookmark). Record the exact stdout/stderr per version in a fixture file `src/test/resources/jj-push-dryrun/<version>.txt` (golden captures). Find the version where the format switched (bisect over 0.37..0.44) and note it here.
Step 2 - parser: replace the three string-contains parsers (gitRemoteActions.kt:254-285) with one `parseDryRun(stdout+stderr): DryRunPlan(actions: List<PushAction>, refusedNew: List<String>)` that understands BOTH formats:
 - legacy: `Move forward|sideways|backward bookmark X from A to B`, `Delete bookmark X from A`, `Add bookmark X to B`, `Refusing to create new remote bookmark X@Y`
 - bracketed (0.4x): `  bookmark: X [add to B]`, `[move forward from A to B]`, `[move backward from A to B]`, `[move sideways from A to B]` (confirm wording in step 1), `[delete from A]`, and tag lines (`tag: v1 [add to ...]`?) 
 `PushAction(kind, name, from?, to?, isTag)`. `forcePushBookmarks = kind in {MOVE_SIDEWAYS, MOVE_BACKWARD}`; `deletedBookmarks = kind == DELETE`. The existing public/internal functions `parseForcePushBookmarks`, `parseDeletedBookmarks`, `parseRefusedNewBookmarks` become thin wrappers (callers + tests unchanged).
Step 3 - decide the new-bookmark flow: if 0.44 no longer refuses new remote bookmarks with `--bookmark X` (probe shows "[add to ..]"), the `confirmUntrackedPush`/`trackAndPush` path (gitRemoteActions.kt:176-205) never triggers on new jj; that's possibly desired (jj stopped requiring --allow-new) - but then the plugin also pushes new bookmarks WITHOUT the "this will create a remote bookmark" confirmation the dialog previously gave. Rec: keep behaviour parity: treat `ADD` actions for bookmarks with no existing remote ref as "new remote bookmark" and show the same confirmation (the information is in the plan: kind ADD + remote has no tracked ref - or simply kind ADD where the local bookmark is untracked for that remote, known from bookmark data). Decision below.
Step 4 - drift canary: if the output contains "Changes to push to" (or any non-empty stdout/stderr on a successful dry-run) but the parser extracted ZERO actions, log `log.warn` ONCE per session with the raw text (jj output format may have changed) and, for the safety confirms, FAIL SAFE: when the plan can't be parsed and the user's push scope includes bookmarks that the plugin's own state says are non-fast-forward/deleted, still show the generic confirm ("jj reported changes the plugin couldn't interpret; push anyway?"). Rec: warn+generic confirm only when our own bookmark state (ahead/behind/deleted) says a force/delete is involved - avoids nagging on ordinary pushes.
Step 5 - tests: golden-file parser tests (one per captured version), the legacy-format tests kept (GitPushActionTest.kt:86,106,169), contract test running real jj dry-run and asserting the parsed kinds for each fixture scenario (runs against the installed jj, CI matrix per contributing.md), canary test (garbled text => warn once, fail-safe confirm path).
Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Keep parsing text vs derive from bookmark state? Rec: parse (jj is the authority on what it will do), plus the state-based fail-safe in step 4. Reverse: compute plan from `Bookmark` ahead/behind/deleted data.
2. Q: Preserve new-bookmark confirmation on new jj? Rec: yes (parity). Reverse: drop the confirm for jj versions that no longer refuse.
Scale: none (O(output lines)). Manual: MT-GIT (force-push confirm appears on a non-fast-forward move; deletion confirm; new bookmark confirm) - run on current jj AND the minimum jj; regression scope: MT-GIT, MT-BOOKMARK (push entry points), MT-CTXMENU.
Priority note: P2 because it silently removes a safety confirmation (force/delete push) on current jj - worth confirming the finding with the user first thing.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run parser handles legacy and bracketed formats for all jj versions >= MINIMUM (golden captures); force-push/delete/new-bookmark confirmations fire on jj 0.44; drift canary + fail-safe confirm; contract + golden + canary tests; MT-GIT re-run on min and current jj.
close_reason: Parser handles legacy + bracketed dry-run formats (golden captures from jj 0.37/0.39/0.44/0.45), contract test runs against real jj (verified on 0.37, 0.39, 0.44, 0.45). Note: on jj>=0.39 a specific-bookmark push of a new bookmark is no longer refused, so no 'create remote bookmark' confirmation for it (default scope still refuses and still prompts).

title: IntelliJ-style long-edge collapsing in log graph
description: Once edges can be hundreds of rows long (more common with progressive paging), draw edges longer than ~30 rows as short ends with arrows and release the lane in between, keeping the graph narrow. Prior art: intellij-community platform/vcs-log/graph PrintElementGeneratorImpl (LONG_EDGE_SIZE=30, LONG_EDGE_PART_SIZE=1). Builds on jj-idea-sc8m's hover/click navigation for the collapsed ends. Optional companion to the progressive paging bead.
design:
PLAN: draw very long edges as short end-caps with arrows and RELEASE the lane in between (IntelliJ's vcs-log approach), keeping the graph narrow. Optional/companion to jj-idea-2570.5; do after 2570.4 (paged log default) since long edges are mostly a paged-window phenomenon.
Prior art (verify before copying the numbers): ../intellij-community platform/vcs-log/graph `PrintElementGeneratorImpl` - `LONG_EDGE_SIZE = 30` (edges spanning more rows than this are "long"), `LONG_EDGE_PART_SIZE = 1` (rows of line kept at each end; the middle is hidden/replaced by an arrow); their lane layout (`GraphLayout`) still reserves the column - their lane release happens at layout level via `collapsed edges`? READ the source: if IntelliJ keeps the lane reserved and only hides the paint, the "keeps the graph narrow" benefit requires OUR layout to free the lane, which is a layout-engine change (riskier). Decide after reading.
Our code: lanes assigned by `LayoutCalculatorImpl` (ui/log/graph/); per-row passthrough lanes in `RowLayout`; edge geometry/hover/navigation indexed by `GraphEdgeIndex` (ui/log/GraphEdgeIndex.kt: `HoveredEdge(span, emphasized, direction, navigable)`, long-edge navigation from jj-idea-sc8m: hover thickens the span, click jumps/loads the other end); painted by JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.
Design (two layers, ship layer 1 alone if layer 2 proves too invasive):
1. PAINT-ONLY collapse (low risk): for an edge with span > LONG_EDGE (30 rows, a constant `GraphConstants.LONG_EDGE_ROWS`, tweakable), paint only the first and last 1 row(s) of its line plus an arrow glyph (down arrow at the top cap, up arrow at the bottom cap), leave the middle rows' lane EMPTY in the paint of that lane. The column is still reserved, so width doesn't shrink, but the graph reads much cleaner and the arrows invite the click that sc8m already implements (hover = preview the other end, click = jump). Edge hit-testing (GraphEdgeIndex) must treat the hidden middle as still part of the edge for hover thickening (sc8m: whole span thickens on hover) - on hover show the full line (temporary un-collapse) so users can see where it goes; this preserves the existing sc8m behaviour exactly.
2. LAYOUT-LEVEL lane release (the actual "keep it narrow" win): after computing lanes, for each long edge release its lane for the middle rows so later branches can reuse that column: implement as a post-pass `compactLongEdges(layout, threshold)` that, for each edge (child row c, parent row p, lane L) with p - c > threshold, marks lane L free in rows c+K..p-K and, if another node/edge in those rows would have used a lane > L, tries to reassign into L (only for edges fully contained in the freed span to avoid creating crossings). Hard part: reassigned lanes must not create new line crossings/diagonals (cf. jj-idea-euv "minimize diagonal crossings"); safest v1 rule: only move SHORT-LIVED branches (entirely within the freed interval) into the freed lane; leave everything else. Needs property tests: no two edges share (row, lane); every node's parent edge endpoint lane == the lane drawn at its row; total width never increases (monotone).
3. Interaction with jj-idea-hlu3 (elided edges) and NOT_LOADED stubs (2570.5): stubs are one-row edges (no change); elided edges are real edges and may be long -> same collapse applies. With incremental layout (`appendGraph`, IncrementalLayoutEquivalenceTest): post-pass must be recomputed over the affected tail or the incremental==full equivalence breaks. Rec: apply compaction only in the FULL layout path and make incremental append fall back to full when a long edge's span crosses the append boundary; add an equivalence test.
Decisions made without the user: Q: ship layer 1 only? Rec: yes first (low risk, immediate readability), layer 2 behind a hidden registry flag / only if users report width problems (large repos). Q: threshold 30? Rec: 30 (IntelliJ's) as a named constant, no setting. Reverse: raise/lower constant, or add a setting under graph options (jj-idea-jnv graph style config).
Scale: paint: O(visible rows) with a per-row O(#lanes) check against a precomputed long-edge set from GraphEdgeIndex (already per-graph-update O(n+e)); no new per-repaint traversal. Layout compaction (layer 2): O(n + e) one pass; operation-count test on 10k rows with 200 long edges.
Testing: layer 1: renderer paint test (cap rows painted, middle rows not, arrows present; hover un-collapses) in existing graph render tests; layer 2: LayoutCalculator property tests above + equivalence test. Manual: MT-LOG-GRAPH (stress fixture FX-STRESS deep branch: arrows at ends, hover shows full line, click navigates; paged scroll), MT-LOG-TABLE (hover). Regression scope: MT-LOG-GRAPH, MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-DND (edge hit-testing vs drop targets).
acceptance_criteria: Layer 1: edges longer than the threshold paint as capped segments with arrows, hover restores the full line and sc8m navigation still works; layer 2 (lane release) optional and gated on property tests; manual rows added.
notes: 2026-10-03: raised P3->P2. r80k-git shows ~557 graph cells/row at 49k rows (keycloak ~63): the O(rows x active lanes) data model is what freezes the EDT (5-6 s) and exhausts a 2 GB heap on wide graphs. See jj-idea-2570.6 / jj-idea-2570.7 / jj-idea-2570.11.
close_reason: Long edges (50+ rows) collapse to arrowed caps with the lane released between; hover thickens both caps and click jumps to the other end. Hover-restores-full-line dropped by design.

title: Spike: jj behaviour for commit-ID reads / divergent change IDs (for jj-idea-wiz0, GitHub #130)
description: Verify against the minimum supported jj before designing the fix for jj-idea-wiz0: (a) a bare divergent change ID errors in single- and multi-revision args; (b) a hidden full commit_id resolves for file show/diff/log; (c) behaviour after op abandon + util gc; (d) short commit-ID prefixes with hidden commits; (e) whether --at-op is useful for consistent reads. Also ask reporter whether Piper keeps superseded commits resolvable by commit ID.
design:
PLAN: scripted spike, output is a findings doc + contract tests, not production code. Unblocks jj-idea-wiz0.

Method: a throwaway script in the scratchpad (and then committed as contract tests under the existing contractTest source set, which already runs real jj; see jj-idea-blkg for CI) that builds a repo with: change A (commit a1), amended to a2 (a1 hidden), a divergent pair via `jj op restore`/two `jj describe --at-op`, and a remote bookmark pointing at the hidden a1 (`jj git init` + local bare remote; fetch, then amend locally and keep `cl/X@origin` at a1). Run against the pinned minimum (JjVersion.MINIMUM) AND the current jj (0.44.0 locally); record both.
Matrix to record (one row per question; output verbatim in docs/jj-commit-id-reads.md):
(a) `jj log -r <bare divergent change id>` / `jj file show -r` / `diff --from X --to Y` with one and with several revs: error text and exit code (expect "Change ID is divergent"). The plugin must recognise this error (stable text? else detect via exit code + stderr substring) - record the exact message per version.
(b) hidden full commit_id: does `jj file show -r <commit_id> path`, `jj diff -r`, `jj log -r` resolve with default revset? (jj resolves commit IDs of hidden commits for explicit args; confirm no `--hidden`-style flag is needed.)
(c) after `jj op abandon <op>` + `jj util gc --keep-newer` (or equivalent): does the hidden commit remain readable (object still in store) or error "No such revision"? Determines whether the plugin needs a "commit no longer available" fallback.
(d) short commit-id prefix resolution when the prefix is ambiguous with hidden commits (jj prefix uniqueness is computed over visible+hidden? record `jj log -T 'commit_id.shortest()'` for the hidden commit).
(e) `--at-op <op>` for consistent multi-read snapshots (diff + file show of the same state while another process mutates): works for reads, and `jj --at-op` implies --ignore-working-copy? Record whether it snapshots @.
(f) Template availability: `hidden`, `divergent`, `change_offset`, `commit_id` keywords at the minimum version.
Also: comment on GH #130 asking the reporter whether Piper keeps superseded commits resolvable by commit_id (the only item needing a human reply; draft the comment text in this bead's notes rather than posting - posting is outward-facing, ask first).

Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Min-version too, or only latest jj? Rec: both; any behaviour difference becomes a JjFeature gate or a documented limitation (contributing.md says never emulate on older versions). 
2. Q: Post the Piper question on GitHub myself? Rec: no - draft only; user posts.

Scale: spike on a tiny repo; no plugin code. Testing: the contract tests are the deliverable and must be deterministic (fixed ids via `--config` and `JJ_TIMESTAMP`/`JJ_OP_TIMESTAMP`, `JJ_RANDOMNESS_SEED` where available).
acceptance_criteria: docs/jj-commit-id-reads.md records answers (a)-(f) with exact jj output for min and current jj; contract tests pin the behaviours wiz0 relies on; draft GH #130 question to reporter stored in notes; wiz0 design updated with findings.

description: All DnD gesture batches (0-5) are closed; batch 6 (jj-idea-3uhu live preview, jj-idea-9d7r adaptive zones) and jj-idea-f1ms are P4 polish and do not block GA. Blocked on jj-idea-ymuu (reject/allow drop hint text) being confirmed live. Per docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md Part B ('At GA'): (1) remove PreviewFeature.DRAG_AND_DROP and its guards at the install sites - JujutsuLogTableDnD.kt, JujutsuChangesTreeDnD.kt, JujutsuBookmarksPanelDnD.kt, IconAwareHtmlPaneDnD.kt, and the dragScope check in CommitTablePanel.kt - and retire bit 0 permanently (never reuse; document in PreviewFeature.kt); (2) update tests that set jjidea.preview.dragAndDrop or assert the off state (JujutsuLogTableDnDTest, JujutsuChangesTreeDnDTest, PreviewEntitlementTest, PreviewCodeTest) - PreviewCodeTest/PreviewEntitlementTest use DRAG_AND_DROP as their sample feature, so they need another fixture; (3) decide what the Settings 'Preview features' group shows with zero features (PAGED_LOG_LOAD may still be in it - see jj-idea-2570.4, which may graduate in the same release); (4) condense docs/preview-changelog.md's DnD entries into a few user-facing CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] entries; (5) update MT-DND and the Preview-features settings section in docs/manual-tests.md, plus README/ROADMAP; (6) full MT-DND manual pass with no access code and no system property set.
design:
PLAN: follow docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md Part B 'At GA' - the bead's description already enumerates the work; this is the executable ordering.

Pre-check: jj-idea-ymuu (reject-drop hint) is closed per the dependency; confirm "confirmed live" by one manual drag-rejection in runIde before starting (MT-DND reject-drop rows). If it still shows a blank tooltip, stop and reopen ymuu.
Steps (one commit each so any is revertible):
 1. Remove the guards: `PreviewFeature.DRAG_AND_DROP` checks at install sites ui/log/JujutsuLogTableDnD.kt, ui/common/JujutsuChangesTreeDnD.kt, ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanelDnD.kt, ui/components/IconAwareHtmlPaneDnD.kt, and the dragScope check in ui/common/CommitTablePanel.kt. Make the installers unconditional. Delete enum entry; leave `/** bit 0 retired - never reuse */` in PreviewFeature.kt (its class kdoc: reuse would let an old still-valid access code grant a new feature). Remove bundle keys preview.dragAndDrop.* and the jjidea.preview.dragAndDrop system property handling.
 2. Tests: JujutsuLogTableDnDTest, JujutsuChangesTreeDnDTest drop the entitlement/property setup and the "off state" assertions (delete the off-state tests: the state no longer exists). PreviewEntitlementTest/PreviewCodeTest need a new sample feature: switch to CONFLICT_GUTTER (still gated) - if jj-idea-2570.4 or conflict-gutter graduate first, introduce a test-only enum value behind `@VisibleForTesting` rather than leaving the tests fixture-less. Also grep for "dragAndDrop" in src/test resources and gradle runIde/test JVM args.
 3. Settings 'Preview features' group (JujutsuConfigurable.kt): decision below.
 4. Docs: docs/preview-changelog.md - delete DnD entries; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] - 3-5 user-facing lines (what you can drag where: changes -> rebase/squash/duplicate, bookmarks/tags move, with live drop hints). README/ROADMAP feature lists. docs/manual-tests.md: MT-DND preconditions no longer mention access code/system property; Preview-features section in MT-SETTINGS updated.
 5. Full MT-DND manual pass with no access code and no system property (acceptance).
 6. Batch 6 (3uhu live preview, 9d7r adaptive zones, f1ms drag chip count) stay P4 post-GA - not blockers.

Decisions made without the user

2. Q: Release together with 2570.4? Rec: independent; whichever is second handles the empty group.
3. Q: Announce in release notes prominently? Rec: yes, headline entry - DnD is the most user-visible feature in the plugin.

Scale: removes gating only; no new traversal. Manual regression scope: MT-DND (full), MT-LOG-TABLE (table DnD installer), MT-BOOKMARK (bookmarks panel DnD), MT-WORKINGCOPY (changes tree DnD), MT-SETTINGS (preview group); 5 sections - shared surface, broad pass advisable.
acceptance_criteria: DnD works with no code/property; zero DRAG_AND_DROP references (grep); bit 0 documented retired; preview-group empty-state handled; CHANGELOG/preview-changelog/README/ROADMAP/manual-tests updated; ./gradlew check green; MT-DND pass recorded.
notes: Implemented in change wpvnnols (gate removed, tests/docs updated, ./gradlew check green). Preview group still has PAGED_LOG_LOAD + CONFLICT_GUTTER so no empty-state code needed; whichever graduation lands last owns that. Release-summary extraction verified. Remaining: manual MT-DND pass.

title: Bug: hidden commit behind a remote bookmark resolves to the current visible change with the same change ID (GitHub #130)
description:
Reporter (SergejSalnikov), Piper-backed jj repo. The plugin identifies commits by change ID (change_offset only added when divergent). When a remote bookmark points at a *hidden* commit — e.g. a change amended locally after fetch, so the local and remote bookmark point at different commits of the same change — the bare change ID resolves to whichever commit is currently visible with that ID (often @). Diffs, file contents, file history and diffbase comparisons for the remote bookmark then silently show working-copy content instead.

Repro (see issue for full jj bookmark/log transcript):
1. Local bookmark cl/X and remote cl/X@piper point at the same change_id but different commit_ids (remote's is hidden=true).
2. Viewing files/diff for cl/X@piper in the IDE shows the working-copy commit's content instead of the actual target commit's content.
Also reproducible without Piper: create a working copy, note its change id, amend further, then diffbase/compare against the earlier change id (or revset `all() | <that change>`) — content compares as identical when it shouldn't.

Root cause (reporter's analysis, needs verification):
- TemplateParts.qualifiedChangeId / changeIdWithOffset only add change_offset when divergent(); a hidden older commit isn't divergent (only one visible commit shares its change ID) so it gets a bare change ID.
- CliLogService.bookmarkListTemplate (using normal_target) and the log/file-history templates build a ChangeId from that bare value.
- Later jj calls (-r/--from/--to) pass that change ID and jj resolves it to the currently visible commit.
- ChangeId equality compares only `full` (id + optional offset), so the hidden target compares equal to @.

Suggested fix directions from the report:
- Emit commit_id alongside change_id in templates, or add a hidden() branch to qualifiedChangeId.
- For hidden commits, use a Revision/ContentLocator based on commit_id for all jj calls.
- Make equality distinguish a hidden commit from the visible commit sharing its change ID.
- Add a test: remote bookmark pointing at a hidden commit (local bookmark amended after fetch).

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/130
design:
PLAN (conditional on spike jj-idea-29l3 findings (a)-(f); steps marked [spike] may change).

Code facts: ChangeId (jj/ChangeId.kt:7) is both `Revision` and `ContentLocator`; equality = `full` (id + optional "/offset"), so a hidden commit and the visible commit sharing its change id compare equal and render identical `-r` args. `CommitId` (jj/CommitId.kt) is already a `Revision`. LogEntry (jj/LogEntry.kt:12) already carries BOTH `id: ChangeId` and `commitId: CommitId`, so the data is already loaded for log rows; the gap is (1) bookmark/remote-bookmark targets and file-history rows that only build a ChangeId (CliLogService.bookmarkListTemplate / normal_target, lines ~346/508/562 use TemplateParts.qualifiedChangeId), and (2) read paths that pass `entry.id` where they should pass `entry.commitId`.
Principle (from the maintainer's 2026-10-01 note, adopted as the design): READS address by full commit_id; WRITES keep change id; no read/write optimistic lock.

Steps
1. Model: keep ChangeId as the identity for UI/selection; add commit-id parity - `Bookmark`/`BookmarkGroup` targets (jj/Revset.kt:23-46) gain `commitId: CommitId` next to `changeId`; templates emit `commit_id` alongside change_id via the existing `TemplateParts.commitId()` (TemplateParts.kt:21). [spike (f): confirm `commit_id`, `hidden` template keywords at JjVersion.MINIMUM].
2. Read-path switch: introduce `ReadLocator`/use `ContentLocator` implemented by CommitId (extend the sealed `ContentLocator` at Revset.kt:195 - it is sealed, so add `CommitId : ContentLocator`) and change these callers to pass commit ids: file show (JujutsuVirtualFile.fetch, JujutsuFileRevision.loadContent), diff/diffGitFile/diffSummary(Between) for the log details pane and diff-preview, file history rows, compare-with-branch (CompareFileWithBranchAction / compareWithRevisionAction.kt), diffbase resolution (jj/diffbase: resolve configured base to a commit_id once, then use it), annotate. Grep targets: `\.id` passed into `executor.show/diff*`, `ContentLocator` users (VcsExtensions.kt, JujutsuRevisionNumber.kt, JujutsuAnnotationProvider.kt, DiffRequestBuilder.kt). Hidden-commit reads now hit the right object. [spike (b)/(c): if a gc'd hidden commit errors, add a clear "commit no longer available" message instead of a stack trace]
3. Write path unchanged (change id with offset when divergent). Divergence protection inside the write command: on jj's divergent-change error text (exact string from spike (a)), surface a dialog "This change has become divergent - refresh and pick which version" and refresh the log; NEVER auto-retry. Centralise in the executor error mapping (jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt execute()) as a typed `CommandResult` failure kind rather than string-matching in each action.
4. Equality: do NOT change ChangeId.equals (it is used as a map key everywhere; making hidden != visible would fracture selection/refresh). Instead distinguish at the locator level (CommitId vs ChangeId) - the type system now says which one a read uses.
5. Regression test required by the bug: fixture repo - remote bookmark `cl/X@origin` at hidden a1, local `cl/X`/@ amended to a2; assert that diff/show/history for the remote bookmark return a1's content, not a2's. Contract test (real jj) + unit test on arg building (`-r <commit_id>` for reads, change id for writes).
6. Counter-proposal from the reporter (commit_id only when no longer latest) rejected per maintainer note: rule decided at log-read time is fragile (a change can become divergent/hidden before use).

Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Reads always commit_id, even for visible commits? Rec: yes (the maintainer's direction). Cost: after an external rewrite, an open diff shows the old version until refreshed - acceptable and correct ("what I clicked").
2. Q: Short commit-id prefixes? Rec: always use full ids in reads (spike (d)).
3. Q: Fix everything in one PR? Rec: two PRs: (A) bookmark targets + the specific bug repro paths; (B) remaining read paths + divergence error mapping.
Scale: adds one field per bookmark row and one template field; no new loop or traversal; template cost negligible (the jj walk dominates per jj-idea-2c8k). Operation-count test: bookmark list still one jj call.
Manual regression scope: MT-BOOKMARK, MT-DIFF, MT-DIFFBASE, MT-LOG-DETAILS, MT-LOG-REFRESH (stale-after-external-rewrite behaviour changes), MT-CROSS; >4 -> broad pass recommended (read paths are shared).
acceptance_criteria: Remote bookmark at a hidden commit shows that commit's diff/files/history; read paths use commit_id; writes still use change id; divergent-write error surfaces a refresh prompt without auto-retry; fixture regression test + contract test pass; spike findings reflected.
notes:
2026-10-01: SergejSalnikov (GH #130 comment) counter-proposes: commit IDs alone are fragile (external rewrites); use commit_id only when it is no longer the latest commit of its change (hidden = immutable snapshot), change ID otherwise. Maintainer analysis: any rule decided at log-read time is fragile (a non-divergent change can become divergent before use). Design direction: store full commit_id + change_id on every entry. Reads (diff, file show, history, compare) always use full commit_id. Writes keep the change ID (absorbs @ snapshots and ancestor rebases). Rejected: commit-ID optimistic lock for writes - check-then-write is not atomic, acting on a hidden commit creates divergence, and @ snapshots/ancestor rebases make it noisy. Divergence protection must come from inside the write command: on jj's divergent-change error, refresh and ask, never retry automatically. Blocked on spike jj-idea-29l3.
2026-10-01: Reporter (GH #130) agrees to start small. First case to fix is 'Compare with Another Commit...' with a manually typed revision (commit id of a past state of a change), which currently resolves to the latest commit. Use as first acceptance case, then widen to other read paths.

title: Review & land native image/binary diffs (GitHub PR #127)
description:
Contributor PR #127 (watbe) fixes historical file content being decoded as UTF-8 too early, which made binary/image diffs (e.g. PNGs) show as garbled text instead of using IntelliJ's native image diff viewer.

Approach: keep content as bytes until the platform decides file type — new CommandExecutor.showBytes/CliExecutor.executeBytes (draining stdout+stderr concurrently), ContentLogEntryImpl implementing ByteBackedContentRevision, DiffSideImpl using DiffContentFactory.createFromBytes for the historical side, and byte-based paths in JujutsuVirtualFile.fetch and JujutsuFileRevision.loadContent. text-only callers (annotate, merge-parent reconstruction, diffbase, split, open-in-remote) keep using the string-based show().

Author explicitly says 'I wouldn't merge this code as is' and flags two known gaps (see jj-idea bead for binary corruption in split, and merge-parent commits still reconstructing via text diff).

Review for: correctness of the concurrent stdout/stderr draining in executeBytes, whether execute()/executeBytes() should share more setup, coverage of the existing test suite (unit + FileShowBytesContractCliTest + HistoricalDiffContentPlatformTest, said to pass on 2025.1/2025.2/2026.2 on the author's fork), and CHANGELOG/docs/manual-tests.md entries already included in the diff (MT-DIFF, MT-DIFF-PREVIEW, MT-DIFFBASE regression scope).
design:
PLAN: this is a REVIEW bead for contributor PR #127 (522+/39-, 14 files, state OPEN, mergeable UNKNOWN, no CI statuses attached) - not an implementation design. Author says it is not merge-ready.
Review checklist (in order):
1. Fetch: `jj git fetch` the PR head or `gh pr checkout` is git-based - use `gh pr diff 127 -R kkkev/jj-idea` to read, and `jj new master` + apply patch / fetch the fork branch into a lane (jj-parallel-lanes skill) to run the tests. Do not push anything; any PR comment/merge needs the user's OK.
2. Concurrency core - CliExecutor.executeBytes (CliExecutor.kt, +101/-18): stdout and stderr must be drained on separate threads (or stderr redirected), else a >64KB stderr or stdout deadlocks; check timeout/cancellation kill the process and join readers, exit-code handling, and that stdout bytes are never passed through a charset. Check it shares setup with execute() (env, `--no-pager`, `--color=never`, JJ_* config, working dir, ignore-working-copy) - extract a common `startProcess()` rather than duplicating; this is the main "should share more setup" question in the bead.
3. Byte path wiring: `CommandExecutor.showBytes` (+14) interface addition -> StubCommandExecutor and every fake (test+contract) updated; ContentLogEntryImpl/ByteBackedContentRevision (JujutsuContentRevisions.kt) correct for `getContentAsBytes` and consistent with `getContent` for text (BOM/charset handling); DiffSideImpl `DiffContentFactory.createFromBytes(project, bytes, filePath)` - file-type detection by name vs content; JujutsuVirtualFile.fetch and JujutsuFileRevision.loadContent: memory (large binaries held in a cache? check any LRU/size cap - scale rule: a 200MB binary must not be cached/duplicated as both String and bytes), and that text callers (annotate, merge-parent reconstruction, diffbase, split, open-in-remote) still use string show().
4. Known gaps the author lists: binary corruption in split (jj-idea-qel6, DISCOVERED from this) and merge-parent commits still via text diff. Decide: accept as documented follow-ups (Rec) provided no regression vs master - verify a split of a PNG no worse than today.
5. Tests: run FileShowBytesContractCliTest (contract, real jj), HistoricalDiffContentPlatformTest (platform - author says passes on 2025.1/2025.2/2026.2; we also support 2025.3/2026.1 per build.gradle.kts verifier list - run on default), JujutsuContentRevisionsTest, JujutsuVirtualFileTest, JujutsuFileRevisionContentTest, then `./gradlew check`. CI shows no checks on the PR - run it ourselves.
6. Docs: PR includes CHANGELOG +1 and manual-tests +8; verify manual rows are under MT-DIFF/MT-DIFF-PREVIEW/MT-DIFFBASE and that Manual regression scope is those three plus MT-LOG-DETAILS (details-pane file diff) and MT-CTXMENU (file history Get/Compare). Attribution: keep the author's commits (jj squash keeps authorship only with --use-destination-message / preserve author; land via fetching their branch, rebasing, adding fixup commits on top rather than squashing, so credit is preserved).
7. Scale: confirm no new per-file loop: bytes fetched lazily per diff side, one jj call per side.
Outcome options: (A) request changes via review comments for specific blockers (draft text kept in notes; user posts), (B) take over: push fixup commits onto a branch based on theirs and land. Rec: B if only the shared-setup refactor and a size cap are needed (small), A if executeBytes has a deadlock.

Decisions made without the user: Rec B-or-A rule above; do not post/merge without approval.
acceptance_criteria: Review complete with written findings in notes; tests run locally incl. ./gradlew check; executeBytes concurrency verified; decision (request changes vs take over) recorded; if landed: author credit preserved, CHANGELOG + MT-DIFF/MT-DIFF-PREVIEW/MT-DIFFBASE updated.
notes: Review done. executeBytes: no deadlock (stdout/stderr drained concurrently); setup shared via commandLineFor/cmdNameFor. Gap fixed in fixup commit: reader joins now bounded by the command deadline, futures cancelled on failure. Wiring/text callers OK; no new loops (1 jj call per side). Known gaps accepted: split (jj-idea-qel6), merge-parent binary (jj-idea-1jli). PR commit imported via jj duplicate (author watbe kept) + my fixup on top. Tests: ./gradlew check, contractTest FileShowBytes (5/5), platformTest HistoricalDiff (5/5) all green. Pending: user 'finish', PR #127 comment/close needs approval.
close_reason: Landed PR #127 (author credit kept) + executeBytes timeout fixup; follow-up jj-idea-1jli

title: Squash/rebase dialogs: long source list pushes the picker off-screen (GitHub #125)
description:
Reported by aaronmallen (GitHub #125): squashing many commits at once makes the target-selection area disappear off the bottom of the dialog; workaround is to squash in smaller batches.

Root cause verified: createSourcePanel (ui/common/DialogHelpers.kt:32) builds an unbounded IconAwareHtmlPane and SquashIntoDialog places it in a BoxLayout topSection at BorderLayout.NORTH (SquashIntoDialog.kt ~369). With enough source entries it grows without limit and squeezes the CENTER content (the destination picker) down to zero height. The same createSourcePanel helper is shared by Split, Rebase, Duplicate and NewChange dialogs, so they likely have the same latent issue with enough entries.

Fix: wrap the fixed-side source list in a scroll pane capped at a handful of rows (e.g. ~5), still sizing to content for short lists so the common case is unchanged.

Needs: a platform test constructing the dialog with e.g. 50 source entries and asserting the picker/destination area retains non-zero height. Update docs/manual-tests.md (MT-SQUASH, and MT-REBASE if affected) with a step for a large source list.
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/125
close_reason: Closed

title: Settings not ignored
description: Jujutsu plugin settings are local, but they are stored in .idea/jujutsu.xml, which is not ignored by default. Perhaps these settings should be in .idea/workspace.xml?
design:
PLAN: stop JujutsuSettings (project-level) from landing in a VCS-visible file.

Facts: settings/JujutsuSettings.kt:21 `@Storage("jujutsu.xml")` (project-level => .idea/jujutsu.xml). JujutsuApplicationSettings.kt:18 also uses "jujutsu.xml" but application-level (config dir, roaming disabled) - unaffected, and its name only coincides.
Decision: move project settings to `StoragePathMacros.WORKSPACE_FILE` (`.idea/workspace.xml`), which the IDE itself marks as not-for-VCS and which JetBrains' default .gitignore templates exclude. Alternative (ship a .idea/.gitignore entry) rejected: jj tracks .idea by default and writing ignore files into a user's repo is intrusive.
Mechanics: `@Storage(StoragePathMacros.WORKSPACE_FILE)`. Existing users: the platform does NOT migrate between storages, so loadState would see defaults. Add a one-time migration: on first load with workspace storage empty, read the legacy file via `ProjectStorage`-free approach - simplest is keep a second tiny `@State(name="JujutsuSettings", storages=[Storage("jujutsu.xml", deprecated = true)])`: IntelliJ's `Storage(deprecated=true)` entries are read as a fallback and are removed on next save, which is exactly the supported migration path. Use `@Storage(value = WORKSPACE_FILE)` plus `@Storage(value = "jujutsu.xml", deprecated = true)` on the same @State; the existing settingsVersion migrations in loadState keep working unchanged.
Caveat to verify in a test: settings that are meant to be team-shared (is any field shared on purpose? audit JujutsuSettingsState: logChangeLimit, hideStandardCommitToolWindow, etc. are per-user prefs; confirm none is a project policy). If one is, split it into a second @State that stays in jujutsu.xml.
Also: users who already committed .idea/jujutsu.xml keep a stale tracked file; changelog line telling them it can be untracked/deleted.

Decisions made without the user
1. Q: workspace.xml vs a per-user `.idea/jujutsu.local.xml` + auto-ignore? Rec: workspace.xml (platform-standard, zero-config). Reverse: change the Storage value; deprecated fallback still reads both.
2. Q: Move the application-level file too? Rec: no, it's already user-local.

Testing: LightPlatform/ComponentManager test: write legacy jujutsu.xml, load, assert values; save, assert workspace.xml has them and jujutsu.xml is dropped. Manual: MT-SETTINGS (change a setting, restart, value persists; .idea/jujutsu.xml no longer appears in `jj st`). Scale: none.
acceptance_criteria: Project settings persist in workspace.xml; existing users' values migrate from jujutsu.xml automatically; .idea/jujutsu.xml no longer produced; migration test passes; CHANGELOG notes it; MT-SETTINGS re-run.
close_reason: Closed

title: Short feature-scoped preview access codes, mintable without a build (GitHub #69 early access)
description:
kkkev wants to give GitHub #69's reporter (cYDN48) early access to PAGED_LOG_LOAD only, and more generally to mint preview-feature access codes for any feature combination at any time without cutting a new plugin release.

Today's AccessCode (preview/AccessCode.kt) checks a salted SHA-256 hash against a flat list shipped in preview/access-codes.txt - every new code needs a release, and any valid code unlocks every PreviewFeature via the settings checkboxes (no per-code scoping).

Chosen design: short truncated-HMAC codes (format JJP1), 16 characters after the prefix, e.g. JJP1-ABCD-EFGH-JKMN-PQRS. Payload (4 bytes): features:u8 bitmap (bit 7 = ALL, includes future features), expiry:u8 (months since 2026-01, 0=never), serial:u16 (uniqueness/attribution/revocation). Tag: HMAC-SHA256(key, "JJP1"+payload) truncated to 6 bytes, base32 (Crockford) encoded together with the payload.

An Ed25519-signed alternative was considered and rejected: its 64-byte signature pushes codes to 88-117 characters, and it only defends against someone decompiling the jar to mint their own codes - moot while the existing -Djjidea.preview.<id>=true system property already bypasses the whole gate (AccessCode's own docs: "noise reduction, not DRM").

The HMAC key is kept out of the public repo entirely: injected at release build time from a GitHub Actions secret (PREVIEW_CODE_KEY) into a generated resource, so it exists only in the shipped jar, on kkkev's machine, and in a password manager. A companion minting CLI (Gradle tools source set, never shipped in the plugin) lets kkkev mint/inspect codes offline against the local copy of the key, with no new build.

See the full design in the plan file this was executed from (triage-latest-github-issue-velvet-russell.md) for the exact API shapes (PreviewCode.kt codec, AccessCode.grant()/grantedFeatures(), settings UI status line, revoked-serials.txt, build.gradle.kts key-injection task, minting tool commands) and the private GitLab-wiki registry of issued codes.
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/69 (early-access request follow-up)
close_reason: Implemented JJP1 signed access codes (PreviewCode.kt/AccessCode.kt/settings UI), key injection, minting CLI, and private code registry. ./gradlew check green.

title: Graduate paged log loading (PAGED_LOG_LOAD) out of preview, on by default (GitHub #69)
description:
GitHub #69 retest on 0.8.17 (cYDN48, log limit 10,000, ~7,000-commit repo): a simple write op still takes several seconds to show in the log. Reporter measured 'time jj log -r "all()" --no-pager' at ~3s standalone - about the same as the plugin's refresh time - and suggested looking at how IntelliJ's git4idea handles large repos for inspiration.

Analysis: this matches docs/design/jj-idea-2c8k-paged-log-loading.md's Phase 1 finding - jj's own per-invocation walk over N commits is the dominant cost and barely depends on the template, so no amount of plugin-side optimization beats jj's own ~3s walk if the plugin still re-reads the whole configured window on every write. The fix for exactly this (frontier-cursor paged loading, so a write only re-fetches page 1 instead of the whole limit) was built and shipped as jj-idea-2c8k, but landed behind PreviewFeature.PAGED_LOG_LOAD (preview/PreviewFeature.kt), which defaults off and requires an access code via PreviewEntitlement - so the reporter's 0.8.17 retest was still on the old full-reload path. The 0.8.17 graph work (xi58/1pgy/sc8m/jnqi, GitHub #69's O(n^2) merge/layout fix) addressed plugin-side rendering cost, not this.

git4idea's approach (a persistent on-disk commit index, refreshed incrementally from known heads rather than re-walked) is the prior art the reporter pointed at; paged loading is the plugin's equivalent mechanism, already built.

Scope: review the paged-log-loading design doc's Status section (elided-parent paint treatment, cross-refs to jj-idea-hlu3/jj-idea-xi58) as graduation criteria, close out any remaining items, then flip PAGED_LOG_LOAD to on-by-default and remove the preview gate once satisfied. No new filesystem/per-commit traversal is introduced by this bead itself - it turns on an already-scale-tested path (PagedLogWindowTest, PagedLogWindowContractTest, JujutsuLogTableModelRowOfScaleTest per the design doc's Status section).
design:
PLAN: graduate PAGED_LOG_LOAD (bit 1 of PreviewFeature, preview/PreviewFeature.kt) to default-on.

Single gate site: ui/log/UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:95 `private val pagedLoading = PreviewEntitlement...isEnabled(PreviewFeature.PAGED_LOG_LOAD)`. The test references (PagedLogDeepPageRefreshTest, PagedLogRevsetChangeTest, PagedLogLoaderConcurrencyTest) must stop depending on the entitlement.

Step 0 - graduation checklist (do first; each item verified, result recorded in notes):
 1. Design-doc open items (docs/design/jj-idea-2c8k-paged-log-loading.md): elided-parent paint treatment (shipped as the faded NOT_LOADED stub; see jj-idea-hlu3 / xi58 / sc8m), the "hard ceiling above ~8-12k heads" case: decide the fallback when `heads()` exceeds the ceiling (Rec: fall back to the legacy full-window load for that repo with an INFO log + one-time notification, never an error). Confirm that fallback exists in code; if not, it is a blocker -> implement it under this bead.
 2. Bug 6 in the doc ("refresh() vs forceRefresh()" had no regression test): add the targeted test now - a simulated `logRefresh` notify must invoke `dataLoader.refresh()` and never `forceRefresh()`. Blocker.
 3. Re-run contractTests (PagedLogWindowContractTest) against min jj and current jj.
 4. Re-measure on jj-stress-test (scripts/fixtures/fx-stress.sh SCALE=7000): write op -> log updated latency, record before/after in notes (target: independent of log limit; the #69 reporter's ~3s should drop to one page's cost).
 5. Confirm 2570.5 (stub auto-paging) is NOT a blocker: stubs stay clickable (sc8m), so graduation can precede it; it is the follow-up that smooths the UX. Rec: ship graduation first, 2570.5 next release. Reverse: add 2570.5 to the blocker list.
Step 1 - remove the gate: delete the `PAGED_LOG_LOAD` enum entry but KEEP bit 1 reserved (comment in PreviewFeature.kt "bit 1 retired: never reuse", per its own kdoc rule); delete its bundle keys preview.pagedLogLoad.*; drop `pagedLoading` branches in UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader (keep the legacy full-load path ONLY if step 1.1's heads-ceiling fallback needs it - then the condition becomes "heads exceed ceiling", not an entitlement).
Step 2 - settings: Preview-features group (see jj-idea-jxii item 3) - coordinate: if CONFLICT_GUTTER is still previewed the group stays. Whichever of this bead / jxii lands second must handle the empty-group case; note that in both beads.
Step 3 - tests/docs: tests that set the property or entitlement for paging now run by default; PreviewEntitlementTest/PreviewCodeTest fixtures (they use DRAG_AND_DROP/PAGED_LOG_LOAD as samples) need a surviving sample - use CONFLICT_GUTTER or a test-only enum constructed via a seam. Condense docs/preview-changelog.md entry into CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] ("Large repos: log updates after a change no longer re-read the whole log"). Update README/ROADMAP; update docs/manual-tests.md MT-LOG-REFRESH / MT-LOG-TABLE (remove "requires access code" preconditions).

Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Graduate before 2570.5 (stub auto-paging)? Rec: yes (see above).
2. Q: Keep the legacy path as a fallback? Rec: only for the heads-ceiling case.
3. Q: Release in same version as DnD graduation (jxii)? Rec: either; no code dependency except the settings-group edge case.
Scale: removes an O(limit) per-write path for everyone; adds none. No new traversal. Existing scale tests (PagedLogWindowTest, JujutsuLogTableModelRowOfScaleTest) remain and run unconditionally.
Manual regression scope: MT-LOG-REFRESH, MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-GRAPH (stubs at page boundaries), MT-LOG-FILTER (filtered paging), MT-SETTINGS (preview group); >4 sections -> shared log surface, recommend a broader log pass.
acceptance_criteria: Paged loading is the default for all users with no access code; heads-ceiling fallback verified; refresh-vs-forceRefresh regression test exists; stress-repo write latency recorded; PreviewFeature bit 1 retired and documented; CHANGELOG/docs/MT updated; ./gradlew check green.
notes:
Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/69#issuecomment-5799420694
2026-10-03 (from jj-idea-2570.5): paged loading now uses a fixed 500-row page (PagedLogWindow.PAGE_ROWS), decoupled from 'Changes to show'; that setting is the hard limit for the non-paged path only (flag off / implicit default revset / >8000 heads / fetch failure). Decide at graduation whether to remove it from Settings or relabel it as the fallback limit ('Changes to load when paging is unavailable', Advanced), and update the preview.pagedLogLoad / settings.log.limit.comment texts accordingly. Also no CHANGELOG entry until graduation (see 2570.5); graduation needs one.

Graduation checklist (changelog, preview-changelog, release summary, ROADMAP/README, manual tests, minor bump plan): see docs/design/graduating-preview-features.md - single source of truth.

title: Bookmarks panel truncates closest-bookmark label at the widget's fixed char cap and drops '+n' (GitHub #107)
description:
GitHub #107 (cYDN48), on the new dangling-heads feature (jj-idea-lig7): long bookmark names (or multiple names) in the bookmarks panel's 'Unbookmarked heads' rows get cut off early even when there's plenty of horizontal space, and when truncated the '+n' suffix disappears entirely too.

Root cause (verified): danglingHeadLabel() (ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkTreeModel.kt:362) calls bookmarkWidgetText() (actions/bookmark/BookmarkMenu.kt:109) to render the '[closest] +n' text - the same helper used for the fixed-width toolbar bookmark widget. bookmarkWidgetText hard-caps the *entire* composed string (names + ' +n' + capped marker) at MAX_WIDGET_TEXT_LENGTH characters and appends '…', so a long name pushes the '+n' out of the truncated string entirely. This is correct for the toolbar widget (genuinely fixed-width) but wrong for the bookmarks panel tree, which has variable available width and should lay out/truncate by pixel width like the rest of the tree, not by a constant char count.

Scope:
1. Bookmarks panel working-copy and dangling-head rows (JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt, BookmarkTreeModel.kt) must not go through bookmarkWidgetText's fixed char cap - truncate against actual available pixel width instead (reuse existing FragmentLayout/TextCanvas truncation helpers used elsewhere in the panel).
2. Truncation (in both the panel and the toolbar widget) should only ever shorten the bookmark *names* portion, never drop the trailing ' +n' (and capped '+' marker).
3. Unit test: bookmarkWidgetText with a long name list still contains the '+n' suffix.

No filesystem/per-commit loop added; O(1) per row, no scale-test needed. UI-affecting: update docs/manual-tests.md for the bookmarks panel section and report manual smoke steps + MT-* regression scope per contributing.md.
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/107#issuecomment-5798875755
close_reason: Fixed: bookmarkWidgetText now truncates only the names portion, never the +n suffix; panel rows pass maxLength=Int.MAX_VALUE

title: Redesign @-drag zones, drag-scope picker, live moved-row highlight
description: Follow-up refinement to the closed jj-idea-pk2c (@ drag) and jj-idea-j8ij (drag-scope) beads after manual UX review: (1) replace the @ drag's modal immutable-target dialog with zone semantics (drop on commit=edit, drop in band above=jj new, always allowed); (2) replace the View Options checkbox-radio hack with a toolbar ComboBoxAction; (3) live-highlight the rows a -s/-b drag would move, reusing the already-computed moved-id set and the existing GraphNode.highlightColor mechanism.
close_reason: Redesigned @-drag onto zones (edit/new-on-top), drag-scope picker onto a toolbar ComboBoxAction, and added a live moved-row highlight during -s/-b drags, per manual UX review of jj-idea-pk2c/jj-idea-j8ij's shipped behavior

title: [bug] Bogus ahead count for a local bookmark tracking a remote ref that doesn't exist on the remote
description:
cYDN48 (GitHub #110, 2026-09-18): a brand-new local bookmark showed as 1000+ commits ahead of origin, with a dashed/faded remote entry. Reporter traced the trigger to their own jj config:

    [remotes.origin]
    auto-track-created-bookmarks = "*"

which creates and tracks <bookmark>@origin at creation time, before the bookmark has ever been pushed. kkkev confirmed publicly (2026-09-20) that this is still a plugin bug and asked the reporter to put that config back once fixed - it is a legitimate thing to want.

This is the MIRROR IMAGE of jj-idea-lc43, and that fix does NOT cover it:
- lc43 / zeroedIfLocalDeleted (jj/Revset.kt:152) handles a remote row whose LOCAL side is absent (jj bookmark delete leaves foo@origin measuring from the absent local ref back to the repo root).
