- This bead is the opposite: the local ref is real, but the tracked foo@origin ref is absent ON THE REMOTE, so jj measures from that absent remote ref to the root instead. Same meaningless root-distance number, opposite side, so zeroedIfLocalDeleted never fires.
- Bookmark.withDivergenceFrom (jj/Revset.kt:129) then swaps the remote row's counts onto the local bookmark, propagating the bogus number to the local row too - which is why it shows up on the local bookmark in the panel.

Agreed UX (stated on the issue): show NO arrow and NO number for a bookmark tracking a remote ref that does not exist on the remote, rather than inventing a direction. Deliberately not 'arrow without a number meaning needs pushing' - that would assume every local bookmark is destined to be pushed.
design:
The data needed is already parsed: bookmarkListTemplate emits a per-row 'present' boolean (jj/cli/CliLogService.kt:523, consumed at :537). So the correction is symmetric to the existing one and sits right next to it in jj/Revset.kt:

    fun Bookmark.zeroedIfRemoteAbsent(): Bookmark =
        if (isRemote && tracked && !present) copy(aheadCount = 0, behindCount = 0) else this

applied BEFORE withDivergenceFrom, so the local row derives from corrected remote rows. Check whether Bookmark currently carries 'present' through from the parse - if it is only used to build the row and then dropped, it needs threading onto the model.

Also confirm the intended rendering: an absent-on-remote tracked row should show no indicator at all, and the local bookmark deriving from it should fall back to 0/0 (no chip), in BOTH the panel (BookmarkTreeModel.toRollup, ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkTreeModel.kt:249) and the log chips (ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:132).

Tests: unit coverage in the Revset/bookmark tests for tracked-but-absent remote rows, alongside the existing lc43 cases, including the roll-up path so a collapsed remote group doesn't resurrect the number.

Related: jj-idea-ks5k (divergent panel vs log numbers), jj-idea-spt6 (per-remote notation), jj-idea-uyu9 (tooltips) - all three remain open and were restated to the reporter on 2026-09-20.
close_reason: Fixed via LogService.withDerivedDivergence (jj/BookmarkDivergence.kt): one shared derivation computed once per repo (JujutsuStateModel.references) feeds both the bookmarks panel and the log table's bookmark chips, so they always agree. Conflicted/divergent local bookmarks now get exact bidirectional counts via bounded revset queries instead of jj's one-directional tracking_ahead/behind_count hint (confirmed empirically against jj 0.44.0). A remote ref absent on the remote (jj-idea-j58e) is zeroed and excluded from derivation - no arrow, no number. The git pseudo-remote is now hidden from log chips too (jj-idea-e4ln), matching the panel. ./gradlew check green; contractTest/stubTest green against real jj.

title: Move '<bookmark>' to Change... dialog doesn't register undo
description: moveBookmarkToChangeAction.kt's executeMoveToChange runs 'jj bookmark set' via repo.createCommand{...}.onSuccess{...}.onFailure{...}.executeAsync() but never calls .addUndoTracking(...), unlike the sibling moveBookmarkAction.kt's executeMove (used by 'Move Bookmark Here...' and drag-and-drop), which does. Net effect: moving a bookmark via 'Move <bookmark> to Change...' succeeds but shows no undo balloon and isn't undoable via the plugin's undo action, unlike every other bookmark-move path. Found by manual retest of jj-idea-t7cz.
close_reason: Fixed: executeMoveToChange in moveBookmarkToChangeAction.kt now calls .addUndoTracking("action.bookmark.moveTo.undo"), matching moveBookmarkAction.kt's executeMove. Landed alongside jj-idea-t7cz. ./gradlew check green.

title: Auto-refresh dead in secondary jj workspaces: .jj/repo is a file, not a directory
description:
Split from jj-idea-ul3o's cause (b), which is confirmed and fixable without any polling infrastructure (unlike ul3o's cause (a), which is deferred behind a shared poller — see jj-idea-<polling-bead>).

In a secondary jj workspace (jj workspace add), <root>/.jj/repo is a *regular file* whose contents are the shared repo's .jj/repo path, relative to <root>/.jj/ (verified: contains e.g. ../../jj-idea/.jj/repo). Consequences in JujutsuStateModel.kt:
- watchOpHeads (line 546-558) builds its watch path as ${repo.directory.path}/.jj/repo/op_heads via OP_HEADS_RELATIVE_PATH — this directory does not exist for a secondary workspace, so nothing is watched and refreshAndFindFileByPath materializes nothing.
- isOpHeadsChange (line 560-562) additionally requires the event file to be an ancestor-relative path under the repo root, which the real (shared) op_heads directory is not — so even a delivered event would be filtered out.

Fix: when <root>/.jj/repo is a regular file (not a directory), read and resolve its contents against <root>/.jj/ to find the real repo directory, then watch <resolved>/op_heads instead of <root>/.jj/repo/op_heads. Match events by whether they fall under the resolved path(s) rather than by ancestry under the workspace root. Default (non-workspace) repos are unaffected — .jj/repo is already a directory there.

Reported via GitHub #115 (SergejSalnikov); this is the workspace-layout half of that report, distinct from the network-mount watcher-reliability half.
close_reason: Closed

title: Extract ChangeIdentity (repo+ChangeId) into jj/ from GraphableEntry
description: Pure refactor ahead of dnd-batch-4: extract a strict repo+ChangeId identity concept (ChangeIdentity) into jj/, have GraphableEntry extend it, dedupe LogClickTarget's redundant repo fields, and replace hand-written ChangeKey(entry.repo, entry.id) call sites with entry.key. No behaviour change. See docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md and the do-dnd-batch-4 plan.
close_reason: Extracted ChangeIdentity into jj/, adopted by GraphableEntry and LogClickTarget dedup

title: Bookmarks panel doesn't zero jj's garbage ahead/behind count for an absent-local remote row
description:
cYDN48 (GitHub #110, 2026-09-15): saw a brand-new bookmark reported as 1000+ commits ahead of origin, with the remote-side entry shown with a dotted outline. Not reproducible at home.

Diagnosable from existing code, not just a report to sit on: when a local bookmark has no target, jj reports the remote row's tracking_ahead_count as the distance from the absent local to the repo root - a known artifact already corrected on the log path by enrichWithDeletedBookmarks (ui/log/UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:561-577), which zeroes the counts and injects a deleted=true local bookmark. The bookmarks panel has no equivalent correction: buildRepoNodes (ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkTreeModel.kt:143-200) builds remote leaves straight from refs.bookmarks with no such cleanup.

The reporter's 'dotted outline' matches exactly how a deleted bookmark renders elsewhere (JujutsuIcons.BookmarkDeleted + strikethrough, ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:118,137) - so their 'brand new' bookmark most likely reused a name whose remote-tracking row still existed from a previous, now-deleted local bookmark.

Fix: lift enrichWithDeletedBookmarks' correction (or an equivalent) into shared code the bookmarks panel path also uses, so a remote-only stale row never surfaces a meaningless huge ahead count in the panel either.
close_reason: Pushed

title: Divergent bookmark's ahead/behind numbers disagree between panel and log
description:
cYDN48 (GitHub #110, 2026-09-15 retest, with screenshot): for a divergent/conflicted bookmark the up/down arrow numbers shown in the bookmarks panel differ from those shown in the log, and neither the direction nor the number is intuitive. Reporter expects the counts a non-divergent bookmark at the local position would show (their example: up 1, down 2).

Touches Bookmark.withDivergenceFrom (jj/Revset.kt, used by the panel via BookmarkTreeModel.buildRepoNodes) vs. CliLogService.localBookmarkTemplate, which per jj-idea-spt6's notes still doesn't compute local-bookmark divergence for the log's bookmark chips at all. Needs a single, shared definition of a divergent local bookmark's ahead/behind so panel and log agree.

Linked: jj-idea-spt6 (per-remote divergence notation follow-up), same underlying representation gap.
close_reason: Fixed via LogService.withDerivedDivergence (jj/BookmarkDivergence.kt): one shared derivation computed once per repo (JujutsuStateModel.references) feeds both the bookmarks panel and the log table's bookmark chips, so they always agree. Conflicted/divergent local bookmarks now get exact bidirectional counts via bounded revset queries instead of jj's one-directional tracking_ahead/behind_count hint (confirmed empirically against jj 0.44.0). A remote ref absent on the remote (jj-idea-j58e) is zeroed and excluded from derivation - no arrow, no number. The git pseudo-remote is now hidden from log chips too (jj-idea-e4ln), matching the panel. ./gradlew check green; contractTest/stubTest green against real jj.

title: Move Bookmark Here excludes the bookmark's current change, blocking divergent-resolve
description:
cYDN48 (GitHub #121): after fetching remote changes, a divergent bookmark can't be moved to the change it was already on before the divergence via right-click -> Move Bookmark Here..., because that's the natural resolution.

Root cause confirmed in src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/actions/bookmark/MoveBookmarkToChangeDialog.kt:429 (and the incremental candidate path at :362), both of which do entries.filter { it.id != currentId }. That's correct for a single-target bookmark (moving to its own target would be a no-op), but wrong for a conflicted/divergent bookmark, where currentId is only one of several targets and re-pointing at it is a legitimate resolve.

Fix: when the bookmark is divergent (multiple targets), don't exclude a candidate purely for being one of the bookmark's existing targets; word/label it so it reads as a resolve action rather than a no-op move.
notes: Root cause is actually two paths: (1) BookmarkClassifier.eligible (the 'Move Bookmark Here...' path the reporter hit) drops a bookmark whose targets[0] equals the clicked change; (2) MoveBookmarkToChangeDialog's currentId exclusion, as originally noted. Fixing both.
close_reason: Fixed: BookmarkClassifier.eligible/classify and MoveBookmarkToChangeDialog now read every target of a divergent bookmark (RefItem.targets, jj-idea-bico) instead of only the first, and a new MoveDirection.RESOLVE lets a candidate that is one of the bookmark's own targets be selected without ticking 'Allow backward or sideways move'. Applies to both Move Bookmark Here... and Move '<bookmark>' to Change.... ./gradlew check green.

title: Conflict editor banner: live block count + Accept side actions
description:
Upgrade ui/editor/JujutsuConflictEditorNotificationProvider.kt from a static 'This file has merge conflicts [Resolve]' banner into one that reflects jj's actual incremental-resolution model: live conflict-block count parsed from the editor Document (decrements as the user hand-edits markers, disappears once the last block is gone, independent of ChangeListManager's binary MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS status), model-accurate copy, an 'Accept <side-1 label>' / 'Accept <side-2 label>' pair of action links using ExtractedConflict.currentTitle/lastTitle for labels (GitHub #112) routed through CommandExecutor.resolve(paths, ":ours"/":theirs") - the same call JujutsuMergeProvider.acceptFilesRevisions already makes, so modify/delete conflicts correctly delete rather than leaving empty content - and a secondary 'Open Merge Tool' link that keeps calling the existing resolveConflicts(project, files) funnel (actions/change/workingCopyConflicts.kt:30) unchanged.

See docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md section S1. Bind the live count to a DocumentListener with a debounce (same 300ms-class pattern as JujutsuStateModel.scheduleRepositoryRefresh), not a naive per-keystroke rescan.
close_reason: Implemented S1 (live block count + Accept side actions) in JujutsuConflictEditorNotificationProvider; new unit tests all green (targeted run) and ktlintCheck clean. Full ./gradlew check blocked in this session by a shared IJPGP platform-cache corruption from concurrent jj-parallel-lanes usage (see layoutindex-race-parallel-lanes memory) — recommend re-running ./gradlew check once resolved.

title: Populate JujutsuConflictRegistry for arbitrary revisions, not just working copy
description:
jj/ChangeService.kt:68 conflictedPathsFor re-implements jj resolve --list path extraction by hand instead of reusing ConflictInfoParser.parse(...).keys (which vcs/changes/JujutsuChangeProvider.kt:196 parseConflictPaths already does), and discards the sides/deletions shape entirely. Net effect: JujutsuConflictRegistry (jj/conflict/JujutsuConflictRegistry.kt) is only ever populated for the working copy, never for a historical revision. Fold conflictedPathsFor onto ConflictInfoParser and feed the parsed ConflictInfo into the registry for the revision being processed, not just WorkingCopy. Prerequisite for jj-idea-n6fz's S3 (Conflicts view) and S4 (resolve at any revision), which both need modify/delete shape data at non-@ revisions.

Scale note: this changes per-log-entry work already inside the existing per-revision loop in ChangeService (gated on entry.hasConflict) - no new per-file/per-commit loop is added, so no new operation-count test is required, but confirm with a quick check that registry writes stay O(conflicted paths at that revision), not O(all log entries).
close_reason: Registry now keyed by revision (WC slot pinned, LRU-32 for others); ChangeService.conflictInfosFor reuses ConflictInfoParser instead of the whitespace hand-parser, fixing conflicted paths with spaces at historical revisions.

title: Spike: is interactive conflict resolution safe at a non-@ revision?
description:
jj resolve -r <rev> and jj file show -r <rev> already work and are already exercised read-only by JujutsuConflictDiffRequestProvider (GitHub #119 / jj-idea-ct7e). JujutsuMergeProvider.loadConflict is hard-coded to WorkingCopy though (see its own doc comment, JujutsuMergeProvider.kt:47-51), which is why actions/change/resolveConflictsAvailability.kt has a NEEDS_EDIT state (visible+disabled) for any conflicted commit other than @ - a git-shaped 'you can only resolve what's checked out' restriction jj itself doesn't have.

Timeboxed spike, not a feature: prototype interactive write-back (resolve one file's markers, write result) targeting an arbitrary revision, and answer in writing: (1) does resolving a conflict at a non-@ revision correctly rebase every descendant that inherited the conflict, matching jj resolve -r's CLI behavior, and does the UI need to warn about that before the user commits to the action? (2) does the existing invalidate/refresh machinery (JujutsuRepository.invalidate) correctly refresh a log view for revisions far from @? Deliverable is a written recommendation (design doc addendum or beads note), not shipped UI. See docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md section S4.
notes: S4 spike complete. Findings appended to docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md under '### S4 spike findings (jj-idea-cf2c)' (between S4 and S5). Q1: resolving at non-@ propagates to descendants correctly (change ids stable, commit ids rewritten); if @ is a descendant it is silently rewritten underneath the user — UI must warn for that case specifically, not uniformly. Q2: invalidate()'s logRefresh path is a deliberate page-1-only reconcile (jj-idea-2c8k/GitHub #69) — a resolved row on an already-loaded page 2+ stays stale until an explicit forceRefresh; S4 feature needs to call forceRefresh (or patch the row in place) after an off-page resolve. Verdict: go, with conditions (descendant warning + deep-page refresh fix). Landed as production plumbing: resolveArgs/CommandExecutor.resolve gained a configArgs param, DiffEditTool.mergeToolConfigArgs + diffedit/MergeApplyMain.kt prototype the ephemeral-merge-tool write-back mechanism, proven end-to-end against real jj 0.44 via two new contract CLI tests (ResolveAtRevisionContractCliTest, ResolveWriteBackContractCliTest). No action/banner/NEEDS_EDIT changes — that's the follow-on S4 feature's scope. Also corrected doc's stale registry-gap claim (already fixed). ./gradlew check green; ./gradlew contractTest green for all new tests (one unrelated pre-existing failure, LogContractCliTest bookmark-field formatting, confirmed unrelated).
close_reason: Spike complete: written recommendation delivered in docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md § S4 spike findings, backed by 2 real-jj contract tests. Go-with-conditions verdict for retiring NEEDS_EDIT.

title: Split dialog: name sides by identity, not position, in all modes
description:
GitHub #101 follow-up (after jj-idea-o6sw). The parallel-mode preview title fix made wording
internally consistent but the UX is still confusing: the dialog names its two sides by DAG
POSITION and the nouns change per mode (Parent/Child, First/Second, Here/New commit), when the
real invariant is by IDENTITY — unticked always stays on the existing change ID, ticked always
moves to a brand-new commit; only the new commit's position varies (child/sibling/parent).

Redesign: identity-first labels ("Stays on <id>" / "New commit (child of|sibling of|parent of
<id>)") shared across all three modes, replacing Parent/Child/First/Second/Here entirely. Add a
live mode note (mirroring the existing working-copy note) stating the resulting shape, including
that existing children become merges of both siblings in parallel mode. Verify and fix the
working-copy note for parallel mode with new contract tests (no --parallel coverage exists in
MutatingCommandsContractTest today). Clean up now-dead bundle keys.

See plan at ~/.claude/plans/fix-jj-idea-o6sw-jolly-squirrel.md for full design and rationale.
close_reason: Identity-first labels (Stays on <id> / New commit child-of|sibling-of|parent-of <id>) shared across all three split modes, live mode note, working-copy note verified correct for --parallel via new contract tests, dead bundle keys removed

title: CI guard: CHANGELOG's newest released section must only name commits that predate its own release tag
description:
2026-09-13 incident: two bookmarks-panel CHANGELOG entries under the [0.8.15] heading (git
pseudo-remote removal + collapse/persist-expansion, commits b14d47f3/953729c3) were actually
authored ~3 hours AFTER v0.8.15 was tagged and published (e652fd99, 2026-09-07 10:34 UTC) - i.e.
they were never actually released in 0.8.15, despite the CHANGELOG saying so.

This caused real damage: two GitHub reporters (cYDN48 on #110 and #111) were told to retest
against "0.8.15" for behavior that didn't exist in that build, wasting a round trip for both and
for the maintainer. Confirmed via `jj file show -r v0.8.15 <path>` showing neither change present,
and via `jj log -T 'author.timestamp()'` on the two commits vs. the release's published_at/
target_commitish (from `gh api repos/.../releases`).

## How this likely happened
The release/tag process and the CHANGELOG-section-heading process are apparently not the same
gate - it's possible to keep committing under a `## [X.Y.Z]` heading (rather than `[Unreleased]`)
after the tag for X.Y.Z has already been cut, if the two steps aren't atomic or aren't checked
against each other.

## Fix direction
Add a CI check (or extend the existing "finish" checklist per this project's CLAUDE.md) that, for
the most recent released section in CHANGELOG.md, resolves the release's tag commit and verifies
every commit that touches CHANGELOG.md under that heading is an ancestor of (or is) that tag
commit - fail the build/check if a commit postdating the tag is found under an already-released
heading. Alternatively/additionally: the release process itself could freeze that CHANGELOG
section's content at tag time (e.g. copy it into the GitHub Release body verbatim, which IS
already done - build.gradle.kts's extractChangelogNotes - and diff it against the CHANGELOG's
current text for that version to catch drift after the fact, in case prevention isn't practical).
acceptance_criteria: A CI check (or documented finish-checklist step) fails or warns when the CHANGELOG's most recently released version section contains an entry from a commit that isn't an ancestor of that version's release tag. Verified against the 2026-09-13 incident as a regression case (the two now-corrected entries should trip the check if reintroduced under [0.8.15]).
close_reason: CI guard shipped: ChangelogReleaseGuard/ChangelogReleaseDriftTest fail ./gradlew check if the newest released CHANGELOG section gains an entry absent at its tag; opt-out marker documented in contributing.md

title: Split rejects a hunks-only selection ("Move at least one file to the child")
description:
When splitting a change, ticking zero whole files but picking individual hunks from one or more
files (via "Pick Hunks...") is rejected with "Move at least one file to the child" - hunk-only
splits should work.

## Root cause
SplitDialog.doValidate() (ui/split/SplitDialog.kt:545-556) rejects included.isEmpty()
(fileSelection.includedChanges, i.e. FULLY ticked files) unconditionally - it never consults
firstCommitOverrides (the map of per-file partial/hunk selections). The very next validation
branch, a few lines below (line 557: `if (included.size == total && firstCommitOverrides.isEmpty())`),
DOES consult firstCommitOverrides - so the omission on the first branch looks like a plain
oversight rather than intentional.

applyPickedContent() (lines 313-341) deliberately leaves the tick state untouched for a genuine
partial pick ("the tick is inert once an override exists... Force-ticking a partial file here
previously made a half-picked file look fully committed to the child, which wasn't true") - so a
hunks-only split is EXACTLY the state (included.isEmpty() but firstCommitOverrides non-empty) that
the first validation branch wrongly treats as "nothing selected."

## Fix
Add a firstCommitOverrides.isNotEmpty() escape to the included.isEmpty() branch in doValidate().

## Also verify
doOKAction() (lines 575-600) computes selectedPaths from ticked/unticked sets and only builds
hunkSelection via buildHunkSelection() when `!newParent && firstCommitOverrides.isNotEmpty()`
(line 583) - confirm this path produces the correct split when ZERO files are fully ticked and
only overrides exist (not just the already-covered "some ticked + some overridden" case).
acceptance_criteria: Splitting with zero fully-ticked files but one or more files partially picked via 'Pick Hunks...' succeeds instead of being rejected. Test covers 'nothing ticked, one file partially picked' end to end (doValidate + doOKAction).
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/117
close_reason: Fixed: doValidate() now consults firstCommitOverrides via new isPartialSplit guard, matching Squash's existing isPartialSquash pattern

title: Conflicted file's diff from the log always fails for any commit but the working copy
description:
## Steps to Reproduce (confirmed via code reading + a repro script, 2026-09-13)
```sh
jj git init /tmp/conflict-repro && cd /tmp/conflict-repro
printf 'base\n' > f.txt && jj describe -m base && jj new -m A
printf 'A side\n' > f.txt && jj new -r 'description("base")' -m B    # sibling of A
printf 'B side\n' > f.txt
jj rebase -r 'description("A")' -d 'description("B")'                # A is now conflicted
jj new 'description("B")'                                            # @ is a clean sibling of A
```
Double-click f.txt in commit A's diff in the log -> "Cannot show diff: Could not extract conflict
data from f.txt".

## Root cause
JujutsuMergeProvider.loadConflict() (vcs/merge/JujutsuMergeProvider.kt:47-56) resolves conflict
content via createContentRevision(filePath, WorkingCopy) -> CurrentContentRevision(filePath)
(jj/JujutsuRepository.kt:139-141), i.e. the bytes ON DISK, with file.contentsToByteArray() as
fallback - it never consults the commit whose diff was actually opened.

ChangeService.loadChanges() (jj/ChangeService.kt:37-64) stamps FileStatus.MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS
on a conflicted path for EVERY log entry that has one, not just @. The platform routes any such
change through createMergeRequest -> vcs.getMergeProvider().loadRevisions(file)
(intellij-community ChangeDiffRequestProducer.java:271,328), which calls loadConflict().

Net effect: the three-pane diff only produces anything at all when the SAME file is currently
conflicted in the working copy, regardless of which commit's diff you opened - and even then it
shows the working copy's conflict, not the clicked commit's. Sitting on a clean commit elsewhere
in the graph (the normal position when browsing the log to understand a past conflict) means
there's nothing on disk to parse, hence the error every time.

## Why it "worked exactly once" (reporter's words)
If @ is an ancestor-inheriting descendant of the conflicted commit (jj propagates conflicts
downward), @ carries the same markers, and the panes happen to be correct by coincidence - not
because the revision was actually respected.

## Fix direction
Make the conflict content revision-scoped: read the conflicted file at the clicked entry's
revision (ContentLogEntryImpl / `jj file show -r <rev>` already exists for this,
JujutsuRepository.kt:148-153) instead of always using CurrentContentRevision. loadRevisions(file)
is the platform interface and carries no revision parameter, so either derive the revision from
the Change being diffed (thread it through from ChangeDiffRequestProducer's call site/context) or
stop marking non-@ conflicted changes MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS and produce a dedicated three-pane
request instead.

## Test cases to cover
1. @ is the conflicted commit itself - already works (existing behavior), must keep working.
2. @ is a descendant that inherited the conflict - already works by coincidence, must start
   working for the RIGHT reason (the fetched revision, not disk).
3. @ is a clean sibling/unrelated commit - currently fails with "Could not extract conflict data"
   - must show the CLICKED commit's conflict.
4. @ is itself conflicted from an unrelated rebase, different from the commit being viewed -
   currently silently shows @'s conflict content in the wrong commit's diff (no error, wrong
   data) - must show the clicked commit's own conflict, not @'s.
acceptance_criteria: Double-clicking a conflicted file in any commit's diff (not just @ or its conflict-inheriting descendants) shows that commit's own three-way conflict content, never the working copy's. Regression test at the ChangeService/JujutsuMergeProvider seam covering the four cases above.
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/119
close_reason: Fixed via JujutsuConflictDiffRequestProvider (ChangeDiffRequestProvider EP) reading the conflict from the Change's own after-revision instead of disk. Note: actions/filechange/DiffRequestBuilder.kt's buildDiffRequests (the ShowDiffAction fallback for project view/editor gutter) still builds bare two-side requests without going through Change, so it's unaffected by this fix — not broken, just not three-pane there; left out of scope.

title: Paged log loading: follow-up work
description:
Entry point for continuing jj-idea-2c8k (paged log loading, GitHub #69) follow-up work across sessions. jj-idea-2c8k itself is closed and retested clean. Five open follow-ups remain, tracked as children of this epic:

1. jj-idea-xi58 + jj-idea-1pgy + jj-idea-sc8m - ONE implementation session (they share the same per-parent graph state and renderer function). Replaces the shipped wiggly-line stub's Boolean hasElidedParents with a NOT_LOADED/HIDDEN per-parent classification (a paged-window-boundary parent isn't elided, it just hasn't loaded yet - the wiggle wrongly implies elision); adds long-edge navigation (hover thickens + arrow, click jumps to the other end, loading it first if needed); gives the mixed-merge case (one loaded parent, one not) its own stub lane. Full design: docs/design/jj-idea-hlu3-xi58-elided-ancestor-rendering.md.
2. jj-idea-hlu3 - decoupled, additive, its own session whenever: the nearest-visible-ancestor remap for HIDDEN (filtered-out) edges, upgrading their tooltip into a real connector. Explicitly NOT sequenced with (1) - see the design doc's superseded-approach section for why an earlier version of this plan had them coupled.
3. jj-idea-5gof - paged loader's per-repo ReentrantLock has no automated concurrency test.
4. jj-idea-wrza - post-write refresh()'s page-1 splice can still shift rows under a fixed viewport (loadMore()'s equivalent jump was already fixed).

Reading order for a new session: this bead's DESIGN field below, then docs/design/jj-idea-hlu3-xi58-elided-ancestor-rendering.md (for 1-2) or the individual bead for 3-4, then docs/design/jj-idea-2c8k-paged-log-loading.md for the original mechanism/validation if deeper context is needed.
design: Recommended order: (1) first - it's the one with a wrong-information bug live in production (the wiggle misimplying elision) and the user has flagged it as increasingly visible. Then whichever of (2)/(3)/(4) has the best size-for-available-session-time; they're independent of each other and of (1).
notes: Parent: jj-idea-2570 (Large-repository support). Resume with a prompt like 'continue on the paged loading' - bd prime surfaces this epic and its children via bd ready/bd list.
close_reason: All 5 children shipped (xi58, 1pgy, sc8m, wrza, 5gof). Paged log loading follow-up work is complete; remaining related work (hlu3 elided-ancestor connector, 06t5/a0wp stress-fixture hang) is decoupled/separate and tracked on its own.

title: Bookmark tree expansion state not restored after IDE restart
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. In the bookmarks panel, collapse git/origin/tags (or other folders).
2. Restart IntelliJ.
3. Folders are expanded again instead of staying collapsed.

## Root cause found (2026-09-13): this was a released-vs-shipped mismatch, not a code bug
The reporter confirmed on 0.8.15 that Local/Tags are also affected, that collapse/expand state
DOES survive closing and reopening the log tab (only a full IDE restart loses it), and that a
`git` folder is still visible in their colocated repo.

That was traced to a CHANGELOG/release mismatch: the two 0.8.15 CHANGELOG entries this behaviour
depends on (git-pseudo-remote removal + collapse/persist-expansion, commits b14d47f3/953729c3)
were both authored ~13:05-13:18 UTC on 2026-09-07, roughly 3 hours AFTER release v0.8.15 was
published (10:34 UTC, tagged at e652fd99). `jj file show -r v0.8.15 .../BookmarkTreeModel.kt`
confirms neither the git-remote filter nor default-collapsed/persisted expansion is present in the
actual released code - they were written into the CHANGELOG under the 0.8.15 heading in error.
CHANGELOG.md has been corrected (moved to [Unreleased]); see also jj-idea note on a
release-process guard to catch this automatically in future.

This fully explains both reporter symptoms: nothing to persist yet, and the git folder never
removed. The tab-reopen-survives / restart-loses distinction that motivated the original xmlb
round-trip hypothesis is not informative here - there's no persistence code active at all in the
reporter's build.

## Remaining work once actually released
Ship a release containing b14d47f3+953729c3, then ask the reporter to retest. If it still fails on
a build that genuinely contains this code, revisit the earlier hypotheses (xmlb round-tripping of
`bookmarkNodeExpanded`, or a pathKeyFor()/expansionPathKey() key mismatch) - both remain plausible
if the bug turns out to be real, just not yet demonstrated.
acceptance_criteria: Reporter confirmed on a build that actually contains b14d47f3/953729c3 (not just claims to, per CHANGELOG). If a genuine bug remains on that build: bookmarkNodeExpanded survives an IDE restart for at least Local/Tags and a remote category, with an XmlSerializer round-trip test.
notes:
Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/111 (follow-up on #48 split). Ship an
XmlSerializer round-trip test for bookmarkNodeExpanded regardless - currently untested, and still
the first acceptance-criterion gap even though the reported bug turned out to be a release
mismatch rather than a code defect. Raised P3->P2: blocks giving the reporter a correct retest
target, and the underlying CHANGELOG/release drift needs a process fix (see new bead for a CI
guard).
close_reason: Closed

title: Conflicted (divergent) local bookmarks vanish from the bookmarks panel
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Get a bookmark into a conflicted/divergent state (e.g. two operations move it independently, such as concurrent jj bookmark set from two workspaces, or an un-synced fetch).
2. Open the bookmarks panel.
3. Observe the local bookmark is simply missing from the tree, though the log table still shows it (with its conflict marker) on the commit row.

## Analysis
CliLogService.bookmarkListTemplate (jj/cli/CliLogService.kt:500-535) returns null when present && id == null. A conflicted bookmark has multiple targets, so jj's normal_target is empty -> id == null -> the item is dropped, and the local bookmark disappears from stateModel.references (and so from the panel and anything else fed by getBookmarks()).

The log table is unaffected because it gets bookmarks from the per-commit bookmarks template, which carries b.conflict() directly - matching the reporter's observation that the log shows the conflict but the panel shows nothing.

## Likely Fix
Fall back to the first of added_targets (or otherwise represent a multi-target bookmark) instead of returning null, and render it with the existing conflict icon from bookmarkIcon() (ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:116).
acceptance_criteria: A conflicted/divergent local bookmark appears in the bookmarks panel with the same red conflict icon the log table uses, instead of disappearing. Contract/stub test covers a genuinely conflicted bookmark.
notes:
2026-09-13: the reporter's 0.8.15 retest of this area is not informative - the CHANGELOG had
credited two #48 follow-up fixes (git-pseudo-remote removal, tracked-icon/ahead-behind fix,
commits b14d47f3/953729c3) to release v0.8.15, but both were authored ~3 hours AFTER v0.8.15 was
actually published/tagged (e652fd99, 2026-09-07 10:34 UTC). Neither is in the reporter's build.
CHANGELOG.md corrected to move both entries to [Unreleased]. This bead's own fix (conflicted
bookmark disappearing) is unaffected either way - it's still unreleased and still needed - but
don't treat the reporter's 0.8.15 comments on other #48 items as validation of anything beyond
what they explicitly tested.

2026-09-14: root-cause mechanism correction - the bead's original "id == null" framing wasn't
quite it. On a conflicted/divergent ref, normal_target has no commit, and jj renders the literal
text "<Error: No Commit available>" inline for every sub-expression evaluated on it (verified
against real jj 0.37.0/0.39.0/0.44.0 in a scratch repo). That text then throws
NumberFormatException inside ChangeId's constructor while parsing the offset component, and
bookmarkListTemplate.take()'s catch-all swallows the exception - so the row silently becomes null
and is dropped, rather than id resolving cleanly to null. Fixed by reading `added_targets`
instead of `normal_target` in both bookmarkListTemplate and tagListTemplate (same defect, same
shape) - added_targets stays a real (possibly multi-element) commit list even when the ref is
conflicted, and is the same list jj's own `bar (conflicted): + x + y` display uses.
close_reason: Fixed: bookmarkListTemplate/tagListTemplate now read added_targets instead of normal_target, which no longer drops a conflicted/divergent ref. Tests: LogTemplateTest, BookmarkContractTest (stub+CLI, jj 0.37 and 0.44), LogServiceIntegrationTest, BookmarkTreeModelTest.

title: Conflict resolution sides reported swapped on rebase (GitHub #112)
description:
GitHub #112: "When resolving rebase conflicts the yours and their view a swapped."

## Fixed (2026-09-13)

Root cause: jj's diff-style marker parser mapped whichever section physically appeared as a
`+++++++` full-content block to CURRENT/"Yours" and whichever appeared as a `%%%%%%%` diff-from-
base block to LAST/"Theirs" (JjMarkerConflictExtractor.kt's old parseBlock, ~line 146-166). Which
of a rebase conflict's two sides jj renders as content vs. diff is a materialization choice, not
tied to role - real jj 0.44 output puts the rebase destination first as `+++++++` (reporter's
capture), while jj's own bundled CLI docs show the opposite layout for the same kind of conflict.
So the old code assigned "Yours" to whichever role jj happened to render as content - right about
half the time, matching the reporter's 2026-09-10 "sometimes correct" follow-up.

Fix: JjMarkerConflictExtractor now identifies side #1/#2 by file order (mirroring git-style's
unambiguous `<<<<<<<`/`>>>>>>>` convention) and separately parses the role jj embeds in each
side's header (`(rebase destination)`, `(rebased revision)`, `(parents of rebased revision)`, and
the equivalent absorb/revert/squash/restore vocabulary - verified against strings in the jj 0.44
binary). When a block's two roles are a destination/moved pair, the moved side is placed in
CURRENT ("Yours") regardless of which position or rendering it appeared in; a file's blocks must
all agree or the file is left unreoriented (safe default). Merge and squash conflicts carry no
such role pairing and are completely unaffected - unswapped, as before.

Pane titles now show jj's own commit + role label (e.g. `ulmlywnv c280fd5d "my change" (rebased
revision)`) instead of fixed "Yours"/"Theirs" text, falling back to "Side #1"/"Side #2" for
snapshot-style markers (no commit info). The platform's bulk multi-file "Accept Yours"/"Accept
Theirs" (acceptFilesRevisions) is now role-aware too, re-extracting each file to pick `:ours` or
`:theirs` so it matches whatever the interactive dialog would have called "Yours" for that file.

Files: jj/conflict/JjMarkerConflictExtractor.kt, jj/conflict/ExtractedConflict.kt (new),
jj/conflict/ConflictExtractor.kt, vcs/merge/JujutsuMergeProvider.kt,
vcs/merge/JujutsuConflictResolver.kt. Tests: JjMarkerConflictExtractorTest.kt (new real-jj-marker
fixtures for both physical orderings, squash/merge non-reorientation, disagreeing-blocks
fallback), JujutsuMergeProviderTest.kt, JujutsuConflictResolverTest.kt.

Verified live against a real jj 0.44 binary: reproduced the reporter's exact scenario (rebase
directly onto a conflicting destination) and a descendant-of-the-rebased-revision variant; both
now orient correctly and consistently.

Dropped the jj-idea-n6fz dependency: this fix is self-contained on the existing dialog and does
not need the native-conflict-UX redesign epic.
acceptance_criteria: A rebase conflict's pane content and titles correctly identify which side is the reporter's own change vs. the rebase destination, per-conflict-block, by parsing jj's own role text in each block's header - not a fixed position- or operation-type-based assumption. Verified against both of the reporter's cases: a conflict landing directly on the rebased revision, and one landing on a descendant whose parent was rebased. A regression test using the reporter's real jj 0.44 diff-style marker text (both cases, plus existing git-style/commit-description cases) covers JjMarkerConflictExtractor. Merge and squash conflict titles remain correct.
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/112. relates_to jj-idea-n6fz (native jj conflict UX redesign). 2026-09-10 reporter comment confirms the mismatch is per-conflict-block (role-dependent), not a fixed per-operation swap - see description.
close_reason: Fixed: role-aware pane orientation + titles, verified against real jj 0.44 output and full test suite

title: Log becomes unresponsive after creating a merge change in the stress-test fixture (possible dup of a0wp)
description:
## Summary
Reported while manually testing jj-idea-ib1i/p35f: in a large multi-branch stress-test repo
(scripts/fixtures/fx-stress.sh's fixture, ~1084 commits, ~26 concurrent heads incl. a hotfix/*
cluster), creating a new merge change from two hotfix/* bookmarks (e.g. `hotfix/2` + `hotfix/3`,
via "New Change From These") causes the log to stop loading. On IDE restart, the log tab renders
briefly then disappears, and the plugin becomes effectively unresponsive.

## What's been ruled out
Reproduced the underlying data operation against a throwaway copy of the reporter's actual
stress-test repo: `jj new hotfix/2 hotfix/3` completes instantly and cleanly via the CLI, and
every `jj log`/`jj bookmark list` invocation the plugin issues on refresh (`jj log -r all()
--limit 500`, `jj log -r heads(::@) --limit 1000/10`, `jj log -r @`, `jj bookmark list
--all-remotes`) returns near-instantly with correct output. So this is not a jj-CLI-level bug,
not a bad argument list from `newArgs`/`CliExecutor.new`, and not something in this session's
jj-idea-ib1i/p35f bookmarks-panel work (New Change's creation path - NewChangeDialog,
newChangeFromAction, CliExecutor.new - is pre-existing and untouched by that change; the merge
was reproducible identically via a plain jj CLI call, with no plugin action-context involved).

## Suspected root cause
jj-idea-a0wp (open, P4) already documents that this exact stress-test fixture's ~26 concurrent
branches make LayoutCalculatorImpl/JujutsuCommitGraph.paintComponent() very wide (up to 56k draw
calls per repaint), filed as a rendering-perf issue. Adding one more merge commit across two
already-long-lived independent branches plausibly pushes this over an actual hang/crash
threshold, not just a slow repaint - which would also explain "log appears briefly, then
disappears" on restart (the same expensive layout/paint recomputing on every reload). Unconfirmed
without an actual thread dump or exception from the hang.

## Needs
An actual crash artifact from the reporter to confirm: Help > Show Log in Finder for the idea.log
from the session where this happened, or Help > Diagnostic Tools > Analyze Thread Dump if the IDE
was still able to produce one while hanging. The idea.log files checked during investigation (in
this workspace's .intellijPlatform sandboxes) did not contain a matching session - the crash
happened in a run/log this investigation didn't have access to.

## Files to read
- src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/log/graph/LayoutCalculator.kt (LayoutCalculatorImpl)
- src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/log/JujutsuCommitGraph.kt (paintComponent)
- scripts/fixtures/fx-stress.sh (repro fixture, hotfix/* cluster)
notes: 2026-09-14: fixed a real, separate quadratic-repaint bug while investigating this (jj-idea-a0wp, now closed) - JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.drawLinesToParents rescanned every row above the one painting on every repaint (O(visible rows x total rows), worse the further down the log you scroll), and the sc8m hover path rebuilt the full GraphEdgeIndex on every mouse-move/scroll tick. Both are fixed and covered by new scale/equivalence tests; ./gradlew check is green. This is a plausible contributor to 'log appears briefly, then disappears' at ~1084 rows / ~26 heads, but NOT confirmed as 06t5's root cause - the original suspected culprit (JujutsuCommitGraph.paintComponent()) no longer exists in the codebase at all (painting is now a per-cell TableCellRenderer), so the a0wp bead's hypothesis was already stale before this fix. Still needs: (1) manual runIde reproduction with the fix in place - reproduce hotfix/2 + hotfix/3 New Change From These on the fx-stress fixture and confirm the log stays responsive; (2) the original ask, an actual idea.log/thread-dump artifact from the reporter, in case the real cause is unrelated to graph rendering entirely. Keeping open.
close_reason: Not reproducible after the jj-idea-a0wp quadratic-repaint fix (GraphEdgeIndex replaces the per-repaint rescan in drawLinesToParents and the per-mouse-move index rebuild). Manual runIde attempt on the fx-stress fixture no longer hangs; the reporter artifact (idea.log / thread dump) never materialised. Causation is plausible, not confirmed — reopen with an idea.log if a hang or vanishing log tab recurs.

title: Stop ktlint tasks poisoning cross-lane Gradle build cache
description: Decompiling ktlint-gradle-12.1.2.jar showed KtLintCheckTask/GenerateReportsTask are @CacheableTask with @PathSensitive(RELATIVE) inputs but their outputs embed absolute file paths -- non-relocatable. With org.gradle.caching=true shared across jj-parallel-lanes workspaces, one lane can restore another lane's cached report (wrong paths, wrong verdict, including a false PASS masking a real CI failure). This caused CI run 34128422723 to slip past a local ./gradlew check. Fix: opt ktlint's check/report tasks out of the build cache specifically (outputs.cacheIf { false }), rather than the blanket --no-build-cache workaround committed in 8d79368.
close_reason: Fixed: opted ktlint's check/report tasks (BaseKtLintCheckTask, GenerateReportsTask) out of the Gradle build cache via outputs.cacheIf { false }, since their outputs embed non-relocatable absolute paths. Verified caching disabled for ktlint tasks only (compileTestKotlin/instrumentTestCode still FROM-CACHE); ./gradlew check green with no cache flags. Reverted the blanket --no-build-cache wording in CLAUDE.md/contributing.md from 8d79368.

title: bookmark list template omits tracked/ahead/behind — bookmarks panel shows every remote bookmark as tracked and never shows divergence
description:
## Summary
From jj-idea-d65h's spike (jj-idea-3sac's design field, Finding 3): the
bookmarks panel is fed via `getBookmarks()` -> `stateModel.references`, which uses
`bookmarkListTemplate` (jj/cli/CliLogService.kt:463-486). That template only queries `present`,
name, `conflict`, change id, and `immutable` — it never queries `tracked()`,
`tracking_ahead_count()`, or `tracking_behind_count()`, so every `Bookmark` built from it defaults
to `tracked = true` and `aheadCount = behindCount = 0`, regardless of the actual state.

This is a standalone bug, independent of any bookmarks-panel remote-grouping work:
- Every remote bookmark renders with the *tracked* icon (bookmarkIcon(),
  ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:116-121) whether or not it's actually tracked.
- No bookmark in the panel ever shows the `up n down m` divergence indicator, since
  appendBookmarkChip computes it from fields that are always zero here.
- toggleTrackBookmarkAction (actions/bookmark/toggleTrackBookmarkAction.kt:10) branches on
  bookmark.tracked and therefore always offers "Untrack", even on a genuinely untracked remote
  bookmark — a functional bug in the context menu, not just a display gap.

`bookmarkListArgs` already passes `--all-remotes` (jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt:194-215), so untracked
remotes are present in the data; only the template under-reads them.

## Fix
Add the three missing fields to `bookmarkListTemplate`, mirroring the expressions already used in
`localBookmarkTemplate`/`remoteBookmarkTemplate` (CliLogService.kt:324-343):
`b.tracked()`, `b.tracking_ahead_count().lower()`, `b.tracking_behind_count().lower()`.

## Files to change
- src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/jj/cli/CliLogService.kt (bookmarkListTemplate, ~463-486)
- Test coverage: CliLogService's existing bookmark-list template tests


## Steps to Reproduce
1. In a colocated jj/git repo, have a tracked bookmark diverge from its remote (ahead and/or behind), or leave a remote bookmark untracked.
2. Open the bookmarks panel and inspect that bookmark'''s remote leaf.
Expected: tracked icon reflects reality, and divergence shows an up-n-down-m indicator when ahead/behind > 0.
Actual: always renders as tracked, never shows divergence, because bookmarkListTemplate (CliLogService.kt:463-486) never reads tracked()/tracking_ahead_count()/tracking_behind_count().
design: Mirror localBookmarkTemplate/remoteBookmarkTemplate's per-field expressions rather than inventing new ones.
acceptance_criteria: A remote bookmark's tracked/ahead/behind state, as parsed via getBookmarks()/bookmarkListTemplate, matches what jj log's bookmark template reports for the same ref. The bookmarks panel's context menu offers Track (not Untrack) for a genuinely untracked remote bookmark.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. In a colocated jj/git repo with a tracked bookmark that has diverged from its remote (ahead and/or behind), or an untracked remote bookmark.
2. Open the bookmarks panel and look at that bookmark's remote leaf.
Expected: tracked icon reflects reality, and divergence shows an up-n-down-m indicator when ahead/behind > 0.
Actual: always renders as tracked, never shows divergence, because bookmarkListTemplate (CliLogService.kt:463-486) never reads tracked()/tracking_ahead_count()/tracking_behind_count().
close_reason: Shipped: bookmarkListTemplate tracked/ahead/behind fix, git pseudo-remote hidden, remote categories collapse by default with persisted expansion and roll-up badges (GitHub #48).

title: Fix flaky LeakHunter retained-Project failure in two new stateModel platform tests
description: ClickActionGroupDefaultActionTest and JujutsuAuthorFilterComponentToggleTest read/write project.stateModel via a real projectFixture but didn't drain JujutsuStateModel's fire-and-forget pooled-thread loaders in @AfterEach before fixture teardown (the jj-idea-q49j pattern), so a loader could still be in flight when the fixture disposed the project. Added the same drainBackgroundLoads() @AfterEach used by JujutsuStateModelPlatformTest/JujutsuLogTableDnDTest to both files.

close_reason: Added drainBackgroundLoads() @AfterEach to ClickActionGroupDefaultActionTest and JujutsuAuthorFilterComponentToggleTest (both touch project.stateModel via a real projectFixture without draining, per the jj-idea-q49j pattern). Verified: platformTest passes locally on 2025.1, 2025.2, and 2026.2; ./gradlew check passes.

title: 20 platform tests fail in ./gradlew check (JujutsuEditorActionGroupTest, FileChangeActionGroupPlatformTest, HunkPickerDialogTest, etc.), unrelated to jj-idea-r5tx
description:
While running ./gradlew check to verify jj-idea-r5tx's fix, 20 platformTest failures showed up that are unrelated to that change (confirmed: they fail identically in isolation, without the r5tx fix or its new test present).

Failing tests observed on 2026-09-05 in a full ./gradlew check run:
- JujutsuEditorActionGroupTest: getChildren(null) does not crash..., Annotate is filtered out in a diff editor..., Annotate is present in the plain code editor context() — all NullPointerException at JujutsuEditorActionGroupTest.kt:42
- FileChangeActionGroupPlatformTest: Compare and Remote actions appear..., ShowDiff and OpenFile appear before..., SquashFiles and SplitFiles appear..., TrackedToggle appears in the last block(), all expected action IDs are registered..., group contains all expected registered actions(), Restore actions appear... — AssertionFailedError/AssertionError/IndexOutOfBoundsException at various lines
- HunkPickerDialogTest: right arrow moves a hunk..., OK reports the exit code..., multiple hunks move independently(), squash labels render distinct pane titles..., pickRemainderContent applies an arrow click... — IllegalArgumentException at HunkPickerDialogTest.kt:186 (and one IllegalStateException at :148)
- JujutsuLogContextMenuActionsLiveSelectionTest: live selection includes New and Edit..., live selection reuses the registered Rebase and Describe... — AssertionFailedError
- JujutsuLogTableEnterActionTest: Enter is bound to Show Diff in the default keymap() — AssertionError
- A cascading 'JUnit Jupiter > executionError' from LeakHunter.java:126 at the end of the run, likely caused by state leaked from one of the above.

Needs triage: is this environment-specific (e.g. shared ~/.gradle cache / concurrent jj-parallel-lanes workspace interference), a genuine regression, or dependent on test execution order/registered-action state bleeding between tests?
close_reason: Environmental: truncated .intellijPlatform/layoutIndex in the lane1 workspace meant the platform modules Groovy Scripting depends on were unresolved, so the plugin itself was excluded and no actions registered. Fixed by deleting the index cache and letting IJPGP re-index; confirmed with a clean 288-test platformTest run and a full ./gradlew check pass. contributing.md now documents the symptom under Building & Running.

title: [bug] Describe dialog shows full 64-char change ID instead of short ID (GitHub #76 regression)
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Right-click any change in the log and select "Describe" (or edit the working copy description).
2. Observe the dialog title/prompt reads "Enter description for change <full-length-id>:" instead of the short id shown elsewhere in the UI.
Screenshot: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5076577-ae0f-4d58-910a-09a7a06f2cd5

## Root Cause
describeAction.kt:40 passes target.id (a ChangeId) as the {0} parameter for dialog.describe.input.message=Enter description for change {0}:. ChangeId.toString() returns .full (ChangeId.kt:15), so the dialog shows the full unique change id instead of the short displayed id.

This is distinct from the original #76 (ambiguous short-id CLI arguments, fixed by jj-idea-dq7z/jj-idea-atfz by using full ids for CLI calls) — that CLI-argument fix is correct and must stay; only the *display* string needs to use the short id.

## Fix
Pass target.id.short (or .title, which returns short) instead of target.id. Swept other JujutsuBundle.message(...) call sites for the same mistake (interpolating a raw ChangeId/Revision) and found no other instance.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/76 (comment 2026-09-04T13:30:20Z)
acceptance_criteria: Describe dialog title/message shows the short change id; a test asserts the composed message contains the short id and not the full one.
close_reason: Fixed: describeAction.kt now passes the short change id (via describePromptId) to the dialog message, not the full id. Added DescribeActionMessageTest; CHANGELOG and manual-tests.md updated.

title: [bug] Move Bookmark dialog OK button disabled until selection changes (GitHub #105)
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Right-click a change in the log that has at least one bookmark reachable forward.
2. Select "Move Bookmark Here..."
3. Observe the dialog opens with a bookmark already selected (the first selectable row), but the OK button is greyed out.
4. Select another bookmark, or check "Allow backwards or sideways move" — OK becomes enabled.

## Root Cause
MoveBookmarkDialog.kt: init() calls rebuildList() (~line 196), which ends by calling selectFirstSelectable(), setting list.selectedIndex directly. The list.addListSelectionListener { updateOkButton() } registration (~line 250) is added AFTER rebuildList() runs, so the initial auto-selection never triggers updateOkButton(), leaving isOKActionEnabled at the false set on line 193 even though a valid forward-movable bookmark is already selected.

## Fix
Call updateOkButton() explicitly at the end of init (after listener registration), rather than relying on the selection event firing. Also check MoveBookmarkToChangeDialog.kt and AdvanceBookmarkPickerDialog.kt for the same init-ordering bug.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/105
acceptance_criteria: OK is enabled immediately after the dialog opens when the first selectable row is a forward-movable bookmark; a unit test on the dialog model covers both the initially-enabled and initially-disabled (backward-only / empty) cases.
close_reason: Fixed init-ordering bug: rebuildList() now calls updateOkButton() after selectFirstSelectable() in both MoveBookmarkDialog and MoveBookmarkToChangeDialog

title: DnD: reject-drop tooltip was always blank instead of showing the real guard reason
description: Bug found manually: dragging a commit over an undroppable row (cross-repo, cycle, immutable destination) showed a reject cursor with no explanation - inconsistent/confusing feedback. Root cause: JujutsuLogTableDnD.kt's target checker discarded DragContext.rejectionReason's real message and always called event.setDropPossible(false, ""). Fixed by threading the reason through a new DropResolution.Rejected(reason) case; only the deliberate self-drop and unwired-operation cases stay silent.
notes:
THIRD attempt, this one addressing a mechanism found by tracing the actual platform behavior against the user's exact new symptom ('flashes briefly over the source, never appears again' after the 2nd attempt using event.setHighlighting(FILLED_RECTANGLE)). Root cause: DnDManagerImpl.updateCurrentEvent unconditionally calls hideCurrentHighlighter() on every drag-over tick where the point differs from the last-processed one AND isDropPossible()==false - there is no Highlighters.isVisibleExcept() preservation check on that branch (unlike the isDropPossible()==true branch, which is why the ALLOWED-drop outline was always fine). The only thing re-queued afterward is a delayed, registry-gated (ide.dnd.textHints) ERROR_TEXT balloon - never RECTANGLE/FILLED_RECTANGLE. So ANY event.setHighlighting(...) call made while dropPossible=false gets wiped by the platform itself on the very next tick, regardless of the highlighting type requested - the 2nd attempt's FILLED_RECTANGLE could never have persisted, full stop. Fix: ui/log/JujutsuLogTableDnD.kt's new RejectOverlay class paints its own JComponent directly into the same JLayeredPane Highlighters uses, entirely bypassing DnDEvent.setHighlighting/DnDManagerImpl's hide/show bookkeeping - shown/hidden/positioned purely from our own target-checker state, so the platform can't wipe it. Uses JBUI.CurrentTheme.Validator.errorBackgroundColor()/errorBorderColor() for a themed error-red fill, visually distinct from the allowed-drop outline. Confirmed live 2026-09-30 for the cross-repo case (fill persists). FOURTH attempt (2026-09-30), after live retest of the cross-repo case: the RejectOverlay red fill now persists (third fix confirmed), but no reason text was shown. Root cause: DnDManagerImpl's ERROR_TEXT/TEXT balloon is gated in Highlighters.show on Registry ide.dnd.textHints, default false (platform/util/resources/misc/registry.properties:153), so every label in DropOperation.kt and every reason in DragGuards.kt was being computed and discarded - allowed-drop labels too. Fix: new ui/dnd/DropHint.kt paints its own text bubble in the layered pane (layer DRAG_LAYER+1, above RejectOverlay), wired into JujutsuLogTableDnD.kt and JujutsuBookmarksPanelDnD.kt target checkers; defers to the platform when ide.dnd.textHints is on. Also found+fixed a latent RejectOverlay bug: in Kotlin layeredPane.add(c, JLayeredPane.DRAG_LAYER) binds to add(Component,int index), not Java's layer-constraint overload, so the overlay lived in the default layer - now add()+setLayer(). Tests: DropHintTest, RejectOverlayTest (platform). Awaiting live retest of MT-DND 'Drop hint text next to the cursor'. 2026-09-30 follow-up: hint is now HTML. New ui/dnd/DropMessage.kt (text + ChangeId parts; .plain = old strings, .html/.render = log-style id formatting). DropOperation.label is now derived from DropOperation.message; DragContext.rejectionMessage is primary (rejectionReason = its plain text); DropResolution.Rejected / PanelDropResolution.Rejected carry message. DropHint renders a JLabel (deliberately not a text component - those install a default DropTarget that would swallow drags over the hint); wraps via (a div's CSS width overshoots ~90px in JLabel). Only rebuilds label HTML when message/width changes. 2026-09-30 follow-up 2: live retest confirmed ids styled + wrapping OK, but bookmarks were plain text. Chips are elements a JLabel can't resolve, so DropHint(project) now renders into IconAwareHtmlPane (transferHandler/dropTarget nulled so it can't swallow a drag; asserted in DropHintTest). DropMessage gained Bookmark and Tag parts (plain = name, html = log's chip). Bug found by test: pane.preferredSize must be reset to null before re-measuring, else a later longer message keeps the first message's size. 2026-09-30 follow-up 3 (live retest): long bookmark name spilled over the bubble and garbled wrapping ('Move / bookmark [icon] name-cut / o [id]'); spacing had no gap between chip and following 'to'. Causes: (a) a plain space right after a chip's collapses (HtmlTextCanvas.space() exists for this) - DropMessage.render now emits nbsp + zero-width space (legal break) for spaces following a chip; (b) a chip is one unbreakable unit and Swing's row breaker mishandles a wide one (drags the preceding word onto its row, clips the tail), and DropHint's width caps were unscaled while fonts scale with UI zoom. Fix: DropHint builds a RefFit from measured font metrics (scaled widths): a chip wider than 40% of the bubble gets its own line (
before/after), one wider than 90% is middle-ellipsized (DropMessage.ellipsizeToWidth). Verified by painting the real component to PNG in a scratch harness (headless paints the icon a row low, but the untouched log rendering does too - harness artifact, icon position NOT verified).
close_reason: Verified live 2026-09-30: red fill persists; reason/operation hint shows next to the cursor with log-styled ids, bookmark/tag chips, correct spacing and wrapping. Fix: ui/dnd/DropHint.kt + DropMessage.kt (platform's ide.dnd.textHints text is off by default).
