title: Installation Help: refresh live on status change, and default to upgrade when jj is available
description:
Settings -> Jujutsu -> Installation Help has two defects.

(1) Stale content. The group body is a one-shot snapshot built in
JujutsuConfigurable.createPanel() (JujutsuConfigurable.kt:155-227) -- the limitation is
already documented in the comment at lines 156-161. Only installGroupRow.expanded reacts
to later availability changes (lines 234-240). So after clicking Test on a newly entered
executable path, or after upgrading jj outside the IDE and rechecking, the "your jj is
too old" wording, the gated-feature list, and the install-vs-upgrade commands all stay
stale until Settings is closed and reopened. Both trigger points already invalidate the
status (testExecutable() at line 1103-1105; apply() at lines 852-863), so the data is
there -- only the UI doesn't rebuild.

Also note: testExecutable()'s invalidate() only fires on the success branch (a too-old or
invalid tested binary never triggers a recheck) and only when the typed path already
equals the saved path (an edited-but-unapplied path never rechecks either). Worth
revisiting alongside the main fix.

(2) Wrong default wording. installHelpIsUpgradeFor (FeatureAvailability.kt:63-67) returns
false for FeatureAvailability.AllSupported, so a user whose jj is present and fully
supported sees "how to install" commands. When jj is known to be installed, the group
should default to upgrade commands.
design:
(1) Extract the group body into a private function returning a DialogPanel
(buildInstallHelpContent(status: JjAvailabilityStatus)), and host it in the collapsible
group through a Kotlin UI DSL placeholder() cell. Reuse the existing
project.jjAvailabilityStatus.connect(disposable) listener already wired at
JujutsuConfigurable.kt:234-240 to swap the placeholder's component and keep the current
auto-expand behaviour, rather than adding a second subscription. Keep the initial
snapshot for the disposable == null path (a test calling createPanel() directly).

(2) In installHelpIsUpgradeFor, map AllSupported to true alongside Gated/BelowMinimum;
leave Unknown (Checking/NotFound/InvalidPath) at false so genuinely-missing jj still gets
install commands. Update the function's KDoc, which currently explains the Scenario A/B
split as the whole rule. Check whether the "settings.upgrade.description" bundle string
in JujutsuBundle.properties reads sensibly for a healthy install (it may be phrased
around being out of date) and add a neutral variant if not.
acceptance_criteria:
Editing the executable path and clicking Test (or applying a path change) updates the
Installation Help wording, gated-feature list, and command rows without reopening
Settings. With jj available and all features supported, the group shows upgrade
commands; with jj not found or the path invalid, it still shows install commands.
InstallHelpTest (src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/settings/InstallHelpTest.kt) covers the
new AllSupported -> upgrade mapping.
notes: Related to jj-idea-oomz (guided in-IDE jj update) -- same settings group, but that one is about running the upgrade, not about content freshness. Neither blocks the other. UI-only change: re-run manual-test sections covering the settings executable/install-help surface (docs/manual-tests.md).
close_reason: Extracted Installation Help body into buildInstallHelpContent(status), hosted in a placeholder cell swapped by the existing jjAvailabilityStatus.connect listener; testExecutable() now invalidates on every branch (guarded on path==saved path); installHelpIsUpgradeFor now treats AllSupported as an upgrade with new neutral wording. Tests updated/added; ./gradlew check passes.

title: Quick action to switch the diff base (GitHub #43)
description:
Follow-up to the per-repo diff-base setting shipped in recent commits (5f8f2931f,
d8180c8bc, 5120ab090, 53462b5b4). In GitHub #43's 2026-09-03 replies, the reporter
(SergejSalnikov) says the diff base is task-driven rather than a permanent project
setting, and asks for it as a quick action/dialog IN ADDITION to the settings row —
not instead of it.

Existing bead jj-idea-4tcf ("Show effective diff base (resolved revision) live in
settings") is settings-UI-only and doesn't cover this quick-action ask.
design:
- Add a Jujutsu.SetDiffBase action opening a revision picker, writing the same
  per-repo setting the settings row writes, so the two stay one source of truth (no
  separate "task diff base" state).
- Reuse the existing revision picker from actions/file/CompareFileWithBranchAction.kt
  (Jujutsu.CompareWithBranch, plugin.xml:234) rather than building a second one.
- Relate to jj-idea-4tcf via `bd dep add` (relates-to, not blocking).
notes: Fourth follow-up (2026-09-04): user pointed out Git/Mercurial/Subversion all register their own init action in Vcs.Import (top-level, not inside their product submenu) - restored that convention for Jujutsu.Init rather than fighting it, and relocated the Jujutsu submenu itself to VcsGlobalGroup anchored after Vcs.Specific, matching Git.Menu's exact placement so 'Jujutsu' and 'Git' sit in the same menu section. Jujutsu.Init is no longer referenced inside the submenu (mirrors Git.Init not being inside Git.Menu); JujutsuMainMenuGroup's visibility guard reverted to project.isJujutsu since nothing left in it needs to be reachable pre-repo. ./gradlew check passes (same known-flaky platformTest leak-detection false positive as before, confirmed clean on immediate rerun).
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] Bookmark toolbar/status-bar widgets visible in non-jj projects (GitHub #100)
description:
Jujutsu.MainToolbarBookmarks (the main-toolbar bookmark widget) shows up in projects
that don't use jj at all, whenever the plugin is installed.

Root cause: JujutsuBookmarkToolbarWidget.update() (ui/toolbar/JujutsuBookmarkToolbarWidget.kt:37)
gates visibility on `project.possibleJujutsuVcs != null`. That property
(vcs/VcsExtensions.kt:33-34) is just
`projectLevelVcsManager.findVcsByName(JujutsuVcsBase.VCS_NAME) as? JujutsuVcs` — it
tests whether the Jujutsu VCS EXTENSION is registered, which is true in every project
once the plugin is installed. It says nothing about whether the current project is
actually a jj repo.

The correct predicate already exists and is used correctly elsewhere:
`Project.isJujutsu` (VcsExtensions.kt:36, backed by stateModel.isJujutsu) — see
JujutsuCustomLogTabManager.kt:68, WorkingCopySignpost.kt:32, SponsorAsk.kt:31,
FeatureUpgradeNudge.kt:25.

Same class of bug also present in:
- ui/statusbar/JujutsuStatusBarWidgetFactory.kt:16 (isAvailable)
- ui/statusbar/JujutsuBookmarkStatusBarWidgetFactory.kt:35 (isAvailable)
Audit (may be intentional per call site, needs individual judgement):
- actions/change/DescribeWorkingCopyAction.kt:25
- actions/change/workingCopyConflicts.kt:43
- actions/file/ResolveSelectedConflictsAction.kt:46

Note: the action id is Jujutsu.MainToolbarBookmarks (plural); the GitHub issue title
says "MainToolbarBookmark" (singular) — same widget, minor title typo in the report.
design:
Swap possibleJujutsuVcs -> isJujutsu at the toolbar widget and both status-bar
factories.

Toolbar widget is polled on ActionUpdateThread.BGT; isJujutsu reads @Volatile
state-model fields so it's safe to poll directly there — consistent with the
existing class KDoc's reasoning against caching.

Status-bar isAvailable is NOT polled — the factory result is cached by the platform,
so flipping isJujutsu after project open (e.g. jj is initialised later via
Jujutsu.Init) needs an explicit widget refresh. There's already a precedent listener
for this shape: JujutsuBookmarkStatusBarSettingsListener (plugin.xml:311-313) —
extend or mirror it to also re-check on jj-ness changes.

Related but distinct: jj-idea-6nas (GitHub #95, status-bar widget width cap) — link
via `bd dep add` as relates-to, don't merge the work.
close_reason: Fixed: swapped possibleJujutsuVcs -> isJujutsu at toolbar widget, both status-bar factories, and DescribeWorkingCopyAction; added StatusBarWidgetsManager.updateWidget refresh in renamed JujutsuUiEnabler for live jj-init transition; added regression platform test

title: Consolidate Feature Availability into Installation Help
description: Second round of live UI feedback on jj-idea-vcqn/vwni/bslw. The standalone 'Feature Availability' group plus its cross-reference hint to Installation Help ('see Installation Help above, now expanded with upgrade commands') reads as feature-boast filler and costs an extra group header. Decision: fold the gated-feature list directly into Installation Help's own description, right above its upgrade commands: 'Your current jj version is too old. Upgrade now to unlock these features: - Advance Bookmark (needs jj 0.39.0) ... Upgrade using: <commands>'. The '(needs jj X)' part should render as grey secondary text, matching the rest of the plugin's de-emphasized version/hint text. Also continues jj-idea-bslw's width work: the Homebrew/Cargo command labels still don't leave enough gap before their input box even with the 12px padding, and the panel is still reported too wide in the user's environment.
acceptance_criteria: No standalone Feature Availability group. Installation Help, when gated (Scenario B) or below the plugin minimum (Scenario A), shows the gated feature list (Scenario B only) inline above its upgrade commands, with per-feature version text in grey. No leftover 'now expanded' or similar boast phrasing anywhere. Homebrew/Cargo labels have a visibly larger gap before their command box than the previous 12px attempt.
notes: Superseded the initial close description: the 12px/28px border-padding approach for Homebrew/Cargo labels turned out to be a no-op on screen (grid absorbs a component's own border as 'visual padding', doesn't push the next cell over). Replaced with .gap(RightGap.COLUMNS), the real inter-cell gap mechanism, verified with a test that does a real layout pass and measures actual pixel positions. Also: gated features now render as an indented bullet list (was a flat paragraph), narrowed 5 more .comment() calls that were still using the DSL default width, and tightened JujutsuConfigurablePanelTest's WIDTH_BUDGET from 640 to 560 to catch future regressions closer to when they're introduced.
close_reason: Removed the standalone Feature Availability group and its cross-reference hint entirely; folded the gated-feature list directly into Installation Help's description ('Your current jj version is too old. Upgrade now to unlock these features: ...'), with the '(needs jj X)' clause in grey secondary text via an inline HTML span baked from UIUtil.getContextHelpForeground(). Also widened the Homebrew/Cargo label padding from 12px to 28px. Added regression tests: no standalone group, command labels still padded.

title: Polish Feature Availability / Installation Help interaction
description: Follow-up from live UI review of jj-idea-vcqn (Feature Availability list). Issues found: (1) the 'Upgrade jj to unlock these' hint wraps too aggressively (360px body width, same constant used for validation-error messages) and isn't styled as secondary/grey text like other DSL comments; (2) it says 'see Installation Help above' but that group is collapsed by default and there's no auto-unfold or clear signpost; (3) Installation Help only ever shows install commands unless status is VersionTooOld (Scenario A) -- when merely feature-gated (Scenario B, e.g. jj 0.37 vs BOOKMARK_ADVANCE's 0.39 minimum), it still says 'if jj is not installed, use one of these commands' instead of upgrade commands, even though jj IS installed and just needs upgrading. Decision: keep the two collapsibleGroups separate (different purposes -- generic install/upgrade reference vs per-feature diagnostic) but link them behaviorally: broaden the upgrade-vs-install decision to also cover Scenario B, and auto-expand Installation Help alongside Feature Availability when something is gated.
acceptance_criteria: Hint text uses comment-style grey secondary color and a wider wrap width (no more than 2 lines for the current message). Installation Help auto-expands when a feature is gated, same as Feature Availability. Installation Help shows upgrade commands (not install commands) whenever isUpgrade is true, where isUpgrade now also covers Available-but-gated status, not just VersionTooOld.
close_reason: Broadened isUpgrade/detectedMethod to cover Scenario B (extracted as installHelpIsUpgradeFor/detectedInstallMethodFor, unit tested), auto-expand Installation Help alongside Feature Availability when gated, and restyled the hint as grey secondary text at a wider (500px) wrap width instead of the 360px validation-message width.

title: Settings width guard misses the per-repo group
description: JujutsuConfigurablePanelTest (jj-idea-bwdk) guards the settings panel's preferred width, but its fixture project has no jj repositories, so it never builds the per-repo 'Repository Settings' group — the test's own doc comment flags this gap. That group now overflows the width budget again (regression noticed 2026-09-02), most likely in the per-repo diff-base row (JujutsuConfigurable.kt ~586-601: combo + COLUMNS_MEDIUM field on one row, three indent levels deep) and/or the per-repo revset row (~550-564).
acceptance_criteria: A test builds JujutsuConfigurable with at least one (stub) repository present and asserts the same WIDTH_BUDGET as the existing test. Settings panel with a real multi-repo project shows no horizontal scrollbar with a repo group expanded.
close_reason: Split the per-repo diff-base combo+field row into two rows and added a test seam + tests exercising the per-repo group with a stub repository.

title: Move selected commit up/down via keybinding (GitHub #93)
description:
CaptaiNiveau (GitHub #93, 2026-08-29) suggested, as an interim ahead of full drag-and-drop reordering (tracked by the now-closed spike jj-idea-6oeg and its follow-ups), a button + keybind to move a selected changeset up or down the log -- similar to lazygit's move keybind (cited in 6oeg's own notes as prior art).

Unlike drag-and-drop, this needs none of jj-idea-6oeg's gesture infrastructure (hit-testing, drag sources/targets, live preview during a continuous gesture, immutability guards mid-drag): CommandExecutor.rebase() (jj/CommandExecutor.kt:288) already accepts destinationMode = RebaseDestinationMode.BEFORE/AFTER generically -- the same -B/-A placement machinery the 'New Change...' dialog (GitHub #83, shipped 0.8.13) already exercises. Moving a commit up/down is simply: take the selected commit and its neighbour in the currently-displayed order, call rebase(revisions=[selected], destinations=[neighbour], destinationMode=BEFORE or AFTER).

Keyboard and mouse-drag are complementary interaction models, not competing ones (lazygit itself ships a move keybind alongside no drag support at all), so this doesn't need to wait on the drag-and-drop follow-up beads and isn't superseded once they land.
design: Two new actions (Move Up / Move Down), enabled only for a single-commit selection with an applicable neighbour in the current log order, each a thin wrapper calling the existing rebase(revisions=[selected], destinations=[neighbour], destinationMode=BEFORE/AFTER). Default keybindings analogous to lazygit's ctrl+j/ctrl+k or similar, following this plugin's existing convention of giving frequently-used log actions default shortcuts (see Rebase/Describe/Edit in 0.8.12, GitHub #78). Immutability guard: reuse whatever check already gates the Rebase action today (an immutable neighbour or selected commit should disable the action, not silently fail).
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a single commit and invoking Move Up/Down (via toolbar button, context menu, or default keybinding) rebases it before/after its immediate neighbour in the currently displayed log order. Disabled when the selection isn't a single commit, has no applicable neighbour, or the move would touch an immutable commit.
notes: GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/93. Complementary to jj-idea-6oeg's drag-and-drop follow-ups, not superseded by them.
close_reason: Implemented Move Up/Down log actions (GitHub #93)

title: Dedicated Restore dialog with adjustable file selection (GitHub #84)
description:
SergejSalnikov (GitHub #84, 2026-08-24) asked for a 'Revert...' button similar to other VCS plugins (referencing IntelliJ's platform RollbackChangesDialog / Mercurial plugin's Revert Changes dialog): select files in the Working Copy tree, click Revert, and get a dedicated dialog pre-checking the selected files but letting you adjust the selection before confirming.

Current state: RestoreSelectionAction (actions/file/RestoreSelectionAction.kt) is the equivalent action today -- it restores the selected files to their parent revision (@-) via 'jj restore', but only after a plain Messages.showYesNoDialog Yes/No confirmation (no selection UI, no way to add/remove files from what's being restored). The maintainer's own reply on #84 confirmed this reading and committed to a dedicated dialog: '...I have it on the backlog, but will raise its priority. I'll address this by wiring that dialog up to jj restore.'

No bead currently exists for this despite the public commitment -- filed during 2026-09-01 triage after the coverage check flagged #84 as having no matching bead.
design: Add a dialog (naming suggestion: RestoreDialog, modeled on the existing Split/Squash dialogs' file-checklist pattern rather than IntelliJ's platform RollbackChangesDialog, since this plugin already has its own file-selection-checklist UI conventions elsewhere) that: lists all files with pending changes relative to the restore target (@- by default), pre-checks exactly the files that were selected in the Working Copy tree when the action was invoked, and lets the user tick/untick before confirming. On confirm, runs 'jj restore' scoped to the checked files only. Wire RestoreSelectionAction's actionPerformed to open this dialog instead of Messages.showYesNoDialog when invoked with a selection (single-file case may still want the simpler Yes/No path per the existing action's UX, or could be unified -- worth deciding during implementation).
acceptance_criteria: Selecting one or more files in the Working Copy tree and choosing Restore/Revert opens a dialog with those files pre-checked; the user can add or remove files from the set before confirming; confirming restores exactly the checked files via jj restore.
notes: GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/84
close_reason: Implemented: RestoreDialog + performRestore shared launcher wired into RestoreSelectionAction and RestoreToChangeAction; tests in RestoreDialogTest.kt; docs/manual-tests.md and CHANGELOG.md updated.

title: Bookmark drag-to-move
description:
Split out of jj-idea-6oeg (Spike: drag-and-drop graph ops feasibility), which currently lumps bookmark repositioning in with squash/rebase/duplicate drag gestures on the commit graph. Bookmark drag (dragging a bookmark chip onto a different commit to move it there, roughly 'jj bookmark set <name> -r <target>') is a distinct gesture surface -- log-table cell/chip hit-testing and drag affordances rather than the custom-painted commit graph -- and should be able to move on its own schedule independent of the graph-gesture spike's outcome.

Relates to jj-idea-6oeg: do the graph-gesture spike's conclusions first for shared infrastructure (drag-source/drop-target patterns, immutability guards during a gesture), but this bead tracks the bookmark-specific slice separately so it isn't blocked on squash/rebase/duplicate UX decisions that don't apply to it.
notes: Relates to jj-idea-6oeg. Filed during 2026-09-01 GitHub triage; not tied to a single GitHub issue -- see jj-idea-6oeg's notes for the GitHub threads (GitHub #93, #97) that raised drag-and-drop generally.
close_reason: Duplicate: jj-idea-6oeg's drag-and-drop spike already completed (closed 2026-09-01) and filed jj-idea-ibth (Drag a bookmark or tag chip onto a commit to move it) as the real follow-up. Filed in error before checking 6oeg's current status.

title: Working-copy status bar widget has no width cap (GitHub #95)
description:
SergejSalnikov (GitHub #95, 2026-08-31) reports that the working-copy status bar widget can take the whole status bar, hiding other widgets. Their diagnosis (full description exposed) is wrong -- the render path already shows only the first line: WidgetPanel.update() -> canvas.append(RevisionChoice.Change(entry)) -> TextCanvas.append(choice) (ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:342) -> appendSummary (LogEntryText.kt:61) -> Description.summary, which is display.lineSequence().first() (jj/Description.kt:7). The real bug: that first line is rendered with no width cap.

Root cause: appendSummary wraps the description in truncate{} and FragmentRecordingCanvas.truncate (FragmentRecordingCanvas.kt:67) records the truncatable range, but TextCanvasPanel.renderFrom (ui/components/TruncatingLeftRightLayout.kt:44) lays fragments out with a plain BoxLayout and never calls FragmentLayout.truncateToFit -- only LaidOutCell.kt:37, TextListCellRenderer.kt:41, and TruncatingLeftRightLayout.configure (:158) do that. So the widget's preferred width is the full first line. IdeStatusBarImpl lays out its right panel with GridBagLayout, fill=VERTICAL (platform IdeStatusBarImpl.kt:508-514) -- nothing shrinks a widget that reports a large preferred width, so the widget must bound itself.

Also: JujutsuStatusBarWidget.displayTextFor (JujutsuStatusBarWidget.kt:35, MAX_DISPLAY_LEN=40) is dead production code -- its only callers are in JujutsuStatusBarWidgetTest.kt. That's why a 40-char cap appears to exist while the widget actually does something else.
design:
Bound the widget's rendered width by BOTH a fixed pixel budget and a proportional share of the status bar width: budget = min(JBUI.scale(MAX_PX), statusBarWidth * MAX_FRACTION). Then reuse FragmentLayout.truncateToFit(canvas.fragments, canvas.truncateRange, budget, font, frc) and render via TextCanvasPanel.renderFrom(FragmentRecordingCanvas(truncated)) -- the same two-line pattern already used at TruncatingLeftRightLayout.kt:158. Because only the description carries the truncate marker (see appendSummary(entry) in LogEntryText.kt:198, which calls appendBookmarks/appendTags outside truncate), the change id and bookmark/tag chips are unaffected and only the description text ellipsizes.

Status bar width: read from the StatusBar/its component passed to install(); add a ComponentListener (resize) to re-run the truncation, since the proportional budget depends on live width. The existing tooltip (buildTooltip) already carries the untruncated text, so no information is lost by truncating the visible label.

Resolve displayTextFor: either wire it into the real render path (unlikely -- it duplicates logic appendSummary already does via different plumbing) or delete it along with its now-vacuous JujutsuStatusBarWidgetTest.kt tests, replacing them with tests of the new truncation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A pathologically long first-line description leaves other status bar widgets visible at any window width (verified both very wide and narrow IDE windows). A unit test pins the budget formula as min(fixed_px, statusBarWidth * fraction) and asserts truncateToFit is applied only to the description fragment range, leaving change-id/bookmark chips intact. displayTextFor is either live or removed; no dead code with passing-but-meaningless tests remains.
notes: GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/95
close_reason: Fixed: widget width now capped via WidgetTextLayout.budget/fit, reusing FragmentLayout.truncateToFit

title: Drag files into a gap to split into a new change
description: A Files payload dropped in a Gap (top/bottom band) opens the pre-filled SplitDialog to split those files out of their own change into a new one at that position (jj-idea-6oeg design doc section 1) - split(revision, filePaths, insertBefore) already accepts exactly this shape (splitArgs, CliExecutor.kt:211). Same zone geometry as the squash bead's drop, different operation chosen by the gap vs centre distinction. Restrict to gaps bordering the files' own change - reject other gaps via setDropPossible(false, 'Files can only be split out next to their own change').
acceptance_criteria: Dragging a file selection into a gap adjacent to their owning commit opens SplitDialog pre-filled with those files and the insertBefore position. Gaps not adjacent to the files' own change are rejected with a reason.
notes: Implemented: DropOperation.SplitFiles wired to performFileSplit (SplitFilesAction.kt) via new DropOperation.SplitFiles.toNewParent() edge mapping; DragGuards.kt rejects a non-owning gap with the exact 'Files can only be split out next to their own change' message. Same test/doc coverage as jj-idea-yvry (shared PR). Manual GUI verification still needed.
close_reason: Implemented, tested, and manually verified in this session; both fixes found during live GUI testing (dialog title, stuck reject overlay) are in.

title: Drag files from the changes tree onto a commit to squash
description: A Files payload dropped on a CommitRow target's centre band opens the pre-filled SquashIntoDialog rather than applying blind (jj-idea-6oeg design doc sections 1 and 3) - squashing is genuinely destructive (merges content, abandons the emptied source, combines descriptions). Drag source via the platform's ChangesTreeDnDSupport (JujutsuChangesTree already extends AsyncChangesTreeImpl.Changes, i.e. is a ChangesTree, so this is largely reusing existing platform infrastructure for the source side).
acceptance_criteria: Dragging a file selection from the changes tree onto a commit's centre band opens SquashIntoDialog pre-filled with those files as source and the target commit as destination.
notes: Implemented: ui/common/JujutsuChangesTreeDnD.kt (installFilesDragSource wired into JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel and UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel), DragGuards.kt filesRejectionReason, DropPerformers.kt SquashFiles now wired to performFileSquashInto (SquashIntoFilesAction.kt), DragContextHolder.kt fixes cross-component drag context bug. Unit + platform tests added, ./gradlew check green. Manual GUI verification (MT-DND > Files -> commit squash, files -> gap split) still needed - no GUI in this session.
close_reason: Implemented, tested, and manually verified in this session; both fixes found during live GUI testing (dialog title, stuck reject overlay) are in.

title: Drag a bookmark or tag chip onto a commit to move it
description: A BookmarkRef/TagRef payload dropped on a CommitRow target runs bookmarkSet(name, revision)/tagSet (jj-idea-6oeg design doc section 1). Reuse the existing backwards-move handling verbatim: actions/bookmark/moveBookmarkAction.kt already parses jj's 'backwards or sideways' stderr and re-prompts with allowBackwards=true on failure - the drag gesture should trigger that same path rather than reimplementing it. Applies immediately with an undo balloon on success.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging a bookmark or tag chip (from the log table) onto a commit row moves it there. A backwards/sideways move triggers the existing confirm-and-retry flow. Cross-repo drops are rejected.
notes:
Depends on jj-idea-6jvh and jj-idea-v9zp.
See docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md for batch scope, sequencing, and the preview-gating design. Find your batch's siblings with: bd list --label dnd-batch-N
close_reason: Shipped batch 2: chip payloads (move bookmark/tag onto a commit, local-onto-remote push dialog) and copy-modifier duplicate, all wired through DropPerformers.forLogTable

title: Drag a local bookmark chip onto its remote chip to push (log-only)
description: jj-idea-6oeg design doc sections 1 and 7. Remote bookmarks already render as chips in the log (CliLogService.kt's remoteBookmarkTemplate emits name@remote, joined into LogEntry.bookmarks) - so when local is ahead of a tracked remote, main and main@origin sit on different rows and dragging one chip onto the other is a natural push gesture requiring no bookmarks panel. MUST open the pre-filled GitPushDialog(initialBookmark, initialRemote) rather than pushing directly - same policy already applied to actions/bookmark/pushBookmarkAction.kt ('mutating a remote is not something to fire with no confirmation'). Never immediate-apply.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging a local bookmark chip onto its name@remote chip opens GitPushDialog pre-filled with that bookmark and remote, never pushes without the dialog. Degenerate case (chips coincide because already synced) is handled gracefully (no-op or disabled, not a crash).
notes:
Depends on jj-idea-6jvh (core). Does NOT depend on the bookmarks-panel bead - this works within the log table alone.
See docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md for batch scope, sequencing, and the preview-gating design. Find your batch's siblings with: bd list --label dnd-batch-N
close_reason: Shipped batch 2: chip payloads (move bookmark/tag onto a commit, local-onto-remote push dialog) and copy-modifier duplicate, all wired through DropPerformers.forLogTable

title: Drag a commit onto a commit: rebase (onto / before / after)
description: Headline gesture of jj-idea-6oeg (docs/design/jj-idea-6oeg-drag-and-drop-graph-ops.md section 1/3). Dragging a Commit payload onto a CommitRow target runs rebase(revisions, [target], ONTO); dropping in the top/bottom Gap runs rebase with destinationMode INSERT_BEFORE/INSERT_AFTER against that row. Applies immediately (no confirmation dialog) and shows the undo balloon on success - uses CommandExecutor.rebase, already implemented.
design:
Implementation plan (researched 2026-09-04, not yet built).

PREREQUISITES / SEQUENCING
Batch 1 = this bead alone (docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md Part C). Blocked on
jj-idea-vpvz (batch 0 preview gating), which also adds the PreviewFeature.DRAG_AND_DROP guard at
the top of installDragAndDrop. jj-idea-p6nb (copy-modifier duplicate) is batch 2 - see the
"COPY-MODIFIER" section below, which this bead must handle even though p6nb ships later.
6jvh (core) and v9zp (undo) are both closed, so everything below is unblocked once vpvz lands.

STATE OF PLAY
6jvh shipped the whole DnD shell: payload/target model, y-aware zone hit-test, hysteresis, guards,
dispatch matrix, indicator painting, DnDSupport wiring. DropPerformers.forLogTable returns null
(ui/dnd/DropPerformers.kt:18), which makes the target checker reject every drop with no indicator
ever painted. This bead supplies the first real performer and turns the headline gesture on.

Throwaway spike commit ywtrquqrrpnl ("wip: DnD verification spike, do not push", a sibling of
master, not an ancestor) has the correct Rebase -> CommandExecutor.rebase argument mapping and
nothing else: no undo tracking, errors swallowed, bare repo.invalidate(), Duplicate unhandled,
over-long lines. Take the mapping, discard the rest, `jj abandon ywtrquqrrpnl` when done.

1. SHARED REBASE EXECUTOR - actions/change/rebaseAction.kt
Split the tail of performRebase (currently lines 32-45) into:

  internal fun executeRebase(project: Project, repo: JujutsuRepository, spec: RebaseSpec) {
      repo.commandExecutor.withUndoTracking()
          .createCommand { rebase(spec.revisions, spec.destinations, spec.sourceMode, spec.destinationMode) }
          .onSuccess {
              repo.invalidate(select = spec.revisions.first(), vfsChanged = true)
              rebaseLog.info("Rebased ${spec.revisions} onto ${spec.destinations}")
          }
          .onFailure { tellUser(project, "log.action.rebase.error") }
          .withUndoBalloon(project, repo, "log.action.rebase.undo")
          .executeAsync()
  }

performRebase keeps only the dialog + dialog.result handling and calls it. DECIDED (Kevin,
2026-09-03): one shared wiring path, accepting that the existing Rebase... dialog action gains the
undo balloon it does not have today - the alternative (an opt-in flag) was rejected as a wart.
withUndoTracking() is mandatory: without it the result is Success.Irreversible(NOT_TRACKED) and
withUndoBalloon never fires. Chain ordering (.withUndoBalloon after onSuccess/onFailure, right
before executeAsync) mirrors abandonChangeAction.kt:51-57, the only undo-wired action today.
Reuses RebaseSpec (ui/rebase/RebaseDialog.kt:22) rather than inventing a parameter object.

2. THE PERFORMER - ui/dnd/DropPerformers.kt
Replace the null stub. Pure, testable mapping:

  internal fun DropOperation.Rebase.toRebaseSpec() = RebaseSpec(
      revisions = sources.map { it.id },
      destinations = listOf(destination.id),
      sourceMode = RebaseSourceMode.REVISION,
      destinationMode = mode
  )

RebaseSourceMode.REVISION is NOT arbitrary - it must match what DragContext.forDrag assumed when
computing the cycle-exclusion set (ui/dnd/DragGuards.kt:72). Comment the coupling; differentiating
source mode is jj-idea-j8ij, which is blocked on this bead.

Performer body: val repo = operation.destination.repo (cross-repo is already rejected by
DragContext.rejectionReason), then executeRebase(project, repo, spec); true. Re-check nothing else -
resolveLive (JujutsuLogTableDnD.kt:102) runs the guard before dispatch.

Make the when exhaustive over the sealed DropOperation (no else), each unwired variant returning
false with a comment naming its own bead. A future new DropOperation variant then becomes a compile
error here rather than a silent no-op drop.

3. COPY-MODIFIER / DropOperation.Duplicate - the batch-1 trap
resolveDropOperation already returns DropOperation.Duplicate for a copy-modifier commit drag, and
installDragAndDrop's target checker only tests `performer != null` - it never asks whether the
resolved operation is actually wired. So the moment this bead installs a non-null performer, a
copy-modifier drag lights the indicator and shows a "Duplicate ..." tooltip, then silently does
nothing on release. Since p6nb is batch 2, this bead must close that gap itself.

Fix: change the seam from `((DropOperation) -> Boolean)?` to a small interface -

  interface DropPerformer {
      fun supports(operation: DropOperation): Boolean   // consulted on every mouse-move; keep O(1)
      fun perform(operation: DropOperation): Boolean
  }

and have the target checker take resolveLive(...)?.takeIf { performer.supports(it.operation) }.
Duplicate (and every other unwired op) then rejects cleanly with no indicator - the same "nothing
looks droppable before it is" discipline 6jvh established. p6nb later flips exactly one branch in
each of supports/perform. Add a test asserting supports is true for exactly the ops perform handles,
so the two halves cannot drift.

4. BUNDLE KEY
JujutsuBundle.properties: log.action.rebase.undo=Rebase, next to log.action.rebase.* (~line 529).
Bare verb phrase, matching log.action.abandon.undo=Abandon - it is interpolated into
notification.undo.content={0} completed. Error keys log.action.rebase.error.title/message already
exist and are reused as-is.

5. DOC COMMENTS
JujutsuLogTableDnD.kt:36-39 and DropPerformers.kt's KDoc both currently state that no performer
exists and nothing is ever droppable. Both become false - rewrite them.

TESTS
New src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/dnd/DropPerformersTest.kt, plain JUnit 5 + kotest + mockk,
following DropOperationDispatchTest.kt's local entry(id) / mockk<JujutsuRepository>(relaxed = true)
style (no @TestApplication):
- toRebaseSpec for all three RebaseDestinationModes and for a multi-source drag; assert
  sourceMode == REVISION (the DragGuards-consistency invariant).
- supports() true for Rebase only; false for every other variant.
- perform() on an unwired variant returns false and never touches the executor
  (verify { repo.commandExecutor wasNot Called }).
executeRebase's chain itself stays manual-verified - it ends in executeAsync() against a real jj
process. If the manual smoke raises doubt, the precedent for asserting the balloon without the
platform is the injected notify seam used in UndoBalloonPlatformTest.kt.

SCALE ANALYSIS (contributing.md Performance & Scale)
No new filesystem traversal and no new per-file/per-commit loop. The performer is O(s) where s =
dragged selection size (bounded by selection, not log size), run once per drop, not per mouse-move.
The per-mouse-move path (DragContext.rejectionReason) is untouched and stays O(1), already locked in
by DragContextScaleTest; supports() must stay a type check to keep it that way. No new
operation-count test required - state this explicitly rather than omitting it.

DOCS
- docs/manual-tests.md: the "Drag and drop - core infrastructure (jj-idea-6jvh)" subsection
  (lines 281-302, under MT-LOG-TABLE) asserts "no drop should ever actually apply" - now false.
  Rewrite into a real gesture checklist: centre band rebases --onto; top band -> -A, bottom band ->
  -B (verify against `jj log` in a terminal - the top/bottom <-> -A/-B mapping is deliberately
  non-identity, see DropTarget.kt:20-34, and was a shipped bug once); undo balloon appears and its
  Undo link reverts; multi-select drag; guards reject (immutable, cycle, self-drop) with the right
  tooltip; copy-modifier drag is rejected with no indicator until p6nb lands. Keep the retained
  regression bullets (selection not fighting the indicator, SmoothAutoScroller).
- CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased], user-facing wording only (no class names).

MANUAL REGRESSION SCOPE (finalise by grepping 'Code:' tags at implementation time; expected union)
- MT-LOG-TABLE - owns the drag-and-drop subsection being rewritten.
- MT-CTXMENU - Rebase... now shows an undo balloon; confirm the dialog path is otherwise unchanged.
- MT-LOG-REFRESH - goes through repo.invalidate(..., vfsChanged = true).
- MT-WORKINGCOPY - shares the Rebase context action with the log menu.
Four sections, under the ~6 escalation threshold.

VERIFICATION
1. ./gradlew check. Pre-existing ktlint failures in CliExecutor.kt, CliExecutorSplitTest.kt,
   CliExecutorSquashTest.kt are untouched by this change.
2. ./gradlew runIde against a scratch repo (scripts/fixtures/; fx-stress.sh for the many-lane case):
   - Drag a mutable commit onto another's centre -> row outline, tooltip "Rebase <id> onto <id>",
     release applies; confirm the new parent with `jj log` in a terminal.
   - Top band -> thin band outline, tooltip "...inserting after..."; confirm with `jj log` that it
     landed VISUALLY ABOVE the destination (this is the -A mapping).
   - Bottom band -> -B, lands visually below.
   - Each shows a balloon; click Undo -> graph returns to its prior shape. Dismiss a balloon and use
     the persistent Undo Last Operation action instead.
   - Hold the copy modifier -> reject cursor, no indicator (until p6nb).
   - Drag onto an immutable commit / onto a descendant of the dragged commit -> reject cursor, no
     indicator, correct tooltip; drop does nothing.
   - Regression: single/shift/ctrl click, double-click diff, right-click menu still behave.
3. jj abandon ywtrquqrrpnl (the spike).
acceptance_criteria: Dragging a commit row onto another commit's centre band performs rebase --onto; dropping in the top/bottom band performs -B/-A against that row. All three apply immediately with an undo balloon. Guarded against immutable destinations and cycles via the core bead's checks.

See docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md for batch scope, sequencing, and the preview-gating design. Find your batch's siblings with: bd list --label dnd-batch-N

description:

title: Diff shows previous commit's contents after switching commits in the log
description:
## Repro
History a -> b -> c, all three commits touch the same file (same relative path, same
change status e.g. all MODIFIED). In the log's commit details panel:

1. Select change b. Double-click the file's row -> opens diff a..b. Correct.
2. Select change c. Double-click the same file's row -> the editor tab title updates to
   "c: file", but the diff content shown is still a..b (stale).
3. Closing that editor tab and double-clicking again from c reproduces the same stale
   content -- it is not a one-off render glitch, and it is not a diff-request cache
   artifact (closing/reopening should have forced a fresh producer lookup).

## Root cause (confirmed by reading the code)

The changes tree backing the details panel is never rebuilt for the new selection, because
of a same-ness check that only compares file paths, not revisions.

- JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.loadChanges (src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/log/JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt:200-217):
  ```kotlin
  if (currentEntries == entries && !sameChangesAndStatuses(changes, changesTree.changes)) {
      changesTree.setChangesToDisplay(changes)
      changesTree.invokeAfterRefresh { changesTree.treeExpander.expandAll() }
  }
  ```
- sameChangesAndStatuses (src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/common/JujutsuChangesTree.kt:182-183):
  ```kotlin
  fun sameChangesAndStatuses(a: List<Change>, b: List<Change>): Boolean =
      a.size == b.size && a.indices.all { i -> a[i] == b[i] && a[i].fileStatus == b[i].fileStatus }
  ```
- Platform `Change.equals` (vcs-api-core Change.java:137-153) compares **only the
  before/after FilePaths** of the two Changes -- it does not look at the ContentRevisions
  (i.e. not at which commit's content they point to). `hashCode` is likewise path-only
  (Change.java:156-169).

So when c's freshly-loaded Change list has the same file path(s) and same FileStatus as
b's currently-displayed Change list (the common case -- same file modified again), the
guard decides "nothing changed" and skips `setChangesToDisplay`. The changes tree keeps
holding b's Change objects, whose before/after ContentRevisions are still a and b.

Everything downstream is then internally consistent but wrong:
- Double-click routes through DiffDataKeys.EDITOR_TAB_DIFF_PREVIEW ->
  JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview (ui/common/JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview.kt) -> the platform's
  TreeHandlerDiffRequestProcessor wraps the *tree's* selected Change (still b's) and builds
  a genuinely-correct a..b diff for that stale Change.
- The editor tab title is computed independently: getEditorTabName reads the contextLabel
  lambda, which reads `currentEntries` (JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt:76-82) -- and
  `currentEntries` HAS been updated to c by this point (set unconditionally before the
  guarded block). Hence "title says c, content shows a..b".
- Closing and reopening the editor doesn't help: nothing about the platform's diff-request
  cache is stale here (see below) -- the changes TREE's data is stale, and it stays stale
  until some other selection eventually produces a Change list with different paths/statuses.

This regressed from the fix for jj-idea-q6vn ("skip no-op tree rebuilds" to preserve diff
scroll position across background refreshes of the *same* selection), later extended by
jj-idea-3cvb to also compare fileStatus. The guard is correct when re-loading the SAME
selection (e.g. background refresh) but wrong when the selection moves to a DIFFERENT
commit that happens to touch the same paths.

Ruled out: this is not a bug in the plugin's ContentRevision equality
(jj/JujutsuContentRevisions.kt) or in the platform's CacheDiffRequestProcessor /
ChangeDiffRequestProducer. Those revisions are already `data class`es with value equality
keyed on change id specifically so the platform's diff-request cache (which DOES compare
ContentRevisions via ChangeDiffRequestProducer.isEquals) works correctly across background
refreshes. The bug is one layer up, in the tree-rebuild guard never handing the platform a
new Change in the first place.

UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt uses the same sameChangesAndStatuses helper, but its selection
is always the working copy, so it isn't affected in practice -- worth a defensive test
regardless since it shares the helper.
design:
Make the rebuild guard revision-aware, not just path/status-aware. Extend
sameChangesAndStatuses (ui/common/JujutsuChangesTree.kt:182) to also require that each
pair's before/after ContentRevisions match:

    a[i].beforeRevision == b[i].beforeRevision && a[i].afterRevision == b[i].afterRevision

The plugin's own ContentRevision implementations (ContentLogEntryImpl,
MergeParentContentRevision, EmptyContentRevisionImpl in jj/JujutsuContentRevisions.kt) are
already data classes, so `==` correctly discriminates by change id. The one wrinkle is
CurrentContentRevision (platform class, used for the working-copy side) which has no value
equality -- compare it by FilePath instead, mirroring
ChangeDiffRequestProducer.isEquals(ContentRevision, ContentRevision)'s special case. Do NOT
call ChangeDiffRequestProducer.isEquals directly: it iterates ChangeDiffViewerWrapperProvider
/ ChangeDiffRequestProvider extension points and needs a live Application, which would break
sameChangesAndStatuses's current pure/unit-testable nature.

This preserves jj-idea-q6vn and jj-idea-3cvb: on a background refresh of the SAME commit
selection, the reconstructed Change list has revisions that are value-equal to what's
already displayed, so the early-out still fires and tree expansion / diff scroll position
are still preserved. It only stops early-outing when the selection has genuinely moved to
a different commit that happens to share file paths and statuses with the old selection.
acceptance_criteria:
- With history a -> b -> c all touching one file: select b, double-click the file -> diff
  shows a..b. Select c, double-click the file -> diff shows b..c (not a..b). Verified both
  as a fresh open and as close-tab-then-reopen.
- A background refresh (e.g. jj snapshot) of an UNCHANGED selection still does not rebuild
  the changes tree -- existing scroll/expansion-preservation behavior from jj-idea-q6vn and
  conflict-decoration behavior from jj-idea-3cvb keep passing.
- Unit test added directly against sameChangesAndStatuses: two Change lists with identical
  FilePaths and identical FileStatus but different ContentRevisions (different change ids)
  -> returns false.
close_reason: Fixed: sameChangesAndStatuses now also compares before/after ContentRevisions

title: Remove dead parent-commit-id field from LogEntry.Identifiers
description: LogEntry.Identifiers(changeId, commitId) carries a parent's commit id, fetched from real jj log output (extra per-parent template field/parse cost), but nothing in production code ever reads it - every consumer (RebaseSimulator, SplitSimulator, DagNode, graph building, topological sort, reference-ancestor-key computation, merge-annotation reconciliation) only reads .changeId. The only read anywhere is one integration-test non-blank check on real CLI output, not a real consumer. This forced RebaseSimulator's DagNode.withParents (jj-idea-fjsg) to fabricate a CommitId.PLACEHOLDER sentinel for a value nothing needs - exactly the kind of silent-lie risk the user flagged (found via code review of jj-idea-fjsg): 'if used later, a sentinel is harder to pin down than null or a sealed hierarchy'. Investigation (see conversation) confirmed zero legitimate consumers, so the fix is to remove the field entirely rather than make it nullable: replace LogEntry.Identifiers with plain parentIds: List<ChangeId>, drop CliLogService's per-parent commit-id template fetch, delete CommitId.PLACEHOLDER, simplify SplitSimulator's parent-Identifiers fabrication (its SYNTHETIC_COMMIT stays for entries' own commitId, which is a legitimate, separate use). Touches ~15 test fixtures that currently build a throwaway CommitId(...) just to satisfy the old constructor.
acceptance_criteria: ./gradlew check passes; LogEntry.Identifiers class no longer exists; CommitId.PLACEHOLDER no longer exists; CliLogService's parents template no longer fetches per-parent commit ids
close_reason: Removed LogEntry.Identifiers/CommitId.PLACEHOLDER entirely - LogEntry.parentIds is now plain List<ChangeId> (the stored field). CliLogService no longer fetches per-parent commit ids from jj. SplitSimulator/RebaseSimulator/DagNode simplified accordingly. Updated ~15 test fixtures and the contract test asserting the old changeId|commitId wire format. ./gradlew check and contractTest green (net -65 lines).

title: Generalize RebaseSimulator onto a minimal DagNode interface
description: Pure refactor, no behavior change. RebaseSimulator's whole dependency on concrete LogEntry collapses to id+parentIds+one copy(parentIdentifiers=...) call (always with a fabricated placeholder commit id already). Extract interface DagNode<T : DagNode<T>> { id, parentIds, withParents(parentIds): T } in ui/log/DagNode.kt (named to anticipate future unification with GraphableEntry, see follow-up bead). Add CommitId.PLACEHOLDER constant (mirrors ChangeId.EMPTY) replacing 4 inline all-zero CommitId literals in RebaseSimulator.kt. LogEntry implements DagNode<LogEntry> via withParents. RebaseSimulator's private helpers become internal + generic over <T : DagNode<T>>; public simulate(List<LogEntry>,...): RebaseSimulation signature unchanged, so RebaseDialog/RebasePreviewPanel need zero changes. Existing RebaseSimulatorTest.kt must stay green UNCHANGED as proof of behavior-preservation; add a new lightweight test using a hand-rolled DagNode stub (no JujutsuRepository/LogEntry/platform types) mirroring GraphTestHelpers' string-based entry() helper for CommitGraphBuilder.
acceptance_criteria: ./gradlew check passes; RebaseSimulatorTest.kt is byte-for-byte unmodified and green; new DagNode-based test exists and is green; no LogEntry.copy() calls remain in RebaseSimulator.kt
close_reason: Extracted DagNode<T> (id, parentIds, withParents) in ui/log/DagNode.kt; RebaseSimulator's internal reparent helpers generic-ized over it; CommitId.PLACEHOLDER added; public simulate() signature and RebaseSimulatorTest.kt untouched (verified behavior-preserving). New DagNodeReparentTest.kt exercises the algorithm via a minimal stub with no platform deps. ./gradlew check green.

title: Add per-file diff preview to Squash Into dialog

Extract/mirror Split's preview panel (currently inline in SplitDialog, not shared) into ui/common or a squash-local equivalent, and wire it into SquashIntoDialog next to the existing FileSelectionPanel (ui/common/FileSelectionPanel.kt). Distinct from jj-idea-uuy9, which is the log-graph simulation preview (mirroring RebasePreviewPanel/RebaseSimulator), not a file diff.

title: Insert a new change before/after a selected change (jj new -A / -B)
description: Today "New Change" only ever creates a child of the selected revision(s) - NewChangeAction / newChangeFromAction in src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/actions/change/, both calling CommandExecutor.new(description, parentRevisions). GitHub #83 asks for the ability to insert a change before or after a selected change from the log, corresponding to `jj new -A` and `jj new -B`, which rebase descendants onto the new change rather than branching the DAG. Work: extend the new contract in CommandExecutor.kt (+ CliExecutor + StubCommandExecutor + a contract test in src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/jj/cli/), then add log context-menu entries alongside the existing New Change entries. Related prior art for insert-before topology: closed bead jj-idea-tkog (jj split -B). Old bead jj-idea-un5 was closed as "already implemented" but only covers jj new <rev>, not -A/-B insertion.
acceptance_criteria: From the log, right-click a change and choose insert-before/insert-after: a new change is inserted before/after it, its descendants are rebased onto it, @ moves to the new change (or stays put per jj semantics), and the log reselects correctly.
close_reason: Implemented via a unified New Change... dialog (onto/insert-after/insert-before, description, --no-edit toggle, live rebase-simulator preview, immutability guard) replacing 'New Change with Description...'; CommandExecutor/CliExecutor/StubCommandExecutor threaded with destinationMode+edit; contract tests added for -A/-B against both real jj and the stub; arg-builder unit tests added; docs/manual-tests.md updated.

title: Stale log toolbar survives in-place plugin update, causing ClassCastException between plugin classloaders (GH #86)
description: Split out of GH #73/#86. Plugin's VCS EP is dynamic, so IDE hot-swaps in place on update. Two contributing leaks: (1) JujutsuCustomLogTabManager/JujutsuFileHistoryTabManager dispose() only clear their internal map, never remove Content from the platform-owned ChangesViewContentManager, so the stale panel+toolbar survive unload; (2) CommitTablePanel.createActionGroup() caches GitFetchAction/GitPushAction instances resolved once via ActionManager.getAction instead of resolving lazily. Stale toolbar keeps calling update() on old-classloader actions, which resolve the new plugin's JujutsuStateModel service and CCE on the implicit checkcast to the old class. See https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/86 for full root-cause writeup and stack traces.
acceptance_criteria: Steps 1+2 fix the CCE and make hot-update clean (verified via install-over-running-IDE smoke test). Step-3 audit tracked as child issues; a leak-free unload confirmed via -Dide.plugins.snapshot.on.unload.fail=true.
notes: Fixed: (1) JujutsuCustomLogTabManager.dispose() and JujutsuFileHistoryTabManager.dispose() now remove their Content from ChangesViewContentManager (dispose=false, to avoid firing the close-disposer which would wipe persisted LogWindowConfig settings). (2) CommitTablePanel's toolbar resolves Jujutsu.GitFetch/GitPush lazily via new LazyActionById instead of caching ActionManager.getAction() instances at construction. (3) JujutsuStateModel.dispose() now also releases repoRootWatchRequests (was only releasing opHeadsWatchRequests) - confirmed watch-root leak found during the step-3 audit scoping. Verified: ./gradlew check green (new LazyActionByIdTest platform test covers the delegation mechanism); a platformTest LeakHunter failure seen once was confirmed to be pre-existing suite flakiness (retention path through platform's own VcsMappingsWatchRootsModifier, unrelated to these files) by reproducing on baseline and re-running with these changes multiple times clean. Remaining broader unload audit tracked separately as jj-idea-8awj.
close_reason: Fix implemented and verified; broader audit split into jj-idea-8awj

title: Log expansion errors when selected change is abandoned/rewritten (GitHub #76 follow-up)
description: loadContext (RepoLogCache) throws when the target revision no longer exists instead of returning empty as documented, surfacing as an uncaught background exception (VcsException: Revision ... doesn't exist). JujutsuLogTable also re-fires the expansion on every refresh because expansionPending/pendingSelection are never cleared on failure, so the error repeats. Fix: wrap loadContext's revset in present(...) and route through a non-throwing fetch; add an onMissing callback from loadExpanding so the log table clears the stale pending selection; same underlying fix for fetchOne so get() throws the documented IllegalArgumentException instead of VcsException. See GitHub issue #76 latest comment for the reporter's stack trace.
close_reason: Fixed: loadContext wraps target in present(...) so a vanished revision resolves to empty instead of erroring; loadExpanding gains onMissing callback so the log table drops the stale pending selection instead of retrying every refresh.

title: Redesign 'Split into New Parent' to use jj split -B (real insert-before topology)
description: jj-idea-qswq shipped a hack: 'Split into New Parent' just pre-ticks SplitDialog with the inverse file selection and runs the same plain jj split, so it doesn't create real insert-before topology and the dialog's Parent/Child labels don't say which side keeps the original change ID or where @ ends up (user feedback after manual testing). jj split gained -B/--insert-before, -A/--insert-after, -o/--onto in jj 0.30.0 (below JjVersion.MINIMUM 0.37.0, so no version gating needed). With -B <rev>, the fileset passed to jj split becomes a NEW commit inserted before <rev>, and everything else stays on the ORIGINAL change ID - the polarity flip needed for a true 'peel off a new parent' operation, vs default (no flag) which is what 'Split into New Child' already correctly uses. Needs: CommandExecutor/CliExecutor insertBefore param threading, SplitDialog relabeling (retire Parent/Child wording, which is backwards for the shipped hack, in favor of role-neutral 'New commit'/'Stays here' labels), explicit working-copy-movement messaging, and updated tests (CliExecutorSplitTest, SplitDialogTest, SplitFilesActionTest, SplitActionParserTest, contract/JjStub + MutatingCommandsContractTest). Requires hands-on verification of jj split -B's stderr polarity and @ behavior before wiring description-chaining logic. Full design in plan at /Users/kevin/.claude/plans/icons-give-edit-immutable-oasis.md (Fix 4).

title: 'Show History' invisible in commit details panel's file-change context menu
description: Regression/incomplete fix from jj-idea-cb3r (batch-3): ShowFileHistoryAction.update() reads CommonDataKeys.VIRTUAL_FILE via e.file, which JujutsuChangesTree never supplies (only VcsDataKeys.CHANGES + LOG_ENTRY), so the action is always disabled/invisible in the commit-details panel's file tree, the working copy panel, and JujutsuCompareChangesPanel - it only worked from the editor/Project View context where VIRTUAL_FILE is real. Fix: resolve target via e.restorePaths/e.singleRepoForRestore (falling back to e.file/e.repoForFile for the editor context), following the OpenChangeFileAction/RestoreSelectionAction pattern. See plan at /Users/kevin/.claude/plans/icons-give-edit-immutable-oasis.md (Fix 3).

title: Give Edit a default keyboard shortcut; make Rebase/Describe show their shortcut hint in the context menu

design:
# jj-idea-9ife — Don't crash the IDE when a `.jj` repo can't be read by jj

## Context

Starting the IDE in a project surfaced a red **"IDE Internal Error"** balloon:

```
com.intellij.openapi.vcs.VcsException: Error from jj log: Internal error:
Failed to determine the secure config for a repo
Caused by: Cannot access /Users/kevin/workspace/feathernet/.jj/repo/config.toml
           No such file or directory (os error 2)
  at CliLogService.getLog (CliLogService.kt:246)
  ... RepoLogCache.fetch (LogCache.kt:119) .getOrThrow()
  ... JujutsuStateModel.workingCopies (JujutsuStateModel.kt:191)
  ... runInBackground (Tasks.kt:39)
```

**Why it happens:** the plugin's only "is this a jj repo?" check is
`JujutsuRootChecker.isJujutsuRoot` = "a `.jj` **directory** exists"
(`JujutsuRepository.kt:96`). A `.jj` dir that jj itself cannot open — a broken/stale
store, or a workspace whose real repo was moved/deleted (missing
`.jj/repo/config.toml`) — passes this check, gets registered in
`initialisedRepositories`, and then the `workingCopies` state-loader calls
`logCache[WorkingCopy].getOrThrow()`, which throws a `VcsException`. Because that
loader runs inside `runInBackground`, its catch-all `log.error(...)` (`Tasks.kt:45`)
escalates the exception into IntelliJ's fatal-error reporter — the red balloon.

**Intended outcome:** a `.jj` directory jj can't read is excluded up front, so none of
the per-repo state loaders ever touch it (no crash, no repeated failing retries), and
the user gets a single clear notification explaining why that repo shows no data.

**Chosen approach (confirmed with user):** up-front exclusion only, plus a one-time
warning notification. No changes to the loader/`runInBackground` fatal-error path.

## Changes

### 1. Repository readability probe — `JujutsuRepository.kt`
- Add to the `JujutsuRepository` interface: `val isReadable: Boolean`, documented as
  "Requires `isInitialised`; probes whether jj can actually open the repo — excludes a
  broken/stale `.jj` that passes the directory check."
- Implement in `JujutsuRepositoryImpl` mirroring `isInitialised` (line 96):
  `override val isReadable get() = commandExecutor.root().isSuccess`.
  (`commandExecutor` already calls `requireInitialised()`, which is a pure FS check — no
  recursion, since `isInitialised` does not probe.)

### 2. Lightweight probe command — `CommandExecutor.kt` / `cli/CliExecutor.kt`
- Add `fun root(): CommandResult` to the `CommandExecutor` interface.
- Implement in `CliExecutor`: `override fun root() = execute(root, listOf("root"))`
  (alongside `status()` at `CliExecutor.kt:337`).
- **Why `jj root`, not the existing `status()`:** any repo-scoped jj command fails with
  the "secure config" error (config load happens early in jj startup), but `jj root`
  does **not** snapshot the working copy, whereas `jj status` does. Since the probe runs
  on the happy path (every readable repo, every repo-set change), the cheaper command
  keeps startup cost negligible.
- Test doubles that mock `CommandExecutor` are `mockk(relaxed = true)` and won't break;
  update any hand-written fake if the build surfaces one.

### 3. Exclude unreadable repos — `JujutsuStateModel.kt` (`initialisedRepositories`, ~lines 127–133)
Replace the current `filterValues { isInitialised … }` with a three-way filter that keeps
the existing uninitialised handling and adds the unreadable case:
```kotlin
.filterValues { repo ->
    when {
        !repo.isInitialised -> {
            JujutsuNotifications.notifyUninitializedRoot(project, repo); false
        }
        !repo.isReadable -> {
            JujutsuNotifications.notifyUnreadableRoot(project, repo); false
        }
        else -> true
    }
}
```
This is the single choke point every per-repo loader reads
(`workingCopies`, `references`, `closestBookmarks`, `gitRemotes`), so excluding here
protects all of them at once.

### 4. One-time notification — `ui/services/JujutsuNotifications.kt`
- Add `notifyUnreadableRoot(project, repo)` mirroring `notifyUninitializedRoot`
  (lines 58–87): a new `ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet<String>()` for per-root dedup,
  `NotificationType.WARNING`, and a single **"Configure VCS Mappings…"** expiring action
  reusing `project.showVcsMappingsSettings()`. Omit the "Initialize" action — init won't
  repair an unreadable repo.
- Extend `clearNotificationState(rootPath)` to also drop the new set's entry so a repaired
  repo can re-notify if it breaks again.

### 5. Bundle strings — `resources/messages/JujutsuBundle.properties` (near line 669)
- `notification.unreadable.title=Jujutsu Repository Could Not Be Read`
- `notification.unreadable.content=The directory ''{0}'' has a .jj directory but jj could not read it — it may be broken or point to a repository that has moved. Its Jujutsu data will not be shown. Check the repository or change the VCS mapping.`
- `notification.unreadable.action.settings=Configure VCS Mappings...`

## Scale analysis (per CLAUDE.md)
The probe adds **one `jj root` subprocess per VCS root**, and only when
`initialisedRepositories` reloads — bootstrap, VCS config change/activation, `.jj`
VFS create/delete, `InitAction`, and jj-became-available (see
`JujutsuStateModel.kt:424–441`). Complexity is **O(number of VCS roots)** (typically 1,
a handful at most), never per-file or per-commit, and `jj root` skips the working-copy
snapshot. It is dwarfed by the per-repo `jj log`/bookmark/remote calls already made on
each repo-set change. This is not a filesystem traversal or per-file/per-commit loop, so
no operation-count test is required by the envelope.

## Critical files
- `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/jj/JujutsuRepository.kt` — `isReadable`
- `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/jj/CommandExecutor.kt` + `jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt` — `root()`
- `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt` — exclusion filter
- `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/services/JujutsuNotifications.kt` — `notifyUnreadableRoot`
- `src/main/resources/messages/JujutsuBundle.properties` — strings

## Tests
- **`JujutsuRepositoryImplTest`** (unit, mockk — existing patterns at lines 27–52): add
  cases that `isReadable` is `true` when `commandExecutor.root()` returns a success
  `CommandResult` and `false` when it returns a failure (non-zero exit) — mirror the
  existing `commandExecutor`/`CommandResult` mocking already in this file.
- **`JujutsuNotifications`** one-time dedup: assert `notifyUnreadableRoot` fires once per
  root path and is suppressed on a second call (small unit test; follow existing
  notification-test conventions if present, else a focused test of the keyset guard).
- The `initialisedRepositories` filter wiring is a one-line pattern over
  `JujutsuRepositoryImpl` built from live VCS mappings + real jj, so its integration is
  covered by manual smoke rather than a heavy platform test.

## Verification (end-to-end)
1. `./gradlew check` — unit + platform tests pass.
2. Manual reproduction of the reported bug:
   - In a scratch project, create a valid jj repo (`jj git init --colocate`), confirm the
     Jujutsu tool window populates.
   - Break it: `rm -rf .jj/repo` (or move the store so `.jj/repo/config.toml` is gone),
     leaving `.jj` present. Reopen the project / trigger a VCS re-scan.
   - **Expected:** no red "IDE Internal Error" balloon; a single WARNING notification
     "Jujutsu Repository Could Not Be Read" with a "Configure VCS Mappings…" action; the
     tool window shows no data for that repo (empty / hidden if it was the only repo);
     `idea.log` shows the excluded root, not a fatal error. Trigger another refresh —
     the notification does **not** repeat.
   - Repair the repo and re-scan — data returns to normal.

## Docs & bookkeeping (per CLAUDE.md)
- Add a manual-test scenario to `docs/manual-tests.md` (new `MT-*`: "broken/unreadable
  `.jj` repo is excluded with a one-time warning, no internal error"), and report the
  **Manual regression scope**: the repo-detection / tool-window-enable path (the
  `initialisedRepositories` → tool-window + working-copy-panel surfaces).
- On "finish": `./gradlew check` → CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry (user-facing:
  "The IDE no longer reports an internal error when a Jujutsu repository can't be read;
  it's skipped with a one-time warning instead") → `jj describe` → `bd export` →
  `jj bookmark set master` → ask before push. Close `jj-idea-9ife`.
## Post-investigation update (2026-08-24)

The `isReadable`/`jj root` probe above was **not implemented**. Investigation found it
doesn't work: `jj root` only resolves the workspace path and never opens the backend, so
it passes exactly the broken-store repos it was meant to catch (measured: `rm -rf
.jj/repo/store` → `jj root` exits 0, `jj log` exits 2). The reported "secure config"
error was also a stale-jj-version artifact (a dangling symlink jj 0.44+ no longer
creates), not reproducible on the current jj.

**Actual fix shipped:** guard the one loader that wasn't already fault-tolerant —
`JujutsuStateModel.workingCopies` — with a `catch (e: VcsException)` that skips the repo
and shows a one-time "Jujutsu Repository Could Not Be Read" warning
(`JujutsuNotifications.notifyUnreadableRoot`), instead of an up-front probe. This also
covers a repo that breaks *after* startup, which a startup-only probe would miss. See
`src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt` (`loadWorkingCopies`) and
`docs/manual-tests.md` § "Unreadable Repository (jj-idea-9ife)".
close_reason: Follow-up UX pass after manual testing: JujutsuRepositoryHealth cache backs JujutsuRootChecker.validateRoot() (red mapping row), a differentiated tool-window empty state with Retry, a Retry action on the notification, and a non-recursive .jj/repo/ watch so repairs are auto-detected without the user needing to reselect the VCS mapping (which is a platform no-op when unchanged).

title: One-time upgrade nudge for version-gated features
description: Surface 2 of jj-idea-xuah. Add JujutsuNotifications.notifyFeaturesGatedByVersion(project, version, gatedFeatures), following the existing pattern in JujutsuNotifications.kt (same GROUP_ID, NotificationAction style). Fire it from JujutsuStartupActivity when JjAvailabilityStatus resolves to Available AND unsupportedFeatures(version) is non-empty. Balloon lists the gated feature names + required version, with actions 'Update jj' (opens Settings -> Jujutsu) and 'Don't show again'. Persist dismissal in JujutsuApplicationSettings keyed by the jj version string (e.g. featureNudgeDismissedForVersion) so it reappears only if the user's jj version changes or a newly-added JjFeature becomes gated - never repeatedly for the same state. Must never fire during Scenario A (VersionTooOld/NotFound/InvalidPath) - that path already has its own notification.
acceptance_criteria: Balloon fires at most once per (jj version, set of gated features) combination; 'Don't show again' persists and suppresses future nudges for that version; the show/skip decision is a pure function under unit test; no nudge fires when status is not Available.
close_reason: Implemented startup upgrade nudge; unit tests + docs + changelog done

title: JjFeature: display name + unsupportedFeatures(version) helper
description: Shared core for the two Scenario-B surfaces (Settings list and upgrade nudge). JjFeature (src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/jj/JjFeature.kt) currently has no user-facing display name. Add a displayNameKey (JujutsuBundle message key) per feature entry, and a pure helper 'fun unsupportedFeatures(version: JjVersion): List<JjFeature>' returning features whose minVersion > version. Also add a convenience overload driven by JjAvailabilityStatus that only reports when status is Available (never during Scenario A / VersionTooOld), reusing the existing versionOrNull/supports helpers.
acceptance_criteria: Pure unsupportedFeatures(version) function exists and is unit tested (empty list when version supports everything; correct subset when it doesn't). Each JjFeature has a bundle-backed display name. Status-based overload returns empty for non-Available statuses.
close_reason: Added displayName + unsupportedFeatures(version)/(status) helpers to JjFeature, bundle-backed name, and unit tests

title: Settings: Feature availability list
description: Surface 1 of jj-idea-xuah. In JujutsuConfigurable.kt (Settings -> Version Control -> Jujutsu, which already shows install/upgrade guidance), add a 'Feature availability' section listing each JjFeature: its display name, required jj version, and a supported/not-supported indicator against the currently detected jj version. This is the passive, no-spam discovery path for a user who noticed a disabled action and wants to know why / what to upgrade to.
acceptance_criteria: Settings -> Jujutsu shows one row per JjFeature with name, min version, and supported/unsupported status vs the detected jj version; updates when jj availability is rechecked.
close_reason: Added a collapsed-by-default Feature Availability group to Settings -> Jujutsu, listing only gated features and auto-expanding when any exist; pure display-state mapping in FeatureAvailability.kt, unit tested.

title: Surface version-gated feature availability to users
description: The plugin has two 'jj is too old' cases. Scenario A (jj below the plugin's hard minimum, JjVersion.MINIMUM) already gets a proactive startup balloon (JujutsuNotifications.notifyJjUnavailable) plus an in-tool-window panel (JjNotInstalledPanel) - this is intentional and complete, no change needed here. Scenario B (jj meets the minimum but is below a specific JjFeature's minVersion, e.g. BOOKMARK_ADVANCE needing 0.39.0) currently only disables the affected action with a relabelled tooltip - no notification at all, per the deliberate 'no global balloon' decision in closed bead jj-idea-asap. This umbrella revises that decision: add two new surfaces for Scenario B so users can discover why actions are greyed out and learn they could upgrade jj to unlock them, without spamming (one-time nudge, dismissible, plus a passive settings list).
acceptance_criteria: Scenario A documented as complete (no code change). Scenario B gets: (1) a passive Feature availability list in Settings -> Jujutsu, (2) a one-time dismissible upgrade nudge balloon fired at most once per detected jj version. Both consume a shared unsupportedFeatures(version) helper on JjFeature.
close_reason: Both Scenario B surfaces shipped: one-time upgrade nudge (jj-idea-sov0) and passive Feature Availability list in Settings (jj-idea-vcqn), both built on the shared unsupportedFeatures() helper (jj-idea-gg1r). Scenario A was already complete, no code change needed.

title: Batch plan: GitHub-issue triage groupings (2026-08-19)
description: Triage of 25 from-github-issue beads (plus a few non-GitHub beads sharing code) into 5 batches, grouped by shared files/mechanism so each batch ships as one PR with one manual-regression pass. Full writeup: /Users/kevin/.claude/plans/i-have-a-barrage-foamy-lerdorf.md (local plan file, not synced — this bead is the durable record). title: Add more toolbar buttons to log window (GitHub #78)
description: toddjonker (GitHub #78) wants frequently-used log actions — specifically calls out Rebase and Describe — available from the log window's own toolbar with keyboard shortcuts, rather than only via the right-click context menu. Notes the toolbar currently has an apparently-unused empty row above the table (unlabeled column headers) that could hold more buttons. jj-idea-cpno (bookmark widget relocation to the main IDE toolbar, shipped unreleased 2026-08-19) explicitly freed up log-toolbar width as a stated prerequisite for this ask, so the space constraint that would otherwise block this is already resolved.
design: Scope needs deciding: which actions earn a permanent toolbar slot (Rebase and Describe are reporter's explicit picks) vs. staying context-menu-only. Most/all of the candidate actions likely already exist as registered Jujutsu.* actions (context menu pulls them via ActionManager, per the pattern noted in jj-idea-66id's investigation of JujutsuLogContextMenuActions.kt) so this is largely a placement/registration exercise plus keybinding assignment, not new action logic. The 'empty row above the table' the reporter points at is worth checking — confirm what it actually is (filter row? column header placeholder?) before assuming it's free real estate.
