design:
# Native jj conflict resolution UX (jj-idea-n6fz)

**Status: design, pre-implementation.** This is the follow-up design work `jj-idea-9ms6`
(GitHub #63) explicitly deferred: that issue fixed a *destructive bug* in the borrowed git-shaped
merge dialog (closing without resolving silently discarded a side) without questioning whether the
dialog itself is the right shape for jj. This document makes that case, inventories what the
plugin already has to build on, and splits the remaining work into sized, independently-shippable
children under this epic.

## The model mismatch

Git's conflict model: resolving is a one-shot, index-mediated transaction. The working file is
disposable scratch — the index is authoritative, and once you `git add` the resolved file the
markers are gone for good. IntelliJ's `MergeProvider2`/`MultipleFileMergeDialog` is built entirely
around that: open a modal, pick sides or hand-edit, close it, done. There is no partial state
between "conflicted" and "resolved" that git's own tooling represents.

jj's conflict model is different in a way that matters for UI design, not just terminology:

- **A conflict is a first-class object stored in the commit**, not an index entry. It has no
  separate "resolved" flag distinct from the markers themselves.
- **The working file's markers ARE the conflict record.** They're materialized fresh from the
  commit on checkout and **re-parsed from scratch on every snapshot** — there is no other source
  of truth to fall out of sync with.
- **Resolution is naturally incremental.** Edit some markers, save, keep working on something
  else, come back later — jj simplifies the conflict on the next snapshot as markers disappear.
  Nothing requires an atomic "did you finish the whole file" transaction.
- **Conflicts exist at any revision, not just `@`.** `jj resolve -r <rev>` and `jj file show -r
  <rev>` both work on arbitrary commits. Multiple descendants can carry copies of the same
  conflict simultaneously (jj propagates conflicts downward through rebases).
- **Full undo history via evolog/op log.** A resolution is just another operation; `jj undo`
  reverses it like any other command.

A modal, one-shot, working-copy-only dialog is a reasonable UI for git's model. For jj's, it's a
borrowed shape that actively fights the tool underneath it — which is exactly why GitHub #63
happened: the platform's merge tool assumes the file it's editing is disposable, and jj's working
file is never disposable.

## What already exists (do not rebuild)

The plugin has already built substantial jj-native infrastructure around conflicts; this design
composes it rather than replacing it.

| Piece | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Marker parser, all 3 styles + GitHub #112 side reorientation | `jj/conflict/JjMarkerConflictExtractor.kt` | `extract(ByteArray): ExtractedConflict?`. Handles git/snapshot/diff marker styles and rebase-conflict "Yours" reorientation. |
| `jj resolve --list` line parser | `jj/conflict/ConflictInfo.kt` | `ConflictInfoParser.parse(stdout): Map<String, ConflictInfo>`; shape text (`"2-sided conflict including 1 deletion"`) preserved verbatim. |
| Per-path conflict shape cache | `jj/conflict/JujutsuConflictRegistry.kt` | **Working-copy only** today — see gap below. |
| #63-safe scratch-document merge tool | `vcs/merge/JujutsuConflictResolver.kt` | Kept as an accelerator (see "What stays as-is"). |
| `MergeProvider2` + bulk `:ours`/`:theirs` | `vcs/merge/JujutsuMergeProvider.kt:114` `acceptFilesRevisions` | Routes through `jj resolve --tool` so modify/delete conflicts actually delete rather than leaving an empty file. |
| Read a conflict at an arbitrary revision (read-only) | `vcs/diff/JujutsuConflictDiffRequestProvider.kt` | GitHub #119 / `jj-idea-ct7e`. The primitive S3/S4 below reuse for the write side. |
| Single funnel all four resolve gestures route through | `actions/change/workingCopyConflicts.kt:30` `resolveConflicts(project, files)` | Log menu, file action, toolbar button, tree-node link, and the editor banner all call this. |
| Editor banner | `ui/editor/JujutsuConflictEditorNotificationProvider.kt` | Today: static text + one "Resolve" link. S1 below extends this in place. |
| "Merge Conflicts" tree node + toolbar button | `ui/common/JujutsuConflictsNode.kt`, `actions/file/ResolveAllConflictsAction.kt` | Unaffected by this design. |
| Command wrappers, both already revision-parametrised | `jj/CommandExecutor.kt:365` `resolveList(revision)`, `:375` `resolve(paths, tool, revision)`; args at `jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt:377,380` | The CLI layer already supports everything S3/S4 need; nothing new to add there. |

### Gaps found while surveying the above

- **`jj/ChangeService.kt:68` `conflictedPathsFor` re-implements path extraction from `jj resolve
  --list` by hand** instead of reusing `ConflictInfoParser.parse(...).keys` (which
  `vcs/changes/JujutsuChangeProvider.kt:196` `parseConflictPaths` already does correctly), and it
  discards the sides/deletions shape entirely. Net effect: `JujutsuConflictRegistry` — the only
  place that shape data is cached — is **only ever populated for the working copy**, never for a
  historical revision. Every design slice that wants shape data (modify/delete detection, a
  Conflicts view row) at a non-`@` revision needs this fixed first.
- **`actions/change/resolveConflictsAvailability.kt`'s `NEEDS_EDIT` state** exists purely because
  `JujutsuMergeProvider.loadConflict` is hard-coded to `WorkingCopy` (see its own doc comment,
  `JujutsuMergeProvider.kt:47-51`) — a git-shaped "you can only resolve what's checked out"
  limitation. jj itself has no such restriction. Retiring this state is the single biggest UX
  unlock in this design (browsing history and fixing a conflict on a non-`@` commit without first
  checking it out) and is scoped as its own spike (see S4) because the interactive write-back path
  has never been exercised off-`@` and needs a safety check before committing to a full feature.
- **No inlay hints, line markers, or `GutterIconRenderer`s exist anywhere in the plugin yet.** The
  only gutter-adjacent code is `diffedit/HunkArrowDiffExtension.kt` (diff-viewer arrows, gated to
  the hunk-picker session) and `vcs/diffbase/DiffbaseContentLoader.kt` (the platform's own
  line-status-tracker gutter, not custom rendering). S2 below is the first consumer of this kind of
  UI in the codebase and should expect to spend real design/prototyping time on it, not just wire
  up an existing pattern.

## What stays as-is

`JujutsuConflictResolver` and the `MergeProvider2`/`MergeSessionEx` wiring in
`JujutsuMergeProvider` are **not removed or replaced** by anything in this design. They remain the
three-way merge tool, reachable as an explicit "Open Merge Tool" action from every entry point.
Reasons to keep it:

- It is the only path that gives a full three-pane diff view for hand-editing a complex conflict —
  genuinely useful, not just a fallback.
- It integrates with the platform's own multi-file merge dialog (Commit tool window, when a user
  opts back into it) via `MergeProvider2`, which several other IntelliJ subsystems key off.
- The GitHub #63 fix living in `JujutsuConflictResolver` (scratch-document output, never handing
  the real file's Document to the platform) is a solved, tested problem. Nothing in this design
  reopens it.

The slices below make the editor — not the modal — the *default*, discoverable path, and demote
the modal to an accelerator reachable in one click, matching how git4idea itself increasingly
treats its own merge tool relative to inline gutter conflict actions.

## The six slices

Ordered by value and dependency. Each becomes its own beads issue (see epic children).

### S1 — Editor as the primary, incremental surface

Upgrade `JujutsuConflictEditorNotificationProvider` from a single static "Resolve" link into a
banner that reflects jj's actual model:

- **Live block count**, parsed from the editor's `Document` text (not just
  `ChangeListManager`'s binary `MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS` status), so the count decrements as the
  user hand-edits markers and the banner disappears once the last block is gone — without waiting
  for a jj snapshot.
- **Text that states the model**: something like "This file has 2 unresolved conflicts — edit the
  markers and save, or use the actions below" rather than the current generic "This file has merge
  conflicts."
- **`Accept <side-1 label>` / `Accept <side-2 label>` action links**, using
  `ExtractedConflict.currentTitle`/`lastTitle` for the label text (the same jj-native commit+role
  labels `JujutsuConflictResolver`'s pane titles already use, GitHub #112), routed through
  `CommandExecutor.resolve(paths, ":ours"/":theirs")` — reusing the exact call
  `JujutsuMergeProvider.acceptFilesRevisions` makes today, so modify/delete conflicts correctly
  delete the file rather than leaving empty content.
- **Secondary "Open Merge Tool" link** that calls the existing `resolveConflicts(project, files)`
  funnel, unchanged.

API sketch: `JjMarkerConflictExtractor` already returns block count implicitly (count of
`Segment.Conflict` entries) — expose a lightweight `blockCount(bytes): Int` alongside `extract`, or
reuse `extract(...)` output directly since the banner already has to call it for labels. No new jj
commands needed.

Risk: keeping the live count in sync with in-progress edits without re-parsing the whole document
on every keystroke — bind to `DocumentListener` with the same 300ms-class debounce pattern
`JujutsuStateModel.scheduleRepositoryRefresh()` uses, not a naive per-edit rescan.

### S2 — jj conflict markers as first-class editor regions

The natural conclusion of "the markers are the conflict record": recognize conflict marker blocks
as live editor regions (like IntelliJ's native git conflict gutter actions), not just something
scanned once for a banner.

- Incremental document scanner (rescans only the changed range after the first full pass — O(edit
  size), not O(file size), per contributing.md's performance rules) feeding `RangeHighlighter`s
  over each block.
- Per-block gutter actions: *Accept side #1 / side #2 / both / base*. Each edits the **document
  text directly** — replace the marker block with the chosen side's lines — with no jj command and
  no modal involved at all. This is the purest expression of the jj model: resolving a block is
  just an edit like any other; jj simplifies the conflict from the markers that remain on the next
  snapshot.
- All three marker styles (`JjMarkerConflictExtractor` already parses git/snapshot/diff) need
  matching editor-region recognition, including the git-style `|||||||` base section for an
  "Accept base" action where one exists.

This is a genuinely new UI surface for the codebase (no precedent — see gap above), largest scope
of the six slices, and depends on S1 only in that it shares the same document-scanning
infrastructure (worth building once, used by both).

### S3 — jj-native Conflicts view

A non-modal, multi-file conflicts list built directly on `resolveList(revision)` /
`ConflictInfoParser`, showing jj's own shape text per row (`"2-sided conflict including 1
deletion"`) rather than reconstructing that information from a platform-shaped `Change` list.

The key differentiator from the platform's `MultipleFileMergeDialog` (which this replaces as the
*bulk* affordance, alongside the existing "Merge Conflicts" tree node for the working copy): a
revision picker, so the view can show conflicts in **descendants and arbitrary other revisions**,
not only `@`. `CommandExecutor.kt:365`'s doc comment on `resolveList` — "infrastructure for the
future Conflicts tool window" — was written anticipating exactly this.

Depends on the registry gap (above) being fixed first, since a useful non-`@` conflicts view needs
`JujutsuConflictRegistry` populated for revisions other than the working copy. Also depends on the
S4 spike's outcome, since bulk actions in this view (accept side #1/#2 for every conflicted file at
a chosen revision) are exactly the write-at-arbitrary-revision operation S4 needs to validate is
safe.

Scale note for the implementing issue: listing conflicts for one revision is O(conflicts at that
revision), which `jj resolve --list -r` already bounds — no new per-file/per-commit loop on the
Kotlin side, so this needs an operation-count test only if the view adds its own scan (e.g.
resolving shape for every row eagerly) rather than lazily per visible row.

### S4 — Resolve at any revision (retire `NEEDS_EDIT`)

`jj resolve -r <rev>` and `jj file show -r <rev>` already exist as `CommandExecutor` calls and are
already exercised read-only by `JujutsuConflictDiffRequestProvider` (GitHub #119). What's missing
is the **write** side: letting the interactive per-file resolve flow
(`JujutsuConflictResolver`/the S1 banner's accept actions) target a revision other than `@` instead
of refusing via `NEEDS_EDIT`.

Filed as a **timeboxed spike**, not a feature, because the plugin has never exercised interactive
write-back off the working copy, and there are real open questions worth answering before
committing engineering time to the full feature: does resolving a conflict at a non-`@` revision
rebase every descendant that inherited the conflict (likely yes, matching `jj resolve -r`'s CLI
behavior) in a way the UI needs to communicate before the user commits to the action? Does the
existing undo/invalidate machinery (`JujutsuRepository.invalidate`) correctly refresh a log view
showing revisions far from `@`? The spike's job is to answer these with a working prototype and a
written recommendation, which S3's bulk-action scope and any follow-on "resolve this conflict from
the log, without checking it out first" feature both then build on.

### S5 — Undo affordance

Route S1's accept actions (and, if it ships, S2's per-block accepts once they trigger a snapshot)
through `createUndoTrackedCommand` — already used elsewhere for exactly this purpose — and surface
an "Undo" action in the resulting success notification. This makes jj's own "change your mind
later, it's all in the op log" property visible in the UI at the moment a conflict is resolved,
rather than requiring the user to know to look at Operation Log / `jj undo` separately.

Depends on S1 shipping first (nothing to attach undo to otherwise).

### S6 — Demote the modal merge tool

Once S1 (and ideally S2) are live and proven, re-point the *default* action of each existing entry
point — editor banner, tree-node link, toolbar button, log context menu — at the new editor-first
flow, with "Open Merge Tool" surviving everywhere as an explicit secondary action rather than the
only option. Ships last, deliberately: it's a pure UI re-wiring with no new logic, and doing it
before S1/S2 are validated in real use would remove the fallback before the replacement has proven
itself.

## Verification for the design itself

This document's own claims are checkable without writing code:

- Every `file:line` citation above resolves against the current tree (spot-checked while writing
  this doc).
- The "gaps found" section names concrete code (`ChangeService.kt:68`,
  `resolveConflictsAvailability.kt`'s `NEEDS_EDIT`) that a reader can independently confirm rather
  than taking on faith.

title: Bookmark reference filter shows wrong-repo ancestry and false graph links in multi-repo projects
description:
When filtering the log to a bookmark's reference (JujutsuReferenceFilterComponent's References
filter) in a multi-repo project, the filtered log incorrectly includes commits from *other*
repositories, and the graph draws lines making it look like the different repos' root commits
are parent/child of each other.

## Root cause

Two related code paths key by a bare `ChangeId` instead of the repo-scoped `ChangeKey(repo, id)`
that `topologicalSort` in UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt already uses for exactly this reason (see
its comment: "jj's root commit has the identical change ID... in every repository since it's
synthetic rather than content-derived, so a bare ChangeId key would conflate different repos' root
commits"). Every repo's root commit shares the id "zzzzzzzz", so any code that doesn't scope by
repo will conflate them - and in principle any other coincidentally-duplicated id would trigger the
same bug.

1. `JujutsuReferenceFilterComponent.getAncestorIds` (ui/log/JujutsuReferenceFilterComponent.kt)
   finds the entry matching the selected bookmark/tag/`@` via `allEntries.find { ... }` (no repo
   scoping) and then BFS-walks `entry.parentIds`/`allEntries.find { it.id == current }` purely by
   `ChangeId`. If any ancestor along the way shares an id with an entry in another repo (guaranteed
   at the root), the walk silently continues into that other repo's ancestry.

2. `JujutsuLogTableModel.setBookmarkFilter`/the filter check `bookmarkFilter.contains(entry.id)`
   (ui/log/JujutsuLogTable.kt, ~line 1040) filters by bare `ChangeId` membership too, so even if
   getAncestorIds were fixed to return repo-scoped ids, the current `Set<ChangeId>` filter shape
   can't distinguish "root of repo A" from "root of repo B" - both would pass.

3. `CommitGraphBuilder.buildGraph` / `GraphableEntry` (ui/log/JujutsuCommitGraph.kt) and
   `LayoutCalculatorImpl<ChangeId>` (ui/log/graph/LayoutCalculator.kt) build graph edges keyed by
   bare `ChangeId` too. Once entries from two repos with a colliding id land in the same rendered
   list (as they now do once #1/#2 pull in the wrong repo), the layout algorithm treats them as the
   *same* node and draws parent/child connector lines between unrelated repos - this is what makes
   the roots in the screenshot appear chained together in one line.

## Reported symptom

In a project with repos foo/bar/another-jj, jj-only, jj-coloc, yet-another-jj, another-jj,
filtering the log to a bookmark shows the bookmark + its real ancestry (correct), but *also* pulls
in every other repo's root commit ("zzzzzzzz", "no description", empty) and draws them as a single
connected line beneath the real ancestry, as if every repo's root were an ancestor of every other
repo's root.

## Fix direction

Both the ancestor-filter path and the graph-layout path need repo-scoped keys:
- `getAncestorIds` should scope its BFS to the repo(s) that actually carry the selected reference
  (a bookmark/tag name could in principle exist in more than one repo).
- The bookmark filter itself likely needs to become `Set<ChangeKey>` (or equivalent
  repo+id pair) rather than `Set<ChangeId>`, mirroring `ChangeKey` already used elsewhere
  (topologicalSort, changeSelection notifier).
- `CommitGraphBuilder`/`GraphableEntry`/`LayoutCalculatorImpl` need a repo-scoped identity for
  graph nodes/edges - either parameterize on `ChangeKey` instead of `ChangeId`, or otherwise
  ensure cross-repo id collisions can never be treated as the same graph node.

Related: jj-idea-2xf3 (Reference filter only shows one instance of working copy in multi-repo) is
the same area of code (getAncestorIds' WORKING_COPY case uses `.find`, so only the first repo's `@`
is matched) but a distinct symptom - fixing repo-scoping properly should likely resolve both
together, but keep them cross-referenced rather than merged since the symptoms differ.
design: Repo-scope the ancestor BFS and the bookmark filter set (Set<ChangeKey> instead of Set<ChangeId>), and give CommitGraphBuilder/GraphableEntry/LayoutCalculatorImpl a repo-aware node identity so cross-repo id collisions can never be laid out as the same graph node.
acceptance_criteria: Filtering to a bookmark/tag in a multi-repo project shows only that reference's own repo's ancestry - no other repo's commits appear, and the graph never draws a connecting line between commits from different repos, even when their ChangeIds coincidentally collide (e.g. the root commit's id).
close_reason: Repo-scoped GraphableEntry/CommitGraphBuilder/reference-filter BFS to ChangeKey; seeding the ancestor walk from every matching entry (not just the first) also fixes 2xf3's single-working-copy bug in the same change.

title: Address plugin compatibility warnings
description: There are several plugin compatibility warnings which, while they do not present as problems in current releases of Idea, could cause future compatibility issues. These need addressing. While doing this, also consider whether the plugin should have a maximum supported version, and find a way to be notified of new API releases ahead of Idea releases to allow time to provide compatible support.
design:
PLAN: triage, fix and then keep the compatibility warnings from reappearing.

Step 0 (data): the plugin verifier report is not currently in the tree (build/reports/pluginVerifier absent). Run `./gradlew verifyPlugin` (build.gradle.kts:240 pluginVerification, IDEs 2025.1-2026.2) and save the per-IDE reports ("Compatibility warnings", "Deprecated API usages", "Experimental API usages", "Internal API usages", "Override-only", "Non-extendable"). Record the full list in this bead's notes before changing anything. Classify each: (a) deprecated with a replacement available in sinceBuild 251 -> migrate; (b) deprecated, replacement only in newer platform -> keep, but isolate behind the existing source-set switch (src/main/kotlin-commitModeOld / -commitModeNew pattern, build.gradle.kts) and add a comment with the removal trigger; (c) internal/experimental with no alternative -> list with justification (contributing.md § Platform API compatibility already allows deliberate internal use, see build.gradle.kts pluginVerification comment); (d) scheduled-for-removal -> fix first, these are the real future breakage.
Step 1: fix (a) and (d); one commit/PR per API family so each is revertible.
Step 2 (the two side questions in the bead):
- Max supported version: Rec NO untilBuild (build.gradle.kts:225 `untilBuild = provider { null }` stays). Why: a pinned until-build makes the plugin vanish from newer IDEs the day they ship, and the plugin has been stable on new builds so far; instead rely on verifier runs. Reverse: set untilBuild to the latest verified branch (e.g. 262.*) and bump each release.
- Early notice of new APIs: Rec: add the IDE EAP/snapshot as an advisory (non-blocking) CI job: `create(IntelliJPlatformType.IntellijIdea, "LATEST-EAP-SNAPSHOT")`-style entry in a separate scheduled workflow (.github/workflows/, nightly cron) running `verifyPlugin` with `continue-on-error`, posting failures to the run summary. Also subscribe to the JetBrains Platform blog / `intellij-community` releases feed manually. Keep the PR-blocking verify list explicit (the comment at build.gradle.kts:262 says add each minor release as it ships).
Step 3: add a short checklist to contributing.md § Platform API compatibility: "when a new IDE minor ships, add it to verifyPlugin ides and resolve new warnings".

Decisions made without the user: the two Recs above (no untilBuild; advisory EAP CI job).
Scale: none (build-time). Testing: verifyPlugin clean or every residual warning justified in notes; ./gradlew check green; run the plugin once in IDE per MT-CROSS smoke only if a code path with runtime behaviour changed (list MT sections per API touched).
acceptance_criteria: Full verifier warning list recorded; all fixable (a)/(d) items migrated; residual items justified in code comments; decision on untilBuild recorded; advisory EAP verify job in CI; contributing.md checklist updated.

title: Stop invoking AnAction.actionPerformed() directly (OverrideOnly API misuse)
description: Plugin Verifier flags in.kkkev.jjidea.actions.ExtensionsKt.performAction(AnActionEvent, String) and performAction(String, DataContext, String) for calling AnAction.actionPerformed(AnActionEvent) directly. That method is annotated @ApiStatus.OverrideOnly — JetBrains reserves the right to change its invocation contract (e.g. update-before-call semantics), and client code should go through the supported entry point (e.g. com.intellij.openapi.actionSystem.ex.ActionUtil.invokeAction/performActionDumbAwareWithCallbacks or similar) instead of calling actionPerformed() directly. Present on every platform version checked (251 through 262), so it's not new API drift — just pre-existing technical debt surfaced by running verifyPlugin for the first time.
acceptance_criteria: ./gradlew verifyPlugin passes with 0 override-only API usage violations.
close_reason: Fixed: route performAction() helpers through ActionUtil.performActionDumbAwareWithCallbacks() instead of calling AnAction.actionPerformed() directly. verifyPlugin passes with 0 OverrideOnly violations across 251/252/253/262.

title: Build a custom hunk-checkbox picker to replace the merge widget in Split's Pick Hunks
description:
"Pick Hunks..." in the Split dialog currently reuses IntelliJ's 3-way merge widget
(createMergeRequest/showMerge/MergeThreesideViewer) for a task it wasn't designed for:
partitioning one commit's linear diff into two pieces (parent-remainder / child), not
resolving a real merge conflict between divergent branches. Across two redesign passes this
session we kept hitting friction traceable to that fundamental mismatch:

1. (jj-idea-5bx9, first pass) Reversed picking: making one side's content track the file's
   tick state meant the "live"/clickable hunks flipped sides depending on state, so accepting
   a change sometimes meant "keep it", sometimes "send it away".

2. (jj-idea-5bx9, second pass) Fixed by pinning both sides permanently (Left = Before, Right
   = Child's content, Middle = editable Parent) instead of tick-dependent flipping - confirmed
   via platform source (TextMergeChange installs both LEFT and RIGHT gutter operations
   unconditionally, gated only by that side's own resolved state) that both sides' accept
   actions are always simultaneously available per hunk, giving real bidirectional
   reversibility. This fixed the "empty diff when unticked" and "no way to reverse a pick"
   bugs.

3. (this issue) Even with the fixed-role redesign, clicking "Apply" while any hunk is left
   untouched (which is the NORMAL case for a genuinely-partial split, since we deliberately
   want the user to be able to leave hunks as-is) triggers a platform confirmation dialog with
   conflict-resolution wording that doesn't fit our context:

     Title: "Apply Changes" (DiffBundle key: apply.partially.resolved.merge.dialog.title)
     Message: "There is one change left unprocessed. Save changes and mark the conflict
       resolved anyway?" (DiffBundle key:
       merge.dialog.apply.partially.resolved.changes.confirmation.message)
     Buttons: "Continue Merge" / "Apply Changes and Mark Resolved"
       (DiffBundle keys: continue.merge / apply.changes.and.mark.resolved)

   Investigated whether this can be customized or suppressed, the same way we override the
   Cancel confirmation via DiffUserDataKeysEx.MERGE_CANCEL_MESSAGE. It cannot: the RESOLVED
   branch of MergeThreesideViewer.getResolveAction() (platform/diff-impl/src/com/intellij/
   diff/merge/MergeThreesideViewer.java:295-304) hardcodes MessageDialogBuilder.yesNo(...)
   directly with no UserDataHolder key, request parameter, or overridable hook consulted for
   title/message/button text - unlike the Cancel path (line ~309), which does go through
   MergeUtil.showExitWithoutApplyingChangesDialog and DOES honor MERGE_CANCEL_MESSAGE. The
   only way to change this wording is subclassing MergeThreesideViewer and reimplementing its
   resolve-action wiring entirely - an unsupported internal API surface (real risk of breaking
   silently on a future IDE update), decided against for now (see jj-idea-5bx9 notes / this
   session).

Given three separate friction points now traced to the same root cause (reusing
conflict-resolution machinery for a non-conflict partition task), the durable fix is a
purpose-built hunk-checkbox picker: a single diff view (base -> after) with a checkbox in the
gutter per hunk, directly matching the file-level tick's polarity (tick a hunk = it moves to
the child, exactly like ticking a file) - no "resolved" concept, no confirmation dialogs, no
merge-conflict framing at all.

Investigated reusing IntelliJ's OWN partial-commit hunk-checkbox UI (used in the Commit tool
window / shelve "exclude changes") for this - not viable: it requires a real VirtualFile +
Document + a PartialLocalLineStatusTracker registered in LineStatusTrackerManager, not two
ad-hoc strings (see jj-idea-5bx9 research notes). The realistic path is a custom viewer built
on the PUBLIC com.intellij.diff.tools.simple.SimpleDiffViewer base class plus
com.intellij.diff.util.DiffGutterRenderer for the checkbox icons (AllIcons.Diff.GutterCheckBox
/ GutterCheckBoxSelected), computing our own LineFragments and owning our own per-hunk
boolean selection state - essentially the SimpleLocalChangeListDiffViewer pattern minus the
VCS tracker coupling.

Related: jj-idea-twis (original tick/child regression, closed), jj-idea-v527 (subprocess
classpath crash, still open), jj-idea-5bx9 (the two merge-widget redesign passes this issue
supersedes, closed).
acceptance_criteria: Pick Hunks opens a custom diff view with per-hunk gutter checkboxes (no merge widget, no 'resolved' concept); ticking a hunk moves it to the child, same polarity as the file-level tick; no confirmation dialogs with conflict-resolution wording appear; selection persists across reopen without extra plumbing (derived directly from the same widget state, not a separate override map); ./gradlew check passes; docs/manual-tests.md updated.
close_reason: Redesigned per user feedback: 3-pane live-parent view (Before | eventual Parent, live | Child) with directional arrows, built on SimpleThreesideDiffViewer + replaceChange, replacing the intermediate 2-pane checkbox design. ./gradlew check, verifyPlugin (Compatible on all 5 pinned IDEs, zero new internal-API usages), and the 2025.1 floor leg all pass.

title: Signpost the Working Copy tool window to new users
description: GitHub #56 follow-up. A reporter didn't know the Working Copy tool window existed and was instead using IntelliJ's standard Commit panel (which looks similar but lacks jj-specific actions and has a broken Rollback, jj-idea-ad5d). The Working Copy panel is the intended jj-native daily-use surface (README.md describes it as the 'Describe-First Workflow' panel) but nothing actively directs new users to it — they land on the familiar Commit panel by default since that's where IntelliJ normally puts VCS work. Need some form of onboarding/signposting: e.g. a first-run notification pointing to the Working Copy tool window, a banner/hint in the Commit panel for jj roots, or making Working Copy the default-focused tool window when a jj project opens.
design: Related to and likely informed by the decision in the paired bead about what happens to the standard Commit tool window — if that gets hidden/suppressed, this may become less urgent since users won't have a confusing alternative to land on.
acceptance_criteria: New users opening a jj project are actively directed to the Working Copy tool window rather than discovering it by accident (or not at all).
close_reason: Implemented: Working copy tool window now auto-opens (once per project, no focus steal) plus a one-time per-install signpost balloon, on first jj project open.

title: Standard 'Rollback' action is a silent no-op (RollbackEnvironment not implemented)
description:
GitHub #56 and #84 (duplicate report). Clicking the platform 'Rollback' on a changed file opens the Rollback Changes dialog but discards nothing. JujutsuVcs (vcs/JujutsuVcs.kt) implements ChangeProvider/DiffProvider/MergeProvider/CheckinEnvironment but no RollbackEnvironment, so the platform dialog has nothing to execute. The intended discard path is the plugin's own 'Restore' action (jj restore, RestoreSelectionAction.kt:53 -> CommandExecutor.restore). Options: (a) implement a RollbackEnvironment on JujutsuVcs that runs jj restore for the selected files, or (b) hide/disable the platform Rollback action so it isn't a dead button. Prefer (a) so the familiar Rollback works. Never worked - RollbackEnvironment has only ever appeared in docs, never in code.

#84 (second, independent report) confirms this preference for (a): the reporter explicitly wants a dedicated 'Revert...' dialog for the Working Copy tree with a pre-checked file list (Mercurial-plugin screenshot attached in the issue), not just a context-menu action - which is exactly the platform RollbackChangesDialog that implementing RollbackEnvironment unlocks for free. Also flags a naming mismatch to resolve/document: platform calls this 'Revert'/'Rollback', the plugin's own equivalent is named 'Restore' (jj nomenclature).
design:
PLAN (option a - implement RollbackEnvironment; option b rejected: hiding the platform action leaves #84's pre-checked dialog request unmet)

Design
- Add `JujutsuRollbackEnvironment : RollbackEnvironment` in vcs/ (new file) and return it from `JujutsuVcsBase.getRollbackEnvironment()` (vcs/JujutsuVcsBase.kt, shared by both commitModeOld/New source sets, so no source-set duplication).
- `rollbackChanges(changes, vcsExceptions, listener)`: group `changes` by owning JujutsuRepository (existing repo-for-path helper used by the Restore actions: `singleRepoForRestore`/`restorePaths` in actions/), collect the FilePaths (for renames include BOTH the before and after paths so the rename is undone, not just the destination), call `CommandExecutor.restore(paths, WorkingCopy.parent)` (jj/CommandExecutor.kt:345; CLI args at jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt:129) once per repo (one jj invocation per repo, not per file), then `listener.accept(change)` for each rolled-back change. A failed CommandResult becomes a `VcsException` appended to `vcsExceptions`; never throw.
- After success: `repo.invalidate(vfsChanged = true)` (same as RestoreSelectionAction) and refresh the VFS for the touched paths so open editors reload (`RollbackEnvironment` contract: `RefreshVFsSynchronously`/`VfsUtil.markDirtyAndRefresh`).
- `getRollbackOperationName()` -> bundle key `rollback.operation.name` = "Restore" (decision below). `rollbackMissingFileDeletion` / `rollbackModifiedWithoutCheckout`: no-ops (jj has no checkout lock, files are never "missing" the way git/hg treat them; a deleted file is a normal change that restore recovers).
- Unversioned/ignored files: the platform dialog may hand us paths that are not in the working-copy diff; restore on such paths is a no-op in jj, so filter to paths present in `changes` only.
- Undo: reuse the Restore action's undo notification (`action.restore.selection.undo`) if performRestore's undo path is factored out; otherwise rely on jj op log and note it. Do not duplicate performRestore's dialog (the platform supplies the dialog).

Decisions made without the user (review/reverse)
1. Q: Name the operation "Rollback"/"Revert" (platform wording) or "Restore" (jj wording)? Rec: platform dialog stays titled by the platform; our operation name says "Restore" and the dialog description is via bundle. Why: jj-idea-hp8m adds a real `jj revert`, so calling this "Revert" would collide with it. Reverse: change one bundle string.
2. Q: Keep the plugin's own RestoreSelectionAction? Rec: yes, keep both - it already works and has the plugin's richer dialog. Reverse: remove later once Rollback is proven.
3. Q: Restore to parent (@-) or to the diff base? Rec: parent, matching RestoreSelectionAction.

Scale: O(selected changes) in memory plus one jj subprocess per repo; no filesystem traversal, no per-commit loop. Operation-count test: N selected files across R repos issues exactly R restore invocations.

Testing
- Unit (MockK executor, as in vcs/ tests): rollback calls restore once per repo with the right paths, listener called per change, rename includes both paths, failed result lands in vcsExceptions, empty list is a no-op.
- Contract test: real jj `restore` for a modified/added/deleted/renamed file (see existing contractTest conventions).
- Manual: new row in docs/manual-tests.md MT-WORKINGCOPY (select changed files -> Rollback -> pre-checked list -> confirm -> files restored; undo via op log). Manual regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY (primary), MT-CTXMENU (shared context menu entry), MT-CROSS (colocated Git projects: Rollback must route to the right VCS).
acceptance_criteria: Platform Rollback on changed files in the Working Copy tree restores them via jj restore (parent), showing the platform's pre-checked dialog; renames undone fully; failures surface as VcsException not silent; one jj call per repo; unit + contract tests pass; manual-tests MT-WORKINGCOPY updated.
close_reason: Closed

title: Annotate unavailable for historical-commit files
description:
When a file is opened from a historical commit (viewed as a JujutsuVirtualFile), the platform's built-in 'Annotate' action is disabled/unavailable.

Root cause: IntelliJ's AnnotateVcsVirtualFileAction (the platform action backing 'Annotate' for a file opened from history) only recognizes files that are instances of com.intellij.openapi.vcs.vfs.VcsVirtualFile or ContentRevisionVirtualFile (see AnnotationData.extractFrom in the platform). JujutsuVirtualFile extends AbstractVcsVirtualFile directly (src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/vcs/JujutsuVirtualFile.kt), so extractFrom() returns null and the action disables itself.

Additionally, that platform action requires the VCS's AnnotationProvider to implement com.intellij.vcs.AnnotationProviderEx (adds an annotate(FilePath, VcsRevisionNumber) overload). JujutsuAnnotationProvider currently only implements the plain AnnotationProvider interface.

Fix requires either:
1. Changing JujutsuVirtualFile to extend VcsVirtualFile instead of AbstractVcsVirtualFile, reconciling its custom async content-loading/cache-invalidation logic (background loads, MutableContentRegistry invalidation on logRefresh, ReadAction guards) with VcsVirtualFile's own myContent/myFileRevision/loadContent() model, plus implementing AnnotationProviderEx on JujutsuAnnotationProvider.
2. Or an alternative path that gets historical-commit files recognized by the platform's annotate-on-VCS-virtual-file action without disrupting existing diff/gutter functionality that depends on JujutsuVirtualFile's current behavior.

This is a real architectural change (JujutsuVirtualFile is used by diffs and gutters too), not a bolt-on fix, so it needs its own design/implementation pass. Found while investigating jj-idea-spyi (fixed separately: annotate-previous-revision for merges) and a related crash (annotate on a merge working copy hitting '@-' resolving to multiple revisions, also fixed separately).
acceptance_criteria: Opening 'Annotate' (right-click or Jujutsu menu) on a file viewed from a historical commit produces a blame gutter, same as for the current working-copy file.
close_reason: Fixed by widening JujutsuVirtualFile to extend VcsVirtualFile (with a JujutsuFileRevision) and implementing AnnotationProviderEx on JujutsuAnnotationProvider, so the platform's built-in Annotate action recognizes historical-commit files and File History revisions.

title: runInBackground silently swallows exceptions via unconsumed Future
description:
util/Tasks.kt's runInBackground(action) wraps work via ApplicationManager.getApplication().executeOnPooledThread<T> { ... }, returning a Future<T>. No caller in the codebase calls .get()/.get(timeout) on the returned Future, and executeOnPooledThread does not itself log exceptions thrown from the Callable - they're only captured inside the Future's internal state. Result: any uncaught exception thrown anywhere inside a runInBackground { ... } block (which is used extensively throughout the action layer, e.g. gitRemoteActions.kt, for network/CLI operations) vanishes completely - no idea.log entry, no user-visible notification, no crash. From the user's perspective this looks exactly like a button that 'doesn't respond'.

Surfaced while investigating jj-idea-3yyb (Push button unresponsive for default push scope) - could not confirm this is the actual cause there, but confirmed it as a real, general architectural gap that makes this whole class of bug silent and hard to diagnose.

Fix direction: have runInBackground (or a wrapping helper) catch Throwable, log it via the class Logger, and optionally surface a generic error notification to the user, rather than relying on every call site to remember to check its Future.
acceptance_criteria: An exception thrown inside any runInBackground block is logged and does not vanish silently; ideally also surfaced to the user via a generic error notification.
close_reason: Root cause fixed: runInBackground now logs uncaught throwables instead of swallowing them silently via an unconsumed Future

title: Migrate deprecated -d/--destination flag to --onto for rebase/duplicate
description: RebaseDestinationMode.ONTO uses the '-d' flag (jj/Revset.kt:176), consumed by both rebaseArgs and duplicateArgs (jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt:248,235). '--destination/-d' was deprecated in jj 0.36 in favour of '--onto/-o', with a finite removal window (following the same pattern as --allow-new's removal in 0.42, see jj-idea-dt2k). Should migrate before it is removed upstream. Note: need to verify 'jj duplicate' accepts --onto (rebase definitely does) before switching the shared enum used by both commands.
acceptance_criteria: RebaseDestinationMode.ONTO flag changed to --onto (or equivalent per-command handling if duplicate/rebase diverge); existing rebase/duplicate arg-builder tests updated; verified against real jj that both commands still work.
close_reason: Migrated RebaseDestinationMode.ONTO from -d to --onto; verified against real jj 0.37.0 for both rebase and duplicate; tests and ./gradlew check pass.

title: Destination/commit pickers in dialogs can't select commits outside the loaded log window
description:
Reported by user on a large repo: opening a picker dialog (Rebase, Squash Into..., Duplicate
Onto..., Move Bookmark to Change) only lets you search/select among commits already loaded
into repo.logCache (capped by settings.logChangeLimit(repo), the same cap that governs the
main log window). Typing a search term for a commit outside that window returns no results,
even though jj could resolve it directly.

All four dialogs share the identical pattern: they read repo.logCache.all once and filter it
client-side with `matchesSearch` on every keystroke (RebaseDialog.kt:129,256;
SquashIntoDialog.kt:196,323; DuplicateDialog.kt:109,204; MoveBookmarkToChangeDialog.kt:346).
None of them fall back to an actual `jj log -r <revset>` query when the search term doesn't
match anything in the loaded set.

Related but distinct: jj-idea-lpbv covers the same root limitation for the MAIN log window's
search box (Enter triggers a live jj query via loadExpanding). This issue is about the
picker dialogs specifically, which don't share that code path at all today - fixing lpbv
would not fix these dialogs.

Suggested approach: once lpbv establishes the "resolve a revset against jj and merge into
the loaded set" pattern (RevisionChoicePanel.scheduleResolve is another existing example of
that pattern), reuse it in these dialogs' loadDestinations/loadCandidates: if the local
filter returns nothing (or the user presses Enter) and the search text looks like it could
be a revision, run `present(<text>) | description(substring-i:"<text>") | ...` and splice
any hits into the picker.
acceptance_criteria: Rebase, Squash Into..., Duplicate Onto..., and Move Bookmark to Change dialogs can find/select a commit not in the currently-loaded log window (e.g. by full change ID or Git hash) via a live jj query fallback, not just client-side filtering of the loaded set.
close_reason: Shipped: shared CommitPickerPanel/LogSearchField give Rebase/Squash Into/Duplicate Onto/Move Bookmark to Change the log window's regex/case/whole-words search plus a whole-repo jj log fallback on Enter, so off-window commits are now findable.

title: Guard Duplicate Onto dialog against immutable-commit failures
description:
The Duplicate Onto... dialog (ui/duplicate/DuplicateDialog.kt, from jj-idea-vu35) lets the
user pick insert-after/insert-before destinations that jj will reject at the CLI because
they'd require rewriting an immutable commit. The dialog should prevent constructing an
invalid combination instead of surfacing a raw command failure.

See design in /Users/kevin/.claude/plans/lucky-napping-hennessy.md (this session) for the
full derivation from `jj duplicate --help` semantics and the immutable-set ancestor-closure
argument that collapses the check to two one-pass set builds (no graph search needed).
acceptance_criteria: Selecting an immutable commit disables insert-after/insert-before radios as appropriate (insert-after stays enabled for immutable heads); switching placement mode hides invalid destinations from the picker. Both directions are covered by unit tests on the pure guard functions.
close_reason: Added DuplicateImmutabilityGuard + bidirectional dialog wiring (hide invalid destinations by mode, disable invalid modes by selection)

title: Show a "Changes" file-list pane for the compare-with-working-copy diff flow
description: GitHub #52. The Compare with Working Copy action (and sibling compare actions) currently open changed files via ChainDiffVirtualFile(SimpleDiffRequestChain) — a bare diff chain with a file-selector dropdown and Next/Previous Difference navigation, but no persistent Changes pane listing the files with the current one highlighted. The plugin already owns the building blocks (JujutsuChangesTree + JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview, used by the commit-details and working-copy panels). Implementing this means routing the compare actions through a changes-tree-backed view instead of the bare chain. Files: actions/change/compareWithWorkingCopyAction.kt, actions/filechange/DiffRequestBuilder.kt (openDiffChain), and the sibling compare actions (CompareWithLocalAction, CompareBeforeWithLocalAction, ShowDiffInNewTabAction).
design:
# jj-idea-vtdl — "Changes" file-list pane for the compare-with-working-copy diff flow

## Context

GitHub #52 / beads `jj-idea-vtdl`. The **Compare with Working Copy** action and the
**Show Diff in New Tab** action open changed files via
`ChainDiffVirtualFile(SimpleDiffRequestChain)` — a bare diff chain with only a file-selector
dropdown and Next/Previous-difference navigation. There is **no persistent Changes pane**
listing the files with the current one highlighted, so the user loses the at-a-glance view of
"what changed" that Git's compare flows give.

The plugin already owns the building blocks used by the commit-details and working-copy panels:
`JujutsuChangesTree` (an `AsyncChangesTreeImpl.Changes`) driving a `JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview`
(a platform `TreeHandlerEditorDiffPreview`). This change routes the multi-file compare actions
through a **new panel** built from those blocks, shown in the platform's **VcsChanges tool
window** via `ChangesBrowserToolWindow.showTab(...)` — the same mechanism git4idea's
`GitShowDiffWithBranchPanel` uses for "Compare with Branch". Selecting a file in the tree
opens/updates the diff in the editor area (with the working-copy side editable).

**Decisions locked with the user:**
- **Mechanism:** own panel around `JujutsuChangesTree` + `JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview`, shown via
  `ChangesBrowserToolWindow.showTab`. (Not the platform `CompareWithLocalDialog`, and not a custom
  editor-tab VFS — keeping our jj-specific right-click actions in the pane.)
- **Scope:** multi-file actions only — `compareWithWorkingCopyAction` and `ShowDiffInNewTabAction`.
  The single-file `CompareWithLocalAction` / `CompareBeforeWithLocalAction` keep their current
  `DiffManager.showDiff` behavior (matches git, which uses a bare diff for single files).

## Why this works

The tree needs platform `com.intellij.openapi.vcs.changes.Change` objects. Our
`JujutsuRepository.createContentRevision(fileAtVersion)` already produces the right
`ContentRevision` per side — and returns an editable `CurrentContentRevision` when the side is the
working copy (`JujutsuRepository.kt:123-139`). So every `FileChange` the compare actions already
enumerate converts directly to a `Change`, exactly as `ChangeService.loadChanges` does
(`ChangeService.kt:35-47`).

## Changes

### 1. New panel + tool-window launcher — `ui/common/JujutsuCompareChangesPanel.kt` (new file)

Model it on `JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel`'s changes half (`ui/log/JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt:57-64,
124-161`) and `GitShowDiffWithBranchPanel`.

- `class JujutsuCompareChangesPanel(project, contextLabel: () -> String?)` — `JPanel(BorderLayout)`,
  `Disposable`, `UiDataProvider`.
  - `changesTree = JujutsuChangesTree(project)`; toolbar with Expand/Collapse All + `ChangesView.GroupBy`
    (reuse the `createChangesToolbar()` shape from the commit-details panel / `FileSelectionPanel`).
  - `diffPreview = JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview(changesTree) { contextLabel() }`;
    `Disposer.register(this, diffPreview)`.
  - `changesTree.installHandlers()` for the jj context menu. Do **not** inject
    `JujutsuDataKeys.LOG_ENTRY` — a compare-between-two-revisions view has no single owning entry, so
    entry-scoped actions correctly stay disabled.
  - `uiDataSnapshot(sink)` publishes `sink[DiffDataKeys.EDITOR_TAB_DIFF_PREVIEW] = diffPreview` so the
    tree's Enter/double-click opens the reusable diff editor tab (same wiring as commit-details).
  - `fun setChanges(changes: List<Change>)`: `changesTree.setChangesToDisplay(changes)` then
    `changesTree.invokeAfterRefresh { treeExpander.expandAll(); select first leaf; diffPreview.performDiffAction() }`
    so the first file's diff opens immediately (preserves today's "diff shows right away" behavior).
- `fun showCompareChangesTab(project, changes: List<Change>, tabTitle, contextLabel)`: build the panel,
  `ContentFactory.getInstance().createContent(panel, tabTitle, false)`, set the disposer + preferred
  focus component, then `ChangesBrowserToolWindow.showTab(project, content)` (auto-registers the
  "VcsChanges" tool window; replaces any prior compare tab). Empty-`changes` guard stays in the callers.

### 2. `Change`-producing builders — `actions/filechange/DiffRequestBuilder.kt`

Add alongside the existing `buildDiffRequests`, sharing the same before/after resolution:

- `fun FileChange.toChange(repo): Change = Change(before?.let(repo::createContentRevision),
  after?.let(repo::createContentRevision))` (platform derives added/deleted/modified/moved from the
  two sides; rename = differing before/after paths).
- `fun buildChanges(project, changes: List<FileChange>, files: List<VirtualFile>): List<Change>` —
  a mirror of `buildDiffRequests` (`DiffRequestBuilder.kt:22-75`) that emits `Change` instead of
  `DiffRequest`, keeping the three branches (changes / files-with-directory-expansion / empty) so
  `ShowDiffInNewTabAction`'s behavior is preserved. Same `O(files)` cost, no new filesystem traversal.

### 3. Route the two multi-file actions

- `actions/change/compareWithWorkingCopyAction.kt`: replace
  `buildDiffRequests(...)` + `openDiffChain(...)` with `buildChanges(project, changes, emptyList())`
  then `showCompareChangesTab(project, changes, "compare working copy: <id.short>", contextLabel = { id.short })`.
  Keep the off-EDT/`runLater` split and the existing empty-changes notification.
- `actions/filechange/ShowDiffInNewTabAction.kt`: in both branches build `List<Change>`
  (`ChangeService.loadChanges(logEntry)` for the logEntry-only branch; `buildChanges(project, changes, files)`
  otherwise) and call `showCompareChangesTab` with the same titles it computes today.
- Leave `openDiffChain` in place (still referenced elsewhere / fallback), unless it becomes fully unused.

## Key files

- New: `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/common/JujutsuCompareChangesPanel.kt`
- `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/actions/filechange/DiffRequestBuilder.kt`
- `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/actions/change/compareWithWorkingCopyAction.kt`
- `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/actions/filechange/ShowDiffInNewTabAction.kt`
- Reference (reuse, unchanged): `ui/common/JujutsuChangesTree.kt`,
  `ui/common/JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview.kt`, `jj/ChangeService.kt`, `jj/JujutsuRepository.kt`

## Testing

- **Unit test** the conversion in `DiffRequestBuilder`: `buildChanges` / `FileChange.toChange` maps
  add/delete/modify/rename to the correct before/after `ContentRevision`s and puts a
  `CurrentContentRevision` (editable) on the working-copy side. Use the existing contract stub infra
  (`contract/JjStub.kt`) for a repo whose `createContentRevision` is exercised; there is currently no
  test for `buildDiffRequests`, so this is net-new coverage.
- **Scale note (deliverable):** `buildChanges` is `O(files)` with no filesystem traversal added over
  `buildDiffRequests`; state this in the PR. No operation-count test needed (no new traversal/loop
  class introduced).
- **Manual smoke** (UI surface — update `docs/manual-tests.md`):
  1. In the log, right-click a commit → **Compare with Working Copy**; verify the VcsChanges tool
     window opens with a Changes tree of all differing files and the first file's diff open in the editor.
  2. Select other files in the tree → diff updates in the same reusable editor tab; working-copy side
     is editable.
  3. From a multi-file selection, **Show Diff in New Tab** → same pane appears.
  4. Compare a commit with no differences → info notification, no empty pane.

## Wrap-up (per CLAUDE.md "finish")

`./gradlew check` → add a user-facing `[Unreleased]` CHANGELOG entry → update `docs/manual-tests.md`
→ `bd close jj-idea-vtdl` → `jj describe` → `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl` →
`jj bookmark set master` → stop and ask before any push.
notes: Full implementation plan saved in the DESIGN field. Scratch plan file: /Users/kevin/.claude/plans/implement-jj-idea-vtdl-abstract-nova.md
close_reason: Implemented: Compare with Working Copy and Show Diff in New Tab now route through JujutsuCompareChangesPanel

title: Log filter: search whole repo on Enter (find commits outside loaded window)
description:
Today the log search field only matches commits already loaded in the log window (per the configured logRevset). Pasting a Git hash (or typing text) for a commit outside that window returns nothing, even though jj can resolve it. On Enter in the search field, run a jj query so hashes/text for commits outside the loaded window are still found.

Feasible via jj revsets (jj 0.37): build a revset from the box text, e.g. present(<text-as-revision>) | description(substring-i:"<text>") | author(substring-i:"<text>"), run one jj log -r, then load/select results by reusing loadExpanding (UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader) and project.stateModel.changeSelection / JujutsuLogTable.requestSelection.

Entry point: the Enter ActionListener at CommitTablePanel.kt:92; resolve off-EDT via runInBackground {} + runLater {} (util/Tasks.kt), mirroring RevisionChoicePanel.scheduleResolve.

Open questions to resolve during design: replace the loaded log with results vs. jump-to-single match; no-match UX; which surfaces opt in (main log only, not file history).
design: Mirror RevisionChoicePanel.scheduleResolve's debounced, off-EDT jj log -r resolution pattern. Build the revset from the search box text combining present()/description()/author() predicates.
close_reason: Shipped: Enter in the log search field now runs a whole-repo jj revset search, merging off-window matches into the log.

title: Filter changes deselect the current commit even when it remains visible
description:
Any filter change on the log table (clearing/changing the reference, author, date, text, or root filter) deselects the currently-selected commit, even when that commit still matches the active filters and stays visible in the table.

Root cause: JujutsuLogTableModel.applyFilter() (JujutsuLogTable.kt ~line 777-849) calls fireTableDataChanged() whenever any filter setter runs (filterText, authorFilter, bookmarkFilter, dateFilterCutoff, pathsFilter, rootFilter — see setters around lines 688-748). Swing's JTable clears its selection by default whenever the underlying TableModel fires a full data-changed event, since it can no longer assume row indices map to the same rows. This is separate from JujutsuLogTable.setEntries() (line 404), which already has selection-preservation logic (captures selectedEntry as pendingSelection, re-selects by ChangeId after the model update) for data reloads — but applyFilter() operates directly on the model and bypasses that path entirely.

Reported by the user while verifying jj-idea-f27g (log horizontal-scroll fix): clearing the reference/bookmark filter deselected the current change even though it remained visible in the filtered list. The user wants this fixed generally for any filter change that keeps the current entry visible, not just the reference filter.
close_reason: Fixed: capture selected entry identity before filter rebuild, restore/clear by identity after; deferred+idempotent selection listener avoids flicker/duplicate reload

title: [epic] Faster change creation from the log (fewer clicks, VisualJJ parity)
description: A new user reported (GitHub #51 point 8) that creating a new change requires too many clicks: right-click a commit, 'New change from this', clear/skip the description field, OK. jj (like git) expects you to describe changes later, not upfront, so most of the time an unnamed change is wanted immediately. VisualJJ gives these operations dedicated buttons directly in the log view. This epic covers: a no-description quick-new action with a default keybinding, and dedicated New/Edit toolbar buttons in the log.
acceptance_criteria: Creating a new change from the log takes at most one click/keypress in the common (no-description) case
notes: GitHub #51 point 8.
close_reason: all steps complete

title: [bug] Selecting a log commit resets horizontal scroll position
description: A new user reported (GitHub #51 point 6) that selecting a commit in the log resets the table's horizontal scroll position, which is especially annoying combined with the existing need to scroll horizontally on narrower windows. JujutsuLogTable.kt has autoResizeMode = AUTO_RESIZE_OFF (line 194) enabling manual horizontal scrolling; find what selection-handling code (row selection / scrollRectToVisible / table repaint on selection change) is resetting the scroll offset and stop it from doing so.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a row in the log table (via click, arrow keys, or programmatic selection) does not change the table's horizontal scroll position
notes: GitHub #51 point 6 (scroll-reset half). Companion feature bead covers responsive column sizing to reduce how often horizontal scroll is needed at all.
close_reason: Verified in sandbox IDE: plain click, details-panel parent link, and beyond-limit link all preserve horizontal scroll and selection correctly.

title: Setting to disable log hover tooltip
description: A new user reported (GitHub #51 point 3) that the log's mouse-over commit-details popup (IdeTooltip, JujutsuLogTable.kt lines 66-241, content built by JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.buildTooltip ~line 122) is not useful as-is: slow to appear, blocks the view since it doesn't disappear on scroll, and text can't be selected/copied. Rather than force a behaviour change on everyone, add a setting to disable the log hover tooltip entirely (details pane already covers the same info on selection). Companion bead jj-idea (tooltip behaviour fix) improves it for users who keep it on.
design:
The companion behaviour fix (GitHub #51 point 3's "slow to appear, blocks the view,
can't select/copy" complaint) landed as edae7624e (jj change wuyvoqtn wvpypxzvwprnnpnqrkukntxp),
touching src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/components/IconAwareTooltip.kt with tests in
IconAwareTooltipBehaviourTest.kt. It adopts the platform's TooltipWithClickableLinks recipe:
the tooltip is a hint with canAutohideOn overridden so moving into it no longer dismisses it
(links clickable, text selectable), and it force-hides on JViewport scroll. Remaining
"slow to appear" complaint is governed by the IDE's own global tooltip initial-delay setting,
not this plugin.

Deferring rather than closing: the off-switch itself was never built, and it's still a
reasonable escape hatch if someone dislikes the tooltip on principle even once usable.
Revisit trigger: a user asks for an off-switch after the fix ships (0.8.8+).

Pre-agreed implementation shape if revisited (~1 hour):
- Gate at JujutsuLogTable level (covers log window + working-copy panel via
  CommitTablePanel.kt:48 - same tooltip, same switch, no extra plumbing).
- Add `var showLogHoverTooltip: Boolean = true` to settings/JujutsuSettingsState.kt,
  matching hideStandardCommitToolWindow pattern.
- Add checkBox row to settings.group.log group in JujutsuConfigurable.kt (~line 180),
  mirroring the hideStandardCommitToolWindow checkbox at line 174.
- Two bundle keys in messages/*.properties near settings.group.log (~line 291).
- Gate LIVE (not at install time): return null early from the htmlAt lambda passed to
  installIconAwareTooltip in JujutsuLogTable.kt:239 when setting is off. beforeShow()
  already treats null/blank htmlAt as "show nothing" (IconAwareTooltip.kt:151), so no
  reinstall/restart needed. Do NOT guard the installIconAwareTooltip call itself.
- Test: extend IconAwareTooltipBehaviourTest.kt's TooltipHost seam, or assert
  beforeShow() returns false when htmlAt yields null.
- Manual regression scope: MT-* sections for log hover tooltip + settings panel.

Note: jj-idea-w2qh (tooltip for many-bookmark commit only reachable via graph column) is
a separate, unaffected bug - stays open.
acceptance_criteria: A settings toggle turns off the log row hover tooltip; default can remain on until the behaviour-fix bead lands
notes: Revisit trigger fired: GitHub #75 (second independent reporter, MadelineRitchie) asked for the off-switch after the 0.8.7 tooltip behaviour fix shipped. Un-deferred 2026-08-19 during triage.
close_reason: Shipped in one PR (batch 2 of jj-idea-exgr)

title: [bug] Log graph merge parent order/colours inconsistent with actual parent order
description: A new user reported (GitHub #51 point 2) that the log graph inconsistently orders the parents of a merge commit — e.g. trunk sometimes renders on the right — and that merge source/target edge colours look wrong. The order is displayed correctly in the commit details panel, so this is a graph-rendering bug, not a data bug. Likely touchpoints: LayoutCalculator.kt (lane/parent-order assignment, merge/fork lane selection ~lines 84-114) and JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.kt drawLinesToParents (~lines 257-299, edge colour selection at line 296). Root cause investigation needed: verify parentLanes ordering is preserved end-to-end from LogEntry.parentIds through GraphNode to the paint routine.
acceptance_criteria: Merge commit parent edges render in the same left-to-right order as entry.parentIds, matching the details panel; edge colours match the correct source/target lanes. Add/extend a LayoutCalculator or graph-rendering test for a merge with >=2 parents where parent order matters.
notes: GitHub #51 point 2. Distinct from jj-idea-gpf5 (octopus-merge diff correctness) and jj-idea-xi58/jj-idea-hlu3 (passthrough-line bugs) — this is specifically about parent ORDER and edge COLOUR for merges.
close_reason: Fixed: generalized LayoutCalculator to reserve lanes for all non-first Pure Merge parents (adjacent or not), fixing merge parent order/colour bug for both 2-parent and octopus merges. Added regression tests, updated LOG_GRAPH_ALGORITHM.md.

title: Document UX-priority tenet: IntelliJ-native > jj-native > bespoke
description: Add a design-decisions entry to contributing.md establishing a tie-breaker for look-and-feel/behaviour calls: prefer IntelliJ-native UX conventions, then jj-native semantics, then other-VCS/bespoke conventions. Prompted by GitHub issue #51 comment thread (double-click-to-checkout expectation vs IntelliJ's own VcsLogGraphTable, which has no double-click-to-checkout/diff — commit actions are keymap-bound there). This tenet is the driver for how B9 (double-click behaviour) is resolved and should guide future similar decisions.
acceptance_criteria: contributing.md has a documented UX-priority tenet in the design-decisions section
notes: From GitHub issue #51 triage.
close_reason: Added UX-priority tenet to contributing.md § Key Design Decisions

title: Ignore-scan watchdog never fires when repo has no ignore files
description:
Surfaced in GitHub issue #35 comment thread: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/35 (SergejSalnikov)

The IGNORE_SCAN_WATCHDOG_MS check (auto-disable ignored-file scanning after ~5s on huge repos) lives inside the collectIgnored callback, which is only invoked when an ignore file is actually found. On repos with no ignore files at all (e.g. hundreds of millions of files), the callback never runs, so the watchdog never fires and the scan just hangs instead of prompting to disable.

Related to jj-idea-ixju (app/global disable toggle, currently project-level only) and jj-idea-0xqp (scan only source/content roots instead of full repo root) — this is a distinct correctness bug in the watchdog trigger condition, not a duplicate of either.
acceptance_criteria: Ignore-scan watchdog also fires (and offers to disable) on repos with zero ignore files once the time budget is exceeded.
close_reason: Already fixed by jj-idea-la8w (shipped v0.7.11, 2026-06-28): collectIgnored now calls the watchdog checkCanceled once per directory entered and every IGNORE_SCAN_CHECK_INTERVAL visited entries, independent of onIgnored, so it fires on repos with zero ignore files. Reporter's complaint was against v0.7.9, pre-la8w, and was never re-hit. Added explicit regression test in GitignoreScanTest.kt.

title: List all bookmarks including remote-only, not just local
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/47

The 'References'/'Bookmarks' selector above the log graph only shows locally available bookmarks (equivalent of 'jj bookmark list'). It should also include bookmarks that exist only on a remote (visible via 'jj bookmark list --all-remotes'), so users can start work off a remote branch without first tracking it locally.

Relevant code: present=false filter at jj/cli/CliLogService.kt:338 and actions/git/GitPushDialog.kt:171 (LOCAL_BOOKMARK_TEMPLATE). See bd memory bookmark-data-model-key-files-bookmark-bookmarkgroup-at.
acceptance_criteria: Bookmark filter/selector includes remote-only bookmarks, clearly distinguished from local ones.
close_reason: Added --all-remotes support to bookmark list CLI, threaded through getBookmarks(), and updated the References selector to show remote-only bookmarks as name@remote with a distinct icon, collapsing synced local+remote pairs into one entry.

title: Dedicated bookmarks/branches panel
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/48

Requester wants a dedicated bookmarks panel to the left of the graph, similar to the Git plugin, with feature/A, feature/B style directory-tree grouping for slash-namespaced bookmark names.

This is the roadmap item ('Bookmark Management & Branches Panel') that was accidentally dropped from ROADMAP.md in commit ff8e4898c during a release-prep edit on 2026-07-07; restored in ROADMAP.md as part of this triage. Complementary to jj-idea-lfe2 (log toolbar bookmark widget, gated on GitHub PR #29).
acceptance_criteria: Dedicated panel/tool window listing bookmarks, grouped hierarchically by / in the name, matching Git plugin UX.
notes:
If ever pursued, should consume actions/bookmark/BookmarkActions.kt (jj-idea-reiz) as its
per-bookmark action source rather than reimplementing move/rename/delete/forget/track/advance.

Update (jj-idea-cpno, 2026-08-19): the full popup-building logic (single-repo flat vs.
multi-repo per-repo submenus) is now factored out into
actions/bookmark/BookmarkMenu.kt's bookmarkActionGroup(), shared by the main-toolbar widget
and its status-bar fallback. This panel should call bookmarkActionGroup() directly for its
per-bookmark context menus rather than rebuilding the grouping logic a third time.
close_reason: Implemented: bookmarks panel shipped in the log tab (tree, /-hierarchy, context menu reusing existing bookmark actions, Filter/Navigate). See commit b4c37230.

title: Capture reporter context (repo size, personal vs commercial) on large-repo bug reports
description: When users report large-repo perf/scale problems, we currently lack the signal needed to decide when to build speculative scale infrastructure (see jj-idea-er06 triage). Add a prompt for repo size and personal-vs-commercial usage to the bug-report path, and ask this on existing open GitHub large-repo issues. This context is what would later justify a commercial/large-repo tier and unpark the P4 perf work (edjs.4/.5/.6, a0wp, ix4v).
design:
PLAN: gather scale/usage context on large-repo reports without adding telemetry.

Facts: no .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE exists; only .github/FUNDING.yml and workflows/. The plugin has no in-product bug-report flow found by grep (no "issues/new" URL builder), so "bug-report path" == GitHub issue creation. Collecting data automatically would be telemetry - out of scope and a privacy problem for a plugin used on commercial repos.
Deliverables (all outside product code, low risk):
1. `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` (GitHub issue form) with fields: plugin version, IDE + build, jj version (`jj --version`), OS, steps/expected/actual, and an OPTIONAL "Scale" section: approx tracked files, approx commits in `jj log -r 'all()' | wc -l`, whether the repo is colocated, and a dropdown "Usage: personal / open-source / commercial-employer / prefer not to say". Every scale field optional with "skip if unsure" wording.
2. `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`: blank issues still allowed, link to docs.
3. A copy-paste helper in docs (contributing.md or docs/reporting-bugs.md): one shell snippet printing repo-size stats safely (`jj file list | wc -l`, `jj log --no-graph -r 'all()' -T '"x\n"' | wc -l`).
4. Draft (do not post) the question comment for each existing open large-repo GitHub issue: list them with `gh issue list --label ... --state open --search "large OR slow OR performance"`; store draft text + the issue numbers in this bead's notes. Posting is outward-facing -> ask the user first.
5. Optional later: "Help > Copy diagnostics" action; separate bead if wanted.

Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Automatic collection? Rec: no - manual optional form fields only. Reverse: add a diagnostics action that fills the template URL (still user-submitted).
2. Q: Mark commercial-usage question as required? Rec: optional; required fields reduce report volume.
Link: this evidence is what unparks edjs.4/.5/.6, a0wp, ix4v (see edjs epic).
Testing: render the form via GitHub's issue-form validator (`gh api` lint not available; check YAML with `yamllint` and open the template in a fork or the new-issue page). No code => no manual-tests entry; no scale impact.
acceptance_criteria: Issue form template merged with optional scale/usage fields; docs snippet present; draft comments for existing large-repo issues stored in notes (not posted); user approves posting.

title: Add 'Compare with Working Copy' to the log commit context menu
description:
GitHub #40: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/40
Like Git's 'Compare with Local' on a commit: right-click a commit in the Jujutsu log to diff the whole working copy against it, working-copy side editable (supports final absorb workflow). Existing CompareWithLocalAction is file-level only; this is a commit-level log action.
close_reason: Implemented: two-revision diff-summary path + new commit-level 'Compare with Working Copy' log context-menu action, opening a reusable editor tab with the working-copy side editable.

title: Stop bundling kotlin-stdlib in the plugin distribution
description:
GitHub #41: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/41
kotlin-stdlib is provided by the JetBrains platform and should not be shipped. Set kotlin.stdlib.default.dependency=false in gradle.properties; verify the built .zip no longer contains kotlin-stdlib and the plugin still runs.
close_reason: Set kotlin.stdlib.default.dependency=false in gradle.properties; verified the built plugin zip no longer contains kotlin-stdlib jars and ./gradlew check passes (including platform tests that load the plugin in a real IDE instance).

title: Annotate provider logs ProcessCanceledException on project dispose
description:
GitHub #45: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/45
JujutsuAnnotationProvider.annotateInternal (JujutsuAnnotationProvider.kt:117-122) catches and Logger.error()s a ProcessCanceledException (ContainerDisposedException from getStateModel/getWorkingCopy) raised while the project is being disposed on window close. IntelliJ forbids logging control-flow exceptions. Fix: rethrow PCE/ContainerDisposedException instead of logging; guard getWorkingCopy against disposed containers.
close_reason: Fixed: annotateInternal now rethrows CancellationException (ContainerDisposedException) as well as ProcessCanceledException instead of routing it through log.error().

title: Set up donation system (GitHub Sponsors)
description:
Add a low-friction donation channel while the plugin stays free, to start capturing goodwill from a 4.63-rated tool as market share grows. Decision: donate-not-paywall while the jj-on-JetBrains market is still small.

Primary channel: GitHub Sponsors (audience already on GitHub), surfaced in 3 places. Optional Ko-fi/Buy Me a Coffee as a no-enrollment fallback.

Steps:
1. (User) Enrol kkkev in GitHub Sponsors — identity verification + Stripe Connect/bank; set 1-2 tiers + one-time amounts.
2. Add .github/FUNDING.yml (github: [kkkev]) -> renders Sponsor button on repo.
3. Add a Support/Sponsor section to README.md (short, gracious, no guilt-tripping).
4. (User) Paste the Sponsors URL into the JetBrains Marketplace dedicated Donation link field (plugin id 30576) — NOT the description (violates guidelines). Confirmed supported for free plugins.
5. (Optional, low-key) single static 'Support this plugin' hyperlink in the Jujutsu settings panel. NO popup/notification nags — those would tank the 4.63 rating, which is the asset being protected.

Only-user-can-do: Sponsors enrolment, Stripe/bank, Marketplace admin field. Agent can prep FUNDING.yml + README now.

Verify: Sponsor button appears on repo; donation link renders on marketplace page; README Support section renders.
design: JetBrains Marketplace has a dedicated per-plugin Donation link field (works for free plugins; link must not be in the description). GitHub Sponsors chosen as primary because the user base already lives on GitHub. In-plugin nudge must be a passive hyperlink only to avoid rating damage.
acceptance_criteria: FUNDING.yml committed and Sponsor button visible on GitHub repo; README has a Support section; (user) donation link set on marketplace listing 30576.
close_reason: FUNDING.yml, README Support section, and settings-panel link all shipped. User still needs to add donation URL to Marketplace listing 30576.

title: Make hunk picker label consistent with split dialog commit label
description: The split dialog calls the selected-files commit 'Parent' (non-parallel) or 'Second' (parallel), but the hunk merge picker always says 'First Commit' regardless of mode. Both target the same commit, so the labels should match. Fix: thread the commit label from the dialog into HunkMergePicker so its title, apply button, center panel, and cancel message use the same name as the file list.
close_reason: Closed

title: split: graph rebuild races fireTableDataChanged, causing flash of misaligned graph
description: After fixing 7jkr, filtering first fires fireTableDataChanged (Swing repaints with old renderer), then the MergingUpdateQueue fires 250ms later and swaps in the correct renderer. The brief intermediate paint with the stale layout is visible. Fix: invoke onFilterApplied (and thus rebuild the renderer) synchronously BEFORE fireTableDataChanged, so the renderer is correct when Swing first paints the filtered rows. The MergingUpdateQueue can be removed.
close_reason: Closed

title: Harden discoverClasspath to use UrlClassLoader.getFiles() instead of URL string parsing
description: Current discoverClasspath() parses getResource().toString() to reconstruct the jar path, then globs the sibling lib/ dir. Three concerns: (1) fragile assumption about lib/ layout (would break if packaging changes), (2) URL-string hazards on different OSes (spaces encoded as %20, Windows drive letters /C:/, UNC paths, ! jar separator), (3) resource-URL parsing is conceptually wrong when getFiles() is available directly. Fix: use UrlClassLoader.getFiles() (the platform's own accessor for plugin classpath jars) which returns Path objects, joined with File.pathSeparator. Falls back to java.class.path for non-IDE classloaders (unit tests).
close_reason: Closed

title: Native merge tool hunk picker for split
description: Replace the basic +/- JTextArea HunkPanel with an embedded native diff preview + IDEA merge-tool picker. The merge window is used to let users accept/reject individual hunks for the first commit, replacing checkbox-driven reverseApplyHunks. See approved plan at /Users/kevin/.claude/plans/implement-jj-idea-5isf-1-atomic-lampson.md
close_reason: Closed

title: Recompute graph layout when log filter changes
description: When filtering the log, the graph layout (graphNodes) stays anchored to the full unfiltered set while the renderer's rowPassthroughCache goes stale (row indices shift). Clearing the filter doesn't help — only a manual refresh calls updateGraph(), which recreates the renderer. Fix: rebuild graphNodes from the visible (filtered) entries on every filter commit, via a callback from JujutsuLogTableModel.applyFilter() into UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel, which owns CommitGraphBuilder and calls logTable.updateGraph(). Debounce rapid text-filter keystrokes. No re-topo-sort needed (filteredEntries is already a topo-ordered subset).
close_reason: Closed

title: Scan only project source/content roots for ignored files, not full repo root
description: Raised by contributor SergejSalnikov on GitHub issue #35, deliberately deprioritised: their repo (google3/Piper-backed, hundreds of millions of files) makes the ignored-file tree walk (GitignoreCache.collectIgnored, walked from repo root in JujutsuIgnoredFilesService.scan — see JujutsuIgnoredFilesService.kt:161 'val repoRoot = File(repo.directory.path)') prohibitively expensive even with the watchdog/abort fix (jj-idea-la8w) and the global disable toggle (jj-idea-ixju) as escape hatches. Their suggestion: scan only the project's source/content roots instead of the entire repo root, since users rarely care about ignored-file status outside source roots. This is a genuinely useful idea but is a larger redesign serving a corporate non-paying use case, so it's deprioritised behind community-useful work; raised here so it isn't lost.
