design: Sketch (refine at implementation time): per SergejSalnikov, two cases must be handled differently: (1) repo root lies inside a single source root — this is what the current full-repo-root walk already handles correctly, so behavior should be preserved/equivalent; (2) one or more source roots lie INSIDE the repo (the problematic case for huge repos) — here, instead of walking the whole repo root, walk only from each source root's directory, using the repo's nested .gitignore chain at that root's depth (GitignoreCache.getNode already builds the PatternList stack lazily per directory, so seeding the walk's initial 'stack' parameter at a source root's depth instead of from repoRoot should be feasible without restructuring GitignoreCache itself). NOTE: there is currently NO usage anywhere in src/ of ProjectRootManager, ModuleRootManager, ProjectFileIndex, .sourceRoots, or .contentRoots (confirmed by grep) — this would be net-new platform API integration. Need to handle: multiple source roots, source roots that don't exist yet, and projects with no module model (this plugin may run on non-IDEA-project setups). Relevant files: JujutsuIgnoredFilesService.kt (scan(), repoRoot construction ~line 161), GitignoreCache.kt (collectIgnored signature takes an IgnoreScanNode root and an initial pattern stack — could be adapted to start at an arbitrary subdirectory instead of repo root).
acceptance_criteria: Not yet refined — to be fleshed out when this is picked up. At minimum: an operation-count test showing the walk's entry count scales with source-root size rather than full repo size on a synthetic large-repo-small-source-root fixture (reuse the IgnoreScanNode in-memory test abstraction, see GitignoreScanTest.kt/GitignoreCacheTest.kt).

title: Log/working-copy load crashes when backend can't evaluate descendants(::remote_bookmarks())
description: GitHub issue #35 (SergejSalnikov, Google-internal Piper/p4base-backed jj): log/working-copy load fails with 'com.intellij.openapi.vcs.VcsException: Error from jj log: Error: Failed to parse template: Failed to evaluate revset ... = Failed to evaluate revset'. User correlated this with leaving the 'Revset expression' setting empty, but that is a red herring: the stack trace (JujutsuStateModel.workingCopies -> RepoLogCache.fetch/fetchOne -> LogCache.kt:105-113 -> CliLogService.getLog at line 59/180) shows this is the WORKING-COPY fetch, which always uses the fixed revset '@' (Revset.kt WorkingCopy object), never the user's logRevset setting. Verified locally (jj 0.37): the blank-revset guard already works correctly — LogCache.kt:94 converts a blank user setting to Revset.Default (omits -r entirely), and '-r ''' produces a DIFFERENT jj error ('a value is required'), not this one. jj's error caret instead points INSIDE the log TEMPLATE at the embedded revset literal in self.contained_in("descendants(::remote_bookmarks())") — the hasPushedAncestor field at CliLogService.kt:279. The user's backend (a non-standard jj implementation backing Piper) apparently cannot evaluate that revset expression, so this one optional decoration field (used to show whether a commit has a pushed ancestor) takes down the entire log/working-copy load with no recovery.
design: MINIMAL workaround only (the proper fix — per-repo backend-capability detection/caching to avoid even attempting the field — is deliberately deprioritised; see companion P3 issue). No per-repo caching of the degraded state in this minimal version — every query on a broken backend pays one extra jj invocation, acceptable given this use case is deprioritised; the proper fix would cache capability per repo to avoid the double call. In CliLogService: 1) Build a second reduced template, e.g. 'fullLogTemplateWithoutPushedAncestor', identical to the existing fullLogTemplate (CliLogService.kt ~line 312, built from basicLogTemplate + author + committer) but omitting the hasPushedAncestor field (line 279). Parsing already keys off template.count (see parse() at lines 186-192), so this just needs to be a real LogTemplate with one fewer field and a corresponding take()/constructor that defaults the 'has pushed ancestor' value to false. 2) In the private getLog (CliLogService.kt:165-184), when executor.log(...) fails (result.isSuccess false) and result.stderr matches a template-evaluation failure (contains 'Failed to evaluate revset'), retry ONCE with the reduced template instead of immediately returning Result.failure. On retry success, parse normally with hasPushedAncestor defaulted to false. Log one WARN the first time this degradation happens for visibility. If stderr does NOT match the pattern (e.g. a genuinely bad user-supplied revset expression), do NOT retry — surface the original VcsException as today, to avoid masking real user errors.
acceptance_criteria: - Stub-based test (extend LogServiceIntegrationTest / StubCommandExecutor, no platform fixture needed — see existing stub wiring in src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/integration/LogServiceIntegrationTest.kt and JjStub.kt): first jj log call's stub response simulates stderr containing 'Failed to evaluate revset'; the retry (reduced template) call succeeds; assert the returned log entries parse correctly and the pushed-ancestor field defaults to false. - A second test asserts that a non-matching stderr (e.g. a genuine bad revset error unrelated to template evaluation) is NOT retried and surfaces as a VcsException, same as before this change. - Manual smoke note added to docs/manual-tests.md: document that a backend without remote_bookmarks revset support now loads the log successfully minus the pushed-ancestor decoration, instead of failing outright.
close_reason: Implemented: CliLogService retries with a reduced template on template-evaluation failure, caches backend incapability per repo path for the session (folding in jj-idea-eqm3), and only the doomed remote_bookmarks() field is dropped. Tests in LogServiceIntegrationTest.BackendCapabilityFallback; ./gradlew check + stubTest pass.

title: Interactive hunk-level split
description:
Support hunk/line-level selection in SplitDialog (jj split --interactive equivalent) so users can move specific hunks into the split-out change, not just whole files.

## Background
The current SplitDialog (jj-idea-wp0q) supports file-level selection via the checkbox tree. It does not support choosing individual hunks within a file.

## Goal
Add a way to invoke `jj split --interactive` (or build an equivalent in-dialog UI) so users can pick specific hunks/lines to split out into the new change.

## Notes
- Mirror of jj-idea-4q7m for the split side; the two likely share the same hunk-selection infrastructure (in-dialog diff editor, possibly built on IntelliJ's LineStatusTracker).
- jj's CLI `--interactive` opens $EDITOR with a diff edit UI; we likely need our own in-dialog diff editor.
close_reason: Implemented: single file-list + hunk-panel layout, reverseApplyHunks, DiffEditTool/HunkApplyMain, CLI splitInteractive, all tests passing

title: Operation-count scale test for wc-rebuild fan-out (working-copy refresh)
description:
Follow-up to jj-idea-edjs.2, deferred because UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.updateChangesView is Swing/EDT/VFS-coupled and needs a platform test rather than a plain unit test.

Add a @Tag("platform")/@TestApplication/@RunInEdt test asserting the MergingUpdateQueue("wcReload", 200ms) coalescing + the 'changes != changesTree.changes' early-out in UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.updateChangesView (ui/workingcopy/UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt:~374) keeps rebuilds to <=1 per burst of VFS/change-list events, rather than one rebuild per event (cf. closed jj-idea-7jn1 per-VFS-event rebuilds). May require exposing a rebuild counter (similar to report.count("changes", ...) already wired) for the test to assert on, since the rebuild itself drives a real ChangesTree.
notes: Created as a deferral from jj-idea-edjs.2 implementation (3 hot paths already satisfy the acceptance criterion: ignore-scan, log-load, graph-layout).
close_reason: Added platform-tagged scale test asserting wc-rebuild coalescing (<=1 reload per burst) and the changes-equality early-out, via two new test-seam counters on UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel

title: Differentiate bookmarks and tags in reference filter
description: The Reference filter shows a list of all bookmarks and tags. Now that tags are there as well as bookmarks, it would be useful to differentiate them. Therefore show the icon next to each name. Consider whether the mutable indicator should be there too.
close_reason: Implemented: distinct, correctly-sized, themed bookmark/tag/working-copy icons in the Reference filter popup, plus a persistent checkmark+icon selection marker (consistent with JujutsuRootFilterComponent's ToggleAction pattern) since the toolbar label is hidden while the popup is open.

title: collectTrackedAbsolutePaths includes phantom 'Parent commit' line as tracked path
description: collectTrackedAbsolutePaths in JujutsuChangeProvider.kt (line 217) fails to set inWorkingCopy=false when it encounters the 'Working copy (@):' summary line (it skips it via !startsWith check, but doesn't terminate the section). So the next 'Parent commit (@-): ...' line passes the inWorkingCopy guard and gets added as a phantom tracked path '/repo/rent commit (@-): ...'. Reported indirectly by SergejSalnikov on GitHub #35. parseStatus handles this correctly by flipping inWorkingCopy off; collectTrackedAbsolutePaths must mirror that. Impact is low (phantom path never matches a real file on disk) but correctness bug with zero test coverage.
close_reason: Fixed: added 'Working copy' to the termination conditions in collectTrackedAbsolutePaths so it matches parseStatus behaviour. Two regression tests added.

title: Restoring a rename leaves the file deleted
description:
1. Rename a file.
2. Restore the file

Observe that the file remains in the working copy, but showing up as deleted.

Worse, in this state, there is no 'restore' option to undo the deletion.
close_reason: Fixed: allPaths on FileChange returns both source and target for renames and the before-path for deletes; restore actions now use restorePaths/singleRepoForRestore to cover all cases

title: Resolving conflicts leaves working copy still showing conflicted files
description: After resolving conflicts, the working copy window fails to update showing the conflicts as resolved. Even hitting refresh doesn't update this. Worse, trying to resolve again throws an error.
close_reason: Fixed: updateChangesView now compares FileStatus per change (Change.equals ignores it), and resolveConflictsAction reads conflicted files live instead of a stale snapshot. Verified via new regression test + gradlew check; user confirmed manual smoke test.

title: Operation-count scale tests for hot paths (deterministic, PR-blocking)
description:
Establish the operation-count test pattern: inject a counting/fake collaborator (filesystem walker, command executor, list-copy counter) and assert on work performed, not wall-clock. Deterministic, CI-noise-immune, runs in the normal ./gradlew test gate — this is the test class that would have directly caught GitHub #35 ('a repo with a 100k-file ignored tree must visit O(non-ignored) entries').

Scope:
- First instance lands with jj-idea-2570.1 (ignore-scan visit count); this bead generalizes the pattern and applies it to the other scale-sensitive paths: log parse/load (no quadratic list ops — cf. closed jj-idea-iivd RepoLogCache O(n^2)), graph layout, working-copy refresh fan-out (cf. jj-idea-7jn1 per-VFS-event rebuilds).
- Add a short 'how to write a scale test' note to contributing.md referencing an example.
- Keep them fast (<1s each) with synthetic in-memory structures, no real repos.
acceptance_criteria: At least 3 hot paths have operation-count assertions running in the default test task. Pattern documented in contributing.md with a pointer to an exemplar test.
close_reason: 3 hot paths now have operation-count scale tests in the default test task: ignore-scan (existing GitignoreScanTest), log-load (new RepoLogCacheScaleTest), graph-layout (new GraphLayoutScaleTest + LayoutCalculatorImpl.operationCount counter). Pattern documented in contributing.md 'Writing a scale test' section. wc-rebuild fan-out deferred to jj-idea-f21f (Swing/EDT-coupled, needs platform test).

title: Delegate ignored-file enumeration to git for colocated repos
description:
jj cannot enumerate ignored files (jj file list shows tracked only; jj status has no --ignored), but for colocated repos we can delegate to native git like git4idea does: git status --porcelain -z --ignored=matching --untracked-files=no (see git4idea/index/GitIndexStatusUtil.kt appendParameters). Git's C traversal prunes ignored directories and reports an ignored dir as a single '!! dir/' record — always faster than a JVM walker and uses git's canonical gitignore semantics (our GitignoreCache is a reimplementation that can drift).

Scope:
- Detect colocation (.git alongside .jj at repo root).
- In the ignored-files holder (jj-idea-2570.2), use git when colocated; fall back to the pruned JVM walker (jj-idea-2570.1) otherwise. Non-colocated repos cannot use the .jj/repo/store/git dir — its index does not reflect the working copy.
- Handle git executable missing/old gracefully: silent fallback to the walker.

Depends on jj-idea-2570.2 (the holder is where the delegation slots in).
acceptance_criteria: Colocated repos enumerate ignored files via git with output parsed into the same RecursiveFilePathSet. Non-colocated repos and missing-git environments fall back to the walker with no user-visible error. Parser covered by a contract test on porcelain -z output including '!!' records and quoted paths.
close_reason: Superseded by CLAUDE.md Performance & Scale guidance (jj-idea-edjs.3, commit d288d2edb): 'Never write a fast path that delegates to git and a broken slow path for the non-colocated case.' The pruned + cancellable JVM walker GitignoreCache.collectIgnored is now the canonical path (deps 2570.1/2570.2 done), proven O(non-ignored) by GitignoreScanTest. Git-delegation rejected. Drift concern spun off to a new test-hardening task.

title: Diagnose doubled working-copy switcher widget
description:
The status-bar working-copy switcher (JujutsuStatusBarWidget) sometimes paints doubled — two icons + two copies of text, sometimes interleaved as icon/text/icon/text.

## Investigation so far

All three refresh() callers already run on the EDT:
- install(statusBar) — called by platform on EDT
- workingCopies.connect(this) { refresh() } — delivered via runLater = invokeLater → EDT (Messaging.kt:162-164)
- FileEditorManagerListener.selectionChanged — fired by platform on EDT

TextCanvasPanel.renderFrom() already calls removeAll() before re-adding components (TruncatingLeftRightLayout.kt:28).

So a single EDT render cannot double, and there is no visible cross-thread caller to race. The doubling points to something not visible from static analysis: either a hidden off-EDT mutation of the component tree, or redundant accumulation (removeAll() not covering everything, or the widget being installed more than once).

## Instrumentation added (temporary, in current code)

TextCanvasPanel.renderFrom():
- assertIsDispatchThread() — throws immediately if called off-EDT
- Logs componentsBefore / fragmentCount / componentsAfter at INFO

JujutsuStatusBarWidget.install():
- Logs widget=$this identity so double-install is visible

JujutsuStatusBarWidget.refresh(source):
- source param tags each call as 'install' / 'workingCopies' / 'selectionChanged'
- Logs thread name

WidgetPanel.update():
- Logs contentBefore / contentAfter component counts

## How to reproduce

./gradlew runIde in a jj repo. Open Help → Show Log, filter by JujutsuStatusBarWidget and TextCanvasPanel. Exercise: switch editor tabs, save files (wait ~300ms debounce), run jj new from terminal, toggle widget in status bar settings.

## Outcome table

| Observation | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| assertIsDispatchThread() throws | Hidden off-EDT caller reaching renderFrom | Fix that caller to use invokeLater/runLater |
| componentsBefore keeps growing (never resets to 0) | removeAll() not clearing a parent panel | Track down which container is accumulating |
| Two install: lines same widget=@... address | Platform calling install() twice on same instance | Add guard in install() |
| Two install: lines different widget=@... addresses | Factory created two instances, both installed | Check JujutsuStatusBarWidgetFactory |
| contentAfter=2 when entry has 1 icon + 1 text run | renderFrom works, doubling is elsewhere (paint artifact, nested panel) | Investigate WidgetPanel layout hierarchy |

## Next step

Run runIde, reproduce the doubling, read the log output, identify which row in the outcome table matches, then apply the targeted fix and remove all DIAGNOSTIC-tagged code.
close_reason: Root cause confirmed: IdeStatusBarImpl.doInit calls install() off-EDT; workingCopies.connect replay fires refresh() on EDT concurrently. Fixed by wrapping panel.update() in runLater and moving currentRepo assignment inside that block. assertIsDispatchThread() retained as permanent guard.

title: Allow arbitrary change ids in revision selector
description: The revision selector used to find a target revision for comparison and in the working copy widget currently doesn't allow selection of an arbitrary change id, in the same way that https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/pull/28/changes provides. This is particularly evident for change ids that fall outside the configured revset and log limit. We need to introduce this. Consider whether we can also have fast/slow results from the filter - providing an immediate response for cached commits but a slower one for other change ids in the repository that would need to be loaded.
close_reason: Added RevisionChoice.FreeForm fallback + debounced (MergingUpdateQueue) background resolve via existing LogCache.get off-window fallback. Shared RevisionChoicePanel benefits both the compare popup and working-copy switcher. Also hardened CompareFileWithBranchAction.showDiff to show an error dialog instead of throwing on an unresolvable free-form revision.

title: Compare with another commit doesn't work from comparing with another commit
description:
1. Comparue with another commit.
2. Open the right-hand editor, select again 'Compare with another commit'
3. Nothing happens.
close_reason: Fixed in CompareFileWithBranchAction.kt: actionPerformed now uses e.jujutsuFiles (new helper in ActionEventExtensions.kt) which filters synthetic ChainDiffVirtualFile entries and falls back to the single focused file, so the action correctly resolves the repo and shows the revision selector from a diff editor side.

title: [bug] [correctness] Mutability indicator wrong for bookmarks/tags in revision pickers — defaults to mutable for out-of-window targets
description:
The mutable/immutable icon shown next to bookmarks and tags in the working-copy switcher and revision-choice popups is mostly wrong: references pointing at immutable commits (main, releases, old history) are rendered as mutable.

Root cause: RevisionChoicePanel.MutabilityAwareRenderer derives a reference's mutability from membership in immutableChangeIds, which is built ONLY from the loaded log window (repo.logCache.all). Bookmarks/tags pointing at commits outside that window are absent from the set, so 'in immutableChangeIds' returns false and the renderer defaults to mutable.

  is RevisionChoice.Ref -> when (val item = value.item) {
      is TagItem -> allEntries.find { e -> e.tags.any { it.name == item.tag.name } }?.immutable == true
      else -> item.id?.full in immutableChangeIds   // bookmark: false for out-of-window targets
  }

Tags have the same latent defect: allEntries.find{} only searches the loaded window.
design:
Do NOT load/cache a log entry per reference (N extra jj log resolutions + cache churn).

Bookmarks: have jj compute immutability in the SAME 'jj bookmark list' call already made. Add a template field 'normal_target.immutable()' to bookmarkListTemplate (CliLogService.kt ~L363); add 'immutable: Boolean' to BookmarkItem (BookmarkItem.kt); renderer reads item.immutable directly. Verified the template works: jj bookmark list -T 'name ++ normal_target.immutable()'.

Tags: 'jj tag list' exposes no target template (no 'normal_target' / target keyword — see tagListTemplate comment, CliLogService.kt ~L345), so tag immutability cannot come from the list call. Resolve tag targets via the cache on demand (tags are few) and surface immutable on TagItem, OR keep tag mutability derived from the window but stop defaulting wrong. Decide during implementation.

Test fixture: jj-stress-test repo now has immutable_heads() = builtin_immutable_heads() | main (in .jj/repo/config.toml), giving ~69 immutable / 62 mutable bookmarks for manual verification.
acceptance_criteria: Bookmarks pointing at immutable commits render with the immutable icon in the working-copy switcher and revision-choice popup, even when the target is outside the loaded log window. Same for tags. Verified manually against the jj-stress-test repo (main + releases immutable; most feature/hotfix branches mutable).
close_reason: Tag immutability now resolved via enriched tagListTemplate (present + qualifiedChangeId + immutable fields), matching the bookmark approach. No per-tag jj subprocess fan-out. The stale comment about jj tag list having no target keyword was wrong for jj 0.37+.

title: Commit details panel breaks bookmark names at hyphens and splits icon from text
description: In the commit details panel, when a commit has many bookmarks they wrap to multiple lines. Line breaks occur at hyphens within bookmark names (e.g. 'hotfix/issue-' on one line, '123' on the next) rather than treating each bookmark as an atomic unit. Additionally, some lines split between the bookmark icon and the bookmark text. Fix: treat each bookmark (icon + name) as a non-breaking unit in the HTML canvas layout; use a non-breaking space or inline-block span wrapping to prevent mid-bookmark line breaks.
close_reason: Wrapped each bookmark/tag chip in a white-space:nowrap span (TextCanvas.kt) so HTML line-wrapping treats icon+name as one atomic unit; added HtmlTextCanvasTest regression coverage and a manual-tests.md checklist item.

title: Log row with 30+ bookmarks hides description and truncates bookmark list without indication
description: When a commit has ~30 bookmarks, the decoration rendering in the log table consumes the full row width: the description column shows no text at all, and not all bookmarks are rendered (some are cut off with no ellipsis or '+ N more' indicator). The user has no way to know the list is incomplete without discovering the tooltip accidentally. Fix: cap bookmark rendering at a reasonable count (e.g. 5) with a '+ N more' overflow indicator; ensure description always has a minimum allocated width.
close_reason: Fixed: bookmark/tag decorations now capped to 50% of column width with a clickable +N more overflow popup; description always keeps the remainder. Verified via ./gradlew check (new CappedDecorationsTest, all existing tests pass).

title: [perf] Working copy panel slow with 40+ changed files — ChangeListManager.getAllChanges scans on every VFS event
description:
The stress-test repo's working copy (@ = wip: working copy with many changed files) has 40 new files + 20 modified lines in src/main.txt = 41 changes. UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel subscribes to ChangeListListener; on every file-system event the panel rebuilds the changes tree.

JujutsuChangesTree uses IntelliJ's ChangesBrowserNode which groups files by directory. With 40 files and 'group by directory' enabled, the tree rebuild iterates all 40 changes per VFS event. During active editing this can fire 10-20 times/second, causing visible stutter in the working copy panel.

Additionally, the panel calls VcsDirtyScopeManager.fileDirty() per changed file in BulkFileListener — with 40 files in the working copy and a broad save-all, 40 fileDirty() calls fire in a single batch.

Test with the stress-test repo: open it, make a change to any wip_file, and observe whether the working copy panel updates smoothly or flickers/lags.
close_reason: Panel rebuild coalesced via MergingUpdateQueue (200ms window, identity merge on both ChangeListListener and workingCopies paths). VFS batch dirty marking replaced with single filesDirty() call. ./gradlew check passes.

title: [correctness] Bookmark filter in log toolbar searches only loaded entries — misses out-of-limit bookmarks
description:
JujutsuBookmarkWidget.createActionGroup() builds allGroups from logTable.logModel.getAllEntries().flatMap { it.bookmarks } — this only includes bookmarks on commits that are currently loaded in the table. If the log limit is 200 and there are bookmarks on older commits (e.g. deep-branch at depth 250 with the stress-test repo), those bookmarks appear in 'jj bookmark list' but NOT in the widget's bookmark list.

The RevisionChoicePanel (used for 'Compare with…' actions) does call repo.logService.getBookmarks() which returns all bookmarks, but the bookmark widget does not — it derives from the already-loaded log entries.

This creates a confusing split: the compare popup shows all 117 bookmarks, but the log toolbar Bookmarks widget only shows bookmarks visible in the current log window. There is no visual indication that some bookmarks are hidden.

Fix: load bookmarks from repo.logService.getBookmarks() in the bookmark widget (same source as RevisionChoicePanel) and annotate which ones are currently visible vs out-of-range.
close_reason: Fixed: widget now sources bookmarks from LogCache.bookmarks (complete jj bookmark list) not from loaded log entries

title: [render] Log table rows with very long descriptions don't truncate — causes wide horizontal scroll
description:
The stress-test repo has a commit (long-description) with a 900+ character single-line description. JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer and SeparateDecorationsCellRenderer render the description at full width. The table column can't shrink below the renderer's preferred width, which forces a horizontal scrollbar and may make other columns invisibly narrow.

Also: the description TextCanvas.append(description) function (ui/Formatters.kt) has no max-width guard on its display string. Description.display returns the first line only, but with a 900-char first line the cell becomes enormous.

Fix: cap description rendering to the column's available width (or a configurable max chars), appending '…' when truncated. This is separate from the Description.display trimming (which handles newlines, not length).
close_reason: Invalid as written. Descriptions already truncate via TruncatingLeftRightLayout + FragmentLayout.truncateToFit (in place since cd0a4f51e, 2026-02-17, predating this bead). No horizontal-scroll mechanism exists: getPreferredSize returns column width, adjustDescriptionColumnWidth clamps the column to viewport, canvas computes no width. Named class SeparateDecorationsCellRenderer does not exist. Residual cosmetic ellipsis-placement nuance split out to a new bead.

title: [render] Many bookmarks on one commit overflow cell renderer and details panel
description:
The stress-test repo has a commit with 30 bookmarks (hotfix/issue-1 through hotfix/issue-25 plus 5 more). TextCanvas.appendBookmarks() renders all bookmarks inline as chips. In the SeparateDecorationsCellRenderer and JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer this causes the cell to overflow its width with no truncation or 'and N more' ellipsis.

The commit details panel (JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel via appendSummaryAndStatuses) also renders all bookmarks which can produce a very tall HTML pane if they wrap. The working copy panel shows these in the description — 30 chips in a single line with no overflow guard.

JujutsuBookmarkWidget.getCurrentText() joins all bookmarks before truncating to 30 chars, so the join itself is unbounded before the check fires.

Fix: cap the inline chip list (e.g. show first 5 + '…and N more' tooltip), and fix getCurrentText() to short-circuit the join.
close_reason: Fixed the remaining real gap: the row-hover tooltip wasn't width-bounded, so commits with many bookmarks (e.g. 30) laid out as one oversized line and got clipped by the screen, hiding the description and/or bookmarks. Added tooltipComponent() in JujutsuLogTable.kt to bound width (forcing HTML reflow) and wrap in a scroll pane if still taller than the screen. Also short-circuited JujutsuBookmarkWidget.getCurrentText(). The other listed sub-items were already fine: log table cell capped by jj-idea-w61m; commit details panel already inside a JBScrollPane with a finite parent width. Verified via ./gradlew check (new platform-tagged TooltipComponentTest, all existing tests pass).

title: [perf] RepoLogCache.store() is O(n²) — list filter+concat on every store call
description:
RepoLogCache.store() (jj/LogCache.kt:132-134) does synchronized(orderLock) { orderedIds = orderedIds.filterNot { it in newIds } + entries.map { it.id } }. With 500 cached entries and a loadContext() call adding 20 more, this allocates and copies all 520 IDs. If loadContext() is called repeatedly during navigation (each arrow-key press expands by 20), this becomes O(n²) with the cache size.

The newIds HashSet lookup is O(1) so the filterNot scan is O(n), but the list concatenation creates a new list each time. In the worst case (1000 entries, 100 context expansions), this is 1000×100 = 100k element copies.

Fix: use a LinkedHashMap (or LinkedHashSet of IDs) to maintain insertion order with O(1) remove+add, replacing the sorted list rebuild.
close_reason: Replaced orderedIds: List with LinkedHashSet; store() is now O(|newIds|) per call instead of O(n). snapshot() acquires orderLock before toList() since the set is mutated in place.

title: [perf] RevisionChoicePanel runs jj bookmark list on every search keystroke
description:
RevisionChoicePanel.buildRevisionChoices() (ui/components/RevisionChoicePanel.kt:50-63) calls repo.logService.getBookmarks() fresh on every keystroke — executes 'jj bookmark list' per character typed. With 100+ bookmarks each keypress blocks for 100-500ms. loadData() spawns a new runInBackground{} on every DocumentEvent with no debounce or caching. Bookmarks don't change while the popup is open.

Fix: fetch bookmarks once when the popup opens (already happens in loadData()), cache in the panel instance, re-filter in memory on subsequent keystrokes. Also add a debounce on the search field so rapid typing only triggers one load.
notes: With revset=all() (500 entries), lag IS noticeable on first keystroke in comparison popup — confirms issue at scale. With revset=main (1 entry), fast. Additional finding: change ID search in popup only covers first 100 log entries — there appears to be a separate result cap on log entry results independent of the bookmark search.
close_reason: Central bookmark cache added to LogCache.bookmarks; widget pre-loads from cache off-EDT; RevisionChoicePanel uses cache instead of per-call jj bookmark list

title: [perf] Bookmark widget createActionGroup is O(entries×bookmarks) — scans all log entries on every open
description:
JujutsuBookmarkWidget.createActionGroup() (ui/log/JujutsuBookmarkWidget.kt) calls logTable.logModel.getAllEntries() three times per open: once to build repoByBookmark, once to build allGroups via flatMap+distinctBy+grouped(), once to get repo list. With 500 entries each carrying 2-3 bookmarks this is ~1500 object allocations before the popup even opens.

Root: getAllEntries() returns the full log list, then flatMap { it.bookmarks } materialises all bookmark objects, then distinctBy and grouped() iterate again. With the stress-test repo (1080 commits, 117 bookmarks) this runs on the EDT — clicking the Bookmarks toolbar button will block the UI thread.

Fix: pre-compute the grouped bookmark map as a field updated by the same workingCopies listener that already updates wcEntries, or fetch it from logTable.logModel directly as a cached structure rather than recomputing from entries every time.
notes: Confirmed in stress-test: widget shows 54/117 bookmarks. Root cause confirmed: sourcing from getAllEntries() (log table entries) not jj bookmark list. Commits beyond the 500-entry log limit have their bookmarks silently dropped. Fix must switch to jj bookmark list as the source of truth, then cross-reference log entries for position/navigation.
close_reason: Central bookmark cache added to LogCache.bookmarks; widget pre-loads from cache off-EDT; RevisionChoicePanel uses cache instead of per-call jj bookmark list

title: Reduce and cache-route getLog calls
description:
LogService.getLog(...) issues a full-metadata 'jj log' shell-out (author, committer, timestamps on top of the basic template). It is still called directly from several places, including the deprecated, fully-dead repositoryStates state in JujutsuStateModel. Meanwhile the per-repo LogCache (jj/LogCache.kt) already provides indexed, in-memory LogEntry lookup by ChangeId/CommitId/BookmarkName with a transparent getLogBasic fallback on miss, but most single-entry retrievals bypass it and re-shell-out.

Goal: delete the dead getLog call, eliminate a redundant working-copy getLog, and route single-revision getLogEntry lookups through the cache where the cache can serve them.

Audit of every direct getLog call site:
- JujutsuStateModel.kt:154 (repositoryStates loader) - DEAD (deprecated, never read/subscribed/invalidated). Delete the whole repositoryStates state.
- WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt:368 (loadCurrentDescription) - working-copy entry on bind; already available in the workingCopies state. Replace with a cached state read.
- JujutsuRepository.kt:152 (getLogEntry(revision)) - single-revision lookup. Route through logCache for ChangeId/CommitId/BookmarkName.
- JujutsuStateModel.kt:138 (workingCopies loader) - source of truth for working copy (mutable, must be fresh). Keep.
- UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:78 - main log fetch, the cache writer. Keep.
- JujutsuFileHistoryDataLoader.kt:29 - file history filtered by filePaths (cache has no path index; needs full author/timestamps). Keep.
design:
basicLogTemplate omits only author, committer, authorTimestamp, committerTimestamp (CliLogService.kt:270,297). All getLogEntry consumers (JujutsuVirtualFile -> .repo/.immutable; JujutsuAnnotationProvider/ChangeService -> .id/parentContentLocator; CompareFileWithBranchAction -> .id; SquashFilesAction -> .immutable/parents) use none of those four fields, so a cache hit (full) or cold-miss (basic) are both correct.

Changes:

1. Delete dead repositoryStates - jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt
   - Remove the @Deprecated val repositoryStates block (lines 142-156).
   - Fix now-stale comments naming repositoryStates to say workingCopies/logRefresh: architecture diagram (~42, 46, 49, 65) and log message (~265). Keep repositoryStateAlarm/scheduleRepositoryRefresh (they drive workingCopies + logRefresh).
   - Reword stray references in: jj/LogEntry.kt:48 (StateKey doc), util/Messaging.kt:106, ui/workingcopy/UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt:193,323, ui/log/UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.kt:45,54, settings/JujutsuConfigurable.kt:421.
   - Keep LogEntry.StateKey itself: still used by workingCopies equalityCheck; only its doc comment changes.

2. Route getLogEntry through the cache - jj/JujutsuRepository.kt:152
   override fun getLogEntry(revision: Revision) = when (revision) {
       is ChangeId -> logCache[revision]
       is CommitId -> logCache[revision]
       is BookmarkName -> logCache[revision]
       else -> logService.getLog(revision).getOrThrow().singleOrNull()
   } ?: throw VcsException("No log entry found for revision $revision")
   logCache[...] already does the getLogBasic fallback on miss and returns null only when jj has no such revision, matching the existing throw-on-absent contract. ChangeId, CommitId, BookmarkName all implement Revision/Ref.

3. Drop redundant working-copy getLog - ui/workingcopy/WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt
   The panel already has update(logEntry: LogEntry) driven by workingCopies.connect in UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel (:194/:211). The on-bind loadCurrentDescription(repo) (:282) re-fetches the same working-copy entry via getLog.
   - At line 282 replace loadCurrentDescription(repo) with: project.stateModel.workingCopies.value[repo.directory.path]?.let { update(it) }
   - Delete the now-unused loadCurrentDescription method (:366-387) and any imports left unused (runInBackground, WorkingCopy).

Out of scope (documented, not changed): RevisionChoicePanel/dialogs that read logCache.all and use .author/.authorTimestamp can render null author on a cold-cache (basic) fallback - a pre-existing cache-fidelity property, unrelated to this change.

Verification:
- ./gradlew check (unit tests + ktlint). LogServiceIntegrationTest exercises getLog; JujutsuStateModelPlatformTest mocks logCache (relaxed) so cache-routed getLogEntry stays green.
- Manual (./gradlew runIde) in a jj sandbox: (1) working-copy panel description/label populate on root/change switch (now from cached state, no extra jj log); edit+revert still work. (2) Open a file from a non-working-copy revision, Compare file with branch, Squash files - all resolve entries via the cache. (3) Confirm jj log not re-issued on working-copy bind (CliExecutor debug log).
close_reason: Deleted dead repositoryStates state, routed getLogEntry through LogCache for ChangeId/CommitId/BookmarkName, and dropped redundant loadCurrentDescription getLog call in WorkingCopyControlsPanel.

title: Tag support: create/set and delete tag actions
description:
Depends on jj-idea-7im4 (tag display). jj 0.37 made tags mutable from the CLI: 'jj tag set <names> -r <rev>' (create/update) and 'jj tag delete <names>'. There is no rename, track/untrack, or push-tag workflow, so this is a much thinner action surface than bookmarks.

Implementation:
- jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt: add tagSet / tagDelete arg builders + executor methods, parallel to the bookmark wrappers (bookmarkSet line ~312, bookmarkDelete ~305). tagSet takes names + a -r target revision; tagDelete takes names.
- jj/CommandExecutor.kt: add the interface methods.
- actions/tag/ (new package): setTagAction.kt (prompt for tag name via a dialog like BookmarkNameDialog, target = selected revision), deleteTagAction.kt. title: Working copy cannot handle copied files
description:
Jujutsu can report a file as copied similarly to how it reports a file as moved. The plugin cannot cope with this, and such files display as conflicted instead. For example, a status output of:

Working copy changes:

title: Switcher polish: picker ellipsis, bookmark summaries, icon placement, highlight, multi-repo
description: The switcher popup and status-bar widget have several visual deficiencies introduced when the widget landed: the popup is too wide for long-description non-bookmarked changes, bookmark rows show no description summary, rows don't ellipsise, the selection highlight is absent, immutable/mutable icons are on the wrong side, and multi-repo behaviour is undefined. This bead fixes all of these on top of the Bead-1 refactored foundation (jj-idea-a5qa must land first).
design:
Reference implementation: origin branch reference/switcher-widget (commit 47dca5d3). Depends on jj-idea-a5qa (RevisionChoice, TextCanvas.append, cachedEntries).

BOOKMARK ROWS SHOW DESCRIPTION SUMMARY (+ bookmark chip icon). Today the Bookmark branch of RevisionChoice renders only 'name (shortId)'. Resolve the target change's summary via the cachedEntries extension from jj-idea-a5qa: BookmarkItem.id: ChangeId? → look up entry in cachedEntries → append summary. Render like the log: chip icon + name + summary.

WIDTH-AWARE ELLIPSIS, consistent in popup AND status bar. TextListCellRenderer does NOT truncate today. Reuse the log's pixel-accurate machinery: FragmentRecordingCanvas + FragmentLayout.truncateToFit / TruncatingLeftRightLayout.configure (ui/components/). Make the picker renderer truncation-aware or swap to a fragment-recording renderer.

STATUS-BAR TEXT WIDTH FIX (interim). displayTextFor (JujutsuStatusBarWidget.kt:106) already falls back to description.summary; add width-aware ellipsis. NOTE: DvcsStatusWidget renders text + one icon only, so full table-style rendering is jj-idea-a5qa's follow-up widget bead — if that bead lands first this item is absorbed. Do not do both.

SELECTION HIGHLIGHT. Selected list row should be visually distinct — bold, like the log window. Verify TextListCellRenderer honours isSelected (selection background / bold); fix if it ignores it.

STATUS ICON ON THE LEFT, BOTH MUTABLE + IMMUTABLE. Switcher's ImmutableAwareRenderer currently appends JujutsuIcons.Immutable on the RIGHT, immutable only. Move to the LEFT and show JujutsuIcons.Mutable (green, JujutsuIcons.kt:48) for mutable items too. Reuse appendStatusIndicators (already toggles Immutable/Mutable in the log). Keep this decoration SWITCHER-SPECIFIC (compare selector does not need it) — wrap canvas.append(choice) with a leading status icon.

MULTI-REPO BEHAVIOUR. guessCurrentRepository (JujutsuStatusBarWidget.kt:52) picks the repo owning the active editor file (JujutsuWidgetSupport.currentRepository); the popup is scoped to that repo (createPopup(repository.repo)). Verify coherence in a multi-root project and that the tooltip shows the root (:84). Document expected behaviour; a repo-picker is out of scope.

Verify (runIde): long-description working copy → status bar narrow + ellipsised; popup rows ellipsise; bookmark rows show summary + chip; selected row highlighted/bold; immutable = left lock icon, mutable = left green icon; multi-root → widget tracks active file's repo.

title: Switcher refactor: RevisionChoice type, TextCanvas.append, cachedEntries extension
description: The working-copy switcher (JujutsuWorkingCopySwitcher) leans heavily on RevisionSelectorPopup: CompareItem is defined inside it, rendering is a top-level extension (appendCompareItem), and log-entry caching lives in buildItemList. This refactor separates concerns so the picker and switcher share well-placed utilities without one depending on the other's internals. Done on a CLEAN base (master, without the widget) so the infrastructure is right before the widget is re-introduced via rebase. No behaviour change — revision selector and switcher must render identically after.
design:
Reference implementation: origin branch reference/switcher-widget (commit 47dca5d3) — the already-built switcher widget + immutable fix (beads alft/5p9h/ca7p). Consult it before re-deriving design.

Files: ui/components/RevisionSelectorPopup.kt, new ui/components/RevisionChoice.kt, ui/components/TextCanvas.kt, jj/LogCache.kt, jj/JujutsuRepository.kt (or a new jj/ extension file), JujutsuCompareWithPopupTest / revision-selector test.

1. RENAME + RELOCATE THE UNION. Move RevisionSelectorPopup.CompareItem into its own UI-layer file RevisionChoice.kt as sealed class RevisionChoice (variants Change(entry: LogEntry), Bookmark(item: BookmarkItem), plus displayName/revision). Keep it in ui/components so popup and switcher share it without one depending on the other. It is a UI view-model, NOT a domain object — do NOT move it to the jj package (Revision alone is just an address, insufficient for rendering). The name avoids RevisionRef because Ref is already a domain interface at Revset.kt:21.

2. MOVE RENDERING ONTO TextCanvas. Replace the top-level appendCompareItem extension (RevisionSelectorPopup.kt:343-360) with a TextCanvas overload fun TextCanvas.append(choice: RevisionChoice) in TextCanvas.kt, consistent with the existing append(changeId) / append(description) / append(bookmarks) overloads (drop the type-suffixed name per user feedback). CompareItemRenderer → RevisionChoiceRenderer calls canvas.append(value). The switcher's ImmutableAwareRenderer also calls canvas.append(value).

3. EXTRACT THE ENTRY CACHE LOADER. buildItemList (RevisionSelectorPopup.kt:306-340) fetches entries via LogCache.getInstance(project) keyed by Expression.ALL. Extract get-or-fetch into a JujutsuRepository extension, e.g. fun JujutsuRepository.cachedEntries(revset: Revset = Expression.ALL): List<LogEntry> (jj layer, near LogCache), following the JujutsuRepository.invalidate extension pattern (JujutsuStateModel.kt:360). buildItemList becomes repo.cachedEntries().filter(...) + logService.getBookmarks().

4. REBASE THE WIDGET. After the refactor change builds clean, jj rebase the reference widget change (pntvqksl / 47dca5d3) on top of it. Resolve conflicts by updating the switcher call sites (JujutsuWorkingCopySwitcher, ImmutableAwareRenderer, the switcher test) to RevisionChoice / TextCanvas.append / cachedEntries. Net: refactor + adapted widget, tree builds, behaviour unchanged.

Verify: ./gradlew check; runIde — Compare-with-Another-Commit selector and switcher popup render exactly as before.
close_reason: RevisionChoice extracted to RevisionChoice.kt, TextCanvas.append(RevisionChoice) added, cachedEntries extension in LogCache.kt. Widget rebased and adapted. ./gradlew check passes.

Fix: per-selection authoritative jj query + act on commit id. Also add a confirmation dialog (Edit / New on Top / Cancel) and visual hint (dim + lock icon) for immutable items.

Add a 'squash into here' action on a destination mutable log entry that allows the user to pick changes from other commits and squash into the selected commit. This emulates IntelliJ's Git support's 'fix up' mechanism.

title: Ignored files need different action enablement
description: Currently, ignored files get all Jujutsu menu items enabled, even when they don't make sense because we know the file will not be versioned. We need to disable these menu items.
design:
PLAN: a shared "selection is only ignored, untracked files" predicate that file-scoped Jujutsu actions use in update().

Reality check first: tracked-but-ignored files (jj tracks anything already snapshotted even if later gitignored; see docs/jj-track-untrack-model.md and jj-idea-ih95) DO have meaningful actions (history, restore, squash, Track toggle). So "ignored" is only a reason to disable when the file is ignored AND not tracked. Prediction alone (JujutsuIgnoreService.isIgnored -> GitignoreCache) is a heuristic (misses global excludes, jj-idea-k5vy); tracked state is authoritative via `jj file list` (JujutsuTrackedFilesService).
Design:
1. New helper beside actions/file/trackUntrackAvailability.kt: `selectionIsOnlyUntrackedIgnored(paths, repo, isIgnored, isTracked): Boolean` - bounded by TRACKED_TOGGLE_SELECTION_LIMIT (=100) like `anySelectedIgnored`; for a selection beyond the bound answer false (do not disable - fail open, never wrongly disable). Cheap path first: only consult the tracked service for paths already predicted-ignored (normally 0-1), keeping update() BGT and O(min(selection,100)).
2. Apply in update() of the file-scoped actions, which are exactly those registered in the `Jujutsu` editor/project-view group (plugin.xml ~:355-368) and the working-copy tree group: RestoreSelectionAction, RestoreToChangeAction, ShowFileHistory(ForSelection)Action, SquashFiles/SquashIntoFiles, SplitFiles/SplitIntoNewParentFiles, ResolveSelectedConflicts, AcceptConflict*, CompareFileWithBranch, annotate. Pattern: `e.presentation.isEnabled = false` + description explaining ("File is ignored and not tracked by jj"), keep visible (matches the JjFeature convention: visible-but-disabled, never hidden). The Tracked toggle is exempt - it is the way out.
3. Platform actions (Reformat/Optimize Imports) offered on the WC tree selection (jj-idea-4lfi/showsLocalFiles): those are the platform's, not ours; limit scope to our own actions and note it. Reformat on an ignored file is harmless.
4. Mixed selections: enable if at least one selected path is NOT (ignored and untracked); the action then operates on the applicable subset (filesets already ignore unmatched paths in jj; verify restore/squash don't error on an ignored path - add a test; if they do, filter paths in the action).
5. Directories: ignore prediction for directories is available but tracked-state per directory is not cheap; treat a directory as applicable (fail open).

Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Disable vs hide? Rec: disable with explanatory description. Why: consistency with JjFeature convention in contributing.md; hidden reads as a bug. Reverse: flip `isEnabled` to `isVisible`.
2. Q: Disable for tracked+ignored files? Rec: no - they are real versioned files.
3. Q: Fail-open at selection >100? Rec: yes.

Scale: per update(): <=100 ignore-cache lookups (in-memory pattern match) + at most one tracked-state query when any predicted-ignored (existing service, cached). Operation-count test: 10k-path selection performs <=100 isIgnored calls and 0 tracked queries when none predicted ignored.
Testing: unit tests for the predicate (pure function with injected lambdas, like trackUntrackAvailability's existing tests); per-action update() tests for 2-3 representative actions. Manual: MT-IGNORE (right-click an ignored untracked file: menu items disabled with tooltip; Track toggle still works; after Track, items enable), MT-CTXMENU, MT-WORKINGCOPY. Regression scope: MT-IGNORE, MT-CTXMENU, MT-WORKINGCOPY.
acceptance_criteria: Jujutsu file actions are visible-but-disabled (with reason) for selections consisting only of ignored, untracked files; enabled again after Track; tracked-ignored files unaffected; update() bounded at 100 paths; unit tests + MT-IGNORE steps added.
notes: jj-idea-4lfi widened what platform-global actions (Reformat Code, Optimize Imports) offer on a Working Copy tree selection, via JujutsuChangesTree.showsLocalFiles. This enablement work should account for that: an ignored file selected in the tree now also gets these platform actions offered, same as any other file, which this bead's 'disable menu items that don't apply' goal should probably cover too.

title: jj file track / untrack context menu actions
description: Add right-click context menu actions wrapping 'jj file track <paths>' and 'jj file untrack <paths>'. Untrack stops tracking a file (only works if it already matches .gitignore). Track explicitly includes a file even if it matches .gitignore. Follow-up to jj-idea-ww5. Add fileTrackArgs/fileUntrackArgs to CliExecutor and create action files in vcs/actions/.
notes: Round 5 (2026-07-15) fixed a real UX gap: clicking Tracked gave no feedback at all. Root causes: (1) executeAsync() has no progress UI - switched to executeWithProgress, matching git fetch/push convention; (2) no success/failure notification - added JujutsuNotifications balloons (INFORMATION on success, ERROR on failure - a deliberate non-blocking exception to this codebase's usual tellUser modal-dialog convention, scoped to this action only); (3) a genuine bug - isSelected() could silently revert the checkbox because it re-read JujutsuTrackedFilesService's cache before the async command's invalidate() landed. Fixed via JujutsuTrackedFilesService.setKnown(): an optimistic cache write made BEFORE the command starts (kept on success, reverted on failure), with resolveTrackedPaths now checking the cache before the free ChangeListManager shortcut (previously the other way around, which could let a stale pending-change entry override a fresh optimistic write).
close_reason: Implemented Track/Untrack context-menu actions (jj file track/untrack) with an always-reachable design: visible in Project view, editor, Working Copy panel, and Commit view (working-copy context only). Ignore-status prediction only drives a non-blocking warning hint, never hide/disable, since our GitignoreCache predictor misses global git excludes that jj honors. ./gradlew check passes.

title: Add preview panel to Squash Into dialog
description:
Add a live preview panel to `SquashIntoDialog` showing the log graph after the squash, similar to `RebasePreviewPanel` used in `RebaseDialog`.

## Background
`RebaseDialog` shows a live simulation of the log graph after rebase via `RebaseSimulator.simulate(...)` + `RebasePreviewPanel`. The `SquashIntoDialog` introduced in jj-idea-1m24 ships without a preview panel — users only see source/destination textually.

## Goal
Compute and render a preview graph showing:
- Source change(s) abandoned (or emptied if keep-emptied)
- Destination change with combined diff/description

## Implementation hints
- Sibling to `RebaseSimulator` — likely a `SquashSimulator` that takes sources, destination, keepEmptied, allEntries and returns a simulated entry list with source state marked.
- Reuse `RebasePreviewPanel` if generic enough, or create `SquashPreviewPanel` mirroring it.
design:
PLAN: live graph preview in SquashIntoDialog, mirroring RebaseDialog (ui/rebase/RebaseDialog.kt:75 `previewPanel = RebasePreviewPanel(project)`, updated from picker selection listeners at :86/:106).

Semantics to simulate (jj squash --from S... --into D): each source S's diff moves into D; S is abandoned unless `--keep-emptied` (then S stays, shown as empty); S's children are rebased onto S's parents (a source with multiple children gets them all re-parented; if D is a descendant of S's parents the usual DAG collapse applies); D keeps its place and gains a "combined" marker; D's descendants rebased (no graph change). If a source has a non-empty remainder (file-subset or hunk-picked squash, `fileSelection` partial), S is NOT empty after the squash, so it is kept like keepEmptied - the preview must reflect "all files ticked && no partial hunks" => abandoned, else kept (modified). Descriptions: when sources have descriptions and the dialog's description box is edited, preview label reflects D's new description (`mergeDescriptions`, SquashIntoDialog.kt:79).
Design:
1. `ui/squash/SquashSimulator.kt` (pure logic, sibling of ui/rebase/RebaseSimulator.kt, whose generic DagNode core - topologicalSort/reparent/scopeToRelevant - is reusable: factor the reparent step out as an internal helper rather than copying). `SquashSimulation(entries, sourceIds, destinationId, abandonedIds, emptiedIds)`; `simulate(allEntries, sources, destination, keepEmptied, sourcesFullyConsumed)`.
2. Reuse RebasePreviewPanel (ui/rebase/RebasePreviewPanel.kt:29): its `update()` is rebase-specific (RebaseSimulator call + highlight + description). Extract the render half into `setSimulation(entries, sourceIds, destinationIds, descriptionText)` (RebasePreviewPanel.update then delegates), and have the squash path call it - one panel, two simulators. Abandoned sources: render faded/strikethrough via a new GraphNode highlight (reuse `JujutsuColors.SOURCE_HIGHLIGHT` family; add a ABANDONED style only if GraphNode supports it, otherwise omit the source rows entirely - Rec: omit; the description label says "N changes abandoned").
3. Dialog wiring: add the panel in `createCenterPanel()` (SquashIntoDialog.kt:360) as a splitter section under the picker (or a collapsible "Preview" group to keep dialog height sane); update on picker selection, keepEmptied checkbox (`deleteEmptyAndMoveCheckBox`), and `onFileInclusionChanged` (:265) so partial-file selections flip abandon<->keep. Both modes: PickDestination (sources fixed) and PickSources (destination fixed, multi-source).
4. Candidate scope: use `picker.entries` (already loaded commits) as `allEntries`; entries outside the loaded window are simply absent (same limitation as rebase; RebaseSimulator.excludedDestinationIds handles unloaded ancestry - reuse the same guard).

Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Show abandoned sources or omit? Rec: omit + description text. Reverse: add faded row style.
2. Q: Share RebasePreviewPanel vs new SquashPreviewPanel (bead allows either)? Rec: share - avoids a 160-line copy; extraction is small.
3. Q: Combine with jj-idea-77i5 (Duplicate Onto preview)? Rec: do the panel extraction in this bead; 77i5 then only adds `DuplicateSimulator`. Cross-link both beads.

Scale: simulator is O(n) over loaded picker entries (n <= page/limit, existing RebaseSimulator has the same shape) run on selection change; must not run per keystroke - debounce through the existing listeners only. Operation-count test: simulate over 10k entries performs one topological sort and no per-source full scans (assert via counting DagNode accessor calls like RebaseSimulatorTest if present).
Testing: SquashSimulatorTest (pure): linear squash into parent, into ancestor, into sibling branch, multi-source, keepEmptied, merge-commit source, partial-selection keeps source; dialog test extending SquashIntoDialogPickSourcesModeTest style (see h8ys for the mock caveat) asserting preview updates on selection. Manual: MT-SQUASH (new rows: preview matches result after OK), MT-CTXMENU. Regression scope: MT-SQUASH, MT-CTXMENU (entry points), MT-LOG-GRAPH (shared RebasePreviewPanel/graph renderer), plus rebase dialog rows in MT-CTXMENU since the panel was refactored.
acceptance_criteria: SquashIntoDialog shows a live post-squash graph preview in both modes, updating on destination/source selection, keep-emptied and file-inclusion changes; RebasePreviewPanel shared with unchanged rebase behaviour; SquashSimulatorTest covers the listed topologies; MT-SQUASH updated.

title: Interactive hunk-level squash
description:
Support `jj squash --interactive` for hunk-level selection from the Squash and Squash Into dialogs.

## Background
The current Squash dialogs (`SquashDialog`, `SquashIntoDialog` from jj-idea-1m24) support file-level selection via the checkbox tree. They do not support choosing individual hunks within a file.

## Goal
Add a way to invoke `jj squash --interactive` (or split via interactive UI) so users can pick specific hunks/lines to move into the destination.

## Notes
- jj's CLI `--interactive` opens `$EDITOR` with a diff edit UI; we likely need our own in-dialog diff editor (similar to IntelliJ's commit message hunk selection).
- Consider building on top of IntelliJ's `LineStatusTracker` or `SelectFilesDialog` infrastructure.
- Applies to both 'Squash into Parent...' and 'Squash Into...' dialogs.
notes: Sequencing (2026-08-25): now depends on jj-idea-xuob (build the checkbox picker first — reuse its picker rather than wiring squash to the old merge-widget HunkDiffPicker) and jj-idea-8a8z (squash needs a per-file diff preview before a Pick Hunks button has anywhere to live). Small note for whenever this is implemented: squashIntoArgs (CliExecutor.kt:266) emits a '--' separator before filesets; squashArgs (:164) does not — align if convenient. Also verify jj squash --interactive support with multiple --from sources before designing the UI; if unsupported, gate hunk-picking to single-source squashes via the existing JjFeature/version-gating mechanism.
close_reason: Shipped: hunk-level squash via jj's diff-editor protocol, reusing Split's 3-pane arrow picker with squash-specific wording (HunkPickerLabels.forSplit/forSquash). Shared extractions: ui/common/HunkSelectionModel.kt (moved+generalized from ui/split, +buildHunkSelection +deletedPaths), ui/common/HunkPickPreviewController.kt (cache/load/render shared by Split and Squash), DiffEditTool.withStagingTree + a deletion manifest (.jj-idea-deleted) so a ticked deletion can move into the destination. CLI: squashIntoInteractiveArgs/CommandExecutor.squashIntoInteractive mirroring splitInteractive; squashArgs now aligns the -- separator with squashIntoArgs. Single-source only (Pick Hunks hidden for multi-source squashes). Verified end-to-end against real jj (partial hunk squash + deletion-move both land correctly in the destination via HunkApplyMain). ./gradlew check green. docs/manual-tests.md and CHANGELOG.md updated. Filed jj-idea-5g8h as a follow-up for Split's symmetric deletion gap (deferred, not in scope here).

title: Suppress IntelliJ commit dialog (Ctrl+K) in Jujutsu projects
description:
Reported in https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/30.

User pressed Ctrl+K in a project with Jujutsu VCS enabled. IntelliJ's standard commit dialog opened, they clicked "Commit", the dialog closed, and the change was lost — nothing appears in `jj log`.

Jujutsu has no "commit" concept in the git sense: changes are snapshotted to the working-copy commit (@) automatically on every jj command. The IDEA commit dialog has no meaningful mapping to a jj operation and silently discards the user's input.

Per owner comment on the issue: "the problem here is that it is still possible to open the commit dialog in a Jujutsu repository." The dialog should not be reachable when the project's VCS is Jujutsu.

Investigation notes:
- Look at `JujutsuVcs` and whether it returns a CheckinEnvironment from `createCheckinEnvironment()`. If it returns non-null, that's likely what's enabling the dialog.
- The platform mechanism for opt-out is typically `AbstractVcs.getCheckinEnvironment()` returning null, plus possibly suppressing the `ChangesViewManager.checkin` action group.
- Ctrl+K (`CheckinProjectAction`) needs to either be disabled for Jujutsu roots or routed to a jj-appropriate alternative (e.g. opening the Describe dialog on the working copy commit). Decide which during implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pressing Ctrl+K in a Jujutsu project does not open the standard IDEA commit dialog
- If routed to a jj-appropriate action (e.g. Describe @), that action works end-to-end; otherwise the shortcut is a no-op with a clear notification explaining jj's model
- No path through the UI silently discards user-typed commit messages
- In a project with both a Jujutsu root and a Git (or other VCS) root, the standard commit dialog still works for non-jj roots — only jj-rooted changes are affected
- Verified in the IDE against (a) a pure jj repo and (b) a multi-root project mixing jj with at least one other VCS
notes: Implementation: isCommitActionDisabled() disables Ctrl+K in jj-only projects; DescribeWorkingCopyAction bound to Ctrl+K opens describe dialog; JujutsuCheckinEnvironment.commit() returns a clear error message in mixed-VCS projects instead of silently discarding the commit. Git changes in the same commit proceed normally.
close_reason: Implemented isCommitActionDisabled() override in JujutsuVcs and added DescribeWorkingCopyAction bound to Ctrl+K

title: Show conflicted files in log details pane; allow resolution from working copy
description:
When a conflicted change is selected in the log, the commit details panel should mark conflicted files with MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS status so they appear in red. The 'Resolve Conflicts…' action should be visible in the details panel only when the selected entry is the working copy.

## Why
Currently ChangeService.loadChanges() assigns no special status to conflicted files — they appear as plain modifications. Users expect to see which files are in conflict when inspecting a conflicted commit in the log, and to be able to resolve them if it's the working copy.

## What to build

### 1. Extend ChangeService.loadChanges(entry)
After loading file changes for entry, call repo.commandExecutor.resolveList(entry.id) to get conflicted paths. resolveList(revision) already accepts any Revision — it's not limited to WorkingCopy. Build Change objects for those paths with FileStatus.MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS instead of the default.

### 2. Guard ResolveSelectedConflictsAction in details pane context

design:
## Design: FileChange.isConflicted integration

### Prerequisite (done or in-progress)
FileChange now carries `isConflicted: Boolean` (default `false`). `FileChange.from(change)` checks `change.fileStatus == FileStatus.MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS` and propagates it to the `Modified` variant. `ResolveSelectedConflictsAction` uses `e.changes.filter { it.isConflicted }` — it no longer reads raw `Change` objects.

### Implementation approach

#### Step 1: ChangeService.loadChanges(entry) — cross-reference with resolveList
After `repo.logService.getFileChanges(entry)` returns `List<FileChange>`, call `repo.commandExecutor.resolveList(entry.id)` to get conflicted paths. When mapping `FileChange` → `Change`, pass `FileStatus.MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS` for paths in the conflict set:

```kotlin
val conflictedPaths = repo.commandExecutor.resolveList(entry.id)
    .takeIf { it.isSuccess }
    ?.let { parseConflictPaths(it.stdout) }
    ?: emptySet()

return fileChanges.map { fileChange ->
    val before = ...
    val after = ...
    val status = if (fileChange.filePath.path in conflictedPaths) FileStatus.MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS else null
    if (status != null) Change(before, after, status) else Change(before, after)
}
```

The details pane tree passes these `Change` objects through `VcsDataKeys.CHANGES`. When an action calls `e.changes`, `FileChange.from(change)` preserves the conflict status via `isConflicted`. So `ResolveSelectedConflictsAction` works in the details pane automatically.

#### Step 2: Guard resolution on working copy
`ResolveSelectedConflictsAction.update` — add:
```kotlin
val logEntry = e.logEntry  // null in working copy panel (always allow)
if (logEntry != null && !logEntry.isWorkingCopy) { e.presentation.isEnabled = false; return }
```

This uses `JujutsuDataKeys.LOG_ENTRY` already injected by `JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.additionalDataProvider` (line ~67). Action is visible but disabled for historical conflicted commits, enabled only for working copy.

#### Cost consideration
One extra `jj resolve --list -r <revision>` subprocess per log entry shown in details pane. This only runs on selection, not on log load. Could memoise in ChangeService or cache on LogEntry if perf becomes an issue.

### Key files
- `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/jj/ChangeService.kt` — add resolveList cross-reference
- `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/actions/file/ResolveSelectedConflictsAction.kt` — add isWorkingCopy guard
- `src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/vcs/changes/JujutsuChangeProvider.kt` — reuse `parseConflictPaths()` (extract if needed)

title: open in remote at line
description: When opening a file in remote from the editor, respect the line number or selection
design:
## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Editor (independent)

**Line mapping approach**: Capture local document text + caret/selection on EDT before runInBackground. In background: fetch remote file content via commandExecutor.show(commitHash, relativePath). Use ComparisonManager.getInstance().compareLines(remoteText, localText, DEFAULT, EmptyProgressIndicator()) to get List<LineFragment>. Walk fragments: lines in context sections get remoteLine = localLine + accumulatedDelta; lines inside a locally-changed block map to the start of that block's remote range. Fallback: if remote fetch fails, open without fragment.

**URL fragment format**:
- GitHub: single=#L42, range=#L42-L50
- GitLab: single=#L42, range=#L42-50

**Files to change**:
1. RemoteUrlBuilder.kt — add lineRange: IntRange? = null to fileUrl(); append fragment based on kind
2. OpenInRemoteFromEditorGroup.kt — capture localText + localRange on EDT, call mapToRemoteRange() in background, pass result to fileUrl()
3. RemoteUrlBuilderTest.kt — tests for single line / range fragments for both GitHub and GitLab

### Phase 2 — History/Diff views (blocked by dependencies)
Once jj-idea-7e5n and jj-idea-6dvh are done, extend to pass line numbers when opening from diff viewers and Open Repository Version editors (caret available from the diff viewer's editor component).
notes:
Prerequisites: jj-idea-7e5n (Open Repository Version editor menus) and jj-idea-6dvh (Diff view editor menus) must be done before Phase 2 (history/diff case). Phase 1 (editor case) can be done independently.

Line number mapping approach: fetch remote file content via commandExecutor.show(), use IntelliJ ComparisonManager.compareLines() to build a line map, then walk fragments to translate local line numbers to remote. Lines inside locally-added blocks map to the start of that block's remote range.

title: Interdiff
description: Add jj interdiff support — compare diffs between two revisions. Useful for reviewing how changes evolved across revisions.
design:
PLAN: Interdiff (jj interdiff --from A --to B): "what changed between two versions of a change / between two arbitrary commits, ignoring changes that came only from rebasing".

What jj does: compares (A rebased onto B's parent) with B - i.e. diff-of-diffs. Output modes: --summary, --git, --stat, --tool. It produces NO materialised file contents for either side, so the IDE side-by-side viewer cannot be fed through the existing ContentLocator/DiffRequestBuilder path (actions/filechange/DiffRequestBuilder.kt, vcs/VcsExtensions.kt) which fetches before/after via `jj file show`.
Approach (v1): patch-based viewer.
1. jj layer: `interdiffSummary(from, to)` -> `jj interdiff --from F --to T --summary` (file list + status, reuse the existing summary parser behind diffSummaryBetween, CommandExecutor.kt:153) and `interdiffGit(from, to, filePath?)` -> `--git` (mirror diffGit/diffGitFile, CommandExecutor.kt:331/340; args builders next to diffGitArgs, CliExecutor.kt:117, READ_ONLY). Add cache entries keyed by (from commit_id, to commit_id) - commit ids not change ids, because both sides may be hidden/divergent (see jj-idea-wiz0 for why change ids are unsafe for reads).
2. Entry points: (a) Log context menu with exactly 2 selected rows: "Interdiff Between Selected" (from = older by log order? NO - order matters semantically; define from = the one the user selected first/anchor, and label the dialog "A -> B" with a Swap button); (b) single selected change with an evolog predecessor: depends on jj-idea-1y76 (Evolog) - out of scope here, but design the action to accept (from,to) so Evolog can call it; (c) file history "compare with..." not in v1.
3. UI: a dialog/tool-window tab with the standard JujutsuChangesTree of changed files (from the summary) and, on selection, a read-only unified-diff viewer built from the `--git` patch text for that file via the platform `PatchDiffRequest` (platform/vcs-impl/.../changes/patch/tool/PatchDiffRequest.kt - confirm it is public API for sinceBuild 251 via verifyPlugin before relying on it; fallback: render with `DiffContentFactory` against reconstructed before/after text from hunks, or plain `UnifiedDiffViewer`-like editor with diff highlighting). Header explains "changes in B not explained by rebase of A".
4. Empty result ("no interdiff") -> friendly message: the two commits have identical changes.

Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Patch viewer (unified) vs side-by-side? Rec: unified patch v1 - interdiff has no real file contents, side-by-side would need synthesising a temp commit (mutating/op-log noise) or scratch workspace. Reverse/follow-up: synthesise sides with `jj duplicate`+`--at-op` read-only snapshot (needs spike).
2. Q: Which entry first? Rec: two-row log selection; Evolog integration follows jj-idea-1y76.
3. Q: Version gate? interdiff is old; no JjFeature.

Scale: bounded by jj; plugin parses one summary + one patch per selected file (lazy on selection), no loop over commits. Operation-count test: opening the dialog = 1 jj call; selecting k files = k patch calls (cached; reselect = 0).
Testing: CliExecutor args tests; summary/patch parser tests from captured jj output (include rename + binary + delete rows); contract test: commit X, `jj rebase` + amend to Y, assert interdiff excludes rebase-only noise. Manual: new MT-LOG-DETAILS/MT-CTXMENU rows; scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-LOG-TABLE (multi-select enablement), MT-DIFF.
acceptance_criteria: Two-row log selection offers Interdiff; dialog lists changed files and shows per-file patch; empty-result message; Swap works; uses commit ids; arg/parser/contract tests; manual-tests rows added.

title: Absorb operation
description: Add jj absorb support — automatically move working copy changes into the right ancestor commits. Accessible from toolbar or context menu.
design:
PLAN: jj absorb (GitHub #70 too)

Command: `jj absorb [--from <rev>=@] [--into <revset>] [--] [FILESETS]` moves each hunk of the source into the nearest mutable ancestor that last touched those lines; unmatched hunks stay. Present far below JjVersion.MINIMUM, so no JjFeature gate.
Layers (follow the squash pattern):
1. jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt: `absorbArgs(from: Revision, into: Revision?, filePaths)` -> `JjInvocation(REVERSIBLE, "absorb", "--from", rev, ["--into", rev], ["--", filesets])` next to `squashArgs` (CliExecutor.kt:365); `override fun absorb(...)`; declare `fun absorb(...)` in jj/CommandExecutor.kt beside squash (~:443). Result parsing: absorb prints "Absorbed changes into N revisions:" + per-revision lines and "Rebased N descendant commits"; surface that text verbatim in the success notification (do not parse into structure - format is not stable). Exit 0 with "Nothing changed." means nothing absorbable -> notify info, not error.
2. Action `actions/filechange/AbsorbAction` (DumbAwareAction, BGT update, mirrors SquashFilesAction): source = working copy by default; enabled only when the entry is the working copy (v1: no `--from <other>` UI), not empty, and has a mutable parent. Operate on selected files when a selection exists (filesets), else the whole working copy. Register in plugin.xml `Jujutsu.Absorb`, add to: Working Copy toolbar/panel (GH #70 asks for it there), Working Copy tree context menu next to Squash (plugin.xml ~:364), the editor/project-view group (~:364 group), and the main menu group (actions/JujutsuMainMenuGroup.kt). Icon: a new SVG via the icon conventions (see jj-idea-kcgf "icons for squash actions" - reuse that family when it lands; until then AllIcons.Vcs.Merge-like placeholder is NOT acceptable; draw one in ui/common/JujutsuIcons.kt).
3. Preview: absorb is non-interactive and may touch many commits, which is a surprise risk. v1 shows no dialog but uses the standard undo notification (REVERSIBLE -> op-log undo via actions/undo) so one click reverses it. Follow-up bead: dry-run preview (jj has no --dry-run; would need `jj op` snapshot diff) - leave out.
4. After success: `repo.invalidate(vfsChanged = true)` (history was rewritten and files may change), log refresh via the standard path.
Immutable ancestors: jj skips immutable commits automatically; if every candidate is immutable the result is "Nothing changed." (covered above).

Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Dialog with `--into` revset picker? Rec: no for v1 - the headline value is one-click distribute; `--into` is a power option and can be a later "Absorb Into..." action. Reverse: add dialog reusing SquashIntoDialog's commit picker.
2. Q: Selected-files absorb in v1? Rec: yes - cheap (filesets) and matches Squash/Restore behaviour.
3. Q: Confirm before running? Rec: no confirm, undo notification instead (consistent with jj-idea-t0iy undo balloon).

Scale: one jj invocation; O(1) in plugin. No traversal.
Testing: argument unit tests in CliExecutorTest style (`absorbArgs` with/without files, from/into); action update() tests (hidden for historical/immutable entries); contract test: repo with 3 stacked commits editing distinct lines, edit in @, absorb, assert each ancestor got its fix and @ is empty. Manual: MT-WORKINGCOPY (button/context menu), MT-CTXMENU, MT-SQUASH (shares menu group; check ordering). Regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-CTXMENU, MT-SQUASH.
acceptance_criteria: Absorb available from Working Copy panel, tree context menu, and main menu; absorbs whole WC or selected files; success notification shows jj's summary with Undo; 'Nothing changed' shown as info; unit + contract tests pass; manual-tests updated with MT-* scope.
notes: Also requested via GitHub #70 (cYDN48, 2026-08-15): suggests placing the absorb button in the Working Copy area, and gives a concrete motivating workflow — implement several separate changes, test, find bugs across a few of them, fix them all in one new change, then jj absorb distributes each fix back into the change that introduced it.
