title: Log context menu: use registered Jujutsu.GitFetch/GitPush (and other registered actions) instead of factory instances (GitHub #135)
description:
Reporter (SergejSalnikov) wants the jj log context menu to inject actions via ActionManager rather than instantiating them, specifically Jujutsu.GitFetch and Jujutsu.GitPush, ideally the others too (suggests: liveSelection -> ActionManager.getAction(id), else the factory).

JujutsuLogContextMenuActions.kt:168-169 uses gitFetchAction/gitPushAction factories even on the liveSelection path, unlike New/Edit/Describe/Rebase (ManagedActions[...]). Do the same for Fetch/Push; the registered Jujutsu.GitPush must read the selected log entries from the data context to keep 'push selected changes'. Audit other factory-built entries for registered equivalents. Narrower, earlier step than jj-idea-66id (declarative groups, GH #68). Treat the action IDs as a stable contract if the reporter overrides them.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/135
design:
PLAN (label for-human: decisions flagged): route Fetch/Push in the log context menu through the REGISTERED actions (`Jujutsu.GitFetch`/`Jujutsu.GitPush`) on the live-selection path, after bringing the registered actions to parity with the factories - because today they are NOT drop-in equivalents.
Facts: the log menu builds `add(gitFetchAction(project, uniqueRepo)); add(gitPushAction(project, uniqueRepo, entries))` unconditionally (ui/log/JujutsuLogContextMenuActions.kt:~168-169) while New/Edit/Describe/Rebase use `ManagedActions[...]` on the `liveSelection` path (:~88-137, ManagedActions = `ActionManager.getAction(id)`, actions/Extensions.kt:9-21). Differences between factory and registered versions (verified in code):
 - Fetch: factory `gitFetchAction(project, repo)` (actions/git/gitRemoteActions.kt:~55-75) fetches ONLY the selection's repo (`GitFetchDialog.loadDialogData(target)`, skips the dialog when it has 1 remote) and is disabled when `repo == null` (ambiguous multi-repo selection); registered `GitFetchAction` (actions/git/GitFetchAction.kt:20-65) loads ALL repos' data and shows the repo-selector dialog when several.
 - Push: factory `gitPushAction(project, repo, entries)` (:88-140) scopes the DEFAULT push to the single selected change (`val revision = entries.singleOrNull()?.id`, `GitPushDialog.loadDialogData(target, revision)` and `checkAndPush(spec, project, revision)`); registered `GitPushAction` (GitPushAction.kt:28-90) reads `e.logEntries`/`e.repoForFile` and builds change targets from them (so "push selected changes" works) but loads `loadAllDialogData(repos)` with no revision scoping and calls `checkAndPush(spec, project)` WITHOUT `revision` => the "push this commit's ancestry" scoping is lost.
Steps:
1. Parity in the registered actions (behaviour-preserving for their current invocations: toolbar/VCS menu with an empty selection): in `GitFetchAction.actionPerformed`: `val repo = e.logEntries.uniqueRepo` (actions/ActionEventExtensions.kt:46) - if non-null, fetch/dialog scoped to that repo exactly like the factory; else current all-repos behaviour. In `GitPushAction`: `val revision = e.logEntries.singleOrNull()?.id`; pass to `GitPushDialog.loadAllDialogData(repos, revision)` (extend to accept the revision for the initial repo, or reuse `loadDialogData(target, revision)` for the selection's repo) and to `checkAndPush(spec, project, revision)`.
2. Then the log menu (liveSelection path only): `add(ManagedActions["Jujutsu.GitFetch"]); add(ManagedActions["Jujutsu.GitPush"])`; keep the factories for `liveSelection = false` (the "link menu"/fixed-selection path used by the details pane/popups where no data context selection exists - `JujutsuLogContextMenuActions` KDoc ~:60-100; same reason as the other liveSelection branches).
3. Enablement parity: factory is disabled for ambiguous multi-repo selections (`nullAndDumbAwareAction(repo=null)`); the registered actions enable whenever `e.project.isJujutsu` - for Push with a cross-repo selection the registered code handles it (`changeRepo = logEntries.uniqueRepo` null hides one scope) so enabled is fine; for Fetch ambiguous selection -> falls back to all repos (acceptable, arguably better).
4. "Audit other factory-built entries for registered equivalents" (bead): inventory in `createActionGroup`: compare*, copy*, Duplicate(+Onto), Squash/SquashInto/SquashFrom, Split(+NewParent), createBookmark/advance/move/setTag, abandon, resolveConflicts, openInRemote: of these only some have registered ids (Jujutsu.MoveChangeUp/Down are already ManagedActions); abandon/squash/split/bookmark have NO ids (documented at ui/log/JujutsuLogContextMenuActions.kt:69-77 and in jj-idea-plpa). Record the inventory in this bead's notes; converting them is the larger jj-idea-66id (declarative groups) territory.
5. Stability contract: the action ids `Jujutsu.GitFetch`/`GitPush` are a public contract if reporters override/keymap them - add a unit test asserting the ids exist in plugin.xml and resolve to the expected classes (a guard against accidental rename), and mention in CHANGELOG.
Decisions made without the user: Q: do parity changes alter the toolbar/VCS-menu behaviour? Only when a log selection exists in the data context (toolbar: LOG_ENTRIES present when invoked from the log toolbar with selection - that is today's "push selected changes" behaviour already); empty selection unchanged. Q: keep factories? Yes for non-live menus. Depends on jj-idea-1y1j/66id per the bead - those are `DEPENDS ON` edges in beads but this narrower step can land independently (bead says "Narrower, earlier step than 66id") - recommend removing the hard dependency on 1y1j (decision bead) so this isn't blocked: user to confirm.
Scale: none. Testing: update JujutsuLogContextMenuActionsLiveSelectionTest/ActionsTest to expect registered instances (identity equals `ManagedActions["Jujutsu.GitFetch"]`) on the live path and factories on the other; parity tests: GitFetchAction scoping with a stub project and `e.logEntries` (single repo -> only that repo in the dialog data), GitPushAction passes revision for a single selection (capture `checkAndPush`/dialog data through the existing seams); manual: MT-CTXMENU (right-click a commit: Fetch/Push entries show keymap hints; Push on a selected change pushes that change's bookmarks only), MT-GIT. Regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-GIT.
acceptance_criteria: Log live-selection menu uses registered Jujutsu.GitFetch/GitPush with behaviour parity (repo scoping, revision-scoped default push); factories remain for non-live menus; inventory of other factory entries recorded; id-contract test; MT-CTXMENU/MT-GIT rows.
notes: 2026-10-01: Reporter confirms they override Jujutsu.GitFetch/GitPush with jj sync / jj upload implementations. Action IDs are a real external contract - don't rename them. Registered GitPush must still read the selected entries from the data context.

title: Bulk conflict accept: single op + undo
description: Follow-up to jj-idea-5k16. The multi-select AcceptConflictSideAction goes through JujutsuMergeProvider.acceptFilesRevisions, one raw resolve per file (N ops), so a single undo balloon would only revert the last. Group by tool into at most 2 resolve calls (or revert an op range) and attach addUndoTracking.
close_reason: Bulk accept groups by (repo, tool): one resolve op and one undo balloon

title: Details pane width is set by the non-wrapping author/date row, so chips clip at high zoom
description: At Zoom IDE 200% the commit details pane's width is governed by the 'Name <email> · date' row, which doesn't wrap; the pane doesn't get narrower than it, and a bookmark chip (unbreakable) on the line above can be clipped at the right edge (e.g. '@origin' shown as '@origir'). At 100% the date wraps onto its own line. Not caused by jj-idea-3as8 (no break/wrap logic changed in AtomicHtmlView), but unconfirmed against the base commit; found during manual testing 2026-10-01. Investigate preferred/minimum span of the pane and whether the date can wrap at high zoom.
design:
PLAN: reproduce at 200% zoom, then make the author/date line wrap (or the pane's minimum width ignore it).
Facts: the details pane is ui/log/JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt; its metadata HTML builds the author line in `appendUserWithTimestamp` (:~45-57): name/email as a link chip, then `space()` (breakable, jj-idea-myje) then `appendUnbreakable("· <timestamp>")` - the date chip is an unbreakable AtomicHtmlView (ui/components/AtomicHtmlView.kt, UnbreakableContent) so the longest unbreakable unit on the line is "· 2026-10-01 14:03" and, with the email chip, the minimum content width the HTML view reports can exceed the pane at high zoom. Bookmark chips are also unbreakable (kds1), so when the pane can't shrink below the widest unbreakable run, the chip line is clipped on the right (the "@origir" symptom). The bead notes it was not caused by 3as8; step 0 must confirm against the base commit.
Step 0 (30 min): runIde at 200% zoom with a commit having a long bookmark `name@origin` and an author with an email; log `JBHtmlPane`'s `preferredSize`/`minimumSize`/`getMinimumSpan(View.X_AXIS)` for the root view (AtomicHtmlView.getMinimumSpan returns its full width, as for any atomic leaf - confirm in AtomicHtmlView.getMinimumSpan/getPreferredSpan) and the splitter/scroll container's behaviour (the details panel lives in a JBSplitter/scroll pane - check whether `setHorizontalScrollBarPolicy(NEVER)` forces width = viewport and clips instead of growing a scrollbar).
Fix options, in order of preference:
 A. Make the unbreakable date chip breakable *as a unit from the author name* only (already true via space()) and ensure the overall pane never reports a minimum span > its viewport: override `getMinimumSpan` on AtomicHtmlView to return min(content width, available width)?? - NO: an atomic chip wider than the pane must still be clipped or ellipsized; so choose B.
 B. (Rec) Cap each unbreakable chip's width to the pane width and ellipsize at the chip level: AtomicHtmlView.paint truncates its last text run with "..." when `allocation.width < preferred` (tooltip carries the full text via the existing chip tooltip path), so a long `name@remote` degrades to `name@rem...` instead of a hard clip mid-glyph, and the pane's minimum is no longer dominated by one chip. This also fixes the clipped-chip symptom for chips unrelated to the date row.
 C. Allow the details pane to scroll horizontally when content exceeds the width (JBScrollPane HORIZONTAL_SCROLLBAR_AS_NEEDED) - simplest and lossless but adds a scrollbar at high zoom; fallback if B proves invasive.
Decisions made without the user: Q: B vs C? Rec: B (matches how the log table's capped decorations behave, `cappedDecorations` in JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt:~128) with C as fallback. Reverse: switch the policy.
Scale: none (per-render, one detail pane). Testing: HtmlTextCanvas/AtomicHtmlView platform tests exist (3as8 area): add a test laying out a chip in a 60px allocation asserting the painted text ends with the ellipsis and `getMinimumSpan` <= allocation; zoom-sensitive geometry via JBUIScale override. Manual: MT-LOG-DETAILS at 100% and 200% IDE zoom, light/dark, with long bookmark names, long email, and committer line present. Regression scope: MT-LOG-DETAILS, MT-LOG-TABLE (shares AtomicHtmlView/ChipContent? only if the log table uses it - grep first), MT-BOOKMARK (chip rendering).
acceptance_criteria: At 200% zoom no chip is clipped mid-glyph in the details pane (ellipsis or scroll instead); behaviour at 100% unchanged; repro captured in notes; layout test + MT-LOG-DETAILS zoom row added.

title: Platform test runs end with an AllVcses ProjectImpl leak (subset runs; seen intermittently on full runs)
description: Pre-existing (also on base commit 57f6408d): running only a subset of platform tests ends with 'Found a leaked instance of ProjectImpl' via AllVcses$MyExtensionPointListener (LeakHunter, testApplication.kt:381). The full ./gradlew check normally does not hit it, but during jj-idea-3as8/5zio manual testing (2026-10-01) full platformTest failed the same way on 3 consecutive runs - including on the untouched branch code - and passed again once no runIde sandbox was running/leftover (cause unproven; suspect state left by killed runIde runs or the shared sandbox). Investigate the leak root path and whether the test project is disposed before the VCS EP listener releases it.
design:
PLAN: root-cause the ProjectImpl leak reported via AllVcses$MyExtensionPointListener, then fix test teardown (or the plugin if it is ours).
Facts: LeakHunter fails platform tests at JVM end ("Found a leaked instance of ProjectImpl", testApplication.kt:381). Retention path runs through `AllVcses$MyExtensionPointListener` - a listener the PLATFORM registers on the `com.intellij.vcs` extension point; it holds `Project` strongly while a test project is alive. Typical causes: (1) a test creates the project via projectFixture() and a VCS is activated for it (our `JujutsuVcs`, or `AbstractVcs` activation through `ProjectLevelVcsManager.setDirectoryMapping`) and the project is not disposed/closed before the application test fixture ends - the EP listener's reference is released only on project close; (2) our code registers something Project-bound against an application-level collection that outlives the project (static caches keyed on Project/VirtualFile, `ManagedActions`, Disposer parents) - cf. jj-idea-8awj (plugin-classloader retention audit) which owns that production-side hunt; (3) leftover killed-runIde state (the bead's observation: passes once no runIde sandbox runs) pointing to shared sandbox dirs (`build/idea-sandbox`, system dir locks) making project close fail/hang.
Investigation steps (timeboxed 2h):
 1. Reproduce deterministically: `./gradlew platformTest --tests '<single class>'` x3, with and without a running runIde; capture the LeakHunter report (it prints the root-to-leak reference path) and save it in notes.
 2. Bisect which test class leaves it: run each @Tag("platform") class alone (script loop over test class names) and record the failing set; the common factor (uses `ProjectLevelVcsManager`? `JujutsuVcs`? `ChangeListManager`?) names the cause.
 3. Check teardown: for failing classes, does the `projectFixture()` use `openAfterCreation`/`isOpenedCompletely`, and is the project closed (`ProjectManagerEx.closeAndDispose`)? Add a shared `@AfterAll` helper (test support) that deactivates VCS mappings (`ProjectLevelVcsManager.getInstance(p).directoryMappings = emptyList()`) before disposal - this removes the VCS from AllVcses' active set so the listener releases the project.
 4. If the path includes plugin classes (Jujutsu*), it is production retention: fix via Disposer parenting (jj-idea-8awj) and add the offending class to that bead's audit list.
 5. Runner hygiene: in `platformTest` (build.gradle.kts:393) make the sandbox directory per-invocation (or document: don't run platformTest with runIde alive) if cause (3) is confirmed; add a Gradle pre-check that fails fast with a clear message when a sandbox lock/process exists.
Decisions made without the user: Q: suppress LeakHunter for this path (allowlist) as a stop-gap? Rec: no, only as a last resort with a TODO linking this bead - suppressing hides real plugin leaks (the very thing 8awj audits).
Scale: none. Testing: acceptance = 3 consecutive full `./gradlew platformTest` runs and a subset run all pass, with and without a runIde sandbox open. Manual: none. Related: jj-idea-8awj, jj-idea-h8ys (same test infra pitfalls, document findings in contributing.md Testing Strategy).
acceptance_criteria: Retention path captured; root cause identified and fixed in test teardown or production code; subset and full platformTest runs pass 3x (with and without runIde running); no LeakHunter suppression added.

title: Headless platform tests can't render SvgIcon (1x1 placeholder), so icon pixels at zoom are untestable
description: Our SvgIcon loads through a private class loader that yields a 1x1 placeholder in the headless platform-test environment, and headless icons don't grow with the test's scale. IconZoomRenderingTest (jj-idea-3as8) therefore can only check reserved width, text positioning and centring around a platform icon, not our icons' own pixels at real zoom. Find a way to render our real icons headless (or a test-only icon loader) so icon size/vertical centring at 85/150/200% can be asserted, replacing part of the manual MT-LOG-DETAILS zoom pass.
design:
PLAN: find a headless way to render the plugin's REAL SVG icons so icon pixels/centring at 85/150/200% can be asserted; time-boxed spike (2h) with three candidate approaches in order of cost.
Facts: `SvgIcon` (ui/common/SvgColorPatcher.kt:42-100) patches colours into SVG bytes and loads via `IconLoader.findIcon(path, SvgBytesClassLoader(resourceName, modifiedBytes))` - a private `ClassLoader(null)` serving the bytes through a `data:image/svg+xml;base64,...` URL with a custom `URLStreamHandler` (:104-125). The existing `IconZoomRenderingTest` (ui/components/IconZoomRenderingTest.kt) already calls `IconLoader.activate()` ("Unit-test mode swaps real icons for blank placeholders; render the real ones here", :~50-52) and emulates zoom with `JBUIScale.setUserScaleFactorForTest(scale)`; its limitation per this bead: our own SvgIcon still yields a 1x1 placeholder, and headless icons don't grow with the test's scale.
Approaches:
 A. (cheapest) Verify the ordering: `IconLoader.activate()` must run BEFORE the first `SvgIcon.delegate()` call (the delegate is cached forever in `SvgIcon.delegate` after first creation: a delegate created while `IconLoader` was in "test mode" stays a placeholder even after activate()). Test fix: construct fresh icons AFTER activate (SvgIcon instances are created in `JujutsuIcons` static init - object initialisation may happen before the test calls activate; so create new `SvgIcon.load(path, ...)` instances inside the test, or reset via a test seam `SvgIcon.resetCachedDelegateForTest()`; also clear `IconLoader`'s icon cache (`IconLoader.clearCache()`/`IconLoaderKt.clearCacheInTests`?) between zoom levels because `findIcon` caches by path+classloader (our classloader instance is new per colour digest so cached entries are keyed by it). Cheap to try first.
 B. Bypass the platform icon pipeline in tests: render the patched SVG bytes ourselves with the SVG loader the platform uses internally (`SVGLoader`/ `com.intellij.ui.svg.SvgKt.renderSvg`? internal) or with a test-time dependency (Apache Batik) to rasterise to BufferedImage at a given scale: test-only dependency in build.gradle.kts `testImplementation("org.apache.xmlgraphics:batik-transcoder:1.17")`; assert bounding box of non-transparent pixels is centred within a tolerance and size == 16*scale. Adds a dependency and tests the SVG, not the plugin's loading code path (acceptable: the question is icon geometry, not the loader).
 C. Make SvgIcon's loader injectable (`SvgIcon.iconFactory: (path, bytes) -> Icon` default = IconLoader path) and have tests supply an `ImageIcon` produced via approach B for deterministic pixel assertions - gives a seam for other tests (e.g. recolour tests: assert the patched colour appears in pixels).
Recommendation: try A (30 min); if it fails, B+C. Acceptance: a new test class (or extension of IconZoomRenderingTest) asserting for Bookmark/Conflict/Immutable/Repo icons at scales [0.85, 1, 1.5, 2]: rendered width/height == base*scale (+-1px), vertical centre of painted pixels within 1px of the line centre when placed via the real chip layout; then delete the corresponding manual MT-LOG-DETAILS zoom bullets (the part covered; keep a short eyeball check).
Decisions made without the user: Q: add Batik as a test dependency? Rec only if A fails (dependency weight). 
Scale: tests only. Manual: MT-LOG-DETAILS zoom pass partially retired. Regression scope: none (test-only) unless C touches SvgIcon (then MT-LOG-TABLE icons smoke).
acceptance_criteria: Real plugin icons render with correct size/centring assertions at 85/100/150/200% in headless platform tests (approach A, else B+C); corresponding manual zoom bullets reduced.

title: platformTest full-suite-only LeakHunter flake: AllVcses extension-point listener leaks ProjectImpl
description:
./gradlew check (running the full platformTest suite together) intermittently fails LeakHunter
with "Found a leaked instance of class com.intellij.openapi.project.impl.ProjectImpl". Confirmed
across multiple sessions (first noted during jj-idea-82fo, reproduced again during jj-idea-sr42)
that this is NOT caused by any specific test's own code - running platformTest alone (isolated
from the rest of the suite) is consistently clean; the leak only appears intermittently when the
full test task runs together with other suites in the same JVM/session.

The leaked instance's strong-reference path (from the LeakHunter assertion output) consistently
names:
  com.intellij.openapi.vcs.impl.projectlevelman.AllVcses.myProject
    -> AllVcses$MyExtensionPointListener.this$0
    -> held in the "com.intellij.vcs" ExtensionPointImpl's listeners collection

i.e. AllVcses registers an ExtensionPointListener that captures its owning Project, and that
listener isn't being unregistered when some (disposed) test's Project is torn down - a platform/
test-fixture-level teardown gap, not application code in this plugin. Likely a per-test-suite
ordering interaction: some earlier test suite's Project disposal doesn't fully unwind the
AllVcses-registered EP listener before a later suite's LeakHunter check runs against a fresh
snapshot.

Not blocking day-to-day work (re-running platformTest alone, or check with this the only
failure, has always confirmed the change under test is unaffected) but worth a real
investigation/upstream report rather than continuing to just note it away each time it's hit.

Next steps to investigate:
- Try to build a minimal multi-suite repro (two platformTest classes run back-to-back) to nail
  down which specific test's teardown leaves the AllVcses EP listener registered.
- Check if this is a known JetBrains platform test-framework issue (search YouTrack for AllVcses
  + LeakHunter + ExtensionPointListener) before assuming it's fixable from this codebase's side.
close_reason: Root cause: AllVcses ctor adds app-level VcsEP listener before registering removal with Disposer; JujutsuStateModel's pooled loader was first to create AllVcses and could do so during project teardown, leaking ProjectImpl. Fix: JujutsuStateModel.init eagerly creates AllVcses on live project; SimpleNotifiableState skips loaders/publishes on disposed projects. Tests added. check green once; intermittent flake so can't be proven absent. Possible upstream report: ExtensionPointImpl.addExtensionPointListener adds listener before Disposer.register.

title: Conflict gutter: tidy display of DIFF-style '-'/'+' prefixed lines
description:
Follow-up to jj-idea-82fo's per-side gutter icons/highlighting. A DIFF-style conflict block's
%%%%%%% section (ui.conflict-marker-style = "diff") renders its raw unified-diff lines verbatim,
literal leading '-'/'+' characters included (see ConflictMarkerFixtures.diffDestinationFirst,
e.g. "-base content" / "+destination content" inside the raw span JujutsuConflictGutterInstaller
already tints as one side's background). Unlike jj-idea-6ja9 (which folds the block's own
<<<<<<< / ||||||| / ======= / >>>>>>> marker lines into a divider), this is about the '-'/'+'
prefixed *content* lines inside that one diff section - distinct scope, no existing bead covers
it (confirmed via bd list search while answering a user question in jj-idea-sr42's session).

Candidate treatment, to validate against real jj diff-style output in runIde: strip the leading
'-'/'+' from each line for display (ConflictSide.lines already exists as the materialized,
stripped-of-marker-machinery content per side - check whether it already strips this prefix, or
whether contentStartOffset/contentEndOffset's raw span is what the gutter tint currently shows
verbatim) and color each line by add/remove (matching DiffColors.DIFF_DELETED/DIFF_INSERTED,
consistent with how side1/side2 already get colored) rather than leaving the raw diff-format
characters in the editor text-flow, which reads as noise once the block already has its own
side-colored background.

Needs a decision on whether this only affects *display* (a rendering trick - inlay/line-painter
that visually strips the prefix without touching the underlying document text, since the raw
text is the actual document content and any accept action still needs the real characters) or
whether jj-idea-82fo's replacementFor/JjConflictBlockParser's own side.lines extraction is
already doing this stripping correctly for the *accepted* result and this bead is purely about
the editor's own visual presentation before acceptance.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bug: bookmarks panel ahead/behind counts stale until a second refresh (GitHub #128)
description:
Reporter (SergejSalnikov), commenting on GitHub #128 (a different reporter's question about what the ↑n/↓m bookmark arrows mean — see CHANGELOG 'A local bookmark ahead of or behind its tracked remote now shows the same ↑n/↓m divergence indicator...' from #48/#110 for what they are). SergejSalnikov reports that after an operation that changes divergence (e.g. a push/fetch), the bookmarks panel's ↑n/↓m numbers only update after clicking Refresh twice — the first refresh doesn't pick up the new counts. Likely a caching/staleness bug in whatever computes tracking_ahead_count/tracking_behind_count (or the divergent-bookmark exact-count logic added for #110) not being invalidated on the first refresh pass.

Separately, the original reporter's question ('what do the arrows mean, can I disable them') suggests the feature could use better in-product discoverability (e.g. making sure the hover tooltip from #110 clearly explains a single-remote bookmark's arrows, not just the multi-remote case) — worth a look but is secondary to the staleness bug.

title: Warn before abandoning an empty change that has a bookmark on it (GitHub #129)
description:
Reporter (cYDN48): abandoning a non-empty change already prompts for confirmation. Abandoning an *empty* change that carries a bookmark silently deletes both the change and the bookmark with no confirmation.

Scenario: create a new (empty) change on top of a feature branch, advance the bookmark onto it, decide the change isn't needed, abandon it — the bookmark disappears along with the change with no warning, and has to be recreated.

title: Log graph: show indirect/elided edges when a filtered revset hides intermediate commits (GitHub #131)
description:
Reporter (SergejSalnikov): when the log revset excludes commits between two visible ones, `jj log` draws an indirect (dashed) edge and, by default, a synthetic `~ (elided revisions)` row (see `ui.log-synthetic-elided-nodes`). jj-idea draws neither — commits whose direct parents were filtered out appear disconnected.

Current behaviour per the report:
- CliExecutor.kt runs `jj log --no-graph` and the plugin builds its own graph from each commit's *direct* parents only.
- LayoutCalculator.kt (~lines 88-92) silently skips any parent not among the loaded entries — no edge, no marker.

Requested behaviour:
- For each visible commit, draw an edge to its nearest ancestor(s) within the revset, matching jj's GraphEdge rules: direct (parent visible, as now), indirect (nearest visible ancestor, dashed), missing (no visible ancestor, short stub or `~`).
- Drop transitive indirect edges, as jj does.
- Optionally show a synthetic "(elided revisions)" row/badge on indirect edges, following `ui.log-synthetic-elided-nodes"; must not be selectable as a commit.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/131
close_reason: Duplicate: jj-idea-hlu3 already covers this exact request (nearest-visible-ancestor remap + wiggly/dashed elided edges for filtered-out revisions), open since 2026-06-28. Folded GitHub #131 into hlu3 as an external ref/note instead.

title: Verify: binary file wholly included in a hunk-level split may be corrupted via text staging tree
description:
Known gap flagged in PR #127 (watbe): Split writes whole-file contents as text through DiffEditTool's staging tree, so a binary file fully included in a split could still be corrupted in the resulting commit, even after the byte-preserving diff-view fix lands.

Also noted in the same PR: MergeParentContentRevision reconstructs merge-parent content by reverse-applying a text diff, so binary diffs on merge commits still come through as text after that fix.

To do: confirm whether Split's existing whole-file fast path (see jj-idea-ygtw, MT-SPLIT 'Binary/conflicted files' — binary files currently get no Pick Hunks button, whole-file only) already avoids routing binary content through the text staging tree, or whether it needs to carry bytes explicitly. If it's a real gap, fix or file as its own tracked bug with a regression test using non-UTF8 content (e.g. a PNG signature, matching the fixture used in PR #127's tests).
design:
PLAN: characterise, then add a byte-safe "keep $right" path to the diff-edit staging protocol. (Companion to jj-idea-5g8h which touches the same call site; sequence 5g8h first or in the same PR - both edit SplitDialog's buildHunkSelection call.)

Step 0 - verify (the bead is a "Verify:" item): the mechanism that can corrupt binaries is concrete in code: `DiffEditTool.buildStagingTree` (diffedit/DiffEditTool.kt:~45) does `target.writeText(content)` for every non-null perFileContent value, and `buildHunkSelection` (ui/common/HunkSelectionModel.kt:80) feeds it `contentFor(change, included)`, which for Split is `previewController.cachedContents(path)?.after` - a String decoded from the file's bytes. Any file in `allChanges` that is NOT ticked (so its full change lands in the first commit) is written through that String path whenever `isPartialSplit` (at least one hunk-picked file) forces the hunk route (SplitDialog.kt:~610). A binary file (PNG) among those is decoded/re-encoded as UTF-8 => corrupted (invalid sequences become U+FFFD). Confirm with a contract test (real jj): repo with a PNG-signature file (bytes 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A + non-UTF8 bytes) and a text file; split with the text file hunk-picked and the binary unticked; compare bytes of the binary in the first commit (`jj file show`) with the original - expect mismatch today. Also test binary TICKED (restored from $left via Files.copy: byte-safe, expect pass) and binary-only splits (no hunk route: whole-file fileset path, expect pass, per jj-idea-ygtw). Squash's hunk route has the same shape (SquashIntoDialog.kt:558 buildHunkSelection -> same staging tree) - include a squash case.
Fix (if confirmed): never route a file through String content unless it is text.
1. Protocol: add a second manifest `.jj-idea-keep-right` (const next to DELETED_MANIFEST_NAME) listing repo-relative paths that must be left exactly as jj placed them in `$right` (i.e. take the full change into the first commit). In `HunkApplyMain.mirrorTree` (diffedit/HunkApplyMain.kt:49): paths in the keep-right manifest are excluded from all three loops (the "delete files in right not in staging/left" loop, the "restore from left" loop, and staging copy) - `$right` already holds the right bytes. Same pattern as the deleted manifest; backwards compatible (absent manifest = old behaviour).
2. `buildStagingTree(perFileContent, deletedPaths, keepRightPaths)` and `HunkSelection` gain `keepRightPaths`; `buildHunkSelection` classifies a change as binary (use `change.afterRevision`'s FileType.isBinary or `ByteBackedContentRevision` from PR #127 if landed - see jj-idea-yypr; before that, detect via `FileTypeManager.getFileTypeByFileName(path).isBinary || content contains NUL in first 8KB`) and for an "included in staging" binary file adds it to keepRightPaths instead of contentFor. Hunk overrides never exist for binary files (no Pick Hunks button), so the override branch is unaffected.
3. The same detection feeds the dialog: if a binary file's inclusion state is "lands in first commit", nothing else changes in the UI.
Decisions made without the user: Q: byte-level contents in the staging tree instead of a manifest? Rec: manifest - zero copying of large binaries, and `$right` already has them (scale-friendly: no 100MB temp copy). Reverse: change perFileContent to Map<String, ByteArray?> (bigger API change).
Merge-parent text-diff gap (second item in the bead) belongs to jj-idea-yypr's follow-up (MergeParentContentRevision) - record there; out of scope here.
Scale: classification is O(changed files) with a bounded 8KB sniff only when the file type is unknown; no per-commit loop. Operation-count test: 1k changed files -> staging tree builds with no String decode of binary entries (count contentFor calls == text files only).
Testing: unit - mirrorTree with keep-right manifest (binary bytes identical after, text unaffected, manifest not copied into right); buildHunkSelection classification table; contract tests above (byte-for-byte). Manual: MT-SPLIT ('Binary/conflicted files' row: add the mixed text-hunk + binary-unticked case), MT-SQUASH. Regression scope: MT-SPLIT, MT-SQUASH.
acceptance_criteria: Contract test proves binary bytes survive split/squash hunk routes (or documents it already does); keep-right manifest implemented if not; unit tests for mirrorTree/buildHunkSelection; MT-SPLIT/MT-SQUASH rows added.
notes:
Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/pull/127 (comment by watbe)
2026-10-02 investigation: CONFIRMED. Repro (real jj 0.44, contract-style): unticked binary file (PNG-like bytes 89 50 4E 47 .. FF FE 00 80) routed through DiffEditTool.withStagingTree as text -> first commit has EF BF BD (U+FFFD) replacement bytes, corrupted. Cause: unticked, never-previewed files are backfilled via CommandExecutor.show() stdout String (splitAction.executeSplitInteractive :136-146; same pattern in squashIntoAction ~:111-125) then written by buildStagingTree writeText. Simpler fix than planned: for any 'lands in staged side' file WITHOUT an override, content equals what jj already put in $right, so use a keep-right manifest (.jj-idea-keep-right; HunkApplyMain.mirrorTree skips those paths in all three loops) for ALL such files - no binary detection and it removes the per-file jj show backfill calls (an O(files) subprocess loop). Size: ~100 LOC (DiffEditTool, HunkApplyMain, HunkSelection+buildHunkSelection, Split/Squash callers+executors) + tests (mirrorTree unit, buildHunkSelection, binary-bytes contract test for split and squash). Est. 1-1.5h; touches the shared staging protocol so run MT-SPLIT/MT-SQUASH.

title: Conflict gutter: fold marker lines into a styled divider
description:
Follow-up to jj-idea-82fo's per-side gutter icons/highlighting (stage A/B). Collapse the raw
<<<<<<< / ||||||| / ======= / >>>>>>> marker lines into a compact, styled divider (e.g. a
colored horizontal rule) instead of showing them as plain text.

First use of folding in this codebase (grepped: no FoldingBuilder/FoldRegion/FoldingModel
use exists anywhere yet). Likely needs programmatic FoldRegions via FoldingModelEx, driven
directly by ConflictRegionScanner's block list - NOT a PSI/language-based FoldingBuilder,
since these are plain-text marker lines with no language of their own, embedded in an

title: Conflict gutter: mouseover highlight feedback on a side
description:
Follow-up to jj-idea-82fo's per-side gutter icons/highlighting (stage A/B). Add a mouseover
brighten/tint effect on a conflict block's side highlight as the cursor moves over it -
the first EditorMouseMotionListener use in this codebase (grepped: none exist anywhere yet).

Needs to hit-test the cursor position against ConflictRegionScanner's current block/side
ranges (from the A/B work) and must:
- stay cheap per mouse-move event (no re-scanning, no per-event allocation of note)
- never interfere with normal text editing/selection outside a conflict block
- coexist with the existing debounced rescan lifecycle in ConflictGutterController

See docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md and the jj-idea-82fo bead history for
the per-side offset-range model this depends on.
notes:
2026-09-29 Follow-up in the same session, before finish: added a rounded background highlight
behind the hovered side's gutter icon itself (user asked "is it possible to change the
background of the icon too?").

RangeHighlighter's TextAttributes background never reaches the gutter strip - confirmed by
reading EditorGutterComponentImpl's paint order (solid fill, then LineMarkerRenderers, then
icons on top; icon rendering never consults per-row TextAttributes). The platform's own diff
viewer (com.intellij.diff.util.DiffLineMarkerRenderer) paints custom gutter backgrounds via
exactly this route: cast Editor to EditorEx, read .gutterComponentEx, LineMarkerRendererEx with
Position.CUSTOM (the only position whose Rectangle covers the icon column - LEFT/RIGHT are the
free-painter strips flanking it), paint into iconAreaOffset/iconsAreaWidth. Confirmed
EditorGutterComponentEx.getIconAreaOffset/getIconsAreaWidth and EditorEx.getGutterComponentEx
are plain public API (not @ApiStatus.Internal) - only the concrete renderer classes using them
are marked internal, not the SPI surface itself.

Offered two visual options: same tint as the text side color, or a separate rounded "button
hover" highlight (JBUI.CurrentTheme.ActionButton.hoverBackground(), the same color IDE toolbar
buttons use on hover) distinct from the side tint, so the icon reads as *the clickable thing*.
User picked the rounded highlight.

Implementation: ConflictSideHover now adds a second, zero-length RangeHighlighter anchored at
the same offset the gutter icon itself sits at (side.contentStartOffset, matching
JujutsuConflictGutterInstaller's own offsetFor), carrying a new singleton object
ConflictIconHoverBackground : LineMarkerRendererEx in ConflictSideHover.kt. Cleared/swapped
together with the text highlighter on every side transition, mouseExited, and document edit -
no new state-machine complexity, just a second RangeHighlighter tracked alongside the first.

Tests: extended ConflictSideHoverTest (platformTest) with textHoverHighlighters()/
iconHoverHighlighters() helpers (distinguished by zero-length vs non-zero-length, both keyless)
- new/updated cases cover: icon highlighter appears at the icon's own offset with
ConflictIconHoverBackground as its lineMarkerRenderer, reused (not churned) across small moves,
cleared together with the text highlighter on marker-line/exit/edit, swapped together on a
side-to-side transition, and present for the gutter-row-event and DIFF-derived-base cases too.

./gradlew test platformTest ktlintCheck and compileKotlin -PplatformVersion=2025.1 all green.
docs/manual-tests.md MT-CONFLICT hover section updated to describe the icon's own rounded
highlight as a separate, distinctly-colored effect from the side-text tint.

Still not done: CHANGELOG entry, jj describe, bookmark set - held per CLAUDE.md until "finish".
Manual runIde click-through also still not personally verified (same reasoning as the prior
note - a real IDE instance from another workspace lane was already running).
close_reason: Added rounded hover highlight behind the gutter icon itself, on top of the side-text hover from the first pass. Automated checks green. Manual runIde verification and finish-sequence left for the user.

title: Multi-select accept-side label: detect same commits in swapped order
description:
Follow-up to jj-idea-wk7p's SideDisplayLabel work. Currently sideDisplayLabels is atomic
(both accept actions succeed or both fall back to generic "Side #1"/"Side #2" together) - see
its own doc comment. A user found a case worth handling better: selecting two files that name
the same two commits ("change A", "change B") but assign them to *opposite* CURRENT/LAST slots
(file 1's CURRENT is "change B", LAST is "change A"; file 2's CURRENT is "change A", LAST is
"change B") currently falls back to the generic wording for both, even though a human looking
at both files would recognize "this is the same pair, just reordered" and expect a coherent
swapped-pair label instead (either "change B"/"change A" or "change A"/"change B" - either
order is fine).

Implementing this requires computing both sides' labels jointly with awareness of each file's
own individual (current, last) resolution as an unordered pair, then checking whether every
selected file's pair matches (as a set) and is either identical to or an exact swap of a
reference file's order - a meaningfully larger and riskier heuristic than the current atomic
rule, deferred deliberately (see docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md and
jj/conflict/SideDisplayLabelTest.kt for the reported scenario and current behavior).
close_reason: Closed

title: Restore: add toolbar button to Working Copy window and use 'Restore…' ellipsis (GitHub #84)
description:
GitHub #84 follow-up (SergejSalnikov), after jj-idea-g2p8 shipped the dedicated Restore dialog in 0.8.17: (1) add a 'Restore' button directly to the Working Copy tool window toolbar, pre-checking whatever files are currently selected in the tree; (2) the action that triggers the dialog should end in '...' per platform convention, since it now opens a dialog rather than acting immediately.

Verified current state:
- UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.createChangesToolbar() (ui/workingcopy/UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt:168) builds the Changes tree toolbar (Refresh, Resolve all conflicts, tree expanders, Group by) but has no restore entry.
- Jujutsu.RestoreFile (actions/file/RestoreSelectionAction.kt) already reads the current tree/editor selection via e.restorePaths and now opens RestoreDialog through performRestore (ui/restore/performRestore.kt) - it can be added to the toolbar as-is, no new action needed.
- action.restore.selection='Restore' and action.restore.to.revision='Restore to This' (JujutsuBundle.properties:274,279) have no ellipsis despite both now opening RestoreDialog.
- RestoreSelectionAction's KDoc ('This is an immediate action with no popup') is stale since g2p8 wired it to the dialog - fix while touching this.

Scope: add Jujutsu.RestoreFile to the Working Copy changes toolbar; rename the two bundle keys to 'Restore…' / 'Restore to This…' (leave the *.undo keys as-is, they're undo-stack labels not menu text); fix the stale KDoc. UI-affecting: update docs/manual-tests.md and report manual smoke steps + MT-* regression scope.
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/84#issuecomment-5797709470
close_reason: Restore toolbar button added to Working Copy changes toolbar (with empty-selection fallback to the panel's bound repo); 'Restore…'/'Restore to This…' now carry the ellipsis; stale KDoc fixed. Tests + docs/manual-tests.md updated; ./gradlew check green.

title: 'Repository could not be read' balloon is misleading when jj merely timed out (GitHub #123)
description:
GitHub #123 (skycatminepokie): reporter saw the 'Jujutsu could not read the repository' balloon after IDE thrashing under system-wide resource pressure (see jj-idea-3ft0's diagnosis). The underlying error was: Error from jj log: jj log -r @ --no-graph -T change_id... timed out after 30 seconds That is CliExecutor.defaultTimeout (jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt:665) on the repository health probe (30s), not a broken/missing repo. But the balloon and the empty-workingcopy message both use the same wording, which names three specific causes, none of which is 'jj was slow': - notification.unreadable.content (JujutsuBundle.properties:850): "Jujutsu could not read the repository at ''{0}'', so its data will not be shown. It may be broken, moved, or created by an incompatible version of jj.
{1}" - workingcopy.empty.unreadable.message (JujutsuBundle.properties:763): same framing. Scope: give a timeout its own wording (e.g. "jj didn't respond within {0}s - the system may be busy" with a Retry action, distinct from the broken/moved/incompatible message), and reconsider whether a single 30s probe timeout should flip the repo into the 'unreadable' state at all versus just showing a transient warning and retrying.
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/123 (comment https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/123#issuecomment-5771013700 and follow-ups)
close_reason: Timeouts now classified as NotResponding (distinct wording, Retry only); last-known working copy kept

title: Resolve conflicts per-file from the Working copy window (GitHub #66)
description:
Reframed S3 (was jj-idea-qmws, a standalone Conflicts view with a revision picker). The actual requirement is
GitHub #66: a single place listing every conflicted file the user picks from and resolves as/when they like,
without a modal queue forcing an arbitrary order. The Working copy tool window's 'Merge Conflicts' node
(ui/common/JujutsuConflictsNode.kt) is already that list; it lacks per-file resolve gestures and jj's shape text.

Scope:
1. jj shape text per conflicted row (e.g. "2-sided conflict including 1 deletion") via a ChangeNodeDecorator
   reading JujutsuConflictRegistry, passed into JujutsuChangesTree.buildTreeModel's insertChanges call.
2. Double-click a conflicted row resolves just that file via the existing #63-safe resolveConflicts funnel
   (actions/change/workingCopyConflicts.kt), not the whole selection.
3. New "Accept Side #1"/"Accept Side #2" context-menu actions for selected conflicted files (multi-select ok),
   reusing JujutsuMergeProvider's per-file :ours/:theirs orientation logic, backgrounded via createCommand +
   invalidate(vfsChanged=true) like the editor banner's acceptSide.
4. Resolve-order test: multi-select "Resolve Conflicts..." must resolve in tree/selection display order.

Working-copy only (non-@ resolving is jj-idea-cmc3 / S4). See docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md
section S3 (needs updating to reflect this reframing) and GitHub #66.
close_reason: Shipped in zypzpntm; resolve-order now pinned by JujutsuConflictResolverTest + ResolveSelectedConflictsActionTest

title: TextTableCellRenderer leaks the previous row's toolTipText when a cell value is null
description: ColoredTableCellRenderer.clear() (called before customizeCellRenderer runs) resets fragments/icon but not toolTipText, so a row with a null value (e.g. a pending log entry's null author/date) silently kept showing the previous row's tooltip (UserCellRenderer's email, DateCellRenderer's absolute timestamp). Fixed alongside jj-idea-uyu9 by clearing toolTipText at the top of TextTableCellRenderer.customizeCellRenderer before dispatching to render().
close_reason: Fixed as part of jj-idea-uyu9: TextTableCellRenderer.kt now clears toolTipText before render() dispatch; regression test in TextTableCellRendererTooltipTest.kt.

title: [bug] Investigate: 30s health-probe timeout + IDE hang and RAM spike (GitHub #123, awaiting reporter)
description:
skycatminepokie (GitHub #123, 2026-09-20): IntelliJ occasionally hangs showing a progress bar the reporter read as 'fetching Jujutsu commits', eats a lot of RAM (possibly thrashing), and afterwards shows the 'Jujutsu could not read the repository' balloon with:

    Error from jj log: jj log -r @ --no-graph -T change_id... timed out after 30 seconds

Established so far (2026-09-20):
- The reporter's premise is wrong: there IS no auto-fetch. No match for autofetch|auto-fetch anywhere under src/main; the only fetch surfaces are the manual action (JujutsuBundle progress.git.fetch / action.git.fetch). The issue was opened off the back of kkkev's own auto-fetch promise on #90, which is still backlog-only.
- The 30s in the error is CliExecutor.defaultTimeout (jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt:665), i.e. the repository health probe - not fetch, which uses networkTimeout = 120s (CliExecutor.kt:666). So the timing-out command does no network I/O at all.
- Reporter follow-up: repo is on LOCAL DISK (not a network mount), and nothing else should be touching the repo concurrently - which rules out the two cheapest explanations. Cannot reproduce on demand yet.

BLOCKED ON REPORTER for: exact progress-bar text/screenshot, threadDumps-freeze-* from Help -> Collect Logs and Diagnostic Data, Help -> Activity Monitor per-plugin CPU, and whether it still happens with the plugin disabled.

Do not start work until that arrives - keep this open so the thread isn't dropped.
notes: Open question worth holding on to regardless of the outcome: if a bare 'jj log -r @' can take >30s on a local disk, defaultTimeout may be too tight as a hard constant for large repos, and the balloon's wording ('may be broken, moved, or created by an incompatible version of jj') is actively misleading for a timeout - it names three causes, none of which is 'jj was slow'. Both are worth separate beads if the reporter's data confirms a slow-but-healthy repo rather than a genuine hang.
close_reason: GitHub #123: logs show system-wide thrashing (loadavg 27/8 CPUs, heap-starved); EDT stuck in painting (HoledIcon.paintIcon, NiceOverlayUi.redrawMainComponent/XRender), plugin threads only waiting on jj subprocesses in OSProcessHandler.waitFor. Not a plugin hang.

title: Resolve at any revision: retire NEEDS_EDIT (S4 feature)
description: Real feature building on the jj-idea-cf2c spike (findings in docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md § S4 spike findings). Go-with-conditions verdict: build a log-shaped resolve flow (not an extension of MergeProvider2, which has no revision slot) using the ephemeral-merge-tool write-back mechanism proven in that spike (DiffEditTool.mergeToolConfigArgs + diffedit/MergeApplyMain.kt). Must include: (1) a warning when the resolved revision's descendants include @ - resolving rewrites @ underneath the user, silently updating the working-copy file; (2) after resolving a revision whose log row is on an already-loaded page 2+, call forceRefresh() (or patch the row in place) since invalidate()'s normal logRefresh path is a deliberate page-1-only reconcile (jj-idea-2c8k/GitHub #69) and will leave the row showing stale hasConflict=true otherwise. Retires actions/change/resolveConflictsAvailability.kt's NEEDS_EDIT state once shipped.
design:
PLAN: build the S4 feature exactly as recommended by the verdict "go, with conditions" in docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md § "S4 spike findings (jj-idea-cf2c)" (read that section first; it is the design input and is backed by contract tests ResolveAtRevisionContractCliTest / ResolveWriteBackContractCliTest against real jj 0.44).
Three deliverables (the bead's must-haves) plus the retirement:
1. LOG-SHAPED resolve flow (NOT an extension of MergeProvider2 - it has no revision slot; JujutsuConflictResolver writes bytes to disk which is meaningless off-@): a new dialog/editor `ResolveAtRevisionDialog` invoked from the log context menu "Resolve Conflicts..." for a non-working-copy row with `hasConflict`. Steps in the flow: (a) list conflicted paths via the existing `CommandExecutor.resolveList(revision)` (CommandExecutor.kt:371; `resolve --list -r REV`), (b) per path load the conflict sides read-only at that revision with the existing read primitive `vcs/diff/JujutsuConflictDiffRequestProvider.kt` (GitHub #119) + `jj file show -r` (materialised markers parsed by jj/conflict/JjMarkerConflictExtractor / ConflictExtractor, the same extractor the S1/S2 editor uses), (c) present a 3-way/result editor using the platform's merge viewer in a dialog (reuse what the existing resolve dialog builds from `MergeData`; the platform's `MergeRequest`/`TextMergeRequest` can be created standalone via `DiffRequestFactory.createMergeRequest(project, fileType, document, contents, title, titles, applyCallback)` - this does NOT need MergeProvider2), (d) on apply, write back via the ephemeral merge tool: stage resolved bytes in a temp file, `DiffEditTool.mergeToolConfigArgs(MERGE_TOOL_NAME, stagedFile)` (diffedit/DiffEditTool.kt:135) registered through `resolve(paths, tool, revision, configArgs)` (CommandExecutor.kt:385) = `jj resolve -r <rev> --tool jj-idea-merge-apply <path>`; one jj call per file (the merge tool is per-path-content), batch sequentially with ONE operation each; wrap the whole set in `createUndoTrackedCommand`/undo balloon (S5) - multiple files => multiple operations: group label "Resolve conflicts in <short id>" and offer undo of the last op only unless jj op log grouping exists (decision below).
2. WARNING when the resolved revision's descendants include @ (spike Q1): resolving rewrites @ underneath the user and silently updates the working-copy file. Compute cheaply from loaded log data: `@` is a descendant iff the selected entry's id is in the ancestor set of the working copy - from `LogEntry.parentIds` walk from @ within the loaded window (bounded O(window)); if the window doesn't contain the full chain use `jj log -r '<rev>::@' --limit 1`-style check (1 cheap call: `-r "<rev>::@"` count). Show a confirm dialog: "Resolving this change will rewrite N descendant changes including your working copy; files on disk will be updated." with [Resolve] [Cancel]; skip when @ isn't a descendant.
3. STALE ROW fix (spike Q2): after a non-@ resolve, the row on an already-loaded page 2+ would keep `hasConflict=true` because `invalidate()` -> `logRefresh` -> `refresh()` is a page-1-only reconcile (CommitTablePanel.kt:~672-683, UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:~343-349; jj-idea-2c8k/#69). Two options in the doc; Rec: call `dataLoader.forceRefresh()` ONLY when the resolved revision is outside page 1 (known from the loaded window position: `logTable` row index vs `pageSize`; or simply when `entry` is not among the first page's ids) - a one-off per resolve, not per write, so the 2c8k cost goal is untouched. Alternative (patch hasConflict in place) rejected for v1: needs descendant propagation too (descendants lose the inherited conflict as well - patching only one row leaves descendants stale; forceRefresh handles all). REQUIRED regression test (spike says none exists): contract/platform test with a deep page: write that clears a conflict on a page-2 row, assert row state updates after the post-resolve refresh (extend PagedLogWindowContractTest / jj-idea-hp6c's test, hp6c is a closed dependency).
4. Retire NEEDS_EDIT: delete the state from `ResolveAvailability` (actions/change/resolveConflictsAvailability.kt:~19-30: `NEEDS_EDIT`, `needsEditHint`) and make non-WC conflicted rows `ENABLED` (opening the new flow); the file-level action `ResolveSelectedConflictsAction` (resolveSelectedAvailability) for a historical context also routes to the new flow. Update bundle hint strings (needs-edit hint keys) and tests (`resolveAvailability` table tests).
Edge cases: immutable revision -> disabled with reason (jj refuses to rewrite immutable commits; ties to policy bead jj-idea-jamk); conflicts of kinds the merge tool can't express (binary, modify/delete, executable-bit): reuse the ":ours/:theirs" non-interactive tools for those (spike notes `:ours/:theirs` handle modify/delete by deleting) and offer only "Take ours / Take theirs" for them; revision with no remaining conflict after another process resolved it: re-check `resolveList` at open and on apply, show "already resolved".
Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Dialog vs editor tab? Rec: modal dialog v1 (platform merge viewer in a DialogWrapper) - simplest and the existing resolve flow is dialog-based. 
2. Q: Undo grouping for N files? Rec: one balloon per file is noisy -> after the final file show ONE balloon whose Undo reverts only the last op unless `jj op log` shows consecutive ops from our run: store the list of OperationIds from the batch and revert them newest-first ("Undo resolve of N files"); `performUndo` takes one id today - extend to a list. Reverse: single-op undo.
3. Q: forceRefresh vs patch-in-place? Rec forceRefresh (above).
Scale: one `resolve --list` + one jj call per file; forceRefresh = O(pages loaded) once per resolve (user-initiated, rare). Operation-count test: resolving k files = k resolve calls + 1 forceRefresh; non-page-1-only case none.
Testing: availability table updated; descendant-detection unit tests (linear, branch, merge, window-missing fallback); write-back contract tests already exist (extend with multi-file); dialog logic test with a stub executor; stale-row regression test; manual: MT-CONFLICT (new rows: resolve a conflict on an ancestor change from the log: warning appears when @ is a descendant; row's conflict marker clears on page 2+; undo works; immutable disabled). Regression scope: MT-CONFLICT, MT-CTXMENU, MT-LOG-REFRESH.
close_reason: Won't do: jj's standard workflow (edit the conflicted change, or new on it + resolve + squash) is already fully supported in the plugin; the NEEDS_EDIT hint points users there. A parallel log-shaped resolve flow isn't worth its cost.

title: Regression test: post-write log refresh doesn't restate an already-loaded deep page
description: Gap found during jj-idea-cf2c's S4 spike: PagedLogWindowContractTest.kt covers paging correctness (no missing/duplicate commits) but nothing pins CommitTablePanel.refresh()'s documented page-1-only splice behavior (jj-idea-2c8k/GitHub #69) against a content mutation on an already-loaded deeper page. Add a test that loads page 2+, mutates a row's state there (e.g. resolves a conflict), calls the cheap refresh() path, and asserts the deep-page row is still stale (pinning current behavior) vs. forceRefresh() picking it up (pinning the fix). Required before/alongside the S4 feature issue that depends on this distinction.
close_reason: PagedLogDeepPageRefreshTest pins refresh() page-1-only vs forceRefresh() deep-page restate

title: Generic background polling infrastructure for state that VFS/watchers can't reach
description: Shared, reusable polling mechanism (scheduled background check, debounced, cancellable) for state the platform can't push events for. First two consumers: (1) jj-idea-ul3o's op-heads fallback for repos where the native VFS watcher never delivers events (e.g. network-mounted filesystems) — poll each repo's op_heads/heads/ listing outside VFS and refresh only when the head id changes; (2) recurrent jj git fetch (periodic background fetch, separate from this poll's own scheduling but wants the same underlying primitive). Design once: interval config surface (settings field vs constant vs registry key), start/stop lifecycle tied to project/repo set changes, and a scale-test-friendly seam (injectable clock/executor) so per-repo poll cost is O(1) and testable without wall-clock timing.
design:
PLAN: a small project-level poller primitive, consumers plug in a "probe" and a "changed" callback.

Design inputs already decided by notes (GitHub #115): the probe must be a jj call (`jj op log -n1`), not a directory listing, because custom backends keep op state server-side. Each tick = one subprocess per polled repo => the cost model is "one cheap jj process per interval per repo", not O(1) filesystem reads.
API (new file jj/poll/Poller.kt, project-level service `JjPoller : Disposable`):
- `fun <T> register(key: Any, interval: () -> Duration, probe: suspend () -> T, onChange: (old: T, new: T) -> Unit): Handle` ; `Handle.cancel()`. A probe's value is compared with `==` to the previous result; the first result only primes (no onChange). Errors from probe: log at DEBUG once per distinct message, back off exponentially up to 10x interval (network flaps must not spam subprocesses), reset on success.
- Scheduling: coroutines on the project's `CoroutineScope` (service constructor-injected scope, cancelled at project dispose - fixes the lifecycle ask) with `delay(interval)`; NOT Alarm/ScheduledExecutor (cancellable, structured). Each tick runs the probe on `Dispatchers.IO`; `ensureActive()` before and after; at most ONE in-flight probe per key (skip a tick if the previous is still running - slow network must not stack processes). Pause when the IDE is inactive/frame not focused (`ApplicationActivationListener`) - polling a network repo while the user is away is waste; run one probe on re-activation (this alone also fixes most "external change while in terminal" staleness for everyone).
- Injectable seam: constructor takes `TimeSource`/`Clock` and `CoroutineDispatcher` (test uses `kotlinx.coroutines.test.TestScope` virtual time) so scale/ordering tests don't use wall clock (contributing.md scale-test guidance).
- Consumers: (1) ul3o: probe = `repo.commandExecutor.opLogHead()` (new tiny READ_ONLY `op log -n1 --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -T 'self.id().short(12)'` via the executor, no undo tracking), onChange = existing external-change refresh (`stateModel.invalidateRepositoryState()` + logRefresh, the same call the VFS op_heads listener makes - JujutsuStateModel.kt ~:600 watchOpHeads handler); (2) crik (periodic `jj git fetch`): its probe is the fetch itself with `onChange` ignored - it needs a different loop shape (action not observation); keep the primitive to "periodic task with result diffing" and let crik pass a probe that runs fetch and returns the new op id, so the same change detection drives the refresh.
- Interval config: Rec - project setting `pollIntervalSeconds: Int` (0 = off, default 0), exposed in Settings > Version Control > Jujutsu ("Poll for external changes every N seconds (0 = off; for network drives/custom backends)"), minimum 5s clamped. Rationale for a setting (not a constant): the reporter's op log latency over a network is unknown (waiting on p50/p99 from #115; note in this bead's notes once it arrives - if it is sub-second a constant 10s default may suffice; revisit then). Hold the DEFAULT decision on that data; implement the primitive + setting now.
Decisions made without the user: Q: default on or off? Rec off + one-time hint when the watcher looks dead (see ul3o). Q: pause when IDE inactive? Rec yes. Reverse: remove the activation listener.
Scale: per repo: 1 jj process per interval (>=5s => <=0.2 proc/s/repo); multi-root with 20 repos = 4 proc/s worst case - mitigate by staggering start offsets (hash(key) % interval) and a global concurrency cap of 2 in-flight probes. No filesystem traversal. Operation-count test (virtual time): 10 repos, 60s virtual, interval 10s => <= 60 probes; slow probe (30s) with interval 10s => no stacking (in-flight <= 1); paused when inactive => 0 probes.
Testing: unit tests with TestScope: priming, change detection, backoff, cancel, project dispose cancels children, one-in-flight. Manual: MT-LOG-REFRESH (set interval 5, run `jj new` in a terminal, log refreshes within ~5s with IDE focused; switch away - no jj processes spawned (check `ps`)), MT-SETTINGS (field). Regression scope: MT-LOG-REFRESH, MT-SETTINGS.
Related: jj-idea-ulg3 (repositoryStateAlarm -> MergingUpdateQueue) touches the same refresh funnel; do not couple, but the poller's onChange must go through the same debounced entry (`invalidateRepositoryState`) so a poll tick and a VFS event in the same moment coalesce.
acceptance_criteria: JjPoller service with injectable clock/dispatcher; one in-flight probe per key; backoff; paused when IDE inactive; project-dispose cancels; setting (default off) wired; virtual-time scale tests pass; MT-LOG-REFRESH/MT-SETTINGS rows added.
notes:
2026-09-20 - GitHub #115 upgraded this from hypothetical to a confirmed, named consumer with no alternative. Two design inputs that change the shape described above:

1. The poll CANNOT be 'poll each repo's op_heads/heads/ listing outside VFS' as consumer (1) is currently written. Sergej's repo has no op_heads/heads/ and no local file that moves on an external operation at all (see jj-idea-ul3o's 2026-09-20 note) - the backend keeps operation state server-side. The primitive must poll the current operation id through jj itself (jj op log -n1 or equivalent) and compare, not stat/list a directory. That makes each tick a subprocess, not a filesystem read, which materially changes the cost model and the 'O(1) per repo' scale claim.

2. Interval config surface (the open question in the description) is now decidable by data rather than by guess: kkkev has asked the reporter for p50/p99 of a bare 'jj op log -n1' on that repo. If it is hundreds of ms over the network, the interval must be a settings field rather than a constant. HOLD the interval decision until that number arrives on #115.

Priority note: kkkev told the reporter publicly on 2026-09-20 that this sits below wider-impact features and fixes, since it serves a custom setup. P2 is probably now generous relative to that statement - worth a deliberate decision rather than drift, especially as jj-idea-ul3o (P3) blocks on it and the other consumer (recurrent jj git fetch, GitHub #90) is itself unstarted backlog.
2026-09-20 - priority dropped P2 -> P3 per kkkev, resolving the tension noted above: this now matches what was said to the reporter on GitHub #115 (below wider-impact features and fixes, since it serves a custom setup) and sits level with jj-idea-ul3o, which blocks on it.

title: Bookmarks panel: dragging a conflicted bookmark treats one of its targets as a silent no-op
description:
BookmarkItem.id (CliLogService.bookmarkListTemplate, 'ids.firstOrNull()') collapses a conflicted/divergent bookmark's multiple added_targets to just the first one. jj-idea-0rdm wired the bookmarks-panel node as a drag payload/target keyed on that single id (JujutsuBookmarksPanelDnD.kt), so for a conflicted bookmark: dropping it on whichever target happens to be ids.first() hits resolveDropOperation's self-drop check (payload.id == target.id) and silently no-ops, while dropping it on the OTHER conflicted target goes through the normal move path and (after the existing backwards-or-sideways confirm prompt) succeeds. Net effect: one of the two legitimate conflict-resolving targets looks unreachable by drag.

The log table's own chips don't have this bug - they're per-row (LogEntry.bookmarks), so each conflicted target already gets its own chip with the correct id. This is panel-specific, introduced by jj-idea-0rdm.

Root fix likely needs RepositoryReferences/BookmarkItem to carry every target of a conflicted ref (not just ids.firstOrNull()), which also affects any other panel action keyed on BookmarkItem.id, not just DnD - worth a real design decision, not a one-line patch. Related but distinct from jj-idea-t7cz (same underlying awareness - a conflicted bookmark's own id shouldn't gate which of its targets is reachable - but t7cz is the MoveBookmarkToChangeDialog candidate-exclusion path, this is the drag-and-drop path).
close_reason: Fixed: RefItem/BookmarkItem/TagItem now carry every added_target (not just the first), DragPayload.BookmarkRef/TagRef carry the full target set, and resolveDropOperation's self-drop check only fires when the dropped-on row is the ref's sole target - so both targets of a conflicted bookmark/tag are reachable by drag from all three drag surfaces (log table chip, bookmarks panel node, commit details panel chip). MoveBookmark's tooltip reads 'Resolve...' instead of 'Move...' when the bookmark is conflicted. ./gradlew check green.

title: Bookmarks panel: New Change/Edit/Rebase disable for a bookmark outside the loaded log window
description: JujutsuBookmarksPanel.selectedLogEntries() (JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt) returns null whenever any selected bookmark/tag leaf's change isn't in the log table's currently-loaded window, silently dropping the log's own change actions (New Change/Edit/Rebase/Duplicate) from that row's context menu - discovered while planning dnd-batch-4 (jj-idea-0rdm), which deliberately did NOT fix this by hydrating a LogEntry per bookmark, since that would add a second O(bookmarks+tags) 'jj log' invocation (including the expensive hasPushedAncestor field) behind the 300ms-debounced JujutsuStateModel.references refresh on every VCS operation, widening the plugin's scale envelope. Decide on its own merits (a lighter template without hasPushedAncestor may be enough) and ship its own scale analysis/test per contributing.md if pursued.
design:
PLAN: let bookmark/tag rows resolve to a LogEntry even outside the loaded window, without a second O(bookmarks) heavy `jj log`.
Facts: ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:447 `selectedLogEntries()` resolves each selected leaf via `entryLookup(ChangeKey(repo, id))` (the log table's loaded window) and returns null if ANY leaf misses (`resolved.takeIf { it.size == leaves.size }`), so New Change/Edit/Rebase/Duplicate vanish from the context menu (publishes LOG_ENTRY/LOG_ENTRIES at :481-484 and addChangeActions :497 only when non-null). dnd-batch-4 (jj-idea-0rdm) rejected hydrating all bookmark targets eagerly (extra O(bookmarks+tags) `jj log` incl. the expensive hasPushedAncestor field behind the 300ms-debounced references refresh).
Design - hydrate lazily, only for the SELECTED leaves, only on demand:
1. In `selectedLogEntries()` split resolved vs missing; for missing leaves schedule ONE background fetch `jj log -r 'change_id(a) | change_id(b)'` (use the offset-qualified `ChangeId.full`; see wiz0 for hidden/divergent caveats - for bookmark targets that are hidden, fetch by commit id once wiz0 adds it) with the LIGHT template: reuse the log's field list minus `hasPushedAncestor`/immutable predicates (TemplateParts + CliLogService template builders ~:346-393; add `lightTemplate` variant gated by a parameter). Cost: O(#selected missing) - bounded by the selection, not by bookmark count; it runs once per selection change (cache by key in a small LRU of ~64 LogEntry, invalidated on `stateModel.references`/log refresh), never on the refresh path.
2. Threading: `uiDataSnapshot` (:~469) runs on BGT and must not block on jj: it publishes whatever is cached (resolved + hydrated), and the selection listener kicks the fetch on a pooled thread, then calls `ActivityTracker.getInstance().inc()` so the menu/toolbar re-evaluates. Context-menu build (actionGroupFor :506) reads the same cache; if hydration is still pending, add the change actions disabled with a tooltip "Loading..." - OR (simpler, Rec) show them only once resolved; the menu is rebuilt on each popup so a second right-click works.
3. The light-template LogEntry has `immutable`/`hasPushedAncestor` = false/unknown. Actions that use `immutable` (Edit/Rebase guards) would then wrongly allow acting on immutable commits -> jj rejects with its own error, but better to keep correctness: include `immutable` (it is a cheap revset-set membership `self.contained_in('immutable_heads()...')`? it IS part of the cost) - decision below.
Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Include `immutable` in the light template? Rec: yes include `immutable`, exclude `hasPushedAncestor` only - because Edit/Rebase enablement depends on immutability and a wrong enablement is user-visible; measure cost on the stress fixture (jj-idea-ro53 style) and drop if >2x the light template.
2. Q: Alternative of just disabling the actions with an explanatory tooltip for out-of-window bookmarks? Rec: no, hydration is cheap enough; keep fallback if measurement says otherwise.
3. Q: Interaction with paged loading (2570.4)? Rec: independent; paged just changes what "window" means.
Scale: one jj call per selection change with k = #selected out-of-window leaves; no per-bookmark loop on refresh. Operation-count test: refresh with 5k bookmarks issues 0 extra log calls; selecting 3 out-of-window bookmarks issues exactly 1.
Testing: panel test with stubbed entryLookup (miss) + stub log service: after hydration LOG_ENTRY/LOG_ENTRIES published; no calls on refresh; LRU invalidation. Manual: MT-BOOKMARK (right-click bookmark far back in history -> New Change/Edit/Rebase present); regression scope MT-BOOKMARK, MT-CTXMENU.
acceptance_criteria: Bookmark/tag rows outside the loaded log window still offer New Change/Edit/Rebase/Duplicate; hydration is selection-scoped (1 jj call), nothing added to the refresh path; scale test + panel test; MT-BOOKMARK row added.

title: Split dialog parallel mode: rename 'First'/'Second' to clearer terms
description:
SergejSalnikov (GitHub #114, 2026-09-13): "'First'/'Second' is bad wording in the context of split. I'd use something like 'new' and 'remaining'."

Raised while discussing jj-idea-ih1c's bookmark-placement preview for split; this is a distinct, smaller wording fix for the parallel split mode's own labels, independent of the bookmark-placement work. See jj-idea-ih1c for the fuller context (the reporter confirmed the same wording confusion, not a placement bug, applies to parallel mode).
