Reporter's 2026-09-13 comment predates the fix, which is still unreleased. Added a parallel-mode regression assertion that the positional wording cannot return.

title: .jj/repo/op_heads VFS watch may never fire, leaving auto-refresh dead on some setups
description:
SergejSalnikov (GitHub #115, 2026-09-13): confirms no external jj change (e.g. an out-of-IDE jj bookmark create) is ever picked up automatically - the toolbar Refresh button is their only way to see updated state. The op_heads/ directory they inspected holds only files that never change (repo_id, type, user); what actually changes on a working-copy update is .jj/working_copy/checkout.

This is the follow-up jj-idea-bbn3 anticipated asking about, now answered: the watch appears dead for this reporter, not just slow.

Two candidate causes worth checking, both cheap:
(a) IntelliJ's native VFS watcher not delivering events at all on this repo's network-mounted filesystem (reporter's repo lives on a remote drive per GitHub #113 - 50-100K files, millions in the whole tree).
(b) The watched path itself: JujutsuStateModel.kt:522-560,597 watches .jj/repo/op_heads recursively (OP_HEADS_RELATIVE_PATH = "/repo/op_heads"), but in a non-default jj workspace .jj/repo is a *file* (a pointer to the shared repo), not a directory, so the actual op_heads directory being written to lives elsewhere and this watch may be watching nothing. Also note the real head file lives under op_heads/heads/<op-id>, one level below the directory being watched.

Scope: diagnose which of (a)/(b) applies (or both), and add a lightweight polling fallback for refreshing repository state if the native watcher can't be trusted on network mounts - this is the more serious problem hinted at in jj-idea-bbn3's notes, now confirmed rather than hypothetical.
design:
PLAN: cause (b) is already fixed (jj-idea-xhnw closed: `jjRepoDirPath`/`resolveJjRepoDir` handles the pointer-file case in JujutsuStateModel.watchOpHeads, ~:560-600). Remaining scope = cause (a) for custom-backend/network repos, delivered ENTIRELY by consumer #1 of the poller (jj-idea-j2vl) - this bead is the consumer wiring + detection + user messaging. Blocked on j2vl.
Steps (after j2vl lands):
1. Probe: add `CommandExecutor.opLogHead(): CommandResult` (READ_ONLY, `jj op log -n1 --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -T 'self.id().short(12)'`; `--ignore-working-copy` is essential so the probe never snapshots or writes) in jj/CommandExecutor.kt + CliExecutor.kt next to the other READ_ONLY args builders (see `resolveListArgs` ~:387 for the pattern).
2. Wiring: in JujutsuStateModel (where `watchOpHeads(repos)` runs on `initialisedRepositories` change, ~:538), when polling is enabled, register one poller key per repo: probe above; onChange -> same funnel the VFS op_heads event uses (invalidateRepositoryState + logRefresh). Unregister on repo-set change (the existing `watchOpHeads` re-aim point). Keep the VFS watch too: both paths converge on the debounced refresh, so a double signal costs nothing.
3. Detect-and-suggest (the bead's "dead watcher" problem should not require reading docs): at watch setup, if `<jjRepoDir>/op_heads/heads` does not exist or is empty (the signature from #115: repo_id/type/user only; also directory mtime == epoch), log INFO "no local op head files; native watching can't see external operations" and show ONE project-level notification (JujutsuNotifications, dismissible, "don't show again") offering "Enable polling (every 10s)" which sets pollIntervalSeconds. Never auto-enable.
4. Document in docs (user-facing README/FAQ line): when auto-refresh doesn't pick up terminal changes, enable polling.
Decisions made without the user: Q: auto-enable polling when the signature matches? Rec: no - suggest only (a subprocess every N seconds against someone's network repo is a decision for them). Reverse: set default when signature detected.
Edge: reporter's `jj op log -n1` latency unknown (j2vl notes) - the notification text should state the interval is configurable.
Scale: unchanged by this bead beyond j2vl's counts; detection is one `exists()` + one `list()` of op_heads/heads at setup per repo (tiny directory).
Testing: unit - signature detection on temp dirs (normal layout, missing heads, empty heads); wiring test with a fake JjPoller verifying register/unregister on repo-set changes and that onChange triggers exactly one refresh; contract test for the probe (id changes after `jj new`, unchanged after a read-only command, no new operation created by the probe itself - assert op log length stable). Manual: MT-LOG-REFRESH (polling on, external `jj describe` shows up), MT-SETTINGS. Regression scope: MT-LOG-REFRESH, MT-SETTINGS.
acceptance_criteria: With polling enabled, an external jj operation in a repo whose VFS watch never fires refreshes the IDE within one interval; dead-watcher signature detected with a one-time suggest-to-enable notification; probe never writes (contract test); VFS path unchanged.
notes:
Diagnosis complete (2026-09-18), deferred rather than fixed this session:

(a) Native-VFS-watcher-dead-on-network-mounts: confirmed as the remaining scope of this bead, but it's workaround-only — the fix is a poll, and the user wants that designed once as shared infrastructure (there's also a recurrent jj git fetch use case), not a one-off Alarm here. Tracked as jj-idea-j2vl (this bead now blocks on it); priority dropped to P3 accordingly.

(b) .jj/repo being a file (not a directory) in secondary workspaces: confirmed with on-disk evidence and is fixable without any polling infra. Split out to its own bead, jj-idea-xhnw, so it isn't stuck behind the deferred poller.

No code/test/doc changes made for this bead itself this session.
2026-09-20 - GitHub #115: cause (a) is now RESOLVED as a diagnosis, and it is worse than 'watcher dead on a network mount'. Reporter's 'tree ../.jj -s -D' shows .jj/repo IS a directory (so this is not the jj-idea-xhnw workspace-indirection case), but:
  - no op_heads/heads/ at all - op_heads/ holds only repo_id, type, user
  - no operations/ or views/ under op_store/ - same three files
  - repo_id and user files that jj's own local op store does not write
  - every directory stamped Jan 1 1970

That is a custom backend holding operation state server-side, not a local simple_op_heads store. So there is NO local file that changes when an external operation lands: the watch cannot be repaired by changing the watched path, because there is nothing to watch. Any path-level fix is wasted effort for this reporter.

Consequence: for this setup the poll (jj-idea-j2vl) is not a fallback, it is the only mechanism. Note the poll ALSO cannot read op_heads/heads/ here as this bead's description proposes - it must poll the current operation id via jj itself (e.g. jj op log -n1), not by listing a directory.

kkkev told the reporter on 2026-09-20 that this stays below wider-impact work, given it is a custom setup. P3 remains correct.

title: Bookmark-state tooltips in the bookmarks panel
description:
cYDN48 (GitHub #110): tooltips on hover briefly explaining each bookmark state (ahead/behind, conflicted, tracked/untracked etc.) - good for newcomers to jj and this plugin, or infrequent users who forget what a conflicted bookmark's icon means.

Maintainer explicitly committed to this in the #110 thread and it's the one item from that discussion not delivered in 0.8.16 (icons/arrows for ahead-behind and conflict landed; tooltips didn't).
notes: As of jj-idea-ks5k/j58e/e4ln, this (bookmark-state tooltips) is the last undelivered item from GitHub #110's original thread.
close_reason: Implemented: hover tooltips for every bookmarks-panel row kind (local/remote/tag/folder/@-row/dangling head/repo group), wired via installIconAwareTooltip on the tree. New ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkNodeTooltip.kt + BookmarkNodeTooltipTest.kt (unit) + a JujutsuBookmarksPanelTest platform test for the hit-test seam.

title: Hide git pseudo-remote bookmarks in the log view (already hidden in panel)
description:
cYDN48 (GitHub #120): as of 0.8.16 the git folder is hidden in the bookmarks panel, so for the same reason it should also stop showing @git bookmark chips in the log view - they always mirror the local jj bookmark and add no information.

The panel already filters on GIT_PSEUDO_REMOTE (ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkTreeModel.kt:162,193; constant in jj/Revset.kt:107); the log's bookmark chips (ui/components/LogEntryText.kt / CliLogService's bookmark template) do not. Apply the same filter there.

The eventual escape hatch to show git bookmarks belongs with jj-idea-k5d7's settings gear / jj-idea-3sac's configurable-remotes epic, not a new setting of its own.
close_reason: Fixed via LogService.withDerivedDivergence (jj/BookmarkDivergence.kt): one shared derivation computed once per repo (JujutsuStateModel.references) feeds both the bookmarks panel and the log table's bookmark chips, so they always agree. Conflicted/divergent local bookmarks now get exact bidirectional counts via bounded revset queries instead of jj's one-directional tracking_ahead/behind_count hint (confirmed empirically against jj 0.44.0). A remote ref absent on the remote (jj-idea-j58e) is zeroed and excluded from derivation - no arrow, no number. The git pseudo-remote is now hidden from log chips too (jj-idea-e4ln), matching the panel. ./gradlew check green; contractTest/stubTest green against real jj.

title: Undo affordance after conflict resolution
description: Route the conflict banner's accept actions (jj-idea-n6fz S1 child), and per-block accepts once they trigger a snapshot (S2 child), through createUndoTrackedCommand - already used elsewhere for exactly this - and surface an 'Undo' action in the resulting success notification. Makes jj's own 'it's all in the op log, change your mind later' property visible at the moment a conflict is resolved, instead of requiring the user to separately know about Operation Log / jj undo. Depends on the banner shipping first (nothing to attach undo to otherwise). See docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md section S5.
close_reason: Closed

title: Demote the modal merge tool to a secondary action across all conflict entry points
description: Once the conflict banner (S1) and ideally the in-editor marker regions (S2) are live and proven, re-point the default action of every existing conflict-resolve entry point - editor banner, 'Merge Conflicts' tree-node link, Resolve All toolbar button, log context menu 'Resolve Conflicts...' - at the new editor-first flow, with 'Open Merge Tool' surviving everywhere as an explicit secondary action rather than the only option. Pure UI re-wiring, no new logic; JujutsuConflictResolver and the MergeProvider2/MergeSessionEx wiring in JujutsuMergeProvider are kept as-is throughout this whole epic, never removed. Ships last, deliberately, after S1/S2 are validated in real use. See docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md section S6.
close_reason: Editor-first default + explicit Open Merge Tool at all entry points

title: In-editor jj conflict marker regions: per-block gutter accept actions
description:
Recognize jj conflict marker blocks (all 3 styles - git, snapshot, diff, per jj/conflict/JjMarkerConflictExtractor.kt) as live editor regions via an incremental document scanner + RangeHighlighters, with per-block gutter actions: Accept side #1 / side #2 / both / base (base only where a ||||||| section exists). Each action edits the document text directly - replace the marker block with the chosen side's lines - no jj command, no modal; jj simplifies the conflict from the markers that remain on the next snapshot. This is the purest expression of the jj model and the first inlay/gutter-action UI in the codebase (no precedent - the only existing gutter-adjacent code is diffedit/HunkArrowDiffExtension.kt, diff-viewer only), so expect real prototyping time.

Scale rule (contributing.md Performance & Scale): rescan only the changed range after the first full pass, O(edit size) not O(file size); ship an operation-count test proving that. Depends on the banner (jj-idea-n6fz S1 child) only in that it shares the same document-scanning infrastructure - build once, use by both. See docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md section S2.
notes:
2026-09-28 User tried the colors + per-side icons in runIde: colors good, but reported the
single-click-to-accept felt surprising (destructive edit, no visual cue it's clickable). Walked
through options (A: post-accept undo balloon; B: more button-like icon; C: revert to
click-opens-menu; D: click opens a 1-item confirm popup; E: bring hover feedback forward). User
picked "B now, E next session" first, then on seeing it live said the checkmark icon read worse
than the original merge icon and asked to revert the icon and switch to D instead.
Final state: icon reverted to AllIcons.Vcs.Merge (checkmark tried and rejected - was briefly on
disk, now gone). Left-click now shows a small one-item confirmation popup ("Accept <label>") via
new ConflictAcceptConfirmAction (built directly with JBPopupFactory, since GutterIconRenderer's
own click-falls-back-to-popupMenuActions behavior is wired to the SAME menu right-click uses, so
it can't show a smaller menu on left-click while keeping the full 4-item menu on right-click).
Also cleaned up KDoc that had drifted into narrating the icon trial/reversion in the CODE
comments themselves (user flagged this: that history belongs here in bead notes / the commit
message, not baked into the code) - code comments now state only the current, durable design
rationale.
./gradlew test + platformTest + ktlintCheck all green. One transient ZipException failure from
running two concurrent gradle builds against the same cache - confirmed not a real regression on
a clean re-run. The full-suite-only LeakHunter flake noted earlier this session remains
unresolved, still not reproducible in isolation - still a follow-up, not blocking.
Next: user wants E (mouseover hover feedback, jj-idea-sr42) in a NEW session, not this one.
close_reason:
All 4 original stages (scanner, gutter icon, accept actions) plus a follow-up visual-UX round
(per-side offset ranges, background colors reusing DiffColors keys, per-side icons with a
left-click confirmation popup, right-click still offering the full menu) are done, tested, and
manually verified live by the user in runIde across several rounds of feedback. Hover feedback
(jj-idea-sr42) and folding the marker lines (jj-idea-6ja9) were split out as separate follow-up
beads under the epic - deliberately not part of this bead's own scope.

title: jj-native Conflicts view over resolve --list -r
description:
Non-modal, multi-file conflicts list built directly on CommandExecutor.resolveList(revision) / ConflictInfoParser, showing jj's own shape text per row (e.g. '2-sided conflict including 1 deletion') rather than reconstructing that from a platform-shaped Change list. Key differentiator from the platform's MultipleFileMergeDialog (which this replaces as the bulk affordance, alongside the existing 'Merge Conflicts' tree node for the working copy): a revision picker, so the view can show conflicts in descendants and arbitrary other revisions, not only @. CommandExecutor.kt:365's own doc comment on resolveList - 'infrastructure for the future Conflicts tool window' - anticipated exactly this.

Depends on the registry fix (populate JujutsuConflictRegistry for arbitrary revisions) landing first, and on the resolve-at-any-revision spike's recommendation, since bulk actions in this view are exactly the write-at-arbitrary-revision operation that spike validates. See docs/design/jj-idea-n6fz-native-conflict-ux.md section S3.

Scale note: listing conflicts for one revision is O(conflicts at that revision), already bounded by jj resolve --list -r - no new per-file/per-commit loop on the Kotlin side. Only add an operation-count test if the view ends up eagerly resolving shape for every row instead of lazily per visible row.
close_reason: Superseded by jj-idea-wk7p: the actual requirement (GitHub #66) is resolved inside the existing Working copy tool window's Merge Conflicts node, not a new standalone view. The revision picker/non-@ scope was unrequested design speculation; non-@ resolving is jj-idea-cmc3 (S4).

title: [perf] LaidOutCell.forRow does a full text/chip layout per visible row per repaint, no cache
description: Noted while fixing jj-idea-a0wp: JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.configureTextPanel (ui/log/JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.kt) calls LaidOutCell.forRow(...) fresh on every getTableCellRendererComponent call - full text/fragment layout plus cappedDecorations measuring chips via FontRenderContext, with no cache keyed on (entry, width, columnManager state). Bounded (O(visible rows) per repaint, not O(total rows) - unlike the a0wp bug), so left out of that fix, but still real allocation/measurement work repeated on every scroll tick and hover repaint for rows whose content hasn't changed. Candidate fix: cache the last LaidOutCell per row (invalidated on width/columnManager/entry change) the way GraphEdgeIndex now caches per graph update. Worth its own scale/perf pass - see LaidOutCellScaleTest.kt's CountingLinkifier pattern for how to measure it.
design:
PLAN: per-row cache of the laid-out cell, invalidated by a cheap key - measure first, ship only if measurable.

Facts: ui/log/LaidOutCell.kt:75 `forRow(entry, columnWidth, textStartX, columnManager, linkifier, fg, font, frc)` builds fragments (entryCanvas/linkifier) and `cappedDecorations` (chip measuring via FontRenderContext) on EVERY call; callers: JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.configureTextPanel (:223, per paint of each visible row incl. hover repaint) and JujutsuLogTable.kt:528 (tooltip/hit-testing path - it recomputes the same cell).
Step 0 - measure (acceptance gate): extend LaidOutCellScaleTest's CountingLinkifier pattern into a repaint benchmark: 60 visible rows x 100 repaints (scroll tick/hover) with 1k-row model; record forRow call count and ms. Only proceed if forRow cost is a non-trivial slice of the frame (>~2ms/repaint on the stress fixture); otherwise close as won't-fix with the numbers (bounded O(visible rows), per the bead).
Design: a small LRU cache (size ~ 2x visible rows, e.g. 256 entries) owned by the renderer (or the table, so JujutsuLogTable.kt:528 shares it): `LinkedHashMap(accessOrder=true)` EDT-only (renderers/paint are EDT; assert `EDT` in the accessor, no locking). Key = data class(entry identity: `entry` is a data class - value-equality hash of a whole LogEntry per paint is itself expensive and includes `repo`; use a cheap composite instead: `(entry.id.full, entry.commitId.full, rowVersion)`), columnWidth, textStartX, columnManager.layoutStamp (add an int that increments on show* toggle/column resize, columnManager state change), fg (selection colour: key on isSelected boolean rather than Color), font+frc identity (invalidate cache wholesale on UI scale/L&F change: LafManagerListener + the table's `updateUI`). Hover: forRow output is hover-independent (hover cues are applied afterward in configureTextPanel via `underlining(...)`), so hover repaints become pure cache hits - confirm in code.
Invalidation: clear on table model data change (model listener `tableChanged`), on column width change, on columnManager change, on font/theme change, on linkifier config change (issue-navigation settings). Risk = stale cells (wrong text after refresh) - mitigate with the commitId in the key (entries rewritten get new commitId) plus description text hash? Description edits change commitId in jj, so commitId suffices; the pending-entry path (LogEntry.pending, no real commit id) must key on its description hash - include `entry.pending` + description hashCode in key.
Decisions made without the user: Q: cache at all? Rec: only if step 0 shows cost; prefer this over per-column micro-optimisations. Reverse: delete the cache class; callers unchanged because forRow stays pure.
Scale: memory bounded (256 cells; each a few KB of fragments); O(1) per paint on hit; operation-count test: N repaints of unchanged rows => forRow runs <= visible rows once; width change => recompute.
Testing: LaidOutCellScaleTest extension (above); unit: invalidation cases (width, columnManager toggle, entry rewrite, theme). Manual: MT-LOG-TABLE (scroll smoothness, column resize, toggle columns, hover chips/links still correct, selection colouring), MT-LOG-REFRESH (rows update after write). Regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-REFRESH, MT-LOG-DETAILS (shared renderer).
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark shows cost before/after (or bead closed with numbers); if cached: repaint of unchanged rows makes no forRow calls, all invalidation triggers covered by tests, no stale text/colours in MT-LOG-TABLE.

title: [perf] mergeAndNotify re-lays-out the whole accumulated log on every refresh/loadMore
description: Noted while fixing jj-idea-a0wp: UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.mergeAndNotify() (ui/log/UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:310-320) calls topologicalSort(...) then graphBuilder.buildGraph(merged) over the FULL accumulated entry set on every merge - initial load, expand, whole-repo search, paged refresh, per-repo refresh, and loadMore() all funnel through it. Each of these is O(total loaded rows), not O(new rows), even though LayoutCalculatorImpl.calculate() itself is linear per call - the cost is re-running the whole linear pass from scratch every time one page is appended or a refresh ticks. Same shape as jj-idea-ix4v's topologicalSort concern (sits right beside this call in mergeAndNotify), and likely wants the same fix: skip re-sort/re-layout when the entry set hasn't actually changed, and/or an incremental LayoutCalculator entry point that extends a previous GraphLayout rather than recomputing it. Scale envelope: contributing.md ~100k commits in the log. Needs a scale test asserting buildGraph/topologicalSort's total operationCount across N sequential loadMore() calls stays O(total rows), not O(total rows * N).
notes:
2026-09-20 follow-up: manual testing surfaced two real bugs in the shipped implementation, both fixed same-session (still pre-push). (1) CommitGraphBuilder.buildGraph() never actually reseeded the incremental engine as the close-reason/doc-comments claimed - the first appendGraph() after any load treated its delta as the whole log, silently dropping every earlier row's GraphNode ('lose the graph for previous commits'). Fixed: buildGraph()'s unfiltered overload now does incrementalEngine.reset()+append() for real. (2) loadCommits() mutated graphBuilder/snapshot outside mergeLock (mergeLock.withLock only wrapped the snapshot write, not the buildGraph() call before it), so a loadMore()/refresh() firing while the initial load was still in flight could race on graphBuilder's now-stateful engines - harmless pre-jnqi (calculate() was fully local), corrupting post-jnqi. Fixed: widened mergeLock to cover both loadCommits() call sites. New regression tests: CommitGraphBuilderAppendTest (map completeness + equivalence across buildGraph/appendGraph sequences including a full-recompute-after-appends transition, plus a direct 'loaded parent never shows NOT_LOADED after append' check) and an extended LogMergeScaleTest assertion - both verified to fail without the fix by temporarily reverting it. ./gradlew check green (2084 tests).
2026-10-03 measurement: on r80k-git the append path is no longer cheap at depth - graph-layout per 500-row page 8 ms @500 rows, 390 ms @15k, 3.0 s @44k, 6.9 s @48k (see jj-idea-2570.7).
close_reason: Implemented the guarded append-only fast path: UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.mergeAndNotify(delta) now extends a cached MergedSnapshot instead of re-flattening every repo's logCache and re-sorting from scratch, gated by appendGuardHolds() (no expansion/search bucket in play, deletedNamesByRepo unchanged, no delta entry is a child of an already-merged entry, no delta entry newer than the snapshot's oldest entry - any failing falls back to the prior full recompute, never incorrect). Extracted LayoutCalculatorImpl's forward pass into IncrementalLayout, a resumable engine with checkpoint+rewind (every 256 rows) so a page resolving an earlier row's NOT_LOADED parent reprocesses only a bounded suffix, plus a retroactive parentLanes patch for the one-hop case where a reprocessed row's lane change invalidates an already-built earlier child's cached parentLanes. CommitGraphBuilder gained appendGraph()/resetIncremental() alongside the existing buildGraph() (which now transparently reseeds the incremental engine for the unfiltered case). loadMoreOneRepoLocked now returns the newly fetched page instead of a bare boolean, feeding mergeAndNotify's delta. New tests: IncrementalLayoutEquivalenceTest (8 cases incl. checkpoint-boundary rewind and the retroactive-patch wrinkle, brute-force pinned against calculate() on the full set), IncrementalLayoutScaleTest and LogMergeScaleTest (the bead's own ask: N sequential loadMore()-shaped appends stay O(total rows), not O(total rows * N) - caught a real guard bug in development, where the child-of-existing-row check compared the wrong key). ./gradlew check green (2081 tests, 0 failures). GitHub #69's fetch half was already fixed by jj-idea-2c8k; this is the remaining CPU half.

title: Bookmarks panel: per-remote divergence notation for a multi-remote bookmark
description:
Follow-up to jj-idea-we1n (GitHub #110). we1n's fix (Bookmark.withDivergenceFrom, jj/Revset.kt)
derives a local bookmark's ahead/behind from its tracked remote-tracking rows, but with more than
one tracked remote it collapses them into a single max(ahead)/max(behind) pair rather than
distinguishing per remote. The reporter (cYDN48, GitHub #110) suggested an expanded notation for
this case, e.g. for a bookmark tracking two remotes with different divergence per remote:

    master @origin1 (ahead 2) @origin2 (ahead 5)

This needs:
- A richer divergence representation than Bookmark.aheadCount/behindCount (probably a per-remote
  map) threaded through BookmarkTreeModel.BookmarkNode.Local and into the panel's rendering
  (JujutsuBookmarksPanel / LogEntryText.appendBookmarkChip).
- A decision on whether the log table's per-commit bookmark chips should show this too, or stay
  panel-only (today even the single-remote case is panel-only - see we1n's notes).
- Consideration of how this interacts with jj-idea-3sac's configurable-remotes epic, since both
  touch how multiple remotes are surfaced per bookmark.

Also out of scope for we1n and worth folding in here: the **log table**'s bookmark chips
(jj/cli/CliLogService.kt's localBookmarkTemplate) still show no local-bookmark divergence at all -
its `b.tracking_ahead_count()`/`b.tracking_behind_count()` calls error on a local ref the same way
bookmarkListTemplate's did before jj-idea-ita2's guard, and nothing analogous to
withDivergenceFrom has been wired in there. Whether that's worth fixing depends on whether the
per-remote notation above is meant to reach the log table too.
design:
PLAN: render per-remote divergence on the panel's local-bookmark leaf when a bookmark tracks more than one remote. The data already exists - no new model is needed.
Facts (verified): `BookmarkNode.Local(repo, item, displayName, onWorkingCopy, remotes: List<Bookmark>)` (ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkTreeModel.kt:174-180) already carries the tracked, non-git remote-tracking rows (`remotesByLocalName`, :281-287 filter `isRemote && remote != GIT_PSEUDO_REMOTE && tracked`), and after `LogService.withDerivedDivergence` (jj/BookmarkDivergence.kt, jj-idea-ks5k) each remote row's `aheadCount/behindCount` is already correct per remote (the conflicted-bookmark path writes exact per-remote counts back, :~75-95). The local bookmark's own `aheadCount/behindCount` is the max across remotes (`Bookmark.withDivergenceFrom`, jj/Revset.kt:129) - that collapse is what the reporter wants expanded. Rendering: `appendBookmarkChip(bookmark, label)` (ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:140-153) draws icon + label + `divergenceText(ahead, behind)` in DIVERGENT colour when `showBookmarkDivergence()` (qr78 toggle). The log TABLE already shows per-remote chips for groups (`append(group: BookmarkGroup)` :157-160 emits the local chip then one `@remote` chip per remote, each with its own counts) - so the notation "per remote" is already available in the log; the gap is the bookmarks PANEL leaf, which shows only the aggregate.
Design:
1. Panel leaf rendering (`BookmarkNodeRenderer`, JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:~590-700, `is BookmarkNode.Local` branch): when `node.remotes.count { it.aheadCount > 0 || it.behindCount > 0 } >= 2` OR (`node.remotes.size >= 2` and the counts differ between remotes), render the label followed by per-remote segments instead of the aggregate arrows: `master @origin1 ↑2 @origin2 ↑5` - each segment = grey `@<remote>` + `divergenceText(ahead, behind)` in DIVERGENT colour, wrapped `appendUnbreakable`; remotes with 0/0 are omitted from the list (only divergent ones listed; if none diverge nothing is shown - same as today). Single remote or identical counts keep today's compact aggregate arrow (a deliberate no-regression rule). Respect `showBookmarkDivergence()` (hidden -> keep just the dot/"needs attention" marker rules already in place).
2. Direction/semantics: the local bookmark's perspective (↑n = local is n ahead of that remote, ↓m = behind) - note that the remote row's own counts are the SWAP of the local's (BookmarkDivergence.kt comment: "the matching remote row gets the swap"), so per-remote segments must use `swap(remote.ahead, remote.behind)` to express the LOCAL's relation to that remote - unit-test this explicitly (easy to get backwards).
3. Tooltip (BookmarkNodeTooltip.kt, `is BookmarkNode.Local` :55): list each remote with a plain-language line ("origin: 2 commits ahead; upstream: 5 commits ahead") - there is already a remote in-sync / force-push block (:212-218); extend it to enumerate per remote.
4. Log table chips: unchanged (per-remote chips already exist via BookmarkGroup rendering); the bead's side note about `localBookmarkTemplate` erroring for local refs was superseded by ks5k's derivation (log chips for local bookmarks get panel-equivalent numbers through `enrichBookmarks`, UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt ~:787-803) - verify with the stress fixture that a multi-remote bookmark's chips agree with the panel segments; if they disagree, fix in the enrichment (not the renderer).
5. Interaction with jj-idea-3sac (configurable treatment of remotes, epic with a design): the per-remote notation is independent of how remote categories are displayed; keep the rendering in a small function `appendRemoteDivergence(node.remotes)` so the epic's "primary remote" idea (me4f) can later filter/prioritise.
Decisions made without the user: Q: only when >= 2 remotes diverge differently? Rec yes. Q: show remotes with 0/0? Rec no (noise). Q: show in log table too? Rec: already via chips.
Scale: O(#remotes of a bookmark) per painted leaf; no jj calls (data from state). Testing: renderer tests with Local nodes (1 remote diverged; 2 remotes same counts; 2 remotes different; one in sync; toggle off) asserting the rendered text segments (`FragmentRecordingCanvas` text); swap-direction unit test; tooltip text tests; manual: MT-BOOKMARK (fixture: bookmark tracking origin and a second remote, each at different distances: panel leaf shows both; tooltip lists both; toggling 'Show bookmark counts' hides numbers). Regression scope: MT-BOOKMARK, MT-LOG-TABLE (chips agree).
acceptance_criteria: Panel leaf for a bookmark tracking multiple remotes with differing divergence shows per-remote segments (local perspective, correct direction); single-remote/equal cases unchanged; tooltip enumerates remotes; tests + MT-BOOKMARK row.
notes: jj-idea-ks5k shipped the shared 'what are a local bookmark's ahead/behind counts' representation this bead's per-remote notation was waiting on (LogService.withDerivedDivergence, jj/BookmarkDivergence.kt) — exact counts per remote are now computed during the conflicted-bookmark path, so the per-remote notation can build on that instead of designing the representation from scratch.

title: Toolbar Refresh reloads log rows but not repository state (bookmarks/working copies)
description:
SergejSalnikov (GitHub #115): clicking the toolbar Refresh button doesn't pick up external
bookmark changes - closestBookmarks stays stale.

## Root cause
CommitTablePanel's RefreshAction.actionPerformed (ui/common/CommitTablePanel.kt:321-324) calls
dataLoader.refresh() -> UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.refresh() -> loadCommits() only
(ui/log/UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:221-224). It never touches
project.stateModel.references / .workingCopies / .closestBookmarks - those are refreshed only by
JujutsuStateModel.invalidateRepositoryState() (jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt:311).

Normally this isn't noticed because external jj operations are picked up automatically: the
plugin watches .jj/repo/op_heads via VFS (jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt:522-560), which jj rewrites on
every operation, and that triggers a full state refresh without the user doing anything.

## Why it matters for this reporter specifically
Reporter's repo lives on a remote/network drive (per their own comment on GitHub #113 - "Typical
project size is 50-100K files on remote drive"). IntelliJ's native VFS watcher commonly fails to
deliver events for network-mounted filesystems, so the op_heads-triggered auto-refresh path may
be silently dead for them - which would make manual Refresh their ONLY way to pick up external
changes, and explain why they reached for it in the first place.

## Fix (this bead)
Apply the reporter's suggested one-liner: call project.stateModel.invalidateRepositoryState()
from RefreshAction.actionPerformed alongside dataLoader.refresh().

## Open question / possible follow-up bead (NOT yet confirmed)
Asked the reporter (draft, unposted as of 2026-09-13): on their remote-drive repo, does an
external `jj bookmark create foo` in a terminal appear in the panel WITHOUT touching the IDE
(i.e. does the op_heads watch actually fire for them)? If the watcher is dead on network mounts,
that's a separate and more serious bug (auto-refresh entirely non-functional there) needing a
polling fallback - out of scope for this bead, which only fixes what Refresh itself does.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking toolbar Refresh re-syncs bookmarks/working-copy/closestBookmarks state, not just log rows. No regression to Refresh's existing cost profile (one state re-read per manual click, not a new poll loop).
notes:
Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/115. Watcher-on-network-drive question asked but unanswered as of 2026-09-13 - may spawn a follow-up bead depending on the answer.

2026-09-17 update: reporter answered (2026-09-13 comment, picked up in this triage pass) - no external jj change is ever picked up automatically for them; op_heads/ holds only files that never change; .jj/working_copy/checkout is what actually moves. So the op_heads watch does appear dead for this reporter, not just slow. Spawned jj-idea-ul3o to investigate root cause (native watcher on network mount vs. the watched path being wrong for a non-default jj workspace) and add a polling fallback. This bead's own one-line invalidateRepositoryState() fix for the Refresh button stays in scope and is now more clearly necessary, since manual Refresh is this reporter's only working path to fresh state.
close_reason: Fixed: RefreshAction now calls invalidateRepositoryState() alongside forceRefresh() via new manualRefresh(). Regression test added in CommitTablePanelRefreshPathTest. CHANGELOG + docs/manual-tests.md updated.

title: Custom revset as a log filter (GitHub #116)
description:
fan-tom (GitHub #116) wants to filter the graph by an arbitrary jj revset, not just the existing
reference/author/date chips.

## Design direction (from maintainer's draft reply, 2026-09-13)
A revset FILTER (constrains what's loaded/shown), persisted per log tab like the existing filter
chips, and INTERSECTED with any other active chips (author/date/reference) rather than replacing
them - matching how the existing chips already compose with each other. Reporter's example
(`parents(@, 10)`) reads as a filter, not a search.

This is distinct from the EXISTING revset machinery behind the search box
(logSearchRevset/searchWholeRepo, ui/log/UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:159-193): that's a search
OVERLAY that pulls additional matching commits into the loaded set from outside the current
window (e.g. a pasted hash or a description match in an old commit) - it doesn't constrain what's
shown, it adds to it. A revset FILTER needs the opposite: constrain the loaded/shown set, and
interact sanely with paged loading (see jj-idea-4kfh epic - paged log loading follow-ups).

## Requirements
- New filter chip alongside author/date/reference, same persistence-per-tab pattern.
- Intersects with other active filter chips (pending reporter confirmation this matches their
  expectation vs. wanting it to replace the others while active - asked in draft reply, unanswered
  as of 2026-09-13).
- An invalid revset must report jj's own error inline (e.g. next to the chip), never silently show
  an empty graph.
- Must be compatible with / not break paged loading (jj-idea-4kfh epic's per-page fetch machinery).
acceptance_criteria: A revset filter chip is available alongside author/date/reference; it constrains the loaded graph rather than only adding search hits; invalid revsets surface jj's own error message inline; behavior with paged loading is verified, not just the common small-repo case.
notes:
2026-09-29 (second manual-test round): even after the JujutsuConfigurable.apply()
missing-notify fix, a repo-level revset/limit config change still didn't update the log
window until an explicit Refresh, when paged log loading was on. Root cause #2:
UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.refresh()'s cheap per-write path (refreshOneRepoLocked)
unconditionally reused the existing PagedLogWindow, whose baseRevset/pageSize are fixed at
construction and never re-read from settings - only forceRefresh() (explicit Refresh)
built a fresh window from current settings. Fixed by comparing the window's
baseRevset/pageSize against settings.resolvedLogRevset(repo)/logChangeLimit(repo) on every
refresh() and, if stale, reseeding via loadFirstPageOrFallbackLocked (same cost as an
initial load: one getLogHeads + one page fetch) instead of splicing a fresh page 1 onto the
stale window. New test: PagedLogRevsetChangeTest (revset change, limit change, and a
must-not-reseed-when-nothing-changed/must-preserve-deeper-pages case).
close_reason: Shipped: Revset filter chip (client-side, ANDed with repo-level revset), plus two bugfixes found via manual testing (JujutsuConfigurable.apply() missing per-repo-override notify, and paged log loading's stale PagedLogWindow on refresh).

title: Surface "Open Jujutsu Log" in the VCS menu and VCS Operations popup
description:
Reporter closed the JJ log window (they run it as a separate window from the main editor) and
could not find a way to get it back short of Find Action.

## Current state
Jujutsu.OpenLogTab (META-INF/plugin.xml:232-236, class OpenJujutsuLogTabAction) already exists and
is keymap-assignable, but is deliberately added to no action group ("Not added to VcsGroup to
avoid StandardVcsGroup requirement" per its plugin.xml comment) - reachable only via Find Action
or a manually-bound shortcut.

The plugin already has the right homes available:
- Jujutsu.MainMenuGroup (plugin.xml:158-170), the "Jujutsu" submenu already anchored into
  VcsGlobalGroup alongside "Git".
- Vcs.Operations.Popup.NonVcsAware, which the plugin already adds to elsewhere (plugin.xml:139).

## Fix
Add a reference to Jujutsu.OpenLogTab in Jujutsu.MainMenuGroup, and to the VCS Operations popup.
Reporter suggested placement "second item, above Refresh VCS changes" in the popup - reasonable
starting point. Must ACTIVATE/FOCUS an existing log tab if one is already open (even if not
currently visible/docked), not just create a duplicate one every time it's invoked - confirm
current OpenJujutsuLogTabAction behavior here before wiring the new entry points.
acceptance_criteria: "Open Jujutsu Log" (or equivalent wording) is reachable from VCS -> Jujutsu submenu and from the VCS Operations popup, without needing Find Action or a bound shortcut. Invoking it when a log window/tab already exists focuses it rather than creating a duplicate.
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/118. UI-affecting - report manual smoke steps and update docs/manual-tests.md per contributing.md.
close_reason: Fixed: added menu/popup entry points and tool-window activation; ./gradlew check green

title: Add issue navigation to bookmark panel intermediate nodes
description: Often, bookmark names contain issue ids in their name before slashes, so these ids become intermediate nodes in the bookmark panel. These nodes should be subject to issue navigation.
design:
PLAN: apply the same IssueLinkifier to the prefix (folder) nodes in the Bookmarks panel so `PROJ-123/` segments are clickable issue links, mirroring how leaves already work.
Facts: leaves linkify via `appendLinkified` inside `BookmarkNodeRenderer` (ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:590-650: `FragmentRecordingCanvas(linkifier = IssueLinkifier(IssueNavigationConfiguration.getInstance(project)))`) and clicks resolve through `installLinkHandler`/`linkTargetAt` (:343-382: re-render the cell and `getFragmentTagAt(x - bounds.x) as? URI` -> `BrowserUtil.browse`). Prefix/category nodes render via the `is BookmarkNode.WithRefKind` branch (:~633: `canvas.colored(node.refKind.color) { smaller { append(node.displayName) } }`) - plain `append`, no linkification. `BookmarkNode.Prefix` carries `displayName` (the single path segment) and `fullPath` (accumulated `/`-path, BookmarkTreeModel.kt:146-160).
Design:
1. In the renderer, for `BookmarkNode.Prefix` use `appendLinkified(node.displayName)` instead of `append` (same canvas/linkifier; the `colored/smaller` wrappers stay). Categories ("Local", remote names, "Tags", repo names) must NOT be linkified (they're not user names) - restrict to `Prefix` (and its `WithRefKind` branch split: handle `is BookmarkNode.Prefix` before the generic `WithRefKind` branch).
2. Link target semantics: `displayName` alone is the segment (e.g. `JIRA-123`), which is exactly what the issue-navigation regexp matches; matching against the folder's own segment is right (the bead: "ids before slashes become intermediate nodes"). A segment that is only part of an id split by `/` (e.g. `JIRA/123`) won't match - acceptable.
3. Click handling: `linkTargetAt` already works for any node whose renderer tags fragments with URIs, so no change; but a folder click also toggles expansion/selection: clicking the link text opens the browser AND (default Swing) toggles/selects; same as leaves - keep consistent (BrowserUtil.browse happens in mouseClicked; selection change is harmless). Double-click expands folders: a double-click on a linked segment would browse twice? `mouseClicked` fires per click -> two browser opens on double-click! Check how leaves handle this (same handler => same issue for leaves already, where double-click triggers `invokeEnterBoundAction`); guard: ignore clicks with `e.clickCount > 1` for link opening (and for folders, let the double click expand). Add that guard and a test; it benefits leaves too.
4. Tooltip: folder tooltips (`bookmarkNodeTooltip`) show group identity/rollup; no change.
5. Hover cursor: `installLinkHandler.mouseMoved` already sets hand cursor when a link is under the pointer - works for folders once fragments carry tags.
Decisions made without the user: Q: linkify categories too? Rec no. Q: only when issue navigation is configured (IssueNavigationConfiguration has patterns)? Automatic - no patterns => no links.
Scale: renderer does one regex pass over a short string per painted prefix node (visible rows only) - same as leaves. No new data/jj calls.
Testing: renderer unit test (existing BookmarkNodeRenderer tests? find `JujutsuBookmarksPanel*Test`): a `Prefix(displayName="JIRA-123")` with a configured issue pattern yields a fragment tagged with the issue URI; category/repo nodes yield none; `linkTargetAt` returns the URI; double-click guard test. Manual: MT-BOOKMARK (configure Settings > Version Control > Issue Navigation `[A-Z]+-\d+`; bookmark `JIRA-123/fix-x` shows `JIRA-123` as a link in the folder; click opens browser once; double-click expands without opening twice). Regression scope: MT-BOOKMARK.
acceptance_criteria: Prefix nodes whose segment matches an issue-navigation pattern render as clickable links (hand cursor, single browser open); categories unaffected; tests + MT-BOOKMARK row.

title: Long-edge navigation: hover to preview, click to jump (and load) the other end
description: Any graph edge whose other endpoint's row is outside the current viewport has no way today to answer 'where does this go?'. This applies symmetrically: down to a distant/unloaded parent, up to a distant child. Hovering a long edge should thicken it along its visible span and show an arrowhead at the viewport boundary pointing toward the other end, plus a tooltip naming the target (or 'Parent not loaded yet - click to load' for an unloaded one). Clicking navigates via JujutsuLogTable.requestSelection(ChangeKey(repo, targetId)) - for an already-loaded target this selects and scrolls to it; for an unloaded parent the existing load-and-reveal path (requestSelection -> onSelectionExpansionNeeded -> loadExpanding -> merge -> scroll, since requestSelection sets pendingSelectionIsExplicit=true) already does the rest with no new code needed there.
design: Hit testing is lane-granular, not pixel-granular: map pointer x to a lane, then ask whether this row has an edge in that lane - avoids reproducing the sine-wave stub's paint geometry in a hit test (the JujutsuLogTableDnDChipTest experience showed geometry-mirroring assertions are fragile under CI font metrics), and keeps the hit test a pure, unit-testable function. The row->lane->edge index reuses JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.getRowPassthroughs's existing pass/cache, extended to record each lane's (childKey, parentKey). A HIDDEN (filtered) edge gets the tooltip but no click action - showing its target needs clearing the filter, which is jj-idea-hlu3's job. See docs/design/jj-idea-hlu3-xi58-elided-ancestor-rendering.md for full context, including the constraint (lane-leak risk) that rules out drawing an actual connector to a distant ancestor instead of navigating to it.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering a long edge (parent or child row outside the viewport) thickens it and shows a directional cue; clicking it selects and scrolls to the target, loading it first if not yet in the model; a HIDDEN (filtered-out) edge shows the cue but has no click action.
notes: Deferred out of this session (2026-09-10) despite the 'one session' plan: xi58+1pgy's LayoutCalculator/renderer changes ate the session's budget, and sc8m's hover/click mouse-interaction surface (lane-granular hit test, hover thickening+arrowhead spanning rows, tooltip, click-to-load-and-navigate) is real, separately-testable scope that deserved its own careful pass rather than a rushed integration into JujutsuLogTable's already-intricate mouse listener chain. Still fully unblocked - xi58/1pgy shipped the per-parent ParentState + stubLane data GraphNode/RowLayout now carry, which is exactly what the edge index (getRowPassthroughs-style pass) needs. Start next session directly on the design doc's § 'Long-edge navigation'.
close_reason: Shipped: pure GraphEdgeIndex (edge lookup, lane hit-test, hover classification) + JujutsuLogTable hover/click/double-click wiring + renderer thickening/arrowhead/tooltip. Folded getRowPassthroughs and graphTextStartX's duplicate passes into the shared index.

title: Split preview pane titles are wrong in parallel mode
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Split on a change, switch to parallel mode (produces 'First'/'Second' siblings rather than parent/child).
2. Tick a file to move between the two resulting commits.
3. Look at the preview pane titles/labels.

## Analysis
In parallel split, the two commits are labelled 'First'/'Second' (dialog.split.child.header.parallel, dialog.split.legend.first/second in JujutsuBundle.properties), but the diff preview still frames one side as the unchanged parent (dialog.split.hunks.parent.unchanged={0} (unchanged)), which is nonsense when neither side is a parent of the other - they're siblings.

Fix: retitle the preview panes per split mode (parent/child vs. parallel First/Second) instead of always using parent/child wording.
acceptance_criteria: Split dialog's preview pane titles make sense in both normal (parent/child) and parallel (First/Second) modes.
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/101 (SergejSalnikov's 2026-09-09 follow-up: 'the new diff view works fine with child/parent pairs, but mentally wrong when used with parallel'). Ask reporter for a screenshot to confirm exact labels seen.
close_reason: Fixed: preview refreshes live on parallel toggle; sibling wording no longer says 'unchanged'

title: Bookmark placement control/preview when splitting
description:
Reporter has repeatedly had a bookmark end up on the 'wrong' side of a split, with no warning or
way to control it.

Bookmarks pointing at the change being split silently follow jj's own rule (they stay on the
*second*/parent commit by default), so if the 'interesting' half of the split went into the first
commit, the bookmark appears to be on the wrong one.

## 2026-09-13 update: the rule is config-dependent, not fixed
The reporter traced their own experience of "bookmarks automatically advance to the child" to a
jj setting: `[split] legacy-bookmark-behavior = false`. This means the maintainer's original
"master will stay on the second commit" framing is only correct for jj's *default* config - with
legacy-bookmark-behavior explicitly set false (or true, depending on jj version defaults), the
outcome flips. A preview line must therefore state the actual outcome for the user's current jj
config (read via `jj config get split.legacy-bookmark-behavior` or equivalent), not a hardcoded
rule string.

Maintainer proposed splitting this into two beads/phases:
1. Preview only - show, for each affected bookmark, which resulting commit it will actually end
   up on, computed from the user's live config. (Higher priority - this alone fixes the "silent,
   confusing" complaint.)
2. Post-split bookmark move - let the user pick the other side and have the plugin perform the
   move automatically (reuse moveBookmarkAction.executeMove, already internal + undo-tracked; see
   jj-idea-ib1i/p35f shipped work). Lower priority, additive on top of (1).

## Proposed Fix
Phase 1: preview line(s) in the Split dialog computed from the live jj config, not a static
string. Phase 2: explicit per-bookmark choice + automatic move via executeMove.

Also applies to jj's parallel split mode (First/Second) - still unconfirmed whether the same
confusion shows up there; asked the reporter, no answer yet as of 2026-09-13.
design:
PLAN: Phase 1 only now (live-config-driven preview in the Split dialog); Phase 2 (post-split bookmark move) recorded as a follow-up bead recommendation. Phase 1 is "ready to design" per the 2026-09-17 note.
Verified jj behaviour (jj 0.44.0, probed with real repos): `jj config get split.legacy-bookmark-behavior` returns `true` by default even when unset (the key has a built-in default - `jj config get` succeeds; older versions may return "No matching config key"). With true (default): the ORIGINAL change id (the commit that keeps the description/id) keeps the bookmarks - in my probe the bookmark stayed on `[orig]` which was the second commit (remaining files); with `false`: bookmarks move to the FIRST (parent, selected-files) commit (`feat` landed on `[first]`). Which of the dialog's panes that is depends on the plugin's mode (SplitSpec KDoc, ui/split/SplitDialog.kt:55-65): default (child) mode = unticked pane keeps the original id; `insertBefore`/newParent mode = ticked files become a new commit inserted BELOW the original (original keeps id); parallel mode = siblings. => must be verified per mode against real jj (3 modes x 2 config values = 6 cells) in a contract test before trusting the mapping.
Design:
1. Config read: `CommandExecutor.configGet(key)` (CommandExecutor.kt:595, existing) wrapped in `SplitBookmarkPolicy.read(repo): LegacyBookmarkBehavior(enabled: Boolean?)` - null when unreadable (older jj without the key => treat as `true`, the historical behaviour; verify at MINIMUM 0.37 whether the key exists: if not, legacy behaviour is the only behaviour). Cache per dialog open (one call), run on a pooled thread when the dialog opens (dialog shows the line after load).
2. Pure function `bookmarkOutcome(bookmarks: List<Bookmark(local only)>, mode: SplitMode, legacy: Boolean): List<BookmarkPlacement(bookmark, side: FIRST|SECOND)>` + mapping `side -> the dialog's pane label` ("new commit"/"existing commit (ID)" wording per the reporter's preference noted 2026-09-17: prefer "new"/"remaining" wording; use the dialog's existing header names `dialog.split.stays.header` / `dialog.split.new.header.*`).
3. UI: below the description editors (or under the source note), an info line only when the source entry has local bookmarks: `Bookmark 'main' will end up on the new commit.` / `... on the existing commit (abc123).`; for several bookmarks group by side ("main, release stay on the existing commit"); tooltip/link "Why?" explaining `split.legacy-bookmark-behavior` and showing the effective value + "change in your jj config". Remote bookmarks (`main@origin`) are not moved by split (they stay at the old commit): mention only if the bookmark is tracked & would diverge? v1: ignore remote rows.
4. Phase 2 follow-up (create bead if wanted): a per-bookmark "after split, move to: [new|existing]" dropdown; after the split succeeds (undo-tracked op), call `moveBookmarkAction.executeMove` (`actions/bookmark/moveBookmarkAction.kt`, internal + undo-tracked per the bead) for bookmarks whose chosen side differs from the preview side - needs the post-split change ids (resolve via log: the new commit id = `jj log -r 'description(exact:"...")'`? fragile; better read the two resulting ids from the split command's output or from `jj op` diff - design when Phase 2 starts). Not part of this PR.
5. Parallel/First-Second wording (luxb) is a separate bead.
Decisions made without the user: Q: wording "new"/"remaining"? Rec: follow the dialog's existing header terminology ("new commit"/"existing commit") which matches the reporter's stated preference. Q: Phase 2 now? Rec no.
Scale: one `jj config get` per dialog open; O(#local bookmarks on the source) computing placement. Operation-count test: opening the dialog = exactly 1 config call.
Testing: `bookmarkOutcome` table tests (modes x legacy x bookmark counts); contract test for the 6 cells with real jj (asserting `jj log` bookmark location after split for each); dialog test with stub config returning true/false/error showing the right line; manual: MT-SPLIT (split a bookmarked change in each mode with the config default and with `split.legacy-bookmark-behavior=false` in repo config; preview matches the result; no bookmarks -> no line). Regression scope: MT-SPLIT, MT-BOOKMARK.
acceptance_criteria: Split dialog shows, per bookmarked source, which resulting commit keeps each bookmark based on the live split.legacy-bookmark-behavior value and the chosen mode; verified against real jj for all modes/config values; one config call; tests + MT-SPLIT rows. (Phase 2 tracked separately.)
notes:
Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/114. Maintainer proposed the phase 1/phase 2 split in a draft reply on 2026-09-13; reporter had not yet responded to confirm agreement or to the parallel-split-mode question (both from 2026-09-10/13) as of last check.

2026-09-17 update: reporter answered both open points in their 2026-09-13 comment (picked up in this triage pass). On parallel split mode: the confusion there is wording ("First"/"Second" reads badly for split), not placement - split into its own bead, jj-idea-luxb, since it's independent of this bead's bookmark-placement preview work. On the phase split: reporter implicitly accepted it by engaging with phase 1's design (preferring "new"/"remaining" wording) without objecting to deferring phase 2. Treat phase 1 (live-config-driven preview line) as ready to design/implement; phase 2 (post-split move) stays lower priority as originally proposed.

title: Mixed merge with one elided parent still renders without a stub
description: jj-idea-2c8k's wiggly-line elided-parent stub (JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.shouldDrawElidedStub) only fires when a row has no loaded parent at all. A row with two parents, one loaded and one elided, keeps rendering as it does today - the loaded parent already occupies the row's own lane, so the elided one needs a free-lane offset, not just 'draw somewhere in this row'. Orthogonal to finding the nearest ancestor (the filtering/paging scenarios); it's a layout question inside LayoutCalculator/textStartX instead.
design: See docs/design/jj-idea-2c8k-paged-log-loading.md's 'The paint treatment for an elided parent' section, and docs/design/jj-idea-hlu3-xi58-elided-ancestor-rendering.md scenario 3, for the full cross-bead context.
notes: Ships in the SAME session as jj-idea-xi58 (per-parent NOT_LOADED/HIDDEN state) and jj-idea-sc8m (long-edge navigation) - all three touch JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer/LayoutCalculator together. Once state is per-parent, shouldDrawElidedStub's 'no loaded parent at all' restriction is arbitrary; a mixed-merge row's stub needs its own free lane (LayoutCalculator's laneFor/reservation logic), scoped to that row only so no passthrough leaks to the rest of the graph. Full design: docs/design/jj-idea-hlu3-xi58-elided-ancestor-rendering.md. Entry point for the whole follow-up set: jj-idea-4kfh (epic).
close_reason: Shipped in the same change as xi58: LayoutCalculator now allocates a free stubLane (scoped to that row only, no passthrough/reservation) when a row has an unresolved parent AND a loaded parent, so a mixed merge draws its stub instead of silently rendering as fully-resolved. Renderer/textStartX updated to draw at and reserve room for stubLane.

title: Post-write refresh()'s page-1 splice can shift rows under a fixed viewport
description: jj-idea-2c8k fixed loadMore() jumping the viewport back to the selection on every page load (selectEntry(scrollIntoView=false) for a merely carried-over selection). refresh()'s page-1 splice (not loadMore()) can still shift row indices under a fixed viewport pixel position if a new commit appears at top - e.g. a post-write refresh while scrolled deep into history. Out of scope for jj-idea-2c8k since it wasn't the reported symptom (loadMore() only ever appends rows after everything currently loaded).
design: Needs a viewport-anchor mechanism: capture the top-visible row's ChangeKey + pixel offset before the update, restore by looking it up post-update. See docs/design/jj-idea-2c8k-paged-log-loading.md, bug 11, for the full context and the loadMore() fix this follows.
notes: Parent: jj-idea-2570 (Large-repository support).
close_reason: Shipped: JujutsuLogTable.setEntries() captures the top-visible row's ChangeKey + pixel offset before the model swap and restores the same pixel relationship after (ViewportAnchor.kt, pure; JujutsuLogTableModel.rowOf for O(1) post-update lookup, also replacing selectEntry's old linear scan). Explicit requestSelection navigation still wins over the anchor.

title: Paged log loader's per-repo lock has no automated concurrency coverage
description: jj-idea-2c8k's per-repo ReentrantLock (UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.lockFor) serializes refresh()/forceRefresh()/loadMore() against a shared PagedLogWindow, fixing a real ConcurrentModificationException found via manual runIde testing (rapid scroll events each spawning an independent background task). No automated test exercises this race - it would need either a platformTest or substantial mocking of JujutsuSettings/ApplicationManager to construct a real UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader, which the original fix's turnaround time didn't allow.
design: See docs/design/jj-idea-2c8k-paged-log-loading.md, bug 9, for the full incident writeup (including a round-3 false-alarm crash report traced to a stale runIde sandbox build, not a regression).
notes: Parent: jj-idea-2570 (Large-repository support).
close_reason: Added PagedLogLoaderConcurrencyTest (platformTest): fakes a chain repo's LogService with an in-flight fetch counter and proves refresh()/loadMore() never overlap on the same repo's PagedLogWindow, that two repos' locks are independent, that loadMore's tryLock skips rather than blocks, and that a fetch failure racing with a concurrent loadMore is handled cleanly. Verified the test actually catches a regression by temporarily removing the lock (3 of 4 tests failed) then reverting. No production code changed. ./gradlew check passes.

title: Inline per-hunk checkboxes in Split/Squash diff preview (GitHub #101 follow-up)
description:
GitHub #101's reporter posted a screenshot of the IDE's built-in commit dialog: checkboxes in
the diff gutter on each changed range, a select-all checkbox in the pane header, and a
tri-state checkbox on the file node. That's a different interaction model from Split's
existing "Pick Hunks..." — inline and always-visible vs. modal and behind a button — not a
discoverability gap on top of an equivalent feature.

## Do not adopt the platform's implementation
LocalTrackerDiffUtil, PartialLocalLineStatusTracker, LocalChangeListDiffRequest and
SimpleLocalChangeListDiffViewer (../intellij-community platform/vcs-impl) are all
@ApiStatus.Internal, and are built on LineStatusTracker — a local file vs. its VCS baseline
within a changelist. Split diffs an arbitrary change's parent->child, often not the working
copy, so there is no tracker to attach to. Do not depend on this internal stack.

## Supported route, reusing what we already have
- Source of truth stays ui/common/HunkSelectionModel.kt + buildHunkSelection; apply path
  stays util/GitDiffReverseApplier.kt. No new model.
- Register a DiffExtension (public EP com.intellij.diff.DiffExtension, platform/diff-api)
  whose onViewerCreated recognises our own requests via a Key set with
  DiffRequest.putUserData, and installs gutter highlighters on the SimpleDiffViewer's editor.
  Needed because ui/common/FileDiffPreviewPanel.kt renders through DiffRequestPanel, which
  does not expose its viewer.
- Checkbox renderer: small subclass of the PUBLIC DiffGutterRenderer (platform/diff-api), using
  AllIcons.Diff.GutterCheckBox / GutterCheckBoxSelected. The platform's own equivalent is
  LocalTrackerDiffUtil.kt:327-351 (createCheckboxToggle/CheckboxDiffGutterRenderer) — read as a
  model, don't call (internal).
- Click toggles the hunk in HunkSelectionModel and re-renders.
- Tri-state file node: per CHANGELOG, Split already renders a file half-checked after a partial
  pick via "Pick Hunks..." — confirm ui/common/FileSelectionPanel.kt / JujutsuChangesTree.kt
  already covers this before building anything new there.
- Optional follow-on: a select-all-in-file checkbox in the pane header (write our own small
  component; platform's ExcludeAllCheckboxPanel is internal).

## Open questions
- Whether "Pick Hunks..." stays as an advanced/three-pane affordance once inline checkboxes
  cover the common case, or is retired.
- Pane wording: the reporter's screenshot is the commit flow (working copy vs HEAD, "Current
  version"); Split's non-working-copy case needs different wording since there's no single
  "current version" concept.

Files: ui/common/FileDiffPreviewPanel.kt, ui/common/HunkSelectionModel.kt,
ui/common/HunkPickPreviewController.kt, ui/split/SplitDialog.kt, ui/squash/SquashFilePreview.kt,
ui/squash/SquashIntoDialog.kt.
design:
PLAN: the description already contains the right architecture decisions (public DiffExtension + public DiffGutterRenderer, reuse HunkSelectionModel/buildHunkSelection/GitDiffReverseApplier, do NOT adopt the platform's internal LocalTracker stack). This adds an implementable step order, answers its open questions with recommendations, and the test/manual plan.
Precedent verified in code: `diffedit/HunkArrowDiffExtension.kt` is a registered `diff.DiffExtension` (plugin.xml:124) that no-ops unless `HUNK_PICKER_SESSION` is in the `DiffContext`, uses `DiffGutterOperation` + `DiffGutterRenderer` subclasses (`ArrowGutterRenderer`, `ArrowInstaller`) and `DiffViewerListener` for reinstall on rediff - build the checkbox gutter the same way, in the same package style. `ui/common/FileDiffPreviewPanel.kt:32-47` renders via `DiffManager.createRequestPanel(project, parent, null)` (a `DiffRequestPanel` that hides its viewer), which is why a DiffExtension keyed on a request user-data Key is needed.
Steps:
1. Shared helper first (the cross-ref with jj-idea-82fo): extract `ui/gutter/ClickableGutter.kt` from HunkArrowDiffExtension's arrow plumbing: `ClickableGutterRenderer(icon, tooltip, onClick)` (public `DiffGutterRenderer` subclass) + an installer that (re)installs `DiffGutterOperation.Simple` entries per change, disposing/reinstalling on `onAfterRediff`. Migrate HunkArrowDiffExtension onto it in the SAME PR (behaviour-preserving; its existing tests must pass). If 82fo lands first, reuse its helper instead.
2. `HunkCheckboxDiffExtension : DiffExtension` registered in plugin.xml next to the arrow one; no-op unless the request carries `HUNK_CHECKBOX_SESSION` (a Key set by `FileDiffPreviewPanel`/the Split & Squash preview controllers via `DiffRequest.putUserData`, value = a small interface `HunkInclusionSource { fun isIncluded(hunk): Boolean; fun toggle(hunk) }` backed by `HunkSelectionModel`). For each `SimpleDiffViewer` change (`viewer.diffChanges`, each = a line range pair) install a checkbox renderer on the SIDE that represents the child/"selected to move" content (left or right editor depending on Split mode: for default split, ticked = moves to the NEW child commit; see SplitSpec KDoc ui/split/SplitDialog.kt:55-65 and `HunkPickerLabels.kt` for the side wording). Icons: `AllIcons.Diff.GutterCheckBox` / `GutterCheckBoxSelected` (public AllIcons, per the description) with a `GutterCheckBoxIndeterminate`? (verify exists) for mixed.
3. Click -> `source.toggle(hunk)` -> HunkSelectionModel updates -> `HunkPickPreviewController` re-renders the preview (the existing pipeline that "Pick Hunks..." feeds: `ui/common/HunkPickPreviewController.kt`: `cachedContents`, `refresh(fp)` :112) and the file tree's tri-state (below). Hunk identity: map a diff change to the model's hunk by index in the ORIGINAL diff (stable across toggles since the preview diff is always computed vs the unmodified base; verify: after a toggle the preview content changes - the right side shows "base + included hunks" - so rediff changes the change list! Use the earlier-planned strategy: always diff `before` vs `after` (full change) and render the checkbox state as gutter icons on THOSE changes; show the resulting content only in the footer/other pane to avoid hunk renumbering. Decision below.)
4. Tri-state file node: verify `ui/common/FileSelectionPanel.kt`/`JujutsuChangesTree.kt` partial-inclusion rendering exists (CHANGELOG says half-checked after "Pick Hunks...": `partialChanges` field in JujutsuChangesTree.kt ~:100 `getNodeStatus` returns DONT_CARE for partial); wire inline toggles into the same `partialChanges` set.
5. Header select-all checkbox (optional follow-on): small own component above the diff (`FileDiffPreviewPanel.header` area :33-40) toggling all hunks of the current file.
6. Squash Into: same treatment where the preview exists (`ui/squash/SquashFilePreview.kt`, `SquashIntoDialog.kt` uses `HunkSelectionModel` via `destinationOverrides`): wire the same extension with the Squash semantics (ticked = moves into destination).
Open questions - recommendations:
 Q1: keep "Pick Hunks..." once inline checkboxes exist? Rec: keep as the advanced three-pane affordance for now (it supports line-level edits of the eventual parent; checkboxes only toggle whole hunks); revisit after user feedback; both write the same model so they stay consistent (checkbox state must reflect picker results and vice versa: after the picker applies, `HunkSelectionModel` changes -> checkboxes refresh via the model listener).
 Q2: wording for the non-working-copy case? Rec: pane titles "Before" / "Change (tick hunks to move)" consistent with HunkPickerLabels; do not use "Current version".
 Q3: platform internal stack? No (description).
Scale: O(#hunks in the previewed file) per render (a diff is computed anyway); no loops over files beyond the selected one. Operation-count: toggling a hunk re-renders ONE file preview and updates one tree node.
Testing: model-level unit tests (toggle updates HunkSelectionModel; picker<->checkbox consistency; tri-state derived values), `ClickableGutter` tests using a headless `SimpleDiffViewer` via `DiffManager`/test fixtures (platform tests exist for the arrow extension? look under src/test/.../diffedit), extension no-op test for foreign requests (no session key => zero highlighters); manual: MT-SPLIT/MT-SQUASH (inline checkboxes toggle hunks, file node tri-state, picker consistency, undo of selections not needed), light/dark/zoom. Regression scope: MT-SPLIT, MT-SQUASH, MT-DIFF-PREVIEW (shared preview panel), MT-DIFF (DiffExtension fires for all viewers - verify no behaviour change/perf hit in ordinary diffs).
acceptance_criteria: Split (and Squash Into) diff previews show per-hunk gutter checkboxes backed by HunkSelectionModel with tri-state file nodes, no modal needed; shared ClickableGutter helper extracted with HunkArrowDiffExtension migrated; no-op for foreign diffs; tests + MT rows.
notes:
Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/101 (screenshot 2026-09-05, https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f37f6e2b-3c41-456b-a855-eedc88d2eda0).
2026-09-23 cross-ref jj-idea-82fo (in-editor conflict marker regions with per-block gutter accept actions, conflict epic jj-idea-n6fz S2): no functional overlap (different model/apply path), but both need the same clickable-gutter plumbing — DiffGutterRenderer subclass with click callback via DiffGutterOperation.Simple, disposed and reinstalled on change (s5yx: onAfterRediff; 82fo: DebouncedDocumentScan). Precedent: diffedit/HunkArrowDiffExtension.kt (ArrowGutterRenderer, ArrowInstaller). Whichever lands second should extract a shared helper (e.g. ui/gutter/ClickableGutter.kt) and migrate HunkArrowDiffExtension onto it. No dependency between the two.
