title: Style change id in describe dialog
design:
PLAN (bead has no description - inferred from its title and the code): style the change id shown in the Describe dialog like change ids everywhere else in the plugin (bold unique prefix + grey remainder), instead of plain text.
Facts: the Describe dialog is `DescribeDialog` (ui/describe/DescribeDialog.kt:20-59), opened via `Project.requestDescription(prefix, initial, vararg params)` (actions/Inputs.kt:13) with `label = JujutsuBundle.message("$prefix.message", *params)`; for a log-row describe the label is `dialog.describe.input.message = "Enter description for change {0}:"` with `{0}` = `describePromptId(target)` = `target.id.short` (actions/change/describeAction.kt:30) - plain text in a `label(label)` JBLabel (DescribeDialog.kt:40). Elsewhere ids are rendered via `TextCanvas.append(ChangeId)` (bold shortest prefix + grey remainder, used by `createSourcePanel`, log rows, tooltips: `append(entry.id)` in ui/common/DialogHelpers.kt:44-52).
Design:
1. Give `requestDescription` an optional structured label: `requestDescription(prefix, initial, changeId: ChangeId? = null, vararg params)`; when `changeId != null`, DescribeDialog builds its header with an `IconAwareHtmlPane` (or the DSL's `text()` with HTML) using `htmlString { append(JujutsuBundle.message("$prefix.message.prefix")); append(changeId); append(":") }`... but sentence structure/localisation: keep ONE bundle message with a placeholder and split around it: `val (before, after) = message.split("{0}")` at runtime is fragile; instead add two keys `dialog.describe.input.prefix=Enter description for change ` / `...suffix=:` (translators get two fragments - acceptable for such a short string) OR render the whole message through `MessageFormat` with a sentinel token then replace the token by styled fragments. Rec: sentinel approach `JujutsuBundle.message(key, "\u0000ID\u0000")` then `split`, so the single translatable message stays intact.
2. Where else: `DescribeWorkingCopyAction` (actions/change/DescribeWorkingCopyAction.kt:36, label "Enter description for working copy (@):" - could show the id too), NewChange dialog header `dialog.newchange.input` (WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt:443 - no id), so only the log-row describe has an id today; implement the general `changeId` parameter and pass it from `describeAction`/`DescribeChangeAction`/`DescribeWorkingCopyAction` (working-copy id shown too, the id is useful there as well).
3. `describePromptId(target)` becomes redundant for the label (keep for any caller/test; or return the ChangeId).
4. Accessibility: `labelFor` association (DescribeDialog.kt:41 `it.component.labelFor = editor.focusTarget`) - an HTML pane isn't a JLabel; keep a hidden/accessible name via `AccessibleContext` (`pane.accessibleContext.accessibleName = plain label text`) and set the dialog's focus order unchanged (focus goes to the editor already via getPreferredFocusedComponent).
Decisions made without the user: Q: interpretation (style the id in the dialog label)? Rec yes - tell me if the bead meant something else (e.g. the description box's own styling). Q: also show the first line of the current description in the label? No.
Scale: none. Testing: DescribeDialog test (platform, existing DescriptionEditorEnabledTest style): the header contains the styled id fragments (assert `htmlString` output includes the shortest-prefix bold span) and plain-text fallback when no id; message split test for the sentinel (en bundle); manual: MT-CTXMENU (Describe from log row / toolbar: id looks like in the log (bold prefix + grey rest); Describe working copy; dark/light). Regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-WORKINGCOPY.
acceptance_criteria: Describe dialog header renders the change id with the standard styled id (bold unique prefix, grey remainder); accessible name preserved; tests + MT-CTXMENU row.

title: Bookmarks panel: configurable treatment of remotes (GitHub #48)
description:
## Summary
GitHub #48 (comment 2026-09-04T17:56) asked to collapse "git"/"origin" by default in the
bookmarks panel (colocated repos otherwise show every bookmark three times) and make
unsynced/diverged bookmarks more visible. The maintainer flagged that not everyone has a
primary "origin", and some setups have several remotes, so this needed design before
building — jj-idea-d65h was filed as a timeboxed spike to answer that before any of this
epic's children were built. jj-idea-d65h is closed; its recommendation is recorded below and
drives the children of this epic.

## Children
- jj-idea-ita2 (bug, P2) — bookmarkListTemplate omits tracked/ahead/behind (blocks jj-idea-a7a7)
- jj-idea-j0zv (feature, P3) — hide the reserved `git` pseudo-remote
- jj-idea-a7a7 (feature, P3) — collapse remotes by default + persist expansion + roll-up
- jj-idea-me4f (task, P4, backlog) — parked: is there a defensible "primary remote"?

jj-idea-k5d7 (bookmarks panel settings gear, pre-existing, not a child of this epic) was
separately extended with a "show git remote" toggle as jj-idea-j0zv's escape hatch.
design:
# Spike findings (jj-idea-d65h)

## Existing infrastructure surveyed

**Tree model**: `BookmarkNode` (`ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkTreeModel.kt:33-78`) is a sealed
interface — `WorkingCopy`, `RepoGroup`, `Category` (one per kind: "Local", one per remote name,
"Tags"), `Prefix` (`/`-grouping), and leaves `Local`/`Remote`/`Tag`. `buildRepoNodes`
(`BookmarkTreeModel.kt:108-152`) derives remote categories purely from bookmark names —
`remote()`/`isRemote` on `BookmarkName` (`jj/Revset.kt:29-35`) split on `@` — with no
`jj git remote list` involved and no ordering concept beyond alphabetical.

**Panel**: `JujutsuBookmarksPanel` (`ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt`) is a plain `Tree`
rebuilt from scratch on every state-model invalidation (`rebuild()`, lines 95-106), ending in an
unconditional `TreeUtil.expandAll(tree)` (line 105) — any user collapse is wiped by the next
rebuild. `bookmarks.panel.expandall`/`collapseall` bundle keys already exist
(`JujutsuBundle.properties:129-130`) but are referenced from no Kotlin. Category/Prefix nodes get
no context menu (`actionGroupFor` returns `null` for them, line 224) and render as a folder icon
+ plain name (`BookmarkNodeRenderer`, line 270) — no counts, no badges.

**Bookmark data model**: `Bookmark` (`jj/Revset.kt:41-72`) carries `tracked`, `deleted`,
`conflict`, `aheadCount`, `behindCount`, and derives `isDiverged = aheadCount > 0 && behindCount >
0` (line 71). `appendBookmarkChip` (`ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:129-141`) already renders
`↑n↓m` from those counts, reused by the panel's leaf renderer.

**Two separate bookmark templates** in `jj/cli/CliLogService.kt` populate this model differently:

- `localBookmarkTemplate`/`remoteBookmarkTemplate` (lines 324-343, feeding `jj log`, i.e.
  `LogEntry.bookmarks`) capture all five fields: name, `tracked()`, `conflict()`,
  `tracking_ahead_count().lower()`, `tracking_behind_count().lower()`.
- `bookmarkListTemplate` (lines 463-486, feeding `jj bookmark list --all-remotes`, i.e.
  `getBookmarks()` → `stateModel.references` → the bookmarks panel) captures only `present`,
  name, `conflict`, change id, `immutable`, and constructs `Bookmark(name, conflict = conflict)` —
  leaving `tracked` defaulted to `true` and both counts at `0`.

**Remote enumeration**: `jj git remote list` is parsed once per repo into
`JujutsuRepository.gitRemotes`/`cachedGitRemotes` (`jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt:215-232`,
`jj/JujutsuRepository.kt:90-102`); `cachedGitRemotes` is explicitly non-blocking and can be empty
when cold.

**jj config access**: `jj/cli/Config.kt`'s `Key` enum has only `USER_NAME`/`USER_EMAIL`. Nothing
in the plugin reads `git.push` or `git.fetch` today; adding a key is a one-line addition to the
enum plus `Config.get()`/`resolve()`, already generic.

**Settings pattern**: project state lives in `JujutsuSettingsState` (flat `var`s), per-log-window
state in `LogWindowConfig` (already holds `bookmarksPanelVisible`), written back via
`JujutsuSettings.upsertLogWindow`. UI is Kotlin UI DSL `checkBox(...).bindSelected(...)` in
`JujutsuConfigurable.createPanel()`.

## Finding 1 — `git` is not a remote

```
$ jj git remote add git https://example.com/x
Error: Git remote named 'git' is reserved for local Git repository

$ jj git remote list          # in this colocated repo
github  git@github.com:kkkev/jj-idea.git
origin  git@gitlab.home.marigoldfeathers.com:kevin/jj-idea.git
```

`@git` nonetheless appears against nearly every bookmark in `jj bookmark list --all-remotes`,
because it is jj's view of the colocated repo's own Git refs — a local mirror, not a peer of
`github`/`origin`. Suppressing it needs no heuristic, no configuration, and no notion of a
primary remote: it is a name jj reserves, and the plugin can special-case it on that basis alone.
Recommend keying on the literal name `"git"`, not "absent from `cachedGitRemotes`" —
`cachedGitRemotes` is deliberately non-blocking and returns empty when cold, which would
transiently hide *every* remote category rather than just the pseudo-remote. See jj-idea-j0zv.

## Finding 2 — real remotes have no defensible primary, and none is needed

For `github` vs `origin` in this repo there is no honest winner. jj offers three weak signals —
`git.push` (a single remote; unset here), `git.fetch` (defaults to the glob "origin"; also unset
here), and the built-in `trunk()` alias's origin-then-upstream preference order — and the plugin
reads none of them today.

The reporter's complaint is vertical noise, fixed by collapsing, not ranking. Collapsed-by-default
remote categories with persisted expansion state solve it completely with no primary-remote
concept: the user expands what they care about, and it sticks. The expansion state itself is the
explicit user setting the maintainer asked for, earned by a gesture rather than a Settings page.
Decision: the primary-remote question is parked, not answered — see jj-idea-me4f.

## Finding 3 — blocking bug: `bookmarkListTemplate` drops tracked/ahead/behind

Not anticipated by the issue, but blocks the visibility half of the ask regardless of any design
choice above. Because `bookmarkListTemplate` never queries `tracked()`,
`tracking_ahead_count()`, or `tracking_behind_count()`, every `Bookmark` reaching the panel has
`tracked = true` and `aheadCount = behindCount = 0` regardless of reality:

- every remote bookmark renders with the tracked icon (`bookmarkIcon`,
  `ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:116-121`), whether or not it's actually tracked;
- no bookmark in the panel ever shows `↑n↓m`;
- `toggleTrackBookmarkAction` (`actions/bookmark/toggleTrackBookmarkAction.kt:10`) branches on
  `bookmark.tracked` and so always offers Untrack, even for a genuinely untracked remote bookmark
  — a functional bug, not just a display gap.

`bookmarkListArgs` already passes `--all-remotes`, so untracked remotes are present in the data;
only the template under-reads them. See jj-idea-ita2.

## Finding 4 — collapsing and visibility are one feature, and the coupling runs backwards

The `↑n↓m` indicators live on leaves; collapsing a remote category hides its leaves; so shipping
collapse without a roll-up would make the reporter's second ask *worse*, not neutral. The roll-up
is what keeps collapse honest, not an enhancement bundled alongside it.

Once Finding 3 is fixed, the roll-up is pure derivation over
`Bookmark.tracked`/`.conflict`/`.deleted`/`.aheadCount`/`.behindCount`/`.isDiverged`, all already
in memory — no new `jj` invocation, folds into the existing `buildBookmarkTree`/`buildPrefixTree`
walk, O(B) over bookmarks already loaded for the toolbar widget and reference filter, O(1) in
commits and working-tree files. `BookmarkTreeModelTest` is the natural home for an
operation-count assertion. See jj-idea-a7a7 (collapse + roll-up ship together, not split).

## Mechanics the children will need

- Persistence: expansion state belongs in `LogWindowConfig`, alongside `bookmarksPanelVisible`,
  written back via `JujutsuSettings.upsertLogWindow`. `rebuild()`'s unconditional
  `TreeUtil.expandAll(tree)` (`JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:105`) needs to become per-node.
- Unused bundle keys `bookmarks.panel.expandall`/`collapseall` should be wired to real actions.
- `actionGroupFor` returning `null` for `Category`/`Prefix` (line 224) is a clean, currently
  unused hook for future per-remote actions.
- Roll-up badge belongs in `BookmarkNodeRenderer`'s `WithRefKind` branch (line 270), reusing
  `JujutsuColors.DIVERGENT` to match leaf styling.

## Recommendation

1. Hide the `git` pseudo-remote unconditionally — no config, no primary-remote reasoning.
2. Do not attempt to rank real remotes. Collapse by default, persist per-window expansion state.
3. Fix `bookmarkListTemplate` first — standalone bug, prerequisite for visibility work.
4. Ship collapsing and the roll-up together as one feature.
5. Park the primary-remote question as backlog; nothing else depends on resolving it.

title: Collapse remote categories by default, persist expansion state, and roll unsynced/diverged counts up onto collapsed nodes
description:
## Summary
From jj-idea-d65h's spike (jj-idea-3sac's design field, Findings 2 & 4),
GitHub #48: the bookmarks panel currently unconditionally expand-alls on every rebuild
(JujutsuBookmarksPanel.rebuild(), line 105 -> TreeUtil.expandAll(tree)), so a colocated/
multi-remote repo shows every bookmark repeated once per remote category, all fully expanded,
with no way to collapse that sticks.

The spike concluded there is no defensible "primary" remote among real remotes (github vs origin
here, neither privileged by jj.git.push/git.fetch) — see jj-idea-h4wp, filed separately and NOT a
dependency of this issue. Noise is fixed by collapsing + persisting user choice, not by ranking
remotes.

Collapsing alone would make GitHub #48's second ask (unsynced/diverged visibility) *worse*: the
`up n down m` divergence indicators (appendBookmarkChip, ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:129-141)
live on leaf nodes, so collapsing a remote category hides exactly what the reporter wants
surfaced. So this issue ships collapse and a roll-up badge together as one behavior, not two.

## Design decisions
- Remote Category nodes default to collapsed; Local and Tags default to expanded (current
  behavior unchanged there).
- Persist per-node expansion state in LogWindowConfig (settings/LogWindowConfig.kt), alongside
  the existing bookmarksPanelVisible field, written back via JujutsuSettings.upsertLogWindow.
  JujutsuBookmarksPanel.rebuild() needs to apply saved expansion per-node instead of
  unconditional TreeUtil.expandAll.
- Wire the existing unused bundle keys bookmarks.panel.expandall/collapseall
  (JujutsuBundle.properties:129-130) to real toolbar/menu actions rather than adding new ones.
- Roll-up badge: derive from Bookmark.tracked/.conflict/.deleted/.aheadCount/.behindCount/
  .isDiverged (jj/Revset.kt) already loaded into BookmarkNode.Category/Prefix's children — no new
  jj invocation. Render in BookmarkNodeRenderer's WithRefKind branch
  (JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:270), reusing JujutsuColors.DIVERGENT for consistency with leaf chips.

## Scale
O(B) over bookmarks already loaded for the toolbar widget/reference filter (folds into the
existing buildBookmarkTree/buildPrefixTree walk); O(1) in commits and working-tree files. Add an
operation-count assertion to BookmarkTreeModelTest.

## Files to read/change
- src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkTreeModel.kt
- src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt (rebuild(), renderer)
- src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/settings/LogWindowConfig.kt
- src/main/resources/messages/JujutsuBundle.properties (bookmarks.panel.expandall/collapseall)
- Tests: BookmarkTreeModelTest, JujutsuBookmarksPanelTest

## Manual regression scope
UI-affecting change once implemented — report exact manual smoke steps and MT-* section IDs per
contributing.md at that time; not applicable to this filing.
design: Collapse+roll-up ship together; do not split. See jj-idea-d65h design doc Finding 4 for why.
acceptance_criteria: A repo with 2+ real remotes shows remote categories collapsed by default; collapsing/expanding one persists across panel rebuilds and IDE restarts within the same log window. A collapsed remote category with an unsynced or diverged bookmark inside it shows a roll-up indicator; expanding it reveals the per-bookmark indicator matching today's leaf rendering.
close_reason: Shipped: bookmarkListTemplate tracked/ahead/behind fix, git pseudo-remote hidden, remote categories collapse by default with persisted expansion and roll-up badges (GitHub #48).

title: Hide the reserved git pseudo-remote category in the bookmarks panel
description:
## Summary
From jj-idea-d65h's spike (jj-idea-3sac's design field, Finding 1),
GitHub #48 (comment 2026-09-04T17:56): in a colocated repo, `jj bookmark list --all-remotes`
reports a `@git` remote ref for nearly every bookmark, alongside the repo's real remotes (e.g.
`@github`, `@origin`). This is not a peer remote — `jj git remote add git ...` fails with
"Git remote named 'git' is reserved for local Git repository", and `jj git remote list` never
lists it. It's jj's own view of the colocated repo's local Git refs, and today it makes every
bookmark in the panel appear three times (Local, @git, @origin/etc) instead of two.

Unlike real multi-remote setups (see jj-idea-h4wp, parked separately), this needs no heuristic
and no user setting — `git` is a name jj itself reserves, so it can be special-cased
unconditionally.

## Design decision
Key on the literal remote name `"git"` (BookmarkName.remote == "git"), not on absence from
`repo.cachedGitRemotes` — cachedGitRemotes is deliberately non-blocking and can be empty when
cold, which would transiently hide every remote category rather than just this one. The `jj git
remote list` behavior is the *justification* for special-casing "git", not the runtime test.

## Files to read/change
- src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkTreeModel.kt (buildRepoNodes,
  ~lines 134-140: filter the remote-names list to exclude "git" before building Category nodes)
- Test: BookmarkTreeModelTest

## Escape hatch
jj-idea-k5d7 (bookmarks panel settings gear) has been extended to include a "Show the git remote"
toggle, so this isn't a hard, unconfigurable hide forever — just the default.
design: Filter by literal remote name 'git', not by cachedGitRemotes absence (see rationale in description).
acceptance_criteria: In a colocated repo, the bookmarks panel's remote categories never include a 'git' category by default. A bookmark tracked only by @git and a real remote still appears correctly under the real remote's category.
close_reason: Shipped: bookmarkListTemplate tracked/ahead/behind fix, git pseudo-remote hidden, remote categories collapse by default with persisted expansion and roll-up badges (GitHub #48).

title: Spike: bookmark x working-copy combination actions, and whether custom actions/workflows are the right shape (GitHub #48 spike 2/2)
description:
## Summary
Timeboxed investigation, not shipped UI. From GitHub #48 (comment 2026-09-04T17:56): reporter requested "Merge with current change" and "Rebase current change onto" actions on bookmarks. Maintainer flagged that actions combining bookmarks and working copies risk a combinatorial explosion of menu entries, and that this overlaps with another user's request (GitHub #68, context-menu extensibility) for user-defined custom actions grouped into shareable "workflows".

## Question to answer
Do we enumerate a small fixed set of bookmark x working-copy actions, or is this the point at which user-defined actions/workflows earn their place? If the latter, is it one piece of work with #68 or two separable ones?

## Deliverable
A written recommendation, plus follow-up issues (either a small fixed action set, or scoped work toward #68's custom-actions/workflows concept). This spike does not implement anything itself.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/48 (comment 2026-09-04T17:56:14Z), relates to GitHub #68
design:
# jj-idea-tohr — Spike: bookmark × working-copy actions vs. custom workflows

## Context

GitHub #48's reporter asked for two bookmark-panel actions that combine a bookmark with the
working copy: **"Merge with current change"** and **"Rebase current change onto"**. The
maintainer's reply flagged two worries and deferred:

> I'm not yet sure about actions that involve bookmarks and working copies... that will need a
> bit more thought to avoid a combinatorial explosion. This is starting to stray into
> customisable workflow territory. Another user has suggested custom actions, and I wonder if we
> actually need a way to make custom actions like this and group them into "workflows".

`jj-idea-tohr` is the timeboxed spike that answers that. It ships **no UI** — the deliverable is
a written recommendation plus follow-up issues, with the relationship to GitHub #68
(context-menu extensibility, `jj-idea-66id`) stated explicitly.

This is the last remaining substantive #48 item apart from `jj-idea-lig7` (dangling heads) and
`jj-idea-me4f` (parked, P4). It fits one session because it is prose + `bd create`, and because
most of the evidence it needs already landed in this repo.

## The answer the spike should reach (to be verified, not assumed)

The combinatorial worry has largely **already been dissolved** by work that shipped after the
#48 comment was written. Two mechanisms did it:

1. **Parameterised dialogs, not enumerated menu entries.** `jj-idea-p35f` wired the log's own
   change actions into the panel's context menus
   (`ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:404-411`, `addChangeActions`). Those actions are
   dialog-driven, and both dialog specs already take **lists of `Revision`**:
   - `NewChangeSpec(parents: List<Revision>, …, edit: Boolean)` — `ui/newchange/NewChangeDialog.kt:26`
   - `RebaseSpec(revisions: List<Revision>, destinations: List<Revision>, sourceMode, …)` — `ui/rebase/RebaseDialog.kt:22`

   `WorkingCopy` is itself a `Revision` (`jj/Revset.kt`). So "merge bookmark with current change"
   is `NewChangeSpec(parents = [bookmark, @])` and "rebase current change onto bookmark" is
   `RebaseSpec(revisions = [@], destinations = [bookmark])`. Neither needs a new menu entry per
   combination — the *dialog* is where the second operand is chosen.

2. **Gestures, not menu entries.** The DnD suite (`jj-idea-6oeg`; batches 1–2 shipped) already
   expresses bookmark × commit combinations by dragging. `jj-idea-0rdm` (panel as payload
   source/drop target), `jj-idea-3xab` (drag local bookmark onto its remote = push),
   `jj-idea-j8ij` (branch-mode drag-rebase) and `jj-idea-pk2c` (drag the `@` marker onto a row =
   `jj edit`) are the open beads that cover exactly the "combine two operands" shape without any
   menu growth.

3. **A dialog-free execution seam already exists.** `executeRebase` is `internal` and already
   called without a dialog from the DnD path, so "quick action" versions of these combinations
   cost a factory function each — they do not need new command plumbing, undo wiring, or a
   workflows engine. See Gap B below, which is the concrete instance of this.

So the expected recommendation is: **a small fixed set — one quick action plus at most one
dialog gap — not a custom-workflows feature**, and **#68 stays separate**. #68's requester
(`SergejSalnikov`) wants *third-party plugin* extensibility for forge-ish actions ("send for
review", "submit", "jj sync" on the toolbar) — an API-stability commitment, deliberately P4 in
`jj-idea-66id`. #48's reporter wants *two specific built-in jj operations*. Conflating them
would gate a small user-facing fix behind a public SPI.

The session must actually confirm this against the code rather than restate it — in particular
whether the two gaps below are real.

## Work to do

### 1. Verify the two concrete gaps

Read and confirm (or correct) each:

- **Gap A — `@` can't be a second parent from the panel.** `NewChangeDialog` is constructed with
  `targetEntries: List<LogEntry>` from the panel selection
  (`JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:407`, `actions/change/newChangeFromAction.kt`). The panel's
  `selectedLogEntries()` (`JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:358-373`) only resolves bookmark/tag leaves
  — the `BookmarkNode.WorkingCopy` node is not among them, and `actionGroupFor`'s `WorkingCopy`
  branch (`:479-482`) offers only create/advance. So multi-select can already merge two
  *bookmarks*, but not a bookmark with `@`.
- **Gap B — "rebase my branch onto this bookmark" has no quick action, and the direction is
  backwards.** This is the headline gap and the single highest-value one; the maintainer named
  it directly:

  > the common rebase action for a bookmark is to rebase an entire branch to the bookmark, most
  > often to rebase a local strand of work onto master. It would be great to have a quick action
  > for that.

  Today `Jujutsu.RebaseChangeToolbar` reads `LOG_ENTRY`/`LOG_ENTRIES`, so from a bookmark row it
  rebases *the bookmark's own change*, with the destination chosen in the dialog — the converse
  of what's wanted, and always via a dialog.

  The seam already exists and needs no new plumbing. `executeRebase(project, repo, spec)`
  (`actions/change/rebaseAction.kt:47`) is `internal`, runs `jj rebase` with undo tracking, a
  repo invalidate and an undo balloon, and is **already invoked dialog-free by
  `ui/dnd/DropPerformers.kt:73`**. The wanted operation is one `RebaseSpec`:

  ```kotlin
  RebaseSpec(
      revisions = listOf(WorkingCopy),          // -b @
      destinations = listOf(bookmarkRevision),  // --onto <bookmark>
      sourceMode = RebaseSourceMode.BRANCH,     // "-b", jj/Revset.kt:179
      destinationMode = RebaseDestinationMode.ONTO
  )
  ```

  So the follow-up is a thin `nullAndDumbAwareAction` factory in
  `actions/bookmark/`, added to the panel's `Local`/`Remote` branches in `actionGroupFor`
  (`JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:425-462`) — not a dialog change, and not a workflows feature.
  Verify: whether it should be no-dialog outright or confirm-first (rebasing a whole branch is
  not trivially reversible, though the undo balloon covers it), and how it enables/disables when
  `@` is already a descendant of the bookmark (no-op) or the bookmark is immutable
  (cf. `jj-idea-jamk`, immutable-change policy).

  **This is both a menu action and a DnD gesture, not one or the other.** `jj-idea-j8ij`
  ("Drag-rebase: differentiate commit / descendants / branch source mode") is the open bead for
  choosing `BRANCH` mode on the *drag* path; the quick action is its menu twin over the same
  `executeRebase` call. The spike should state that relationship explicitly and cross-link the
  two beads rather than letting them be discovered independently.

Also confirm the operand-count claim concretely: count the entries the `Local` context menu
already renders (`actionGroupFor`, `JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:425-449`) and state what a naive
"one entry per bookmark × working-copy pairing" would add. That number *is* the combinatorial
argument, and it is what makes the recommendation credible.

### 2. Write the recommendation

`docs/design/jj-idea-tohr-bookmark-workingcopy-actions.md`, following the house style of
`docs/design/jj-idea-6oeg-drag-and-drop-graph-ops.md`. Structure:

- Existing infrastructure surveyed (the two dialog specs, `addChangeActions`, DnD dispatch).
- Finding 1: the explosion is avoided by parameterised dialogs — with the entry count.
- Finding 2: gestures cover the rest (DnD beads already filed).
- Finding 3: whichever of Gap A / Gap B survives verification.
- Finding 4: #68 is a different problem — quote both requesters' actual asks, and note
  `jj-idea-66id`'s P4 rationale (public SPI = API-stability commitment) and `jj-idea-1y1j`
  (the `LazyActionById` decision that depends on #68 landing).
- Recommendation + the follow-ups.

Note that `jj-idea-d65h` (spike 1/2) claimed a `docs/design/…` doc in its close reason but the
writeup actually landed in `jj-idea-3sac`'s DESIGN field, and no such file exists. To avoid
repeating that drift: write the file **and** paste a condensed version into `jj-idea-tohr`'s
design field before closing.

### 3. File follow-ups

`bd create` one issue per surviving gap (P3, labels `bookmarks`, `from-github-issue`,
`working-copy`), each naming the exact seam. Expected set:

- **Gap B (file this one regardless — it is the maintainer's own ask):** "Quick action: rebase
  the current branch onto a bookmark (`jj rebase -b @ --onto <bookmark>`)", naming
  `executeRebase` + the `RebaseSpec` above and `actionGroupFor`'s `Local`/`Remote` branches.
  `bd dep add` onto `jj-idea-tohr`; `relates_to` `jj-idea-j8ij` (the drag-gesture twin).
  Consider P2 rather than P3 given it is a named, frequent workflow.
- **Gap A (only if verification confirms it):** "Let the bookmarks panel contribute `@` as a
  `NewChangeSpec` parent", covering the reporter's "Merge with current change".

Also add a `relates_to` between `jj-idea-tohr` and `jj-idea-66id` recording the explicit "these
are separable" decision. Do **not** file a custom-workflows epic unless verification overturns
the expected answer.

### 4. Close out

`bd close jj-idea-tohr --reason="…"` naming the doc path and the follow-up ids, then
`bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl`.

## Two side-deliverables worth folding in (cheap, same context)

- **GitHub hygiene.** The reporter split #48 into #107–#111 and closed it. Of those,
  **#109** (keymap-assignable bookmark actions) shipped as `jj-idea-ib1i`, **#110** (bookmark
  states in the panel) as `jj-idea-ita2`, and **#111** (persist expand/collapse) as
  `jj-idea-a7a7`; **#108** (more bookmark actions) is largely `jj-idea-p35f`. Report which are
  closeable and ask before commenting/closing anything on GitHub. **#107** is `jj-idea-lig7`.
- **Record the `jj-idea-lig7` decisions taken this session** into that bead's design field, so
  the build session doesn't re-litigate them:
  - dangling rule = **local bookmarks only**, revset `visible_heads() ~ ::bookmarks() ~ @`,
    matching `closestBookmarks()`'s own `bookmarks()` query (`jj/ClosestBookmarks.kt:27`);
  - presentation = **bookmarks panel *and* a log-table marker** (note the wider blast radius:
    `LogEntryText`/`JujutsuLogTableRenderers` feed MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-GRAPH, MT-LOG-DETAILS
    as well as MT-BOOKMARK);
  - the per-head cost model: 1 + 2·N bounded `jj log` calls (reusing `closestBookmarks(to =
    head)`), so it needs a `DANGLING_HEADS_LIMIT` cap and an invocation-count test modelled on
    `src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/jj/ClosestBookmarksScaleTest.kt`.

## Files

Read-only for this spike: `ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt`,
`ui/newchange/NewChangeDialog.kt`, `ui/rebase/RebaseDialog.kt`,
`actions/change/{newChangeFromAction,rebaseAction}.kt`, `ui/dnd/DropPerformers.kt`,
`docs/design/jj-idea-6oeg-drag-and-drop-graph-ops.md`.

Written: `docs/design/jj-idea-tohr-bookmark-workingcopy-actions.md`, `.beads/issues.jsonl`,
and beads records.

## Verification

No code changes, so no `./gradlew check` requirement beyond confirming the tree is still clean.

- Every code claim in the doc cites a real `file:line` — re-open each cited site and confirm the
  quote before the doc is declared done.
- `bd show jj-idea-tohr` shows the recommendation in its design field and a close reason naming
  the doc and follow-up ids.
- `bd show <new-id>` for each follow-up shows a dependency on `jj-idea-tohr` and acceptance
  criteria naming a concrete seam, not a restatement of the ask.
- **Manual regression scope: none — no manual surface affected** (documentation and task
  tracking only; `docs/manual-tests.md` unchanged).
- **CHANGELOG**: internal-only, so no `[Unreleased]` entry; use `[skip changelog]` in the commit
  message per contributing.md.

title: Spike: configurable treatment of remotes in the bookmarks panel (GitHub #48 spike 1/2)
description:
## Summary
Timeboxed investigation, not shipped UI. From GitHub #48 (comment 2026-09-04T17:56): reporter wants "git"/"origin" collapsed by default in the bookmarks panel (otherwise colocated repos show every bookmark thrice), and wants unsynced (local ahead of @origin) and diverged bookmarks made more visible. Maintainer flagged that not everyone has a primary "origin", and some setups have several remotes, so this needs design before building.

## Questions to answer
- Is there a defensible notion of a "primary" remote — jj's git.push/git.fetch config, single-remote repos, the colocated "git" remote — or must this always be an explicit user setting?
- Can the same remote-comparison data used for collapsing also drive unsynced/diverged visibility, so this is one feature not two?

## Files to read
ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkTreeModel.kt, actions/bookmark/BookmarkClassifier.kt

## Deliverable
A written recommendation, plus the follow-up build issue(s) to file based on it. This spike does not implement anything itself.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/48 (comment 2026-09-04T17:56:14Z)
acceptance_criteria: A recommendation is recorded (defensible-primary-remote heuristic vs. explicit setting) and follow-up build issues are filed.

title: Visually indicate dangling heads (not ancestors of any bookmark) (GitHub #107, #48 split 3/3)
description:
## Summary
Part 3 of the maintainer's three-way split of GitHub #48 (comment 2026-09-04T17:56).

Mark heads that are not ancestors of any bookmark — in the bookmarks panel and/or log — so a forgotten `jj bookmark advance` is obvious. Reuse the existing ClosestBookmarks plumbing (jj/ClosestBookmarks.kt) rather than a new traversal.

Reporter's suggested presentation: similar to the existing "[closest_bookmark] +x @" shown at the top of the panel — for every head that is not bookmarked, show "[closest_bookmark] +x [change_id]", double-clickable to jump to that change in the log.

## Acceptance Criteria
A dangling head (log head with no bookmark reachable forward from it) is visually distinguishable in the bookmarks panel.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/48 (comment 2026-09-04T17:56:14Z)
acceptance_criteria: Dangling heads are visually distinguishable in the bookmarks panel, reusing ClosestBookmarks.
notes:
Canonical issue is now GitHub #107 (this bead was filed citing only #48; #107 is cYDN48's
standalone re-filing of split 3/3 since no bead existed under that number yet).

From #107: reporter wants these rendered in the existing area above the bookmarks tree
(currently showing "[closest bookmark] +n @"), extended to one row per dangling head:
"[closest bookmark] +n [change id] (@)", double-click to jump the log to that change.
