title: Default merge descriptions when merging bookmarked changes (GitHub #103)
description:
## Summary
Prefill the description field in NewChangeDialog (opened by newChangeFromAction.kt) when the user creates a merge (jj new A B, i.e. 2+ selected parents).

## Behaviour
- When exactly 2 parents are selected and both carry a bookmark name, offer:
  - "Merge branch 'A' into 'B'" and "Merge branch 'B' into 'A'" (direction cannot be inferred in jj — no concept of "being on a branch")
  - or the directionless "Merge branches 'A' and 'B'"
- Silent (no prefill / current behaviour) when parents have no bookmarks, when there are more than 2 parents, or bookmarks are ambiguous.
- Prefill only — fully editable, does not block a custom description.

## Open design question to settle before implementing
Dropdown of the three phrasings vs. a single default plus a swap affordance. Recommendation: default to the directionless form, and offer the two directional forms via the existing description history/quick-pick, to avoid cluttering the dialog with a new control.

## Implementation notes
Reuse the existing bookmark-name plumbing already available on LogEntry/ClosestBookmarks rather than adding a new query.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/103
design:
PLAN: prefill NewChangeDialog's description for a 2-parent bookmarked merge, with a configurable template and a gentle direction default (the bead's 2026-09-06 refinement notes are adopted as the design; this plan makes them concrete).
Facts: `NewChangeDialog` (ui/newchange/NewChangeDialog.kt:62; ctor `(project, repo, targets: List<LogEntry>)` called from actions/change/newChangeFromAction.kt:28) owns `descriptionEditor` (:72, `DescriptionEditor` - note jj-idea-k68t's trailing-whitespace normalisation applies to what we set) and returns `NewChangeSpec(description, parents, destinationMode, edit)`. LogEntry has `bookmarks: List<Bookmark>` (local+remote), `authorTimestamp`, `committerTimestamp` (jj/LogEntry.kt). Description history/quick-pick exists (`saveDescriptionToHistory` in actions/Extensions? used at newChangeFromAction.kt:6).
Design:
1. Pure function `defaultMergeDescription(targets: List<LogEntry>, template: String): MergeDescriptionSuggestion?` in ui/newchange/ (testable w/o Swing): returns null unless EXACTLY 2 targets AND each has a usable bookmark name: prefer a LOCAL bookmark; if none, the remote's `localName` (strip `@origin`); if several, pick deterministically by (a) bookmark that is not the working-copy-only, then alphabetical (ambiguity rule from the bead: "silent when bookmarks are ambiguous" - define ambiguous = a target has >1 local bookmark names (e.g. `main` + `release`): then return null, do not guess). Output: `primary` (preselected phrasing) + `alternatives` (flipped direction, directionless).
2. Phrasing & direction: template string setting `mergeDescriptionTemplate` default `Merge branch '{source}' into '{destination}'` (JujutsuSettingsState field + Settings > Version Control > Jujutsu > Descriptions group; validated: must contain both placeholders or neither; unknown placeholders rejected with an inline error). Direction default per the 2026-09-06 note: the OLDER tip (min of committerTimestamp, fall back authorTimestamp, tie/absent -> the order the user selected them) becomes {destination}; the newer becomes {source}. Directionless form `Merge branches '{a}' and '{b}'` is a second built-in template (not user-editable v1, or `{a}`/`{b}` placeholders in a second setting - Rec: keep one editable template; directionless is built-in).
3. UI: do NOT add a new control (recommendation in the bead): prefill `descriptionEditor.text` with `primary` ONLY when the editor is empty AND the user hasn't typed; offer the two alternatives through the existing description history/quick-pick popup (add them as the first entries, labelled "Suggested") - find the quick-pick source (`saveDescriptionToHistory` neighbour; if the dialog has a "history" dropdown). If the dialog has no quick-pick yet, add a small link-button under the editor "Swap direction" that rewrites the prefilled text only when the text still equals the previous suggestion (never clobber user edits).
4. Skip cases (unchanged behaviour): 1 or >2 targets; bookmark-less targets; pending/immutable irrelevance - none; dialogs opened with `edit=false`? unaffected.
5. Merge-bookmark naming nuance: when both bookmarks are REMOTE-only (e.g. `main@origin`), use `main` (strip remote) so descriptions read naturally; when the same bookmark name appears on both parents (divergent) -> null.
Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Direction default by timestamp tie-breaker as the 2026-09-06 notes describe? Rec yes (preselection only, never silent). Reverse: always directionless.
2. Q: Template setting location? Rec: Settings (project-level setting, like other description defaults - check whether descriptions group exists; else general Jujutsu page).
3. Q: Which timestamp? Rec: committerTimestamp (rewritten commits update it; author time stays old after rebase) with author as fallback.
Scale: O(2) per dialog open; no jj calls (data already on LogEntry). Testing: `defaultMergeDescriptionTest` table: 0/1/3 targets -> null; two local bookmarks -> prefill with older as destination; tie -> selection order; multiple bookmarks on one target -> null; remote-only names; same name on both; custom template; invalid template falls back to default; dialog test: prefill happens only when editor empty, Swap respects user edits. Manual: MT-CTXMENU New Change dialog rows (select two bookmarked rows -> New Change From These: description prefilled; edit then Swap does not overwrite; >2 parents none); regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-BOOKMARK (bookmark panel multi-select -> New Change), MT-SETTINGS (template field).
acceptance_criteria: Creating a new change from two bookmarked parents prefills a sensible merge description; single-parent and >2-parent flows are unaffected.
notes:
Design refinement (2026-09-06, from user discussion, not yet posted to GitHub):

Direction default: do NOT silently pick a direction from commit timestamps — a bookmark tip's
timestamp does not reliably indicate which is "the branch you're on" vs. "the one being merged
in" (a stable/release bookmark can have a very recent commit; a feature bookmark can sit
un-rebased for a while, etc). Instead, use the older parent's tip timestamp only as a
tie-breaker for *which phrasing is pre-selected* (older bookmark defaults to the destination,
Y, in "Merge branch X into Y" — matches the common convention of merging newer work into an
established line), while still surfacing the flip and the directionless phrasing as
easy-to-reach alternatives, not buried. This keeps the risk of a wrong choice low since it is
just an initial selection, not a silent unchangeable pick.

Template support: add a settings string with {source}/{destination} placeholders, default
`Merge branch '{source}' into '{destination}'`, so teams with their own merge-commit
convention can customize the wording. This mirrors how the project already exposes other
jj-adjacent strings as configurable settings (e.g. DiffbaseStrategy's custom revset in
settings/DiffbaseStrategy.kt). Cheap to add alongside the direction-default logic.

Available data confirmed: LogEntry.kt has authorTimestamp (Instant?) and committerTimestamp
(Instant?) already on the model, so no new plumbing is needed to read timestamps.

title: [bug] "Advance Bookmark Here" in log menu is misleading — reads as targeting clicked row, actually targets @ (GitHub #104)
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. In the log, right-click any change other than @ that has a bookmark ahead of it.
2. Select "Advance Bookmark Here".
3. Observe the closest bookmark to @ is advanced to @ — not to the clicked row.

## Root Cause
JujutsuLogContextMenuActions.kt:148 adds advanceClosestBookmarkAction(uniqueRepo, closestBookmarks[repo]) to the row right-click menu. closestBookmarks is closest-to-@, and jj bookmark advance always moves the bookmark to @, never to the clicked row. In a per-row context menu, "Here" naturally reads as "to this row."

## Decision (maintainer, 2026-09-04)
Relabel only, do not retarget. Give the log context-menu instance different wording that names the working copy explicitly, e.g. "Advance Bookmark to Working Copy" (matching the Working Copy panel phrasing), threaded through advanceClosestBookmarkAction as an optional text override — it currently hardcodes action.bookmark.advance.closest (advanceBookmarkAction.kt:155-177). "Move Bookmark Here..." already covers targeting the clicked change directly.

Leave WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt:269, JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:221, and BookmarkMenu.kt:73 as-is unless it is simpler to align all call sites on the new wording.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/104
acceptance_criteria: The log right-click menu entry no longer implies it targets the clicked row.
notes: Closed: relabeled 'Advance Bookmark Here' to 'Advance Bookmark to Working Copy' across all 4 call sites (single JujutsuBundle.properties key change, no retargeting per maintainer decision); regression test added in AdvanceBookmarkAvailabilityTest.kt.
close_reason: JujutsuLogTable.kt already had setTargetComponent; added it to the two remaining popup call sites (JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt, JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt).

title: Mark the current diff base in the log table
description:
Follow-up from jj-idea-g1io: once a custom diff base is active (per-repo override or project default, DiffbaseStrategy != WORKING_COPY_PARENT), there's no visual indicator in the log table showing which row is currently being used as the base for gutter markers/Annotate. A user has to remember what they picked, or reopen the Set Diff Base popup / Settings to check.

DESIGN QUESTIONS to resolve during implementation:
- What resolves the marker: DiffbaseService.resolve(repo) already resolves the configured strategy to a ChangeId (vcs/diffbase/DiffbaseService.kt) - reuse it, don't duplicate resolution logic.
- Where it renders: the log table row for that ChangeId, if it's within the currently-loaded log window/revset - may not always be visible (e.g. base is outside the filtered revset). Decide the fallback (nothing shown? a note elsewhere?).
- What it looks like: needs to coexist with existing per-row markers (working-copy bold, mutable/immutable icons via JujutsuIcons, bookmark/tag chips in ui/components/TextCanvas.kt and ui/log/JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt) without visual clutter or ambiguity with the working-copy marker.
- Liveness: DiffbaseService already fires project.stateModel.diffbaseChanged after every base change (notifyDiffbaseChanged()) - the log table's renderer needs to subscribe to that and repaint, same pattern already used by JujutsuAnnotationProvider.
- Only relevant when DiffbaseService.isActive(repo) is true (custom base configured) - the default @- case needs no marker, since that's just 'the working copy's parent', not a separate distinguishable state worth calling out.

Relates to jj-idea-4tcf (live effective diff base in Settings - same resolver, different surface: settings text vs. log row) and jj-idea-g1io (Set Diff Base quick action, which is what makes switching the base fast enough that losing track of it becomes a real problem).
design:
PLAN: show a "diff base" tag in the status bracket of the resolved base row (and a left-edge accent), live, only when a CUSTOM base is active.
Facts: the status brackets are built in `TextCanvas.appendSummaryAndStatuses` (ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:~428-480: `@ working copy`, closest-bookmark, conflict, empty, divergent, immutable parts via `statusParts`/`appendBracket`) - used for the details/tooltip text; the log TABLE row text path is `LaidOutCell.forRow` (ui/log/LaidOutCell.kt:75) -> `appendStatusIndicators(entry)` when `columnManager.showStatus`. Resolution: `DiffbaseService.getInstance(project).resolve(repo)` (vcs/diffbase/DiffbaseService.kt:85; needs a background thread, cached; `isActive(repo)` is EDT-safe and false for the default) and liveness `project.stateModel.diffbaseChanged` (JujutsuStateModel.kt:294, notified from DiffbaseService.notifyDiffbaseChanged :138; the annotation provider already subscribes at JujutsuAnnotationProvider.kt:73).
Design (answers the bead's four design questions):
1. WHAT: a per-repo `diffBaseId: ChangeId?` cache exposed to the table: `LogDiffbaseMarkers` (small per-panel holder) = `Map<JujutsuRepository, ChangeId?>`, populated on a pooled thread via `resolve(repo)` for repos where `isActive(repo)` is true, null otherwise; refreshed on `diffbaseChanged` and on `logRefresh` (since PREVIOUS_COMMIT/IMMUTABLE_ANCESTOR strategies move with the repo state; DiffbaseService.resolve already caches until logRefresh, so the call is cheap). Paint path only READS the holder (no jj on paint).
2. WHERE: the row whose `entry.id == diffBaseId(entry.repo)`: if it is not in the loaded/filtered window nothing is drawn (fallback decision below: also show a one-line hint in the log toolbar/status bar "Diff base: <short id> (not in view)" with a click that navigates via `changeSelection.notify(ChangeKey)` (jj-idea-7m8 pattern) - cheap, uses `requestSelection`/`loadExpanding`).
3. LOOK: a status-part `[diff base]` in the same bracket as the other statuses with a dedicated small icon (new `icons/diffBase.svg`, theme-aware via the JujutsuIcons recolour helpers, JujutsuIcons.kt:51-76 pattern) and a distinct colour (`JujutsuColors.DIFF_BASE`, not red/green used for conflict/WC); NOT the working-copy colour/bold. Tooltip text: "Current diff base for gutter markers and Annotate (change <id>). Change it with Set Diff Base." Coexists: it only adds one short bracket item; multi-status rows already wrap as comma-separated parts.
4. LIVENESS: subscribe in UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel/CommitTablePanel to `diffbaseChanged` -> recompute holder -> `logTable.repaint()` (no data reload). Disposable-bound subscription (`connect(this)`).
5. ONLY WHEN CUSTOM: gate on `isActive(repo)`; default `@-` shows nothing (per the bead) - careful: when the base resolves to the SAME commit as @- (custom strategy that happens to equal default) still show (the user chose a custom strategy; marker confirms it).
6. Multi-repo: per-repo marker (each repo may have an override: `settings.diffbaseStrategy(repo)`).
Decisions made without the user: Q: bracket tag vs row background tint vs left-edge bar? Rec: bracket tag + small icon (consistent with immutable/conflict tags; no new visual language). Reverse: swap rendering only. Q: add the "(not in view)" toolbar hint? Rec: yes small, optional - skip if UI crowding; can drop without affecting the rest.
Scale: resolve = existing 1 cached jj call per repo per logRefresh; paint = O(1) lookup per visible row; no per-row work. Operation-count test: 100 repaints => 0 resolve calls; diffbaseChanged => 1 resolve per active repo.
Testing: unit - marker holder (active/inactive, resolve None/Ambiguous -> no marker, per-repo override), status-part builder includes the tag only for the matched id; platform renderer test for the tag text; liveness test: notify diffbaseChanged -> holder updated -> repaint requested. Manual: MT-DIFFBASE (set custom base via quick action: marker appears on that row immediately; change base: marker moves; default base: none; base outside window: hint), MT-LOG-TABLE (row text/tooltips unchanged otherwise). Regression scope: MT-DIFFBASE, MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-DETAILS (appendSummaryAndStatuses shared).
Related: jj-idea-4tcf (settings live line; shares resolver).
acceptance_criteria: With a custom diff base active and its resolved commit visible in the current log window, that row shows a clear, unambiguous marker distinguishing it from the working-copy/mutable/immutable markers already there. The marker updates live when the diff base changes (via the quick action or Settings) without needing a log refresh. No marker appears when the diff base is the default (working copy parent).

title: DescriptionEditor.text round-trips unequal for trailing-whitespace descriptions
description: DescriptionEditor.text's setter writes value.actual verbatim while its getter returns CommitMessage.getComment() = trimTrailing(document). A description ending in whitespace therefore round-trips unequal, causing a phantom modified marker (*) right after a load with no real edit. Found while investigating jj-idea-4d7p. Fix: normalise the setter to write value.actual.trimEnd().
design:
PLAN: one-line normalisation plus a property test.
Fix: ui/components/DescriptionEditor.kt:45 `var text: Description` - setter currently writes `value.actual` verbatim, getter returns the document through CommitMessage.getComment() (= trimTrailing). Make the setter write `value.actual.trimEnd()` so set->get round-trips equal and the modified marker (*) does not appear after a load with no edit. Only trim TRAILING whitespace (leading whitespace/blank lines are semantically part of a description; getComment doesn't strip them, so don't either).
Check the other direction: where the editor's text is compared against the stored description to compute "modified" (grep callers of `.text` in the working-copy panel/describe dialog, jj-idea-4d7p's code path) - compare via the same normalisation, otherwise a description stored WITH trailing newline (jj stores "msg
") keeps a phantom diff. Normalise the baseline once at load (`Description.actual.trimEnd()`) rather than at every comparison.
Edge cases: whitespace-only description -> "" (jj treats as empty); CRLF endings inside the description are left alone (only the tail trimmed); a description whose real content ends with intentional trailing spaces is lossy - jj itself strips trailing whitespace on commit messages in `jj describe` (it cleans up the message), so no real data is lost.
Decisions made without the user: none.
Scale: none. Testing: DescriptionEditorTest (platform, existing patterns): for inputs ["", "a", "a
", "a 

", "  ", "a

b
"] assert `editor.text = d; editor.text.actual == d.actual.trimEnd()` and `isModified == false`; plus the 4d7p scenario (load description with trailing newline in WC panel -> no `*`). Manual: MT-WORKINGCOPY (jj-idea-4d7p row: describe a change via CLI with a trailing blank line, open panel, no modified marker). Regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-LOG-DETAILS (shared editor if used there).
acceptance_criteria: DescriptionEditor.text round-trips equal for trailing-whitespace descriptions; no phantom * after load; unit test over the listed inputs; MT-WORKINGCOPY 4d7p row re-run.

title: Filter components mutate selection sets on EDT while BGT update() reads them unsynchronized
description:
Code-review finding from jj-idea-qcks (tri-state root filter, GitHub #96): JujutsuRootFilterComponent's CycleRootAction/SelectAllRootsAction mutate the plain, unsynchronized includedRoots/excludedRoots MutableSets from actionPerformed (EDT) while state()/update() read them on a background thread - both actions declare getActionUpdateThread() = BGT, and they sit inside BackgroundActionGroup which forces recursive BGT updates.

Rapidly clicking a root to cycle it fires actionPerformed on the EDT (add/remove on includedRoots or excludedRoots) concurrently with an in-flight BGT update() pass calling state() -> set.contains(). Unsynchronized concurrent mutation-while-read on a plain HashSet is undefined behavior - worst case a spurious exception, more likely a stale/torn icon during the click.

This is a pre-existing pattern, not new to jj-idea-qcks: the old single `selectedRoots` set had the same contract, and JujutsuAuthorFilterComponent / JujutsuReferenceFilterComponent (and likely other JujutsuFilterComponent subclasses with BGT-updated toggle/cycle actions) share the same shape - a plain mutable Set/collection written from actionPerformed (EDT) and read from update() (BGT). jj-idea-qcks's dual-set split widens the window slightly (a two-step remove-then-add transition for INCLUDED -> EXCLUDED) but did not introduce the underlying hazard.

Fix should likely be systemic: audit ui/log/Jujutsu*FilterComponent.kt subclasses for this shape and pick one approach (e.g. synchronized/concurrent collection, or copying the selection into an immutable snapshot on the EDT that BGT update() reads) applied consistently, rather than a one-off fix in the root filter alone.
design:
PLAN: systemic fix - selection state read by BGT update() must be an immutable snapshot published from the EDT.

Audit (confirmed by grep): plain `mutableSetOf` selection collections in ui/log/JujutsuRootFilterComponent.kt:31-32 (includedRoots/excludedRoots, read at :35-44, :129-130), JujutsuAuthorFilterComponent.kt:14 (selectedAuthors), JujutsuPathsFilterComponent.kt:16 (selectedPaths); JujutsuReferenceFilterComponent.kt:59 `result` is a local build set (fine - verify). JujutsuDateFilterComponent / RevsetFilterComponent hold scalar values: check they are `@Volatile` or only touched on EDT.
Approach: Rec = "copy-on-write immutable snapshot in a @Volatile var". Each component keeps `@Volatile private var selection: Selection` (an immutable data class / Set, e.g. RootFilterSelection which already exists as a value type: ui/log/RootFilterSelection.kt, `currentSelection()` at JujutsuRootFilterComponent.kt:44). EDT mutators compute a new immutable value and assign it (single volatile write = atomic publish, no torn two-step INCLUDED->EXCLUDED transition because both sets live in ONE object); BGT update()/state() read the field once into a local and use that. Put the pattern in the base class JujutsuFilterComponent (ui/log/JujutsuFilterComponent.kt): `protected inner class SnapshotState<T>(initial)` or document the rule in its KDoc + one shared helper, so subclasses can't reintroduce plain sets.
Alternatives rejected: ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet (fixes torn reads of one set but not the two-set INCLUDED/EXCLUDED consistency, and iteration order changes); `synchronized` (blocks BGT update on EDT click for no reason).
Steps: (1) RootFilter: fold both sets into RootFilterSelection held in the volatile field; adapt getSelectedRootPaths/getExcludedRootPaths/restore/clear (lines 53-68, 102-103). (2) Author/Paths: `@Volatile var selected: Set<String>` replaced wholesale (`selected = selected + a`). (3) Check `tableModel.setRootFilter(includedRoots, excludedRoots)` (line 48) receives copies, not live sets (otherwise the model aliases mutable state). (4) KDoc rule in JujutsuFilterComponent.

Decisions made without the user: Q: snapshot vs concurrent collections - Rec snapshot (above). Reverse: wrap with ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet.
Scale: O(selection size) copy per click on EDT, selection <= #roots/authors (tens-hundreds); negligible; no traversal.
Testing: unit test that hammers cycle() on one thread while another loops state() (CountDownLatch, N=10k iterations) asserting no exception and only legal (included,excluded) pairs observed (never a root in both) - fails on current code under ConcurrentModificationException/inconsistency; deterministic variants: assert `state()` after cycle returns consistent pair. Manual: MT-LOG-FILTER (rapid-click root cycling; author and path filters), regression scope MT-LOG-FILTER only.
acceptance_criteria: No plain mutable Set shared between EDT mutators and BGT readers in ui/log filter components; root include/exclude published atomically as one snapshot; stress test passes; MT-LOG-FILTER rapid-click smoke clean.

title: Run IDE code cleanup over the working copy from the Jujutsu panel (GitHub #98)
description:
Feature request from a Rider user (CaptaiNiveau): they use IDE code-cleanup commit
hooks (format-on-commit) in git and want the equivalent for jj. They note jj has no
"I'm done" moment analogous to git's commit button, and propose an interim button in
the Working Copy panel that runs "Full Cleanup" over the working copy's changed
files, with automatic hook-in to be figured out later.

Findings:
- The plugin registers no CheckinHandler / checkinHandlerFactory anywhere (grep over
  src/main/kotlin and plugin.xml is empty) — the platform's before-commit machinery
  isn't reused today, so there's no existing hook point to attach cleanup to.
- Nearest "I'm done" moments today: Jujutsu.DescribeWorkingCopy (plugin.xml:151),
  Jujutsu.NewChange (plugin.xml:159).
- Rider distinguishes CodeCleanup (opens a profile-choice dialog) from
  SilentCodeCleanup (runs the default profile silently) — need to ask the reporter
  which they want bound, since the plugin has to invoke it by action id and
  Rider-only ids need a graceful no-op/absence in IDEA.
design:
PLAN: a manual "Cleanup" button/action over the working copy's changed files, running the IDE's Silent Code Cleanup with the profile the user already configured for commit - per the reporter's answers on GitHub #98 (SilentCodeCleanup, mirror the commit-dialog profile config, automation later). (Phase 2 range cleanup = jj-idea-5auo, blocked on this.)
Platform facts (verified in ../intellij-community): action id `SilentCodeCleanup` (platform-resources/src/idea/LangActions.xml:364, class `SilentCodeCleanupAction`, `@ApiStatus.Internal`; IDEA-edition resource - so absent on IDEs without the idea LangActions, e.g. some Rider configurations -> graceful absence) vs `CodeCleanup` (profile-choice dialog, :359). `SilentCodeCleanupAction.actionPerformed` builds an `AnalysisScope` from the DataContext via `AnalysisActionUtils.getInspectionScope(dataContext, project, false)` (selected files/module/project from standard data keys), saves all documents, then `GlobalInspectionContextBase.codeCleanup(scope, profile, title, postRunnable, false)` with `InspectionProjectProfileManager.getCurrentProfile()` - ignoring the commit-dialog profile. The platform's commit-time handler `CodeCleanupCheckinHandler` (platform/vcs-impl/lang/.../CodeCleanupCheckinHandler.kt, `@ApiStatus.Internal`) shows the supported mechanics: profile = `VcsConfiguration.getInstance(project).CHECK_CODE_CLEANUP_BEFORE_PROJECT_COMMIT_PROFILE` (+ `..._LOCAL` application-vs-project profile flag), `GlobalInspectionContextImpl.findProblems(scope, profile, indicator)` then `PerformFixesTask`. `VcsConfiguration` fields are public API; the handler classes are Internal (do not reference them: verifyPlugin ... INTERNAL_API_USAGES is not fatal per build.gradle.kts:240-256 but the contributing.md rule says avoid regular internal use).
Design (two layers; layer 1 is the MVP):
1. Layer 1 - invoke by action id with a constructed DataContext (no Internal class references): `ActionManager.getInstance().getAction("SilentCodeCleanup")`; if null (non-IDEA edition or id removed) the button is disabled with reason (visible-but-disabled convention). On click: collect the working copy's changed files that exist on disk (`ChangeListManager.allChanges.filterInJujutsuRepo(project)` -> after-revision virtual files, excluding deleted; same source UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel uses :499; for the panel's bound repo only), build a `DataContext` with `CommonDataKeys.PROJECT` + `CommonDataKeys.VIRTUAL_FILE_ARRAY` = those files (via `SimpleDataContext.builder()`), invoke via `ActionUtil.performActionDumbAwareWithCallbacks(action, AnActionEvent.createFromDataContext(...))` (public ActionUtil API) on the EDT. Result: platform cleanup runs with the CURRENT project profile and shows its own progress; undo grouped as one command. This honours answer 1 (Silent) but not answer 2 (commit-profile mirroring).
2. Layer 2 - honour the commit-dialog profile: replicate the small `getProfile()` logic from CodeCleanupCheckinHandler (public pieces: `VcsConfiguration`, `InspectionProfileManager.getInstance()` / `InspectionProjectProfileManager.getInstance(project)`) and run our own `GlobalInspectionContextBase.codeCleanup(scope, profile, title, null, false)` - needs lang-impl types (`com.intellij.codeInspection.ex.GlobalInspectionContextBase`, public in lang-impl but not the stable platform API surface; `plugin.xml` must depend on `com.intellij.modules.lang` (already? check) ). Verify with verifyPlugin on the 2025.1-2026.2 matrix; if any API is missing on 251, stay with layer 1 and document. Settings UI for profile choice: don't duplicate; reuse the existing commit settings (Settings > Version Control > Commit > "Cleanup code" profile) by linking to it: hint text under the button "Uses the cleanup profile configured for commits (Settings > Version Control > Commit)" - no new config panel (answer 2 satisfied by reuse, simpler than "mirror the panel").
3. Placement: Working Copy panel toolbar/controls (WorkingCopyControlsPanel / UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel toolbar: find the toolbar group like WorkingCopyToolbarTest covers) + the Jujutsu VCS menu entry `Jujutsu.CleanupWorkingCopy` (registered action, keymap-assignable) with `AllIcons.Actions.CleanupCode`? (exists: AllIcons.Actions.Cleanup? check) - visible/disabled when no changed files.
4. After cleanup: files change on disk/in documents -> `jj` snapshot happens on next command; call `repo.invalidate(vfsChanged = true)` after completion? The platform action is fire-and-forget (postRunnable null) - our VFS listener already marks dirty on file edits; no extra refresh needed. Do NOT auto-describe/auto-new.
5. Automatic trigger: explicitly deferred (reporter has no settled opinion; bead says ship manual first). Record candidates for a follow-up: before `jj new`/describe (NewChange action), or on `Jujutsu.Push`.
Decisions made without the user: Q: reuse the commit-dialog cleanup setting (link) vs own panel? Rec link (no duplicate config; platform setting is per-project `VcsConfiguration`). Q: layer 2 now? Rec ship layer 1; layer 2 behind a spike since it touches lang-impl APIs. Q: scope = changed files only vs project? Changed files only (the bead's ask).
Scale: O(changed files) to build the data context (<=~1k working set); cleanup cost is the platform's. Testing: availability test (action id missing => disabled with reason; no files => disabled); data-context builder test (deleted files excluded, files outside the repo excluded, multi-repo scoping: bound repo only); manual (IDEA): edit files with fixable warnings, press Cleanup: fixes applied, one undo step; no changes -> disabled; Rider: absent-id behaviour. Regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-CROSS (IDE variants).
acceptance_criteria: Working Copy panel/menu 'Cleanup' runs the IDE Silent Code Cleanup over the working copy's changed files (action-id based, disabled when absent or no files), pointing at the commit cleanup profile setting; automatic trigger deferred; tests + manual rows.
notes:
2026-09-06 follow-up from CaptaiNiveau (GitHub #98): pointed at `jj run`, which accepts a
range of commits and is intended for exactly this kind of code-cleanup-with-linters workflow,
as a possible guide rail for a future range/log-based cleanup action (the "button in the log
to run cleanup on one changeset or a range" idea already noted below as out of scope for this
bead). Tracked separately as jj-idea-5auo, which depends on this bead landing first (reuses
SilentCodeCleanup / profile-selection-config decisions from the reporter's earlier answers).

Deliberately deferred: which lifecycle moment (describe-time? pre-push?) should trigger cleanup automatically, if any. Ship the manual Working Copy panel button first; automation is a follow-up once real usage patterns are known.

Reporter answers (2026-09-03T21:15:58Z, CaptaiNiveau):
1. Use SilentCodeCleanup (matches git-commit-hook behaviour), not the profile-picker CodeCleanup.
2. Mirror the cleanup-profile-selection config panel from the default VCS commit dialog, so the button runs the selected profiles now and an automatic trigger can reuse the same settings later.
3. No settled opinion on the automatic-trigger moment — floated "on creating a new changeset" as a possibility, but is not confident in this since their jj workflow is not yet settled.

Follow-up idea from the same thread (2026-09-03T21:19:08Z), NOT in scope for this issue — now tracked as jj-idea-5auo: a button in the log to run cleanup on one changeset or a range of changesets (auto-edit + run + return), so every changeset in history has passed cleanup, not just the current working copy.

title: Settings: align Installation Help command labels, tighten width further
description: Follow-up from live UI review of jj-idea-ye1x (settings width fix). Two related issues: (1) 'Homebrew:'/'Cargo:' labels in the Installation Help commandRow sit much closer to their input field than 'JJ executable path:' does above them, because each collapsibleGroup computes its label column width independently (short install-method names vs the long path label) -- fix via Cell.widthGroup() to sync label widths across groups. (2) In a narrower Settings window (e.g. a resized/pinned single-configurable view), the Executable row's path field + Test button still overflows requiring horizontal scroll -- shrink the path field's base columns (COLUMNS_MEDIUM -> COLUMNS_SHORT; it stays resizable/FILL so usability is unaffected) to reduce that row's minimum width contribution.
acceptance_criteria: Homebrew/Cargo labels visually align with the JJ executable path label's column width (verified manually, not practical to assert pixel-for-pixel in a headless test). Executable row's measured preferred width decreases without changing behavior (path field still expands to fill available width).
close_reason: Added 12px right-padding to Installation Help's command labels (Cell.widthGroup doesn't sync across separate collapsibleGroups, confirmed empirically, so used a border instead) and shrank the executable path field from COLUMNS_MEDIUM to COLUMNS_SHORT (still resizable/FILL). Added a regression test asserting the padding is present.

title: Drag-rebase: differentiate commit / descendants / branch source mode
description: jj-idea-8fxs's rebase-by-drag gesture (docs/design/jj-idea-6oeg-drag-and-drop-graph-ops.md section 1) hardcodes RebaseSourceMode.REVISION - only the single dragged commit (or exact multi-selection) moves; descendants/the whole branch stay put. jj rebase also supports -s (REVISION + descendants) and -b (whole branch containing the revision) via RebaseSourceMode (jj/Revset.kt:171). There is currently no drag-and-drop affordance to pick -s/-b instead of the default -r, so a user who wants to drag a commit and bring its descendants (or its whole branch) along has to fall back to the existing Rebase dialog. Raised during manual testing of jj-idea-6jvh; deliberately deferred rather than folded into the core infra bead, since it's gesture-level UX (belongs with jj-idea-8fxs), not shared plumbing.
design:
UX decision (resolved, was previously open): a persisted "Drag scope" radio group in the log's
View Options popup (in.kkkev.jjidea.ui.common.CommitTablePanel.DragScopeAction), gated behind
PreviewFeature.DRAG_AND_DROP the same way the guarded install site is. Mid-drag key cycling was
ruled out - DnDManagerImpl handles no KeyEvents, only the Move/Copy/Link action modifiers, and
Copy is already the duplicate gesture (jj-idea-p6nb). The chosen scope is read once per gesture
(DragContextHolder.forPayload's sourceMode supplier) and echoed in both the drop tooltip
(DropOperation.Rebase.label via sourceScopeLabel) and the drag chip, naming the exact descendant
count or "the branch containing <id>" - deliberate anti-footgun since the setting is sticky.

Copy-modifier drag stays -r regardless of the selector (jj duplicate has no -s/-b axis) - see
DropOperation.Duplicate's doc for the follow-up this leaves open (expanding revisions ourselves).

Guard correctness fix bundled with this: DragContext.forDrag's source-immutability check now
reads the full moved-id set (RebaseSimulator.excludedDestinationIds, which already computes the
same set for the cycle guard) rather than just the dragged entries - under -s/-b a mutable tip
with an immutable descendant/branch-mate must still reject.
acceptance_criteria: A drag gesture can select REVISION (default, current jj-idea-8fxs behaviour), SOURCE (-s, revision+descendants), or BRANCH (-b, whole branch) as the rebase source mode, discoverably (not memorization-only), with the resolved mode reflected in the DnDEvent tooltip label before drop.
notes:
Depends on jj-idea-8fxs landing first (this extends its gesture, doesn't duplicate it).
See docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md for batch scope, sequencing, and the preview-gating design. Find your batch's siblings with: bd list --label dnd-batch-N
close_reason: Implemented: @ marker drag-to-edit (jj-idea-pk2c) and drag-scope selector -r/-s/-b (jj-idea-j8ij), per docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md batch 5

title: Guided jj update: detect install method and run/guide the upgrade
description: Follow-up to jj-idea-sov0/jj-idea-xuah. The version-gated upgrade nudge and Settings -> Jujutsu -> Install/Upgrade group both currently only show/copy the upgrade command for the detected InstallMethod (jj/InstallMethod.kt) - the user still has to paste it into a terminal themselves. InstallMethod already models canRunDirectly (true for Homebrew today) and per-method upgradeCommand, but nothing acts on canRunDirectly yet (JujutsuConfigurable.commandRow only offers a copy button). Add a guided update flow: for a canRunDirectly method, run the upgradeCommand directly (e.g. via CliExecutor's process-running infra or a dedicated ProcessBuilder call) with progress/output shown to the user, then recheck jj availability (JjAvailabilityChecker.recheck()) so the plugin picks up the new version without a restart; for methods that aren't canRunDirectly, keep today's copy-to-clipboard/manual guidance but make it clearly a step in the same guided flow (e.g. a small dialog: 'Run this command in your terminal, then click Retry'). Wire the nudge balloon's 'Update jj...' action (JujutsuNotifications.notifyFeaturesGatedByVersion) to launch this flow directly instead of just opening Settings.
design:
PLAN: guided jj update flow, phase 1 = run the upgrade for `canRunDirectly` install methods (Homebrew today) with live output and an availability recheck; phase 2 = guided copy-and-retry dialog for the other methods; phase 3 = wire the nudge balloon's "Update jj..." action to the flow.
Facts: `InstallMethod` (jj/InstallMethod.kt:67-172): sealed class with `name`, `installCommand`, `upgradeCommand`, `open val canRunDirectly = false`; `Homebrew` = `("Homebrew", "brew", <PATH dirs + /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin>, "brew install jj", "brew upgrade jj")` with `canRunDirectly = true`; others (Scoop, Chocolatey, Winget, Cargo, Apt, Snap, Manual, Unknown) false (Apt/Snap need sudo, Windows managers need elevation or are shell-specific - correct to keep manual). UI today: Settings "Installation Help" rows (settings/JujutsuConfigurable.kt:~856-870 `commandRow(method.name, command)` = text field + Copy button, :1422-1440); upgrade nudge `JujutsuNotifications.notifyFeaturesGatedByVersion` (ui/services/JujutsuNotifications.kt:458-483; action "Update jj..." just opens Settings, :473-475). Availability: `project.jjAvailabilityStatus.invalidate()` recomputes (JujutsuConfigurable.kt:~1355 comment: "NotifiableState.invalidate only republishes when the recomputed status actually differs").
Design:
1. `JjUpgradeRunner` (jj/ or ui/services/): `fun run(project, method: InstallMethod, onFinished: (Result) -> Unit)` - requires `method.canRunDirectly`; builds a `GeneralCommandLine` from `method.upgradeCommand` split safely (no shell: `brew` + `upgrade` + `jj`; resolve the executable via the method's detected path list - `DetectableInstallMethod` already finds `brew` in SYSTEM_PATH/`/opt/homebrew/bin`: store the resolved `Path` on detection and reuse (GUI-launched IDEs on macOS often lack /opt/homebrew/bin on PATH - this is exactly why the path list exists)); environment: inherit + `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`? NO - default behaviour; but set `HOMEBREW_NO_ENV_HINTS=1`, `NO_COLOR=1`. Run under `ProgressManager.getInstance().run(Task.Backgroundable(project, "Updating jj...", cancellable = true))` with `CapturingProcessHandler`/`KillableProcessHandler`, streaming stdout/stderr lines to a small console: either the VCS Console (jj-idea-cdi's `JujutsuConsole`/platform `addMessageToConsoleWindow` - reuse if cdi landed; else a modal-less "Update jj" dialog with a `ConsoleView` (ConsoleViewImpl) created from `TextConsoleBuilderFactory`). Cancellation kills the process (ties to jj-idea-1a4c's registry); timeout 10 min.
2. After exit code 0: `project.jjAvailabilityStatus.invalidate()` (shared recheck, no restart needed), then show a balloon "jj updated to <new version>" (read from the refreshed status) or "Update finished but jj version is still X (is another jj earlier on PATH?)" when the version didn't change (common: two installs) with a link to Settings > JJ executable path. Failure: keep the console open with the error and offer Copy Command + Retry.
3. Non-canRunDirectly flow (phase 2): modal `UpgradeGuideDialog(method)`: title "Update jj via <method>", the command in a copyable monospace field (reuse `createCommandField`), steps text ("Run this in a terminal (it may ask for administrator rights), then click Check Again"), buttons [Copy Command] [Check Again] (= `jjAvailabilityStatus.invalidate()` then close on success with a balloon) [Close]. For `Unknown`/`Manual`: link to install docs (`InstallMethod.INSTALL_DOCS`) instead.
4. Entry points: (a) the nudge balloon's "Update jj..." -> `launchUpgradeFlow(project)` which picks the detected method (`InstallMethod` detection result used by Install Help: find the detection call, e.g. `InstallMethod.detected`/`allAvailable` at JujutsuConfigurable ~:856) and opens dialog or runner; (b) Settings Install Help rows: `commandRow` gets a "Run" button when `method.canRunDirectly` (next to Copy); for the detected-upgrade case also a prominent "Update now" button; (c) the existing "version too old" notification (notifyJjUnavailable, JujutsuNotifications.kt:269) action.
5. Safety: never run commands the user didn't see: show the exact command in a confirmation line in the dialog/task title ("Running: brew upgrade jj"); first run requires clicking the explicit button (no auto-run from the balloon without the dialog's confirm step: balloon action -> opens the dialog with a [Run] button). 
Decisions made without the user: Q: auto-run directly from the balloon? Rec no - opens the flow dialog with explicit Run. Q: support more methods as canRunDirectly (Scoop/Cargo don't need elevation)? Rec: Cargo (`cargo install --locked jj-cli`... long compile, skip), Scoop (`scoop update jj`) is safe but unverified - leave false until someone tests on Windows. Q: use VCS console vs own dialog console? Rec: reuse VCS console if cdi exists else a dialog.
Scale: none. Testing: runner tests with a fake executable (shell script) emitting output + exit codes (success/failure/cancel/missing binary) via an injectable `commandLineFactory`; recheck-called-once test; version-unchanged message test; guide dialog state tests; manual (macOS Homebrew): `brew install jj@old` then Update now -> output streams, status updates, nudge gone; Linux/apt: guide dialog; Windows: guide dialog; regression scope: MT-SETTINGS (Installation Help), MT-WORKINGCOPY (nudge balloon), MT-CROSS.
acceptance_criteria: Homebrew upgrade runs in-IDE with streamed output, cancel, and availability recheck; other methods get a guided copy-and-check-again dialog; nudge 'Update jj...' opens the flow with an explicit Run step; runner/dialog tests; MT rows.

title: Tri-state root filter with select-all/select-none header (GitHub #96)
description:
JonasKuhnEtu (GitHub #96, 2026-08-31) works with many repos in one IntelliJ window, most untouched, and wants to exclude a few roots from the log rather than having to select all-but-those. Proposed UX: cycle each root through unset -> included (only these shown) -> excluded (all shown except these). With a mix of included and excluded, included wins (only included shown); if the included set is later cleared back to empty, any excluded roots remain excluded.

Current single-state model: selectedRoots: Set<JujutsuRepository> in ui/log/JujutsuRootFilterComponent.kt, applied in JujutsuLogTable.setRootFilter() (ui/log/JujutsuLogTable.kt:990) as rootFilter.isEmpty() || rootFilter.contains(entry.repo) (JujutsuLogTable.kt:1074). Per-root UI is JujutsuRootFilterComponent.ToggleRootAction, a ToggleAction with a colored square icon. Selection persists via JujutsuRootFilterComponent.getSelectedRootPaths()/setSelectedRoots(), read/written by UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.kt:203 and :315 (config.selectedRootPaths).
design:
Keep the two-set model (includedRoots + excludedRoots), NOT a select-all/none replacement for it -- see rationale below. Filter predicate unchanged: if includedRoots is non-empty, show only those; else if excludedRoots is non-empty, show all but those; else show all. Replace ToggleRootAction (a ToggleAction, inherently 2-state) with a 3-state cycling action -- an AnAction whose actionPerformed advances unset->included->excluded->unset and whose update() paints a third icon state (filled/outline/crossed-out) for excluded.

Add a Gmail-style select-all/select-none header action above the per-root list in the popup (BackgroundActionGroup in createActionGroup()) as a genuine ergonomic addition, not a replacement for the excluded state: it cycles included-empty -> all roots included -> included-empty again, purely as a bulk-toggle convenience on top of the same includedRoots set. This does NOT replace the excluded state -- see rationale.

RATIONALE for keeping both include and exclude as first-class, persisted states (not simulating 'exclude 2 of 20' via 'include 18 of 20' plus a bulk select-all convenience): JujutsuStateModel already reacts live to VcsListener mapping changes (JujutsuStateModel.kt:463), so a repo added mid-session -- not just at settings-file-schema-evolution time -- is a real, routine scenario for someone managing many repos in one window (the reporter's own framing). The two models diverge exactly here:
- Included non-empty (user deliberately narrowed to a specific few) -> a newly-added repo defaults to HIDDEN, matching the standard allowlist idiom (e.g. IntelliJ's own Git Log branch/user filters: a newly-created branch isn't auto-included in an active branch filter).
- Included empty, some excluded (user is muting a couple of noisy repos) -> a newly-added repo defaults to SHOWN, matching the standard denylist/mute-list idiom (e.g. VCS ignored-files list: files not explicitly ignored are tracked by default; muting a Slack channel doesn't mute channels created afterward).
Simulating exclusion via 'select all but N' collapses to the allowlist case: a new repo silently lands outside the persisted included set and is hidden until the user remembers to add it -- the opposite of what a 'hide 2 noisy repos, show everything else' user expects, with no obvious visual cue that a repo exists but isn't shown. Keeping excludedRoots as a real, separate persisted set gets the correct default for each case for free, without adding a separate 'new-repo default' setting -- the two modes already encode user intent about future repos, so a dedicated setting would be solving a problem this design solves on its own.

Persistence: config gains a second field (e.g. excludedRootPaths) alongside selectedRootPaths; on load, an existing .idea/jujutsu.xml with only selectedRootPaths must degrade gracefully (empty/absent excludedRootPaths = no exclusions, unchanged existing behavior).
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a root cycles it unset -> included -> excluded -> unset; a header action bulk-selects/deselects all roots into the included set. With any root included, the log shows only included roots; with none included but some excluded, the log shows all but excluded. A repo added mid-session (live VcsListener mapping change) defaults to hidden when the included set is non-empty, and to shown when only exclusions are active -- covered by a test exercising both branches. The selection persists across restarts and old settings files without excludedRootPaths load without error.
notes: GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/96
close_reason: Shipped: tri-state root filter with select-all/select-none header

title: Status-bar working-copy widget chrome diverges from platform (GitHub #95)
description:
Separate from the width-cap bug (jj-idea-6nas), also on GitHub #95: JujutsuStatusBarWidget.WidgetPanel hand-rolls its hover/border/foreground instead of using the platform's status-bar widget tokens, so it looks inconsistent next to stock widgets.

Divergences (JujutsuStatusBarWidget.kt vs JBUI.CurrentTheme.StatusBar.Widget / platform TextPanel.kt):
- Hover fill: UIUtil.getPanelBackground().darker() vs Widget.HOVER_BACKGROUND. darker() is wrong-direction in a dark theme, where the platform hover goes lighter, and getPanelBackground() is the generic panel background, not StatusBar.BACKGROUND.
- Hover shape: fillRect(0, 0, width, height) edge-to-edge vs inset by StatusBar.hoverInsets().
- Border: JBUI.Borders.empty(0, 4) vs Widget.border() -- insets(6, 8) on New UI.
- Foreground: Swing default vs Widget.FOREGROUND / HOVER_FOREGROUND.
- Pressed state: not handled at all vs Widget.PRESSED_BACKGROUND / PRESSED_FOREGROUND.

User-supplied screenshots show no hover state, so the hover-fill divergence is not confirmed as the visible symptom; since WidgetPanel is isOpaque=false, the resting background is inherited and unlikely to be the cause. The resting-state candidates are the foreground colour and the tighter-than-platform border/padding. Aligning all of the above to platform tokens should resolve whichever it turns out to be, and stops relying on hand-picked colours that can drift from the theme.

Note: JujutsuBookmarkStatusBarWidget (ui/statusbar/JujutsuBookmarkStatusBarWidget.kt) contains a near-identical copy of WidgetPanel with the same divergences. It is the status-bar fallback for the main-toolbar bookmark widget (ui/toolbar/JujutsuBookmarkToolbarWidget.kt) -- a different, healthy-looking widget the user confirmed looks fine in a toolbar screenshot. That confirmation does not clear the status-bar fallback copy, which is out of scope here but should be fixed as a follow-up once this one is verified.
design: Replace the hand-rolled hover fill/shape/border/foreground in JujutsuStatusBarWidget's WidgetPanel with JBUI.CurrentTheme.StatusBar.Widget.HOVER_BACKGROUND (respecting hoverInsets()), Widget.border(), Widget.FOREGROUND/HOVER_FOREGROUND, and handle a pressed state via PRESSED_BACKGROUND/PRESSED_FOREGROUND to match platform TextPanel/status-bar widget behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Widget's resting and hovered appearance is verified against a stock platform status-bar widget in both a light and a dark theme; no hand-picked colours remain in WidgetPanel.
notes: GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/95. Follow-up (not in scope): JujutsuBookmarkStatusBarWidget has the same WidgetPanel divergences.
close_reason: Fixed both bottom status-bar widgets (JujutsuStatusBarWidget and JujutsuBookmarkStatusBarWidget, the deferred follow-up folded in): removed hand-rolled paintComponent hover overpaint, adopted JBUI.CurrentTheme.StatusBar.Widget.border()/FOREGROUND. Platform now paints hover/pressed via WidgetEffectRenderer.

title: Push by dragging a local bookmark onto its remote in the bookmarks panel
description: jj-idea-6oeg design doc section 7. Complements the log-only push bead (jj-idea-vdwh) for the case where the remote bookmark isn't visible as a log chip (e.g. outside the loaded revset) - drag a local bookmark node onto its BookmarkNode.Remote node in the bookmarks panel. MUST open the pre-filled GitPushDialog(initialBookmark, initialRemote), never push directly - same hard constraint as jj-idea-vdwh.

See docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md for batch scope, sequencing, and the preview-gating design. Find your batch's siblings with: bd list --label dnd-batch-N

title: Details panel as drag payload source for bookmark/tag chips
description: jj-idea-6oeg design doc section 1. The commit details panel renders via IconAwareHtmlPane (a JEditorPane subclass) which has its own built-in text-selection drag gesture. Making a bookmark/tag chip inside it draggable requires suppressing that pane's TransferHandler specifically for drags starting on a chip (hit-tested via viewToModel), while leaving normal text selection elsewhere in the pane untouched. The operation logic needs no new code - only this hit-test, since RefChip/BookmarkRef are already modeled.
acceptance_criteria: A bookmark or tag chip in the commit details panel can be dragged as a BookmarkRef/TagRef payload onto any valid drop target, without breaking normal text selection elsewhere in the panel.
notes:

See docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md for batch scope, sequencing, and the preview-gating design. Find your batch's siblings with: bd list --label dnd-batch-N

title: Bookmarks panel as drag payload source and drop target

The bookmarks panel (ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt) is a plain JTree beside the log table in a splitter, with leaves already typed as BookmarkNode.Local/.Remote/.Tag/.WorkingCopy. title: Copy-modifier drag to duplicate
description: Same gesture as the rebase-drop bead (jj-idea-6oeg design doc section 1/3) but held with the platform's copy modifier (DnDAction.COPY / Ctrl on most platforms) - calls duplicate(revisions, [target], mode) instead of rebase. Applies immediately with an undo balloon (duplicate is purely additive so this is low-risk even before full undo confidence, but keep the balloon for consistency).
design:
Small delta once jj-idea-8fxs lands - see 8fxs's design field for the full DnD performer plan,
which this mirrors. Researched 2026-09-04, not yet built.

WHAT 8fxs LEAVES READY
8fxs replaces the `((DropOperation) -> Boolean)?` performer seam with a two-method interface
(supports/perform) precisely so a copy-modifier drag rejects cleanly - with no indicator and no
tooltip - until this bead lands. resolveDropOperation already returns DropOperation.Duplicate for a
copy-modifier commit drag on all three zones, so the core needs no change. This bead flips exactly
one branch in each of supports() and perform().

1. SHARED DUPLICATE EXECUTOR - actions/change/duplicateOntoAction.kt
Mirror 8fxs's executeRebase extraction:

  internal fun executeDuplicate(
      project: Project, repo: JujutsuRepository,
      revisions: List<Revision>, destinations: List<Revision>, mode: RebaseDestinationMode
  )

with repo.commandExecutor.withUndoTracking() ... .withUndoBalloon(project, repo,
"log.action.duplicate.undo") ... .executeAsync(), and upgrade the current bare target.invalidate()
to repo.invalidate(vfsChanged = true) - no `select`, since jj duplicate mints a new change id we do
not know until after. duplicateOntoAction then calls it, which means the Duplicate Onto... dialog
also gains the undo balloon, consistent with the decision recorded on 8fxs (Kevin, 2026-09-03: one
shared wiring path, dialog gains undo).

Note CommandExecutor.duplicate (CommandExecutor.kt:231) has NO source-mode axis - only
(revisions, destinations, destinationMode). So the mapping is:
  revisions = sources.map { it.id }; destinations = listOf(destination.id); destinationMode = mode

2. BUNDLE
log.action.duplicate.undo=Duplicate (bare verb phrase - interpolated into
notification.undo.content={0} completed.). log.action.duplicate.error.* already exists.

3. TESTS
Extend DropPerformersTest (created by 8fxs): the Duplicate mapping for all three
RebaseDestinationModes and a multi-source drag; supports() now true for Duplicate too.

4. DOCS
docs/manual-tests.md MT-LOG-TABLE drag-and-drop subsection: 8fxs leaves a bullet asserting the
copy-modifier drag is REJECTED - flip it to assert it duplicates instead, for all three zones, with
the original left in place and an undo balloon. Manual regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE,
MT-CTXMENU (Duplicate Onto... gains the balloon), MT-LOG-REFRESH, MT-WORKINGCOPY.

SCALE: no new traversal or per-commit loop; O(s) in dragged selection size, once per drop.
acceptance_criteria: Holding the copy modifier while dragging a commit runs duplicate instead of rebase, for all three zone positions.
notes:
Depends on jj-idea-6jvh and jj-idea-v9zp. Small delta once the rebase-drop bead exists - same hit-test, different CommandExecutor call keyed off DnDActionInfo.isCopy().
See docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md for batch scope, sequencing, and the preview-gating design. Find your batch's siblings with: bd list --label dnd-batch-N
close_reason: Shipped batch 2: chip payloads (move bookmark/tag onto a commit, local-onto-remote push dialog) and copy-modifier duplicate, all wired through DropPerformers.forLogTable

title: Operation log UI (jj op log browser with per-entry revert)
description: Stage 3 of the undo mini-roadmap (docs/design/undo-support-roadmap.md) - the ROADMAP.md item 'Operation Log & Undo'. Parse jj op log into an OperationEntry (id, description, timestamp, user, tags, parents) and present it as a browsable list. Default per-entry action is 'Revert this operation' (jj op revert <id>), NOT 'Restore to here' (jj op restore <id>) - restore is a reset that can discard work landed after the target point, revert undoes exactly one entry safely. Offer restore only as an explicit, clearly-labelled secondary action. Model the UI on IntelliJ's own Local History.
design:
PLAN: Stage 3 of docs/design/undo-support-roadmap.md - an Operation Log browser modelled on IntelliJ's Local History, default action Revert. (Also covers jj-idea-rau3 "add op log" - recommend closing rau3 as duplicate.)
Existing plumbing: `CommandExecutor.opLog(limit, template)` (CommandExecutor.kt:639) and `opRevert(id, what)` (:648); `OperationId` type; undo service/balloon (ui/services/JujutsuUndoService.kt, performUndo); a tool-window tab pattern from file history (ui/history/JujutsuFileHistoryTabManager.kt) and the log's CommitTablePanel base.
Design:
1. Parse model - ALREADY EXISTS: `OperationEntry` (jj/OperationEntry? imported by jj/cli/OpLogParser.kt) with `OP_LOG_TEMPLATE` and `parseOpLog(stdout)` (jj/cli/OpLogParser.kt: NUL-separated fields id, parents, description, start time, user, `snapshot` flag, `root` flag, `tags` (raw argv); built for undo-token matching (`findTaggedOperation`, used at CliExecutor.kt:~1155) and verified on 0.37-0.44 per its KDoc). So no new parser: add a service method `CommandExecutor.opLog(limit, template = OP_LOG_TEMPLATE)` consumer `OpLogService.load(repo, limit)` returning `List<OperationEntry>` (paging by growing `-n`, cache by head id). The `snapshot` flag is exactly what the "hide snapshot ops" filter below needs (no description-string matching). Missing from the entry model: end time/host - add only if the UI needs them (verify `time.end()` keyword at 0.37).
2. UI: tab "Operations" in the Jujutsu tool window (new `JujutsuOperationLogPanel`, list/table: time (relative + absolute tooltip), user, description, tags (e.g. "args: jj rebase ..." from `tags().get("args")`) with row actions: primary = "Revert This Operation" (`jj op revert <id>`, REVERSIBLE-class? an op revert is an operation - classify IRREVERSIBLE (no balloon-on-balloon), but refresh state), secondary (separated, clearly labelled, confirm dialog) = "Restore Repository to This Point" (`jj op restore <id>`) with a warning listing that later operations' effects are discarded. Selection shows details: full description, the op's parents, and "View repo at this operation" (read-only `--at-op` log) as a v2 follow-up. Search/filter by description text (reuse LogFilterMatcher).
3. Multi-repo: repo selector (like fetch dialog) - one op log per repo; default = repo of current selection.
4. Auto-refresh: re-query on `stateModel` op-change notifications (same funnel as log refresh) - cheap `-n1` head probe to decide whether to reload (avoid reparsing 100 ops on each refresh): compare head id.
5. Relationship: Revert from this UI must also reconcile `JujutsuUndoService` records (`clearIfCurrent`) and invalidate with `vfsChanged = true`; actions Undo/Redo from jj-idea-x30x reuse `OperationInfo` (share the parser: x30x's head-op read model becomes a view over this service - implement x30x first with `limit=3`, aii0 extends).
6. Local-History model details to mirror: grouped by day separators ("Today", "Yesterday"), "Show system operations" toggle to hide snapshot noise: jj records an operation per working-copy snapshot ("snapshot working copy") which dominates the log; default HIDE ops whose description starts with "snapshot working copy" (and `jj` internal `reconcile divergent operations`) with a toggle - pure UI filter, documented.
Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Hide snapshot ops by default? Rec yes (Local History-style signal-to-noise); toggle to show. Reverse: default show.
2. Q: Where does it live - tool window tab vs dialog? Rec: tool window tab (persistent, refreshes live). Reverse: dialog from VCS menu.
3. Q: Restore secondary action included in v1? Rec: yes but behind a confirm dialog, visually separated; matches roadmap doc.
4. rau3: close as duplicate of this bead (user confirms).
Scale: ops parsed O(limit) once per head change (limit 100 default, growth on demand); render O(limit) rows; no per-op subprocess (all fields from one template). Operation-count test: opening = 1 call; head unchanged refresh = 1 `-n1` call and 0 reparse; load more = 1 call.
Testing: parser tests (captured op log: multi-line descriptions, tags, merge ops with 2 parents (concurrent ops)); contract test: perform ops, revert one, assert list + effect; filter-hide-snapshot test; confirm dialog test for restore; manual: new MT-OPLOG section (list, revert, restore confirm, hide-snapshots toggle, external terminal op appears after refresh); regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY (state invalidation), MT-LOG-REFRESH.
acceptance_criteria: A UI lists operations from jj op log with description/timestamp/user. Each entry offers Revert as the primary action; Restore exists only as a secondary, clearly distinguished action.
notes: Depends on jj-idea-v9zp.

title: First-class Undo/Redo actions naming the operation
description: Stage 2 of the undo mini-roadmap (docs/design/undo-support-roadmap.md). Register Jujutsu.Undo/Jujutsu.Redo actions (jj undo / jj redo) in the VCS menu and log toolbar. The presentation must read the head operation's description from jj op log and show it in the action text - a blind 'Undo' on a whole repository is unnerving. Disable with a reason when the head op isn't undoable. Explicitly do NOT bind to Cmd+Z/Shift+Cmd+Z by default (see the roadmap doc's dedicated section on why) - leave rebindable via Keymap, or use a distinct chord such as Cmd+Alt+Z.
design:
PLAN: Stage 2 of docs/design/undo-support-roadmap.md - first-class `Jujutsu.Undo`/`Jujutsu.Redo` backed by `jj undo`/`jj redo`, naming the target operation. (Also the plan for the duplicate jj-idea-a4eh "Undo/redo operations".)
What exists: `Jujutsu.UndoLastOperation` (actions/undo/UndoLastOperationAction.kt, registered plugin.xml:169, in the VCS menu :203) reverts only operations the plugin itself issued (token-identified via `JujutsuUndoService.Record`, ui/services/JujutsuUndoService.kt) using `jj op revert` (CommandExecutor.opRevert :648); `opLog(limit, template)` (:639) exists for reading the op log. Not covered: terminal-originated operations, redo, chained undo/redo.
Design:
1. Executor: `CommandExecutor.undo(): CommandResult` (`jj undo`), `redo()` (`jj redo`) - args builders `undoArgs()/redoArgs()` in CliExecutor.kt. Reversibility class: these ARE operations, but undo of an undo is redo: classify IRREVERSIBLE (no undo balloon on top of an undo; the user has the Redo action) to avoid balloon recursion.
2. Head-op read model: reuse the EXISTING op-log parsing - `OP_LOG_TEMPLATE`/`parseOpLog` -> `OperationEntry(id, parents, description, start, user, snapshot, root, tags)` (jj/cli/OpLogParser.kt, used by undo-token matching). Add `JujutsuOperationService` (project service) holding per-repo `headOperations: List<OperationEntry>` (limit 5) invalidated on every op change like gitRemotes (JujutsuStateModel funnel); the presented target = the operation `jj undo` will actually undo. NOTE the `snapshot` flag: jj snapshots the working copy as its own operation, so the head may be a snapshot op - skip snapshot ops when choosing the label (same exclusion `findTaggedOperation` makes). Semantics check (contract test, required): sequence A, B, undo, undo, redo - assert at each step which operation `jj undo` targets and that the label computed from op log (skipping snapshots, accounting for undo-marker ops - `tags`/description "undo operation <id>") equals it; if the rule is not derivable reliably from op log text, label from `jj undo --help` semantics: undo targets the "current operation" = op log head after skipping already-undone chain; fall back to a generic label "Undo last operation" with the head description in the tooltip rather than a wrong name.
3. Actions (actions/undo/): `UndoAction` text "Undo <description>" (e.g. "Undo 'describe commit a1b2c3...'"), `RedoAction` text "Redo <description>"; update(): disabled with reason when no previous op / nothing to redo (jj redo errors when there's nothing: read `jj op log` for undo-markers; disabled description "Nothing to redo"); multi-repo: act on the repo of the current context (log selection/working copy panel binding, `e.repoForFile`/panel repo), else disable with "Select a repository" (UndoLastOperationAction treats ambiguity as disabled - same convention).
4. Placement: VCS menu group next to UndoLastOperation (plugin.xml:203), log toolbar overflow (not primary), Working Copy panel context. Keymap: registered ids so users can bind; NO default Cmd+Z/Shift+Cmd+Z (roadmap doc "On Cmd+Z" section); suggested default chord Cmd+Alt+Z? Rec: none by default (conflicts risk) - leave to keymap.
5. Safety: undoing something that did NOT come from the IDE can drop work in progress made by another process (e.g. a terminal edit); `jj undo` restores the whole repo state of the previous op, including working-copy commit pointer; files on disk are updated -> show a confirmation the first time per session? Rec: a confirm dialog naming the operation and its time ("Undo 'rebase 3 commits' from 12:03? This restores the repository to the state before it.") with "Don't ask again" - this is the explicit blind-undo protection the bead requires, stronger than a bare menu item. Reverse: remove dialog.
6. After success: `repo.invalidate(vfsChanged = true)`; reconcile `JujutsuUndoService` (clear its record if it referred to the undone op: `clearIfCurrent`).
7. Relationship with UndoLastOperation: keep both (different semantics: revert-ours vs jj undo); in the VCS menu group show UndoLastOperation first when a record exists, else hide it? Rec: keep as is (disabled when nothing); document the difference in the actions' descriptions. Consider consolidating after aii0 (op log UI) ships.
Decisions made without the user: Q: confirm dialog? Rec yes (default on, dismissible). Q: Dup a4eh: recommend closing a4eh as duplicate of this bead (and rau3 as duplicate of aii0). Q: default shortcut? Rec none.
Scale: one `jj op log -n3` per op change per repo (cached, same invalidation funnel); no loops.
Testing: args tests; presentation function tests (pure, like resolveUndoLastOperationPresentation); contract test A,B,undo,undo,redo label/behaviour; confirm-dialog test; manual: MT-CTXMENU/VCS menu rows (terminal `jj describe` then IDE Undo names it and reverts, Redo restores) - new MT-UNDO section recommended; regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY (invalidate), MT-CTXMENU.
acceptance_criteria: Jujutsu.Undo and Jujutsu.Redo actions exist, are visible in VCS menu and log toolbar, show the target operation's description, and are not bound to the editor undo chord by default.
notes: Depends on jj-idea-v9zp (opLog/opRevert plumbing). Partly pre-satisfied: v9zp shipped Jujutsu.UndoLastOperation, a persistent VCS-menu action that already names the operation it targets (per this issue's own presentation requirement) and is not bound to Cmd+Z. What remains here is genuinely additional: Jujutsu.Redo (jj redo exists, verified as a real top-level jj command), a jj-undo-backed action for undoing something that did NOT originate from an in-IDE gesture (UndoLastOperation only ever reverts operations the plugin itself issued and identified by token, by design - it structurally cannot reach a bare terminal jj command), and repeated undo/redo chaining. See docs/design/undo-support-roadmap.md's Stage 2 section (updated) for the full rescoping.

title: Expose JujutsuChangesTree selection as VIRTUAL_FILE/VIRTUAL_FILE_ARRAY for working-copy trees
description: JujutsuChangesTree never published CommonDataKeys.VIRTUAL_FILE/VIRTUAL_FILE_ARRAY, so IntelliJ's globally-bound file actions (Reformat Code, Optimize Imports) had nothing to act on in the Working Copy tool window. GitHub PR #94 (sindrenm) proposed publishing them unconditionally, but JujutsuChangesTree is shared by four surfaces (working copy panel, commit details pane, compare-changes panel, file-selection dialog) and in historical ones a change's local file is not the revision on screen - publishing there would misdirect platform actions and, via Project.filesFor()'s fileList-wins precedence, break 'Open File' on historical commits. Implemented instead: JujutsuChangesTree.showsLocalFiles gates the two keys (true for the Working Copy panel and for the commit details pane when the selected entry is the working copy @), published lazily via sink.lazy(...) mirroring the platform's own ChangesListView.uiDataSnapshot.
design: Gate on LogEntry.isWorkingCopy via a new JujutsuChangesTree.showsLocalFiles: () -> Boolean property (default false), not a CurrentContentRevision check - the commit details pane builds change-id-based ContentLogEntryImpl revisions even for @, so CurrentContentRevision would never match there. Does NOT publish NAVIGATABLE/NAVIGATABLE_ARRAY (F4/Jump to Source): Jujutsu.OpenChangeFile already owns F4 in this tree via plugin.xml and works in every context already; adding the platform's generic Jump to Source too would create a same-keystroke conflict rather than add value.
acceptance_criteria: Reformat Code and Optimize Imports act on a Working Copy tool window file selection and on a commit-details-pane selection when @ is shown; neither fires (or falls back to the editor's file) for a historical commit selection; ShowFileHistoryAction and Project.filesFor() correctly disambiguate multi-file tree selections from the new VIRTUAL_FILE key (regression found and fixed during this work).
close_reason: Implemented: JujutsuChangesTree.showsLocalFiles gates VIRTUAL_FILE/VIRTUAL_FILE_ARRAY, wired for UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel and JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel (@ only); tests added/passing

title: Local bookmark ahead of its remote never shows a divergence indicator
description:
Originally filed as "the bookmarks panel doesn't render aheadCount/behindCount on tree leaves" - that premise turned out to be wrong: leaves already render them via appendBookmarkChip (ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:129-141), which the panel's renderer calls directly (ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt).

The real gap is upstream, in the CLI template: CliLogService.bookmarkListTemplate (jj/cli/CliLogService.kt:500-535) computes tracking_ahead_count/tracking_behind_count only 'if(remote && tracked, ..., "0")'. A local bookmark ahead of its remote therefore always carries aheadCount=0/behindCount=0 from the plugin's point of view, so the panel (and anything else reading Bookmark.aheadCount) never shows a divergence indicator for it, even though it's fully able to render one.

This is the same gap as the first bullet in GitHub #110's report (cYDN48): "Local bookmark ahead of remote... could be done with an upward-pointing arrow." They also suggested an expanded multi-remote form, e.g. for a bookmark tracking two remotes with different divergence per remote: master @origin1 (ahead 2) @origin2 (ahead 5).

Fix: fetch/derive ahead/behind counts for the local side too (not only when remote && tracked), and extend the multi-remote case per the reporter's suggested notation.
acceptance_criteria: A local bookmark ahead of (or behind) its remote shows the same ↑n↓m indicator the panel already draws for remote bookmarks. With more than one remote, the indicator distinguishes counts per remote.
notes:
Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/110 (first bullet: 'Local bookmark ahead of remote').

2026-09-13: unrelated to this bead's own fix, but flagging for context - the CHANGELOG had
mis-credited two other #48 follow-ups to release v0.8.15 (they were committed ~3 hours after the
v0.8.15 tag/publish and are actually unreleased); corrected in CHANGELOG.md. Doesn't change this
bead's scope.
close_reason: Fixed core case: Bookmark.withDivergenceFrom (jj/Revset.kt) derives a local bookmark's ahead/behind from its tracked remote-tracking rows (swapped, since jj reports tracking_ahead/behind_count from the remote's perspective), applied once per repo in BookmarkTreeModel.buildRepoNodes. Multi-remote takes max not sum (documented placeholder); log-table chips and true per-remote notation are out of scope, tracked as a follow-up.

title: Bookmarks panel: settings gear for grouping toggles
description:
jj-idea-b2ae's bookmarks panel (ui/log/bookmarks/) always groups by repository and by '/' prefix. git4idea's Branches dashboard makes both independently toggleable via a settings gear action. Add the same toggles here once there's demand, keeping the current behaviour (both on) as the default.

Also include, per jj-idea-3sac's design field (jj-idea-d65h spike): a "Show the git remote" toggle, off by default, as the escape hatch for jj-idea-j0zv's unconditional hiding of the reserved `git` pseudo-remote category. No separate settings bead needed for that.
design:
PLAN: a settings gear in the Bookmarks panel toolbar with three independent toggles: Group by repository, Group by '/' prefix, Show the git remote - defaults preserve today's behaviour (both groupings on; git pseudo-remote hidden).
Facts: panel toolbar built in `JujutsuBookmarksPanel.createToolbar()` (ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:163-181: `DefaultActionGroup` with Expand All/Collapse All; target `tree`); tree built by `buildBookmarkTree(references, workingCopies, closestBookmarks, danglingHeads)` (BookmarkTreeModel.kt:217): repo grouping = `if (repos.size > 1) RepoGroup per repo else flat` (:~230-236), prefix grouping = `buildPrefixTree(repo, leaves, RefKind, label)` (:~299, :328, :344) splitting names on '/', and the git pseudo-remote filter `.filter { it != GIT_PSEUDO_REMOTE }` (:~315) whose comment names this bead as its escape hatch ("An escape hatch to still show it lives in jj-idea-k5d7's settings gear"). Rebuild path: `rebuild()` (:~187) is triggered by `queueRebuild()`; per-window UI state lives in `LogWindowConfig` (already holds `bookmarksPanelVisible`; written back via `JujutsuSettings.upsertLogWindow`) and application-level display flags in `JujutsuApplicationSettings` (e.g. `showBookmarkDivergence`, LogEntryText.kt:131).
Design:
1. State: three booleans in `LogWindowConfig` (per window, since panel visibility is per window): `bookmarksGroupByRepo: Boolean = true`, `bookmarksGroupByPrefix: Boolean = true`, `bookmarksShowGitRemote: Boolean = false`; persisted via the existing xmlb bean (round-trip guard in jj-idea-ajd0 will cover them); the panel gets them through its existing config reference (see how `bookmarksPanelVisible` is read/written).
2. Builder options: `buildBookmarkTree(..., options: BookmarkTreeOptions(groupByRepo, groupByPrefix, showGitRemote))` with defaults = current behaviour so existing call sites/tests are unchanged: (a) `groupByRepo=false` with multiple repos -> flatten all repos' categories into one tree?? Ambiguous: with several repos, flattening mixes same-named bookmarks; Rec: when off and >1 repos, prefix every Category label with the repo name ("Local (repoA)") - OR keep RepoGroup when >1 repos regardless (the toggle only matters for single repo, where it is already flat)! git4idea's toggle "Group by repository" is meaningful for multi-root only. Rec: honour it for multi-repo by flattening with repo-name suffix; no effect (and greyed-out in the gear) for single-repo projects. (b) `groupByPrefix=false` -> `buildPrefixTree` replaced by a flat leaf list (leaves keep full names). (c) `showGitRemote=true` -> don't filter GIT_PSEUDO_REMOTE (a "git" Category appears like other remotes).
3. UI: gear = `DefaultActionGroup` popup action (`AllIcons.General.GearPlain`, `isPopup = true`) with three `ToggleAction`s (text via bundle: `bookmarks.panel.group.repo`, `...group.prefix`, `...show.git.remote`); toggling writes the config, then `queueRebuild()`. Expanded/collapsed state: rebuild ends with `TreeUtil.expandAll` per the spike finding (state wiped on rebuild) - toggling a grouping changes structure so default expansion is acceptable.
4. Interaction with the panel's other consumers: DnD targets, filters (reference filter uses names - unaffected), `BOOKMARK_TARGET` data keys derive from leaf nodes - unaffected by grouping; `selectedLeaves()` must still work in flat mode.
Decisions made without the user: Q: per-window vs global? Rec per-window (matches panel visibility). Q: repo toggle behaviour (flatten with suffix)? Rec above; alternatively drop the repo toggle entirely if confusing - say so. Q: more toggles (show tags/dangling heads)? Rec not now.
Scale: toggles only change tree construction (O(#bookmarks) as today; flat mode is cheaper). Operation-count: building with options doesn't add jj calls (data from state model).
Testing: `BookmarkTreeModelTest` additions per option (single/multi repo x flags; names with '/', git remote visible/hidden; leaves identical in all modes); settings round-trip; toggle action tests (state flips -> rebuild queued); manual: MT-BOOKMARK (gear popup: each toggle changes the tree immediately and persists across restart; multi-root project; colocated repo with Show git remote). Regression scope: MT-BOOKMARK, MT-SETTINGS (persistence), MT-DND (bookmarks panel DnD uses leaf nodes).
acceptance_criteria: Gear popup with Group by repository / Group by prefix / Show git remote toggles (defaults unchanged), persisted per log window, tree rebuilds immediately; builder options with unchanged defaults; tests + MT-BOOKMARK rows.

title: Show effective diff base (resolved revision) live in settings
description: Add a live status line in Settings > Version Control > Jujutsu > Diff Base showing the actual revision each strategy currently resolves to (e.g. 'Effective diff base: qpwrqnxk'), updating as the user changes strategy/revset selection. Promotes the existing Test-button machinery (DiffbaseService.resolve / testDiffbaseRevset) into a persistent status line rather than an on-demand check. Per-repo output needed in multi-repo projects. Follow-up from jj-idea-fwea's settings-page width cleanup (contextHelp/comment now carry the raw revset text; this would show the resolved commit instead of/alongside it).
design:
PLAN: live "Effective diff base" status line in Settings > Version Control > Jujutsu > Diff Base, one per repo.
