Facts: `DiffbaseService.resolve(repo)` (vcs/diffbase/DiffbaseService.kt:~85) reads SAVED settings (`settings.diffbaseStrategy(repo)` / `customDiffbaseRevset(repo)`), caches per repo, and returns a `ChangeId?` (null = default `@-`, or failed/ambiguous); the revset for a strategy is `strategy.revset(customRevset)` (settings/DiffbaseStrategy). The Settings page (settings/JujutsuConfigurable.kt:317 `group(settings.group.diffbase)`) has radio buttons per strategy, a custom-revset field with a Test button (`testDiffbaseRevset()` :1168 -> `runRevsetTest(repo, revset)` per repo, honouring per-repo override panels `RepoSettingsPanel.diffbaseOverrideCb/diffbaseCombo/diffbaseRevsetField` :123-126) and a validation label.
KEY POINT: the live line must reflect the UNSAVED form state, so it cannot call `resolve(repo)` (saved settings + cache). It must compute the revset from the pending UI selection and evaluate it with the same single-revision check `resolveExactlyOne(repo, revset)` the service uses (already a public top-level function, vcs/diffbase/DiffbaseService.kt:165, returning `ResolveResult.Single(id)/None/Ambiguous(count)`, parameterised by revset, no caching, also used by SetDiffbaseAction - extend `Single` to optionally carry the description first line, or add a sibling `describeExactlyOne` for the line's extra text) - one implementation, so settings preview and runtime can't disagree (the service KDoc's stated goal).
Design:
1. New label row under the strategy radios: "Effective diff base: <short change id> <first description line>" or states: "@- (default)" for WORKING_COPY_PARENT when it resolves, "not found" / "ambiguous (N revisions)" with the error colour (reuse `showRevsetResult(label, ok, text)` helper used by the Test button - the Test button then becomes redundant for display but stays as an explicit retry/validation; keep it).
2. Per repo: single-repo projects show one line; multi-repo shows a line per repo inside each repo's collapsible group (the per-repo override panels exist at :123-126) plus the global line labelled "Default:". Avoid listing every repo in the global area.
3. Triggers: radio/combo selection change, custom revset text change (debounced 400ms; reuse the same debounce helper the log revset field uses, or `Alarm`/`MergingUpdateQueue` with the dialog's modality), panel open, and after Apply (service cache invalidated -> re-evaluate). Evaluation runs on a pooled thread via `runInBackground`; each trigger cancels/ignores stale results (token compare) so a slow jj can't overwrite a newer selection's result. While loading show "..." (not blank, to avoid layout jump).
4. Content: shorten with `ChangeId.short` + bookmark names if cheap? Rec: `short id` + first line of description from the same `jj log -r <revset> -T` call (one call: `-T 'change_id.shortest() ++ "\0" ++ description.first_line()' --limit 2` to also detect ambiguity: the existing `resolveExactlyOne` uses a similar limited query - reuse/extend it to return the description).
5. Do not show for strategies that cannot differ from `@-` without a repo state? Show always; PREVIOUS_COMMIT and IMMUTABLE_ANCESTOR resolve against current repo state and may change after operations - the line is a snapshot at evaluation time; add a small tooltip "As of now; changes as the log changes" (no polling).
Decisions made without the user: Q: replace the Test button? Rec: keep (explicit error text for invalid revsets) - the live line shows the resolved outcome, Test shows the jj error message. Q: Show also in log table (a4i5)? Separate bead; this bead's `resolveExactlyOne(revset)` refactor is the shared helper.
Scale: <= one `jj log --limit 2` per repo per (debounced) edit; multi-root with 20 repos = 20 short calls on pooled threads at panel open - cap concurrency (sequential per panel, lazily for collapsed per-repo groups: evaluate a repo's line only when its group is expanded).
Testing: unit - revset-from-pending-state function (strategy x custom text -> revset, incl. blank custom = invalid state message without calling jj); stale-result discarding test with a controllable fake evaluator; platform test of the settings panel (existing `JujutsuConfigurable` test seams like showEffectiveIdentityForTest, :143-146) asserting the line text after selecting each strategy using a stub resolver. Manual: MT-SETTINGS (Diff Base group: switch strategies and watch the line; invalid revset; ambiguous revset; multi-repo override), MT-DIFFBASE. Regression scope: MT-SETTINGS, MT-DIFFBASE.
acceptance_criteria: Settings Diff Base group shows the live resolved revision (short id + description) per repo for the unsaved selection, with none/ambiguous states; stale async results discarded; shares resolveExactlyOne with DiffbaseService; tests + MT-SETTINGS rows.

title: Run stubTest (and contractTest) in CI
description: Two registered Gradle test tasks never run in CI: stubTest (build.gradle.kts:402, JUnit tag 'stub') needs no jj binary and can be added to the check task / compatibility matrix with no new infra. contractTest (build.gradle.kts:368, JUnit tag 'contract') shells out to a real jj CLI, deliberately excluded from check; running it in CI needs a jj install step on the runner and a decision on which jj version(s) to pin/matrix. tasks.check currently only depends on test, platformTest, ktlintCheck (build.gradle.kts:436); .github/workflows/build.yml only runs compileKotlin test, platformTest, verifyPlugin, ktlintCheck (lines 109, 118). Originates from stale GitLab issue #43 ('Run a fuller suite of tests in the workflow').
design: stubTest: cheap win, add to tasks.check and/or the CI compatibility-matrix job directly. contractTest: needs jj installed on the runner; decide pin-one-version vs matrix before wiring in.
acceptance_criteria: stubTest runs in the GitHub Actions workflow (either as part of check or its own step) on every PR. A decision is recorded (design doc or bead notes) on whether/how contractTest runs in CI, and if yes it runs there too.
notes: Related but distinct from open beads jj-idea-j0hs and jj-idea-pcp8, which add contract-test coverage but don't address CI execution.

title: Settings identity ignores jj scoped config overrides (GitHub #89)
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/89

CaptaiNiveau uses jj's [[--scope]] --when.repositories to set a different user.name/user.email per directory (e.g. work vs personal). What actually breaks:

- The global identity section of the settings page reads and writes through rootlessConfig (settings/JujutsuConfigurable.kt:489 and :518), which is built on CliExecutor.forRootlessOperations (jj/cli/Config.kt:49-54) — jj runs with no repo cwd, so --when.repositories scopes never match. The page therefore shows (and offers to overwrite) the unscoped [user] values while commits in that repo actually use the scoped ones.
- The per-repo path is already correct: JjUserConfigChecker uses repo.config.effective (setup/JjUserConfigChecker.kt:13), which resolves scopes because jj runs inside the repo.

Fix direction: show the effective identity for the selected repository and label the scope it came from; suppress the 'set your identity' prompt when a scope already supplies one.

Latent oddity found nearby, not to fix here: Config.ScopedConfigImpl.set with a null scope silently writes to REPO scope (jj/cli/Config.kt:36-42).
acceptance_criteria: Settings page shows the identity actually in effect for the selected repository (including scope-derived values) and does not prompt to set an identity that a scope already supplies.
notes: Reported by CaptaiNiveau 2026-08-26.
close_reason: Fixed: settings page now shows repo-effective identity (incl. scoped values) with source file; rootless executor no longer inherits IDE's CWD; JjUserConfigChecker's already-correct scope handling now has regression coverage

title: Periodic automatic jj git fetch, with optional auto-rebase (GitHub #90)
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/90

CaptaiNiveau requests auto-fetch (as VisualJJ has), optionally followed by auto-rebase. They're split on wanting auto-rebase themselves.

Reuse rather than build: GitFetchAction.performFetch / GitFetchDialog.GitFetchSpec (src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/actions/git/GitFetchAction.kt) already do the fetch and notification; the periodic-trigger pattern exists as the pooled-thread Alarm in jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt:284-320. Needs a settings entry (interval, on/off, and whether auto-rebase follows) in settings/JujutsuConfigurable.kt.

Ship auto-fetch first, default off; treat auto-rebase as a separate opt-in on top since running it silently mid-edit is a much bigger surprise to undo. Overlaps SergejSalnikov's 'jj sync' toolbar-action ask on GitHub #68 — a built-in auto-fetch action may partially satisfy that even before an extensibility SPI exists.
design:
PLAN (GitHub #90): auto-fetch first, default OFF; auto-rebase as a separate later opt-in. Built on the poller primitive from jj-idea-j2vl (coordinate: crik's loop is "action on a schedule", which j2vl lists as consumer #2).
Facts: manual fetch = `performFetch(spec, project)` (actions/git/gitRemoteActions.kt:~31; `GitFetchDialog.GitFetchSpec(repos, remote, allRemotes)`; used from GitFetchAction.kt:46 with `remote = null`), a notification on completion and `invalidate` after. The bead cites `JujutsuStateModel.kt:284-320` pooled-thread Alarm as the periodic pattern; j2vl supersedes that with a proper cancellable scheduled primitive.
Design (v1 = auto-fetch):
1. Settings: project-level `autoFetchIntervalMinutes: Int` (0 = off, default 0; allowed 1-120; clamp), exposed in Settings > Version Control > Jujutsu (group "Remotes": checkbox "Fetch from remotes automatically" + interval spinner "every N minutes" + "Fetch only when the IDE window is active" default on). Per-repo override is overkill v1.
2. Scheduling: register one poller entry per repo with interval = N minutes (JjPoller from j2vl: `register(key, interval, probe = { runFetch(repo) ; headOpId(repo) }, onChange = refresh)`). If j2vl isn't merged when this starts, implement the minimal coroutine loop locally behind the same interface and swap later - but prefer sequencing: j2vl first (P3 both).
3. What it runs: `repo.commandExecutor.gitFetch(remote = null, allRemotes = false)` = default remotes per jj config (matches the manual Fetch default and respects `remotes.<name>.fetch-*`); on a multi-remote repo `allRemotes=false` fetches the default `origin`; add a setting "Fetch all remotes" (default off). Errors: network failure must NOT spam: exponential backoff (j2vl's backoff), one INFO log, and show a notification only on the FIRST failure after a success ("Automatic fetch failed: <message>", with "Disable automatic fetch" action) - never a modal.
4. Concurrency/safety: skip when another jj write is in flight for the repo (take the same lock/queue the executor uses? `jj git fetch` takes jj's own lock; but avoid colliding with a user-triggered operation by checking `JujutsuStateModel` busy flag if one exists; else rely on jj locking and ignore lock errors quietly). Skip while the repo is stale (RepositoryHealth) or jj unavailable.
5. Visibility: after a fetch that changed anything (compare op head before/after - `fetch` creates an operation only when refs changed; "Nothing changed." output) show a quiet balloon only if remote bookmarks moved? Rec: no balloon on success (silent refresh of the log and bookmarks panel via `invalidate`); status text "Last fetched <time>" in the Fetch action tooltip or the status bar widget (nice-to-have, tracked as follow-up). Optional: balloon "N bookmarks updated" disabled by default.
6. Auto-rebase is NOT part of this bead (recommendation, needs your call): there is no single obviously-safe revset. `jj rebase -b @ -d 'trunk()'` would move the active working-copy stack silently under an in-progress edit (the bead's own warning), and rebasing "all local stacks" needs a source revset that excludes work the user doesn't want touched. If wanted, create jj-idea-crik.2 with these constraints: opt-in per repo; destination = configurable revset, default `trunk()`; source = configurable revset, default `mutable() & ::bookmarks() ~ ::trunk()` evaluated per fetch (stacks that carry a local bookmark - the user's published work - and exclude the working copy unless it is empty and undescribed); run via the undo-tracked command so the balloon offers Undo; conflicts are first-class in jj so a conflicted rebase is recoverable, but show a balloon naming the count of conflicted commits. Because that needs your design review, the first PR covers fetch only.
Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Auto-rebase in this bead? Rec: no, separate (the bead itself says treat it as a separate opt-in; spec details need your call).
2. Q: Default interval when enabling? Rec 10 minutes (VisualJJ-like order of magnitude; each fetch is a network call).
3. Q: Only when IDE is active? Rec yes (default).
Scale: 1 `jj git fetch` per repo per N minutes (>= 1 min => <= 1 proc/min/repo), no loops over commits; multi-root: staggered start offsets and max 2 concurrent fetches (j2vl cap). Operation-count test (virtual time): 3 repos, 60 min, interval 10 => <= 18 fetches; paused when inactive => 0; failure => backoff.
Testing: poller wiring tests with fake executor/clock; settings tests (round trip, clamp); failure-notification dedupe test; contract test with local bare remote (fetch picks up a pushed commit; "Nothing changed" path); manual: MT-GIT (set 1 minute, push from another clone, watch the log update; disconnect network - single failure notice; disable stops fetching), MT-SETTINGS. Regression scope: MT-GIT, MT-SETTINGS, MT-LOG-REFRESH.
acceptance_criteria: A settings option enables periodic jj git fetch on a configurable interval, off by default; a separate opt-in setting can follow it with an automatic rebase.
notes: Cross-ref jj-idea-66id (#68 'jj sync' toolbar ask).

title: Change-id run has variable width, so log descriptions don't line up (GitHub #91)
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/91

CaptaiNiveau reports that commit-message alignment breaks in the log panel because change ids of different lengths push descriptions to different start positions.

Root cause, confirmed by reading the code:
- LaidOutCell.forRow (src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui/log/LaidOutCell.kt:93) appends entry.id then a single " ", then the description — all one free-flowing run in one cell, with no column boundary or padding between id and description.
- ShortenableImpl.displayRemainder (src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/jj/ShortenableId.kt) pads to 8 characters, not 8 pixels-worth — and TextCanvas.append(shortenable) (ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:26-29) paints the unique prefix bold at normal size and the remainder smaller and grey, so two ids with different unique-prefix lengths occupy different pixel widths in a proportional font. Divergent-change ids add a further +N suffix (LogEntryText.kt:31-34).

Fix direction: measure a fixed pixel budget for the id run once per repaint and pad to it, reusing the existing widthOf { ... } helper already used for the decoration separator at ui/log/JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt:133. Cheaper alternative: render the id in a monospace font so character-count padding buys pixel alignment for free. The reporter's own suggestion (a separator character) is a weaker third option — it doesn't fix alignment on its own while widths still vary.
design: Measure/pad a fixed pixel budget for the id run (reuse widthOf{} pattern from JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt:133), or switch the id run to a monospace font.
acceptance_criteria: Commit-description start position is visually aligned across rows regardless of unique-prefix length or divergent-id +N suffixes.
notes: Reported by CaptaiNiveau 2026-08-26, after disabling alternating row colors (GitHub #79).
close_reason: Single status slot sized to widest status run

title: Split: unticked file deletion writes an empty file instead of landing in the parent
description: jj-idea-4q7m added a deletion manifest to DiffEditTool/HunkApplyMain so hunk-level squash can move a file's deletion into the destination. Split's own hunk-level path (SplitDialog.doOKAction's buildHunkSelection call) still passes isDeletion={false} unconditionally, so an UNticked deletion (meant to land in the parent, i.e. the first commit) writes the file with its 'after' content (which loadSquashFileData-style loading would treat as empty string for a deleted file) instead of expressing the deletion via the manifest. Fix: wire isDeletion={change.afterRevision==null} through SplitDialog's buildHunkSelection call and add a deletedPaths test case to CliExecutorSplitTest / a platform test mirroring the squash one.
design:
PLAN: wire deletion awareness into Split's hunk path, mirroring the squash fix (jj-idea-4q7m).

Facts: ui/split/SplitDialog.kt:617-626 `buildHunkSelection(changes = allChanges, root, overrides = firstCommitOverrides, isIncluded = { it in tickedPaths }, isDeletion = { false }, contentFor = { change, included -> if (included) null else previewController.cachedContents(change.filePath)?.after })`. Squash already does it right: ui/squash/SquashIntoDialog.kt:558-563 `isDeletion = { it.afterRevision == null }`. For a deleted file `cachedContents(...).after` is empty/null, so the unticked-deletion branch writes an EMPTY FILE into the parent-remainder tree instead of recording a deletion via the DiffEditTool/HunkApplyMain deletion manifest (added by 4q7m; see common/buildHunkSelection).
Fix (CAUTION: the bead's one-liner `isDeletion = {afterRevision==null}` alone is WRONG - verified by reading buildHunkSelection, ui/common/HunkSelectionModel.kt:80-105):
`buildHunkSelection` records a deletion in the manifest only when `included && isDeletion(change)`, and `included` means "this file's change is written INTO the staging tree ($right = first commit)". Squash's `isIncluded` has that meaning (ticked = moves to destination). Split's call passes `isIncluded = { it in tickedPaths }` where ticked = stays in the SECOND commit, i.e. the OPPOSITE; for split `contentFor(change, included)` returns null for ticked (left as $left = not in first commit) and `after` for unticked (the change lands in the first commit). So an unticked deletion hits the `else -> contentFor` branch and writes the empty `after` string; and merely flipping isDeletion would instead record TICKED deletions as deleted in the first commit - the reverse bug.
Correct fix: at SplitDialog.kt:617-626 invert the predicate to the function's meaning, `isIncluded = { it !in tickedPaths }` (included = lands in first commit), `isDeletion = { it.afterRevision == null }`, and `contentFor = { change, included -> if (included) previewController.cachedContents(change.filePath)?.after else null }` (swap the branch). Delete the stale "deferred" comment (:614-616). Update the call-site comment to say "included = lands in the first commit (unticked in default mode)". Note newParent mode never reaches this path (Pick Hunks hidden there), so only the default mode semantic matters; add a require/assert comment.
Behaviour to preserve: `overrides` (hunk-picked content) still wins first. Add a rename check: a rename is a deletion of the old path plus an add of the new path - confirm `allChanges` yields the old path as a separate entry (or only the new path with a Moved before-revision); if only the new path is present the old path must also go to the manifest when the move lands in the first commit (otherwise the old file lingers in commit 1).
3. Rename-aware: for a rename, the before path deletion + after path add are two entries - verify `allChanges` shape (FileChange.Moved) so the deleted *source* path isn't left behind when only the add is unticked (add a case).
Tests: (a) CliExecutorSplitTest - deletedPaths case (manifest contains path; invocation args), as the bead says; (b) platform test mirroring the squash one in SquashIntoDialog tests (see h8ys for the mock pitfall: avoid relaxed mocks over Result<T>); (c) contract test with real jj: file F deleted in @ plus file G modified; split with F unticked, G ticked and a partial hunk in G; assert F is deleted in the FIRST commit and absent from the second; no empty F anywhere. Add the mirror case (F ticked deletion) asserting the deletion stays in the SECOND commit - this is the case a naive flip of isDeletion breaks. Existing SquashIntoDialog callers must be unchanged (squash tests keep passing).
Decisions made without the user: none needed beyond step 2's verification.
Scale: none (per selected file; same loop as today). Manual: MT-SPLIT (new row: split with an unticked deleted file + Pick Hunks; verify via log details that the deletion is in the first commit), regression scope MT-SPLIT, MT-SQUASH (shared buildHunkSelection).
acceptance_criteria: Unticked deletion in a hunk-level split lands as a deletion in the first commit (no empty file); stale deferred comment removed; unit + platform + contract tests added; MT-SPLIT row added.
close_reason: Fixed polarity of buildHunkSelection call in SplitDialog; dialog tests + real-jj contract test added

title: Reconcile DagNode/GraphableEntry and repo-scoped identity
description: Investigate whether GraphableEntry's repo-baked-in key/parentKeys (added for jj-idea-1ra9, cross-repo root-commit-id collisions) could instead be solved by making parent links repo-scoped at the source, so identity doesn't need to be patched on after the fact via ChangeKey -- and whether CommitGraphBuilder and RebaseSimulator could then share one DagNode-shaped abstraction (see jj-idea-fjsg) instead of two similar-but-different interfaces. Touches CommitGraphBuilder, ChangeKey, LogEntry, and the multi-repo regression test CommitGraphBuilderRepoScopingTest.kt -- a deeper, riskier change than fjsg/0gtl. Explicitly not a blocker for either.
close_reason: Investigated and decided NOT to unify - closing with no code change. Root finding: LogEntry needs two identity views simultaneously (ChangeId for business logic - .divergent, ContentLocator, CLI prefix parsing; ChangeKey for cross-repo dedup in CommitGraphBuilder/UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader/JujutsuReferenceFilterComponent). Kotlin/JVM cannot implement one generic interface (DagNode<K,T>) twice with different K on the same class - GraphableEntry's distinct key/parentKeys naming (vs DagNode's id/parentIds) is the direct, necessary expression of that constraint, not accidental duplication. A wrapper-adapter type would only relocate the duplication (three types instead of two) since GraphableEntry's key/parentKeys are consumed directly by 2 other call sites beyond CommitGraphBuilder's own algorithm, not just it. Also confirmed via investigation: the vast majority of bare-ChangeId-keyed consumers (RebaseSimulator, SplitSimulator, LogCache, Rebase/Squash/Duplicate dialogs) are provably single-repo and would gain nothing from repo-scoping; the actual multi-repo hazard is narrowly confined to CommitGraphBuilder + UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader's merge logic, both already correctly and consistently ChangeKey-scoped since jj-idea-1ra9, with no other unfixed cross-repo comparison site found. Current split (GraphableEntry repo-scoped, DagNode repo-free) is the correct design, not a smell.

title: Settings page too wide
description: The settings page now needs right-scrolling to see the right-justified controls, which is annoying. There is inefficient usage of the available width, including labels that could wrap to the next line and input boxes that are too wide.
close_reason: Fixed: shrank settings panel fields, restacked wide rows, wrapped validation messages; added JujutsuConfigurablePanelTest width regression guard

title: Register/cancel in-flight jj processes so project dispose doesn't wait out CLI timeouts
description:
Split out of jj-idea-c4tp (IDE hangs on "Saving settings" when quitting runIde sandbox).

Hazard 3 from that investigation: jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt has no cancellation/registry for
in-flight jj CLI processes.
- CliExecutor.kt:767 - processHandler.runProcess(timeout.toInt()) has no checkCanceled,
  no indicator wiring, and no registry of live processes.
- CliExecutor.kt:676 - handler.waitFor(networkTimeout) for git clone, same gap.

Nothing can kill an in-flight jj process at project dispose - worst case a caller waits out
the full networkTimeout (120s) even though the project is closing. This is bounded (unlike
the 5-minute latch in jj-idea-c4tp's hazard 2, already fixed), but should still be addressed:
a project-level registry of live CapturingProcessHandlers, destroyed at project dispose, and/or
running jj under the current ProgressIndicator where one exists so checkCanceled propagates.
design:
PLAN: make in-flight jj processes cancellable and killable at project dispose.

Facts: jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt `execute()` (~:1059-1130) builds a CapturingProcessHandler and calls `processHandler.runProcess(timeout)` (the bead cites :767 and :676 for git clone's `handler.waitFor(networkTimeout)`; line numbers drifted - find by those calls). No registry, no ProgressIndicator wiring, so cancel/dispose waits out `defaultTimeout`/networkTimeout (120s).
Design (two complementary parts, both small):
1. Cancellation: use `CapturingProcessHandler.runProcessWithProgressIndicator(indicator, timeoutMs)` when `ProgressManager.getInstance().progressIndicator` (or ProgressIndicatorProvider.getGlobalProgressIndicator()) is non-null - it polls `indicator.isCanceled` and destroys the process; otherwise keep `runProcess(timeout)`. Result timeout/cancel flags map to the existing CommandResult failure kinds (add `cancelled` handling so a user cancel is not logged as an ERROR; INFO only, per contributing.md error philosophy) and `ProcessCanceledException` must be rethrown for callers inside read actions/progress, never swallowed. Preserve the trackUndo `op log` follow-up call: skip it when cancelled.
2. Registry: a project-level light service `JjProcessRegistry : Disposable` (Service.Level.PROJECT) holding a `ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet<ProcessHandler>()`; `execute()` registers the handler before start and removes in `finally`; `dispose()` calls `destroyProcess()` on all remaining. The executor needs the Project/Disposable: CliExecutor currently takes `root`; thread an optional `Disposable parent` (the executor is created by JujutsuRepository which has the project) - register via `Disposer.register(parent, registry)`. Rootless executors (clone/init, workingDir == null) register with the application-level instance instead.
Interaction with c4tp (in progress, same hang): that bead fixed the 5-minute latch; this is the second line of defence. Coordinate: do not touch the latch code; check c4tp's notes before editing execute().
Important caution: killing a REVERSIBLE write mid-flight can leave a half-applied operation? jj operations are atomic (op-log commit at end), so destroying the process is safe; but a killed `git push`/fetch can leave a partial network state - acceptable, jj handles it.
Decisions made without the user: Q: kill on dispose even for IRREVERSIBLE pushes? Rec: yes - project is closing and the user can retry; the alternative is blocking IDE shutdown up to 120s. Reverse: exempt IRREVERSIBLE invocations from dispose-kill (keep them alive but detached).
Scale: O(#in-flight processes) set operations; no traversal.
Testing: unit - fake process handler registered then registry.dispose() destroys it; cancellation test with a long-running stub process (`sleep 30` via a test executable provider) and a cancelled indicator returns within ~1s with a cancelled result; assert no ERROR log on cancel. Manual: MT-WORKINGCOPY / MT-GIT smoke: start a push to an unreachable remote, close project, IDE shuts down promptly. Regression scope: MT-GIT, MT-WORKINGCOPY.
acceptance_criteria: Cancelling a progress task kills its jj process within ~1s; closing the project destroys all registered in-flight jj processes; cancel is not logged as error; ProcessCanceledException propagates; tests added.

title: Contribute jj operations to the VCS Operations Popup (Ctrl+V / Alt+~)
description:
The IntelliJ platform has a 'VCS Operations Popup' - a numbered quick-action list bound to Ctrl+V (macOS) / Alt+~ (Windows/Linux), shown by the platform-internal Vcs.QuickListPopupAction. It is a well-known power-user surface for reaching common VCS operations without a menu or the mouse.

Today jj-idea contributes nothing to it. For a project where Jujutsu is the active VCS, the popup falls back entirely to the platform's Git-shaped defaults: ChangesView.AddUnversioned, CheckinProject, ChangesView.ToggleCommitUi, CheckinFiles, ChangesView.Revert, then Vcs.ShowTabbedFileHistory, Annotate, Compare.SameVersion (platform/vcs-impl/resources/META-INF/VcsActions.xml:647-670 in intellij-community). Two of those defaults are actively misleading for jj: ChangesView.Revert is the silent no-op tracked by jj-idea-ad5d (no RollbackEnvironment), and Vcs.ShowTabbedFileHistory was the platform history tab that was blank until the jj-idea-qrne/GH#88 fix. Nothing jj-specific (New Change, Edit, Describe, Squash, Split, Rebase, Abandon, Push, Fetch, bookmarks) is reachable from this popup.

The plugin already partially uses this surface: plugin.xml registers Jujutsu.Init into Vcs.Operations.Popup.NonVcsAware, but that subgroup is visible only when the project has no VCS configured - the moment a jj repo is detected the plugin's contribution disappears. The VcsAware side (shown once a jj repo IS detected) has never been wired up.

Mechanism: extension point com.intellij.vcsPopupProvider (platform/vcs-impl/resources/META-INF/VcsExtensionPoints.xml:126, dynamic=true), interface com.intellij.openapi.vcs.actions.VcsQuickListContentProvider. Git, Mercurial and Subversion all register one. Two styles:
- Append - VcsQuickListContentProviderBase (platform/vcs-api/.../actions/): implement getVcsName() + collectVcsSpecificActions(ActionManager); actions added after the defaults. Used by Subversion.
- Replace - DvcsQuickListContentProvider, whose replaceVcsActionsFor() returns true for its VCS, suppressing the whole default VcsAware group and re-emitting a curated list. Used by Git and Mercurial.

RECOMMENDED APPROACH: extend VcsQuickListContentProviderBase (append style), registered as <vcsPopupProvider implementation="..."/> under <extensions defaultExtensionNs="com.intellij"> in src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.xml. getVcsName() returns JujutsuVcsBase.VCS_NAME (= "Jujutsu", vcs/JujutsuVcsBase.kt:84).

CRITICAL BUILD CONSTRAINT - do NOT extend DvcsQuickListContentProvider. It lives in intellij.platform.vcs.dvcs.impl, which build.gradle.kts:128-129 only declares for 253+ platforms; using it would break the pre-253 build. VcsQuickListContentProviderBase is in vcs-api and is always available. If the replace style is ever wanted, implement replaceVcsActionsFor on the interface directly rather than taking the dvcs dependency.

WHICH ACTIONS TO SURFACE: only ID-registered actions can be looked up via ActionManager (the base class's static add(actionId, manager, actions) helper) and only they show a keymap shortcut hint. The plugin's ID-registered candidates: Jujutsu.NewChange, Jujutsu.EditChange, Jujutsu.DescribeWorkingCopy, Jujutsu.DescribeChangeToolbar, Jujutsu.RebaseChangeToolbar, Jujutsu.GitPush, Jujutsu.GitFetch, Jujutsu.OpenLogTab, Jujutsu.ShowFileHistory.

DESIGN NOTE (folded into this bead rather than split out): Abandon, Squash, Squash Into, Split, Duplicate and every bookmark operation are factory-built anonymous actions with no action ID (actions/change/abandonChangeAction.kt, squashAction.kt, splitAction.kt, actions/bookmark/*), so they cannot be fetched by ID and can never display a shortcut hint - the pattern is already documented at ui/log/JujutsuLogContextMenuActions.kt:69-77. They can still be returned as instances from collectVcsSpecificActions, but they are built against a log-row selection, whereas this popup's context is an editor/file. Decide during implementation whether to (a) ship only the ID-registered set first, or (b) give the primary operations real action IDs with working-copy-scoped behaviour. (a) is the recommended first cut.

ALTERNATIVE/COMPLEMENTARY ROUTE worth recording: a plain <add-to-group group-id="Vcs.Operations.Popup"/> contributes an entry without implementing the EP at all, and such entries survive a replacing provider because replaceVcsActionsFor only suppresses the VcsAware subgroup, not its siblings. LocalHistory.ShowHistory does exactly this (platform/lvcs-impl/resources/intellij.platform.lvcs.impl.xml:31). Also note <override-text place="ActionPlace.VcsQuickListPopupAction"/> for a popup-specific label - the plugin already uses the override-text place= idiom for Jujutsu.Init/Vcs.Toolbar.Widget.

NOTE FOR IMPLEMENTER: the same Vcs.Operations.Popup group also backs the main toolbar's VCS widget (platform/vcs-impl/.../VcsQuickActionsToolbarPopup.kt), so this change affects that surface too - check it during manual testing.

SCALE ANALYSIS: N/A - none needed. The provider assembles a fixed-size action list per popup invocation; it adds no filesystem traversal and no per-file or per-commit loop.

MANUAL-TEST NOTE: this is UI-affecting - add a new subsection under MT-CTXMENU (docs/manual-tests.md:594) and record a Manual regression scope of MT-CTXMENU plus MT-GIT (Push/Fetch entries).
design:
PLAN: the description is already a thorough design (read it first); this adds the decisions, concrete steps and tests so it can be executed. Recommended first cut = append-style provider with the ID-registered actions only.
Steps:
1. `JujutsuQuickListContentProvider : VcsQuickListContentProviderBase` (vcs/): `getVcsName() = JujutsuVcsBase.VCS_NAME` ("Jujutsu", vcs/JujutsuVcsBase.kt:84) and `collectVcsSpecificActions(ActionManager)` adding, in order, via the base class's static `add(actionId, manager, actions)` helper (skips missing ids): Jujutsu.NewChange, Jujutsu.EditChange, Jujutsu.DescribeWorkingCopy, Jujutsu.RebaseChangeToolbar, Jujutsu.GitFetch, Jujutsu.GitPush, Jujutsu.OpenLogTab, Jujutsu.ShowFileHistory, then the shipped-since actions Jujutsu.SetDiffBase and Jujutsu.UndoLastOperation (per the 2026-09-04 note; verify the exact ids in plugin.xml: grep shows which exist today). Optionally a leading `Separator` + the 'Jujutsu' submenu group (actions/JujutsuMainMenuGroup.kt) as one entry instead of ~10 loose items if the list is long (the popup is numbered quick-access: keep it to <= ~9 entries so the digit shortcuts stay usable).
2. Registration: `<vcsPopupProvider implementation="in.kkkev.jjidea.vcs.JujutsuQuickListContentProvider"/>` in plugin.xml `<extensions defaultExtensionNs="com.intellij">`. DO NOT extend `DvcsQuickListContentProvider` (253+-only module, build.gradle.kts:128-129; per the description's constraint).
3. Misleading defaults (Rollback no-op ad5d, history tab fixed): once jj-idea-ad5d lands (RollbackEnvironment) the `ChangesView.Revert` default becomes functional - then keep append style. If ad5d is NOT done, consider the replace style by implementing `replaceVcsActionsFor` directly on `VcsQuickListContentProvider` (not the DVCS base) returning true for Jujutsu and emitting a curated list (changes view add/commit actions are meaningless for jj: AddUnversioned, CheckinProject/CheckinFiles (no commit concept - the plugin hides the commit UI by default, JujutsuHiddenCommitMode), ToggleCommitUi). Recommendation: REPLACE style is arguably the better UX since 4 of the 5 default entries are Git-shaped commit operations that do nothing useful in jj; but it's a larger behavioural statement - decision below.
4. (b) from the description (give primary operations real action ids with working-copy scope): out of scope v1; track as a follow-up only if users ask for Abandon/Squash/Split in the popup.
5. Same group feeds the toolbar VCS widget popup (VcsQuickActionsToolbarPopup.kt) - verify in manual testing (description note).
Decisions made without the user: Q: append vs replace? Rec: append (safe, matches the description's recommendation and Subversion) now; revisit replace after ad5d. Q: which entries? Rec: the 8-10 ID-registered ones above. Q: group under a 'Jujutsu' submenu? Rec: flat first (the popup is a quick-pick list).
Scale: none (fixed-size action list per popup open). Testing: unit test of the provider's action id list against a stub `ActionManager` (missing ids skipped, order stable); EP registration test (provider found via `VcsQuickListContentProvider.EP_NAME`/`vcsPopupProvider` extension list for VCS name "Jujutsu"); `getVcsName` equals the registered VCS name (guards the rename pitfall); manual: new MT-CTXMENU subsection (open the popup in a jj project: entries listed with shortcut hints, enablement correct per context, entries invoke the same operation as log/toolbar; non-jj project unchanged; no-VCS project still shows Jujutsu.Init) + MT-GIT (Fetch/Push entries) + the toolbar widget popup. Regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-GIT.
acceptance_criteria: With a jj project open, pressing the VCS Operations Popup shortcut (Ctrl+V macOS / Alt+~ Windows/Linux) lists the plugin's primary jj operations alongside the platform defaults; each entry is enabled/disabled correctly for the current context and invokes the same operation as its log/toolbar counterpart; ID-registered entries show their keymap shortcut; nothing regresses for a non-jj project or a project with no VCS configured (Jujutsu.Init still appears there).
notes: Update (2026-09-04, from jj-idea-g1io follow-up): the 'WHICH ACTIONS TO SURFACE' candidate list predates two now-shipped ID-registered actions that are eligible append-style candidates here — Jujutsu.SetDiffBase (Set Diff Base quick action, opens its own popup with strategy/custom-revset/pin sub-choices — only the top-level action would appear in this list, same as any other multi-step action) and Jujutsu.UndoLastOperation (persistent 'Undo <last action>'). Both are also now grouped under a 'Jujutsu' submenu in Vcs.MainMenu (actions/JujutsuMainMenuGroup.kt) rather than being loose top-level entries — worth mirroring that grouping if/when this bead's popup entries multiply.

title: User-defined log columns from jj templates (GitHub #87)
description:
GitHub #87 (SergejSalnikov): expose jj log's revset/template properties that the plugin doesn't surface, by letting the user declare extra columns with their own --template fragment. Follow-up comment relaxes the requirement: no UI needed - an EP or a plain configuration service is acceptable for a first cut.

Design notes: the template plumbing is already generic - LogTemplate/logTemplate and singleField/stringField in jj/cli/TemplateParts.kt and jj/cli/CliLogService.kt compose fields positionally, so an extra user-supplied field appends cleanly. Hard parts: (a) carrying arbitrary extra values on LogEntry (jj/LogEntry.kt) without bloating it, (b) failure handling when a user's template fragment doesn't parse or references an unsupported property (must not break the whole log), and (c) column registration/width persistence in the log table (ui/log/JujutsuLogTable*.kt), which overlaps jj-idea-ajd0.

Not covered by existing beads: jj-idea-3rq is about custom-vs-standard log choice and is effectively obsolete; jj-idea-ajd0 is column persistence testing only.
design:
PLAN: user-defined log columns from jj template fragments (GitHub #87), v1 = a documented configuration path, no UI beyond Settings text rows; scale-safe by NOT adding user fragments to the main log query.
Facts: log columns are fixed constants `JujutsuLogTable.COLUMN_*` (ui/log/JujutsuLogTable.kt:~1156, e.g. `COLUMN_AUTHOR = 2`) with visibility in `JujutsuColumnManager` (ui/log/JujutsuColumnManager.kt) persisted per window (`LogWindowConfig.columnWidths: Map<String,Int>`, string-keyed since migration v3 - settings/JujutsuSettings.kt:43-56) and rendered by `JujutsuLogTableRenderers`; template plumbing is generic: `LogFields.singleField(spec, parser)`, `LogTemplate<T>` composed positionally with `recordSize` (jj/cli/CliLogService.kt:40, :306-324, `logTemplate(...)`), main templates `fullLogTemplate`/`basicLogTemplate` (:463). `LogEntry` (jj/LogEntry.kt:12) is a data class with fixed fields.
Why not put user fragments in the main template: every extra field is evaluated by jj per commit in the dominant query (jj-idea-2c8k: jj's walk + per-commit template cost scales with N); a user could add `diff.stat()` and make every refresh 5x slower, and a malformed fragment would make the WHOLE log fail (the acceptance criterion forbids that: "bad fragment degrades to an empty/error cell"). So: custom columns are loaded by a SEPARATE, lazy, visible-rows batch loader - the same mechanism designed for jj-idea-788j (changed files) and jj-idea-nhk2 (size): build it once as `RowDataProvider` infrastructure.
Design:
1. Config (v1, minimal): `JujutsuSettingsState.customColumns: MutableList<CustomColumnConfig>` (`id` (stable slug), `title`, `template` (jj template fragment evaluated in the commit context, e.g. `committer.timestamp().ago()` or `trailers.map(|t| t.value())`), `width`, `visible`). Settings UI v1: a small table in Settings > Version Control > Jujutsu > Log ("Custom columns": Title | Template | Add/Remove) with a Validate button (see 3); EP/service option from the issue's follow-up comment: also expose `CustomLogColumnProvider` as an application-level EP in plugin.xml so another plugin can contribute - defer unless asked (YAGNI; the config service covers the request).
2. Loader: `CustomColumnLoader` (project service): for the currently visible, settled rows (viewport + margin, debounced after scroll, reusing the batch design from 788j) run ONE jj call per batch: `jj log -r 'c1|c2|...' --no-graph -T '<commit_id>\0' ++ <col1 template> ++ '\0' ++ ...'` using each column's fragment wrapped with `stringify(...)` so non-string results work; values cached by (commitId, columnId) in an LRU (immutable per commit id); results delivered to the table via a `LogEntry`-independent side map `customValues[ChangeKey][columnId]` (keeps `LogEntry` unbloated - acceptance (a) of the bead's "hard parts").
3. Failure isolation (b): validate each fragment when the column is added/changed and at first use: `jj log -r @ --limit 1 --no-graph -T '<fragment>'` on the repo (one cheap call): failure -> column marked INVALID with jj's error message shown in Settings and as the cell tooltip; batch calls evaluate columns INDEPENDENTLY? One batch template containing all columns fails entirely if one is bad; mitigate by validating first and excluding invalid columns from the batch; additionally if a batch fails at runtime, retry per column once to isolate the offender, mark it invalid, and log a WARN (never ERROR) - never touches the main log load.
4. Column registration (c): extend `JujutsuColumnManager`/`JujutsuLogTableModel` with dynamic columns after the built-in ones (model column ids `custom:<id>`; widths/visibility persisted through the existing string-keyed `columnWidths` + a `visibleCustomColumns` list in LogWindowConfig; toggles appear in the column-visibility popup). Header row text = title. Renderer: plain `TextTableCellRenderer<String>` (uses the same hover/selection machinery); empty cell while loading, error glyph + tooltip when invalid.
5. Version/safety notes: fragments run read-only (`jj log` is READ_ONLY, no snapshot side effects? `jj log` snapshots the working copy as usual - same as every refresh; add `--ignore-working-copy` for the batch query to avoid creating snapshot ops from column loads); fragment length cap (1 KB) and a count cap (<= 5 custom columns) to bound per-batch cost; document recommended cheap keywords vs expensive (`diff.*`) in docs.
Decisions made without the user: Q: Settings table vs hand-edited XML only? Rec small Settings table (bead says no UI needed - config-path acceptable; the table is the "documented config path"; a hand-edit-only first cut is possible if you want to ship sooner). Q: EP? Rec no (v1). Q: load in main query for cheap ones? Rec never - one code path.
Scale: per scroll-settle one jj process per batch (<= ~60 ids x <=5 columns), cached per commit id; zero cost when no custom columns configured (loader idle); never on refresh path. Operation-count tests as in 788j (fake clock/executor): scrolling N pages -> <= N batches; cache hits -> 0; invalid column excluded.
Testing: config round-trip (ajd0 reflective guard covers new fields), validation tests with stub executor (valid/invalid/timeouts), batch template builder tests (escaping, NUL separators, column isolation), loader debounce/cache tests, table-model dynamic column tests (visibility/width persistence), renderer tests; manual: MT-LOG-TABLE (add `author.email()` column -> appears, widths persist, bad template -> error tooltip, log still loads), MT-SETTINGS (table + validate), docs page with examples. Regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-SETTINGS, MT-LOG-REFRESH.
Related: jj-idea-788j, jj-idea-nhk2 (shared loader), jj-idea-ajd0 (persistence tests).
acceptance_criteria: Documented config path adds extra log columns from jj template fragments, loaded lazily for visible rows via a shared batch loader (not in the main query); bad fragments degrade to an error cell/tooltip without affecting the log; persistence + validation + operation-count tests; docs.

title: Commit Time column in file history sorts by committer name, not date
description: Found while investigating GitHub #88 (blank file-history metadata). CommitTimestampColumnInfo.getComparator() in vcs/history/JujutsuHistoryColumns.kt sorts by it.committer (the name string) instead of committerDate, so the 'Commit Time' column in the platform file-history table sorts alphabetically by committer rather than chronologically. Only visible once the #88 fix populates the column with actual content.
acceptance_criteria: Sorting the Commit Time column in the file history table orders rows by committer timestamp, not committer name.
close_reason: Fixed CommitTimestampColumnInfo comparator to sort by committerDate instead of committer name

title: Wire up or delete unused SplitPreviewPanel/SplitSimulator
description: ui/split/SplitPreviewPanel.kt and ui/split/SplitSimulator.kt (log-graph preview mirroring RebasePreviewPanel/RebaseSimulator) are referenced nowhere outside their own files — not used by SplitDialog or exercised by any test besides SplitSimulatorTest. Either wire SplitPreviewPanel into SplitDialog (the same gap jj-idea-uuy9 identifies for squash) or remove the dead code. Found during exploration for jj-idea-xuob/4q7m sequencing.
close_reason: Deleted dead SplitPreviewPanel/SplitSimulator as part of jj-idea-2md7's tooltip fix

title: Rename Bookmark dialog should prepopulate and select the current name
description: GitHub #82: BookmarkNameDialog (src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/actions/bookmark/BookmarkNameDialog.kt) always starts its nameField JBTextField empty. For rename specifically, this forces retyping the whole name and offers no way to copy the old one. Prepopulate nameField with the existing name and select it all on focus, so Enter-to-replace still works but editing/copying is also possible. Must stay opt-in per subclass - createBookmarkAction / moveBookmarkAction reuse the same base dialog and should keep starting empty. Cheapest shape: an open initialName: String? = null constructor param (or protected open val) on BookmarkNameDialog, set by RenameBookmarkDialog.
acceptance_criteria: Rename dialog opens with the old name present and fully selected; other bookmark dialogs (create, move) unchanged; existing validation (doValidate, failedNames) still behaves correctly.
close_reason: Closed

title: Revisit LazyActionById once GH #68 (context-menu/toolbar extensibility) lands
description: LazyActionById (added in jj-idea-nd8x, GH #86) resolves Jujutsu.GitFetch/GitPush by id on every toolbar call instead of caching the instance, to survive a dynamic plugin unload. GH #68 requests declaring the jj context-menu/toolbar action groups in plugin.xml (<group>/<reference>/<add-to-group>) instead of the current hardcoded Kotlin lists in CommitTablePanel.createActionGroup() and UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.primaryActions(), so third-party plugins can extend them. XML-declared groups are the platform's own dynamic-plugin-aware mechanism (IntelliJ tracks <action>/<group>/<add-to-group> specially around dynamic reloads). If/when #68's refactor lands, revisit whether LazyActionById is still needed for Fetch/Push, or whether resolving the whole declared group fresh via ActionManager.getAction(id) makes it redundant. Also worth deciding then whether primaryActions()'s four actions (NewChange/EditChange/RebaseChangeToolbar/DescribeChangeToolbar) need the same lazy-resolution treatment for consistency - today they don't strictly need it because none of their update() methods touch Project.stateModel/isJujutsu (they only read e.logEntry/e.logEntries), so a stale instance wouldn't throw, but that's incidental to their current implementation, not a structural guarantee.
design:
PLAN: a decision bead - blocked on the refactor (jj-idea-66id, P4). Nothing to build until it lands; this plan fixes WHAT to decide, the evidence to gather, and the default outcome so it can be executed in ~1 hour.
Facts now: `LazyActionById` (actions/LazyActionById.kt) delegates to `ManagedActions[actionId]` on every update/performed call, so a toolbar built once by `CommitTablePanel.createActionGroup()` / `UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.primaryActions()` never holds an instance from a previous plugin classloader (jj-idea-nd8x, GH #86). wdqg (P3, for-human) is blocked on this bead's decision; it wants the log context menu to use registered `Jujutsu.GitFetch/GitPush` ids instead of factory instances.
Evidence checklist once 66id lands (declared `<group id=...>` in plugin.xml with `<reference>`/`<add-to-group>`):
 1. Does the toolbar/menu now get built from `ActionManager.getAction("Jujutsu.<group id>")` per show (`ActionManager.createActionToolbar(place, group, ...)` resolves the group object ONCE at toolbar creation, but XML-declared groups are mutated in place by the platform on dynamic load/unload - children come and go inside the same group instance, so staleness disappears)? Verify with the unload harness from jj-idea-8awj (install-over-running-IDE with `-Dide.plugins.snapshot.on.unload.fail=true`, log tab open): no ClassCastException, no leaked old action instances.
 2. Are Fetch/Push still reachable only through a Kotlin-built list anywhere (CommitTablePanel dynamic parts: bookmark chips actions, selection-dependent items)? Any remaining Kotlin-constructed action that touches `Project.stateModel` in update() keeps the original hazard.
 3. primaryActions() four actions (NewChange/EditChange/RebaseChangeToolbar/DescribeChangeToolbar): once they live in an XML group, lazy resolution is moot for them; if any stays Kotlin-listed, wrap in LazyActionById for structural (not incidental) safety.
Default outcome (Rec): after 66id, RETIRE LazyActionById only if (1) passes AND (2) finds no remaining captured instances; otherwise keep it but narrow to the remaining sites and document the rule in its KDoc ("any action captured outside an XML group must be resolved lazily"). Record the decision in this bead's notes and update contributing.md Architecture/Threading section with the rule.
Decisions made without the user: Q: do anything before 66id? Rec: no. Q: Should 66id be raised in priority since wdqg (a GitHub #135 report) waits on this? Rec: yes mention to the user - wdqg is user-facing, 66id/1y1j are the chain; consider doing 66id when wdqg is prioritised.
Scale: none. Testing: the unload harness above is the test; plus a unit test asserting no `LazyActionById` usages remain if retired (grep test) or that the remaining ones are listed. Manual regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-LOG-TABLE (toolbar), MT-CROSS (dynamic update).
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded on whether LazyActionById / primaryActions lazy-resolution is still needed after #68's action-group extensibility refactor.
close_reason: Merged into jj-idea-66id as a post-refactor verification step (see its notes); no independent work.

title: Audit remaining plugin-classloader retention paths across dynamic unload
description: Follow-up to jj-idea-nd8x (GH #86). Step 1 (tab manager Content cleanup), step 2 (lazy toolbar action resolution), and the confirmed JujutsuStateModel.repoRootWatchRequests watch-root leak are fixed. Remaining candidate holders to verify/fix, driven by the platform's own leak detector rather than inspection: 1) plugin objects (LogEntry) stored via JujutsuDataKeys.VIRTUAL_FILE_LOG_ENTRY on platform VirtualFile user data, which lives in the app-level VFS indefinitely; 2) ToolWindowEnabler's ContentManagerListener removal path (ToolWindowEnabler.kt:139/150) - verify it always runs on unload, not just the specific state transition it currently guards; 3) in-flight runInBackground coroutines not tied to a cancelled Disposable/project scope; 4) JujutsuAnnotationProvider's FileAnnotation cache plus any annotations still attached to open editor gutters. Verify via sandbox IDE run with -Dide.plugins.snapshot.on.unload.fail=true, install-over-running-IDE, confirm no classloader-retention snapshot.
design:
PLAN: leak-detector-driven audit (do NOT fix by inspection alone): build a repeatable "unload leak" harness first, then fix each holder it names.
Step 0 - harness: a documented procedure (contributing.md > Platform API compatibility or docs/dev-unload-test.md) + Gradle `runIde` JVM arg: `-Dide.plugins.snapshot.on.unload.fail=true` (already referenced in the bead; add it to tasks.runIde jvmArgs behind a `-PunloadLeakCheck` property so normal runIde is unaffected, build.gradle.kts:517). Procedure: runIde sandbox with a jj project open + log/working copy/annotate/diff open -> `installPlugin` of a rebuilt zip over the running IDE (dynamic reload) -> the platform dumps a classloader-retention snapshot (.hprof/report in sandbox `log/`) if the plugin's classloader is still reachable. Record the retention path report in notes for each iteration.
Step 1 - fix the four named candidates in this order (cheapest to verify first), re-running the harness after each:
 1. `JujutsuDataKeys.VIRTUAL_FILE_LOG_ENTRY` (actions/JujutsuDataKeys.kt:52). Verify-first: grep shows the ONLY writer is vcs/JujutsuVirtualFile.kt:58 `putUserData(...)` inside JujutsuVirtualFile's own init, i.e. user data lives on OUR virtual-file instance, not on platform VFS files, so it is not obviously app-level-retained (unlike the bead's premise). The real question is whether JujutsuVirtualFile instances themselves stay reachable: they register in `MutableContentRegistry.getInstance(repo.project)` (JujutsuVirtualFile.kt:~60; project service, disposed with project - fine) and may be held by open editors/diff viewers/`FileEditorManager` history (`EditorHistoryManager` keeps VirtualFile refs across the IDE lifetime) and by the platform's `VirtualFilePointer`/`ProjectManager` caches. Harness decides. If retained via EditorHistory: close the diff/editor tabs for JujutsuVirtualFiles in a `DynamicPluginListener.beforePluginUnload` (FileEditorManager.closeFile) and `MutableContentRegistry.unregister`. Reading side: VcsExtensions.kt:45/:75 `getUserData` - unchanged. Also confirm `Key.create("Jujutsu.VirtualFileLogEntry")` (a plugin-classloader Key) is not left in any platform file's user data map by `getUserData` callers on foreign files (`putUserData` is never called on foreign files - verified by grep).
 2. ToolWindowEnabler's ContentManagerListener (the bead's ToolWindowEnabler.kt is now ui/services/JujutsuUiEnabler.kt: `suppressorListener` :38, created :146, added :158 with the non-Disposable overload): ensure the listener is registered with a Disposable parent (the project service / `Disposer.register(parentDisposable, ...)`) so removal runs on unload regardless of which state transition occurred; replace manual add/remove pairs with `contentManager.addContentManagerListener(listener, disposable)` (overload with parentDisposable).
 3. In-flight `runInBackground` coroutines (util): confirm they use the project's injected `CoroutineScope` (cancelled on dispose/unload) rather than `GlobalScope`/application scope; grep `GlobalScope|ApplicationManager.getApplication().executeOnPooledThread|AppExecutorUtil` in src/main and convert long-lived ones to the service scope; short fire-and-forget pooled tasks that capture plugin objects only matter if they outlive unload (bounded by CLI timeout) - cross-ref jj-idea-1a4c (process registry/cancel) which also removes the 120s tail.
 4. JujutsuAnnotationProvider cache / gutter-attached FileAnnotation (vcs/annotate/): annotations attached to editor gutters are held by the platform's `AnnotationsPreloader`/editor; implement `FileAnnotation.dispose()/close()` to drop line data and `Disposer.register(project service, annotation)`; verify via harness with an annotate gutter open at unload time.
Step 2: add a cheap regression guard so new holders are caught early: a platform test (@Tag("platform")) that loads/unloads is not feasible; instead an architectural unit test (reflection over src) forbidding `putUserData(` of plugin-class values anywhere except JujutsuVirtualFile's own init and `GlobalScope` usage (simple text grep test over src/main, like other lint-style tests if present - check existing 'ArchitectureTest').
Decisions made without the user: Q: unit-test enforcement of the rules (grep-test)? Rec: yes, cheap; Reverse: delete the test. Q: fix all four in one PR? Rec: one PR per holder (each independently revertible), harness doc first.
Scale: none (lifecycle). Manual: the harness itself IS the manual test; add a short entry to docs/manual-tests.md MT-CROSS "dynamic plugin update leaves no retention snapshot". Regression scope: MT-CROSS, MT-LOG-DETAILS (annotation/file user data), MT-DIFF.
Related: jj-idea-ejij (test-side ProjectImpl leak via AllVcses) - if its retention path names a Jujutsu class, fix here.
acceptance_criteria: Unload-leak harness documented; sandbox install-over-running-IDE with -Dide.plugins.snapshot.on.unload.fail=true yields no snapshot for each of the four holders; VIRTUAL_FILE_LOG_ENTRY no longer stored on shared VirtualFiles; listener/scope/annotation lifecycles disposer-bound.

title: Log table's column header row renders blank (looks like dead space) (GitHub #78)
description: toddjonker (GitHub #78) pointed at 'an empty row, presumably unlabeled column headers' between the log toolbar and the table as potential real estate for more toolbar buttons. Confirmed: it's real. JujutsuLogTable.getColumnName (JujutsuLogTable.kt:907) unconditionally returns "" for every column, and the table header itself is fully functional — reorderingAllowed/resizingAllowed are both on, with an explicit 24px preferred height (JujutsuLogTable.kt:166-170) — so there's a working JTableHeader row (drag to reorder/resize columns) that renders as blank space because no column has a label. That's presumably why it reads as unused: it's dead-looking, not dead.
design: Two directions, need a decision rather than an obvious pick: (a) give columns real labels, which fixes the 'looks empty' perception and likely improves discoverability of the reorder/resize functionality that's already there but invisible; (b) leave labels blank by design (e.g. the graph/description column may not want a label) but do something else with the row — shrink it, or, per the original #78 idea, host toolbar content in it. Whichever direction is chosen should account for per-column layout — some columns (graph, description) may genuinely not want a text label even if others (author, date) would benefit from one.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is made and implemented: either meaningful column headers replace the blank ones, or the row's blank appearance is deliberately addressed some other way — it should no longer look like accidental empty space.
notes: Split out from jj-idea-ck64 (GitHub #78's main ask: more toolbar buttons) — that bead's own notes flagged the empty row as worth checking before assuming it's free real estate, and it's confirmed to be occupied (a header row, not padding), so it's a separate, smaller decision rather than something ck64 can just claim as space.
close_reason: Blank header row replaced with Git-parity invisible header; last column now resizable via inert trailing spacer; fit-to-width rounding bug fixed

title: Setting for log context-expansion window size (GitHub #80)
description: SergejSalnikov (GitHub #80) asks for the context window used when jumping to a revision outside the loaded log (e.g. from file annotation, or navigating to a bookmark outside the current revset) to be configurable, including a 0/1 option to load only the exact target revision with no surrounding ancestors/descendants. Current behaviour: LogCache.kt:46/125-128 (loadContext) hardcodes window=10, building the revset ancestors(id, window) | id | descendants(id, window) — 19 revisions total. In a monorepo, topologically-nearby commits are often unrelated changes from other teams/projects, so the padding is pure clutter rather than useful context for the reporter's use case (inspecting one historical change to one file).
design: Add a numeric setting (JujutsuSettingsState.kt) for the context window size, threaded through to LogCache.loadContext's window parameter (default parameter is already window: Int = 10, so this is largely wiring a setting through instead of using the hardcoded default). A window of 0 should degenerate the revset to just the target id, skipping the ancestors()/descendants() clauses entirely rather than calling them with 0 (confirm jj accepts an explicit 0 cleanly either way, but the simpler expression is more obviously correct and avoids relying on jj's edge-case handling).
acceptance_criteria: A settings field controls the context window size used by loadContext; a value of 0 shows only the target revision when navigating to an out-of-view commit; a test covers window=0 producing a revset/entry set containing only the target.
notes:
Batch 2 of batch-plan jj-idea-exgr. Shares LogCache.kt:46/125-128 (loadContext)
with jj-idea-dq7z (batch-1, GitHub #76 ambiguous-prefix crash fix). dq7z lands
first; rebase this settings change onto it rather than landing in parallel.
close_reason: Shipped in one PR (batch 2 of jj-idea-exgr)

title: Setting to disable striped log rows (GitHub #79)
description: Junkyards3 (GitHub #79) finds the alternating-row striping in the Jujutsu Log table distracting and asks for a way to disable it, or alternatively to customize the stripe color. setStriped(true) is called in four places: JujutsuLogTable.kt:179, DuplicateDialog.kt:75, SquashIntoDialog.kt:122, RebaseDialog.kt:85 — all plain JBTable/CommitTablePanel-style tables using the platform's built-in striping.
design: Simplest shape matching the reporter's ask: a settings checkbox (JujutsuSettingsState.kt, matching the hideStandardCommitToolWindow/showLogHoverTooltip pattern) gating setStriped on the main log table at minimum. Decide whether to also gate the picker dialogs' tables (Duplicate/Squash/Rebase) for consistency, or scope to just the log window since that's what the reporter is looking at. A color picker is a larger ask (platform striping color is theme-controlled, not trivially overridable per-table) — treat as out of scope unless the on/off switch alone doesn't satisfy the reporter.
acceptance_criteria: A settings checkbox turns off row striping in the log window table; default preserves today's striped behaviour.
close_reason: Shipped in one PR (batch 2 of jj-idea-exgr)

title: Bookmark dropdown: icons on per-bookmark sub-menus
description:
In the bookmark widget's dropdown (actions/bookmark/BookmarkMenu.kt's bookmarkSubGroup(),
shared by ui/toolbar/JujutsuBookmarkToolbarWidget.kt and
ui/statusbar/JujutsuBookmarkStatusBarWidget.kt since jj-idea-cpno), each bookmark's own
sub-menu — DefaultActionGroup(group.localName, true) — has no icon set on its
templatePresentation. Only the outer per-repo submenu (in the multi-repo case) gets an icon
(RepositoryIcons[repo]). The individual action items inside each sub-menu (Advance/Rename/
Delete/Forget/Track) do have icons, but the sub-menu header itself doesn't, so a long dropdown
list is a wall of plain text.

Requested by the user after jj-idea-cpno shipped, alongside jj-idea-emek (highlighting the
current bookmark).
design:
JujutsuIcons already has bookmark-state icons that look purpose-built for this
(ui/common/JujutsuIcons.kt): Bookmark, BookmarkTracked, BookmarkConflict, BookmarkDeleted, plus
the Action-suffixed variants (BookmarkAction, BookmarkTrackedAction) already used elsewhere for
AnAction icons at menu-item size (see JujutsuLogContextMenuActions.kt's
addPopup("action.bookmark.submenu", JujutsuIcons.BookmarkAction), and
toggleTrackBookmarkAction.kt). Chip-icon precedence for a bookmark's *state* is already decided
elsewhere (see jj-idea memory "jj-idea-rskx-shipped": conflict > deleted > tracked > plain) —
reuse that same precedence here rather than inventing a new one.

Per BookmarkGroup (jj/Revset.kt:78 — localName, local: Bookmark?, remotes: List<Bookmark>), the
icon should reflect the local bookmark's state when present (conflict/deleted/plain), or a
tracked/remote-only variant when there's no local bookmark (remote-only group). Set via
templatePresentation.icon on the DefaultActionGroup(group.localName, true) in
bookmarkSubGroup() — actions/bookmark/BookmarkMenu.kt.

If jj-idea-emek (highlighting the current bookmark) is picked up in the same pass, consider
whether the "current" treatment there should also involve an icon variant/accent, to avoid two
different icon-selection code paths for the same sub-menu header.
notes:
Must ship in the same PR as jj-idea-emek (linked via relates_to, 2026-08-25 triage): both edit
bookmarkSubGroup() in actions/bookmark/BookmarkMenu.kt:104, and emek's chosen "current bookmark"
treatment (see its own notes) must share this bead's icon-selection path rather than adding a
second one for the same sub-menu header.

title: Bookmark dropdown: highlight and/or surface the current (@) bookmark(s)
description:
In the bookmark widget's dropdown (actions/bookmark/BookmarkMenu.kt, shared by
ui/toolbar/JujutsuBookmarkToolbarWidget.kt and ui/statusbar/JujutsuBookmarkStatusBarWidget.kt
since jj-idea-cpno), the per-bookmark sub-menus are currently listed in whatever order
List<Bookmark>.grouped() produces, with no visual distinction for the bookmark(s) actually on
the working copy right now. The dropdown's own top-level label already shows the current
bookmark name/distance (bookmarkWidgetText), but once you open the menu it's easy to lose track
of which entry in a long list is "you are here".

Requested by the user after jj-idea-cpno shipped: highlight the current bookmark somehow, and
consider bringing it to the top of the list.

Relevant code: bookmarkActionGroup() -> repoActionGroup() -> bookmarkSubGroup() in
actions/bookmark/BookmarkMenu.kt. bookmarkSubGroup() already receives an `onWc: Boolean`
parameter (currently only used to decide whether to include "Move to Change…") — the data
needed to identify the current bookmark(s) is already there, this is purely a presentation
change.
design:
Options to weigh (not decided — pick one, or combine, when picking this up):

1. Reorder: sort onWc-true group(s) to the front of the sub-menu list, rest unchanged
   (currently List<Bookmark>.grouped()'s natural order — check what that is, likely
   alphabetical). Simple, but reordering a menu each time it opens can be visually jarring if
   the same bookmark name isn't always in the same spot.
2. Visual-only: keep list order stable, but give the onWc group(s) a distinct look — bold text
   on the sub-menu's DefaultActionGroup(group.localName, true), a checkmark/dot prefix, or an
   accent-colored icon (ties into jj-idea-<icons-bead> below if both are done together).
3. Pinned section: a separate "On Working Copy" header + separator above the rest of the list,
   duplicating the current bookmark's sub-menu there (or making it non-duplicated — i.e. moving
   it, similar to option 1, but with an explicit header rather than silent reordering).
4. Combination of 1+2: move to top AND give it a marker, so it's unambiguous even after the
   list has scrolled.

No existing "current bookmark" visual pattern elsewhere in the codebase to be consistent with
(checked TextCanvas.kt/log chip rendering — bookmark chips don't currently distinguish
on-@ from not-on-@ either). Whatever's chosen here might also inform a consistent treatment
there, but that's out of scope for this issue.

Also consider: in the multi-repo case, "onWc" is per-repo (computed from wcEntry per repo in
repoActionGroup()) — the fix needs to work per-repo submenu, not just assume single-repo.
notes:
Must ship in the same PR as jj-idea-0b6b (linked via relates_to, 2026-08-25 triage): both edit
bookmarkSubGroup() in actions/bookmark/BookmarkMenu.kt:104.

Design decision made 2026-08-25 (option 2 from the DESIGN section above, "visual-only"): keep
List<Bookmark>.grouped()'s existing order stable — do not reorder or pin a section — and instead
give the onWc: Boolean group(s) a distinct accented icon and/or bold sub-menu label. onWc is
already threaded into bookmarkSubGroup(), so no new plumbing is needed. Must share one
icon-selection path with jj-idea-0b6b's per-bookmark state icons (conflict > deleted > tracked
precedence from bookmarkIcon(), ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:116) rather than inventing a second
one for the same sub-menu header.

title: Decide policy for acting on immutable changes (GitHub #71)
description: cYDN48 (GitHub #71) asks to allow describe/squash/rebase/etc. on immutable changes via jj's --ignore-immutable, instead of greying the actions out entirely. This needs a one-time policy decision before implementation, because jj's immutable set typically means already pushed/shared, and a one-click override in a graph UI is a materially different risk profile than typing --ignore-immutable deliberately on a command line. Immutability gating is currently spread across multiple call sites with no single chokepoint: SquashIntoDialog.kt, DuplicateImmutabilityGuard.kt, RebaseSimulator.kt, JujutsuLogContextMenuActions.kt, WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt (grep 'immutable' across src/main/kotlin for the full list). A per-action override needs to behave consistently regardless of which of these call sites triggered it.
design: Reporter's own suggestion, and the most promising shape: an opt-in setting (off by default) that, when enabled, makes the gated actions available but requires a confirmation dialog stating plainly what immutable history is about to be rewritten. Icon treatment: highlight in the same red as the existing immutable-lock icon rather than simply greying out, per the reporter's suggestion. First deliverable is enumerating every gating call site and confirming one shared chokepoint can cover them (rather than a scattered per-action flag), then splitting implementation into its own bead(s).
acceptance_criteria: A design doc/notes enumerating all immutability gating call sites, a decided policy (setting + confirmation shape), and a follow-up implementation bead created from it.

title: Spike: run with Git configured as the project VCS (GitHub #72)
description: cYDN48 (GitHub #72) reports the plugin only works when Jujutsu is the VCS configured in the checked-in .idea/vcs.xml. On a team where everyone else uses Git, changing vcs.xml to Jujutsu breaks the Git plugin for teammates, and there's no supported way to keep Git as the checked-in VCS while still getting Jujutsu support locally (jj file untrack .idea/vcs.xml deletes it for everyone, since untracking removes it from the commit — not a viable workaround). This is likely the single biggest adoption blocker for teams migrating gradually or mixed-tooling teams, since it forces every contributor to accept the plugin's VCS choice or opt out entirely.
design: The plugin already sets directory mappings programmatically at Init time (InitAction.kt:58-67, via ProjectLevelVcsManagerEx.setDirectoryMappings / scheduleMappedRootsUpdate). The plausible route is: store 'treat this root as Jujutsu' as workspace-local state (.idea/workspace.xml, normally gitignored, not the shared vcs.xml) and apply/override the directory mapping when the project opens, leaving the checked-in vcs.xml saying Git for everyone else. Open questions this spike must answer: (1) does this survive the Git plugin also claiming the same root at IDE startup — ordering, event contention; (2) do Git-plugin features (commit tool window, git-specific gutters, etc.) end up fighting the jj plugin for the same root; (3) is there a supported IntelliJ API for a per-user mapping override, or does this require watching vcs.xml and re-applying on top of it every time the platform reloads it.
acceptance_criteria: A written go/no-go with findings on the three open questions above — this is a spike, not an implementation. If go, a follow-up feature bead is created with the concrete design.

title: Verify diff preview scroll no longer resets on save-while-previewing (GitHub #67 follow-up)
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/67 (closed, but reopened concern in a
comment on 2026-08-10)

emadpres reported on 0.8.8 that editing code INSIDE the "@: <file>" diff preview tab
(opened by double-clicking a file in the Working Copy panel) and saving causes the diff's
scroll position to jump back to the top. This is distinct from the original #67 bug (saving
switched focus to the preview tab), which was already fixed.

jj-idea-q6vn (commit 190556953, 2026-08-10, currently unreleased in [Unreleased]) plausibly
fixes exactly this path: JujutsuRepository.kt:124 now resolves the working copy's own side
to CurrentContentRevision (the live document) instead of a static `jj file show` snapshot,
and the other content revisions (jj/JujutsuContentRevisions.kt) were made into value-equal
data classes. Together this means saving while the file is shown in the preview produces a
diff request that is equal to the platform's cached one, so the diff viewer doesn't rebuild
and the scroll position survives.

Filed as a verification task, not a bug, because the fix looks like it already covers this
case; only reopen/reclassify as a bug if retesting shows otherwise.
design:
1. Reproduce on 0.8.8 (pre-fix) to confirm the report.
2. Confirm fixed on current master / next release build (0.8.9) using the same repro:
   open the "@: <file>" preview tab, scroll down, edit and save the file, check scroll
   position is preserved.
3. If confirmed fixed, add a regression test for the specific save-while-previewing case
   (extending the coverage already added for jj-idea-q6vn:
   JujutsuContentRevisionsTest.kt / JujutsuRepositoryImplTest.kt / SameChangesAndStatusesTest.kt)
   rather than leaving it implicit.
4. If NOT fixed, reclassify this issue as a bug and investigate further — the preview tab
   component itself (ui/common/JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview.kt) may have its own separate
   scroll-reset path independent of the diff request cache.
close_reason: Verified fixed by q6vn (0.8.9); regression test added in JujutsuChangeProviderTest (qpwrqnxk)

title: Jujutsu > Annotate is a duplicate of the top-level Annotate entry in the Diff viewer popup menu
description: Jujutsu.EditorGroup (plugin.xml) is added to both EditorLangPopupMenu (plain code editor) and Diff.EditorPopupMenu (diff viewer), and references the platform's built-in 'Annotate' action inside it. The platform's own Annotate action (VcsActions.xml) already independently registers itself into Diff.EditorPopupMenu directly, so the diff viewer's right-click menu shows 'Annotate' twice: once at top level, once nested under 'Jujutsu'. In the plain code editor there's no such duplicate, since Jujutsu deliberately isn't registered as a StandardVcsGroup (see plugin.xml comment), so VersionControlsGroup contributes nothing there and Jujutsu > Annotate is the only entry point. Fix: JujutsuEditorActionGroup.getChildren() should filter out the 'Annotate' child specifically when the group is being shown inside a diff editor (com.intellij.diff.util.DiffUtil.isDiffEditor(editor)), keeping it for the plain editor/project-view placements.
close_reason: JujutsuEditorActionGroup.getChildren() now filters out the 'Annotate' child when shown inside a diff editor (DiffUtil.isDiffEditor), since the platform's Annotate action already places itself directly into Diff.EditorPopupMenu. Kept for the plain code editor / project view, where it's the only entry point (Jujutsu isn't a StandardVcsGroup member).

title: Working copy window doesn't show nested repos
description: If a project has a nested repo, i.e. a top-level jj repo and a folder within it that contains a different jj repo, then the log window correctly shows commits from both. However the working copy window does not show the nested repo and change tracking does not work against it either.
design:
PLAN: reproduce, then fix at the VCS-mapping layer (most likely cause: the nested repo is not a valid VCS root mapping for the platform's change tracking); bead says the LOG shows both repos but the Working Copy panel and change tracking ignore the nested one.
Code facts:
 - Repo discovery: `JujutsuStateModel.jujutsuVcsRoots` = the project's Jujutsu directory MAPPINGS (`projectLevelVcsManager.getDirectoryMappings(jujutsuVcs)`, JujutsuStateModel.kt:117-127), then `initialisedRepositories` keeps those with `.jj` (:132-150). So a nested repo is a repo only if the user/auto-detect created a mapping for it.
 - `JujutsuRootChecker` (vcs/JujutsuRootChecker.kt) implements `isRoot/validateRoot/isVcsDir` but does NOT override `areChildrenValidMappings()` (VcsRootChecker.java: "Whether any descendant of VCS root can be registered as valid VCS mapping", default false), and the `<vcs name="Jujutsu" ... administrativeAreaName=".jj"/>` registration (plugin.xml:58) has no `areChildrenValidMappings="true"` (VcsEP.java:27 attribute). Git sets this to true; without it the platform's root detection (VcsRootDetector / "Directory Mappings > Configure" suggestions, auto-detect notifications) treats a `.jj` inside an already-mapped root as not-a-mapping candidate, so a nested jj repo typically stays UNMAPPED -> `VcsUtil.getVcsRootFor(nestedFile)` returns the PARENT root -> `possibleJujutsuRepositoryFor` (vcs/VcsExtensions.kt:81-82) resolves nested files to the parent repo: Working Copy panel groups under the parent, change provider runs `jj status` against the parent (which, depending on parent's ignore config, snapshots the nested repo's files as ordinary files and reports them as the PARENT's changes) - matching "does not show the nested repo and change tracking does not work against it".
 - Why the log "correctly shows both": the log reads `initialisedRepositories`, i.e. whatever mappings exist; if the user hand-added both mappings the log shows both but ChangeListManager dirty scopes may still be wrong if only ... (verify in repro).
Step 0 - reproduce (fixture script scripts/fixtures/fx-nested.sh in the style of fx-stress.sh): `outer/` jj repo + `outer/inner/` jj repo (non-colocated), open `outer` in runIde. Record: Directory Mappings contents, what `jj status` in outer says about `inner/` files (jj ignores nested `.jj`? jj treats nested repos' working tree files as normal files unless ignored; `.jj` dirs are skipped), which repos appear in the Working Copy panel, which `getVcsRootFor` returns for `inner/x`.
