Fix candidates (verify each against the repro):
 1. Declare nested support: `JujutsuRootChecker.areChildrenValidMappings() = true` and `<vcs ... areChildrenValidMappings="true"/>` so detection suggests/auto-registers nested roots. Check `VcsRootChecker.isIgnored(project, root, checkForIgnore)` / `suggestDependentRoots` defaults.
 2. Auto-registration: when `JujutsuVcsRoots`/startup scan finds `.jj` directories below a mapped root (bounded scan: depth <= 3? NOT a full-tree walk - scale rule: large monorepos! use the platform's `VcsRootScanner`/`VcsRootDetector` which the IDE already runs with its own bounded policy, rather than our own traversal), prompt via the standard "VCS roots detected" notification (platform `VcsNotifier`) instead of silently mapping.
 3. Parent-repo hygiene: the parent should not report the nested repo's files as its own changes: add the nested repo directory to the parent's ignore set for the IDE view (`JujutsuIgnoredFileProvider.isIgnoredFile` returns true for paths under a nested repo root that isn't the parent repo, so ChangeListManager doesn't show them twice) - note jj itself still tracks them in the parent unless `.gitignore`d (user responsibility).
 4. UI: Working Copy panel lists every initialised repo (repo selector, xsa8) - nothing to change once the nested repo is mapped.
Decisions made without the user: Q: auto-map nested roots vs notification? Rec notification via platform detector (consistent with Git; avoids surprising repo-count changes). Q: scan depth? Rec: platform-owned. Q: hide nested files from the parent's view? Rec yes (3).
Scale: no new traversal in plugin code (platform root detector, bounded by its own limits: `Registry vcs.root.detector.folder.depth`, default 2); mapping count grows by 1 per nested repo; per-repo `jj status` per refresh as for any root. Operation-count: refresh with R roots runs R status calls (existing).
Testing: JujutsuRootCheckerTest additions (areChildrenValidMappings true; nested `isRoot`); platform test with two mapped roots where nested is under outer: `possibleJujutsuRepositoryFor(inner/file)` returns the nested repo (VcsExtensions tests: VcsExtensionsAncestryTest/ChangeFilter tests exist - extend), `JujutsuIgnoredFileProvider` hides nested files from parent; manual: new fixture + MT-WORKINGCOPY/MT-CROSS rows (nested repo appears in Working Copy panel selector; editing a nested file shows a change under the nested repo only; log shows both). Regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-CROSS, MT-IGNORE.
acceptance_criteria: Nested jj repo is mappable/detected, appears in the Working Copy panel, and its changes are tracked against the nested repo only; parent view doesn't double-report; repro fixture + tests; MT rows.

title: jj-native Code Vision author hints (VcsCodeVisionProvider is Git-only in platform)
description: Platform's VcsCodeVisionProvider (platform/vcs-impl/lang/src/com/intellij/codeInsight/hints/VcsCodeVisionProvider.kt in intellij-community) hard-codes a Git check in two places: getVcsFor(virtualFile)?.takeIf { "Git" == it.name } when resolving the annotation, and if ("Git" != vcs.name) return null in getPlaceholderCollector. This means platform Code Vision author/date inlay hints can never appear for jj files, regardless of jj file annotate speed, even though AnnotationsPreloader (which populates the CacheableAnnotationProvider cache) is itself VCS-agnostic. Surfaced by WeetHet on GitHub issue #64 after patching jj to speed up file annotate to ~7s and still seeing no hints. Fix: ship our own CodeVisionProvider (e.g. id jj.code.vision) mirroring VcsCodeVisionProvider but keyed on JujutsuVcs, reading from JujutsuAnnotationProvider.getFromCache (src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/vcs/annotate/JujutsuAnnotationProvider.kt:56), reusing VcsCodeVisionLanguageContext for per-language anchors.
design: Depends conceptually on jj-idea-1sza (back off annotation preloading when annotate is slow) and jj-idea-a921 (annotation cache is unsynchronized/unbounded) since Code Vision hints on a very large/slow repo would hammer both; consider blocking on those or at least gating hints behind the same slow-repo backoff.
notes: Correction owed to WeetHet on #64: we previously told them Code Vision hints already work VCS-agnostically via CacheableAnnotationProvider, which conflates the preloader (VCS-agnostic) with the renderer (Git-only).

title: Graph: inline changed-files in graph row
description: jjx has an experimental setting (jjx.showChangedFiles) to show changed files inline in the graph, rather than only in a separate details panel. We currently only show changed files in JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel. Consider an inline/expandable file list under each graph row.
design:
PLAN: opt-in, lazy, bounded inline file list under a log row - NOT per-row-for-all-rows (scale).
Facts: changed files currently appear only in ui/log/JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt (loaded per selection via `ChangeService.loadChanges(entry)` -> `logService.getFileChanges(entry)`, jj/ChangeService.kt:25). The log table (ui/log/JujutsuLogTable.kt) uses uniform row height and a custom graph renderer (JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer) whose graph geometry assumes one text line per row (GraphEdgeIndex row math, hit-testing `rowAtPoint`, DnD drop-row calculation, long-edge spans). jjx's experimental `jjx.showChangedFiles` shows files inline.
Constraints that shape the design (contributing.md Performance & Scale): never a `jj` call per visible row on paint (log can be 100k commits; viewport ~60 rows; scrolling would storm jj). Variable row heights break the graph painter (edges drawn per fixed row height) - so DO NOT insert extra table rows or change row heights.
Design (v1):
1. Rendering approach: show a compact "N files" summary chip + the first K (=3) file names (e.g. `M Foo.kt, A Bar.kt +4`) in the existing right-aligned decorations/second text segment of the SAME row, NOT multi-line. This keeps row height constant and graph math untouched. Data = a new optional template field `diff.files()` isn't available in the log template at scale...  jj template can give `diff.summary()`? Check at the version: `jj log -T 'diff.summary()'` exists (CommitDiff? `self.diff().summary()` in 0.3x) but computing diffs for every log row is expensive (it is the dominant cost for large repos) - so DO NOT add to the main log template. 
2. Lazy loading: fetch the summary only for rows that are (a) visible AND (b) idle for >300ms (debounced after scroll) and cap at the viewport; one batched call for the visible set: `jj log -r 'change_id(a)|change_id(b)|...' -T '<id>\0<diff.summary()>'` (one process per batch, <= ~60 ids; use `ChangeId.full`/commit ids per jj-idea-wiz0) and cache in an LRU keyed by commit id (immutable per commit => cache never goes stale; evict at ~2k entries). While loading render nothing (no jump). Setting: Settings > Log > "Show changed files in log rows" (default OFF), reading `JujutsuSettings` state field + column manager toggle (JujutsuColumnManager has `showStatus/showChangeId/showDescription/showDecorations`; add `showChangedFiles`).
3. Expanded multi-line mode (true "inline expandable list", as the bead title says) is explicitly OUT of scope v1: row-height variance would need the graph renderer, DnD, hover, edge index and keyboard navigation reworked; record as a follow-up only if users ask after v1.
4. Interaction: clicking a file name chip opens that file's diff for the commit (reuse the details panel's file-diff action `ShowDiffFor...`); Alt-hover tooltip lists all files (cap 50, "+N more").
5. Empty commits show nothing; merge commits: diff vs auto-merged parent (jj default) - same as details panel.
Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Single-line summary vs real expandable multi-line? Rec: single-line summary v1 (scale + graph geometry). Reverse: schedule the renderer rework as its own epic.
2. Q: Default on/off? Rec: OFF; a visible-rows batched jj call is cheap but still costs on big repos.
3. Q: Do it at all? Honest take: the details pane already provides this on selection; value is for scanning history quickly. Rec: low priority, implement only if the user wants it; kept at P3.
Scale analysis: O(visible rows) per scroll-settle, ONE jj process per batch (<=60 ids), results cached per commit; no per-row call on paint; paint reads the cache only. Operation-count test: scrolling through 10k rows in 100 steps with debounce => <= (#settle events) batches; revisiting cached rows => 0 calls; setting off => 0 calls.
Testing: loader/batching unit test with a fake executor and fake clock (debounce, cap, cache hit/miss, cancellation on scroll); renderer test for the chip text (K files + overflow); template/parse test from captured `diff.summary()` output. Manual: MT-LOG-TABLE (toggle on: chips appear after scroll settles, no jank while scrolling; off: nothing), MT-LOG-GRAPH (rows/graph unaffected), MT-LOG-DETAILS. Regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-GRAPH, MT-DND.
acceptance_criteria: Optional (default off) single-line changed-files summary per log row, lazily batch-loaded for settled visible rows with per-commit cache; no per-row jj call on paint; row height/graph geometry unchanged; operation-count test; MT rows added.

title: Graph: omit author for your own changes
description: jjx omits the author name in the log/graph for changes authored by the current user, reducing visual noise since most rows are the user's own. Our log always shows author. Small polish item from jjx competitive comparison.
design:
PLAN: dim/omit the author for the current user's own rows. Scope clarification first: the log TABLE has a dedicated Author column (`JujutsuColumnManager.showAuthorColumn`, ui/log/JujutsuColumnManager.kt:5; `UserCellRenderer`, ui/log/JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt:26) - "omit" there means rendering an EMPTY (or subdued) cell for own commits; the same idea applies to the author line in the details pane (`appendUserWithTimestamp`, ui/log/JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt:45-57) where omitting would hide information users may want, so Rec: table column only, not the details pane.
Facts: the current user's identity per repo comes from jj config `user.name`/`user.email` (`Config.Key.USER_NAME/USER_EMAIL`, jj/cli/Config.kt:13-14; the Settings page already shows an "effective identity" with provenance, jj-idea-i0e6: JujutsuConfigurable.kt effectiveIdentityLabel); `LogEntry.author: VcsUser?` has name+email. Matching rule must be email-first (names collide/vary): `author.email.equals(me.email, ignoreCase = true)`, fallback to exact name match only when the email is blank on either side.
Design:
1. `CurrentUserService` (project service, `repo -> Identity?` cache): resolves via `repo.commandExecutor.configGet("user.email")`/`user.name` (CommandExecutor.configGet :595; one call each per repo, cached until the config changes: invalidate on `stateModel` op change? config changes don't create ops; invalidate on Settings apply (identity override UI) and on explicit refresh; plus a TTL of 10 minutes) - resolved on a pooled thread; the renderer reads `identityOrNull(repo)` (non-blocking, null until loaded -> shows authors normally, then a repaint after load via `table.repaint()` through a notifier). Per-repo because multi-root repos can have different identities.
2. Setting: `hideOwnAuthor: Boolean` (View options in the log toolbar popup next to column toggles + Settings > Log; default OFF to preserve current behaviour - "Small polish item": opt-in). Alternative rendering modes: hide (empty cell) vs subdue (grey text): v1 = grey/subdued, because an empty cell can be mistaken for "unknown author" and the pending-entry renderer already uses empty for null authors (UserCellRenderer null value -> nothing). Rec: SUBDUE own rows (author text greyed + italic) when the toggle is on; hide-completely as the toggle's second state is YAGNI. Reverse: make it empty.
3. Renderer: `UserCellRenderer.render` consults `(table as? JujutsuLogTable)?.isOwnAuthor(entry)`; the column value is the VcsUser (value-based renderer, no entry) - the renderer needs the row's entry: `table.model.getEntry(row)` is available in TextTableCellRenderer.customizeCellRenderer (it already does `model?.getEntry(row)` for `isWorkingCopyRow`, TextTableCellRenderer.kt:~33) - expose `isOwnAuthorRow` the same way. Committer column: apply the same rule (committer == me).
4. Tooltip still shows the email (UserCellRenderer sets `toolTipText = value.email`) - unchanged so the information remains reachable.
Decisions made without the user: Q: subdue vs hide? Rec subdue. Q: default? Rec off. Q: details pane? Rec unchanged.
Scale: O(1) per painted cell (string compare); identity resolved once per repo (2 jj calls). Operation-count test: 1000 repaints => 0 config calls after the first.
Testing: matcher unit tests (email case-insensitive; name fallback; blank email; null author); service test with stub executor (resolved once, null before load, invalidation); renderer test (subdued attributes when own + toggle on; normal otherwise); settings round-trip; manual: MT-LOG-TABLE (toggle on: own rows grey, others normal; multi-root with different identities; no jj identity configured -> nothing changes). Regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-SETTINGS.
acceptance_criteria: Optional (default off) subdued author/committer cells for the current user's own commits, email-first matching per repo identity; cached identity lookup; tests + MT-LOG-TABLE rows.

title: Graph: elide/compact graph-style toggle
description: jjx supports compact and extended graph display modes (jjx.graphStyle), plus rendering elided commits like the jj CLI. Our JujutsuCommitGraph has no such toggle. Investigate adding a compact/extended display option for the commit graph rendering.
design:
PLAN (pass-2 / needs-your-review): the bead is an "investigate" item from the jjx comparison (jjx has `jjx.graphStyle` compact/extended + elided-commit rendering like the jj CLI). Findings and a recommended scope:
1. "Rendering elided commits like the jj CLI" = jj-idea-hlu3 (elided edges for filtered logs; already designed) - NOT part of this toggle; link, don't duplicate.
2. "Compact vs extended" in jjx (and the jj CLI's `ui.graph.style`/`--graph` styles: ascii/curved/square) is about graph glyph style AND row density: jj's graph styles are line-art variants (that's jj-idea-jnv: straight vs curved - designed). The remaining distinct idea is ROW DENSITY: today one line per commit (summary on one row, `ROW_HEIGHT` 22 JBValue, JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.kt:42) vs an "extended" two-line row (description first line; second line: author - date - bookmarks) like GitHub Desktop / Fork. That is a larger change: row height is a table-wide constant used by hit-testing, the edge index (row-based, not pixel-based), DnD drop zones, hover geometry and LaidOutCell layout.
Recommendation (reversible):
 A. Do NOT build a separate "elide/compact toggle" bead: close this as split into existing beads: hlu3 (elided rendering), jnv (graph line style), and a NEW small decision bead only if you want "extended rows".
 B. If extended rows are wanted, design: setting `logRowDensity: COMPACT|COMFORTABLE|EXTENDED` (per window) mapped to `ROW_HEIGHT` {22, 28, 44}; EXTENDED draws the existing left text on line 1 and moves right-side decorations/author/date into a second line (`LaidOutCell.forRow` returns two rows of fragments; `TruncatingLeftRightLayout` gains a two-line mode; the Author/Date columns are hidden in this mode since the info moves inline). Graph painter: the node circle stays vertically centred on the FIRST line (not the row centre) - `commitY` computed from a `GRAPH_NODE_Y_OFFSET`; passthrough lines span the full row height (unchanged); edge/hover/DnD math unchanged because they are row-indexed - only pixel geometry for hit tests (`rowAtPoint` is height-agnostic). Scale: LaidOutCell cost doubles per visible row (bounded by visible rows, see g7to caching bead); no data-layer cost.
 C. A cheap interim "compact" mode: reduce ROW_HEIGHT to 18 and drop chip padding - purely UI scale: but IntelliJ's own VCS log has "Compact References View"/`vcs.log.compact.references`? (check platform: `PrintElementGeneratorImpl`... not needed).
Decisions made without the user: Q1: split/close or implement? Rec: close this bead after creating `jj-idea-<new>: Log row density (compact/extended two-line rows)` ONLY if you want it - not auto-created (needs your product call). Q2: keep as P3? Rec: the new bead P4.
Scale/Testing/Manual: n/a for the closure; for B: row-height-parametrised renderer tests, graph-geometry tests at 3 densities, MT-LOG-TABLE/MT-LOG-GRAPH/MT-DND full pass (shared surface -> broad pass).
acceptance_criteria: Bead resolved by splitting into hlu3 (elided), jnv (line style) and an optional new row-density bead (user decision), or closed.

title: Push bookmark to all tracking remotes (one-click)
description: jjx offers a single-click action to upload a bookmark/tag to all of its tracking remotes at once. We only have the per-remote push dialog (GitPushDialog). Add a quick one-click convenience action, e.g. in the bookmark context menu, alongside the existing per-remote push flow.
close_reason: Shipped: --change push scope + default-push-scope setting, and push-to-all-remotes submenu entry.

title: Bookmark/tag chip hover background doesn't update on horizontal mouse movement within a row
description:
Hovering a bookmark/tag chip highlights its background (HoverCue.REF_BACKGROUND, jj-idea-a52h), computed correctly per-paint from the live table.mousePosition in JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.configureTextPanel (rightHighlightTarget, ~line 179). But that computation only actually gets painted when something triggers a repaint of the row.

Root cause: JujutsuLogTable.kt's mouseMoved handler (~lines 188-226) only calls repaintRow() in two cases - when the hovered row changes, or when hasHoverCue-target tracking (hoveredLinkRow/hoveredLinkCol) changes. hasHoverCue is always false for bookmark/tag chips (jj-idea-wkcz - they're right-click only, no left-click hint), so moving the mouse sideways between two different bookmark/tag chips within the same row never changes hoveredLinkRow/Col and never triggers a repaint. The highlight only actually updates when the row itself is (re)entered from above/below, matching the user's report: "the bookmark hover background only registers when approaching a chip from above or below... approaching from the side, the background never changes."

Fix direction: the repaint trigger needs to also fire when the REF_BACKGROUND-cued target itself changes (not just when hasHoverCue flips), e.g. by tracking the resolved LogClickTarget/its hoverCue (or just the raw URI from clickTargetAt) alongside hoveredLinkRow/Col, and repainting whenever that changes regardless of hasHoverCue.

Related to jj-idea-ttmp (sibling bead): giving the +N more overflow chip a background highlight too - fix this repaint bug first or together, since testing that bead's fix depends on repaints actually happening reliably on hover.
design:
PLAN: make the chip hover repaint fire whenever the hovered REF target changes, not only when `hasHoverCue` flips. The bead's own design is right; this makes it concrete against current code.
Facts: `JujutsuLogTable.refreshHoverState(point)` (ui/log/JujutsuLogTable.kt:~594-650; called from the mouseMoved listener :222-227 and the viewport-scroll listener) repaints (a) when the hovered ROW changes (`hoveredRow`, :~597-601) and (b) when `hoveredLinkRow/Col` changes, where `newHoveredLinkRow = if (showsHoverCue) newRow else -1` and `showsHoverCue = target?.hasHoverCue == true` (:~626, :644-651). `LogClickTarget.hasHoverCue` is false for BookmarkClick/TagClick/WorkingCopyClick (LogClickTarget.kt:172-173; they have no left-click action, jj-idea-wkcz) but their `hoverCue` is `HoverCue.REF_BACKGROUND` (:183-186). The renderer paints the chip background from the live `table.mousePosition` per paint (JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.configureTextPanel ~:228-232, `rightHighlightTarget`), so only the repaint trigger is missing: sliding from chip A to chip B within one row changes no tracked state => no repaint.
Fix:
1. Track the hovered fragment identity: new field `hoveredRefTarget: URI?` (or the resolved `LogClickTarget`'s key) updated in `refreshHoverState` from the already-computed `target` (`clickTargetAt(point)` is computed once per move, :~626): `val newRefTarget = target?.takeIf { it.hoverCue == HoverCue.REF_BACKGROUND }?.let { it.uri/ key }`. If `newRefTarget != hoveredRefTarget` -> `repaintRow(newRow)` (and the old row if the row changed - already handled by the row-change branch; when the row changed, repaint both rows as today). Also repaint when leaving a chip to empty space in the same row (newRefTarget goes non-null -> null) - same comparison covers it.
2. mouseExited (JujutsuLogTable.kt:~251-262) must clear `hoveredRefTarget` and repaint that row (today it only clears `hoveredEdge`; also check `hoveredRow`/`hoveredLinkRow` cleanup there - cwr's design relies on hoveredRow being cleared on exit, so do both in one change).
3. The "+N more" overflow chip (MoreRefsClick, jj-idea-ttmp sibling bead) shares `REF_BACKGROUND` so is fixed by the same comparison.
4. Same scenario in the details pane (AtomicHtmlView) uses its own hover handling (isHovered, AtomicHtmlView.kt:111-161) - out of scope unless it exhibits the same lag (verify in manual test).
Decisions made without the user: none (bug fix as described).
Scale: O(1) per mouse move (one URI/key compare); repaint limited to the single row (existing `repaintRow`). Operation-count test: 100 mouse moves within one chip => 0 extra repaints; chip-to-chip move => exactly 1.
Testing: table test using the existing hover test seams (find how JujutsuLogTable hover is tested: `hoveredRow`/`hoveredLinkRow` public vars suggest direct tests; add `hoveredRefTarget` as `internal` + a repaint-counter seam): simulate `refreshHoverState` at two points over adjacent chips in one row, assert state changes and a repaint request; leaving to blank space; exit clears. Manual: MT-LOG-TABLE/MT-BOOKMARK: row with 3 chips; move the mouse sideways across them (background follows without leaving the row); fast sweep; overflow chip. Regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-DND (DnD hover state shares `refreshHoverState`? check JujutsuLogTableDnD uses clickTargetAt but not hover fields).
acceptance_criteria: Moving the mouse horizontally between two bookmark/tag chips in the same row updates which chip is highlighted, without needing to leave and re-enter the row.

title: +N more overflow chip has no hover background, unlike bookmark/tag chips
description:
The "+N more" overflow chip (MoreRefsClick) currently gets HoverCue.NONE (LogClickTarget.kt:170) - hovering shows a hand cursor but no background highlight, unlike bookmark/tag chips which get HoverCue.REF_BACKGROUND (LogClickTarget.kt:168, added in jj-idea-a52h). This was an intentional choice at the time (jj-idea-w61m; see docs/manual-tests.md's "not the grey background highlight" bullet), reasoned that the hand cursor was cue enough since it IS left-clickable (opens the hidden-refs popup) unlike bookmark/tag chips (right-click only).

User feedback (jj-idea-lm3o follow-up): this is confusing in practice. Expected behavior, matching bookmark/tag chips: on hover, the background should change as a visual cue that the element is at least right-clickable, and after right-clicking, it should be obvious what was clicked (i.e. the highlight should make the target unambiguous, not just the cursor).

Likely fix: give MoreRefsClick its own HoverCue (or reuse REF_BACKGROUND) instead of NONE, and verify JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.configureTextPanel (rightHighlightTarget) picks it up the same way it does for bookmark/tag chips. Also affects docs/manual-tests.md's MT-LOG-GRAPH bullet describing the current (no-background) behavior as expected.

Related to jj-idea-kba2 (sibling bead): mouse movement within the same row not always triggering the repaint needed to show these highlights - fix that one first or together, since testing this bead's fix depends on repaints actually happening on hover.
design: Change LogClickTarget.hoverCue's MoreRefsClick branch from HoverCue.NONE to HoverCue.REF_BACKGROUND (or a new dedicated cue if it should look distinct from a bookmark/tag chip highlight). Update JujutsuLogTable.kt's mouseMoved doc comment (currently explains why bookmark/tag chips get no hover cue - the +N chip is a different case, already hasHoverCue=true). Update docs/manual-tests.md's MT-LOG-GRAPH bullet and hoverCue tests in LogClickTargetTest.kt.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering the +N more chip shows the same grey background highlight as a bookmark/tag chip, in addition to the existing hand cursor; right-clicking it makes clear what was targeted.
close_reason: Shipped: MoreRefsClick now gets HoverCue.REF_BACKGROUND instead of NONE, matching bookmark/tag chips. One-line change in LogClickTarget.kt; test and manual-tests.md updated.

title: JujutsuBookmarkWidget no longer fits JujutsuFilterComponent's filter contract
description: JujutsuBookmarkWidget extends JujutsuFilterComponent but isValueSelected() is hardcoded false and doResetFilter() is a no-op (:50-52) -- it was never really a filter. Adding a closest-bookmark+distance indicator (jj-idea-l7wd) makes it plainly a status+actions control instead. Keep the base class for now (toolbar layout/overflow behaviour still useful); revisit deliberately when/if a dedicated bookmarks panel (jj-idea-b2ae/#48) is considered, rather than letting this drift.
close_reason: Resolved by jj-idea-cpno: the widget is no longer a JujutsuFilterComponent at all — it moved to a native ExpandableComboAction main-toolbar widget (ui/toolbar/JujutsuBookmarkToolbarWidget.kt) with a status-bar fallback, so the filter-contract mismatch this issue tracked no longer applies.

title: Chip text (bookmark/tag/author/date) cannot be selected, copied, or pasted
description: Bookmark/tag chips and other 'unbreakable' content (author , mid-dot+date) render via AtomicHtmlView as a single opaque element in the outer document (IconAwareHtmlPane). The chip's actual text lives only in the URL-encoded src attribute, not in the Swing Document's real character content, so standard text selection/copy over that range yields nothing useful for the chip - confirmed via jj history that this has been true since chips were first made atomic (d15c69506c43, jj-idea-kds1), not something introduced by the recent AtomicHtmlView redesign. Reported by the user as a 'nasty regression' when testing the commit details pane, even though it predates this session. Proper fix likely requires a custom TransferHandler/copy override on IconAwareHtmlPane: when building the copied text for a selection, walk the selected range's elements and substitute decoded, HTML-stripped plain text for any '' or '' element found, since the Document's own getText() can't see it. Restructuring the encoding itself to preserve real document text isn't compatible with the underlying -atomicity trick (a genuine HTML void element is what makes chips survive JBHtmlPane's Jsoup transpile as a single atomic unit - see jj-idea-vll4/jj-idea-m2wr).
notes: Related to jj-idea-myje (GitHub #77): myje fixed description text getting corrupted to NBSPs on copy/paste in the HTML details pane by removing the blanket space->nbsp conversion in Formatters.escapeHtml (replaced with an explicit TextCanvas.space() primitive for deliberate icon/chip gaps). This issue (chip text itself being uncopyable) is a separate, complementary problem in the same pane - the chip's real text lives only in the URL-encoded src attribute, not in the Swing Document's character content, so it needs its own TransferHandler/copy override. Not addressed by myje. FIXED. Plain-text copy only; the deliberate nbsp gaps between chips (TextCanvas.space()) are unchanged. Two parts: IconAwareHtmlPaneCopy.kt substitutes each chip's ChipContent.plainText (CopyableTextTransferHandler / copyableText), AND - found only by manual testing - the real Cmd/Ctrl+C never reaches a TransferHandler: the keymap binds it to EditorCopy, which wraps the pane as a TextComponentEditor and reads chips as the placeholder char. So IconAwareHtmlPane is now a UiDataProvider supplying COPY_PROVIDER (CopyableTextCopyProvider) and registers the platform Copy action on itself (EmptyAction.registerWithShortcutSet(ACTION_COPY, CommonShortcuts.getCopy(), pane)), which outranks the keymap. Pinned by IconAwareHtmlPaneCopyWiringTest (platform). Manual results 2026-10-01: Cmd+A/Cmd+C in details panel pastes bookmark/tag chips, 'Name · date'; issue-link refs in description and bookmark name copy as plain text; tooltip copy works (tooltip closes on the key press, existing behaviour); description line has ordinary spaces; Copy Description unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: Automate: large ignored-file set cap (IGNORE_REPORT_CAP)
description: docs/manual-tests.md MT-IGNORE has a manual check that the ignored-file report cap (IGNORE_REPORT_CAP, 50,000 entries) triggers the 'very large' notification and that 'disable scanning' empties the Ignored Files node — this only needs a large synthetic ignored-file set, not a real repo or rendering. Good candidate for a unit test similar to GitignoreScanTest.kt. Once automated, remove the corresponding manual checkbox requiring a >50k-entry repo.
design:
PLAN: automate the MT-IGNORE "large ignored set" checks (cap triggers the 'very large' notification; 'disable scanning' empties the Ignored Files node) using the existing test seams; delete the >50k-entry manual bullet.
Facts: `IGNORE_REPORT_CAP = 50_000` (vcs/ignore/JujutsuIgnoredFilesService.kt:38); `JujutsuChangeProvider.reportIgnoredFiles(repo, builder, ignoredService, onCap)` (vcs/changes/JujutsuChangeProvider.kt:~94-110) is `internal` with an injectable `onCap: (Int) -> Unit` (default `JujutsuNotifications.notifyIgnoreScanLarge(project, repo, count)`, JujutsuNotifications.kt:363) - when `entries.size > IGNORE_REPORT_CAP` it calls `onCap(size)` and reports NOTHING, else reports each entry via `builder.processIgnoredFile`. The "disable scanning" action in the notification sets the per-repo `disableIgnoredFileScanning` (RepositoryConfig.kt:12; `JujutsuSettings.disableIgnoredFileScanning(repo)` :128 with app-level default JujutsuApplicationSettings.kt:41) which makes the service report an empty set (verify in `JujutsuIgnoredFilesService.ignoredForRepo`/scan gating).
Tests (pure JVM where possible; mock `JujutsuIgnoredFilesService.ignoredForRepo(repo).filePaths()` to return a synthetic list - build N `LocalFilePath` objects (50_001) cheaply with fake paths; the `FilePath` factory `VcsUtil.getFilePath(String)` needs the platform; use `LocalFilePath(path, false)` which is lightweight):
 1. cap boundary: exactly 50_000 entries -> all reported (`builder.processIgnoredFile` called 50_000 times via a counting fake ChangelistBuilder), `onCap` not called; 50_001 -> `onCap(50_001)` called once, zero builder calls (operation-count test = also the scale test required by contributing.md: reporting cost O(min(entries, cap)) and O(1) beyond cap).
 2. repeated refresh with a large set notifies once per refresh?? `notifyIgnoreScanLarge` is described as "one-shot" (JujutsuNotifications.kt:360-390): test its de-dup latch with a fake notifier or the real one under `@TestApplication` (assert at most one balloon for repeated calls for the same repo; a different repo gets its own).
 3. disable-scanning outcome: with `disableIgnoredFileScanning(repo) == true`, `JujutsuIgnoredFilesService.ignoredForRepo(repo)` returns empty and `reportIgnoredFiles` reports nothing and does NOT call onCap; toggle the setting back -> reports again after rescan (service-level platform test like JujutsuTrackedFilesServicePlatformTest, driving `scan` directly with a stub scan root).
 4. The action callback: invoke the notification's "disable scanning" action handler (the lambda passed in notifyIgnoreScanLarge) via a seam (`onDisable` param or capturing the Notification actions from the test's NotificationGroup) -> asserts the per-repo setting flips and the ignored set empties (end-to-end of bullet 2).
Manual bullet to delete: the one requiring a >50k-entry repo (MT-IGNORE ~:59 '→ automate: jj-idea-s0ab'); keep the notification wording check if it is visual (balloon text) - covered by 2 if message text asserted.
Decisions made without the user: Q: use real notification or seam? Rec seam + one real-notification test. 
Scale: test-only but includes the O(min(n, cap)) assertion. Acceptance: tests pass; manual bullet removed; ./gradlew check green.
acceptance_criteria: Cap boundary (50,000 vs 50,001), one-shot notification, disable-scanning outcome and action callback covered by tests incl. operation-count; manual >50k bullet removed.

title: Automate: .gitignore file coloring and propagation
description: docs/manual-tests.md MT-IGNORE has manual checks that ignored directories/files (and nested children) are colored correctly in the Project tree — a file-classification check against GitignoreCache/JujutsuIgnoreService, testable without rendering. Once automated, remove the corresponding manual checkboxes.
design:
PLAN: automate the MT-IGNORE "Project Tool Window - ignored file coloring" checks (docs/manual-tests.md MT-IGNORE ~lines 9-31) as classification tests; delete the corresponding manual bullets.
What the colouring depends on (no rendering involved): the platform asks `IgnoredFileProvider.isIgnoredFile(project, filePath)` - implemented by `JujutsuIgnoredFileProvider` (vcs/changes/JujutsuIgnoredFileProvider.kt: `.jj/` always ignored; otherwise `JujutsuIgnoreService.isIgnored(filePath, repo.directory)` -> GitignoreCache.isIgnored(File)) and the platform's `FileStatusManager` maps ignored -> IGNORED status colour. "Parent propagation" = nested children of an ignored directory (e.g. `build/classes/Main.class`) are ignored because the matcher treats everything under an ignored dir as ignored (GitignoreCache `file inside ignored directory is also ignored` test exists: GitignoreCacheTest.kt:55,61) - so the classification layer is already unit-covered at the cache level; what the manual bullets add is the PROVIDER wiring + the platform status mapping.
Tests to add (platform-tagged, `@TestApplication` + project fixture + a temp jj-less directory laid out with real files; no jj subprocess needed since the provider only needs `possibleJujutsuRepositoryFor` - check whether it requires an initialised jj repo (`.jj` dir present) and create a minimal `.jj` marker as other platform tests do, e.g. vcs/ignore/JujutsuTrackedFilesServicePlatformTest.kt):
 1. `JujutsuIgnoredFileProviderTest`: `isIgnoredFile` true for `build/` and `.gradle/` dirs and nested `build/classes/Main.class`; false for `src/Main.kt` and tracked files; `.jj/**` always true; file outside any repo false; after editing `.gitignore` (VFS refresh/`JujutsuIgnoreService.invalidate`) the answer changes (propagation of rule edits - bullets at ~:31-32: remove `*.xyz` rule -> not ignored).
 2. Status mapping: `FileStatusManager.getInstance(project).getStatus(vf)` returns `FileStatus.IGNORED` for ignored vfs (requires the ChangeListManager to have scanned; use `VcsDirtyScopeManager.markEverythingDirty` + `ChangeListManagerImpl.waitEverythingDoneInTestMode()`; if flaky, assert at provider level only and keep ONE manual bullet for the visible colour).
 3. Unversioned-vs-ignored distinction bullet (:31-32 "unversioned colour (green/teal)" after removing the ignore rule) belongs to jj-idea-3oxa (untracked files) behaviour: under default auto-track the file is TRACKED not unversioned - verify the manual text; mark that bullet as stale/changed by 3oxa rather than automate it.
Manual bullets to delete after tests pass: the three colouring bullets (:11-13 build/.gradle gray incl. nested, src/ not gray). KEEP: anything that needs the visual Project view colour itself unless step 2 proves stable.
Decisions made without the user: Q: how much of the platform status path to automate? Rec: provider + `FileStatusManager` check if stable, else provider only (and keep a one-line manual visual check). Q: remove the manual subsection? Rec: shrink to the single visual check.
Scale: tests only; add an operation-count assertion that `isIgnoredFile` for 1000 calls performs zero filesystem traversals (cache hits only - spy on `GitignoreCache.getNode` count).
Related: jj-idea-2poe (matcher semantics), jj-idea-otwq (enablement), jj-idea-1lqp.
acceptance_criteria: Provider/status tests cover ignored dirs, nested children, tracked files, rule edits, .jj exclusion; manual colouring bullets removed or reduced to one visual check; ./gradlew check green.

title: Automate: tracked-toggle cache semantics (JujutsuTrackedFilesService)
description: docs/manual-tests.md MT-IGNORE has manual checks for the Tracked checkbox's async-cache semantics (immediate-after-click authority, mixed-selection handling, revert-on-failure) — these are JujutsuTrackedFilesService state-machine behaviors, not rendering. Once automated, remove the corresponding manual checkboxes.
design:
PLAN: extend the existing platform tests around `JujutsuTrackedFilesService` + `TrackedToggleAction` to cover the manual MT-IGNORE "Tracked toggle" bullets (docs/manual-tests.md ~:3115-3150, '→ automate: jj-idea-me8m'), then delete the covered bullets.
Existing coverage: `JujutsuTrackedFilesServicePlatformTest` (vcs/ignore/: cache read/write + dedup via direct `refresh` calls, optimistic `setKnown`), `TrackUntrackAvailabilityTest` (actions/file/: pure helpers `isFullyTracked`, `pathsNeedingChange`, `trackedToggleVisible`, `anySelectedIgnored`). Not covered: the ACTION-level state machine in `TrackedToggleAction` (actions/file/TrackedToggleAction.kt:58-150): `isSelected` reads (cache first, then ChangeListManager shortcut, then safe untracked default + requestRefresh, `resolveTrackedPaths`), `setSelected` optimistic write (`trackedService.setKnown(repo, toChange, state)` BEFORE the command runs), success path (no cache invalidation; `invalidate(vfsChanged = true)`; ignored-files invalidate; notification text incl. stderr warning passthrough), failure path (`setKnown(!state)` revert + error notification), mixed selection (`pathsNeedingChange` -> only the changing subset reaches `fileTrack`/`fileUntrack`; checkbox reads unchecked for mixed).
Tests (platform-tagged like the service test; action driven with a fake `AnActionEvent` via `TestActionEvent`/`MapDataContext`, or by extracting the logic):
 1. Immediate authority: setSelected(true) then `isSelected` == true BEFORE the command completes (command stub blocks on a latch) and still true after success (regression of the earlier revert bug).
 2. Mixed selection: one tracked + one untracked path (cache pre-populated) -> `isSelected` false; setSelected(true) calls `fileTrack` with ONLY the untracked path (verify args: `fileTrackArgs` includes `--include-ignored`, CliExecutor.kt - covered by an args test); cache then reports both tracked.
 3. Untrack of an already-untracked member: stub returns success with stderr `Warning: No matching entries for paths: ...` -> notification message contains that text (assert on a captured `JujutsuNotifications.notify` via a seam or `Notifications` bus subscription).
 4. Failure revert: command returns failure -> cache entries revert to `!state` and an ERROR notification fires; `isSelected` returns the pre-click state.
 5. Predicted-ignored gating: non-ignored path -> action invisible (`trackedToggleVisible`), directories -> hidden (`hasDirectory` rule at update()).
 6. Dedup/in-flight: repeated `isSelected` calls while a refresh is pending enqueue ONE `jj file list` (service test exists - extend for the action path).
Manual bullets to delete: the five listed (checkbox flips immediately/stays, uncheck, multi-select mixed, warning text surfaced, failure revert). KEEP: the visible-progress-in-status-bar/balloon visuals and the end-to-end "file actually appears in jj file list" (needs real jj - this belongs to a contract test: `fileTrack --include-ignored` on an ignored file; add `FileTrackContractCliTest` if absent; check src/test/.../contract for track tests first).
Decisions made without the user: Q: refactor `setSelected` to a testable function (inject executor/service/notifier)? Rec yes, small: extract `performToggle(project, repo, toChange, state, services)`; avoids heavy action-event plumbing in tests.
Scale: tests only. Acceptance: tests pass; manual bullets reduced to the visual/e2e ones; ./gradlew check green.
acceptance_criteria: Action-level tests cover immediate authority, mixed selection, warning passthrough, failure revert; covered manual bullets removed; contract test for --include-ignored tracking exists.

title: Automate: graph layout under filtering
description: docs/manual-tests.md MT-LOG-GRAPH has a manual check that graph lines realign to visible rows only under text/author/date/root filtering, with no stale passthrough lines. LayoutCalculator.kt computes this deterministically — a good candidate for an assertable unit test similar to GraphLayoutScaleTest.kt. Once automated, remove the manual subsection.
design:
PLAN: replace the four manual checks in docs/manual-tests.md MT-LOG-GRAPH > "Graph layout under filtering (jj-idea-7jkr)" (lines ~90-101) with assertable unit tests, then delete that subsection (leaving a one-line pointer to the test class per contributing.md's "Automate vs manual" rule).
Where the logic lives: filtering recomputes the graph via `UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.refreshDisplayedGraph()` (ui/log/UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.kt:212): `graphBuilder.buildGraph(model.getFilteredEntries(), model.getAllEntries())` when a filter hides rows, else reuses `fullGraphNodes`; layout is `CommitGraphBuilder` -> `LayoutCalculatorImpl` (ui/log/graph/). Existing tests: ui/log/graph/LayoutCalculatorTest.kt, GraphLayoutScaleTest.kt, IncrementalLayoutEquivalenceTest.kt.
Tests to add (new `FilteredGraphLayoutTest` in src/test/.../ui/log/graph/, pure JVM, no platform):
 1. Invariant checker `assertGraphConsistent(visibleEntries, graph)`: (a) every visible row has exactly one node; (b) every edge/passthrough lane references only visible rows or an explicit unresolved-parent stub (ParentState.HIDDEN/NOT_LOADED) - no lane line extends toward a hidden commit (the "stale passthrough" symptom); (c) lanes reach their parents' rows in row order (no edge pointing upward past its parent); (d) no empty lanes persist after the last use. Reuse the same shapes `GraphEdgeIndex` exposes (ui/log/GraphEdgeIndex.kt) as the oracle where possible.
 2. Fixtures built in-code from FX-STRESS-like shapes (a generator `branchyHistory(trunk=60, branches=20, octopus=true, deep=100)` - do not shell out to scripts/fixtures/fx-stress.sh in a unit test; mirror its topology: main trunk, short feature branches, long branches, deep branch, octopus merge). 
 3. Cases: text filter (hide ~50% pseudo-randomly with fixed seed, plus structured: hide a whole branch; hide a merge's one parent chain), author filter, date range, root filter (multi-root: two entry sets), clear-filter => `buildGraph(all, all)` result equals the original unfiltered graph (map equality, tests the "returns to full layout immediately" bullet), idempotence (filter A then B then clear == original), and incremental append after filter bails to full rebuild (see hlu3 note).
 4. Rapid-typing bullet (converges within ~250 ms, no flicker): automate the DEBOUNCE logic, not the timing: find the filter debounce in JujutsuLogTableModel/filter component (grep `onFilterApplied`, MergingUpdateQueue/Alarm) and test with a fake clock/queue that N keystrokes within the window produce ONE recompute (operation-count test: counts buildGraph invocations). If the debounce is not injectable, add a minimal seam (constructor-injected scheduler) - small production change, note it.
 5. Property test (seeded, 200 random DAGs x random hide sets, kotest `checkAll` if already a dependency, else a plain loop with fixed seed printed on failure) running the invariant checker - catches the class of bug jj-idea-xi58/1ojh fixed.
Decisions made without the user: Q: property tests in unit scope? Rec yes, deterministic seed, <2s total. Q: keep any manual bullet? Rec: keep NONE of the four except add one smoke line "filtered graph looks right visually" is NOT needed since renderer is covered by hlu3 manual rows; delete the subsection per bead acceptance.
Scale: tests include a 10k-entry filtered build with an operation-count assertion mirroring GraphLayoutScaleTest (layout O(n + e); no per-row rescans).
Manual regression scope after deleting the subsection: none lost; MT-LOG-GRAPH keeps rendering checks.
acceptance_criteria: FilteredGraphLayoutTest covers text/author/date/root filters, clear-filter equality, debounce single-recompute, random DAG property test; manual subsection removed from docs/manual-tests.md with pointer; ./gradlew check green.

title: Automate: log search — Git hash matching, filter AND-combination, regex/case toggles
description: docs/manual-tests.md MT-LOG-FILTER has manual checks for Git-hash search (prefix/case-insensitive matching), filter AND-combination, and regex/case-sensitivity toggles — pure LogFilterMatcher logic, no rendering dependency. Once automated, remove the corresponding manual checkboxes.
design:
PLAN: audit-and-prune, because the unit coverage largely exists already; then delete the corresponding manual checkboxes.
Existing coverage (verified by test names): ui/log/LogFilterMatcherTest.kt - blank/whitespace queries, substring, case-insensitive default, case-sensitive, whole words, change-id prefix (+ divergent forms), commit-hash prefix (`matches by commit hash prefix` :240, `does not match commit hash mid-string fragment` :253), regex (`substring match uses containsMatchIn` :143, respects case :160, invalid regex falls back to literal :168), bookmark name matching. ui/log/JujutsuLogTableModelFilterTest.kt - description/change id/author/email, case toggles, whole words, FULL and ABBREVIATED git hash (:221, :236), hash case-insensitive (:251), hash not loaded -> no match (:264), substring-not-prefix negatives (:279, :294), regex matches/groups/invalid/case (:311-358), multi-author, bookmark/revset key filters, and `Combined filters` (:644: `text and author filters combine with AND` :646, `all filters combine with AND` :663, root filter combination :898).
Manual items to retire (docs/manual-tests.md MT-LOG-FILTER lines ~614-632): (1) "text search filters in real-time; regex and case-sensitivity toggles both work" (:614-615); (2) "multiple active filters combine correctly (AND logic)" (:618); (3) the "Search by Git commit hash (jj-idea-odzo)" subsection bullets 1-3 (full hash, prefix, uppercase) - bullet 4 (hash not loaded -> Enter -> whole-repo search) is a different feature (lpbv) and STAYS (needs the real UI + jj).
Gaps to check/fill (small): (a) "in real-time" = debounce + EDT application - not covered by matcher tests; add a test of the filter component's debounce seam if one exists (same seam as jj-idea-2k2b item 4) else leave that single phrase manual; (b) AND-combination covers text+author and "all filters"; confirm the "all filters" test includes bookmark/reference AND date AND root (read :663 - if date filter missing add it) and a negative: any single non-matching filter excludes the entry; (c) hash matching with uppercase via the UI path (`JujutsuLogTableModel` + component) exists at model level (:251) - sufficient; (d) full 40-char hash vs short/`shortest()` forms: matcher uses `prefixMatch(id.full) || prefixMatch(id.short)` for change ids; for commit ids confirm the same accepted forms are tested (full + shortest + longer-than-shortest prefix).
Steps: 1) read the cited tests, fill gaps (b)/(d) with 3-5 tests; 2) edit docs/manual-tests.md: delete the covered bullets, leave a one-line "covered by LogFilterMatcherTest/JujutsuLogTableModelFilterTest" note (the "→ automate" marker at :622 is replaced by this note), keep the whole-repo-search bullet; 3) check no other doc/`Also re-run:` line points at removed bullets (grep jj-idea-odzo, 4u7j).
Decisions made without the user: Q: leave a pointer note in the manual doc? Rec: yes, one line (matches how other automated sections are marked, e.g. MT-LOG-GRAPH). 
Scale: tests only. Acceptance: manual-tests.md no longer lists those checks; coverage gaps (b),(d) filled; ./gradlew check green. Manual regression scope: MT-LOG-FILTER shrinks - re-run only the remaining bullets.
acceptance_criteria: Gaps in filter AND-combination/hash-form tests filled; corresponding manual checkboxes removed with pointer note; whole-repo-search bullet retained; ./gradlew check green.

title: Automate: settings and column width/visibility persistence
description: docs/manual-tests.md MT-SETTINGS and MT-LOG-TABLE have manual checks that settings, column widths, and column visibility persist across IDE restarts — state-serialization logic (JujutsuSettingsState.kt / JujutsuColumnManager.kt), not rendering. Once automated, remove the corresponding manual checkboxes.
design:
PLAN: pure-JVM + light-platform round-trip tests for settings and log-window column persistence, then delete the matching manual bullets.
Persistence layer facts: project settings `JujutsuSettings : PersistentStateComponent<JujutsuSettingsState>` (settings/JujutsuSettings.kt; migrations v1-v4 in `loadState`), state class settings/JujutsuSettingsState.kt (`columnWidths`, `logWindows: MutableList<LogWindowConfig>`), per-window config `LogWindowConfig` (settings/LogWindowConfig.kt: `columnWidths: MutableMap<String,Int>`, selected repos, visibility flags) and the runtime `JujutsuColumnManager` (ui/log/JujutsuColumnManager.kt: `showRootGutterColumn/showAuthorColumn/showCommitterColumn/showDateColumn/showStatus/showChangeId/showDescription/showDecorations`, fit-to-width flag). Existing tests cover logChangeLimit overrides, migrations v1 and settingsVersion==4 (JujutsuSettingsTest), LogWindowConfig selectedRepos (LogWindowConfigTest), JujutsuSettingsPlatformTest.
Manual bullets to retire (docs/manual-tests.md): MT-SETTINGS "all settings persist across IDE restarts" (~:10, ~:44 "Restart the IDE - the setting persists"), MT-LOG-TABLE "Column widths and visibility both persist across IDE restarts" (:96) and "Column visibility, Fit Columns..., Details Right/Bottom toggles all still..." (:128), and the application-level "applies to every open project" setting (:123, a different store: JujutsuApplicationSettings - include).
Tests (the "restart" = serialize -> deserialize through the REAL xmlb serializer, which is exactly what the platform does on restart):
 1. `SettingsSerializationRoundTripTest` (pure JVM, no platform): populate a `JujutsuSettingsState` with a non-default value in EVERY persisted property (reflectively enumerate bean properties so a newly added field without a test value fails the test: assert all properties differ from defaults after the populate helper; helper uses a table of per-type sample values), `XmlSerializer.serialize(state)` (com.intellij.util.xmlb) -> `XmlSerializer.deserialize(element, JujutsuSettingsState::class.java)` -> assert deep equality property by property. Same for `JujutsuApplicationSettings` state, `LogWindowConfig` list (incl. map-typed columnWidths with several keys, repo override map `RepositoryConfig`s).
 2. Load path: `JujutsuSettings.loadState(roundTripped)` keeps values and leaves settingsVersion = current (migrations don't clobber saved v4 data); unknown/legacy XML (missing new fields) deserializes to defaults (forward compatibility).
 3. Column manager round-trip: `JujutsuColumnManager` <-> `LogWindowConfig` mapping (find the save/load glue in CommitTablePanel/UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel: functions that copy manager flags to config and back; extract into a pure `ColumnConfigMapper` if inlined, with a test: every flag + widths + fit-to-width survive config -> manager -> config).
 4. Light platform test (JujutsuSettingsPlatformTest style): `ComponentManager.getServiceByClass`, `getState()`, `loadState()` via the platform's `ComponentStoreImpl` is heavy - skip; serialization-level coverage is sufficient.
Decisions made without the user: Q: reflective "every property has a non-default sample" guard? Rec yes (prevents the classic silent miss when a field isn't annotated for serialization e.g. a `val` or `@Transient`). Q: keep any manual restart check? Rec: ONE manual smoke bullet "change a setting, restart the IDE, still set" remains in MT-SETTINGS (end-to-end wiring of the storage file `Storage("jujutsu.xml")`/workspace.xml per jj-idea-44db); delete the per-field ones.
Interaction: jj-idea-44db changes the project storage file to workspace.xml - tests at the serializer level are storage-agnostic, so unaffected; the migration test for 44db belongs there.
Scale: none. Acceptance: tests pass; manual bullets reduced to one smoke bullet; ./gradlew check green.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip serialization tests cover every persisted property incl. log window columns; reflective guard fails on unpersisted new fields; manual restart bullets reduced to one smoke check.

title: Automate: Squash Into description auto-population and validation
description: docs/manual-tests.md MT-SQUASH has manual checks for description auto-population (full/partial squash) and validation (button state, error messages) that are pure string/state logic with no rendering dependency — good candidates for a unit test alongside SquashIntoDialog.kt. Once automated, remove the corresponding manual checkboxes and the '→ automate:' marker in MT-SQUASH.
design:
PLAN: automate the squash description/validation checks as dialog-state tests and delete the matching manual bullets plus the '→ automate' marker (docs/manual-tests.md MT-SQUASH ~:1212).
Existing coverage: `SquashDescriptionTest` (ui/squash) covers only the pure `mergeDescriptions(parent, source[s])` helper (SquashIntoDialog.kt:79-83): both/empty/multiline joins. Dialog-level tests exist for modes/title/tooltips (SquashIntoDialogParentModeTest, ...PickSourcesModeTest, ...TitleTest, ...TooltipTest) and use `performOKForTest`/`selectPickerRowsForTest`/`descriptionText` seams (SquashIntoDialog.kt:165-185).
Logic under test (dialog code): `updateDescription()` (SquashIntoDialog.kt:497-523): skipped once the user typed (`userEditedDescription`); for PickDestination uses the selected destination's description (+ the fixed sources' descriptions), for PickSources the fixed destination's + selected sources'; `mergeDescriptions(dest, sources)` ONLY when `fileSelection.allIncluded && !isPartialSquash` else just the destination description (partial squash must not absorb source descriptions - comment at doOKAction); `doValidate()` (:535-548): no destination selected / no sources selected / no files included (and not a partial squash) -> `ValidationInfo` with the bundle messages `dialog.squash.into.destination.none` / `...source.none` / `...no.files`; OK enabled state follows `doValidate()` (DialogWrapper.setOKActionEnabled via validation).
Manual bullets to retire (MT-SQUASH "Destination picker": "Selecting a destination populates the description field (if user hasn't typed)", and the description/validation bullets "below" the automate marker: full vs partial squash description, "Field pre-fills correctly for each source/dest description combination: both non-empty..." (~:1293), "Switching back to all-files-selected restores the combined pre-fill (if user hasn't edited)" (~:1301), validation messages/button state). Read those sections (~:1212-1310) while implementing and map each to a test.
Tests to add (platform-tagged like the sibling dialog tests, `@TestApplication @RunInEdt`, using `createEntry`-style helpers; mind jj-idea-h8ys: stub `logService.getFileChanges` or use `SquashIntoDialog(..., changes = <explicit list>)` to avoid ClassCastException from relaxed mocks):
 1. Auto-population matrix: destination description D in {empty, "d"} x source description S in {empty, "s", multi-line} x mode (PickDestination single/multi-source, PickSources) -> `descriptionText` equals expected via mergeDescriptions.
 2. Partial squash (`applyPickedContent`/`setDestinationOverrideForTest` seam exists, :183): destination description only; switching back (clear overrides / re-tick all) restores combined pre-fill ONLY when the user hasn't edited (set text via editor to flip `userEditedDescription`, then toggle selection - text unchanged).
 3. File selection: unticking one file -> destination-only description; re-ticking -> combined again (drive `fileSelection` inclusion listener `onFileInclusionChanged` :265).
 4. Validation: no destination selected -> `doValidate()` message + `isOKActionEnabled == false`; none for sources in PickSources; zero files included -> message; partial squash with zero whole-file inclusions but overrides present -> valid (the `!isPartialSquash` clause); all valid -> null.
 5. User-edit stickiness: after typing, selecting another destination does not overwrite.
Decisions made without the user: Q: pure-extraction of `updateDescription` into a function `resolveSquashDescription(dest, sources, allIncluded, partial, userEdited, current)` to allow JVM tests without the platform? Rec yes - small refactor makes 80% of the matrix pure JVM (fast), leaving only a couple of platform tests for the wiring.
Scale: none. Acceptance: tests pass; manual bullets deleted with pointer note; ./gradlew check green. Manual regression scope: MT-SQUASH shrinks to rendering/DnD/tooltips/preview.
acceptance_criteria: Description auto-population/stickiness/validation covered by tests (pure resolve function + dialog wiring tests); covered manual bullets and automate marker removed.

title: Automate: Dialog commit-picker ordering (cold-cache logCache fetch)
description: docs/manual-tests.md MT-CTXMENU has a manual check that commit pickers (Rebase, Squash Into..., Duplicate Onto..., Move Bookmark to Change) show correct order on a cold logCache — a cache/ordering invariant, not rendering. Good candidate for a unit/integration test. Once automated, remove the manual subsection.
design:
PLAN: automate the cold-cache ordering checks (MT-CTXMENU "cold logCache" subsection, ~docs/manual-tests.md:98-125 under '→ automate: jj-idea-pa05') and delete the manual bullets.
Invariant under test (from `RepoLogCache` KDoc/code, jj/LogCache.kt): `all`/`get`/`loadContext` always return entries in topological order, newest first (children before parents), whether the cache was warmed by the main log window (`store(allEntries)` after a full load, UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:192) or cold-fetched (`fetch()` runs `topologicalSort(repo.logService.getLog(...).getOrThrow())`). CommitGraphBuilder/LayoutCalculator REQUIRE this order (docs/LOG_GRAPH_ALGORITHM.md) - the picker's graph connector lines in the manual bullets are a consequence, so ordering + a layout-validity check covers all three bullets. Existing tests: jj/RepoLogCacheTest.kt, RepoLogCacheScaleTest.kt (check which ordering cases exist: `rg 'fun \`' RepoLogCacheTest.kt`).
ALREADY COVERED in jj/RepoLogCacheTest.kt: `all topologically sorts a cold fetch, children before parents, even if jj log emitted parent first` (:221, = case 1 below, for one shape), `store deduplicates orderedIds` (:239), loadContext revset/window/empty cases (:253-284), reload (:299). So add cases 2-6 and extend case 1 to merges/octopus/multiple heads (property-style), not re-write it.
Tests to add (pure JVM with a stub `LogService` returning entries in a shuffled/jj-native order; `RepoLogCache` needs a `JujutsuRepository` (mock with `logService`, `project` for the VCS listener subscription - see the existing test's setup)):
 1. Cold `all`: stub returns entries in REVERSE/shuffled order (oldest first, as jj can with certain revsets/`--reversed`, and merges interleaved) -> `cache.all` is topologically sorted newest-first; root last; every child index < every parent index (property assertion over a generated DAG with merges/branches).
 2. Cold `loadContext(id, window)`: same invariant on the returned window and on the stored cache (`all` after loadContext when cache was cold? `snapshot()` semantics: stores window entries; `all` then returns snapshot (partial!) - check: after `loadContext` on a cold cache, `snapshot()` returns the stored subset and `all` skips the full fetch - a possible correctness issue (picker would show only the context window until reload). Characterise this explicitly; if real, fix (loadContext should not mark the cache "complete") and file/describe in the bead).
 3. Warm-by-store: `store(entries)` with the loader's already-sorted order, then `all` equals insertion order; `store` of a second batch (expansion) keeps total topological validity? (`orderedIds` LinkedHashSet remove+reinsert: merging a later batch could place children after parents) -> assert invariant after `store(A)` then `store(B)` where B contains ancestors AND descendants of A's entries; if violated, `snapshot()` must re-sort (O(n log n) once per store, acceptable) - fix with the test.
 4. Multi-repo: two caches, each ordered independently; entries of repo A never appear in repo B (key includes repo) - the manual "multi-repo" bullets (a merged main-log load stores per-repo via `allEntries.groupBy { it.repo }.forEach { store }`, UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:192): test the grouping preserves each repo's relative order from the merged list (merged list is globally sorted; per-repo subsequence must still be topologically valid - true by construction; assert).
 5. Layout validity: feed `cache.all` into `CommitGraphBuilder.buildGraph` and run the 2k2b-style invariant checker (no edge pointing upward, lanes reach parents) - covers "graph connector lines correct".
 6. Picker wiring: `CommitPickerPanel` (ui/components/CommitPickerPanel.kt:123 `val loaded = repo.logCache.all`; :209 `entries = topologicalSort((entries + found).distinctBy { it.key })`) - a platform test constructing the panel with a stub repo whose cache returns shuffled entries and asserting `entries` order; and that whole-repo-search merges keep order.
Manual bullets to delete: all five in the subsection (cold single-repo order, graph lines, same-as-main-log order, multi-repo order, restart consistency). Keep none (restart repeatability is the same code path).
Decisions made without the user: Q: if tests 2/3 expose real violations, fix in this bead? Rec yes (small, in LogCache.kt) - they are exactly the kind of ordering regression this bead guards.
Scale: tests only; add an operation-count assertion that `all` on a warm cache performs no sort (counting sorter seam or time-free: spy `LogService.getLog` call count = 0 and `topologicalSort` not invoked - use the existing scale test style).
Acceptance: tests pass (and any discovered violation fixed); the manual subsection removed with a pointer note; ./gradlew check green. Regression scope after deletion: MT-CTXMENU minus cold-cache section.
acceptance_criteria: Ordering invariant tests for cold fetch, loadContext, store merges, multi-repo grouping, layout validity and picker wiring; discovered violations fixed; manual cold-cache subsection removed.

title: Automate: Split dialog validation, whole-file fast path, and binary gating
description: docs/manual-tests.md MT-SPLIT has manual checks (Validation, Whole-file fast path, Binary/conflicted files subsections) that are state/routing logic in SplitDialog.kt/HunkSelectionModel.kt, not rendering — good candidates for a unit test. Once automated, remove the corresponding manual checkboxes and the '→ automate:' marker in MT-SPLIT.
design:
PLAN: complete the Split dialog automation for the three MT-SPLIT subsections ('Validation', 'Whole-file fast path', 'Binary / conflicted files', docs/manual-tests.md MT-SPLIT ~lines 1520-1534 under '→ automate: jj-idea-ygtw') and delete those manual bullets + the marker. Much is already covered - verify, fill gaps.
Already covered (ui/split/SplitDialogTest.kt): validation fails when nothing ticked (:182), when all ticked (:194), passes mixed (:210), passes with nothing ticked but one partial pick (GitHub #117, :226), newParent mode rejects empty selection even with an override (:270), hunks-only split passes every file as fileset and carries picked remainder (:246), ok action yields null hunkSelection when no partial files (= whole-file fast path at dialog level, :307) and non-null with an override (:287), pickHunks button wiring (:475), newParent hides Pick Hunks (:428).
Manual bullets and their automation status:
 1. Validation - "nothing ticked ... same message in every mode (default, parallel, newParent)": the tests exist for default and newParent(:270); ADD parallel mode (checkbox on) and assert the exact bundle message `dialog.split.validation.new.empty` / `...stays.empty` identity across the three modes (parametrised test over modes, asserting message text equality - the "same message" claim).
 2. "With everything ticked (no overrides) -> disabled (stays-empty message)": covered; the override variant ("everything ticked WITH an override is allowed", the `firstCommitOverrides.isEmpty()` clause SplitDialog.kt:586) - add.
 3. Whole-file fast path: "no partial selection -> file-level `jj split` (no diff-editor overhead)": dialog-level `hunkSelection == null` is tested; add the EXECUTOR-level check: `splitAction` execution picks `CommandExecutor.split(...)` (whole-file) not `splitInteractive(...)` when `spec.hunkSelection == null` - test with a stub CommandExecutor recording calls (actions/change/splitAction.kt: find the branch), and `CliExecutorSplitTest` (jj/cli) already asserts args shape; add a contract test (real jj, `SplitContractCliTest` if absent; check contract dir) asserting both resulting commits have the expected files after a whole-file split and NO `--tool` flag (observe via `jj op log` args tag or by asserting the command line from the executor's `JjInvocation` args builder: no `--tool`/`merge-tools` config).
 4. Binary/conflicted gating: "A binary file in the changed list shows no 'Pick Hunks...' button (whole-file only)": identify the gating predicate (grep in SplitDialog/HunkSelectionModel/FileSelectionPanel for the binary check - the grep above found no `binary` references in SplitDialog.kt; the gating may live in `HunkPickPreviewController`/`isDiffable` or the preview panel (`pickHunksButton.isEnabled` toggled by `updatePickHunksVisibility`-like function at SquashIntoDialog.kt:157 for squash; Split equivalent). Read it, extract the predicate as a pure function `canPickHunks(change: Change): Boolean` (binary file type via `FileTypeManager`/`change.afterRevision` content sniff; conflicted `MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS`) if inlined, then unit-test with text/binary(PNG signature)/conflicted/deleted/added/renamed changes; plus a dialog test: select a binary file -> `pickHunksButton.isEnabled/isVisible == false`; select a text file -> enabled.
 5. (cross-link) jj-idea-qel6: binary bytes survival through the staging tree - separate bead; note in tests that gating only covers the UI, not the corruption risk.
Decisions made without the user: Q: extract `canPickHunks` pure function? Rec yes if currently inline (small, makes the gating assertable without Swing).
Scale: tests only. Acceptance: tests pass; MT-SPLIT 'Validation', 'Whole-file fast path', 'Binary/conflicted files' bullets and the automate marker removed; ./gradlew check green. Regression scope after deletion: MT-SPLIT minus those.

title: Issue-navigation links in remaining description call sites (dialogs, side panels)
description:
GitHub #15 follow-up: several call sites still call append(description)/appendSummary(description) without passing an IssueNavigationConfiguration, so issue-tracker links are missing there even though the details pane, graph view, and (as of jj-idea-n553's WorkingCopyControlsPanel fix) the Working Copy tool window support them: RevisionChoicePanel.kt:101, SquashIntoDialog.kt:303, SplitDialog.kt:600, DuplicateDialog.kt:164, RebaseDialog.kt:207, MoveBookmarkToChangeDialog.kt:116.

Most of these are HTML- or StyledTextCanvas-backed, so they need only the extra IssueNavigationConfiguration.getInstance(project) argument plus a Project already in scope - no hit-testing work like jj-idea-91qf needed.

WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt (originally listed here as line 377) is DONE: updateWorkingCopyLabel now passes IssueLinkifier(IssueNavigationConfiguration.getInstance(project)) into its htmlString call, covering the specific gap Sergej reported on GitHub #15 (bookmarks in the Working Copy tool window). See WorkingCopyLabelIssueLinkTest.kt.
design:
PLAN: the bead's six line references have drifted; re-derive the call sites from current code, fix the shared ones, and explicitly exclude non-interactive surfaces.
Current reality (grep of `htmlString(`/`entryCanvas(`/`appendSummary(` callers without a `linkifier`): 
 (1) `createSourcePanel(project, sourceEntries)` (ui/common/DialogHelpers.kt:~44, `htmlString { append(sourceEntries, "\n") { appendStatusIndicators; append(id); appendDescriptionAndEmptyIndicator; appendDecorations } }` inside an `IconAwareHtmlPane`) - the SHARED source-list header of the Squash/Split/Duplicate/Rebase dialogs (`createSourcePanel` callers: confirm with grep) - this one site covers the dialog call sites the bead lists (SquashIntoDialog, SplitDialog, DuplicateDialog, RebaseDialog); descriptions there are rendered by `appendDescriptionAndEmptyIndicator` -> `appendLinkified`, which is a no-op without a Linkifier on the canvas;
 (2) `MoveBookmarkToChangeDialog` row renderer (actions/bookmark/MoveBookmarkToChangeDialog.kt:~116 `entryCanvas(value.entry, fg) { ... appendSummary(value.entry) }`) - a JList cell renderer (TextCanvasPanel), NOT hit-testable for clicks: linkifying would only restyle text as a link that can't be clicked => exclude (document), unless the list gets a click handler (out of scope);
 (3) Tooltips: `revisionChoiceTooltip` (ui/components/RevisionChoicePanel.kt:87,103), `BookmarkNodeTooltip.kt` (many), `AnnotationLine.getHtmlTooltip`: tooltips vanish on mouse move so links are not clickable - exclude (note: the graph-row tooltip `buildTooltip` DOES pass `linkifier` - JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.kt:188 - because that tooltip is the IconAwareHtmlPane hover popup that stays while hovered? verify behaviour: if sticky, tooltips elsewhere could follow; otherwise that call site is merely cosmetic);
 (4) `JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt:338 metadataPane.text = htmlString {...}` - already part of the details pane (verify it has no description text; descriptions go through `buildCommitHtml` which has the linkifier at :293-294).
Fix:
1. `createSourcePanel(project, sourceEntries)`: `htmlString(linkifier = IssueLinkifier(IssueNavigationConfiguration.getInstance(project)))` (same one-liner as WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt:465-466). Confirm `IconAwareHtmlPane` opens http(s) links on click (HyperlinkListener -> `BrowserUtil`): the grep above - if it only handles `jjref://`/chip schemes, add the http(s) -> BrowserUtil branch (the working copy label uses the same pane type and the bead says its links work, so the handler should exist: verify).
2. Update the bead's stale list in this bead's notes; close items (2)/(3) as intentionally excluded with reasons.
3. Picker tables in dialogs (CommitPickerPanel rows) render via the log table renderer path with linkifier already (JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt:371) - verify the picker uses it (CommitPickerPanel has no `linkifier` mention in grep => rows may be rendered via `LaidOutCell`/`entryCanvas` with `Linkifier.None`) - check and fix if the picker's description column should link (hit-testing: tables use `clickTargetAt`; pickers are NOT JujutsuLogTable => no click handling => exclude, same reasoning as (2)).
Decisions made without the user: Q: linkify non-clickable surfaces for consistent styling? Rec no (a link that can't be clicked is a UX bug). Q: make tooltips interactive? Rec no.
Scale: one `IssueNavigationConfiguration.getInstance` lookup per panel build + regex per description (<= #sources). Testing: render test: `createSourcePanel` with an issue pattern configured yields HTML containing an anchor for `JIRA-123` (model on WorkingCopyLabelIssueLinkTest - find that test: bead says WorkingCopyLabelIssueLinkTest.kt exists; mirror it for DialogHelpers); no link when no pattern. Manual: MT-SQUASH/MT-SPLIT/MT-CTXMENU rebase/duplicate dialogs: with issue navigation configured, the source list description link is clickable (opens browser); regression scope: MT-SQUASH, MT-SPLIT, MT-CTXMENU.
acceptance_criteria: Dialog source lists (shared createSourcePanel) linkify issue references via IssueNavigationConfiguration; non-clickable surfaces explicitly excluded; rendering test; bead's stale list corrected.
notes: Remaining 6 call sites are dialogs/side panels, not reported as a specific user complaint - lower urgency than the Working Copy fix.

title: Cancelling 'Retrieving annotations' does not kill the jj process
description:
Platform runs annotation under a cancellable Task.Backgroundable (AnnotateLocalFileAction.java:128, cancellable=true), but CliExecutor.execute uses CapturingProcessHandler.runProcess(timeout) rather than runProcessWithProgressIndicator, and nothing in the annotate path calls ProgressManager.checkCanceled(). Cancelling the "Retrieving annotations" progress does not destroy the underlying jj process — it keeps running until it exits or hits its timeout.

Matters most for populateCache (JujutsuAnnotationProvider.kt:40-53), which the platform's AnnotationsPreloader fires per opened file — on a repo where each annotate costs ~100s (GitHub #64), abandoned/uncancellable processes can pile up.
design: Thread the ProgressIndicator through to CliExecutor and use runProcessWithProgressIndicator (or manually poll indicator.isCanceled and destroy the process) for the annotate CLI call at minimum.
acceptance_criteria: Cancelling an in-flight annotate destroys the jj subprocess rather than leaving it running to completion or timeout.

title: Native Commit tool window 'Resolve' link still unsafe for jj conflicts (residual #63)
description:
The GitHub #63 fix (jj-idea-9ms6) made jj-idea's own three "Resolve Conflicts..." actions
safe (scratch-document merge tool, never discards on cancel). But the platform's native
Commit / Local Changes tool window has its OWN built-in "Merge Conflicts" node with a
"Resolve" link (ChangesBrowserConflictsNode in intellij platform vcs-impl), which jj-idea
does not suppress and cannot intercept:

  ChangesBrowserConflictsNode.showResolveConflictsDialog()
    -> ConflictsResolutionService.showConflictResolutionDialog(changes)
      -> ChangesViewApi.showResolveConflictsDialog(...) [RPC]
        -> ChangesViewApiImpl.showResolveConflictsDialog(...)
          -> AbstractVcsHelper.getInstance(project).showMergeDialog(files, provider)

This is the exact same vulnerable MultipleFileMergeDialog/iterative-cancel path #63 fixed
elsewhere, using our registered JujutsuMergeProvider directly. Cancelling out of that dialog
still silently discards a side of the conflict for jj.

Investigated fix options:
- MergeResolveActionProvider EP (com.intellij.openapi.vcs.merge.resolveActionProvider):
  @ApiStatus.Internal, added to the platform 2026-07-06 (same wave as the iterative merge
  work), used by nobody in the platform/git4idea yet. Can only add an alternative link
  alongside the platform's unsafe default, not replace/remove it. Declaring it unconditionally
  in plugin.xml risks failing to load on jj-idea's older supported IDE builds (sinceBuild=251;
  CI tests 2025.2 and 2026.2) since the EP likely doesn't exist there - would need proper
  since-build gating (optional dependency config-file, or runtime registration behind a build
  number check) to use safely. Not attempted yet - too much unproven risk for how new/unused
  the EP is.
- Global registry flag (vcs.merge.conflict.iterative.resolution=false) would fix the true root
  cause everywhere, but is an application-wide setting affecting all VCS work in the IDE
  (Git too), and there's no way to toggle it just-in-time since we can't intercept this call
  path at all.
- Suppressing/hiding the "Merge Conflicts" node for jj-tracked files in the native tool window
  entirely - not yet investigated for feasibility.

Current mitigation: documented as a known gap in docs/manual-tests.md with an explicit warning
not to use the native Commit tool window's "Resolve" link for jj conflicts; users are directed
to jj-idea's own Resolve Conflicts entry points instead.
design:
PLAN: this bead is a documented-limitation holder; the notes already ruled out every available mechanism. The plan is to formalise the decision, add cheap monitoring so it is revisited at the right time, and test the one remaining untried idea.
Decision record (from the bead's 2026-07-31 notes, re-verified against intellij-community source: `ChangesBrowserConflictsNode` is `@ApiStatus.Internal` (platform/vcs-impl/shared/src/.../ChangesBrowserConflictsNode.kt), its "Resolve" link runs `showResolveConflictsDialog()` straight into the platform merge flow using our registered JujutsuMergeProvider; `MergeResolveActionProvider` is Internal and 2026.2+ only; no supported suppression API exists.)
Remaining actions (small):
1. One untried, supported-API idea, timeboxed 1h: the node is built from changes whose `fileStatus == FileStatus.MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS` (TreeModelBuilder.java builds `ChangesBrowserConflictsNode` when conflicts exist). The plugin itself reports MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS in several features (ui/common/JujutsuChangesTree.kt:122, editor notification/gutter via ChangeListManager status, JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview.kt:64) - so changing the reported status is a broad behavioural change. Evaluate ONLY whether ChangeListManager can report jj conflicts under a plugin-defined `FileStatus` (via `FileStatusFactory`) that keeps the same colour but is not MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS, and what each of those four consumers would need to switch to (`hasConflict` already exists on LogEntry/FileChange - jj/LogEntry.kt). Expected outcome: reject (too invasive for a rare residual surface, and it would lose platform conflict affordances like "mark resolved"), but record the finding so it isn't re-investigated.
2. Safer fallback inside our own control: audit `JujutsuMergeProvider` (vcs/merge/) for what the platform dialog does on cancel: if the destructive step is the platform's write-back via `MergeProvider.conflictResolvedForFile`/`MergeData` revisions, make our provider defensive: `conflictResolvedForFile` must be a no-op for jj (jj marks resolution by file content, not an explicit call) and `loadRevisions` must return the scratch-copy data so a cancelled iterative merge cannot overwrite the working file. If the audit shows the unsafe behaviour is entirely inside the platform's iterative flow, record "cannot be mitigated at provider level".
3. Revisit triggers (put in notes + contributing.md Platform API compatibility checklist, see jj-idea-nhpq): re-evaluate when (a) sinceBuild is raised to a build where MergeResolveActionProvider is non-Internal, (b) the advisory EAP verifyPlugin job reports ChangesBrowserConflictsNode/IterativeMergeFlow API changes, or (c) a user reports data loss.
4. Keep docs/manual-tests.md known-gap warning (MT-CONFLICT) in sync; ensure it names both exposed configurations (jj+Git mixed; jj-only with `hideStandardCommitToolWindow` off, jj-idea-wb5l).
