Decisions made without the user: Q: close the bead? Rec: keep open at P3 with this plan (the acceptance criteria are unmet and a data-loss class bug should stay visible), but do nothing beyond steps 1-3 until a trigger fires. Reverse: close as wontfix and rely on the manual-tests warning.
Scale: none. Testing: if step 2 yields a provider-level mitigation, a unit test on JujutsuMergeProvider (cancel path leaves file content untouched). Manual: MT-CONFLICT (native Commit window 'Resolve' link on a mixed jj+Git project - confirm warning text, behaviour recorded). Regression scope: MT-CONFLICT only.
acceptance_criteria:
Either: (a) the native 'Merge Conflicts' node is suppressed for jj-tracked files, or (b) a
different safe mechanism is found that doesn't rely on Internal/TestOnly platform APIs at
runtime. Ruled out: a version-gated MergeResolveActionProvider alternative link (both static
plugin.xml and runtime-reflective registration depend on Internal or @TestOnly platform APIs
- see 2026-07-31 notes) and the global vcs.merge.conflict.iterative.resolution registry flag
(too broad a blast radius). Until (a) or (b) is found, this stays documented as a known gap
in docs/manual-tests.md, scoped to jj-only-with-opt-out and mixed jj+Git projects (the
default jj-only case is covered by wb5l hiding the whole tool window).
notes:
2026-07-31 investigation: with wb5l landed, revisited the MergeResolveActionProvider option
(add a safe alternative link alongside the platform's unsafe default). Verified against
intellij-community source that this doesn't hold up:

- The EP interface (com.intellij.openapi.vcs.merge.resolveActionProvider /
  MergeResolveActionProvider) is @ApiStatus.Internal and only exists on 2026.2+ builds, not
  on sinceBuild=251. A static plugin.xml declaration would fail to load on older builds; a
  compile-time Kotlin reference to the Internal interface would fail verifyPlugin there too.
- The reflection-based workaround (detect the EP via
  AreaInstance.getExtensionArea().getExtensionPointIfRegistered(name), build a
  java.lang.reflect.Proxy, and call ExtensionPoint.registerExtension(instance, Disposable) to
  add it at runtime) avoids the compile-time/verifyPlugin problem, but every runtime API
  needed to pull it off is itself unsupported for production use:
    - AreaInstance.getExtensionArea() is @ApiStatus.Internal
    - ExtensionPoint.registerExtension(T, Disposable) - the only overload with a Disposable
      for clean unregistration on plugin unload - is @TestOnly. The one non-deprecated,
      non-TestOnly overload has no Disposable param and would leak on dynamic unload.
  So this doesn't actually de-risk anything vs. the original declarative option - it just
  moves the unsupported-API surface from compile-time to runtime, which is arguably worse
  (no verifyPlugin signal if JetBrains changes/breaks this method later).
- Decision: do not pursue MergeResolveActionProvider in any form (static or reflective).
  Also ruling out the app-wide registry flag (vcs.merge.conflict.iterative.resolution=false)
  as before - too broad a blast radius for a jj-only concern.

Scope after wb5l: this bead's exposure is now limited to (a) jj-only projects where the user
opted out of hiding the standard Commit tool window, and (b) mixed jj+Git projects, where the
window is always shown. Both are documented as a known gap in docs/manual-tests.md, steering
users to jj-idea's own "Resolve Conflicts..." entries. No further safe mechanism was found
that doesn't rely on unsupported platform internals. Downgrading to P3 (documented limitation,
narrow residual surface) rather than closing outright, in case a future platform release adds
a supported way to suppress or replace the native link.
2026-10-05 resolved: JujutsuMergeProvider.loadRevisions now throws VcsException when registry vcs.merge.conflict.iterative.resolution is on. Every MultipleFileMergeDialog path that edits the real Document (Merge..., Resolve automatically, iterative Accept Yours/Theirs) loads revisions first and catches VcsException into an error dialog, so file stays untouched. Public API only. Plugin-defined FileStatus idea rejected (too invasive, loses platform conflict affordances). Revisit if platform stops routing through loadRevisions or renames/removes the registry key.
close_reason: Provider-level refusal of loadRevisions in iterative flow

title: Commit details pane: author/committer email link never shows hover-underline (ChipView bypasses native link styling)
description: Link rendering is inconsistent across the app (reported by user while reviewing jj-idea-iesq): - Author/committer email links in the log table: now colored-always, underline-on-hover (fixed in jj-idea-iesq via SimpleTextAttributes.LINK_PLAIN_ATTRIBUTES + a hovered-cell check). - Change-id links in the commit details pane: colored-always, underline-on-hover, for free - they're genuine flowing `text` HTML, so the JDK's own HTMLEditorKit LinkController/default.css already gives them this behavior with zero custom code. - Author/committer email links in the commit details pane (`TextCanvas.appendWithEmail`): never show underline, hover or otherwise. This bead is about fixing that last case. ## Root cause `appendWithEmail` renders "Name " via `appendUnbreakable`, which on the HTML backend (`HtmlTextCanvas.appendUnbreakable`) routes through the atomic `ChipView` mechanism (`IconAwareHtmlPane.kt`) - an `` element intercepted by `ChipIconExtension` and manually painted via `ChipView.paint()`'s own `g.drawString(...)` call. Because this bypasses Swing's normal text/anchor View hierarchy entirely, it never participates in the JDK's native `` hover-underline behavior (or any CSS-driven styling) - it's an opaque painted unit as far as the HTML engine is concerned, regardless of being nested inside a real ``. ## Why `appendUnbreakable` is used here (and why the obvious fix doesn't work) `ChipView`/`appendUnbreakable` exists specifically to keep "Name " (and bookmark/tag chips, and the date chip) atomic - never splitting across a line wrap. This already has real history: jj-idea-m2wr, jj-idea-vll4, and jj-idea-y4jk were all follow-up P1/P2 bugs from getting this atomic-unit behavior working correctly on IDEA 2026.2's JBHtmlPane. The obvious fix - stop using the chip for this one case, use real flowing text with CSS `white-space: nowrap` instead - was tried during jj-idea-iesq and reverted after empirical verification (a platform test rendering the actual pipeline) showed it does NOT work: JBHtmlPane's Jsoup-based input transpiler appears to inject invisible break-opportunity characters (likely zero-width spaces) at internal punctuation in long unbroken tokens (e.g. between the dots in `users.noreply.github.com`) - probably specifically to allow wrapping of otherwise-unbreakable long URLs/emails elsewhere in the app. `white-space: nowrap` does not suppress breaking at these injected characters, so a long email would still wrap mid-token. This matches the exact failure mode `IconAwareHtmlPaneWrapTest`'s own doc comment already described from an earlier attempt ("a `white-space: nowrap` span was ignored by Swing's glyph-breaking"). ## What would actually be needed `ChipView` itself would need to participate in link hover directly, since it owns its own painting: 1. Give it a per-chip href/link-target (chip encoding currently carries no href info - see `ChipSpec`/`appendChipHtml` in `HtmlTextCanvas.kt`). 2. Track pointer position within `IconAwareHtmlPane` (a `MouseMotionListener` hit-testing to a specific `ChipView`, similar in spirit to the `hoveredLinkRow`/`hoveredLinkCol` tracking added to `JujutsuLogTable` in jj-idea-iesq) and repaint just that chip on hover change. 3. In `ChipView.paint()`, choose link-color-always/underline-on-hover explicitly (matching `SimpleTextAttributes.LINK_PLAIN_ATTRIBUTES`/`LINK_ATTRIBUTES`) instead of the current flat `styleSheet.getForeground(attr)`/no-underline-ever painting. This is real work, not a one-line fix - hence its own bead rather than folding it into jj-idea-iesq.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering the author/committer 'Name <email>' text in the commit details pane shows an underline, matching the change-id link's behavior; the underline disappears when the pointer moves away. Long emails still never split across a line wrap (no regression of jj-idea-m2wr/vll4/y4jk).
notes: jj-idea-iesq. See IconAwareHtmlPaneWrapTest.kt's doc comment for the prior white-space:nowrap failure this would need to avoid repeating.
close_reason: Implemented: IconAwareHtmlPane now tracks pointer position and identifies the hovered chip's Element (linkedChipElementAt), and ChipView.paint() draws an underline only for that element when it's inside a link. The blocker wasn't the atomic-chip painting model itself as originally scoped - it was a Swing HTML parsing quirk: character-level tags like are flattened onto the wrapped leaf's own AttributeSet as a nested set keyed by HTML.Tag.A, not a directly-queryable HTML.Attribute.HREF, which also silently broke the pre-existing refUriAt() (right-click ref-chip menu) the same way - fixed both via a shared hrefOf() helper. Also added an explicit link-color in HtmlTextCanvas.linked() since the HTML backend never consumed the Swing-side style field for chip coloring. Covered by IconAwareHtmlPaneChipHoverTest and IconAwareHtmlPaneRefUriAtTest, both exercising the real rendering pipeline (not just pre-transpile HTML strings) given this exact area's history of pipeline-specific bugs.

title: Diff view resets scroll position when repo files change in background
description: GitHub #58. While viewing a change's diff, any background modification to a file in the repo (e.g. an AI coding assistant editing files) resets the currently visible file's scroll position to the top. Diff requests are built in actions/filechange/DiffRequestBuilder.kt and shown via ui/common/JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview.kt; a VFS/status refresh likely rebuilds the DiffRequest wholesale rather than updating content in place, discarding viewer scroll state. Reporter (tobyclemson) offered to investigate and raise a PR.
acceptance_criteria: Editing a file in the background (outside the diff viewer) while a diff is open does not reset the visible scroll position of the diff being viewed.
close_reason: Fixed: made jj's ContentRevision implementations value-equal so the platform's diff request cache hits across background refreshes; working-copy diffs now use CurrentContentRevision for live content; log details panel skips no-op tree rebuilds.

title: Support jj git fetch --tag
description: jj 0.38 added 'jj git fetch --tag' for optional tag fetching. The plugin already has tag support (tagSetArgs/tagDeleteArgs in CliExecutor.kt) but gitFetchArgs (CliExecutor.kt:97) has no tag option. Low-priority feature opportunity from the 0.38-0.43 changelog sweep.
design:
PLAN: add "specific tags" to the Fetch dialog, gated on jj 0.38.
jj facts (verified with local `jj git fetch --help`, jj 0.44): `-t, --tag <TAG>` repeatable; glob patterns where only `*` expands; without --tag/--branch fetch follows `remotes.<name>.fetch-tags`/refspecs. `--tracked` also exists (separate).
Design:
1. Executor: `gitFetchArgs(remote, allRemotes, tags: List<String> = emptyList())` (jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt:289) appends `--tag <pattern>` per entry (IRREVERSIBLE as today); `CommandExecutor.gitFetch(remote, allRemotes, tags)` (CommandExecutor.kt:413) + `override` in CliExecutor + StubCommandExecutor (contract/StubCommandExecutor.kt) default param. Patterns passed verbatim, but do not allow a leading `-`; escape nothing (jj parses patterns; bad patterns return jj's own error shown in the existing fetch error path).
2. Feature gate: `JjFeature.FETCH_TAG(JjVersion(0, 38, 0), "feature.fetch.tag.name")` (jj/JjFeature.kt:15-20 pattern; MINIMUM is 0.37, so the gate is real). UI is visible-but-disabled with reason on older jj (`disabledReasonIn`), per the enum's contract (never hidden, never emulated). Add the bundle key + the Settings "features unavailable" list picks it up automatically (et35).
3. UI: GitFetchDialog (actions/git/GitFetchDialog.kt): add a "Fetch only these tags" checkbox + text field (comma/space separated patterns, e.g. `v1.*`); `GitFetchSpec` gains `tags: List<String>` (default empty so the two existing constructors at GitFetchAction.kt:46 and gitRemoteActions.kt:65 stay valid). When tags are specified, `--tag` alone limits the fetch to those tags (and NO bookmarks: jj semantics when any --branch/--tag is given: "If no branches nor tags are specified, fetches ... settings" - so specifying only --tag fetches only those tags, not bookmarks; make the dialog text say "Fetch only these tags (skips bookmarks)" and add a second checkbox "Also fetch bookmarks" => then pass `--branch '*'`... NO: keep v1 simple: tags field XOR default behaviour, with the hint text; the "also bookmarks" combo is a follow-up if asked.
4. performFetch (gitRemoteActions.kt:~35): pass spec.tags through to the executor; success notification text mentions tags fetched count if parseable? jj prints nothing structured - keep generic "Fetch completed". After success, tags state refresh: `stateModel.references.invalidate()` (tags appear in the Tags group of the bookmarks panel) - confirm `invalidate(...)` after fetch already refreshes references.
5. Persistence: remember last-used tag patterns? Rec no (rare).
Decisions made without the user: Q: pre-fill with `*`? Rec: no. Q: gate vs raising MINIMUM to 0.38? Rec: gate (see gv1k policy bead for retiring gates).
Scale: none. Testing: `gitFetchArgs` unit tests (no tags, one, several, with --remote, with --all-remotes); dialog test (spec carries tags; field disabled when feature unsupported - see how TAG_PUSH tests do it in actions/tag tests); contract test (real jj >=0.38): repo with remote tags v1.0, v2.0: fetch `--tag 'v1.*'` -> only v1.0 present. Manual: MT-GIT (fetch dialog tags row; old-jj disabled state via the version override used for TAG_PUSH rows). Regression scope: MT-GIT, MT-SETTINGS (features list).
acceptance_criteria: Fetch dialog can fetch only named tag patterns via --tag on jj>=0.38, disabled with reason on older jj; spec/args/contract tests; MT-GIT row added.

title: Support jj rebase --simplify-parents
description: jj 0.39 added '--simplify-parents' to 'jj rebase', useful for cleaning up merge parents after a rebase. rebaseArgs (CliExecutor.kt:248) has no option for it. Low-priority feature opportunity from the 0.38-0.43 changelog sweep; could be exposed as a rebase dialog checkbox.
design:
PLAN: expose `jj rebase --simplify-parents` (jj 0.39+) as an opt-in checkbox in the Rebase dialog, gated by a JjFeature.
jj facts (verified `jj rebase --help`, 0.44): `--simplify-parents`: "Simplify parents of rebased commits, like `jj simplify-parents`, while rebasing them. Any parents that are ancestors of other parents will be removed." MINIMUM jj is 0.37 (jj/JjVersion.kt:28), so the option needs a gate: `JjFeature.REBASE_SIMPLIFY_PARENTS(JjVersion(0, 39, 0), "feature.rebase.simplify.parents.name")` (jj/JjFeature.kt pattern; visible-but-disabled with reason on older jj, per the enum contract).
Design:
1. Args: `rebaseArgs(revisions, destinations, sourceMode, destinationMode, simplifyParents: Boolean = false)` (jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt:609) appends `--simplify-parents` when true; `CommandExecutor.rebase(..., simplifyParents)` (CommandExecutor.kt:400) + CliExecutor override + StubCommandExecutor default; `RebaseSpec` (ui/rebase/RebaseDialog.kt:22) gains `simplifyParents: Boolean = false` (default keeps the existing callers - DnD rebase, toolbar RebaseChangeToolbar, bookmark rebase - unchanged).
2. Dialog: checkbox "Simplify parents of rebased merge commits" with a tooltip: "Removes redundant parents (a parent that is already an ancestor of another parent) from the rebased commits". Placement: with the other options below destination mode. Disabled+explanatory tooltip if `!JjFeature.REBASE_SIMPLIFY_PARENTS.isSupportedIn(project)`. Default UNCHECKED (matches jj default; the redundant-parent case arises when rebasing a merge onto a destination that already contains one of its parents). State persistence: do not persist (rare option) - or persist as a settings default? Rec: no.
3. Preview interplay: RebaseSimulator (ui/rebase/RebaseSimulator.kt) does not model parent simplification; when the checkbox is on and the source set contains merge commits, the preview may show a redundant edge that jj would drop. Implement a cheap simulation step: after reparenting, for each moved commit with >=2 parents remove any parent that is an ancestor of another parent within the loaded entries (ancestry check via the simulated DAG; O(moved x parents x depth) -> use a bounded DFS with a visited set per commit; fine for dialog scale) and mark `simplifyApplied` in the simulation result so the description label can say "N redundant parents removed". If ancestry can't be decided due to unloaded history, leave the edge (conservative) and note "(preview may differ)". Optional for v1: ship checkbox without preview effect and document the limitation in the tooltip. Decision below.
4. DnD: drag-rebase (`DropPerformers`) and the other direct rebase paths don't expose the option - unchanged (dialog-only).
Decisions made without the user: Q: preview support in v1? Rec: no - ship the flag first; add the simulation only if users hit confusion (misleading-preview risk is low: only affects merges with redundant parents). Q: persist the checkbox? Rec no.
Scale: none (one flag). Testing: `rebaseArgs` unit tests (with/without flag, with other modes), JjFeature gate test (disabled with reason on 0.38), dialog test (spec carries flag), contract test on jj>=0.39: rebase a merge with a redundant parent and assert it is removed only with the flag. Manual: MT-CTXMENU rebase dialog rows (checkbox on/off result; old-jj disabled state via the version override used for other gated rows). Regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-DND (rebase via drag untouched), MT-SETTINGS (unsupported-features list).
acceptance_criteria: Rebase dialog has a gated 'simplify parents' option passed as --simplify-parents on jj>=0.39, disabled with reason on older jj; args/dialog/contract tests; MT row added.

title: SquashIntoDialogPickSourcesModeTest logs ClassCastException (relaxed mock + Result<T>)
description:
Discovered while verifying jj-idea-vu35/45id/6fxz: running the full suite locally logs this 8
times during SquashIntoDialogPickSourcesModeTest (tests still pass - the exception is thrown
on a background thread via runInBackground and swallowed/logged by IntelliJ's platform
uncaught-exception handling, not propagated into an assertion):

  java.lang.ClassCastException: class java.lang.Object cannot be cast to class java.util.List
      at in.kkkev.jjidea.jj.ChangeService.loadChanges(ChangeService.kt:25)
      at in.kkkev.jjidea.jj.ChangeService.loadChanges(ChangeService.kt:16)
      at in.kkkev.jjidea.ui.squash.SquashIntoDialog.reloadChangesForSelection$lambda$32(SquashIntoDialog.kt:384)

Root cause: SquashIntoDialogPickSourcesModeTest.kt:29 uses `repo = mockk<JujutsuRepository>(relaxed = true)`
with no explicit stub for `logService.getFileChanges`. That method returns `Result<List<FileChange>>`;
Result is a Kotlin inline/value class, and MockK's relaxed-mock auto-generation doesn't correctly
synthesize a boxed Result wrapping a List for an unstubbed call - it returns something whose
underlying value isn't a List, so ChangeService.loadChanges's `.getOrElse {}` access blows up with
a ClassCastException at the generics-erasure boundary.

Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to jj-idea-vu35/45id/6fxz's changes: neither
ChangeService.kt nor SquashIntoDialog.kt (nor this test file) were touched by that work; `jj log
-r 'files(...)'` shows the last touching commits predate this session entirely.

Also confirmed: this is a *platformTest*-tagged test (@Tag("platform")), excluded from the
default `test` task (see build.gradle.kts:154-156 excludeTags("platform", "contract")) but
included in `check` via `platformTest`. It's easy to miss the noisy log line if you only run
`./gradlew test`.

Fix: explicitly stub `every { repo.logService.getFileChanges(any()) } returns Result.success(emptyList())`
(or similar) in SquashIntoDialogPickSourcesModeTest's repo setup, matching whatever the other
Squash/Rebase dialog tests already do to avoid this MockK+Result<T> pitfall (worth grepping
for how other tests handle this - if none do, this pitfall may lurk elsewhere too).
design:
PLAN: stub the Result<T>-returning call in the test and add a safety net so the pitfall can't hide again.
Root cause (verified in bead): SquashIntoDialogPickSourcesModeTest builds entries whose `repo` is a relaxed MockK mock (test helper `createEntry`, same file ~:261); SquashIntoDialog.reloadChangesForSelection (SquashIntoDialog.kt ~:384) calls ChangeService.loadChanges (jj/ChangeService.kt:25 `repo.logService.getFileChanges(entry).getOrElse{...}`) and the relaxed mock returns a boxed non-List for the inline value class `Result<List<FileChange>>`.
Fix steps:
1. In the test's repo setup (where `createEntry`/`mockk<JujutsuRepository>(relaxed = true)` live - the bead cites :29 but the helper is at :261 now) add `every { repo.logService.getFileChanges(any<LogEntry>()) } returns Result.success(emptyList())` (check overloads: there are `getFileChanges(entry)` and `getFileChanges(entry, filePath)` - ChangeService.loadChanges and the annotation provider use both; stub the one hit, `any()` matchers need the exact overload; because Result is an inline class MockK needs `returns Result.success(emptyList())` - fine on MockK >=1.13; verify version in gradle/libs).
2. Grep for the same pitfall: `rg "mockk<JujutsuRepository>\(relaxed = true\)" src/test` finds ~10 test files (dnd/*, components/*). Only those that reach getFileChanges/other Result<T> returning logService methods are affected; run the full `./gradlew platformTest` with output captured and grep for "ClassCastException" to find all, not by reading files.
3. Prefer one shared fixture: add `fun relaxedRepoWithStubbedLogService()` in the test support package (see how contract/StubCommandExecutor.kt does it) that pre-stubs the Result-returning logService methods, and use it in the affected tests; document the pitfall in a KDoc there and in contributing.md § Testing Strategy (one line: "relaxed mocks + Result<T>: stub explicitly").
Decisions made without the user: Q: fix in the test only, or make ChangeService robust? Rec test only - production code is correct; hiding a failure behind runCatching in prod would mask real bugs.
Scale: none. Testing: acceptance is the test run itself - `./gradlew platformTest --tests '*SquashIntoDialogPickSourcesModeTest*'` logs no ClassCastException (capture stdout/stderr and assert grep count 0). Manual: none (test-only).
acceptance_criteria: No ClassCastException in platformTest output for SquashIntoDialogPickSourcesModeTest or any other relaxed-mock test (grep of full platformTest log is clean); shared fixture/documentation added.

title: Add preview panel to Duplicate Onto... dialog
description:
The Duplicate Onto... dialog (DuplicateDialog.kt, added in jj-idea-vu35) currently has no
preview of the resulting graph, unlike RebaseDialog which shows a live simulated
post-operation graph via RebasePreviewPanel/RebaseSimulator.

RebaseSimulator can't be reused as-is: it *moves* existing nodes (reparents sources away
from their current position). `jj duplicate` does the opposite — originals stay exactly
where they are, and *new* synthetic nodes are inserted into the graph. A DuplicateSimulator
would need to clone source LogEntrys under placeholder change/commit IDs and splice them
into the entry list rather than rewriting existing parent links.

Suggested approach:
1. Start with "onto" placement only: synthesize N copies as children of the chosen
   destination(s), splice into the entries, rebuild the graph via CommitGraphBuilder, and
   highlight source/destination the same way RebasePreviewPanel does (SOURCE_HIGHLIGHT /
   DESTINATION_HIGHLIGHT). RebasePreviewPanel's shape (table + description label) is
   directly copyable for this.
2. Insert-after/insert-before are harder: they require reparenting the destination's real
   children/parents through the new copy, mirroring (not reusing) reparentInsertAfter/
   reparentInsertBefore's logic. Verify against real jj that the reparenting semantics for
   *duplicate*'s insert-after/before actually match rebase's before trusting a preview built
   on that assumption — an incorrect preview here would be actively misleading.

Reference files: ui/rebase/RebaseSimulator.kt, ui/rebase/RebasePreviewPanel.kt,
ui/rebase/RebaseDialog.kt, ui/duplicate/DuplicateDialog.kt.
design:
PLAN: live preview graph in DuplicateDialog, sharing the preview panel extraction planned in jj-idea-uuy9.
Facts: ui/duplicate/DuplicateDialog.kt (no preview); RebaseDialog wires `RebasePreviewPanel(project)` (ui/rebase/RebaseDialog.kt:75-109) with `RebaseSimulator.simulate(...)` (ui/rebase/RebaseSimulator.kt:35-60: collectMovedIds -> reparent -> scopeToRelevant -> topologicalSort), generic core over `DagNode`. `jj duplicate` keeps originals in place and creates NEW commits: `-o/--onto` (children of the destination), `-A/--insert-after`, `-B/--insert-before` - destination modes already modelled by `RebaseDestinationMode` (used by `duplicateArgs(revisions, destinations, destinationMode)`, jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt) and the dialog.
Design (phased as the bead suggests):
1. `DuplicateSimulator` (ui/duplicate/ or ui/rebase/ next to the generic core): `simulate(allEntries, sources, destinationIds, destinationMode)` -> `RebaseSimulation`-shaped result (entries + sourceIds (the originals, highlighted as source) + destinationIds + `newIds` (synthetic copies)). Synthetic copies: clone each source LogEntry with `LogEntry.pending = true`-style flag (jj/LogEntry.kt has `pending` for "a not-yet-created change previewed in a rebase-simulator preview", used by NewChangeDialog) and placeholder `ChangeId("dup-<n>")`/CommitId, description preserved, empty parents set per mode. COPIES KEEP THE SOURCE'S RELATIVE STRUCTURE: duplicating several revisions copies the set with parent links among them preserved (jj duplicates a set as a connected sub-graph: if A->B both duplicated, copy(B) is a child of copy(A), not of the original A). Implement via a map orig->copy and rewiring parents that are inside the source set.
2. Placement semantics - ONTO (v1): copies' roots become children of each destination (multiple destinations => the copy gets all of them as parents, i.e. a merge copy - matches `jj duplicate -o A -o B` creating a merge parent set; confirm in jj 0.44 help); heads of the copy set have no children. Entries for the preview: all existing entries + copies, then `scopeToRelevant`/`topologicalSort` (reuse, same as rebase).
3. INSERT-AFTER (-A D): the copies are inserted between D and D's children: D's children are rebased onto the copy set's HEADS (so children's parents: D replaced by copy heads); INSERT-BEFORE (-B D): copies inserted between D's parents and D: copy roots get D's parents, D's parents replaced by copy heads. These mirror `reparentInsertAfter/Before` in RebaseSimulator but are NOT identical (originals stay). Phase 2; REQUIRES verification against real jj with a contract test before shipping (bead's warning about misleading previews): create a fixture, run real `jj duplicate -A/-B`, read the resulting parent links, and assert the simulator's output topology equals it (compare as (parent-of-child map) over descriptions as stable keys). Ship ONTO first, then INSERT-* only if the contract test passes; otherwise leave the preview empty/hidden for -A/-B with a note "Preview not available for insert modes".
4. Panel reuse: after jj-idea-uuy9 extracts `RebasePreviewPanel.setSimulation(entries, sourceIds, destinationIds, descriptionText)`, DuplicateDialog uses it directly; if 77i5 lands first, perform that extraction here and let uuy9 reuse it (coordination note in both beads: whoever lands first does the panel refactor). Highlight sources/destinations with the existing `JujutsuColors.SOURCE_HIGHLIGHT/DESTINATION_HIGHLIGHT`; copies drawn as pending rows (existing pending render path - dashed/italic description).
5. Immutable guard: `DuplicateImmutabilityGuard.kt` already filters illegal destinations (duplicating onto immutable is allowed; inserting before/after immutable is not) - the preview must not simulate disallowed placements (disable OK + empty preview, same predicate).
Decisions made without the user
1. Q: -A/-B in the first release? Rec: only after the contract test passes (misleading previews are worse than none).
2. Q: Copies for multi-select preserve internal edges? Rec: yes (jj semantics, verified in step 1 contract test).
Scale: O(n) on loaded picker entries per selection change (same as rebase preview); synthetic ids unique per simulation; no per-row full scans (count test with 10k entries).
Testing: DuplicateSimulatorTest (single, multi chain, multi disjoint, multiple destinations merge copy); contract test vs real jj for each placement mode; dialog test: preview updates on destination/mode change (SquashIntoDialog test style); manual: MT-CTXMENU/Duplicate rows (preview matches the result after OK for onto, and -A/-B if shipped). Regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-LOG-GRAPH (shared preview panel), MT-DND (drop-duplicate uses DuplicateDialog? check DropPerformers duplicate path).
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate dialog shows live preview for ONTO with source/destination highlighting and pending copies; insert-after/before only if a contract test proves simulator == real jj; panel shared with squash preview; tests + manual rows.

title: Surface untracked-not-ignored files in the UI like git's red 'untracked' coloring
description:
Git shows files that exist on disk but aren't yet 'git add'ed in a distinct 'untracked' color (red in most themes / FileStatus.UNKNOWN). jj's default snapshot.auto-track='all()' means this state (S4 in docs/jj-track-untrack-model.md: untracked, not-ignored) is almost always transient -- auto-tracked on the very next jj command -- so under default config there's rarely anything to show. But repos using a restrictive snapshot.auto-track (plausible for huge monorepos wanting to avoid an auto-add sweep over a huge tree -- see jj-idea-0xqp's google3/Piper-scale repo) can have this state persist and matter.

Design sketch (verified this session, see jj-idea-i9ol round 3 plan): 'jj status' ALREADY reports these files directly, under an 'Untracked paths:' section (marked with '?'), and -- crucially -- this list is filtered by jj's OWN true ignore logic (confirmed: a file matching .gitignore correctly does NOT appear there), which is MORE authoritative than our own GitignoreCache heuristic. JujutsuChangeProvider already runs 'jj status' every refresh cycle (see JujutsuChangeProvider.getChanges) -- the 'Untracked paths:' section is simply parsed-and-discarded today (parseStatus/collectTrackedAbsolutePaths only handle 'Working copy changes:'). So this feature is mostly a PARSING ADDITION to data already fetched, not a new traversal: cheap/no-op under default auto-track (section is empty), and bounded by jj's own status cost even under a restrictive auto-track config.

Render via ChangelistBuilder.processUnversionedFile(FilePath) (confirmed present in the platform API, JAVA: platform/vcs-api/.../ChangelistBuilder.java), mirroring how processIgnoredFile is already used for the ignored-file set -- see JujutsuIgnoredFilesService for the existing pattern to follow for wiring this into getChanges/the dirty-scope refresh cycle.
design:
PLAN: parse the "Untracked paths:" section of the `jj status` output the change provider already runs, and report those files as unversioned.
Verified locally (jj 0.44, `--config snapshot.auto-track='none()'`): `jj status` prints
```
Untracked paths:
? .gitignore
? a.txt
? b.txt
Working copy  (@) : ...
```
and a file matching .gitignore (x.log) is NOT listed - jj's own ignore logic (authoritative; more so than our GitignoreCache heuristic). Under default `snapshot.auto-track = all()` the section never appears (everything is tracked at the snapshot jj status itself performs) - so it costs nothing in the common case.
Code: `JujutsuChangeProvider.getChanges` runs `jj status` per refresh (vcs/changes/JujutsuChangeProvider.kt:~68 `parseStatus(result.stdout, repo, builder, conflictInfos.keys)`); `parseStatus` (:124-170) handles only "Working copy changes:"; ignored files are reported via `builder.processIgnoredFile(fp)` (:107) from the async ignored-files holder.
Design:
1. Extend `parseStatus` with a second state machine arm: line trimmed == "Untracked paths:" starts the section; lines of the form `? <path>` are collected until the first line that doesn't start with "? " (blank line or next header "Working copy"/"Parent commit"). Collect into a `Set<String>` and, after the loop, `builder.processUnversionedFile(repo.directory.getChildPath(path))` for each (ChangelistBuilder.processUnversionedFile confirmed present). Directories: jj lists FILES (paths), not directories - fine. Paths with special chars: jj prints them verbatim (no quoting) in status; confirm for spaces/unicode and for a path starting with "? " (pathological) - add parser tests; use `line.substring(2)` after `startsWith("? ")` rather than trim() so leading spaces in names survive.
2. Interaction with the Tracked toggle/ignored logic: JujutsuTrackedFilesService + ignored holder (vcs/ignore/) classify files by heuristics; an UNVERSIONED file reported by status must NOT also be reported as ignored (jj's list excludes ignored ones, so no overlap by construction) and must not appear in the changes list. Platform behaviour: `processUnversionedFile` makes the file show red/UNKNOWN in the project view and in Local Changes "Unversioned Files" (our own working-copy panel tree UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel/JujutsuChangesTree: decide whether to show an Unversioned group: Rec yes, under a collapsed "Untracked" node that offers the Track action (jj-idea-i9ol's TrackedToggleAction / `jj file track`) - pairs naturally).
3. Large lists: under a restrictive auto-track config in a huge repo `jj status` could list tens of thousands of untracked paths. Cap reporting: report at most N=10_000 (constant in the same style as IGNORE_REPORT_CAP, jj-idea-s0ab) and log/notify once ("N untracked files; showing first 10,000") - protects the platform tree and ChangeListManager; the cap applies after parsing (parsing is O(output), which is already paid). Operation-count/scale test: 100k "? path" lines parse in O(n) and only 10k builder calls.
4. Add FileStatus colour: `processUnversionedFile` -> `FileStatus.UNKNOWN` which themes colour red-ish; nothing to add.
5. No new jj call (acceptance); verify the status invocation does not pass flags that suppress the untracked section (jj prints it by default; `--no-pager`/colour only).
Decisions made without the user: Q: show an "Untracked" group in the plugin's own Working Copy panel? Rec: yes, collapsed, with Track action (users with restrictive auto-track NEED a way to track from the UI, otherwise the red color is a dead end). If the user prefers colour-only, drop the panel group. Q: cap value? Rec 10,000.
Scale: parse O(status output); report O(min(N,10k)); no traversal, no new subprocess.
Testing: parseStatus tests (empty section, mixed with changes, names with spaces, section at end/start, ignored absent); builder recorded calls via a fake ChangelistBuilder (existing JujutsuChangeProviderTest pattern); scale test above; contract test with real jj under `snapshot.auto-track=none()` verifying format for 0.37 and current. Manual: MT-WORKINGCOPY / MT-IGNORE: set repo config `snapshot.auto-track = 'none()'`, create a file -> red in Project view, appears in Untracked group; Track makes it versioned; ignored file stays ignored-coloured, not red. Regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-IGNORE, MT-CROSS (Git unversioned colouring is the model).
acceptance_criteria: Untracked (not ignored) files from jj status show as unversioned in Project view and Local Changes/working copy panel; no extra jj call; capped at 10k with notice; parser + scale tests; MT rows added.

title: GitignoreCache should honor global git excludes (core.excludesFile, ~/.gitignore/XDG default)
description:
jj-idea-i9ol's design work established that our own ignore-status predictor (GitignoreCache, used by JujutsuIgnoreService.isIgnored) only reads repo-local .gitignore + .git/info/exclude, never global git excludes (core.excludesFile, defaulting to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore or ~/.config/git/ignore, or classic ~/.gitignore if core.excludesFile is set to it).

Empirically confirmed (this session, using an isolated GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL sandbox so as not to touch the real environment) that jj ITSELF honors this global exclude setting in BOTH colocated and non-colocated repos -- a file matching only a global exclude pattern is never auto-tracked by jj, exactly as if it were locally .gitignore'd. This is a real, confirmed gap, not a hypothetical: our client-side predictor will misclassify such files as 'not ignored' when jj actually treats them as ignored.

This gap directly affects: the Track/Untrack context-menu toggle's visibility gating (jj-idea-i9ol), and any future 'flag tracked-but-ignored files' work (jj-idea-ih95). Not a blocker for either (both designs already treat jj as the final authority and degrade safely), but closing it would shrink the residual risk in both.

Design sketch: read git's own config resolution for core.excludesFile (check repo-local git config first, then global ~/.gitconfig, matching git's own precedence), parse that file the same way GitignoreCache already parses .gitignore/.git/info/exclude, and merge its patterns at the repo-root level (same precedence tier as .git/info/exclude currently gets).
design:
PLAN: teach GitignoreCache about global git excludes, at the correct (lowest) precedence, resolved the way git/jj resolve them, with config reading isolated for tests.
Facts: `GitignoreCache.getNode` (vcs/ignore/GitignoreCache.kt:~117-135) builds each directory's `PatternList` from `<dir>/.gitignore` and, for the repo root only, appends `<repoRoot>/.git/info/exclude` lines AFTER the .gitignore lines. Because the matcher is "last matching pattern in the list wins" (PatternList.match), this gives `.git/info/exclude` HIGHER precedence than the root `.gitignore`, which is the opposite of git's real order (lowest -> highest: core.excludesFile < `$GIT_DIR/info/exclude` < `.gitignore` files, deeper dirs higher). Example that is wrong today: `.gitignore` has `!keep.log`, `info/exclude` has `*.log` -> git: keep.log NOT ignored; plugin: ignored. This precedence defect should be fixed in the same change (and jj-idea-2poe's golden tests must pin it - already listed there). Also note: in a NON-colocated jj repo there is no `.git/info/exclude` at the repo root (jj's git dir is `.jj/repo/store/git`; jj honours `core.excludesFile` from the global git config and per-repo `.jj/repo/store/git/info/exclude`? verify empirically before coding).
Step 0 - verify jj's actual sources (1h, contract-style scripted probes, isolated `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` sandbox as the bead did): for colocated and non-colocated repos check which of these jj honours when auto-tracking: (a) `core.excludesFile` in global gitconfig, (b) default `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore` / `~/.config/git/ignore` when core.excludesFile is unset, (c) classic `~/.gitignore` only if configured, (d) repo `.git/info/exclude` (colocated), (e) the jj store's own git dir `info/exclude` (non-colocated), (f) jj's own `core.excludesFile`-like config key if any (grep `jj config list | rg -i exclude`; newer jj may have its own). Record in docs/jj-track-untrack-model.md. Only implement the sources jj actually honours.
Design:
1. Resolver `GlobalExcludes.resolve(env: Env = SystemEnv): File?` (new, vcs/ignore/): returns the effective global excludes file: parse git config in git's precedence order for `core.excludesFile` (system /etc/gitconfig (skip), global `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config` then `~/.gitconfig` (both read; later wins: git reads xdg first then ~/.gitconfig, ~ overrides), repo-local `.git/config` (colocated) highest) via a tiny INI parser handling `[core]` section, `excludesFile = ~/path` with `~`/`~user` expansion and `include.path` ignoring (documented limitation); if unset: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore` else `~/.config/git/ignore`. Do NOT shell out to `git config` (rule 4: no git dependency at runtime, and git may be absent); read files directly. `Env` abstraction (HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL override honoured) so tests use temp dirs, never the real environment (acceptance criterion).
2. Cache semantics: resolution is per JVM per repo-root evaluation but cheap; the global file is read once per `GitignoreCache` instance (lazily, in getNode(root)) and re-read on `invalidate()`; changes to the global file/gitconfig are not VFS-watched (outside project) - add a cheap stat-based staleness check (lastModified + size of the resolved file, checked at most every 30s when `isIgnored` is called, or on explicit Refresh) OR just document "restart/invalidate to pick up". Rec: stat-check at most once per 60s on the BGT path - bounded (one `File.lastModified()`), keeps behaviour fresh without watchers.
3. Merge order: root PatternList lines = [global excludes] + [info/exclude] + [.gitignore]; (last wins => .gitignore highest, which also FIXES the current inversion). Pattern anchoring: global/exclude patterns are relative to the repo root (git: patterns in info/exclude and core.excludesFile with a slash anchor at the repo root) - parse with the same `GitignorePattern.parse`, matching entry paths relative to root - same as the existing exclude handling.
4. Scan (`collectIgnored`) uses the same `getNode(root)` - covered automatically; the scale rules hold (pruned traversal unchanged; extra patterns increase per-entry match cost by the number of global patterns: typical <50).
5. Consumers improved: Track/Untrack gating (`anySelectedIgnored`), ih95 tracked-ignored hint, otwq enablement, JujutsuIgnoredFileProvider colouring.
Decisions made without the user: Q: honour only what jj honours (step 0) vs everything git does? Rec: what jj honours. Q: stat-check refresh vs documented restart? Rec stat-check. Q: fix the exclude-vs-gitignore precedence inversion here? Rec yes (same code, same tests).
Scale: +1 file read per cache lifetime (+ <=1 stat/60s); no traversal change. Operation-count test: 10k isIgnored calls => 1 global read, <=1 stat.
Testing: resolver tests with temp HOME/XDG/GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL (precedence: xdg vs ~/.gitconfig vs local .git/config, `~` expansion, unset default path, missing file, malformed config, CRLF); GitignoreCacheTest additions (global-only pattern ignored; `.gitignore` negation overrides global/exclude (precedence); exclude no longer beats .gitignore); contract test against real jj in a sandbox HOME proving jj and the cache agree for a file matching only the global excludes; manual: MT-IGNORE (add `*.xyz` to the global excludes file; create `a.xyz` in the project: shows ignored colour, Track toggle offered). Regression scope: MT-IGNORE, MT-WORKINGCOPY.
acceptance_criteria: Files matching only jj-honoured global excludes report ignored (sandboxed-config tests); precedence global < info/exclude < .gitignore enforced; no real-environment reads in tests; bounded refresh; MT-IGNORE row.

title: Visually flag tracked-but-ignored files in the Working Copy panel
description:
jj-idea-i9ol added Track/Untrack context-menu actions. A file force-tracked via 'jj file track --include-ignored' despite matching a .gitignore rule is indistinguishable in jj's own output from an ordinary tracked file: verified empirically that 'jj status'/'jj diff --summary' render both as plain 'A'/'M' with no marker. So today, a user has no way to tell from the Working Copy panel alone which entries are 'tracked despite matching an ignore rule' (and thus meaningfully eligible for Untrack) vs. ordinary tracked files.

Needs its own design: a per-row ignore check (reusing JujutsuIgnoreService/GitignoreCache, same predictor Untrack's hint already uses) feeding the working-copy tree renderer with some visual marker (icon overlay, decoration, or tooltip) for tracked+ignored rows. Distinct from and follows on from jj-idea-i9ol.
design:
PLAN: flag "tracked despite matching an ignore rule" rows in the Working Copy changes tree via the platform's ChangeNodeDecorator hook, fed by the existing async tracked-state cache.
Facts: the tree is `JujutsuChangesTree` (ui/common/JujutsuChangesTree.kt); `buildTreeModel` already decorates conflicted rows with `ConflictShapeDecorator` (passed to `builder.insertChanges(conflicted, tagNode, ConflictShapeDecorator(myProject))`) - `ChangeNodeDecorator` is the platform's supported per-row decoration SPI (adds text/icons to a change node renderer). Ignore prediction: `JujutsuIgnoreService.isIgnored(filePath, repo.directory)` (vcs/ignore/JujutsuIgnoreService.kt:16-20, in-memory pattern match, safe off the EDT; note it is a prediction - misses global excludes, jj-idea-k5vy). Authoritative tracked state: `JujutsuTrackedFilesService.trackedStateOrNull(repo, path)` (vcs/ignore/JujutsuTrackedFilesService.kt:63; instant in-memory read; `requestRefresh(repo, paths)` batches one `jj file list` query on a pooled thread, :71). Everything in this tree is, by construction, in the working-copy DIFF (changed files); a file listed there that matches an ignore rule can only be there because it is tracked (jj ignores untracked-ignored files) - so for CHANGED files the tracked state is implied: no `jj file list` needed; the ignore prediction alone suffices for rows in the changes list (the tracked service is only needed for non-changed files). This removes the async cache from the common path.
Design:
1. `TrackedIgnoredDecorator : ChangeNodeDecorator` (ui/common/): `decorate(change, component: SimpleColoredComponent, isShowFlatten)` (pattern to copy: ui/common/ConflictShapeDecorator.kt, which appends a grey `FontUtil.spaceAndThinSpace()` + text via `component.append(..., GRAYED_ATTRIBUTES)`; tooltip via `preDecorate(change, renderer, ...)`): if `isIgnored(change.filePath)` (skip when `change.fileStatus` is DELETED/MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS? a DELETED tracked-ignored file is still tracked-ignored: include) then append a small grey hint `"ignored"` (bundle key `changes.tracked.ignored.hint`) and tooltip `"Tracked by jj although it matches an ignore rule - use Untrack to stop versioning it."` (the renderer's `toolTipText` for the node: set via `renderer.setToolTipText` in the decorator). Icon overlay alternative rejected: the platform node icon is the file-type icon with status colour; adding overlays needs custom icon composition per row (cost + theme risk); text hint is cheap and clear.
2. Cost control (scale rule: nothing O(working-set) heavy on paint): decorators run per rendered node on the EDT during paint; `isIgnored` per node = pattern match cost O(depth x patterns) - acceptable for visible rows only, but cache the result per FilePath in the tree's model build: compute during `buildTreeModel` (background-friendly? it runs on the EDT in the platform's tree builder `buildTreeModel`...) - Rec: precompute a `Set<FilePath>` of tracked-ignored changes once per tree rebuild (O(changes), at most the ~1k-change working-set envelope, using `isIgnored` per change), keep it in a field read by the decorator in O(1). Guard: cap the precompute at TRACKED_TOGGLE_SELECTION_LIMIT-style 5,000 changes, beyond which skip the flagging (log once) so a huge working set can't stall the rebuild.
3. Wire-up: in `buildTreeModel` pass the decorator for the normal (non-conflict) changes: `builder.setChanges(current, TrackedIgnoredDecorator(...))` (currently `setChanges(current, null)`) and for conflicted rows combine decorators (composite). Other trees (file selection panels in Split/Squash dialogs, history trees) are NOT affected (only the working-copy tree: enable via the existing `showsLocalFiles` flag, UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt:71, since only live working-copy rows can be 'tracked despite ignore').
4. Refresh: ignore rules change -> `JujutsuIgnoreService` invalidation fires the same change-list refresh path (VFS .gitignore change -> cache invalidated); ensure the tree rebuilds (`scheduleReloadChanges`) when `.gitignore` edits happen: check the invalidate path posts `VcsDirtyScopeManager` for the repo; add a refresh trigger if not.
5. Interplay with otwq: tracked-ignored files must NOT have actions disabled (they're tracked); the decorator text explains why Untrack is offered (TrackedToggleAction already shows for predicted-ignored).
Decisions made without the user: Q: text hint vs icon? Rec: grey text hint + tooltip. Q: rely on diff-membership as "tracked" (no jj call)? Rec yes (correct by construction; documented in code).
Scale: precompute O(changes) per rebuild with a 5k cap; decorator O(1). Operation-count test: tree rebuild with 1000 changes performs <= 1000 isIgnored calls and 0 jj subprocesses; paint calls O(visible).
Testing: decorator unit test (changes with ignored path vs not; fake ignore predicate; renderer capture); tree rebuild test with cap; manual: MT-IGNORE/MT-WORKINGCOPY (force-track an ignored file via Track toggle -> Working Copy panel row shows 'ignored' hint; Untrack removes the row; ordinary files unmarked). Regression scope: MT-IGNORE, MT-WORKINGCOPY.
acceptance_criteria: Tracked-but-ignored rows in the Working Copy tree show an 'ignored' hint with tooltip; no jj subprocess per row; capped precompute; only in the working-copy tree; unit + scale tests; MT-IGNORE row.
notes: jj-idea-i9ol round 4 built JujutsuTrackedFilesService (vcs/ignore/JujutsuTrackedFilesService.kt) - an on-demand, path-keyed async cache for 'is this path tracked' (jj file list), explicitly designed to be reused here rather than building a second cache. Use trackedStateOrNull/requestRefresh directly.

title: Double-click a log commit triggers the same action as Enter (default: Show Diff)
description: A new user expected (GitHub #51 point 9) double-clicking a commit in the log to check it out (jj edit/new), or at minimum show the diff. There is currently no double-click handler at all on JujutsuLogTable.kt rows. Per the UX-priority tenet (jj-idea-2ffd: IntelliJ-native > jj-native > bespoke), IntelliJ's own VcsLogGraphTable has NO double-click-to-checkout or double-click-to-diff — commit actions there are keymap-bound, and mouseClicked only handles link clicks. So: route double-click through the same single keymap-bound action as Enter (one action id bound to both inputs, not a bespoke 'double-click behaviour' setting), defaulting that action to Show Diff (read-only, satisfies the reporter's stated minimum). Users who want jj edit on double-click can rebind the action in Keymap settings; Edit/New remain available as their own keymappable actions (see jj-idea-0iui epic).
acceptance_criteria: Double-clicking a log row triggers the same action as pressing Enter with that row selected; default action is Show Diff; the action is rebindable via IntelliJ's Keymap settings
notes: GitHub #51 point 9. Depends on jj-idea-2ffd (tenet doc) for rationale. Cross-reference jj-idea (quick-new bead) for Edit as an alternative bindable action, and jj-idea-st7 (post-op selection behaviour).
close_reason: Enter bound to Show Diff via plugin.xml keymap; double-click routes through whichever action is bound to Enter (DoubleClickListener + invokeEnterBoundAction in JujutsuLogTable.kt)

title: Dedicated New/Edit buttons in log toolbar
description: Part of jj-idea-0iui (faster change creation epic). GitHub #51 point 8 notes VisualJJ (https://www.visualjj.com/) puts New/Edit-style operations as dedicated buttons directly in the log view toolbar, rather than requiring a right-click context menu. Add New (no-description, see jj-idea sibling bead) and Edit buttons to the log toolbar (CommitTablePanel.kt createActionGroup(), ~line 237) so the common operations are one click from the log without opening a context menu.
acceptance_criteria: Log toolbar has visible New and Edit buttons that operate on the currently selected commit
notes: GitHub #51 point 8.
close_reason: Shipped: New/Edit buttons in log toolbar

title: 'New change (no description)' quick action with default keybinding
description: Part of jj-idea-0iui (faster change creation epic). GitHub #51 point 8: the reporter almost never wants to enter a description upfront when creating a new change (they'll squash it in shortly). newChangeFromAction.kt (line 24) currently always calls project.requestDescription(...) which blocks on a modal dialog. Add a variant action that skips the dialog entirely and creates an unnamed/empty-description change directly, with a default keybinding so it's reachable without any menu at all.
acceptance_criteria: A 'New change (no description)' action exists, is bound to a default keyboard shortcut, and creates a new change from the selected commit(s) without showing the description dialog
notes: GitHub #51 point 8.
close_reason: Implemented: quick no-dialog New Change action, keybound Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+N, primary in log context menu

title: Responsive log column sizing to avoid horizontal scroll on narrow windows
description: A new user reported (GitHub #51 point 6) that on a laptop-sized screen the log graph view requires horizontal scrolling unless the tool window occupies almost the full screen width, and even more so with the details/file pane open side-by-side. Suggests the graph/message column should scale to available width, shrinking as needed. JujutsuLogTable.kt already has adjustDescriptionColumnWidth() (~line 541) which fills remaining space for COLUMN_GRAPH_AND_DESCRIPTION after subtracting other visible columns; investigate lowering effective minimums / truncation behaviour for narrow windows so scrolling is needed less often.
acceptance_criteria: On a narrow log tool window, fewer/no horizontal scroll is needed for the graph+description column; other columns (author/date) may need to collapse or truncate more aggressively first
notes: GitHub #51 point 6 (responsive-sizing half). Pairs with jj-idea-f27g (scroll-reset bug) and thematically related to jj-idea-kxx4 (toolbar layout under width pressure).
close_reason: Implemented: viewport-aware column fitting (fitColumnWidths pure fn + JViewport listener) gated behind a per-tab 'Fit Columns to Window Width' toggle, defaulting on for untouched tabs and off for tabs with pre-existing custom widths so no one's persisted layout is silently overridden.

title: Make log 'link-styled' items actually clickable/actionable
description: A new user reported (GitHub #51 point 4) that many items in the log render with link styling (blue underline via TextCanvas.kt linked()/LINK_ATTRIBUTES — author names ~line 173, bookmark chips ~lines 298-351, tag chips ~line 338-351) but clicking them does nothing beyond selecting the row (JujutsuLogTable.kt mouseClicked handler ~lines 284-297 just calls changeSelection.notify). Rather than strip the misleading styling, make them do something meaningful: bookmark/tag chip click -> filter or scroll the log to that ref; author click -> filter by that author (reuse JujutsuAuthorFilterComponent). Author email already opens mailto: via TextCanvas.kt:173 — keep that.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a bookmark or tag chip filters/navigates the log to that ref; clicking an author name filters the log by that author; author email mailto link continues to work
notes: GitHub #51 point 4. Sibling to jj-idea-10fo (issue-tracker links in commit descriptions) — that one is about IssueNavigationConfiguration links, this one is about log-row chip/author links; keep them separate but cross-reference.
close_reason: Implemented: bookmark/tag chip left-click filters the log to that reference, author/committer name left-click opens the OS mail client, right-click menus mirror the same actions with the default highlighted plus a 'Filter by author' extra on the author menu. Added PersonClick target, findPersonClickTarget hit-test, JujutsuStateModel.filterToReference/filterByAuthor notifiers, JujutsuReferenceFilterComponent.selectReference, and DefaultClickAction-highlighted right-click popups. Covered by PersonClickTargetTest, ClickActionGroupDefaultActionTest, JujutsuReferenceFilterComponentSelectReferenceTest, and two new JujutsuStateModelPlatformTest cases. ./gradlew check passes.

title: Fix log hover tooltip: dismiss on scroll, allow text selection
description: Companion to the tooltip-toggle bead. Even for users who keep the log hover tooltip enabled, GitHub #51 point 3 reports two concrete bugs: (1) it doesn't disappear when the user scrolls the log, so it blocks the view; (2) the tooltip disappears as soon as the mouse moves, so text inside it can't be selected/copied. Investigate within IdeTooltip/IdeTooltipManager constraints (JujutsuLogTable.kt lines 66-241) whether these are fixable — e.g. hide on scroll events, or make the tooltip content interactive/copyable.
acceptance_criteria: Tooltip dismisses when the log view is scrolled; tooltip content can be selected and copied without disappearing on mouse move (or a documented reason why IdeTooltip can't support this)
notes: GitHub #51 point 3. Depends on/pairs with the tooltip-toggle bead.
close_reason: Fixed via canAutohideOn/isHint (matching TooltipWithClickableLinks) plus scroll-dismissal in IconAwareTooltip.kt; tknb dependency dropped since a settings toggle is no longer needed to make the tooltip usable

title: Log toolbar: don't let filter crowd out Fetch/Push buttons
description: A new user reported (GitHub #51 point 7) that the log title bar gives precedence to the filter field over the Fetch/Push action buttons — the filter grows (especially once a filter is active from the dropdown) and leaves less space for the buttons on the right, which matter more day-to-day. Toolbar is built in CommitTablePanel.kt createToolbar() (~line 179: filter WEST, action toolbar EAST) / createActionGroup() (~line 237: Refresh, Fetch, Push, Columns, DetailsPosition). Ensure the action toolbar (esp. Push) stays visible/reachable under width pressure, e.g. give it priority in layout or cap filter field growth.
acceptance_criteria: On a narrow window, Fetch/Push (and all other action-toolbar buttons: New, Edit, Refresh, Columns, Details) remain visible/clickable even with an active filter, since the action toolbar keeps layout priority (BorderLayout.EAST). The search field shrinks down to a ~150px floor rather than growing unbounded. The filter chips (Reference/Author/Date/Root/Bookmark) collapse into a standard '»' overflow popup under width pressure via a custom FilterPriorityLayoutStrategy: unapplied filters are hidden first, an applied filter stays visible even if filters to its left are hidden, and whatever remains visible keeps its original left-to-right order (no reordering).
notes: GitHub #51 point 7. Related theme to jj-idea B6b (responsive graph column sizing) but a separate surface (toolbar vs table).
close_reason: Fixed: action toolbar keeps layout priority (BorderLayout.EAST), search field shrinks to a floor, and filter chips collapse into a priority-ordered '»' overflow popup (unapplied filters hidden first, applied ones stay visible, no reordering).

title: Show author email in commit details panel
description: The commit details panel (JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt buildCommitHtml, ~lines 231-245) shows the author's display name but not their email, even though LogEntry.author is a VcsUser that already carries .email (see JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt UserCellRenderer, which already exposes it as a tooltip). GitHub #51 point 5 asks for the email to be visible in the details pane too. Add it — e.g. as a mailto link or plain text alongside the name, consistent with how TextCanvas.kt:173 already renders author as a mailto link elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: Details panel shows author email (and committer email when different), not just display name
notes: GitHub #51 point 5. Trivial — data already available on VcsUser.
close_reason: Implemented: author/committer email now rendered as Name <email> mailto link in commit details panel

title: Show immutable padlock icon only (drop mutable icon)
description: The log currently shows a padlock-style icon for BOTH mutable and immutable revisions (JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt:54, appendStatusIndicators), distinguished only by colour. A new user reported this as visual noise (GitHub #51 point 1) since the icons are otherwise indistinguishable. Show the icon only for immutable revisions; mutable (the common case) gets no icon.
acceptance_criteria: Mutable revisions show no status padlock icon; immutable revisions still show theirs
notes: GitHub #51 point 1.
close_reason: Fixed: appendStatusIndicators now only shows the icon for immutable revisions; added AppendStatusIndicatorsTest

title: jj log crashes when Revset expression setting is left empty
description:
Surfaced in GitHub issue #35 comment thread: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/35#issuecomment (SergejSalnikov)

Leaving the 'Revset expression' setting (Settings / Version Control / Jujutsu) empty produces a crash:

Error: Failed to parse template: Failed to evaluate revset
Caused by: 2: UNAVAILABLE: Stream removed (Socket closed)

Stack originates at jj/cli/CliLogService.kt:180 (getLog), via RepoLogCache.fetch/fetchOne/get <- JujutsuStateModel.workingCopies. Need to validate/guard the empty-revset case (fall back to a sane default) rather than sending an empty expression to jj.
acceptance_criteria: Leaving the revset expression setting empty does not crash; falls back to a documented default revset.
notes:
CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (2026-07-27) — supersedes the 2026-07-11 investigation notes.

The 2026-07-11 notes chased the wrong code path. Re-reading the actual GitHub #35 crash stack:

  at CliLogService.getLog-BWLJW6A(CliLogService.kt:180)
  at RepoLogCache.fetch(LogCache.kt:110)
  at RepoLogCache.fetchOne(LogCache.kt:108)
  at RepoLogCache.get(LogCache.kt:105)
  at JujutsuStateModel.workingCopies$lambda$16(JujutsuStateModel.kt:170)

This resolves the WORKING-COPY revision (@) via RepoLogCache.get, passing @ as the -r revset.
It NEVER reads the "Revset expression" setting. So the empty-field/trunk() theory ("case 2" in
the old notes) does not match this stack at all — there is no evidence it's real. Drop it unless
new evidence surfaces.

The error caret in the reporter's paste is the TEMPLATE field hasPushedAncestor, spec
self.contained_in("descendants(::remote_bookmarks())") (CliLogService.kt:344) — this is "case 1"
from the old notes. descendants(::remote_bookmarks()) is a global revset (ancestors of all remote
bookmarks, then their descendants); on a server-backed/gRPC (Google) backend it round-trips to the
server, which returned UNAVAILABLE: Stream removed (Socket closed).

This is ALREADY HANDLED since v0.7.10: CliLogService.getLog/getLogBasic (:60-85) pass a
fallbackTemplate; on "Failed to evaluate revset" (TEMPLATE_EVALUATION_FAILURE, :236) it marks the
repo (pushedAncestorUnsupported) and retries with the reduced template in the same call. Both the
`all` and `get`/`fetchOne` paths funnel through this getLog, so the reported crash IS covered in
the current release. Reporter was on ~v0.7.7/0.7.8 pre-fallback and has not retested v0.7.13.

IMPORTANT DISTINCTION for any future work here: don't conflate the per-commit template keyword
remote_bookmarks (CliLogService.kt:310, in the `bookmarks` field — KEPT in the reduced template,
assumed cheap/local) with the global revset descendants(::remote_bookmarks()) (:344 — DROPPED in
the reduced template, the expensive thing that failed).

WHAT RELIES ON hasPushedAncestor (single consumer): OpenFileInRemoteGroup.update
(OpenFileInRemoteGroup.kt:36) — visibility gate for "Open File in Remote" context action only.
Degrading to false just hides that one additive action; no core functionality depends on it. A
separate action-time query, latestPushedAncestorCommitId (CliExecutor.kt:503), also uses
remote_bookmarks(remote=...) and could fail on click for mutable commits (immutable commits skip
it, using the commit id directly).

KNOWN COVERAGE HOLE, not yet fixed: getLogAndFileStatuses (CliLogService.kt:98) ->
fileStatusesFor (:415) is built from basicLogTemplate, which unconditionally includes
hasPushedAncestor, called with NO fallbackTemplate and without consulting
supportsPushedAncestor(). File-history loading (JujutsuHistoryProvider) on the same backend could
still crash with the identical error. Real follow-up fix, but parked — see below.

WHY THIS BEAD IS NOW BLOCKED/DOWNGRADED: whether descendants(::remote_bookmarks()) fails EVERY
TIME on such a backend or only WHEN OFFLINE/under load decides the whole design (sticky per-repo
disable vs. resettable circuit breaker vs. user-facing setting). Evidence leans transient (gRPC
UNAVAILABLE = retryable/unreachable, not UNIMPLEMENTED), which would mean the current PERMANENT,
session-sticky disable (CliLogService.kt:481-486, pushedAncestorUnsupported, reset only on IDE
restart) is too aggressive. Can't be settled from the codebase alone — needs an affected user.

ACTION: posted a follow-up on GitHub #35 asking the reporter (SergejSalnikov) for: (1) frequency
(every time vs intermittent), (2) connectivity correlation (offline/flaky when it happened?), and
(3) three isolating jj commands separating the cheap per-commit remote_bookmarks lookup from the
expensive descendants(::remote_bookmarks()) revset. Deferred pending their reply. Priority
downgraded P2 -> P3 since the reported crash is already covered in the shipped release.

title: Richer commit-message editor for jj describe (spellcheck, inspections, plugin hooks)
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/46

Requester wants the jj describe editor to behave like IntelliJ's built-in Git commit-message editor: spellcheck, length/format inspections, and support for plugins like Co-Author or Gitmoji that operate on commit messages. Currently the describe editor is a plain text field missing these platform integrations.

Design question to resolve first: can the plugin reuse IntelliJ's actual commit-message editor component (com.intellij.openapi.vcs.ui.CommitMessage or similar) for jj describe, or does it need a bespoke reimplementation of the relevant inspections?
acceptance_criteria: jj describe editor gets spellcheck and commit-message inspections; feasibility of reusing the platform component is documented.
notes: IdeaVim manually verified (2026-08-31) across all six description inputs (Describe, DescribeWorkingCopy, Split x2, Squash Into, New Change, Working Copy panel) - Escape leaves insert mode instead of closing the dialog everywhere. User will report back on GitHub #46 at release time.
close_reason: Shipped: all description inputs use a real commit-message editor; IdeaVim verified manually across every call site

title: Keep colored bookmark icon visible when chips overflow to '(N more)'
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/49

When a commit has many/long bookmark names, the log graph collapses overflow bookmark chips into a plain grey '(N more)' label, losing the colored bookmark icon. This makes it easy to miss that a commit is a branch head. Keep showing a colored bookmark icon (rather than plain grey text) even in the collapsed/overflow state; clicking still opens the existing context menu of all bookmarks on that change.

Relevant code: ui/components/TextCanvas.kt:142-178 (appendBookmarks), ui/log/JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt:194-240 (SeparateDecorationsCellRenderer).
acceptance_criteria: Overflow indicator for many-bookmark commits keeps a colored bookmark glyph instead of plain grey text.
close_reason: Shipped in f2d94f8ed2bb; GitHub #49 closed

title: Log summary count lags behind after loading more commits + Refresh at a limit
description:
Noticed while manually reproducing jj-idea-1ojh against jj-stress-test.

Repro: set Settings -> Version Control -> Jujutsu -> Log Limit to 200. Click a
parent change-id that isn't present in the currently-loaded log -- this loads
more commits as expected, and the summary line correctly shows "Showing 251
changes (limit: 200)". Hit Refresh: the log correctly shrinks back down to 200
rows, but the summary line keeps showing "251 changes (limit: 200)" for a few
seconds before it recalculates to the correct "200".

So there's a lag between the log table refreshing and the summary/count label
refreshing -- they're apparently updated from different triggers/threads and
the summary update trails behind. Not a correctness bug in the graph itself
(distinct from jj-idea-5i6i/jj-idea-1ojh tree-line corruction), just a stale
label for a couple of seconds.
design:
PLAN: characterise first, then make the count derive from one source of truth.
Facts: the label is `CommitTablePanel.updateStatusBar(entryCount, limit)` (ui/common/CommitTablePanel.kt:653; hidden when PAGED_LOG_LOAD is on or entryCount < limit; otherwise "Showing N changes (limit: L)" via `log.status.truncated`). It is called from `UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.onDataLoaded` (UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.kt:233) with `newData.entries.size`. Loading more commits (click on a parent id -> `UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.loadMore()` :632, merged via `mergeAndNotify` :368 which notifies via `runLater { notify(data) }` :380) grows the snapshot past the limit (251). `refresh()` (:471) / `forceRefresh()` (:561) then re-read; the reported lag means a notify with the shrunk list reaches the table but the label update is skipped or overwritten.
Suspects to confirm (step 0, 30 min - add temporary logging in onDataLoaded and updateStatusBar, repro on jj-stress-test with limit 200): (1) the refresh path takes a fast path (`refreshOneRepoLocked` :522 / fastMergeAndNotify) that notifies via a different callback than `onDataLoaded` (e.g. updates the table model only), so the label waits for the next full load (the "few seconds" = next periodic/VFS-triggered load); (2) `showStatusMessage` text from search/revset (`log.status.revset.beyondWindow`, search found/none) replaces the label and nothing restores it; (3) `notify()` ordering race: an earlier `runLater { notify(bigData) }` from mergeAndNotify lands AFTER the refresh's notify (both go through runLater; refresh path at :208 calls notify directly on the BGT-to-EDT?). Check thread/ordering at :99-106 and :208 vs :380.
Fix (shape depends on cause): make the status label a pure function of the table model's row count - derive it in one place on every model change (`tableModel.addTableModelListener` -> `updateStatusBar(tableModel.rowCount, limit)`), instead of at specific data-loaded call sites. Then any path that changes rows updates the label in the same EDT pass; ordering races vanish because the label always reflects the model. Keep search/revset messages as higher-priority overrides cleared on next model change.
Interaction: with jj-idea-2570.4 (paged graduation) this label only exists for the legacy/fallback path (hidden for paged mode), so keep the fix small; if 2570.4 lands first and removes the non-paged path, close this bead as obsolete after confirming the label never shows in paged mode.
Decisions made without the user: Q: fix it at all given 2570.4? Rec: yes if 2570.4 is not yet released, minimal model-listener change (<30 lines); otherwise close. 
Scale: O(1) per model change (rowCount read). Testing: panel test with a fake DataLoader: notify(251 entries, limit 200) then notify(200 entries) -> label text reflects 200 immediately after the second notify; search message cleared on model change. Manual: MT-LOG-TABLE / MT-LOG-REFRESH row: limit 200 repro from the bead. Regression scope: MT-LOG-REFRESH, MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-FILTER (search/revset status messages).
acceptance_criteria: After Refresh shrinks the log to the limit, the status label matches the row count in the same paint pass (no multi-second lag); cause characterised and noted; panel test added; MT-LOG-REFRESH row added.

title: Custom diffbase for gutter markers and annotations
description:
GitHub #43: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/43
Let users pick the base revision (HEAD/@-, latest immutable ancestor, grandparent, or custom revset) used for editor gutter change markers and blame. Both DiffbaseContentLoader (LineStatusTracker) and JujutsuAnnotationProvider must resolve through one shared service to avoid annotation misalignment. Issue includes a full proposed architecture and file list.
close_reason: Implemented: DiffbaseService + DiffbaseContentLoader + JujutsuAnnotationProvider integration, Settings UI (project + per-repo), MT-DIFFBASE manual section, unit+platform tests, CHANGELOG entry.

title: Search log by Git commit hash
description:
GitHub #44: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/44
IntelliJ's Git plugin resolves a pasted git commit hash from the log search bar. jj-idea returns nothing. Resolve a git hash to its jj change (revset) and select it in the log.
close_reason: Log search text filter now matches commitId.short/full alongside change id/description/author. Tests added. Whole-repo search on Enter split into follow-up jj-idea-lpbv.

title: Bridge elided revisions with wiggly edges in filtered log graph
description: When filtering hides intermediate ancestors, the log graph drops the edge to the surviving visible ancestor entirely. jj itself draws wiggly lines to indicate elided revisions. Fix: add a nearest-visible-ancestor remap (O(n+edges), topological walk with memoisation) that rewires each visible commit's parents to their nearest visible ancestors with an 'elided' flag; thread the flag through GraphEntry/RowLayout/GraphNode; render elided edges as wiggly/dashed lines in JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer. The same remap also covers the jj-idea-xi58 limit-cutoff case (out of scope here — just note the connection). The CommitGraphBuilder gains a (allEntries, visibleIds) overload used by the Bead A recompute hook.
design:
PLAN: additive "elided edge" rendering for filtered logs, built on the already-shipped HIDDEN/NOT_LOADED parent classification (docs/design/jj-idea-hlu3-xi58-elided-ancestor-rendering.md; xi58/1pgy/sc8m are closed).
Current state (verified): `CommitGraphBuilder.buildGraph(entries, allEntries)` (ui/log/JujutsuCommitGraph.kt:119) already takes the filtered set plus the full set and classifies each unresolved parent as `ParentState.HIDDEN` (filtered out) vs `NOT_LOADED`; `GraphEdgeIndex` (ui/log/GraphEdgeIndex.kt:243-290) draws a one-row stub for either; the renderer tooltip says "hidden by the current filter" for HIDDEN with no navigation (`navigable = edge.state != HIDDEN`, GraphEdgeIndex.kt:145). The refresh point is `UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.refreshDisplayedGraph()` (:212) which rebuilds from `getFilteredEntries()` + `getAllEntries()` on every filter change.
What hlu3 adds: instead of a dead-end stub for a HIDDEN parent, connect the visible child to its NEAREST VISIBLE ANCESTOR and draw that edge wiggly/dashed (jj's `~ (elided revisions)` behaviour; GH #131: `main | @ | remote_bookmarks()` should show @ and main linked).
Design:
1. Pure function `nearestVisibleAncestors(allEntries, visibleIds): Map<ChangeKey, List<ElidedParent>>` in ui/log/graph/ (beside LayoutCalculatorImpl, generic over DagNode like RebaseSimulator's core so it is unit-testable without LogEntry): for each visible commit, for each parent p: if p visible -> direct edge; else DFS/BFS up through hidden parents collecting the first visible ancestors reached; memoise per hidden node (`Map<ChangeKey, Set<ChangeKey>>`) so each hidden node is expanded once => O(n + edges) total, with the memo shared across all visible commits. Cycle-free by construction (DAG). Cap pathological fan-in: a hidden merge-rich region can produce many visible ancestors per node; keep as is (correctness), but the memo set sizes are bounded by #visible.
2. Graph build: `buildGraph(filtered, all)` rewires each visible entry's parents to those results, each marked `elided = true` when it came through >=1 hidden node. Thread the flag: `GraphEntry`/`RowLayout`/`GraphNode` (ui/log/JujutsuCommitGraph.kt:31, layout in ui/log/graph/) gain `elidedParents: Set<ChangeKey>`; LayoutCalculator treats them as ordinary parent edges for lane assignment (so the connector is a real line to the real row) - the only difference is paint style. An ancestor reached by BOTH a direct and an elided path keeps the direct (solid) edge.
3. Paint: JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer draws elided edges dashed/wiggly (reuse the stub-drawing dash helper `drawElidedParentStub`, JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.kt:306, as the stroke style); GraphEdgeIndex long-edge hover/tooltip: tooltip "N revisions hidden by the filter" (count of skipped hidden nodes on the shortest path is not required - say "revisions hidden by the filter"); elided edges are navigable to the target row (it IS visible) -> reuses sc8m long-edge navigation for free.
4. Roots with no visible ancestor at all: keep the current HIDDEN stub (nothing to connect to).
5. On-demand rows (GH #131 comment 2026-10-01): users can click NOT_LOADED stubs to load revisions into the window; the remap must be RECOMPUTED, not patched: `refreshDisplayedGraph()` already rebuilds from scratch on filter change; ensure `onDataLoaded` after a click-to-load also recomputes (it calls refreshDisplayedGraph, :231) and add the test for several on-demand rows in different positions (see below). Incremental `appendGraph` (:158) must bail to a full rebuild when a filter is active.
Decisions made without the user: Q: dashed or "wiggly" (jj style)? Rec: dashed line first (reuses existing dash helper, cheap, theme-safe); a true wavy stroke is a follow-up. Reverse: swap the stroke. Q: show jj's synthetic `~ (elided revisions)` row? Rec: no - extra rows break row<->entry mapping everywhere (selection, DnD). 
Depends on jj-idea-2570.4 only in the sense of paged windows creating NOT_LOADED vs HIDDEN states (already distinguished); not a hard blocker - set that dependency as soft.
Scale: remap O(n + e) per filter change on EDT at limit <=500 rows (existing note says imperceptible); at 10k rows (paged windows sizes are per-page, but filter applies to loaded rows) still linear. Operation-count test: 10k-row linear history with every 2nd hidden => node visits <= 2n (assert via a counting accessor), no per-visible-commit re-walk.
Testing: unit - remap on: linear chain with hidden middle; diamond with one hidden side; hidden merge; all-hidden ancestors (root stub kept); dedupe direct+elided; several on-demand rows loaded in sequence; layout tests (LayoutCalculatorTest) for lane assignment with elided parents; renderer paint test in the existing graph render tests. Manual: MT-LOG-GRAPH (revset `main | @ | remote_bookmarks()`: connected dashed edges, click navigates), MT-LOG-FILTER (author/path/reference filters). Regression scope: MT-LOG-GRAPH, MT-LOG-FILTER, MT-LOG-TABLE (row hover/edge tooltip).
acceptance_criteria: With a filter hiding intermediate ancestors, each visible commit is connected to its nearest visible ancestors by dashed elided edges; direct edges stay solid; remap is O(n+e) with memo (count test); recomputed (not patched) after on-demand row loads; MT-LOG-GRAPH rows added.
notes:
REVISED (supersedes this bead's earlier note): now decoupled and additive, not sequenced with jj-idea-xi58.
