The xi58/1pgy/sc8m session (see docs/design/jj-idea-hlu3-xi58-elided-ancestor-rendering.md) makes NAVIGATION, not connection, the answer to 'where does this edge go' - so xi58 no longer needs hlu3's nearest-visible-ancestor remap as a prerequisite or companion. hlu3 remains valuable on its own: it would upgrade a HIDDEN (filtered-out) edge's tooltip into a real rendered connector to the nearest still-visible ancestor, purely additive on top of whatever xi58/1pgy/sc8m ship. Its own session, whenever convenient. Entry point for the whole follow-up set: jj-idea-4kfh (epic).
GitHub #131 (SergejSalnikov, 2026-09-28) independently requests this: revset `main | @ | remote_bookmarks()` leaves @ and main showing as unrelated rows with no edge/marker, matching jj's own indirect-edge + `~ (elided revisions)` synthetic row behavior (ui.log-synthetic-elided-nodes). Confirms the general revset-filtering case (not just log-limit cutoff) is real user-facing pain, not just internal design motivation. Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/131
2026-10-01: SergejSalnikov (GH #131 comment) notes users can dynamically add not-yet-loaded revisions to the graph by clicking them; the nearest-visible-ancestor remap must be recomputed (not patched) when revisions are added on demand, and positioning several such rows is tricky. Add a test for several on-demand rows.

title: Per-repo backend-capability caching for log template fields (proper fix for descendants(::remote_bookmarks()) failures)
description: Companion to jj-idea-2wpq, deliberately deprioritised: this google3/Piper-specific backend use case is a non-paying corporate use case, so deep resilience work here is lower priority than community-useful fixes — but raised here so it isn't lost. jj-idea-2wpq ships a minimal per-call retry workaround (drop hasPushedAncestor and retry once when jj log fails with 'Failed to evaluate revset'). That workaround pays one extra jj invocation on EVERY query against a broken backend, forever, because it doesn't remember the degradation. The proper fix is to detect and cache per-repo which optional template fields the backend can't evaluate, so subsequent queries build the reduced template up front and never even attempt the failing field.
design: Sketch (refine at implementation time): add a small per-repo capability cache (e.g. a ConcurrentHashMap<String, Set<degraded field>> keyed by repo directory path, or a @Volatile flag on a repo-scoped service) inside CliLogService or a sibling class. On first 'Failed to evaluate revset' failure for a repo, record that hasPushedAncestor (and potentially other revset-dependent template fields, if more are added later) is unsupported for that repo, and build all subsequent getLog calls for that repo with the reduced template directly — no retry round-trip needed after the first detection. Consider whether this capability should be probed proactively (e.g. on repo open) vs. lazily on first failure (lazy avoids cost for the common healthy-repo case, matches the project's general preference against redundant jj invocations). Also consider exposing the degraded state via a notification or status so the user understands why pushed-ancestor indicators are missing, rather than silently never showing them. Relevant files: CliLogService.kt (getLog 165-184, hasPushedAncestor field 279), possibly JujutsuRepository or a repo-scoped service for the cache lifetime/invalidation (e.g. on jj executable change or repo reload).
acceptance_criteria: Not yet refined — to be fleshed out when this is picked up. At minimum: second and subsequent log queries against a backend known to fail descendants(::remote_bookmarks()) should NOT pay the double jj invocation; should include a test proving the reduced template is used directly without a failed first attempt.
close_reason: Capability caching folded into jj-idea-2wpq's fix: CliLogService caches pushed-ancestor-unsupported repos per repo path for the session (companion object ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet, reset on IDE restart), avoiding repeated doomed jj invocations.

title: Add application/global 'disable ignored-file scanning' toggle
description: GitHub issue #35 (SergejSalnikov): the 'disable ignored-file scanning' escape hatch currently exists only as a per-repository override (RepositoryConfig.disableIgnoredFileScanning, stored in the project-scoped JujutsuSettings/JujutsuSettingsState.repositoryOverrides — see JujutsuSettings.kt:111-123, RepositoryConfig.kt:12). There is no way to switch it off once for all repos/projects on a machine; the only application-level settings class (JujutsuApplicationSettings / JujutsuApplicationSettingsState, JujutsuApplicationSettings.kt:34-36) currently holds only jjExecutablePath. Users on huge repos (and reviewers wanting a quick global kill-switch) requested this be exposed 'outside of project level'.
design: 1) Add 'disableIgnoredFileScanning: Boolean = false' to JujutsuApplicationSettingsState (JujutsuApplicationSettings.kt). 2) Change the resolver JujutsuSettings.disableIgnoredFileScanning(repo) (JujutsuSettings.kt:111-112) from hard-coded '?: false' to '?: JujutsuApplicationSettings.getInstance().state.disableIgnoredFileScanning' — i.e. per-repo override (when non-null) still wins; otherwise fall back to the new global default instead of always false. The single read site (JujutsuIgnoredFilesService.kt:129) needs no change. 3) Add a global checkbox in JujutsuConfigurable.createPanel() (JujutsuConfigurable.kt), bound via the Kotlin UI DSL ('row { checkBox(...).bindSelected(appSettings.state::disableIgnoredFileScanning) }') — place in the existing group(log) block (around lines 171-198) or a new short row near the executable group (lines 85-102). Label clearly, e.g. 'Disable ignored-file scanning (all repositories)'. Keep the existing per-repo checkbox (disableScanCb, ~lines 344-347) but clarify its label/tooltip as an override of the global default. Add the new i18n message key to the existing messages bundle used by JujutsuConfigurable.
acceptance_criteria: - JujutsuSettings.disableIgnoredFileScanning(repo) returns the per-repo override when set, otherwise the application-level default (not always false). - New checkbox visible in Settings / Version Control / Jujutsu, persisted via JujutsuApplicationSettings (PersistentStateComponent at APP level), survives IDE restart. - Extend settings/JujutsuSettingsTest.kt: a test asserting per-repo override (true or false) wins over a conflicting global default, and a test asserting the global default is honoured when no per-repo override exists. - Manual smoke documented/added to docs/manual-tests.md: toggle global checkbox off, confirm scanning stops across repos with no per-repo override; toggle a per-repo override on, confirm it still takes precedence over a global 'off'.
close_reason: Shipped in one PR (batch 2 of jj-idea-exgr)

title: Harden GitignoreCache differential/golden tests against git semantics
description: GitignoreCache (vcs/ignore/GitignoreCache.kt) reimplements gitignore matching in-JVM (anchoring, **, *, ?, [...], negation, dir-only, deepest-wins, .git/info/exclude merge). Risk of drift from git's canonical semantics. Rather than delegate to git at runtime (rejected — see CLAUDE.md Performance & Scale rule 4 and closed jj-idea-2570.3), add golden/differential test cases that pin behavior against documented git gitignore rules. Extend GitignoreCacheTest.kt / GitignoreScanTest.kt with edge cases: trailing-slash dir-only patterns, leading-slash anchoring, mid-path slashes, '**' in various positions, character classes, negation re-inclusion under an ignored ancestor (git forbids re-including under an excluded dir), and .git/info/exclude precedence.
design:
PLAN: pin GitignoreCache semantics to git's actual behaviour with (1) a golden table taken from git's own documented rules and (2) a DIFFERENTIAL test that asks real git as an oracle (test-time only, never at runtime - contributing.md Performance rule 4 bans a runtime git delegate).
Facts: matcher = vcs/ignore/GitignoreCache.kt (`isIgnored(file)` :32, `isIgnored(relPath, isDirectory)` :42, `collectIgnored` :76, `getNode` :117, `.git/info/exclude` merge :123-125); existing tests: vcs/ignore/GitignoreCacheTest.kt (basic cases: exact name, dir-only, anchoring path, comments, nested ignored dir, negation basic, sub-.gitignore scoping, `**` any depth, single `*`, exclude merge, invalidate) and GitignoreScanTest.kt. git is available in dev/CI (/usr/bin/git; GitHub Actions ubuntu/macos runners have it) - the contract tests already require real jj, so a git requirement is consistent.
Part 1 - golden cases (pure unit, no git needed; each case = patterns + (path, isDir) -> expected, with a comment citing the gitignore(5) rule): trailing-slash dir-only (`build/` ignores dir `build` and its contents, not a FILE named build); leading-slash anchoring (`/foo` root only vs `foo` any depth); mid-path slash anchors (`a/b` is relative to the .gitignore dir); `**` leading (`**/foo`), trailing (`abc/**` = everything inside, not abc itself), middle (`a/**/b` matches a/b, a/x/b, a/x/y/b); `?` and `[abc]`/`[a-z]`/`[!a]`; `*` does not cross `/`; escaped `\#`, `\!`, trailing spaces (unescaped trailing spaces ignored, `\ ` kept); negation (`!`) re-inclusion; negation CANNOT re-include under an excluded parent dir (`foo/` then `!foo/bar` -> still ignored) but CAN when the parent isn't excluded itself (`foo/*` then `!foo/bar`); last matching pattern wins within a file; deeper .gitignore overrides shallower; `.git/info/exclude` lower precedence than .gitignore and merged at repo root; case sensitivity (git is case-sensitive unless core.ignorecase - document: matcher is case-sensitive; macOS default FS case-insensitivity noted as a known divergence, add a test pinning current behaviour).
Part 2 - differential test (JUnit5, `@Tag("contract")`-style so it runs with contractTest, skipped (Assumptions) when `git` is not on PATH): generate N pseudo-random cases (fixed seed, e.g. 500) from a grammar of pattern atoms (names, `*`, `**`, `?`, `[x]`, leading/trailing `/`, `!`) over a small fixed path universe (e.g. 40 paths in 3 levels incl. dirs), write them to a temp dir as .gitignore (+ one nested .gitignore), materialise the paths on disk, `git init` + `git check-ignore -v --no-index --stdin` (or `git status --ignored --porcelain` equivalent) for the oracle, and compare to `GitignoreCache.isIgnored`. Report the minimal failing pattern set on mismatch (print seed + patterns + path). Known intentional divergences go into an explicit allow-list with a reason (e.g. core.excludesFile - jj-idea-k5vy, case-insensitive FS), so a new mismatch fails loudly.
Part 3 - wiring: run Part 2 in the contract task (`contractTest`; see jj-idea-blkg for running contractTest in CI), Part 1 in the default `test` task.
Decisions made without the user: Q: git as a test-time dependency OK? Rec yes (skip if absent). Reverse: keep only Part 1. Q: fix every divergence found? Rec: fix real semantic bugs as separate beads (created as discovered, tagged correctness) - this bead delivers the tests + allow-list, not unbounded fixes.
Scale: tests only; but add one operation-count assertion that `isIgnored` for a path of depth d consults O(d) `getNode` entries (no re-parse per call) to protect the cache's performance contract.
Manual: none. Related: jj-idea-aah2 (.gitignore colouring automation), jj-idea-k5vy (global excludes), jj-idea-s0ab.
acceptance_criteria: Golden table covering every listed gitignore rule passes; differential test vs real git (seeded, skipped without git) passes with documented allow-list; any real divergences filed as separate beads; depth-operation-count test.

title: Quiet-log unresolvable single-revision lookups (jj log -r <id>)
description: When a user types a revision that doesn't exist (e.g. in the new arbitrary-revision revision-selector fallback), CliExecutor logged a WARN-level 'jj log -r <id> failed' line, which is misleading since this is an expected user-facing outcome, not a plugin bug. Threaded a quiet: Boolean param through CommandExecutor.log -> LogService.getLog -> CliLogService.getLog -> CliExecutor.execute(warnOnFailure), set true only from LogCache.fetchOne (the single-revision resolution path used by the revision-selector free-form fallback). Other failures (the full log/window loads) remain at WARN.
close_reason: Implemented: quiet param threaded CommandExecutor.log -> LogService.getLog -> CliLogService.getLog -> CliExecutor.execute(warnOnFailure=!quiet); LogCache.fetchOne now resolves with quiet=true so an unresolvable free-form revision logs at INFO not WARN. Updated StubCommandExecutor and RepoLogCacheTest mockk stubs to match new signature. ./gradlew check passes.

title: Contract tests: run full logTemplates specs against jj CLI
description: The jj-idea-ndmn fix introduced a malformed bookmark template spec (nested if-in-if via booleanField wrapping) that passed all tests but crashed at runtime against the real jj CLI. Root cause: no test runs the compiled LogTemplates specs against a real jj process. Unit tests parse pre-canned strings; LogServiceIntegrationTest and BookmarkContractTest use JjStub (no jj syntax validation); LogContractTest/BookmarkContractTest hand-roll their specs from individual LogFields rather than using the combined LogTemplates .spec strings directly. Add a TemplateSpecContractTest (abstract + Cli + Stub variants) that exercises the actual .spec strings from CliLogService(executor).logTemplates: bookmarkListTemplate.spec via jj bookmark list -T; tagListTemplate.spec via jj tag list -T; basicLogTemplate.spec and fullLogTemplate.spec via jj log -r @ --no-graph -T. For each: verify result.isSuccess (catches jj syntax errors) and field-count (catches field-count drift). Tests must use the logTemplates instance, not hand-rolled specs, so any future template change is automatically validated against the real jj CLI.
design:
PLAN: `TemplateSpecContractTest` (abstract + Cli + Stub variants, matching the repo's contract-test triple convention in src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/contract/: e.g. LogContractTest.kt / LogContractCliTest.kt / LogContractStubTest.kt; the Cli variants need the real jj via the existing `RequiresJj` mechanism and run in `contractTest`, excluded from `check`; see jj-idea-blkg for CI).
Facts: the specs live in `CliLogService.LogTemplates` (jj/cli/CliLogService.kt:405 `inner class LogTemplates : LogFields()`; instance `val logTemplates = LogTemplates()` at :59) with members used by the service: `fullLogTemplate`, `fullLogTemplateWithoutPushedAncestor`, `basicLogTemplate`, `basicLogTemplateWithoutPushedAncestor`, `fileStatusesFor(filePath, base)`, `changeIdOnlyTemplate`, plus bookmark/tag list templates (`bookmarkListTemplate`, `tagListTemplate` - referenced in the bead; grep the class for the exact names and enumerate ALL `LogTemplate<T>` members reflectively so new templates are covered automatically instead of the bead's fixed list of four). Each LogTemplate carries `.spec` (the jj template string) and a field count/record size used by `parse()` (CliLogService.parse drops trailing empty element; `recordSize`).
Design:
1. Abstract `TemplateSpecContractTest` with an `abstract val executor: CommandExecutor` (+ repo fixture, as in LogContractTest) and one test per template family:
   - bookmarks: `jj bookmark list -a -T <bookmarkListTemplate.spec>` (create 2 bookmarks, one remote-tracking via a bare local remote fixture so remote/tracking fields are exercised; include a divergent/conflicted bookmark if the fixture helper exists);
   - tags: `jj tag list -T <tagListTemplate.spec>`;
   - log: `jj log -r @ --no-graph -T <fullLogTemplate.spec>` and the WithoutPushedAncestor variant, `basicLogTemplate`, `changeIdOnlyTemplate`, `fileStatusesFor(path, fullLogTemplate)`;
   For each: assert `result.isSuccess` (catches jj template syntax errors - the original failure mode of jj-idea-ndmn: nested if-in-if via booleanField wrapping passed unit tests but crashed on real jj) AND split the stdout on the NUL field separator and assert `fields.size == template.recordSize (+ the trailing empty element)` (catches field-count drift), AND parse via the production parser (`logService.getLog(...)` using the same templates through the real executor) returning a non-empty list with expected values for the fixture (e.g. change id non-empty, bookmark names). The test must obtain specs from `CliLogService(executor).logTemplates`, never hand-rolled strings (the bead's key requirement).
2. Version matrix: run under the min and current jj (contributing.md "Testing against multiple jj versions": `JJ_EXECUTABLE`/settings path to jj-0.37); the WithoutPushedAncestor fallback templates exist precisely for old jj - assert the PRIMARY template either succeeds or fails with the specific unsupported-keyword error the fallback logic expects (so the fallback path is verified, not silently relied on): test `getLog` end-to-end instead of raw spec for those two.
3. Stub variant: `JjStub`-backed executor cannot validate syntax; the Stub variant only checks that the field-count math of `.spec` equals `recordSize` (static consistency) - cheap and runs in default `test`.
4. Drift guard: reflective enumeration (`LogTemplates::class.memberProperties` of type LogTemplate<*>) asserting every property is exercised by at least one test (maintain a covered-set; fail if a new template property isn't registered) - this is the "automatically validated" acceptance.
Decisions made without the user: Q: reflective coverage guard? Rec yes (otherwise the bead's failure mode recurs when someone adds a 5th template). Q: also validate op-log template (`OP_LOG_TEMPLATE`, jj/cli/OpLogParser.kt)? Rec yes - add as a template spec case (same failure mode); it is a plain string const so just add a test.
Scale: tests only; each Cli test = a handful of jj calls on a tiny fixture.
Testing: this IS the test; verify it fails when a spec is deliberately broken (temporarily inject a syntax error / extra field in a local run and confirm the red result, record in PR description). CI: runs in `contractTest` (see jj-idea-blkg to wire into GitHub Actions). Manual: none.
acceptance_criteria: TemplateSpecContractTest (abstract+Cli+Stub) runs every LogTemplates spec (and OP_LOG_TEMPLATE) against real jj verifying success + field count + production parse; reflective guard fails on unregistered new templates; verified red on injected template error.

title: Migrate repositoryStateAlarm to MergingUpdateQueue
description:
We standardised on MergingUpdateQueue for debounced UI/state refresh in UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel (jj-idea-7jn1). The remaining Alarm usage should follow suit for consistency.

Location: JujutsuStateModel.kt:216 — 'repositoryStateAlarm' (Alarm POOLED_THREAD), used by scheduleRepositoryRefresh() (lines ~230-237) to debounce references.invalidate() + workingCopies.invalidate() + logRefresh.notify() by 300ms.

Migration: replace the Alarm with a MergingUpdateQueue parented to the state model (Disposable), queueing a single identity Update ('repoRefresh').

THREADING CAVEAT: the current Alarm uses ThreadToUse.POOLED_THREAD, whereas MergingUpdateQueue flushes on the EDT by default. The queued work (references/workingCopies.invalidate) already hops to pooled threads internally via NotifiableState, so EDT dispatch is likely fine — but verify nothing in scheduleRepositoryRefresh blocks the EDT. If background execution is required, construct the queue with the POOLED_THREAD variant / setExecuteInDispatchThread(false).

Acceptance: no remaining 'com.intellij.util.Alarm' imports in src/main; ./gradlew check passes; debounced repository refresh still coalesces rapid file-save bursts (manual smoke with stress-test repo).
design:
PLAN: replace `repositoryStateAlarm` with a `MergingUpdateQueue`, matching jj-idea-7jn1's standard; keep it a small, behaviour-preserving change and correct the bead's acceptance wording.
Facts: `private val repositoryStateAlarm = Alarm(Alarm.ThreadToUse.POOLED_THREAD, this)` (jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt:335) used only by `scheduleRepositoryRefresh()` (:380-385: `cancelAllRequests(); addRequest({ invalidateRepositoryState(); logRefresh.notify(Unit) }, 300)`), called from the VFS BulkFileListener (:~485), `resumeRefresh()` (:343-347) and elsewhere in the file. The bead's location (:216) and `references.invalidate()+workingCopies.invalidate()+logRefresh` description are stale: the callee is now `invalidateRepositoryState()` (:352-359 invalidates references/workingCopies/closestBookmarks/danglingHeads). Precedent: UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel's `MergingUpdateQueue` (`rebuildQueue`/`scheduleReloadChanges`, jj-idea-7jn1) and JujutsuTrackedFilesService's (`MergingUpdateQueue("jjTrackedFiles", 300, true, null, this, null, false)`, vcs/ignore/JujutsuTrackedFilesService.kt:~52: `executeInDispatchThread = false` = pooled thread - the exact variant needed here).
Design:
1. `private val repositoryRefreshQueue = MergingUpdateQueue("jjRepositoryRefresh", 300, true, null, this, null, false)` (last arg false = NOT in dispatch thread, keeping today's pooled-thread execution; `isActive = true`); `scheduleRepositoryRefresh() = repositoryRefreshQueue.queue(Update.create("repoRefresh") { invalidateRepositoryState(); logRefresh.notify(Unit) })` - the identity "repoRefresh" coalesces repeated queues within the 300ms window (MergingUpdateQueue merges same-identity Updates keeping the LATEST, equivalent to cancelAll+add), timing semantic difference: Alarm restarts the delay on each request (pure trailing debounce), MergingUpdateQueue's merging time is a FIXED window from the first queued item (flush occurs 300ms after the first queue(), not after the last): a continuous burst of file events (e.g. a long checkout) will flush every 300ms instead of waiting for quiet. Consequence: more refreshes during a long burst (each is O(state) jj calls). Mitigation: use `queue.restartTimer()`-style: `MergingUpdateQueue` has `queue(update)` + `setRestartTimerOnAdd(true)` constructor/flag (`restartTimerOnAdd`): set it true to retain trailing-debounce behaviour exactly. Verify the constructor/flag in intellij-community (MergingUpdateQueue(name, mergingTimeSpan, isActive, modalityStateComponent, parent, activationComponent, executeInDispatchThread) + `setRestartTimerOnAdd(boolean)`).
2. Dispose: parented to `this` (the state model is Disposable) - no manual cancel needed.
3. Callers: `resumeRefresh()` and the listener keep calling `scheduleRepositoryRefresh()` unchanged.
4. Acceptance correction: "no remaining com.intellij.util.Alarm imports in src/main" is NOT achievable cheaply: three other files use Alarm for per-editor debounce - ui/editor/JujutsuConflictEditorNotificationProvider.kt:19,106 (`Alarm(POOLED_THREAD, fileEditor)`), ui/editor/conflict/JujutsuConflictGutterInstaller.kt:24,185, and ui/editor/DebouncedDocumentScan.kt:3,29 (an abstraction taking an Alarm). Those are per-editor/Disposable-bound documents debouncers where Alarm is the idiomatic tool (MergingUpdateQueue per editor is heavier). Rec: scope this bead to JujutsuStateModel (the shared-state, process-wide one) and reword the acceptance to "JujutsuStateModel no longer uses Alarm"; leave the editor ones (note why in contributing.md's threading section).
Decisions made without the user: Q: restartTimerOnAdd=true to preserve trailing-debounce? Rec yes. Q: migrate editor Alarms? Rec no.
Scale: unchanged. Testing: unit/platform test of burst coalescing: N rapid `scheduleRepositoryRefresh()` calls within the window -> exactly one `invalidateRepositoryState` (use a test seam for the queue or drive via `flush()`); trailing-debounce test: calls spaced < 300ms keep postponing (with restartTimerOnAdd) - verify with a fake clock if feasible, else platform test with real short window; no EDT blocking (assert the Update runs off EDT). Manual: MT-LOG-REFRESH (stress repo: touch many files / checkout; log refreshes once after quiet). Regression scope: MT-LOG-REFRESH, MT-WORKINGCOPY.
acceptance_criteria: JujutsuStateModel uses a MergingUpdateQueue (pooled thread, restart-on-add) instead of Alarm with unchanged debounce semantics; editor Alarms explicitly left; burst-coalescing tests; MT-LOG-REFRESH smoke.

title: Per-window log expansion caching can interfere between tabs
description: When two log windows show the same repository, calling loadExpanding or clearNavigation writes to the shared repo.logCache. If both windows are expanding different commits concurrently the cache state can be inconsistent for one window. Acceptable for v1 but should be revisited if users report unexpected log truncation when multiple tabs are open.
design:
PLAN: characterise first - the premise of this bead has partly dissolved with later refactors; produce a test, then either close or apply a small fix.
Current code facts: expansion state is NOT in the shared cache any more: each `UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader` instance (one per log window/tab) keeps its own `expansionEntriesByRepo` (ui/log/UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:~291-302) and merges it into ITS snapshot (`mergeAndNotify`, mergeLock-protected, jj-idea-jnqi). `loadExpanding` calls `repo.logCache.loadContext(changeId, window)` (jj/LogCache.kt, `RepoLogCache`: ConcurrentHashMap `store`/`byCommitId`/`byBookmark` + a synchronized `orderedIds`), which STORES entries as a side effect - additive/idempotent. `clearNavigation()` is per-window UI state. The remaining shared mutation points: `repo.logCache.store(allEntries)` after each full load (UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:192), `reload()` (evict + refetch, :226) and `clear()` (any VCS op; also on VCS_CONFIGURATION_CHANGED). The cache feeds the PICKERS (RevisionChoicePanel, CommitPickerPanel `logCache.all`), `getLogEntry`, and status-bar switcher - not the log table rows of other windows.
Possible real interference to test: window A `refresh()` -> `reload()` evicts everything; window B's expansion entries (stored earlier in the shared cache by `loadContext`) disappear from `logCache.all` until B re-expands; pickers then show fewer commits than B's table (cosmetic). Also `all` mixes entries from A's and B's different `logRevset` windows? `RepoLogCache.all` uses the PROJECT/repo setting `logRevset(repo)`/limit - not per-window config - so a window with a custom revset (LogWindowConfig revset?) stores entries outside that revset into the shared cache; `snapshot()` returns whatever was stored last => picker contents depend on which window loaded last. THAT is the plausible "unexpected truncation" mechanism.
Plan:
1. Characterisation tests (unit, with stub log service): two loaders sharing one repo (fake `LogCache` implementation or the real RepoLogCache over a stub LogService): (a) A expands X, B refreshes: assert B's table snapshot still contains X? (B never had X - expected); assert A's snapshot unaffected by B's refresh; assert pickers' `all` after interleavings; (b) concurrent `loadExpanding` from both windows to different commits (CountDownLatch) -> both tables get their own expansion and no exception, store consistent (no lost entries: after both complete, cache contains both expansions unless a reload ran in between).
2. If (a)/(b) show no table-level interference (expected): CLOSE the bead with the finding + keep the tests as regression guards; document in LogCache KDoc that the cache is shared best-effort and that table state is per window.
3. If the picker-contents-by-last-writer issue is judged worth fixing (decision below): make the cache additive-by-key and let `all` be computed from the union of stored entries ordered topologically (instead of "snapshot of last store") - needs care: stale entries (abandoned commits) must be evicted on `reload()`/`clear()`, which already happens globally; or key stores by window id. Rec: do NOT change semantics unless a user report exists (the bead itself says "acceptable for v1 ... revisit if users report").
Decisions made without the user: Q: fix or close? Rec: add tests, close as "no table-level interference; cosmetic picker staleness documented" unless the tests fail. Reverse: reopen with the failing scenario.
Scale: none. Manual: MT-LOG-TABLE (two log tabs on the same repo; expand different commits; refresh one; the other keeps its expansion) - 1 row. Regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-REFRESH.
acceptance_criteria: Two-window interleaving tests exist and pass; bead closed with documented finding or a minimal fix if a table-level interference is demonstrated.

title: Paint repo menus coloured with icons
description:
For a multi-repo project, the bookmark drop-down in the log window first shows a menu of repos. In here, colour each rep
o and precede with its repo icon, matching the repo colour used elsewhere in the plugin.

Also do this in the drop-down of repos in the working copy pane.

Identify other areas of the plugin where we have lists of repos and consider the same treatment there too.
design:
PLAN: apply the repo icon + repo colour treatment wherever the plugin lists repos (the bead asks to "identify other areas"). One shared helper for combo/list renderers; popup menus already done.
Existing building blocks: `RepositoryIcons[repo]` (ui/common/RepositoryIcons.kt: path-keyed, repo-coloured `JujutsuIcons.Repo` via `RepositoryColors.getColor(repo)`, ui/log/RepositoryColors.kt) - already used by: bookmark menu repo submenus (actions/bookmark/BookmarkMenu.kt:55 `templatePresentation.icon = RepositoryIcons[repo]` - so the log toolbar bookmark dropdown's repo menu ALREADY has the icon; verify it shows in the real popup and decide whether the TEXT should be coloured: action menu item text can't be coloured through the Presentation API - icon colour is the identity cue, acceptable), the bookmarks panel (RepoGroup node icon), root filter component (JujutsuRootFilterComponent.kt:117 colour), changes tree repo nodes (JujutsuOtherRepositoriesNode etc.), file path icon provider.
Inventory of repo lists still without icon/colour (grep): 
 1. Working Copy panel repo selector: `WorkingCopyControlsPanel.repoSelector` (ui/workingcopy/WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt:67-77) - `JComboBox<RepoItem>` with a `DefaultListCellRenderer` setting only `text = displayName`.
 2. Fetch dialog repo combo (actions/git/GitFetchDialog.kt:~93 `comboBox(items)` with `SimpleListCellRenderer.create("") { it.displayName }`), Push dialog repo selector (actions/git/GitPushDialog.kt - find its repo combo), other dialogs with a repo picker (NewChange? Rebase? Split? only multi-root pickers: grep `displayName` in combo renderers: Settings per-repo override groups (settings/JujutsuConfigurable.kt per-repo `collapsibleGroup` titles)).
 3. Status bar widgets/popups: `JujutsuStatusBarWidget`/`JujutsuWorkingCopySwitcher` (repo shown in header text), `JujutsuBookmarkStatusBarWidget`, toolbar widget (ui/toolbar/JujutsuBookmarkToolbarWidget.kt).
 4. Log table root gutter (JujutsuRootGutterRenderer - already coloured), details pane repo line (`append(entry.repo)` in LogEntryText.kt:~433 - check whether `appendRepo` renders icon+colour; LogEntryText imports RepositoryIcons/Colors so likely done).
 5. Notifications (balloons name repos in plain text - leave).
Design: shared `RepoListCellRenderer` (ui/common/): `SimpleListCellRenderer` (or `ColoredListCellRenderer`) setting `icon = RepositoryIcons[repo]` and a coloured text attribute `SimpleTextAttributes(STYLE_PLAIN, RepositoryColors.getColor(repo))` only in the NON-selected state (selected rows keep the selection foreground for contrast - same rule the platform uses); use it for sites 1 and 2 (+ other dialog combos found by the inventory). For `Presentation`-based menus keep icons only (documented limitation). Settings per-repo group titles: icon via `collapsibleGroup(title).icon?` not supported - skip.
Decisions made without the user: Q: colour the text or only the icon? Rec: text colour in combo/list renderers (cheap, matches the bead "colour each repo ... matching the repo colour used elsewhere"), icon-only in action menus. Q: scope = sites 1-2 now, others on request? Rec yes.
Scale: renderer O(1) per painted item; `RepositoryIcons` caches by path. Testing: renderer unit test (icon non-null and text colour = RepositoryColors for unselected; selection foreground when selected); platform test for WorkingCopyControlsPanel selector using the renderer; manual: MT-WORKINGCOPY (multi-root: repo dropdown shows coloured icons matching the log's root gutter colours), MT-GIT (fetch/push dialogs), MT-CTXMENU/MT-BOOKMARK (bookmark dropdown repo menu icons). Regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-GIT, MT-BOOKMARK.
acceptance_criteria: Working Copy repo selector and Fetch/Push (and other found multi-repo pickers) show repo icon + colour via a shared renderer; menus keep icons; inventory recorded; tests + MT rows.

title: Log row tooltip for many-bookmark commit only reachable by hovering graph column
description: When a commit has many bookmarks, the only way to trigger the tooltip showing all bookmarks is to hover over the graph glyph column. Hovering over the description or decoration column area does not trigger the tooltip. This makes the full bookmark list effectively hidden. Fix: ensure the tooltip is accessible from anywhere on the row, not just the graph area.
close_reason: Stale: filed 2026-06-06 when graph and description were separate table columns. They are now one merged COLUMN_GRAPH_AND_DESCRIPTION, and JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.kt sets toolTipText on the whole cell panel (description and decoration area included), so hovering anywhere in that column shows the full row tooltip. Verified by reading the renderer; no code change needed.

title: Graph shows unlinked passthrough lines when log limit cuts off commits
description: When Log Limit cuts off commits (e.g. limit=100 on stress-test repo), some passthrough lane lines appear disconnected — floating lines with no visible parent or child commit in the visible range. Root cause: graph layout assumes parent rows are always present; when a parent is beyond the limit, its lane slot persists as a passthrough without a termination glyph or clear visual anchor. Steps to reproduce: open stress-test repo, set limit=100, observe graph near rows 80-100 where branches diverge from ancestors outside the visible window.
notes: jj-idea-2c8k (paged log loading, GitHub #69) shipped a minimal stub covering the all-parents-elided sub-case of this bug (JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.shouldDrawElidedStub - wiggly Path2D line). That wiggle is wrong for this bead's case: a paged-window-boundary parent isn't elided, it simply hasn't loaded yet, and the wiggle wrongly implies deliberate elision (jj's own ~ semantics). Fix: replace RowLayout.hasElidedParents (Boolean) with a per-parent NOT_LOADED/HIDDEN classification; NOT_LOADED gets a faded straight stub, HIDDEN keeps the wiggle. Ships in the SAME session as jj-idea-1pgy (mixed-merge lane offset) and jj-idea-sc8m (long-edge hover/click navigation) - all three touch the same per-parent state and renderer function. Full design, including why a fetch-extended nearest-ancestor remap was rejected (lane-leak risk connecting to a distant ancestor): docs/design/jj-idea-hlu3-xi58-elided-ancestor-rendering.md. Entry point for the whole follow-up set: jj-idea-4kfh (epic).
close_reason: Shipped: RowLayout/GraphNode gained per-parent NOT_LOADED/HIDDEN classification (ParentState), LayoutCalculator.calculate takes allIds to distinguish them, CommitGraphBuilder.buildGraph gained the (visible, allEntries) overload, renderer paints a faded straight stub for NOT_LOADED vs the existing wiggle for HIDDEN. Tests + CHANGELOG + manual-tests.md updated.

title: Contract test: jj status C (copied file) output format
description: StatusContractTest.kt has no coverage for the C (copy) status letter from jj status. Need a test that creates a copy by duplicating file content (jj detects copies by content hash, not a dedicated command), then asserts the 'C prefix{old => new}suffix' output format. Important: the C letter is jj's behavior, and a contract test guards against upstream format changes. See jj-idea-0y24 for context.
design:
PLAN: contract test pinning jj's copy ('C') output in `jj status`/`jj diff --summary`/log templates, per the bead - with the real trigger condition discovered by probing jj 0.44.
Probe results (real jj 0.44.0, scratch repos):
 - A plain copy of an UNMODIFIED file is reported as an add: `cp a.txt b.txt` -> `A b.txt` (no copy detection) - so the bead's "duplicate file content" recipe alone does NOT produce `C`.
 - Copy detection fires when the copy SOURCE is also modified in the same change: with `a.txt` edited (`echo more >> a.txt`) and `cp a.txt dir/a2.txt` -> `jj st` prints `M a.txt` + `C {a.txt => dir/a2.txt}` (also for a copy made in an earlier commit: `jj diff -r @- --summary` -> `M a.txt` / `C {a_copy.txt => ...}`; template: `jj log -T 'diff.files().map(|f| f.status())'` -> `modified,copied`, i.e. the template status string is "copied" - the mapping `fileChangeStatusFor` (jj/cli/CliLogService.kt:469-478) currently has no "copied" case => `UNKNOWN`; see jj-idea-flb0).
 - Rename with spaces: `R {a_copy.txt => dir/with space.txt}`; copy within a shared directory prefix prints `C dir/{x.txt => y.txt}` (the `prefix{old => new}suffix` shape the bead cites; confirm with a fixture: files `dir/x.txt`, `dir/y.txt`).
Test design: add to the existing contract triple (src/test/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/contract/: abstract `StatusContractTest` + `StatusContractCliTest` (@Tag("contract") @RequiresJj, backend `JjCli(tempDir)`) + `StatusContractStubTest`): new cases in the ABSTRACT class so Stub and Cli both run:
 1. `copy of a modified file shows C with braces format`: fixture: commit base with a.txt (>=8 distinct lines so similarity is high), then modify a.txt, copy to dir/a2.txt, run `status`; assert lines contain `M a.txt` and a line matching `^C \{a\.txt => dir/a2\.txt\}$` and that `parseRenameSpec` (jj/FileSpec.kt:5) of that spec returns (`a.txt`, `dir/a2.txt`).
 2. `copy sharing a directory prefix`: `dir/x.txt` modified + `dir/y.txt` copy -> `C dir/{x.txt => y.txt}`; assert regex and parse result (old `dir/x.txt`, new `dir/y.txt`).
 3. `copy of an unmodified file is reported as added` (documents jj's current behaviour, guards the assumption the plugin makes - and fails loudly if a future jj starts detecting it).
 4. Template statuses: `jj log -r @ -T 'diff.files().map(|f| f.status())'` includes `copied` (guards CliLogService.fileChangeStatusFor's string set).
 5. Stub backend: the Stub variant returns canned status text (see how added/modified cases are stubbed in StatusContractStubTest/JjStub) - add the same canned `C {..}` lines so the abstract assertions hold for both.
 Version coverage: run under the MINIMUM jj (0.37) as well (contributing.md multi-version setup, `scripts/jj-install-version.sh 0.37.0` + JJ path setting): copy detection in `jj status` may not exist at 0.37 (introduced later?) - if absent, cases 1-2 and 4 must be guarded with a version assumption (`Assumptions.assumeTrue(jjVersion >= X)`, X found by probing 0.37/0.39) and the plugin's `'C'` handling documented as "newer jj only".
Decisions made without the user: Q: guard behaviour with Assumptions per version? Rec yes. Q: fix the missing "copied" template mapping here? Rec: no - that's jj-idea-flb0's scope; this bead is test-only (but note the finding in flb0: add "copied" -> COPIED there).
Scale: tests only. Manual: none. Related: jj-idea-flb0 (model), jj-idea-i2e2 (rename following), JujutsuChangeProvider.addCopiedChange (vcs/changes/JujutsuChangeProvider.kt:~254).
acceptance_criteria: Contract tests (abstract + Cli + Stub) pin C output with braces and shared-prefix forms, document that unmodified-source copies are reported as A, and cover the 'copied' template status; version-guarded.

title: FileChange.Copied: first-class copy variant in data model
description: Currently, copied files (jj status 'C' lines) are rendered as renames (FileChange.Renamed / FileStatus.MODIFIED+isReplaced). This is a known semantic compromise from jj-idea-0y24. A proper fix: add Status.COPIED enum value and FileChange.Copied data class in FileChange.kt, then update consumers: ChangeService, FileRevision, log diff renderers, and the string→Status mapping in CliLogService (~line 309). Bead jj-idea-0y24 notes this is deferred.
design:
PLAN: model copies explicitly: `FileChange.Status.COPIED` + `FileChange.Copied(before, after)`, and thread it through the few consumers; platform-facing code keeps representing copies as `Change` with `isIsReplaced = true` because the platform has no copy status.
Facts: today 'C' status lines are mapped to `Renamed` in two places: jj/cli/CliLogService.kt:232-247 (`'R', 'C' ->` builds `FileChange.Renamed(old, new)`; the only difference is a log line) and vcs/changes/JujutsuChangeProvider.kt:210-270 (`'C' -> addCopiedChange` creates a `Change(before, CurrentContentRevision(after), FileStatus.MODIFIED)` with `isIsReplaced = true`). Status enum: jj/FileChange.kt:15 `MODIFIED, ADDED, DELETED, RENAMED, UNKNOWN`; consumers of Status: vcs/history/JujutsuFileRevision.kt:22,54 (`isDeleted`), jj/FileRevision.kt:3, CliLogService.kt:469-478 (`fileChangeStatusFor` template mapping: "added/modified/renamed/removed" -> `copied` is a jj template status string too - verify with `jj log -T 'diff.files().map(|f| f.status())'` that jj reports "copied" for copies), `FileChange.from(change)` (:~82: a `Change` with before.file != after.file => Renamed - a copy-as-replaced Change currently round-trips to Renamed).
Probe finding (jj 0.44, see jj-idea-pcp8): `C` only appears when the copy SOURCE is also modified in the same change (an unmodified source copied is reported as `A`), and the log template status string for copies is "copied" (CliLogService.fileChangeStatusFor currently maps unknown strings to UNKNOWN - add the case). This makes real-world copies less frequent than assumed; supports the 'low priority' recommendation below.
Semantic differences that matter (why it is worth modelling): for a COPY the source file STILL EXISTS after the change; code that treats it as a rename wrongly (a) restores/undoes by deleting the new file and recreating the old path (`allPaths` includes both - fine for restore, but "rollback of a rename" would re-create the old file that was never removed - harmless; yet squash/split/hunk logic that treats `before` as deleted would DROP the source file: jj-idea-5g8h/qel6 `buildHunkSelection`'s `isDeletion = afterRevision == null` is based on the platform Change's after==null, unaffected), (b) UI labels ("renamed from X" vs "copied from X"), (c) `RestoreDialog` effects (jj-idea-i40p design: copy's restore = DELETE the new file, NOT move back).
Design:
1. Model: `Status.COPIED`; `data class Copied(before: FileAtVersion, after: FileAtVersion) : FileChange` (`require(before.filePath != after.filePath)`); `allPaths` = both (source untouched by a restore... NOTE: for restore, only the AFTER path must be addressed - override `allPaths`? The documented contract is "every path this change touches ... use when an operation must address all sides (restore)". A restore of a copy must not touch the source; so `Copied.allPaths = listOf(after.filePath)`; KDoc it.)
2. Parsing: CliLogService.kt:232: split 'R' and 'C' branches (`'C' -> FileChange.Copied(...)`); template mapping :475: "copied" -> COPIED; `FileChange.from(change)`: detect `change.isIsReplaced && before.file != after.file` => Copied (the platform marker we set in addCopiedChange; plain renames are produced by the platform with `isRenamed` - actually renames in addRenamedChange: check whether it also sets `isIsReplaced` (:~250 shows rename path sets `change.isIsReplaced = true` too!). Verify: if both set it, `from()` can't distinguish; then record the copy marker differently: custom `ContentRevision` subclass for the copy's before-revision or a `Change` user-data key `JujutsuDataKeys.COPY_SOURCE` set in addCopiedChange and read in `from()`.)
3. Consumers: JujutsuFileRevision/FileRevision (no change besides exhaustive `when`s), diff/tree renderers: labels via bundle (`change.copied.from`), file-history copy tracking (jj-idea-i2e2 rename detection can follow).
4. Contract test (open bead jj-idea-pcp8 "Contract test: jj status C (copied file) output format") must land first or together: pins the 'C' line format (`C {old => new}` / `C path/{a => b}`) per version.
Decisions made without the user: Q: do it now? Rec: low priority; do together with i2e2 (file history rename/copy detection) or when a user-visible bug (restore/squash of a copied file) appears; the representation compromise is documented and currently harmless. Reverse: close as won't-do and keep the documented compromise.
Scale: none. Testing: parser tests ('R' vs 'C' both formats incl. braces), `FileChange.from` round trip for copy/rename, exhaustive `when` compile checks, restore effects test for a copy (after only). Manual: MT-WORKINGCOPY / MT-LOG-DETAILS (copied file shows as copied; restore deletes the new file, keeps source). Regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-LOG-DETAILS, MT-DIFF.
acceptance_criteria: FileChange.Copied/Status.COPIED parsed from 'C' lines and templates; restore of a copy touches only the new path; renamed vs copied distinguishable end to end; contract test for 'C' format exists; tests pass.

Aligned the two UIs by rewriting the switcher to use CompareItem, CompareItemRenderer, and buildItemList from RevisionSelectorPopup.

title: Per-deletion checkbox exclusion in push dialog
description: Allow users to exclude specific pending bookmark deletions from a push. When a bookmark is deleted locally and tracked remotely, it appears in the push dialog's Pending Deletions section (added in f5l2). Unchecking a deletion should exclude it from the push command by switching to explicit --bookmark flags for everything except the excluded items. Requires: (1) restructure GitPushSpec.bookmark from Bookmark? to List<Bookmark>, (2) extend gitPush() executor signature to accept multiple --bookmark flags, (3) rework push dialog radio buttons to support per-deletion checkboxes alongside the existing scope selector.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bookmark chip visual design: tooltips, selection state, and shape options
description:
Bookmark chips in the log table and commit details panel are interactive (left-click navigates, right-click context menu) but have two UX gaps:

1. No per-bookmark tooltip — hovering a chip shows nothing (or the row tooltip). A useful tooltip would identify the specific bookmark and show its ahead/behind status relative to its remotes.

2. No obvious selected/hover state — the hand cursor hints at interactivity, but clicking a bookmark also selects the entire row, making it visually indistinguishable from a plain row click. There is no chip-level highlight.

This bead is a design exploration. Before implementing, we need guidance on the preferred look and feel. Options to evaluate:

**Option A — Inline chip with hover box**
Keep the current inline text rendering (icon + name + ↑↓ badge), but draw a light rounded rectangle behind the chip fragment(s) on hover, and a distinct filled/accent rectangle when 'selected' (last clicked). Tooltip shows name + ahead/behind counts vs each remote.

**Option B — Bookmark-shape graphic beside the row**
Render each bookmark as a small bookmark-flag-shaped component (like a dog-eared page corner) positioned in the left gutter or inline. The flag shape itself is the click target: it highlights on hover, shows a filled/accent color when selected, and has a popover tooltip. The change description continues uninterrupted to the right. This approach makes bookmarks first-class visual objects rather than inline text annotations.

**Option C — Tag/pill chip**
Render each bookmark as a rounded pill (like GitHub/GitLab branch labels): a small colored background, icon, and name. On hover the pill darkens; on 'selected' (i.e., the row the bookmark resolves to is focused) it gets a border. Tooltip on the pill.

**Option D — Status-bar style indicator**
Keep inline text but add a thin underline or left-border accent on the chip when hovered, matching the IDE's existing hyperlink convention. Tooltip shows ahead/behind detail.

Human guidance needed: which shape/style best fits IDEA's VCS log aesthetic and jj-idea's design language? Are there constraints (e.g., icon availability, Swing renderer limitations) that rule out any option?
design:
PLAN (pass-2 / needs-your-review - the bead is a design exploration awaiting your taste call): recommend Option A (inline chip with hover box) because most of it is already built, with the two gaps closed.
What exists now (code facts): chips are inline text fragments (`LaidOutCell` ui/log/LaidOutCell.kt via `cappedDecorations`, ui/log/JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt:128-210), each chip resolves to a `LogClickTarget` (`BookmarkClick`/`TagClick`/`MoreRefsClick`/`WorkingCopyClick`, ui/log/LogClickTarget.kt:101-142) and `LogClickTarget.hoverCue` returns `HoverCue.REF_BACKGROUND` for them (LogClickTarget.kt:181-186): the renderer paints a hover background behind the chip under the pointer (jj-idea-a52h, `rightHighlightTarget` in JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.configureTextPanel :230). So Option A's hover half EXISTS (bead jj-idea-zhyy "implement the chosen hover highlight" is therefore largely already done; its remaining defect is kba2: the hover background doesn't update on horizontal movement within a row). The tooltip gap: there is a per-NODE tooltip in the bookmarks panel (ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkNodeTooltip.kt: group identity, remote in-sync/force-push notes, ahead/behind) but no per-CHIP tooltip in the log table: the table's tooltip is the generic row tooltip (`installIconAwareTableTooltip`, JujutsuLogTable.kt:265-275).
Recommendation by option: A = keep (consistent with IntelliJ's own hyperlink/inline-chip conventions and zero new layout machinery; B (flag graphic in a gutter) and C (pill with filled background) both change row text layout/measure (LaidOutCell caps chips by width; pills add padding/arc painting per chip per row per repaint - cf. perf bead jj-idea-g7to) and D (underline/left border) conflicts with the "underline = real link" convention used for issue links (`HoverCue.ISSUE_LINK_UNDERLINE`). If you want a stronger visual identity later, C can be layered as a paint-only change in the same fragment painter without altering hit-testing.
Concrete work to close the bead:
1. Chip tooltip (gap 1): when the pointer is over a bookmark/tag chip show a tooltip for THAT chip: name, kind (local/remote/tag), tracked remotes with ahead/behind (reuse `bookmarkNodeTooltip` builder: it needs the Bookmark + group data (`BookmarkGroup`/remote rows); from the log the entry carries `bookmarks: List<Bookmark>` incl. remote rows and ahead/behind fields (jj/Revset.kt:44-63) so build the same HTML from them - factor `bookmarkNodeTooltip` core into a shared function taking `(bookmark, remoteBookmarks)`), shown via the existing `installIconAwareTableTooltip` hook by extending its `extraKeyAt`/provider with `clickTargetAt(point)` (the long-edge tooltip at JujutsuLogTable.kt:272-274 is the precedent for position-dependent tooltips).
2. Selected state (gap 2): a chip is "selected" when it was the last-clicked chip AND its row is selected: store `selectedChip: (row, chipKey)?` in JujutsuLogTable, set from the click handler (LogClickTarget click on a chip already selects the row), cleared on selection change; paint with the accent colour border/background (reuse `JBUI.CurrentTheme.List.Selection`/focus ring colours; contrast-check in light/dark and for the row-selected background where the chip would otherwise vanish). 
3. Fix kba2 (separate bug bead, see its own design) so hover tracks horizontal movement.
Decisions made without the user: Q: choose A. Q: do B/C at all? Rec: no unless you want a visual redesign - say so and C becomes a new bead scoped to paint code + perf budget (pill painting must reuse cached `LaidOutCell`, see g7to).
Scale: tooltip: O(1) hit-test per tooltip request (`clickTargetAt` already computed per mouse move); selected-chip state O(1); no per-row work. Operation-count test: tooltip request performs no jj calls (data from LogEntry).
Testing: tooltip HTML tests (tracked/untracked/ahead/behind/conflict/deleted bookmark; tag; overflow chip -> no tooltip or list of hidden refs); selected-chip state tests (set on click, cleared on selection change); renderer paint test for the selected style. Manual: MT-BOOKMARK/MT-LOG-TABLE (hover each chip kind -> tooltip; click chip -> accent state; theme switch; chips clipped by width). Regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-DETAILS (details pane chips use AtomicHtmlView - keep out of scope unless trivial), MT-DND (chips are drag sources/drop targets: hover/selected painting must not interfere with drop highlight).
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded (Option A recommended); per-chip tooltip with ahead/behind; chip selected state; zhyy marked done/superseded; kba2 fixed separately; tests + MT rows.

title: Icons for different squash actions
description: The current squash icon is specific to squashing into the parent. Design icons that work for squash into and squash from.
design:
PLAN (pass-2 / icon design needs your eye): distinct, themeable icons for the three squash flavours using the existing icon pipeline; draft SVG specs and naming so the artwork can be produced and reviewed quickly.
Facts: icons are SVGs under src/main/resources/icons/ (squash.svg, split.svg, rebase.svg, newChange.svg, conflict.svg, ...; no expui/ variants required? there is an `expui` subfolder - check which icons have new-UI twins) loaded through `JujutsuIcons` (ui/common/JujutsuIcons.kt: `load("/icons/x.svg")` + recolour helpers `.accented(color)`, `fillIcon`, `strokeIcon`, `strokeFillIcon` at :51-76 for theme-aware colouring). Squash actions today: `Jujutsu.SquashChange`-style "Squash into Parent" uses `JujutsuIcons.Squash`; `SquashFilesAction`, `SquashIntoFilesAction` and the "Squash Into..." change action (actions/change/squashIntoAction.kt) reuse the same icon (SquashFilesAction.kt:`JujutsuIcons.Squash`), so the three semantics are visually identical in menus.
Semantics to distinguish (jj): (1) Squash into parent (`jj squash`): move a change's content DOWN into its parent - arrow pointing down/into a stacked block; (2) Squash into... (`jj squash --into X`, any destination): content moves to a chosen target - arrow into a block with a "target/pin"; (3) Squash from... (PickSources mode: pick sources INTO a fixed destination, `SquashMode.PickSources`) - multiple blocks converge to one - arrows converging.
Deliverables: `squashParent.svg` (keep today's squash.svg as this - least churn), `squashInto.svg` (down-arrow into a block with a small target ring), `squashFrom.svg` (two small blocks merging into one, converging arrows); 16x16 viewBox, 1px strokes, `currentColor`-friendly single colour (so `.accented` recolours per theme like Squash does), plus dark variants only if the loader requires them (check `fillIcon`'s mechanism: recolours via a colour-replacement SVG patcher => single-colour source suffices). Naming/loading: `JujutsuIcons.SquashInto`, `JujutsuIcons.SquashFrom`; wire: SquashIntoFilesAction + squashIntoAction (destination chosen) -> SquashInto; the PickSources-mode action(s) (find where `SquashMode.PickSources` is launched: log context action "Squash Into This..." for a destination) -> SquashFrom; `SquashFilesAction` (files into parent) keeps Squash.
Decisions made without the user: Q: who draws? Rec: I can author the three SVGs (simple geometric shapes) for your review; you adjust taste. Q: expui variants? Rec: only if the existing icons have them (`ls icons/expui`) - mirror that. Q: also differentiate Split/Rebase? No.
Scale: none. Testing: icon-load smoke test (each new resource resolves and renders non-1x1 per jj-idea-s01y's note: headless SvgIcon returns a 1x1 placeholder, so only assert the resource exists + parses as SVG via an XML parse); manual: MT-CTXMENU/MT-SQUASH menus in light/dark/new UI (icons visible, distinguishable at 16px and 200% zoom). Regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-SQUASH, MT-WORKINGCOPY (squash entries).
acceptance_criteria: Three distinguishable squash icons (parent/into/from) wired to the matching actions, theme-aware; resource-exists tests; visual review in light/dark.

title: Add to .gitignore / Remove from .gitignore actions
description: Implement right-click context menu actions to add or remove files from .gitignore. Requires implementing IgnoredFileContentProvider (JujutsuIgnoredFileContentProvider.kt) following git4idea's GitIgnoredFileContentProvider pattern. This is follow-up to jj-idea-ww5 which added the core .gitignore matching engine.
design:
PLAN: "Add to .gitignore" / "Remove from .gitignore" actions via the platform's ignore framework, not bespoke file editing.
Facts: the plugin has an IgnoredFileProvider (vcs/changes/JujutsuIgnoredFileProvider.kt) and a matching engine (vcs/ignore/GitignoreCache.kt, JujutsuIgnoreService.isIgnored :16-20) from jj-idea-ww5, but NO `IgnoredFileContentProvider` (grep: none). The platform's built-in "Add to .gitignore"-style action ("Ignore" in the VCS popup/Changes tree: `IgnoreFileActionGroup`, `IgnoredFileContentProvider` EP `com.intellij.vcs.ignoredFileContentProvider`) discovers VCS-specific ignore files through that EP, so implementing it makes the platform's own action group appear for jj with the right file and content - the bead's stated approach, following git4idea's GitIgnoredFileContentProvider (check ../intellij-community/plugins/git4idea/.../GitIgnoredFileContentProvider.kt).
Design:
1. `JujutsuIgnoredFileContentProvider : IgnoredFileContentProvider` in vcs/ignore/: `getSupportedVcs() = JujutsuVcs.getKey()`, `getFileName() = ".gitignore"` (jj reads .gitignore; there is no .jjignore), `buildIgnoreFileContent(ignoreFileRoot, ignoredFileProviders)` building the content from the platform's `IgnoredFileDescriptor`s (copy git4idea's mapping: path -> `/relative/path`, mask -> glob) while preserving existing file content (the platform passes existing content via `existingFileContent`?? check the interface at the pinned platform version; in 2025.1 it is `buildIgnoreFileContent(File ignoreFileRoot, IgnoredFileProvider[] providers)` plus `supportIgnoreFileNotInVcsRoot`), `supportIgnoreFileNotInVcsRoot() = true` only if needed for nested repos (jj-idea-plap) - default false.
2. Register in plugin.xml under `<extensions defaultExtensionNs="com.intellij">` : `<vcs.ignoredFileContentProvider implementation=...>` (verify EP name in intellij-community: `IgnoredFileContentProvider.IGNORE_FILE_CONTENT_PROVIDER`). Also add the standard ignored-file-generator wiring for `.gitignore` creation if the file doesn't exist (platform handles via `IgnoreFileActionGroup` / `IgnoredFileGeneratorImpl`).
3. Verify enablement interplay: the platform ignore actions call `VcsIgnoreManager.isPotentiallyIgnoredFile`/`ProjectLevelVcsManager` to decide availability - for a jj mapping they require our VCS to be registered for the file (it is) and `IgnoredFileProvider`s; after the platform writes `.gitignore`, jj snapshots it and the ignore cache must pick up the change: `GitignoreCache` is VFS-invalidated on .gitignore edits (confirm in the cache's listener; else call `JujutsuIgnoreService.invalidate(repo)`).
4. IMPORTANT jj semantics: ignoring a file that jj already TRACKS does not untrack it (docs/jj-track-untrack-model.md; Tracked toggle, jj-idea-i9ol closed). So after "Add to .gitignore" on a tracked file the plugin should offer/perform `jj file untrack` too (otherwise the file stays versioned and the action appears to do nothing); wrap: our registered action `Jujutsu.IgnoreAndUntrack`? Simplest: custom wrapper action group item "Ignore (and untrack)" that does platform ignore then `trackedFilesService` untrack for tracked paths via the existing TrackedToggleAction code path. Decision below.
5. "Remove from .gitignore": the platform has no remove action; implement our own `RemoveFromIgnoreAction` for ignored selections: finds the ignoring rule via GitignoreCache (needs "which rule matched" - extend the cache with `matchingRule(file): IgnoreRule(sourceFile, lineNumber, pattern)?`; if absent, add) and edits that .gitignore: delete the exact line when it matches the path pattern literally; if the match comes from a broader glob (`*.log`, `build/`) don't edit - show a message "Ignored by 'build/' in <file>:<line>; edit the file" with a link (open file at line). Global excludes (jj-idea-k5vy) not editable -> message.
Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Untrack on ignore for tracked files? Rec: yes, with the action text "Add to .gitignore and untrack" shown only when selected files are tracked (bounded check, see trackUntrackAvailability TRACKED_TOGGLE_SELECTION_LIMIT). Reverse: leave tracked state alone and show a note.
2. Q: Ship the platform action only (step 1-3) first, our Remove action second? Rec: two PRs.
3. Q: Support ignore file in subdirectory vs root? Rec: root of the repo by default (platform decides via `ignoreFileRoot`).
Scale: per-action O(selection) (bounded 100 as elsewhere); the rule lookup is a cache lookup. No traversal. Testing: provider content unit tests (existing content preserved, dedupe, directories get trailing slash, paths with spaces/#/! escaped); a platform test invoking the platform action API against a temp jj repo; RemoveFromIgnore: literal-line removal and glob-refusal tests. Manual: MT-IGNORE (right-click file -> Add to .gitignore -> file shows ignored colour, menu disables per jj-idea-otwq; Remove from .gitignore; tracked file path). Regression scope: MT-IGNORE, MT-CTXMENU, MT-WORKINGCOPY.
Related: jj-idea-otwq (enablement), jj-idea-k5vy (global excludes), jj-idea-aah2 (automated tests for .gitignore colouring).
acceptance_criteria: Platform 'Add to .gitignore' works for jj projects via IgnoredFileContentProvider; tracked files are also untracked (or clearly explained); 'Remove from .gitignore' edits literal rules and explains glob/global cases; ignore cache refreshes; tests + MT-IGNORE rows.

title: Local/current naming consistency
description: Sometimes we refer to the working copy file as local, sometimes current. Pick one name and make it consistent throughout the plugin.
design:
PLAN (pass-2 / naming decision): the plugin mixes "local", "current" and "working copy" for the same concept. Recommendation: standardise user-visible text on "Working Copy" (jj's own term, already the tool window title `toolwindow.title=Working copy` and used in most strings) and keep "local" only where it means the opposite of "remote" (local bookmarks, Local category in the bookmarks panel).
Inventory (grep of messages/JujutsuBundle.properties, plugin.xml, code):
 - Actions: `action.open.local.file=Open Local File` + description "Open the local working copy version of this file" (:211-212); `action.compare.with.local=Compare with Local` (+ "...with your local working copy", :213-214); `action.compare.before.with.local=Compare Before with Local` (:215-216); action ids `Jujutsu.CompareWithLocal`/`Jujutsu.CompareBeforeWithLocal` (plugin.xml:328-347) - these mirror IntelliJ platform wording ("Compare with Local" is the platform's standard label in Git/VCS menus for the working-tree version).
 - Diff labels: `diff.label.local=Local`, `diff.label.current=Current` (:352-353; `ContentLocator`/`WorkingCopy.title` = "Current", jj/Revset.kt:184) - the right-hand side title of a diff of the working copy shows "Current" in some places and "Local" in others.
 - Other "current": annotate description "Annotate the current file" (:37, = the open file, fine), "current working copy change (@)" (:244), restore warning "discards the current content" (:303 - ok), diffbase/upgrade strings (unrelated).
Recommendation:
 1. Diff side titles: pick ONE for the working-copy content: "Working Copy" (matches jj + toolwindow) - change `diff.label.local` and `diff.label.current` both to "Working Copy" and retire the duplicate key (`WorkingCopy.title`/`diff.label.current` and wherever `diff.label.local` is used - grep shows only `diff.label.current` referenced in code at Revset.kt:184; `diff.label.local` may be unused -> delete). 
 2. Action names: keep "Compare with Local" / "Open Local File"? These deliberately echo the platform's own `Compare with Local` wording that users know from IntelliJ's other VCS plugins (the UX-priority tenet: IntelliJ-native > jj-native, contributing.md/jj-idea-2ffd) - Rec: KEEP the action labels (platform convention) but make descriptions say "working copy" consistently, and keep diff titles = "Working Copy". Alternative (rename actions to "Compare with Working Copy") would be internally consistent but less IntelliJ-native; user decision flagged.
 3. Document the glossary in contributing.md ("Terminology" section exists at :711): working copy (= @, jj term; never "local" for it), local (only as local-vs-remote for bookmarks/branches), current (only "the file open in the editor").
Decisions made without the user (please review): Q1 platform-echo vs consistency for the two action labels? Rec keep action labels, unify diff titles + descriptions. Q2 title casing "Working Copy" vs "Working copy" (tool window uses sentence case "Working copy")? Rec: sentence case in titles/labels to match the tool window ("Working copy").
Scale: none. Testing: bundle-key guard (rename tests that assert old strings: grep tests for "Local"/"Current" expectations in ui tests, e.g. diff title tests `diff.title.compare`); manual: MT-DIFF (diff window titles for working copy compare), MT-CTXMENU (labels). Regression scope: MT-DIFF, MT-CTXMENU.
acceptance_criteria: Glossary documented; working-copy side titled consistently ('Working copy'); action labels decision recorded; unused keys removed; tests updated.

title: Refactor uses of ChangeListManager to use FileChange
description: ChangeListManager returns Change objects. Elsewhere in the plugin, we use FileChange objects. For consistency, when using ChangeListManager, turn changes to file changes to unify dependent code
design:
PLAN (label for-human: refactor needing your preference): introduce ONE adapter at the boundary where platform `Change` objects enter plugin code from `ChangeListManager`, convert to `FileChange`, and migrate consumers incrementally.
Facts: `FileChange` (jj/FileChange.kt) is the plugin's sealed model (Modified/Added/Deleted/Renamed, `before/after: FileAtVersion?`, `isConflicted`, `allPaths`) with an existing converter `FileChange.from(change: Change)` (FileChange.kt:~82; handles Deleted/Added/Modified/Renamed and conflict flag from `FileStatus.MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS`). Consumers that call ChangeListManager directly (verified grep): ui/workingcopy/UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt:499 `ChangeListManager.allChanges.filterInJujutsuRepo(project)`; ui/editor/JujutsuConflictEditorNotificationProvider.kt:72 (`getChange(file)?.fileStatus`); vcs/annotate/JujutsuAnnotationProvider.kt:81 and vcs/diffbase/DiffbaseContentLoader.kt:52 (`getStatus(file)` - status only, no Change); actions/change/workingCopyConflicts.kt:19; actions/file/ResolveSelectedConflictsAction.kt:66; actions/file/TrackedToggleAction.kt:165. Only some need the full Change; several just need `FileStatus` (and `FileChange.from` doesn't carry the platform FileStatus - e.g. MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS is captured as `isConflicted`; UNKNOWN/IGNORED aren't Changes at all).
Caveat found: the changes TREE (UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel/JujutsuChangesTree) and platform actions (Rollback, diff, DnD, VcsDataKeys.CHANGES) require platform `Change` objects (`isIsReplaced`, `ContentRevision` subtypes used by the platform diff viewers) - FileChange cannot replace Change there; copies are modelled via `Change.isIsReplaced` (JujutsuChangeProvider.addCopiedChange :254, see jj-idea-flb0). So the unification is only meaningful for plugin-internal logic, not the platform-facing tree.
Design:
1. Add a thin facade `JujutsuChangeListAccess` (vcs/changes/): `fun fileChangesFor(project, repo): List<FileChange>` (= `ChangeListManager.allChanges.filterInJujutsuRepo(project).map(FileChange::from)`), `fun conflictedFileChanges(project)`, `fun statusOf(file)` (delegates). Consumers that need only a few facts use the facade, so the "ChangeListManager vs FileChange" duality is confined to one file and tested once.
2. Migrate consumers one at a time in separate commits: workingCopyConflicts.kt and ResolveSelectedConflictsAction.conflictedFilesFromContext (use `FileChange.isConflicted`), TrackedToggleAction (needs only "has pending change" = `fileChangesFor(...).any { it.allPaths.contains(path) }` - careful: O(allChanges) per call; today it is `getChange(vf)` O(1) hash lookup. Do NOT regress: keep a path->Change/FileChange index in the facade, rebuilt on `changeListUpdateDone` (one listener; scale rule: nothing O(working-set) per action update).
3. Leave status-only callers (`getStatus(file)`) as they are (no Change involved; FileChange isn't relevant) - document in the facade KDoc why.
4. Explicitly keep platform-facing code on `Change`.
Decisions made without the user: Q: do it at all? Honest assessment: limited payoff beyond tidiness; the real bug-prone spot is duplicated conflict detection (`MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS` checks scattered in 4 places: JujutsuChangesTree.kt:122, JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview.kt:64, ConflictEditorNotificationProvider.kt:73, workingCopyConflicts.kt). Rec: do steps 1-2 for the conflict/tracked-toggle consumers only (removes the duplication), skip the rest. Reverse: close as won't-do.
Scale: facade index O(changes) rebuilt once per change-list update (already the platform's own cost class), lookups O(1). Operation-count test: 1000 `isTracked`-style lookups after one update => 1 rebuild.
Testing: facade unit tests with fake Change objects (all FileStatus kinds); migrated consumers keep their tests (ResolveSelectedConflictsAction tests, TrackedToggleAction tests). Manual: MT-CONFLICT, MT-IGNORE (tracked toggle) smoke. Regression scope: MT-CONFLICT, MT-IGNORE, MT-WORKINGCOPY.
acceptance_criteria: Facade introduced; conflict-detection and tracked-toggle consumers migrated without O(working-set) per-update cost; platform-facing tree/actions untouched; tests pass.

title: Editor notification banner for conflicted files
description:
Add an EditorNotificationProvider that shows a banner when a conflicted file is open in the editor, with a 'Resolve' button that opens the merge tool for just that file.

## Why
The current 'Resolve Conflicts…' action in the editor right-click menu is scoped to the focused file (after fix in this session), but it is not discoverable — users must know to look in the Jujutsu submenu. Git's equivalent UX is an EditorNotificationProvider (MergeConflictResolveUtil.NotificationProvider in intellij-community) that shows a yellow banner: 'This file has merge conflicts [Resolve]'. This is the standard IntelliJ convention for surfacing per-file conflict resolution.

## How to apply
- Implement EditorNotificationProvider<EditorNotificationPanel> registered as an extension in plugin.xml
- In createNotificationPanel(): check if file has MERGED_WITH_CONFLICTS status via ChangeListManager.getInstance(project).getChange(file)?.fileStatus; if so, return a panel with a 'Resolve' button
- Button action: call `JujutsuConflictResolver(project, mergeProvider).resolve(listOf(file))` (see src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/vcs/merge/JujutsuConflictResolver.kt) — added in the GitHub #63 fix precisely to avoid discarding a side on cancel. Do NOT call `AbstractVcsHelper.getInstance(project).showMergeDialog(listOf(file), mergeProvider)` directly; that is the exact vulnerable call #63 fixed everywhere else, and using it here would reintroduce the bug at a fourth entry point.
- mergeProvider: project.possibleJujutsuVcs?.mergeProvider
- Reference implementation: git4idea MergeConflictResolveUtil.NotificationProvider in intellij-community/plugins/git4idea/src/git4idea/conflicts/MergeConflictResolveUtil.kt
- The notification panel should refresh when conflict status changes (VcsDirtyScopeManager marks the file dirty after resolution, which triggers ChangeListManager to update and the notification provider to re-evaluate)

## 2026-07-30 triage note
Corrected "How to apply" above (originally instructed calling showMergeDialog directly, which
predated the #63 fix and would have reintroduced the discard-on-cancel bug). Otherwise
independent of the other conflicts beads: still valuable as a discoverability improvement
whether or not jj-idea-n6fz's longer-term redesign ships, since even a jj-native inline-editing
flow could use a banner nudging the user toward it.
close_reason: Implemented: JujutsuConflictEditorNotificationProvider shows a warning banner with 'Resolve' link for conflicted jj-tracked files, funneling through the #63-safe JujutsuConflictResolver. JujutsuMergeProvider.refreshResolved now also refreshes the editor notification so the banner clears immediately after resolve. Commit in /Users/kevin/workspace/jj-idea-conflicts2 (ynqowzmx), pending merge into main repo.

title: Select in Working Copy
description: Add a 'Working Copy' entry to the 'Select In' menu that appears when pressing option+F1. This should be present for all editors that represent changes.
design:
PLAN: register a `SelectInTarget` (EP `com.intellij.selectInTarget`) so "Select In..." (Alt+F1) offers "Working Copy" for editors/Project-view nodes of files with a local working-copy change.
Platform shape: `com.intellij.ide.SelectInTarget` - `canSelect(SelectInContext)`, `selectIn(SelectInContext, boolean requestFocus)`, `getToolWindowId()`, `getMinorViewId()`, `getWeight()`, `toString()` (label, bundle). The context gives `getVirtualFile()` and `getProject()`. (Check git4idea/changes-view for a model: platform/vcs-impl `ChangesViewSelectInTarget`? grep intellij-community for `SelectInTarget` implementors in vcs-impl: pattern to mimic.)

Locate the panel instance via the tool window content manager (`toolWindow.contentManager.getContent(0).component`/`getUserData` key) - add a project service `WorkingCopyPanelRegistry`? simpler: tool window content's component is the panel: cast and call `selectFile`; when the tool window hasn't been created yet, `toolWindow.activate` instantiates content first (callback runs after).

Registration: plugin.xml `<selectInTarget implementation="in.kkkev.jjidea.ui.workingcopy.JujutsuWorkingCopySelectInTarget"/>`; `getToolWindowId() = "Working copy"`, `getMinorViewId() = null`, `getWeight() = 100`-ish (after Project view 1, before others: check typical weights: ProjectView 1.0, ChangesView ~ 2?).
