title: Nonlinear history
description: The history log is currently a table, which assumes that the history for a file is linear. In reality, the history could include merges and branches from those. This feature ensures that the history shows a log with a graph
design:
PLAN: show the file history as a graph (merges/branches), reusing the log graph machinery plus the nearest-visible-ancestor remap from jj-idea-hlu3 (this bead depends on it in practice).
Facts: file history = `JujutsuFileHistoryPanel` (ui/history/JujutsuFileHistoryPanel.kt) over `CommitTablePanel`; `JujutsuFileHistoryDataLoader.load()` fetches `repo.logService.getLog(Expression.ALL, listOf(filePath))` (= `jj log -- <path>`: only commits that touch the file, flat list in topological order) and its KDoc says "No graph building since file history doesn't show the commit graph" (ui/history/JujutsuFileHistoryDataLoader.kt:~13-17; `onDataLoaded` just `logTable.setEntries(newData)`, `updateTableStuff` hides graph-related columns, JujutsuFileHistoryPanel.kt:~35-40). Main log graph: `CommitGraphBuilder.buildGraph(entries[, allEntries])` -> `Map<ChangeKey, GraphNode>` -> `logTable.updateGraph(...)` (UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.refreshDisplayedGraph). Key difficulty: `LogEntry.parentIds` are the commit's REAL parents, most of which do NOT appear in a file-filtered list (they don't touch the file) - `buildGraph(entries)` would classify nearly every edge as an unresolved-parent stub. jj's own `jj log -- path` renders a graph with elided edges (`~`) connecting each shown commit to its nearest shown ancestors (the "simplified history" view).
Design:
1. Data: compute the file-history DAG edges = for each listed commit, its NEAREST LISTED ANCESTORS. Option A (client-side, reuse hlu3): `nearestVisibleAncestors(allEntries = <entries needed for ancestry>, visibleIds = <file-touching commits>)` requires the intermediate commits' parent links (all commits between history entries) - not loaded by the file log. Option B (jj does it): use jj's own simplified-graph parents via template: `jj log -- <path> -T '<id>\0' ++ parents.map(...)`: for a log with a path filter, the TEMPLATE `parents` are still the real commit parents, but the graph output `--graph` shows simplified edges - parse jj's ASCII graph? fragile. Option C (revset): per listed commit compute nearest listed ancestors with ONE revset query: `jj log -r 'heads(::<c> & (<set of listed ids>) ~ <c>)'`... O(n) queries - too slow. Option D (recommended): fetch the intermediate ancestry once: ONE call `jj log -r '<fileset-commits>:: ...'`? Simplest correct: load the ancestry subgraph restricted to the history span: `jj log -r 'ancestors(<head of listed>) & descendants(<oldest listed>)' --no-graph -T '<id>,<parents>'` (ids+parents ONLY - a very light template, no descriptions) -> gives every commit's parent links in the span; then run `nearestVisibleAncestors` over it with visibleIds = listed commits. Cost: one jj walk over the span (O(span), light template per jj-idea-2c8k finding that the walk dominates, so comparable to the main log load for a long-lived file; cap: if span > 20,000 commits, fall back to the flat list with an INFO note "history too large to graph").
2. Layout: feed the remapped edges to the generic `LayoutCalculatorImpl` via `CommitGraphBuilder` using lightweight `GraphableEntry` adapters (id + remapped parents with `elided = true` markers from hlu3) so the existing graph painter (including dashed elided edges) shows them; show the graph column in the history panel (`updateColumnVisibility` currently hides it) behind the same column toggle.
3. Merge commits in history: a merge that changed the file (resolution) appears with 2 parents -> both remapped; commits that touched the file only on one side show as branches: exactly the "nonlinear" the bead wants.
4. Renames (jj-idea-i2e2): rename-following adds older-path segments; the graph builder just sees more listed commits (ensure the hop results are included in `visibleIds`).
5. Entry points/perf: only when the user enables "Show graph" (default ON? Rec ON when span <= 2,000 commits else off) - the extra ancestry query runs after the first flat render (background), then graph appears (no blocking).
Decisions made without the user: Q: Option D as above? Rec yes (single light query, reuses hlu3 remap, no ASCII parsing). Q: default on? Rec on with a size guard. Q: do before hlu3? No - depends on its remap function (build the remap generically there as designed in hlu3 step 1: `nearestVisibleAncestors(allEntries, visibleIds)` over a DagNode abstraction).
Scale: one extra light jj query per history open (O(span)), cap 20k; remap O(span + edges) memoised (hlu3 design); layout O(visible). Operation-count test: remap node visits <= 2*span for a 10k-commit span with 100 listed commits; no per-listed-commit jj call.
Testing: remap/graph unit tests (linear, branch+merge touching file on one side, merge resolution commit, renamed-segments, empty history, single commit); loader test with stub executor (2 calls: flat log + ancestry query; cap fallback); panel test (graph column visible, nodes count == entries); manual: MT-DIFF/file-history rows (history of a file in this repo with merges shows a graph with dashed elided edges; toggle off -> flat; huge repo falls back). Regression scope: MT-DIFF, MT-LOG-GRAPH (shared graph code), MT-CTXMENU (history entry points).
acceptance_criteria: File history can show a graph with nearest-listed-ancestor edges (elided where intermediate commits don't touch the file) built from one light ancestry query with a size cap; depends on hlu3's remap; tests + MT rows.

title: Annotate previous revision submenu for merge
description: When annotating a merge commit, 'annotate previous revision' is ambiguous - as there could be several. In this situation, create a submenu for each revision. Ideally, include part of the description in the submenu, with the short change id if there is space, even better if it could be formatted.
design:
PLAN: contribute our own gutter action for lines owned by a MERGE commit: "Annotate Previous Revision >" submenu listing each parent. 
Facts: today `JujutsuFileAnnotation.getPreviousFileRevisionProvider()` (vcs/annotate/JujutsuFileAnnotation.kt:~93-100) returns `getPreviousRevision(line) = null` when the owning change has != 1 parent (`parentIds.singleOrNull() ?: return null`) so the platform's "Annotate Previous Revision" (platform `AnnotatePreviousRevisionAction`, AnnotatePreviousRevisionAction.java:14-40 - single revision from `FileAnnotation.PreviousFileRevisionProvider`) is disabled for merge-owned lines. The platform has no multi-parent concept in that provider, but it offers an EP for extra gutter actions: `AnnotationGutterActionProvider` (platform/vcs-api/.../annotate/AnnotationGutterActionProvider.java; registered in platform/vcs-impl/resources/META-INF/VcsExtensionPoints.xml; sample: platform/vcs-log/impl/.../ShowInFileHistoryAnnotationActionProvider.kt).
Design:
1. `JujutsuAnnotatePreviousMergeActionProvider : AnnotationGutterActionProvider` (vcs/annotate/): `createAction(annotation: FileAnnotation): AnAction?` returns null unless `annotation is JujutsuFileAnnotation`; else an `ActionGroup` (popup, `isPopup = true`, text "Annotate Previous Revision") whose `getChildren(e)` resolves the clicked line (`ShowAnnotateOperationsPopup.getAnnotationLineNumber(e.dataContext)` - same helper the platform uses; internal? it is public static in vcs-impl; if internal-annotated, fall back to `e.getData(VcsAnnotationLocalChangesListener...)`/the gutter data key `AnnotationGutterLineConvertor`: check availability for sinceBuild 251 via verifyPlugin) and, only when the line's change has >1 parents, returns one child action per parent; empty array (hidden group) otherwise so ordinary lines keep the platform's own single "Annotate Previous Revision" with no duplicate entry (our group's `update` hides when parents <= 1).
2. Each child: label = `<short change id> <first line of description>` using the existing chip/summary formatting where possible (the bead asks "ideally formatted": plain text with `ChangeId.short` + `Description.summary`, truncated to ~60 chars; HTML formatting in menu items is not supported by action text - use `getTemplatePresentation().setText` with plain text, plus the description full text as the action description/tooltip). Parent order = jj parent order (first parent = "p1"); disabled child (grey, tooltip "File does not exist in this parent") when `fileExistsAt(parentId)` is false (reuse `fileExistsAt`, JujutsuFileAnnotation.kt:~115 - careful: it blocks on a CLI call via `awaitWithCheckCanceled` inside BGT update: for a menu of k parents that's k calls at popup-build time; use ONE `jj file list -r 'parents(X)' path`-style batched check? simpler: batch with `jj log -r 'parents(<id>)' -T ... files(path)` hmm. Rec: evaluate existence lazily at click time (action performs, shows error balloon if absent) to keep `update` cheap; mark children enabled always) - decision below.
3. Action execution: open the annotation of the file AT that parent in a new tab, reusing the platform path `ParentFileRevision(parentId, file, repo)` + the same code path `AnnotateRevisionAction.performAnnotate` uses: simplest is to delegate to `AnnotateRevisionActionBase`? it is not public API; implement via `VcsAnnotationLocalChangesListener`-free approach: call `AnnotateToggleAction.doAnnotate(editor, project, file, annotation, vcs, ...)`/`AnnotateRevisionAction` internals - Internal. Alternative: open the parent's file content as a `JujutsuVirtualFile` (FileAtVersion(path, parentLocator), existing `repo.getVirtualFile`) in an editor and invoke the standard Annotate (`Annotate` action via `AnnotateToggleAction` on that editor) - public primitives only: `FileEditorManager.openFile(vf, true)` then trigger the platform "Annotate" toggle with `ActionManager.getAction("Annotate")` on the new editor's data context (AnActionEvent.createFromDataContext) - works because JujutsuVirtualFile is annotate-capable (hq4d: `JujutsuFileRevision` is attached for exactly this; see JujutsuVirtualFile.kt:~45-51). Also resolves jj-idea-3jo's "annotate historical revision" model (same mechanism): do after/with 3jo.
4. Commit-id vs change-id (jj-idea-wiz0): use `ParentFileRevision` with the parent's commit id once wiz0's CommitId locator lands (a parent of a merge may be hidden-ness irrelevant - parents are visible ancestors at annotation time) - not required.
5. plugin.xml: `<vcs.annotationGutterActionProvider>`? EP name from VcsExtensionPoints.xml (`com.intellij.openapi.vcs.annotate.AnnotationGutterActionProvider` registered as `annotationGutterActionProvider`? read the xml to get the exact tag) under the plugin's existing `<extensions defaultExtensionNs="com.intellij">` block.
Decisions made without the user: Q: check file existence per parent at menu time? Rec no (lazy at click with a clear message) to keep menu build O(1). Q: show the submenu for non-merge lines too? Rec no (platform item covers it).
Scale: menu build O(#parents) with no jj call; click = one annotate call (as today). Testing: provider unit test (non-Jujutsu annotation -> null; merge line -> N children with labels; single-parent -> hidden); label formatting tests (long/empty description, multi-line, ids); platform wiring test via the EP registry (provider is discoverable); manual: MT-DIFF/annotation rows: annotate a file changed by a merge commit (e.g. conflict resolution), right-click gutter on such a line -> submenu with each parent; choose one -> annotation of that parent opens; ordinary line unchanged. Regression scope: MT-DIFF (annotate), MT-DIFFBASE.
acceptance_criteria: Gutter popup offers 'Annotate Previous Revision' submenu listing each parent (short id + description) for merge-owned lines; ordinary lines unchanged; no per-parent jj calls at menu build; tests + manual rows.

title: Post-delete notification with Push Now action
description: After successfully deleting a local bookmark that was tracking a remote, show a balloon notification: 'Bookmark main deleted. This deletion will be pushed to origin on next push.' with a 'Push Now' action button that triggers the push immediately. This teaches the jj two-step delete workflow (delete local → push deletion) rather than hiding it. Use JujutsuNotifications for the balloon.
design:
PLAN: balloon after deleting a local bookmark that tracks a remote.
Facts: `performDeleteBookmark(repo, bookmark)` (actions/bookmark/deleteBookmarkAction.kt:21) confirms, then `repo.createCommand { bookmarkDelete(name) }.onSuccess { invalidate(); log.info(...) }`. Pending-deletion state is already modelled (jj-idea-7950 closed): a deleted-local bookmark has a remote row still pointing at a commit and `Bookmark.deleted` (jj/Revset.kt:44, `deletedLocalNames()` :142). Notifications go through ui/services/JujutsuNotifications (group "Jujutsu"); the idiom for an action link is `notification.addExpiringAction(messageKey) { ... }` (JujutsuNotifications.kt:32), and the push entry point for a bookmark is `pushBookmarkAction`/`performPushToAllRemotes` / `checkAndPush(GitPushDialog.GitPushSpec(repo, remote, bookmark, allBookmarks=false))` (actions/bookmark/pushBookmarkAction.kt:137-152; actions/git/gitRemoteActions.kt).
Design:
1. Before deleting, snapshot which remotes track this bookmark: from `project.stateModel.references.value[repo].bookmarks` pick remote rows with `remoteBookmark.localName == bookmark.localName` and `isRemote` (use the same `remoteEntriesFor(localName)` helper the panel uses, bookmarks panel ~:519). If none -> no balloon (nothing to push; matches the bead: only for bookmarks tracking a remote). The snapshot must be taken BEFORE `invalidate()` refreshes state, and must tolerate `tracked == false` remote rows (untracked remote -> deleting local does not queue a remote deletion; no balloon).
2. In `.onSuccess`, if the snapshot is non-empty, `JujutsuNotifications.notifyBookmarkDeletionPending(repo, bookmarkName, remoteNames)` (new, next to notifyUndoable :492): INFORMATION balloon, title "Bookmark main deleted", content "This deletion will be pushed to origin on next push." (plural: "to origin, upstream"), action "Push Now" -> `addExpiringAction("notification.bookmark.deleted.push.now") { pushDeletion(...) }`. Compose with the Undo balloon: delete is REVERSIBLE (jj bookmark delete) and other mutating actions already show `notifyUndoable` via the generic path - decision below on one balloon vs two.
3. Push Now: for each tracked remote in the snapshot run the existing push-bookmark path with the deleted bookmark as target (`jj git push --bookmark <name> --remote <r>` pushes the deletion; verify jj's behaviour for a deleted local bookmark with `--bookmark` - yes pushes the deletion; if the bookmark name no longer resolves locally the dialog code that looks up the bookmark must not require a local target: use `GitPushDialog.GitPushSpec` with a synthetic Bookmark(deleted=true) - confirm `pushAvailability(bookmark, remoteBookmark)` allows deleted). Bookmarks tracked on several remotes -> push to each (reuse performPushToAllRemotes' perRemote list) - or only offer per-remote when more than one: decision below. Push failure -> existing error path (no special handling).
Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Separate balloon or fold the info + Push Now into the existing undo balloon? Rec: ONE balloon with both actions "Push Now" and "Undo" - two stacked balloons for one click is noise; extend notifyUndoable with optional extra actions (parameter `extraActions: List<Pair<String, () -> Unit>>`). Reverse: separate balloons.
2. Q: Multi-remote bookmark: push to all tracking remotes? Rec: yes ("Push Now" = push the deletion everywhere it is pending; text lists the remotes).
3. Q: Auto-expire? Rec: standard balloon (user dismisses); the pending deletion remains visible in the bookmarks panel regardless.
Scale: none (O(#remotes) per delete). Testing: unit on the snapshot function (tracked remote -> names; untracked/no remote -> empty); notification content test using NotificationGroupManager test fixtures (platform test) for text + action presence; push-spec construction test for a deleted bookmark. Manual: MT-BOOKMARK (delete a tracked bookmark: balloon text, Push Now removes the remote bookmark; delete a local-only bookmark: no balloon; two remotes). Regression scope: MT-BOOKMARK, MT-GIT (push), MT-CTXMENU.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting a local bookmark tracking one or more remotes shows a balloon naming them with Push Now (and Undo); Push Now pushes the deletion to those remotes; no balloon for local-only/untracked; tests + MT-BOOKMARK rows.

title: Correct merge diff: reverse-apply jj diff --git for auto-merged parent content
description:
When the working copy (or any commit) is a merge, the 'before' content for diffs should be JJ's auto-merged parent tree, not any single parent's content. The first-parent approach (jj-idea-j1lc) prevents the crash but shows wrong diffs when a file was modified in multiple parents.

## Problem
JJ computes the auto-merged tree internally for `jj diff -r <merge>` but does not expose it via `jj file show` or any template. There is no JJ command that outputs auto-merged file content directly. The template system (TreeDiffEntry, TreeEntry) has no .content() method.

## Approach: Reverse-apply `jj diff --git`
For merge commits, use `jj diff --git -r <rev> -- <file>` to get the authoritative diff (which correctly computes against the auto-merged tree), then reconstruct the 'before' content by reverse-applying the unified diff to the current file content.

### Algorithm
1. Read current file content (the 'after') — from disk for working copy, or `jj file show -r <rev>` for historical
2. Run `jj diff --git -r <rev> -- <file>`
3. Parse the unified diff hunks
4. Walk the after content line-by-line, processing hunks:
   - Lines outside hunks: include as-is
   - `+` lines (present in after only): skip
   - `-` lines (present in before only): insert
   - Context lines: include as-is
5. Result is the before content

### Edge cases to handle
- Binary files (git diff shows 'Binary files differ')
- Added files (before is empty, no reverse needed)
- Deleted files (after is empty)
- Empty diff (file unchanged — shouldn't appear in status but handle gracefully)
- Files with no trailing newline

### Implementation outline
- Add `CommandExecutor.diffGitFile(revision: Revision, filePath: FilePath)` → runs `jj diff --git -r <rev> -- <file>`
- Add `GitDiffReverseApplier` utility: (afterContent: String, gitDiff: String) → beforeContent: String
- Modify `JujutsuContentRevision.getContent()`: detect merge parent marker, use reverse-apply path instead of `jj file show`
- Or: add `JujutsuRepository.mergeParentContent(filePath)` encapsulating the logic

### Files to modify
- `jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt` — add diffGitFile method
- `jj/CommandExecutor.kt` — add interface method
- `jj/JujutsuRepository.kt` — modify content retrieval for merge parents
- `jj/util/GitDiffReverseApplier.kt` — new file: parse + reverse-apply
- `vcs/changes/JujutsuChangeProvider.kt` — use merge-aware content
- `vcs/diff/JujutsuDiffProvider.kt` — use merge-aware content

### Scope
This also fixes the same bug for historical merge commits — `ChangeService.convertToChange()` uses `entry.parentIds.firstOrNull()` which has the same first-parent limitation.

### Research notes
- `jj diff --help`: 'If a revision is a merge commit, this shows changes from the automatic merge of the contents of all of its parents to the contents of the revision itself.'
- `jj status --help`: shows changes 'compared to the merged parents'
- git4idea doesn't have this problem — git's working copy is not a commit, HEAD always resolves to one commit
- JJ template TreeDiffEntry has .source()/.target() → TreeEntry, but TreeEntry has no .content() — can't extract file content via templates
- `jj file show -r @-` fails for merges because @- resolves to multiple commits
- The existing diffGit(revision) method in CommandExecutor runs `jj diff --git -r <rev>` (whole revision); need a per-file variant
close_reason: Implemented GitDiffReverseApplier, MergeParentOf revision type, diffGitFile command. workingCopyParent() now returns MergeParentOf for merge WCs; JujutsuContentRevision.getContent() reverse-applies the diff. ChangeService uses MergeParentOf for historical merge commits. JujutsuDiffProvider uses JujutsuMergeParentRevisionNumber to carry merge context through IntelliJ's revision number roundtrip.

title: Diff views: add Open In > Remote for CompareFileWithBranchAction historical side
description: CompareFileWithBranchAction shows a diff between a chosen Revision (bookmark/expression) and the local file. The historical (before) side cannot be annotated with DiffContentInfo.commitId without an extra async jj call to resolve the Revision to a CommitId. Implement this: after resolving the revision content via commandExecutor.show(), also resolve the commitId for the chosen revision (e.g. via jj log -r <revision> --template '{commit_id}'), then attach DiffContentInfo to the historical DiffContent so Open In > Remote works on that side too.
design:
PLAN: give the historical ("left") side of Compare-File-With-Branch a commit id so Open In > Remote works there.
Facts: actions/file/CompareFileWithBranchAction.kt `showDiff` (:~60-100) resolves the chosen revision with `repo.getLogEntry(leftRevision).id` (a ChangeId, used only to build `file.filePath.fileAt(leftChangeId)`), then builds both sides via `repo.createDiffSideFor(...)`; the Open In > Remote machinery reads `JujutsuDataKeys.DIFF_CONTENT_INFO` (actions/JujutsuDataKeys.kt:68-70 `DiffContentInfo(repo, filePath, commitId: CommitId?)`) from the diff content (consumer: actions/file/OpenInRemoteFromEditorGroup.kt:75 `AnActionEvent.diffContentInfo`); another producer already attaches it: jj/JujutsuRepository.kt:222 `DiffContentInfo(logEntry.repo, filePath, logEntry.commitId)`.
The extra async jj call suggested in the bead is NOT needed: `repo.getLogEntry(leftRevision)` ALREADY returns a LogEntry that carries `commitId` (jj/LogEntry.kt:12-15) - it is one `jj log -r` call that the code makes anyway, and currently throws the commit id away (`.id`).
Fix:
1. In showDiff keep the entry: `val leftEntry = runCatching { repo.getLogEntry(leftRevision) }.getOrNull()`; reuse `leftEntry.id` for the existing locator and `leftEntry.commitId` for the new info.
2. Attach to the left DiffContent: look at how JujutsuRepository.kt:~210-225 wires `DiffContentInfo` onto a DiffContent (it `putUserData(DIFF_CONTENT_INFO, ...)` inside `createDiffSideFor`/`DiffSideImpl`): extend `createDiffSideFor(locator, commitId? / logEntry?)` or add an overload `createDiffSideFor(fileAtVersion, info: DiffContentInfo)` so the compare action can pass `DiffContentInfo(repo, file.filePath, leftEntry.commitId)`. Prefer passing the LogEntry (the existing producer already has one) over a bare commit id to keep one code path.
3. Right (local file) side: unchanged (working copy; Open In > Remote on a working-copy side is out of scope - no commit).
4. Interplay with jj-idea-wiz0: reading the left side by ChangeId can resolve to the wrong commit if the chosen bookmark points at a hidden commit; once wiz0 lands, `file.filePath.fileAt(leftEntry.commitId)` should be used for the CONTENT too. Do this in the same change if wiz0's `CommitId : ContentLocator` is available; otherwise note it in wiz0's step 2 caller list (already included: compareWithRevisionAction/CompareFileWithBranchAction).
5. The same gap probably exists in sibling actions: `CompareBeforeWithBranchAction` (actions/filechange/CompareBeforeWithBranchAction.kt) and `compareWithRevisionAction.kt` - audit and fix together (grep `createDiffSideFor(` call sites without DiffContentInfo).
Decisions made without the user: Q: use commit id for content too? Rec yes when wiz0 lands. Q: fix sibling compare actions in the same PR? Rec yes - one pattern.
Scale: zero extra jj calls (reuses the existing getLogEntry). Operation-count test: showDiff performs exactly 1 log resolution + the 2 file reads as before.
Testing: unit/platform test: after showDiff's request is built, the left content's `getUserData(DIFF_CONTENT_INFO).commitId == resolvedEntry.commitId` for bookmark and for change-id revisions; Open In > Remote enabled on that side (action update test with the content). Manual: MT-DIFF (Compare with Branch -> Open In > Remote on left side opens the right commit URL), MT-CTXMENU. Regression scope: MT-DIFF, MT-DIFFBASE, MT-CTXMENU.
acceptance_criteria: Open In > Remote works on the historical side of Compare With Branch (and sibling compare actions) using the already-resolved LogEntry.commitId; no additional jj call; test asserts DiffContentInfo on left content; MT-DIFF row.

title: Indicate size of commit in log
description: Indicate size of a commit based on the changed number of lines. Initially, this could be done in a commit description, then with some indication against file changes, then in the log itself.
design:
PLAN: commit size indicator in three phases (the bead's own staging), designed so the expensive part never rides on the main log query.
jj facts (verified jj 0.44): templates give per-commit diff stats without extra commands - `diff.stat().total_added()`, `diff.stat().total_removed()`, `diff.files().len()` (probe output: `1/0 files=1`); `jj log -T 'diff.stat()'` prints the git-style stat. These force jj to compute each commit's diff - the dominant cost class (jj-idea-2c8k measured walk costs; diffs are worse): NEVER add to the full log template for all rows (scale envelope: 100k commits).
Phase 1 (cheap, selection-scoped): details pane "Size" line for the selected commit(s): `+A -D in N files`, computed from the file changes ALREADY loaded for the details pane (`ChangeService.loadChanges(entry)` -> `FileChange` list gives N; line counts need `diff --stat`: one extra `jj diff --stat -r <commit>` / template `diff.stat()` call per selected commit, lazily after the file list loads, cached by commit id (immutable per commit id). Bundle key + tooltip "lines added/removed (excluding binary files)". Single call `jj log -r <ids> -T '<id>\0' ++ diff.stat().total_added() ++ '\0' ++ ...` batches multi-selection (<= selection size).
Phase 2 (file-level indication): in the changed-files tree (JujutsuChangesTree for history/working copy) show per-file `+a -d` as a grey suffix via a `ChangeNodeDecorator` (pattern: ui/common/ConflictShapeDecorator.kt) - data from `jj diff --stat` per commit already fetched in phase 1 (parse the per-file stat lines `path | N +++--` - or use `diff.stat().files()`? check template availability: `diff.stat().files()` may not exist; fall back to parsing `jj diff --stat` text: format "file | N ++--" with a width-dependent histogram: use `--stat -T`? Prefer `jj diff --git`-free approach: `jj diff --stat --color never` and parse counts only). No extra jj call beyond phase 1's.
Phase 3 (in the log itself - the scale-sensitive one): a "Size" micro-column/badge on rows, loaded lazily for VISIBLE settled rows only (same batching/caching design as jj-idea-788j: debounce after scroll, one batched `jj log -r 'a|b|c...' -T ...` per settle, LRU by commit id, off by default, setting + column toggle in JujutsuColumnManager). Rendering: a compact bar/number like `+120 -8` or a 3-step glyph (S/M/L by total lines <= 10 / <= 100 / more - thresholds configurable) tinted green/red; tooltip has exact numbers. Do phase 3 together with or after 788j to share the visible-row batch loader (one loader serving both "changed files" and "size" so a settle triggers ONE batch call).
Decisions made without the user: Q: lines vs files? Rec lines+files. Q: phase 3 default? Rec off. Q: threshold glyph vs numbers? Rec numbers in tooltip, glyph/bars in the column.
Scale: phase 1/2: 1 call per selection; phase 3: 1 batched call per scroll-settle (<=60 ids), cached; never per paint. Operation-count tests as in 788j.
Testing: stat parsing/template parse tests (captured outputs incl. binary files "Bin", renames, empty commits, merges), batching/debounce tests (fake clock), decorator test, renderer test; manual: MT-LOG-DETAILS (size line), MT-DIFF (per-file counts), MT-LOG-TABLE (column toggle, scrolling smoothness). Regression scope: MT-LOG-DETAILS, MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-DIFF.
acceptance_criteria: Phase 1: details pane shows +added/-removed/files for the selection (1 batched call, cached by commit id); phases 2-3 as separate deliverables behind lazy batching; no diff computation in the main log query; tests.

title: Open file-at-revision on remote (blob URL)

When a file is selected in file history, provide an action that opens the file at that specific revision on GitHub/GitLab using the /blob/<hash>/<path> URL pattern (GitHub) or /-/blob/<hash>/<path> (GitLab). title: Restore new file should be delete
description: The restore action returns a file to its previous state. The word 'restore' makes sense for changes, but for new files, this actually means that the file will be deleted. Consider either renaming this to 'delete', or keeping it as 'restore' for consistency with Jujutsu naming, but making it clear from the confirmation dialog that this means that the file will be deleted. Possibly name the action 'Restore (delete)' as well.
design:
PLAN: make the Restore confirmation say "delete" when the restore will remove files; keep the action name "Restore" (jj terminology).
Facts: ui/restore/RestoreDialog.kt:44 `RestoreDialog(project, targetLabel, changes: List<Change>, preSelectedPaths)` shows a static warning `dialog.restore.warning` ("Restoring discards the current content of the checked files, replacing it with their content at {0}.", messages/*.properties:303), a summary "N files will be restored" (:305-306) and OK button "Restore" (:304). Both entry points (RestoreSelectionAction -> parent @-, RestoreToChangeAction -> historical revision) go through `performRestore` (RestoreDialog.kt:138) which has the `loadChanges` list, so per-file kind is known there: a change whose `beforeRevision == null` (file ADDED in the working copy relative to the restore target) will be DELETED; `afterRevision == null` (deleted) will be recreated; renamed moves back.
Design (the bead's own recommendation, scoped):
1. Compute per-checked-file effect: DELETE (before==null relative to target), RECREATE (after==null), REVERT (modified/moved). Pure function `restoreEffects(changes: List<Change>, checked: Set<FilePath>): RestoreEffects(deleted, recreated, reverted)` in ui/restore (unit-testable, no Swing).
2. Dialog text: replace the static warning with `dialog.restore.warning` + an extra line only when `deleted` is non-empty: "N new file(s) will be deleted: a.txt, b.txt (+3 more)" (cap the listed names at 3). Summary line becomes "1 file will be restored, 2 files will be deleted" (bundle keys with plural-safe MessageFormat, both parts omitted when zero). OK button: stays "Restore" unless EVERY checked file is a DELETE, in which case "Restore (Delete)" - matches the bead's "Restore (delete)" suggestion; the file tree's per-file status icon already shows the Added colour, so the deletion cue is textual only.
3. Editor-context case (no Change object; bead's note): RestoreToChangeAction invoked on a single editor file - `performRestore` still loads `loadChanges`, so the dialog gets the same Change list; no separate check of the locator needed. If the file isn't in the list at all (no diff vs target) the existing `dialog.restore.empty.*` path ("Nothing to restore") applies.
4. Update the summary live on checkbox changes (existing `fileSelection.addInclusionListener { updateSummary() }`, RestoreDialog.kt:69).
Decisions made without the user: Q1 rename the action to "Delete"? Rec: no - same action restores modified files; Q2 "Restore (Delete)" OK-label only when all selected are additions: Rec yes (small, honest); Reverse: drop the button-label branch, keep the text lines.
Scale: O(selected changes) string work; no traversal. Testing: `restoreEffects` unit tests (added/deleted/modified/moved/mixed/checked-subset); RestoreDialogTest asserting summary + OK text for all-add, mixed, none-add. Manual: MT-WORKINGCOPY (Restore on a new file shows delete wording; undo via notification restores it), MT-CTXMENU; i18n: keys in bundle only (no hardcoded strings). Regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-CTXMENU, MT-DIFF (Restore from diff/file history).
acceptance_criteria: Restore dialog states which checked files will be deleted/recreated/reverted; OK label reflects all-deletes; effects function unit-tested; bundle keys only; MT-WORKINGCOPY row added.
notes: In RestoreToChangeAction.actionPerformed(), a 'new file' change has change.after non-null but change.before null. In editor context, there's no change object — check by looking at whether the logEntry's parent content locator resolves to an empty/absent file. Simplest approach: in the confirmation dialog, detect if all selected paths are additions (no before revision) and replace 'restore' with 'delete' in the message text. The action name can stay 'Restore to This' for consistency with JJ CLI terminology.

title: Preview push
description: It would be helpful for the push dialog to preview the changes to be pushed based on the selection of bookmarks/repositories
design:
PLAN: show a live "what will be pushed" preview inside GitPushDialog, powered by `jj git push --dry-run` (already used by `checkAndPush`).
Facts: `checkAndPush` (actions/git/gitRemoteActions.kt:162) runs `gitPush(..., dryRun = true)` AFTER the dialog closes and only to detect: refused new (untracked) bookmarks (`parseRefusedNewBookmarks`), forced moves (`parseForcePushBookmarks`, markers `FORCE_PUSH_MARKERS`) and deletions (`parseDeletedBookmarks`, "Delete bookmark X from Y", :273-283), then confirms. Verified output format (jj 0.44, local probe): stderr/stdout
```
Changes to push to origin:
  bookmark: feat [add to dcb29298f0e3]
  bookmark: main [add to dcb29298f0e3]
Dry-run requested, not pushing.
```
(older/other forms: "Move forward bookmark X from A to B", "Move backward bookmark ...", "Move sideways bookmark ...", "Delete bookmark X from A", "Add bookmark X to B" - verify the exact set per version in a contract test, incl. 0.37 MINIMUM, since the plugin already depends on these strings.) f5l2 (closed) shows pending deletions in the dialog, so scope/selection data is available: `GitPushDialog.GitPushSpec(repo, remote, bookmark/allBookmarks/changeRevisions...)`, loaded by `GitPushDialog.loadDialogData(repo)`.
Design:
1. A `PushPreviewLoader`: given the CURRENT dialog selection (repo, remote, scope = specific bookmark / all bookmarks / change revisions / tag) it runs the dry-run on a pooled thread, debounced (300ms) and cancel-on-change (token compare), and parses stdout+stderr into `List<PushAction(kind: ADD|MOVE_FORWARD|MOVE_BACKWARD|MOVE_SIDEWAYS|DELETE|REFUSED_NEW, bookmark, from?, to?, remote)>` (new parser next to the existing three; refactor the three existing parsers to share it so there is ONE parse of the dry-run text).
2. Preview pane in the dialog (below the scope controls, collapsible, default expanded when the list is short): a table `Action | Bookmark | From -> To` with icons; "To" ids resolved to short change ids + first description line for the target commit via the cached log entries when available (`repo.getLogEntry` only if already loaded; no extra jj calls beyond the dry-run), "Nothing to push" state, error state showing jj's message. Highlight FORCE/DELETE rows (warning colour) - this replaces the post-hoc confirm dialogs' information but the confirms (`confirmPush`) stay as the safety net (don't remove; the preview is informational).
3. Multi-repo dialog (allData per repo like GitFetchDialog): preview per selected repo, sequential, collapsed per repo group; a spinner while loading.
4. OK button stays enabled while loading; the preview never blocks pushing. If preview says "Nothing to push", warn via the existing no-op path but don't disable OK.
5. Commits preview (the bead's wording "changes to be pushed"): v2 option - list the commits that would be pushed per bookmark (`jj log -r 'remote_bookmarks(remote=origin)..bookmark'` limit 20) - separate follow-up; v1 shows bookmark moves (what jj's dry-run reports) which is the actionable summary.
Decisions made without the user: Q: v1 = bookmark-level preview only (not commit lists)? Rec yes (cheap, uses dry-run, no extra calls). Q: run the dry-run automatically in the dialog? It touches the network? NO: `jj git push --dry-run` does not contact the remote (uses remote-tracking state); confirm in jj docs/behaviour (a test with an unreachable remote URL must still succeed) - if it does contact the remote, switch to explicit "Preview" button. 
Scale: 1 jj process per (debounced) selection change per repo; no loops over commits. Operation-count test with a fake executor: 10 rapid selection changes within the debounce window => 1 dry-run; changing repo cancels the in-flight result.
Testing: parser tests over captured dry-run outputs (all kinds, multi-remote, tags, unicode names); loader test with fake clock; dialog test asserting table rows for a stub dry-run; contract test (real jj with a local bare remote; includes the unreachable remote case). Manual: MT-GIT (push dialog preview matches the actual push; deletions/force highlighted; no remote contact when offline). Regression scope: MT-GIT, MT-BOOKMARK (push entry points).
acceptance_criteria: Push dialog shows a live dry-run based preview (adds/moves/forced/deletes) for the current selection; single shared dry-run parser; debounced/cancellable; confirms retained; parser + loader + contract tests; MT-GIT rows.
notes: Now depends on jj-idea-f5l2 (pending deletions in push dialog). Preview push should show both bookmark moves and pending deletions.

title: Signpost merge creation
description: Add UX hints that selecting multiple parents in 'New Change' creates a merge commit. Visual indicators and confirmation to prevent accidental merges.
design:
PLAN: make creating a merge visible in NewChangeDialog (and the quick New Change entry points) so selecting 2+ parents is a conscious act.
Facts: `NewChangeDialog` (ui/newchange/NewChangeDialog.kt) shows "Based on" targets (`createTargetPanel`, :~135), description, placement (Onto/After/Before radios), edit checkbox, and a live preview panel (RebasePreviewPanel with a pending synthetic entry). With 2+ targets and mode ONTO the command is `jj new A B` = a merge commit; nothing says so. Entry points: `newChangeFromAction` (actions/change/newChangeFromAction.kt: "New Change From These..." plural for multi-select), the quick `NewChangeAction` (no dialog; multi-select parents?), DnD? Also the bookmarks panel multi-select -> `newChangeFromAction` (p35f).
Design (all three signposts are cheap; ship 1+2, optional 3):
1. In-dialog banner: when `targets.size >= 2 && destinationMode == ONTO` show an info strip above the preview: icon (existing merge/conflict-neutral icon: add `icons/merge.svg` via JujutsuIcons helpers or reuse AllIcons.Vcs.Merge) + text "This creates a merge commit with N parents (A, B)." with parent short ids; hidden for -A/-B modes where the semantics differ (after/before rewire rather than merge: say "Inserts the change between ..." only if multiple destinations produce a merge - for `--insert-after A B` jj creates a merge of A and B as parent; keep banner for ONTO only in v1). Bundle keys `dialog.newchange.merge.banner` (plural-safe). Title also adapts: "New Merge Change" when merge (set `title` in `updateModeAvailability()`-style refresh).
2. Button label: OK button text switches to "Create Merge" when it is a merge (setOKButtonText), reverting when mode/targets change - cheap confirmation without an extra dialog ("confirmation to prevent accidental merges" = the explicit button + banner; no modal confirm: modal confirms on top of a dialog are friction).
3. Quick entry point guard (no dialog): the toolbar/menu `NewChangeAction` with a multi-select currently merges silently: if it does, route multi-select to `newChangeFromAction` (dialog) or show a one-line confirmation toast "Created merge of A and B" with Undo (t0iy undo balloon / notifyUndoable) - verify current behaviour first (grep NewChangeAction.update/actionPerformed for `logEntries.size`); Rec: show the undo balloon with text "Created merge change (2 parents)" since the quick path exists for speed.
4. Visual in preview: highlight the pending node with the merge style (two parent edges are drawn by the simulator already as the entry has 2 parents) - nothing to add; verify the simulated pending node renders both parent edges.
Decisions made without the user: Q: modal confirmation? Rec no (banner + button text + undo). Q: also warn when selected parents are unrelated/conflicting? Rec no (jj merges are always allowed; conflicts are first-class).
Scale: O(#targets). Testing: dialog logic tests (banner visible only for >=2 ONTO; OK text switches; title) - pure state functions extracted (`mergeSignpost(targets, mode): MergeSignpost?`); quick-action test for the balloon text; manual: MT-CTXMENU New Change rows (multi-select -> banner + 'Create Merge'; single -> unchanged; mode After -> no banner), MT-BOOKMARK (bookmarks multi-select). Regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-BOOKMARK.
Related: jj-idea-b0p2 (prefill merge description) - same dialog, coordinate layout so banner sits above the description.
acceptance_criteria: Dialog shows merge banner, 'Create Merge' button and title for 2+ parents in ONTO mode; quick New Change multi-select gives an undoable 'created merge' balloon; no change for single/>... flows; tests + MT rows.

title: Evolog — change evolution history
description: Add jj evolog support to show how a change evolved over time. Accessible from log context menu as a new action.
design:
PLAN: `jj evolog -r <rev>` browser - "how did this change evolve" - as a log-context-menu action opening an Evolution tab/dialog.
jj facts to verify in step 0 (jj 0.44 local; MINIMUM 0.37, jj/JjVersion.kt:28): `jj evolog -r REV --no-graph -T <template>` lists predecessor commits of a CHANGE, newest first; each entry is a CommitEvolutionEntry (template keywords: `commit` (a Commit: commit_id, description, author, ...) and `operation` (the Operation that created this version: id, description, time) - confirm presence at 0.37 via `jj evolog -T 'commit.commit_id() ++ " " ++ operation.description()'`), `--patch`/`-p` shows the diff of each step. If `operation` is unavailable at 0.37, omit that column below the version (JjFeature gate EVOLOG_OPERATION) - never emulate.
Design:
1. jj layer: `CommandExecutor.evolog(revision, limit?): CommandResult` + `evologArgs(revision, template, limit)` READ_ONLY (CliExecutor.kt near logArgs); `CliLogService.getEvolog(entry): Result<List<EvologEntry>>` parsing with the existing NUL-separated template machinery (CliLogService field helpers, `singleField`/`TemplateParts`). `EvologEntry(commitId: CommitId, hidden-ness not needed, description, author/timestamp, operationDescription?, operationTime?)`. IDs: store COMMIT ids (predecessors are by definition hidden commits of the same change id - the exact case jj-idea-wiz0 addresses; every read of a predecessor's content/diff MUST use commit ids, so evolog depends on/should land with wiz0 step 2's `CommitId : ContentLocator`).
2. UI: action `Jujutsu.ShowEvolog` ("Show Evolution") in the log context menu (registered action, keymap-assignable per jj-idea-wdqg's direction) and details pane link; opens a modal-less tool-window tab or a dialog (Rec: tab in the Jujutsu log tool window beside the file-history tab pattern - see ui/history/JujutsuFileHistoryDataLoader.kt / history tab manager) listing versions: time, operation ("describe", "rebase onto X", "snapshot", "amend"), description first line, author. Selecting a version shows its changed files vs ITS parent at that version (existing JujutsuChangesTree + `diffSummary` with commit-id locator); selecting two versions -> "Interdiff" (jj-idea-varv) button; selecting one -> "Compare with current" = interdiff(current, version). Operation column needs no extra calls (template).
3. Scope guard: evolog of a divergent change id (two visible commits sharing it) must pick one: the action is invoked on a log ROW (commit), so use that row's commit id (`jj evolog -r <commit_id>`), never the bare change id.

title: Create icons for actions
description: Include: describe, new change, squash, rebase, split
design:
# Icon Designs for jj-idea-9629

## Problem

Five actions currently borrow generic IntelliJ icons, with two collision pairs:
- **Describe** and **Edit** both use `AllIcons.Actions.Edit` (pencil)
- **Squash** and **Rebase** both use `AllIcons.Vcs.Merge`
- **Split** has no action yet, needs an icon
- **New Change** uses `AllIcons.General.Add` (green "+") — works but is generic

## Design Constraints

- 16x16 SVG grid, light + dark variants
- Match existing style: simple geometric shapes, single fill color, no gradients
- Must read clearly at small size
- **Children above parents** (matching jj log display convention)
- Graph-native: circles = commits, lines = parent-child edges

## Color Convention

Existing custom icons use strong colors for **status indicators** (green=mutable, red=immutable, gold=bookmark). For **action icons**, I suggest a neutral approach matching IntelliJ conventions:

- **Light theme**: `#6E6E6E` (dark gray) — matches IntelliJ action icon tone
- **Dark theme**: `#AFB1B3` (light gray)

This keeps action icons visually distinct from the colored status indicators.

---

## 1. Describe — Speech Bubble with Text Lines

**Metaphor**: Writing a message/description. Differentiates from "Edit" (pencil) which changes the working copy target.

**Visual**: A rounded-rectangle speech bubble with 2-3 small horizontal lines inside representing text. Small triangular tail at bottom-left corner.

```
     ╭──────────╮
     │ ──────   │
     │ ──────   │
     │ ────     │
     ╰─┬────────╯
       ╰
```

**Details at 16x16**:
- Bubble body: rounded rect from roughly (2,1) to (14,11), corner radius ~1.5
- Three horizontal lines inside: at y=4, y=6.5, y=9 — widths 8, 8, 5px
- Tail: small triangle from (3,11) down to (2,14), back to (5,11)
- Stroke-based (1.5px stroke, no fill on bubble) or filled body with white/contrasting lines

**Why this works**: Instantly reads as "message" or "description." Clearly distinct from the pencil icon used by Edit.

---

## 2. New Change — New Child Sprouting Above Parent

**What `jj new` does**: Creates a new empty child change above the current working copy. The new change becomes the working copy.

**Visual**: Parent node (filled) at bottom, new child node with "+" at top, connected by a vertical line. Children above parents matches the jj log convention.

```
        ⊕          (new child: circle with + inside, at top)
        │
        │
        ●          (parent: filled circle, at bottom)
```

**Details at 16x16**:
- Bottom circle (parent): filled, radius ~2px, center at (8, 13)
- Vertical line: 1.5px stroke from (8, 11) to (8, 7)
- Top circle (new child): outlined (not filled), radius ~3px, center at (8, 4)
- Plus sign inside top circle: horizontal + vertical cross, 1.5px stroke

**Why this works**: Graph-native with correct orientation. The "+" in the upper node shows creation. Distinct from `AllIcons.General.Add`.

---

## 3. Squash — Child Absorbed Down Into Parent

**What `jj squash` does**: Moves changes from a child revision down into its parent. The child becomes empty (effectively removed). Changes flow downward.

**Visual**: Child node (hollow/fading) at top with a downward arrow pointing into a larger parent node at bottom. The hollow top circle conveys "being emptied."

```
        ○          (child at top: hollow — being emptied)
        │
        ↓
        ●          (parent at bottom: filled, larger — absorbing)
```

**Details at 16x16**:
- Top circle (child): stroke only, radius ~2px, center at (8, 2.5), stroke-width 1.5
- Downward arrow: chevron "V" from (5, 7) to (8, 10) to (11, 7), stroke 1.5px
  - Or a solid downward-pointing triangle/arrowhead
- Bottom circle (parent): filled, radius ~3px, center at (8, 13.5)
- Thin connecting lines from child to chevron and chevron to parent

**Why this works**: Correct direction (child above, squashing down into parent below). The hollow-to-solid visual reinforces "emptying into." Purely vertical — distinct from rebase's lateral movement.

---

## 4. Rebase — Node Changing Parents (with Broken Old Link)

**What `jj rebase` does**: Detaches a change from its current parent and reattaches it to a different parent. The old parent relationship is severed.

**Visual**: A change node at top, with a dashed/broken line going down-left to the old parent (severed connection) and a solid line going down-right to the new parent.

```
          ●                 (the change being rebased, at top)
         ╱ ╲
      - -    ──             (left: dashed = old parent, right: solid = new parent)
      ╱        ╲
     ·          ●
   (old)      (new parent)
```

**Details at 16x16**:
- Top circle (rebased change): filled, radius ~2px, center at (8, 2)
- Left dashed line (old parent): from (6.5, 4) down-left to (3, 11), stroke-dasharray="2,2", stroke 1.5px
- Left dot (old parent): small filled circle, radius ~1.5px, at (3, 13)
- Right solid line (new parent): from (9.5, 4) down-right to (13, 11), solid stroke 1.5px
- Right circle (new parent): filled, radius ~2px, at (13, 13)

**Alternative (simpler)**: Just the change node + curved arrow:
```
        ●                (change at top)
        │╶╶╮
        │    ╲
        ·     ↓           (dashed from old position, arrow to new)
              ●
```

**Why this works**: The dashed vs. solid lines clearly communicate "old connection broken, new connection made." The lateral movement distinguishes it from squash's purely vertical motion.

---

## 5. Split — Extracting a Child Out from a Change

**What `jj split` does**: Divides one change into two stacked changes. You select which content stays in the original (now a parent). The unselected content moves into a new child change above it. Bookmarks move to the child.

**Visual**: A parent node at bottom with a new child node being "pulled out" above it. The two half-circles (or a visual division cue) show the content was divided between them.

```
        ◐          (new child at top: left-half filled — has partial content)
        │
        ↑          (upward extraction)
        │
        ◑          (original at bottom: right-half filled — kept partial content)
```

**Details at 16x16**:
- Bottom circle (original, now parent): half-filled circle, radius ~2.5px, center at (8, 13)
  - Left half filled, right half empty (or vice versa)
- Upward arrow: chevron "^" from (5, 9) to (8, 6.5) to (11, 9), stroke 1.5px
- Top circle (new child): half-filled circle, radius ~2.5px, center at (8, 3)
  - The opposite half filled from the bottom circle
- Thin connecting lines from bottom circle to chevron and chevron to top circle

**Alternative (simpler)**: Two nodes stacked vertically with a horizontal "scissor line" / gap between them:
```
        ●          (new child at top)

      ─ ─ ─ ─     (cut line / division)

        ●          (original at bottom)
```
- Two filled circles at (8, 3) and (8, 13)
- Horizontal dashed line at y=8 from x=3 to x=13

**Why this works**: The half-circles (or scissor line) clearly communicate "content was divided." The upward direction (child extracted above parent) matches jj's graph convention. Visually inverse of squash: squash has a downward arrow + hollow→solid; split has an upward arrow + half→half.

---

## Visual Summary

| Action | Shape | Orientation | Mnemonic |
|--------|-------|-------------|----------|
| Describe | Speech bubble + text lines | N/A | "Write a message" |
| New Change | Parent (bottom) → child+plus (top) | Child above | "Sprout a new child" |
| Squash | Hollow child (top) → arrow ↓ → solid parent (bottom) | Child above, arrow down | "Empty child into parent" |
| Rebase | Node (top) → dashed line (old) + solid line (new) to parents below | Child above, parents below | "Switch parents" |
| Split | Half-node (bottom) → arrow ↑ → half-node (top) | Child above, arrow up | "Extract child from parent" |

### Relationship pairs
- **Squash ↔ Split**: Visual inverses (↓ vs ↑, absorb vs extract)
- **New Change ↔ Split**: Both create a child above, but New Change shows "+" (empty new), Split shows division (content shared)
- **Rebase**: Only icon with lateral/diagonal movement (all others are purely vertical)
- **Describe**: Only non-graph icon (speech bubble)

title: Split out command executor by domain
description: Today, we have a giant command executor responsible for every JJ function. While this was helpful to get started, it has now become unwieldy and keeps growing as we add more functionality. It is time to split this out into different domains. Perhaps we could have an executor for each high-level concern, sometimes identified by the first parameter passed to the JJ command line (e.g. git, bookmark, op) but other times with similar operations grouped (e.g. split, squash, rebase; log, status, show; etc.)
design:
PLAN (label for-human): split the executor INTERFACE by domain via interface composition first (non-breaking), then the CLI implementation into per-domain files/classes; do it AFTER (or together with) jj-idea-saki's result-type work so the new interfaces are born with domain-typed returns instead of being split twice.
Measured state: `CommandExecutor` (jj/CommandExecutor.kt) = 795 lines, ~50 command methods in one interface; `CliExecutor` (jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt) = 1178 lines with ~51 `*Args` builders (+ `execute()` machinery ~:1059-1130 and the undo-token op-log matching ~:1155); referenced by ~35 files; per-command CLI tests already split by domain (src/test/.../jj/cli/CliExecutor{Bookmark,Config,Duplicate,FileList,FileTrack,GitClone,GitRemote,New,Op,Rebase,Resolve,Split,Squash*,Tag,Timeout,Workspace}Test.kt).
Domain grouping (from the current method list; the first jj subcommand + cohesion, as the bead suggests):
 - `ChangeCommands`: new, edit, describe, abandon, duplicate, restore, squash, squashInto, squashIntoInteractive, split, splitInteractive, rebase
 - `InspectCommands` (read): status, diff, diffGit, diffGitFile, diffSummary, diffSummaryBetween, show, annotate, log, fileList, latestPushedAncestorCommitId, resolveList
 - `BookmarkCommands`: bookmarkList/Create/Delete/Rename/Set/Advance/Forget/Track/Untrack + `TagCommands`: tagList/Set/Delete (or one `RefCommands`)
 - `GitCommands`: gitInit, gitClone, gitFetch, gitPush, gitRemoteList (+ future remote add/remove: jj-idea-06tq.1)
 - `FileCommands`: fileTrack, fileUntrack, resolve
 - `ConfigCommands`: configGet/List/ListDetailed/SetUser/Unset (already wrapped by `jj/cli/Config.kt`)
 - `OperationCommands`: opLog, opRevert (+ undo/redo from jj-idea-x30x), workspaceUpdateStale (+ workspace add/list/forget from jj-idea-2ol -> `WorkspaceCommands`)
 - `SessionCommands`/core: isAvailable, version, withUndoTracking, createCommand (the `Command` builder plumbing).
Steps (each independently shippable, tree green after each):
 1. Interfaces: `interface CommandExecutor : ChangeCommands, InspectCommands, BookmarkCommands, GitCommands, FileCommands, ConfigCommands, OperationCommands, ExecutorSession` (declare the groups in new files jj/commands/*.kt; move KDoc with the methods). Zero call-site changes (all callers still use CommandExecutor); StubCommandExecutor (contract/StubCommandExecutor.kt) and mocks keep compiling because the composite interface is identical.
 2. CLI implementation: keep `CliExecutor` as the composite class but move each domain's `*Args` builders + overrides into `jj/cli/<Domain>Commands.kt` (extension-style or small classes delegating to a shared `CliRunner` that owns `execute()`/timeouts/undo tracking: Kotlin `class CliExecutor(...) : CommandExecutor, ChangeCommands by ChangeCli(runner), ...` using interface delegation). The shared `execute()` stays in `CliRunner` so domain classes stay thin and unit-testable with a fake runner (the existing per-domain CliExecutor*Test files map 1:1 onto the domains and can retarget the domain class).
 3. Narrow dependencies at consumers where it pays (optional, opportunistic): constructors taking `BookmarkCommands` instead of `CommandExecutor` (bookmark actions/dialogs, Config, FileTrack service) - improves testing (smaller mocks) but is NOT required; do per-feature when touched.
 4. Naming/policy: new commands go into the right domain file; add a short rule + the domain map to contributing.md "Command Executor Pattern" (:75-80) so growth stays organised.
Decisions made without the user: Q: interface composition vs separate executor objects per domain injected independently? Rec composition (non-breaking, one transport/config/undo-tracking context shared); separate objects would multiply process/undo plumbing. Q: sequence with saki? Rec: do saki Phase 0/1 first; split interfaces while moving parsers into domain files. Q: do now? Rec: low-risk mechanical; schedule when someone next adds >3 commands (06tq.1, x30x, 2ol will all add commands - good trigger: do step 1 just BEFORE those land).
Scale: none (refactor). Testing: compile + existing tests; contract tests triple unchanged; add a small architecture test asserting each `CommandExecutor` method belongs to exactly one domain interface (reflection over the composite's declared methods) to keep the map accurate. Manual: none beyond the standard smoke (MT-WORKINGCOPY quick). Regression scope: none expected (no behaviour change); run `./gradlew check` + contractTest.
acceptance_criteria: CommandExecutor composed of per-domain interfaces with unchanged call sites; CliExecutor domain files sharing one runner; contributing.md domain map; ./gradlew check + contractTest green.

title: Make command results domain-specific
description:
Today, commands all return command results, which contain an exit code, stdout and stderr. This does not abstract away the transport mechanism: command results are specific to CLI execution. Worse, the openness of these results means that client code is responsible for interpreting the results, including exit code, to figure out what happened, pushing this responsibility to the wrong side of the command boundary. This will make it difficult to split out execution to have different back ends, which was one of the original points of having a separate 'command executor' interface.

Better would be to ensure that commands in the executor have domain-specific responses, with all of the parsing within the executor implementation.
design:
PLAN (label for-human: an architecture refactor - recommendation: incremental, test-first, retire raw-text interpretation outside the executor; ordered by payoff).
Measured current state: `CommandExecutor` has ~45 methods returning `CommandResult` (jj/CommandExecutor.kt:38-90: sealed `Success.Reversible/Irreversible` / `Failure` kinds carrying `stdout`/`stderr`), 180 references to `CommandResult` and ~35 places OUTSIDE the executor that read `.stdout`/`.stderr` to interpret output (grep: CliLogService 5, JujutsuChangeProvider 4 (parseStatus), JujutsuConfigurable 4, JujutsuRepository 3, Config.kt 3, SplitDialog 2, JujutsuFileAnnotation 2, and single uses in JujutsuTrackedFilesService, JujutsuIgnoredFilesService, DiffbaseContentLoader, ChangeService, pushTagAction, gitRemoteActions, OpenInRemoteFromEditorGroup, splitAction, ...). The READ side already has the target shape: `LogService` returns domain types (`Result<List<LogEntry>>`, `getFileChanges` -> `Result<List<FileChange>>`) with all parsing inside `CliLogService`; the mutation side (`CommandExecutor`) mostly returns raw results - `Command.WithRepo`/`createCommand{}` wraps them with onSuccess/onFailure callbacks (CommandExecutor.kt:660-740) but still hands `String` stdout to callers.
Design principle: parse inside the backend; callers receive either a domain value or a typed failure; `stdout`/`stderr` stay available only on an explicit "diagnostics" field for messages shown to the user.
Phased plan (each phase = independent PRs, each leaves the tree green):
 Phase 0 - guardrails: add an architecture test (grep-style source scan like jj-idea-949l's guard) that FAILS on new `.stdout`/`.stderr` reads outside `jj/cli/` and a short allow-list of existing offenders (the ~35 above) with the bead id for each - stops further drift immediately without any refactor.
 Phase 1 - highest payoff, parse-heavy callers: (a) `status()` -> `WorkingCopyStatus(changes: List<StatusEntry>, conflictedPaths, untracked(3oxa), warnings)` parsed in `CliExecutor` (move `parseStatus`/`collectConflictPathsFromStatus` text parsing out of `JujutsuChangeProvider`, leaving the provider to map entries to ChangelistBuilder calls); (b) `gitPush(dryRun=true)` -> `PushPlan` (the dry-run parsing from gitRemoteActions.kt:254-285 - see jj-idea-spwt, which is the first concrete instance: land spwt's `parseDryRun` inside the executor and return `PushPlan`); (c) `config*` (Config.kt, JujutsuConfigurable) -> `ConfigValue`/`Provenance` types; (d) `diffSummary*`/`resolveList` -> typed lists (ConflictInfoParser is already a parser object: move invocation into the executor).
 Phase 2 - result shape: replace `CommandResult` in executor signatures with `Outcome<T>`: `sealed interface Outcome<out T> { Success<T>(value, undo: UndoInfo?, warnings: List<String>) ; Failure(kind: FailureKind, message: String) }` where `FailureKind` = Stale workspace / DivergentChange (wiz0) / NotFound / Conflict / Timeout / Unavailable / Other - the classification currently done by callers via `classifyRepositoryFailure(stderr)` (jj/JujutsuRepositoryHealth.kt) and string matching moves into the backend (this unlocks wiz0's "typed divergent-write error" and removes message-text sniffing from ChangeService, WorkingCopyRecovery, details panel). Keep `CommandResult` internal to CliExecutor as the transport. Adapter: `Command.WithRepo.onSuccess/onFailure` signatures stay (callbacks receive value/message) so most actions don't change.
 Phase 3 - write commands: `Outcome<OperationId?>`-style results for mutations already largely there (`Success.Reversible.operation`); convert the remaining string consumers (`squash`, `rebase`, ... only use success/failure + undo info today, so mostly mechanical).
 Phase 4 - second backend proof: the stated goal is "different back ends" - validate the abstraction with the existing contract-test triple (`Abstract + Cli + Stub`, src/test/.../contract/): the Stub variants (JjStub) currently return canned TEXT; after phases 1-3 the contract tests assert on domain values, so a stub/in-memory backend implements the same typed interface - the real payoff test.
Decisions made without the user: Q: do it at all now? Honest view: high-value but large; do Phase 0 immediately (cheap, prevents drift), Phase 1(b) with jj-idea-spwt (bug-driven), Phase 1(a) with 3oxa (untracked parsing - same function), Phase 2 only when wiz0 needs the typed divergent failure. Reverse: defer everything except Phase 0.
Q2: name `Outcome` vs Kotlin `Result`? Rec own type (Kotlin Result is an inline class with pitfalls seen in MockK tests, jj-idea-h8ys; and can't carry typed failure kinds without exceptions).
Scale: none (mechanical). Testing: per phase: moved parsers keep their existing unit tests (relocate), contract tests pass for Cli+Stub, architecture guard test; manual: none beyond MT sections for touched features (status/push/config) - regression scope per phase: Phase 1a MT-WORKINGCOPY/MT-IGNORE/MT-CONFLICT; 1b MT-GIT; 1c MT-SETTINGS.
acceptance_criteria: Phase 0 guard test in place; parse-heavy callers (status, push dry-run, config, resolve/diff summaries) return domain types from the executor; typed failure kinds replace caller-side text sniffing; Cli+Stub contract tests assert domain values.

title: Add refresh suppression for compound VCS operations
description:
When a VCS action chains multiple jj commands (e.g. squash + edit @-), file changes from intermediate commands trigger the BulkFileListener's debounced refresh, causing flickering and potentially stale intermediate states in the UI.

## Problem
The BulkFileListener in JujutsuStateModel debounces file changes at 300ms and fires repositoryStates.invalidate(). When two jj commands run back-to-back (e.g. squash then edit), the first command's file changes may trigger a refresh before the second command completes, showing a brief intermediate state.

## Proposed solution
Add a suppression/batching mechanism to JujutsuStateModel:

```kotlin
fun <T> JujutsuRepository.withRefreshSuppressed(action: () -> T): T {
    stateModel.suppressRefresh()
    try {
        return action()
    } finally {
        stateModel.resumeRefresh()  // fires single invalidation if any were suppressed
    }
}
```

The BulkFileListener and explicit invalidate() calls check the suppression flag. If suppressed, they set a 'dirty' flag instead of firing. When suppression ends, a single invalidation fires if anything was suppressed.

## Affected operations
- Squash into parent (squash + edit @-)
- Future compound operations

## Integration with jj-idea-i4k5
When logRefresh notifier is added, suppression should cover both repositoryStates and logRefresh. The suppression mechanism should be generic enough to work with both NotifiableState and Notifier.

## Related
- jj-idea-i4k5: logRefresh notifier (suppression should integrate with this)
- jj-idea-4tbs: UI updates frequently (suppression reduces unnecessary refreshes)
design:
PLAN: finish the job - the primitive already exists but nothing uses it, and the explicit `invalidate()` path isn't covered.
Facts (verified): `JujutsuStateModel.suppressRefresh()/resumeRefresh()` exist (jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt:92 counter `refreshSuppression`, :338-350) and the VFS BulkFileListener skips scheduling while the counter > 0 (:~482 "File changes detected but refresh suppressed, skipping" - note: it DROPS the event instead of marking dirty, so changes made during suppression are only picked up if `resumeRefresh()` runs `scheduleRepositoryRefresh()`, which it does when the counter reaches 0). There is NO caller anywhere (grep outside JujutsuStateModel.kt: none), no `withRefreshSuppressed` helper, and `JujutsuRepository.invalidate(...)` (:737) is not suppression-aware (it fires `invalidateRepositoryState()` + `logRefresh.notify` unconditionally). The only genuine compound command today: `actions/change/squashIntoAction.kt:~125-140` (hunk-level path: `squashIntoInteractive(...)` then `repo.commandExecutor.edit(spec.destination)` inside `DiffEditTool.withStagingTree{}` on a background thread, then ONE `repo.invalidate(select, vfsChanged = true)` in `runLater`). So the flicker scenario is exactly: after the squash command rewrites files on disk, the VFS listener's 300ms debounced refresh may fire BEFORE `edit` finishes.
Design:
1. Helper (jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt or jj/): `inline fun <T> JujutsuRepository.withRefreshSuppressed(block: () -> T): T { val sm = project.stateModel; sm.suppressRefresh(); try { return block() } finally { sm.resumeRefresh() } }` - `resumeRefresh` schedules a refresh at counter 0 (single, debounced via `scheduleRepositoryRefresh`), which is the desired "one invalidation at the end"; but the caller ALSO calls `repo.invalidate(...)` right after -> a double refresh (resume's + invalidate's): avoid by having `withRefreshSuppressed(refreshAfter = false)` variant that decrements WITHOUT scheduling (`resumeRefreshSilently()`) when the caller will `invalidate()` explicitly; default true for callers that don't.
2. Scope per the bead: "suppression should cover both repositoryStates and logRefresh" - the suppressed thing is the file-event path; explicit `invalidate()` is the caller's own deliberate refresh and should stay immediate. So no change to `invalidate()` itself (rejected: making it suppression-aware would swallow user-initiated refreshes during unrelated concurrent operations). Document this in the KDoc.
3. Apply to squashInto (wrap the `withStagingTree` body: suppress around BOTH commands), and audit other multi-command actions for the same shape: grep `commandExecutor.` sequences in actions/ and ui/ dialogs (candidates: bookmark move + advance chains, `performRestore` after multiple restores, `trackAndPush` (track + push), DnD multi-step drops in ui/dnd/DropPerformers (e.g. duplicate + move bookmark?), NewChange with edit, split with describe-after (SplitSpec describes the remaining side after split: two commands)). Wrap each compound sequence.
4. Thread-safety: counter is an AtomicInteger (fine); `resumeRefresh` can be called from any thread; guard against leaks: `try/finally` in the helper only - no raw suppress calls elsewhere (add a detekt-ish test or a doc rule: grep test forbidding `suppressRefresh()` outside the helper).
5. Relationship: jj-idea-4tbs ("UI updates frequently") is blocked on this bead - after landing, measure the refresh count during squash via the existing `refreshCount`/measurePerf hooks to confirm reduction and close 4tbs's relevant part.
Decisions made without the user: Q: leave `invalidate()` unsuppressed? Rec yes (above). Q: helper default `refreshAfter`? Rec: true when no explicit invalidate follows; squash uses silent resume since it invalidates.
Scale: O(1). Operation-count test: with suppression active, N file events produce 0 refreshes; after resume exactly 1 (use the model's refresh counter seam `refreshCount`/ a fake scheduler); nested suppression (counter 2) resumes once at the end; exception inside the block still resumes.
Testing: JujutsuStateModel unit/platform test for the helper (above); squashInto compound test with a stub executor asserting suppress/resume bracket both calls and `invalidate` called once; manual: MT-SQUASH (hunk-level squash with "edit destination after": log doesn't flash an intermediate state; verify via `log.info` counts), MT-LOG-REFRESH. Regression scope: MT-SQUASH, MT-LOG-REFRESH, MT-SPLIT (if wrapped).
acceptance_criteria: withRefreshSuppressed helper brackets compound operations (squash + edit, others found in audit); one refresh after; invalidate() unchanged; leak-proof try/finally; operation-count tests; 4tbs unblocked.

title: Manage Git remotes
description:
Add, remove and modify remotes for a Git-connected repository. Handle providers such as Github and Gitlab, including cloud and self-hosted instances. Handle authentication and token management. Be able to find/list candidate remotes. Allow a repository to add/manage remotes when it is already connected, or to clone a remote to create a project.

This will need splitting out into tasks.

## Absorbed from jj-idea-noc (Git remote management UI)

### Commands
- jj git remote list
- jj git remote add <name> <url>
- jj git remote remove <name>
- jj git remote rename <old> <new>

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] List all remotes
- [ ] Add remote with name and URL
- [ ] Remove remote
- [ ] Rename remote
- [ ] Validation for remote names and URLs
- [ ] Integration with fetch/push actions
- [ ] Provider support (GitHub, GitLab, cloud + self-hosted)
- [ ] Authentication and token management
design:
PLAN: epic-style bead; the bead itself says "needs splitting into tasks". Split created: 06tq.1 (executor commands), 06tq.2 (management dialog), 06tq.3 (provider detection). Existing: `CommandExecutor.gitRemoteList()` (jj/CommandExecutor.kt:547) and `repo.gitRemotes`/`cachedGitRemotes` (jj/JujutsuRepository.kt) already list remotes; fetch/push remote pickers exist (actions/git/gitRemoteActions.kt, GitFetchDialog/GitPushDialog); Open-in-Remote has URL building (actions/git/RemoteUrlBuilder.kt). jj-idea-noc (closed) was the earlier UI bead; nothing in src adds/removes remotes (grep: only list).
Scope decisions (documented, reversible):
1. Add/remove/rename/edit-URL via jj CLI (`jj git remote add|remove|rename|set-url`) - 06tq.1. Classified IRREVERSIBLE in the executor's Reversibility model (CommandExecutor.kt:~65 comment: `git remote` commands are not undone by `jj op revert`), so no undo balloon; the dialog needs an explicit confirm for remove.
2. UI - 06tq.2: Settings > Version Control > Jujutsu > "Git Remotes" table (per repo when multi-root: a repo selector), toolbar Add/Remove/Edit; also reachable from the Push/Fetch dialogs via a "Manage remotes..." link and from the "no remote" notification (gitRemoteActions.kt `noRemoteNotification` gets a "Add remote..." action). Validation: name = jj/git ref-safe non-empty unique; URL = non-blank, accepts https/ssh/scp-like/file paths (do not over-validate; show jj's error verbatim on failure). After each change `repo.gitRemotes` invalidate + `stateModel.gitRemotes.invalidate()` (JujutsuStateModel gitRemotes funnel) so pickers/bookmark panel update.
3. Provider integration - 06tq.3: classify a remote URL into GitHub/GitLab (cloud: github.com/gitlab.com; self-hosted: user-configured host list - shares config with jj-idea-ecyd 'self-hosted GitHub Enterprise and GitLab instances') used for an icon + "Open in browser" in the table. "Find/list candidate remotes" (bead) = NOT via provider APIs (would need tokens): offer "Add remote from URL" with a paste box; listing repos from a provider account is OUT of scope.
4. Authentication and token management: OUT of scope, deliberately. jj shells out to git's transport: credentials come from the user's git credential helper / ssh-agent / `~/.netrc`; storing tokens in the IDE would duplicate that, add secret-handling liability (PasswordSafe) and still not reach jj's subprocess without wiring GIT_ASKPASS. The dialog shows a one-line hint ("Authentication uses your Git credential helper / SSH agent") and surfaces jj's auth error text. Reverse: add a separate bead to integrate IDE Git credentials (`GIT_ASKPASS` via the IDE's askpass service as git4idea does) - that is the supported, token-free-in-plugin route.
5. Clone-to-create-project: exists as jj-idea-tli6 (provider-integrated clone, P4) - link, don't duplicate.
Decisions made without the user: items 3, 4 above (provider listing and token management excluded; recommended to keep the plugin credential-free). 
Scale: O(#remotes) trivial. Testing: see children. Manual (child 2): new MT-GIT rows (add/rename/remove/edit URL; picker refresh; multi-root; failure messages). Regression scope: MT-GIT, MT-SETTINGS, MT-BOOKMARK (remote-aware chips refresh).
acceptance_criteria: Children 06tq.1-.3 implemented (remote CRUD via jj, management UI with validation and picker refresh, provider detection); token management explicitly excluded with documented rationale; MT-GIT rows added.
