title: UI updates frequently
description:
The log reloads on every file change in the IDE because it subscribes to `repositoryStates`, which invalidates via BulkFileListener on a 300ms debounce. File edits don't change log history — only the working copy entry's empty/non-empty flag could change, and that only matters to the working copy panel.

After jj-idea-i4k5 decouples the log from `repositoryStates`, decide whether `logRefresh` should fire on file changes at all, or only on explicit VCS operations.
design:
## Problem

The log reloads on every file change because it subscribes to `repositoryStates`, which invalidates on a 300ms debounce from BulkFileListener. Editing a file in the IDE triggers a full log reload even though only the working copy entry could have changed.

## Analysis

After jj-idea-i4k5 is implemented, the log subscribes to `logRefresh` instead of `repositoryStates`. This creates two options:

1. **Don't fire `logRefresh` from BulkFileListener at all** — file edits don't change log history, only the WC entry. The WC panel already handles this via `repositoryStates`. The log would only refresh on explicit VCS operations and the refresh button.

2. **Debounce `logRefresh` separately** with a longer interval (e.g., 1-2 seconds) for file-triggered refreshes vs immediate for VCS operations.

Option 1 is simpler and probably correct — the log shows commit history, not live file status. The WC entry in the log (empty/non-empty flag, description) only changes via VCS operations, not file edits.

## Depends on

jj-idea-i4k5 must land first to decouple log refresh from `repositoryStates`.

title: Cope with stale workspaces
description:
When a workspace becomes stale, jj commands fail with a hint on how to fix. We need to detect these errors and fix accordingly. See this stack trace:

at java.base/java.util.concurrent.Executors.call(Executors.java:572)
at com.intellij.util.concurrency.ContextCallable.lambda(ContextCallable.java:86)
at com.intellij.util.concurrency.ContextCallable.call(ContextCallable.java:95)
Failed to load commits from 

com.intellij.openapi.vcs.VcsException: Error from jj log: Error: The working copy is stale (not updated since operation 9b03b567c006).
Hint: Run  to update it.
See https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/working-copy/\#stale-working-copy for more information.

	at in.kkkev.jjidea.jj.cli.CliLogService.getLog-0E7RQCE(CliLogService.kt:156)
	at in.kkkev.jjidea.jj.cli.CliLogService.getLog-gIAlu-s(CliLogService.kt:56)
	at in.kkkev.jjidea.jj.LogService.getLog-gIAlu-s(LogService.kt:17)
	at in.kkkev.jjidea.ui.log.UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.run(UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:97)
	at com.intellij.openapi.application.impl.ApplicationImpl.run(ApplicationImpl.j ...
design:
PLAN: most of this bead already shipped under jj-idea-b65g/27b4 (closed). Remaining work is to close the specific gap in the stack trace and then verify/close.
Already in place (verified in code): `classifyRepositoryFailure(message)` -> `RepositoryHealth.Stale` (jj/JujutsuRepositoryHealth.kt); remedy `updateStaleWorkspace(project, repo, onRepaired)` -> `jj workspace update-stale` (jj/WorkingCopyRecovery.kt:92-ish; IRREVERSIBLE, CliExecutor.kt `workspaceUpdateStaleArgs`); notifications with a one-click "Update stale workspace" (JujutsuNotifications.kt:107-135 unreadable-root balloon, :196-211 working-copy-unavailable with retry); recovery wrappers `runRecoverableInBackground`/`runRecoverable` (WorkingCopyRecovery.kt:~55); consumers: UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel (:242-284), JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel (:243), JujutsuFileHistoryDataLoader (:43), ChangeService (:35), JujutsuStateModel (:697), CommandStaleInterceptTest/JujutsuRepositoryHealthTest.
Gap (this bead's stack trace): `UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.run` -> `CliLogService.getLog` throws/returns the stale error and the loader only logs it: ui/log/UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:153-157 `catch (e: Exception) { log.warn("Exception loading commits from $repo: ${e.message}") }`, :170 "All repositories failed to load - jj may not be installed" (misleading for a stale WC), and the paged path :257/:272 `getOrElse { log.warn(...) }`. The log tab therefore shows empty/failed with no remedy even though the Working Copy panel (same root) shows the stale banner.
Fix:
1. In the loader's per-repo failure handlers (non-paged :153, paged heads :257 and page :272) classify the message with `classifyRepositoryFailure`; if Stale, do NOT swallow: surface through the same notification path used elsewhere - `JujutsuNotifications.notifyWorkingCopyUnavailable(project, repo, health, retry = { refresh() })` (once per repo per staleness episode: dedupe via a latch cleared when a load succeeds, because refresh loops would otherwise spam balloons; mirror `liveNotRespondingByRoot` live-notification pattern in JujutsuNotifications.kt:~46).
2. Fix the misleading "jj may not be installed" line to report the actual first error and classification (log at INFO for stale per contributing.md: expected user condition, not ERROR).
3. After `updateStaleWorkspace` success the existing `onRepaired` invalidates state; confirm the log refresh fires (`invalidate(vfsChanged = true)` -> logRefresh) so the log recovers without manual Refresh.
4. Audit remaining jj-calling UI loaders for the same swallow pattern (grep `getOrElse {` + `log.warn` in ui/**): list them in notes, fix the ones on user-visible panels (bookmarks panel refresh in JujutsuStateModel :697 already classifies).
Dependency note: the bead says it depends on jj-idea-2ol (workspace capability) - that dependency is unneeded for this fix (stale handling is independent of creating workspaces); recommend removing the dependency edge (`bd dep rm`) and keep 2ol related-only. Decision made without the user: remove the dependency. Reverse: re-add.
Scale: none (error path). Testing: loader test with a stub LogService returning the stale failure: assert a single notifyWorkingCopyUnavailable-equivalent call across 5 refreshes and a retry after repair; non-stale failure still logs only. Manual: MT-WORKINGCOPY / MT-LOG-REFRESH (make workspace stale: two workspaces, `jj` change in one, open other in IDE -> log tab shows the stale notification with Update action; click -> log loads). Regression scope: MT-LOG-REFRESH, MT-WORKINGCOPY.
acceptance_criteria: Stale workspace during log load shows the update-stale remedy (once, deduped) and the log recovers after repair; no misleading 'jj not installed' message; loader tests; manual stale-workspace row run.

title: Log pane text needs localising

design:
PLAN: sweep hard-coded user-visible strings out of the log UI into messages/JujutsuBundle.properties, then add a guard test so it stays clean.
Known offenders (grep, verified): ui/log/JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.kt:156 `append("Parent not loaded yet — click to load")` and :158 `append("Hidden by the current filter")` (graph-edge tooltip HTML, the "create tooltip HTML" case in the bead); ui/log/JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt:50 `append("Unknown")` (author fallback); ui/workingcopy/WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt:346 `toolTipText = "Reload description from working copy"`; ui/log/UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:132,147 progress text `"Loading commits from N repositories..."` / `"Loading from X..."`; vcs/changes/JujutsuIgnoredFileProvider.kt `getIgnoredGroupDescription() = "Jujutsu internal files"` (platform-visible, in the Ignored Files group header). Also tracked elsewhere: jj-idea-pp0 ("Jujutsu Log" tab display name in JujutsuCustomLogTabManager) and jj-idea-ysew (plugin.xml text) - do not duplicate; list them in the sweep notes.
Method: (1) convert each to `JujutsuBundle.message("<area>.<thing>", args)` with parameterised messages ({0} placeholders, not string concatenation) and plural-safe forms where counts appear ("N repositories": use a `{0,choice,1#repository|1<repositories}` MessageFormat choice or two keys); keys follow the existing naming (`log.status.*`, `details.*`, `workingcopy.*`); (2) full sweep beyond the known list with a repeatable detector: `rg -n --glob '*.kt' '(append|appendUnbreakable|toolTipText|text =|setText|title =|description =|message =)\\s*\\(?\\s*\"[^\"]*[A-Za-z]{3,}[^\"]*\"' src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/actions` and triage (logging, test ids, jj command literals, HTML tags, file names are legitimate); (3) guard: a source-scanning unit test `NoHardcodedUiStringsTest` (pure JVM, reads src/main/kotlin) that fails on string literals passed to a curated list of UI sinks (`toolTipText`, `.append(` on TextCanvas receivers is hard to type-detect - so use an allow-list file `src/test/resources/i18n-allowlist.txt` of `file:line-agnostic literal` entries for legit literals; new literals in those sinks require an allow-list entry with a reason). Keep the guard cheap (regex over ~200 files, <1s) and conservative to avoid false-positive churn; if too noisy, replace with a documented checklist in contributing.md (Rec: try the test; fall back).
(4) Properties hygiene: ensure keys exist in the single bundle only (no locale bundles exist yet - confirm `ls src/main/resources/messages`), and no key is unused/duplicated (a second small test comparing keys referenced in code vs defined - optional).
Decisions made without the user: Q: guard test vs convention only? Rec: guard test with allow-list (the bead title says "needs localising" - regress-proofing is what makes the sweep stick). Q: add actual translations? Rec: no - only extraction; translation is a separate feature (marketplace i18n).
Scale: none. Testing: the guard test; existing UI tests that assert the old literal text (grep tests for "Parent not loaded yet", "Hidden by the current filter", "Unknown") updated to use the bundle message. Manual: MT-LOG-GRAPH (hover long-edge stub tooltips read the same), MT-LOG-DETAILS ("Unknown" author), MT-WORKINGCOPY (reload tooltip), MT-LOG-REFRESH (progress text). Regression scope: those four; low risk (text-identical).
acceptance_criteria: No hard-coded user-visible strings remain in ui/log, ui/workingcopy, loader progress text and ignored-group description; messages parameterised/plural-safe; guard test with allow-list passes; tooltips text unchanged.

title: Implement rename detection for file history
description:
**File**: JujutsuLogFileHistoryHandler.kt:110

**TODO**: "Implement rename detection for file history (lower priority)"

**Context**: The `getRename` method returns null:
```kotlin
@Throws(VcsException::class)
override fun getRename(
    root: VirtualFile,
    filePath: FilePath,
    beforeHash: Hash,
    afterHash: Hash
): Rename? {
    // TODO: Implement rename detection for file history (lower priority)
    return null
}
```

**Implementation needed**:
1. Use JJ to detect if file was renamed between two commits
2. Return Rename object with old and new paths
3. Enables following file history across renames

**JJ Command**: May need `jj diff --summary` or similar to detect renames
design:
PLAN: the bead points at `JujutsuLogFileHistoryHandler.kt:110` (`getRename` returning null) - that class no longer exists (grep across src: none; it belonged to the removed platform-VCS-log integration; the same applies to jj-idea-yki9 "Implement supported filters in JujutsuLogFileHistoryHandler"). The REAL requirement is that the plugin's own file history (ui/history/JujutsuFileHistoryDataLoader.kt:19-45, `repo.logService.getLog(Expression.ALL, listOf(filePath))` = `jj log -- <path>`) stops at the commit that renamed the file, because jj's fileset log does not follow renames (verified: `jj log --help` has no follow/rename option in 0.44; copy/rename info is only available per-commit via `jj diff --summary`/`diff.files()` statuses 'R'/'C').
Design - client-side rename following with bounded hops:
1. After loading the base history for path P (oldest entry E_old = last row), determine whether E_old introduced P by rename: ask for that commit's file changes (`logService.getFileChanges(entry, filePath)` already exists, used in annotation provider, returning FileChange with `Renamed(before, after)` when status 'R'; note jj-idea-flb0 distinguishes copies). If Renamed(old -> P): load `jj log -r '::<parent-of-E_old>' -- <oldPath>` (a revset restricting to ancestors of E_old's parents, fileset old path), append those rows (mark them with their path-at-that-commit), repeat from the new oldest row. Hop cap: `MAX_RENAME_HOPS = 10` (a file renamed >10 times is pathological; log INFO and stop). Each hop = 1 summary call + 1 log call, so total jj calls <= 1 + 2*hops; entirely lazy: do it only when the user has scrolled to the bottom OR eagerly? Rec: eager but BACKGROUND (after the first batch is shown, so the panel renders immediately; extend the table when hops complete) - the hop count is small and typical files have 0 hops.
2. Path-at-revision: history rows after a rename must show/diff the OLD path: `JujutsuFileRevision`/diff builders take `(entry, filePath)`: keep a per-row `pathAtRevision` map in the loader result (`Data(entries, pathByEntry)`) so "Show diff"/"Get"/annotate on older rows use the right path (otherwise diff shows "file absent"). The panel's actions that call `e.fileRevision`/file path from the panel's constant `filePath` (JujutsuFileHistoryPanel ctor param) must switch to the per-row path - audit those call sites (history actions in actions/file/ShowFileHistory*, details panel for a history row).
3. Merge commits & divergent histories: `-r '::parent'` for multiple parents - use `::(parents)`; entries already loaded are de-duplicated by commit id.
4. Platform file-history provider (vcs/history/JujutsuHistoryProvider.kt + JujutsuHistorySession.kt): the platform's own "Show History" path (VcsHistoryProvider) may use the same loader; apply the same rename expansion there (session `getRevisionList` includes renamed segments with `VcsFileRevision.getPath()`).
5. Obsolete beads: recommend closing yki9 as obsolete (class removed; no filters concept in plugin's own history) - user decision.
Decisions made without the user: Q: eager vs lazy? Rec eager background. Q: hop cap 10? Rec yes. Q: close yki9? Rec yes (obsolete).
Scale: <= 1 + 2*10 jj calls per history open worst case; typical 2 (base log + one summary for the oldest row to check for rename); no per-commit loop. Operation-count test: file without rename => 2 calls total (log + summary of oldest); with 3 hops => 1 + 3*2; hop cap enforced.
Testing: contract test with real jj: create file, commit, rename (`mv`), commit, edit, commit; history of the new path includes pre-rename commits with old path; hop-cap unit test with a stub; per-row path used by diff action (unit); manual: MT-DIFF/file-history rows (history across a rename shows old commits; diff on an old row opens correct before/after). Regression scope: MT-DIFF, MT-CTXMENU (file history entry points), MT-LOG-DETAILS.
Related: jj-idea-flb0 (copy vs rename), jj-idea-rmdp (navigate to diff from history entry), jj-idea-7m8.
acceptance_criteria: File history follows renames (<=10 hops) with correct per-row paths for diff/get/annotate; bounded jj calls; contract + unit tests; yki9 closed as obsolete or re-scoped.

title: Implement file system event subscription for log refresh
description:
**File**: JujutsuLogProvider.kt:216

**TODO**: "Subscribe to file system events to refresh when .jj directory changes"

**Context**: The `subscribeToRootRefreshEvents` method returns an empty disposable:
```kotlin
override fun subscribeToRootRefreshEvents(roots: Collection<VirtualFile>, refresher: VcsLogRefresher): Disposable {
    // TODO: Subscribe to file system events to refresh when .jj directory changes
    log.debug("Subscribed to refresh events for ${roots.size} roots")
    return Disposable { }
}
```

**Implementation needed**:
1. Subscribe to VFS events for .jj directory changes
2. Call `refresher.refresh(root)` when changes detected
3. Return proper Disposable for cleanup

**Note**: The ToolWindowEnabler and JujutsuStateModel already have file watching. Consider reusing that infrastructure.

**Impact**: Without this, VCS log doesn't auto-refresh when external JJ operations occur
design:
## Context

This bead is about the standard `VcsLogProvider.subscribeToRootRefreshEvents()` hook, which is for the built-in IntelliJ VCS log. Since we use a custom log panel (not IntelliJ's built-in log), this hook is less relevant — it would only matter if we keep the legacy log integration (jj-idea-v1o).

For the custom log, external JJ operations (CLI commands outside the IDE) should trigger a refresh. After jj-idea-i4k5, the `logRefresh` notifier is the right hook point.

## Design

**For external JJ operation detection**: Watch `.jj/repo/op_heads/` directory for changes. When op_heads change, an external operation has occurred. Fire `logRefresh.notify(Unit)` (debounced).

The BulkFileListener in `JujutsuStateModel` currently filters OUT `.jj` directory events via `isUnderJjDirectory()`. To detect external operations, add a separate check for `.jj/repo/op_heads/` changes:

```kotlin
// In BulkFileListener.after()
if (events.any { isOpHeadsChange(it) }) {
    // External JJ operation detected — debounce and refresh log
    logRefreshAlarm.cancelAllRequests()
    logRefreshAlarm.addRequest({ logRefresh.notify(Unit) }, 500)
}
```

**For the legacy VCS log hook** (`subscribeToRootRefreshEvents`): Same approach — watch op_heads and call `refresher.refresh(root)`. But this is only needed if the legacy log is kept.

## Depends on

jj-idea-i4k5 provides the `logRefresh` notifier to fire.

title: Decide on selection behavior after describe/new change operations
description:
**File**: WorkingCopyPanel.kt:439, 464

**TODOs**:
- Line 439: "Should this select?" (after describe operation)
- Line 464: "Should this also select?" (after new change operation)

**Context**: Both `describeCurrentChange()` and `createNewChange()` call `repo.invalidate()` without the `select = true` parameter. The TODO questions whether the working copy should be selected in the UI after these operations.

**Current behavior**: Working copy is not selected after describe or new change
**Question**: Should the working copy be selected to give visual feedback?

**Recommendation**: Test both behaviors and decide based on UX. If selecting provides better feedback, pass `select = true` to invalidate().
design:
PLAN (decision bead; recommendation + the small code change): keep "describe does not change selection; new change selects the working copy", and make that consistent across all entry points.
Facts (the bead's file/line refs are stale - `WorkingCopyPanel.kt` is now `ui/workingcopy/WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt`): `describeCurrentChange()` (:420-439) calls `invalidate()` with NO select; `createNewChange()` (:441-462) already calls `invalidate(select = WorkingCopy)` - i.e. the "also select?" TODO for new change is already resolved to YES. `JujutsuRepository.invalidate(select, ...)` (jj/JujutsuStateModel.kt:737-750) fires `changeSelection.notify(ChangeKey(repo, select))` which log panels use to select the row (`logTable.requestSelection`, UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.kt:150) and the Working Copy panel uses to bind the repo (:298). The referenced beads th9h (double-click = Enter action) and byfa (quick NewChange, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+N) are CLOSED and implemented; the quick-new action and log context menu `NewChangeAction` paths should be checked for the same behaviour.
Analysis: describing the working copy does not move it - the selected row (if the user selected @ - they usually did, since describe is invoked from the working-copy panel) is still the same change id, so forcing selection only matters when the log selection is elsewhere (user was inspecting an old commit while editing the description in the panel): re-selecting @ would yank the user's context away -> do NOT select after describe. After `new`, the working copy is a NEW change the user will immediately work on; moving the log selection to it is the helpful feedback (and what other IDE VCS plugins do after creating a commit/branch).
Recommendation (reversible): describe: no select. new/edit/new-from-dialog/quick-new: select the new working copy. Audit all `invalidate(` call sites for new-change-like operations and align: `grep -rn "invalidate(" src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/actions src/main/kotlin/in/kkkev/jjidea/ui` and for each: classify (describe-like: none; creates/moves @: select = WorkingCopy). Known candidates: `NewChangeAction` (quick), `newChangeFromAction` result handling, `EditChangeAction` (edit moves @ -> select the edited change), `WorkingCopySwitcher` (status bar switch), abandon of @ (new @ appears: select WorkingCopy), squash/split results already pass explicit `select` ids. Write the rule in contributing.md (one paragraph under "Command Executor Pattern"/UI conventions): "operations that create or move @ select the new @; operations that rewrite without moving @ leave selection alone".
Decisions made without the user: the recommendation above (flip answer to the TODO: describe=no, new=yes). Reverse: pass `select = WorkingCopy` in describeCurrentChange.
Scale: none. Testing: unit tests per action using stub executor + `stateModel.changeSelection` collector asserting notify(WorkingCopy key) for new/edit/quick-new/abandon-@ and none for describe; manual: MT-WORKINGCOPY/MT-LOG-TABLE rows (describe while another row selected: selection stays; new change: log selects the new @). Regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-CTXMENU.
acceptance_criteria: Rule documented (describe: no selection change; actions that create/move @ select it) and applied consistently across entry points with tests; bead's stale TODOs resolved.
notes: Cross-referenced from GitHub #51 triage: jj-idea-th9h (double-click) and jj-idea-byfa (quick-new) both touch post-operation selection behaviour and may want to resolve this TODO as part of their implementation.

title: Optimize state invalidation for single-repo changes
description:
**File**: JujutsuStateModel.kt:42

**TODO**: "This invalidates the entire state even if a single repo changed"

**Context**: The `workingCopies` notifiable state recomputes all working copies across all repositories when any single repository changes. For multi-root projects this is inefficient.

**Optimization**: Consider:
1. Finer-grained invalidation by repository
2. Invalidate only the affected repository's working copy
3. May require restructuring the notifiable state to be keyed by repository

**Impact**: Performance improvement for multi-root projects. Low priority for single-root projects.

**Part of**: jj-idea-dhd (multi-root handling epic)
design:
## Context

`repositoryStates` recomputes all working copies across all repos when any single repo changes. After jj-idea-i4k5, this concern is orthogonal to the log refresh path — `repositoryStates` only serves the working copy panel and dirty scope.

## Design (unchanged from original)

Key `repositoryStates` by repository so that invalidation is per-repo. Options:

1. Change to `NotifiableState<Map<JujutsuRepository, LogEntry>>` with per-repo invalidation
2. Keep current structure but only reload the changed repo's entry, merging with cached entries for other repos

Option 2 is simpler: the loader receives a hint about which repo changed, loads only that repo's `jj log -r @`, and merges with the cached set.

## Relationship to jj-idea-i4k5

Independent. `logRefresh` fires unconditionally (no per-repo optimization needed for the log signal). `repositoryStates` per-repo optimization only affects the WC panel and dirty scope paths.

title: Handle divergent changes (branch conflicts) in VCS log
description:
When JJ has divergent changes (same change ID pointing to multiple commits), they produce the same hash. This causes issues with IntelliJ's VCS log cache.

## Current Workarounds

These fixes were added to address the assertion error:
```
Assertion failed: X details to store, yet Y indexes in cache
```

**Root cause**: IntelliJ's `TopCommitsCache.storeDetails()` uses `containsValue()` to filter duplicates, which relies on object equality. Without `equals`/`hashCode`, new metadata objects for the same commit were treated as different on refresh, causing the cache to have fewer entries than the result list.

**Fixes applied**:
1. Added `equals`/`hashCode` to `JujutsuCommitMetadataBase` and `JujutsuTimedCommit` based on change ID
2. Added deduplication by hash in `readFirstBlock` and `readAllHashes`

## Future Work

Currently we deduplicate by hash, which means only one divergent change is shown. Need to properly handle divergent changes to show all of them.

## Related Code
- jj/JujutsuCommitMetadataBase.kt - equals/hashCode implementation
- vcs/JujutsuTimedCommit.kt - equals/hashCode implementation
- vcs/JujutsuLogProvider.kt - deduplication logic

See: `jj log -r 'divergent_change_id'` to view divergent commits

title: Add console tab
description: The Git plugin puts its console output into a tab in the VCS tool window. Do the same for JJ, and capture all command output (and input) in there. This replicates the Git plugin's console window that shows every command and its output run against a repository, allowing users to see what is going on behind the scenes.
design:
PLAN: a "Console" tab in the VCS tool window that shows every jj command (and its output), by feeding the PLATFORM's VCS console rather than building our own tab.
Platform API (verified in ../intellij-community): `ProjectLevelVcsManager.addMessageToConsoleWindow(@Nls message, ConsoleViewContentType)` and `addMessageToConsoleWindow(VcsConsoleLine?)` (platform/vcs-api/.../ProjectLevelVcsManager.kt:214-219; `VcsConsoleLine.create(chunks)` for multi-style lines, VcsConsoleLine.java) backed by `VcsConsoleTabService` (platform/vcs-impl/src/com/intellij/vcs/console/) which owns the "Console" tab in the Version Control tool window and is exactly what git4idea writes to (plugins/git4idea/backend/src/util/GitVcsConsoleWriter.java). Using it gives the Git-plugin-identical tab for free (same tool window, clear/scroll/search behaviour) and mixed Git+jj projects get one unified console.
Design:
1. Single choke point: `CliExecutor.execute()` (jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt:~1059-1130) already builds the command line, logs `Executing in <dir>: jj <args>` and gets stdout/stderr + exit code. Add a `JjConsoleWriter` (project service `JujutsuConsole`, takes the executor's Project - CliExecutor is constructed per-root by `project.commandExecutorFactory`, so thread the Project/service via the factory like `executableProvider`) that after each command writes: (a) command line `jj <args>` as a USER_INPUT-styled line (`ConsoleViewContentType.USER_INPUT`) with the repo root path prefix ("[<repo name>] jj log -r ..."), (b) stdout as NORMAL_OUTPUT, stderr as ERROR_OUTPUT (or NORMAL for success-with-warnings; use exit code), (c) a trailing "Exit code: N, 120 ms" SYSTEM_OUTPUT line only on failure or when slower than 1s (noise control).
2. Noise control (CRITICAL for scale - the plugin runs a jj command per refresh): do NOT log READ_ONLY commands by default: `JjInvocation.reversibility == READ_ONLY` (jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt, Reversibility) covers log/status/diff/show/file list; those fire constantly (the Git plugin similarly hides most read commands unless "log all"?). Rec: console shows only mutating commands + failures by default; a setting "Log read-only commands to the console" (Settings > Version Control > Jujutsu, default off) shows everything. For huge outputs (log/diff/show) cap each message to 10k chars with "... (N more bytes)" - the platform console buffer is bounded (VcsConsoleView cyclic buffer) but the cost of building huge strings per refresh is ours.
3. Threading: `addMessageToConsoleWindow` is thread-safe (queues to the console); call from the pooled thread after the process completes, NOT from the EDT; never block on it. Skip entirely when `project.isDisposed`; cheap guard: if the console tab service isn't instantiated yet it creates lazily.
4. "(and input)": jj commands that read stdin are rare (none in the plugin?) - log only the invocation line, not stdin content; secrets: command lines could contain `--config user.email=...`/tokens? The plugin passes `--config` with undo tokens (UNDO_TOKEN_CONFIG_KEY) - hide that noise: strip args starting `--config jj-idea.undo-token=...` pairs from the printed line; never print env. `jj git push` URLs with embedded credentials are never in args (remotes are configured in jj), but `jj git clone <url>` args may contain `https://user:token@host` - REDACT userinfo in URLs (regex `://[^/@\s]+@` -> `://***@`) in the printed command line AND in echoed stderr.
5. Registration: nothing to register (platform tab). Verify the tab appears only when something was written (Git behaviour) and that `VcsConsoleTabService` requires an `AbstractVcs`? it doesn't. Add a "Show Jujutsu console" mention in docs.
6. Interplay: our own `log.info("Executing...")` lines remain (idea.log).
Decisions made without the user: Q: build our own tab vs platform console? Rec platform (identical UX, no new tool-window plumbing, mixed VCS projects). Q: log read-only commands by default? Rec no (volume), setting to enable. Q: redaction? Rec yes always.
Scale: per command: O(output cap=10k chars) string work + one queue post; read-only commands skipped by default (so refresh storms add zero); operation-count test: 1000 read-only executes with default setting => 0 console writes; with setting on => 1000 writes each <=10k.
Testing: unit tests for the line formatter (arg stripping of undo token, URL redaction, truncation, exit-code line rules) as a pure function; executor test with a fake `JjConsoleSink` verifying calls per reversibility class + setting; platform test: after running a mutating command through a stub executor, `ProjectLevelVcsManager` console service received the message (use a mock of the manager or `VcsConsoleTabService` test hooks). Manual: new MT row (MT-WORKINGCOPY or MT-CROSS): run describe/new/push -> VCS tool window > Console shows `jj describe ...` + output; read-only toggled on shows `jj log` lines; clone with credentialed URL is redacted. Regression scope: MT-CROSS (console shared with Git), MT-GIT (push/fetch output visible), MT-SETTINGS (new toggle).
acceptance_criteria: VCS tool window Console tab shows mutating jj commands with output (read-only commands optional via setting); secrets/undo tokens redacted; output capped; zero writes for read-only commands by default; tests + MT rows.

title: Add workspace capability
description: While the simple way to create a jj repository is via , the other way is to create a workspace based on an existing repo. This creates a jj repo that is not backed by a git repo in the same folder. This task involves adding workspace capability, which involves (1) creating a workspace from an existing jj repo, (2) maintaining these workspaces, i.e. listing and deleting them.
design:
PLAN: workspace management for jj: create (`jj workspace add`), list (`jj workspace list`), delete (`jj workspace forget`), plus workspace-scoped config (comment 2026-04-04: e.g. user.name differs per workspace).
Context: today the plugin only RECOGNISES secondary workspaces (the `.jj/repo` pointer-file handling in JujutsuStateModel.jjRepoDirPath/resolveJjRepoDir; stale-workspace remedy in WorkingCopyRecovery.kt `workspaceUpdateStale`). There is no add/list/forget (grep: only update-stale in CommandExecutor.kt:233). Colocated git is NOT created in a secondary workspace (bead text) - jj workspaces share the repo store and have no `.git`.
Design (split into phases, ship 1-2 first):
Phase 1 - executor + read model
 - CommandExecutor: `workspaceAdd(path, name?, revision? = -r, sparsePatterns?)`, `workspaceList(): Result<List<Workspace>>`, `workspaceForget(name)`, `workspaceRename(old,new)` (jj 0.2x+; check at MINIMUM 0.37). Args builders in CliExecutor.kt next to `workspaceUpdateStaleArgs`: add = REVERSIBLE? `workspace add` creates files outside the repo dir and a new working-copy commit; `jj op revert` would remove the commit but leave the directory -> classify IRREVERSIBLE (like clone/init) with an explicit warning in UI; forget = IRREVERSIBLE for the same reason (files stay on disk; revert would re-add the workspace record - actually restorable, but keep conservative). Rename: REVERSIBLE.
 - `workspaceList` template: `jj workspace list -T 'name ++ "\0" ++ target.commit_id() ++ "\0" ++ target.change_id() ++ "\0" ++ ...'`: the `list` template context is WorkspaceRef (name, target commit). The workspace PATH is not in `jj workspace list` (jj has no listing of paths in 0.37-0.44; `jj workspace root --name X` exists from 0.2x? verify: `jj workspace root --name <n>` added v0.29) -> Phase-1 spike: determine path discovery; fallback: unknown path shown as "(path unknown)" and not openable.
 - `Workspace(name, commitId, changeId, path?, isCurrent)` cached in state model `workspaces` (a new `CachedState`, invalidated on op change like gitRemotes, JujutsuStateModel.kt gitRemotes funnel).
Phase 2 - UI
 - "Workspaces" section in the Jujutsu tool window/Working Copy panel header (current workspace name already shown? status bar widget JujutsuWorkingCopySwitcher - ui/statusbar/ - switcher is for REPOS; extend the same popup with a "Workspaces" submenu: list (name, @ summary), "Open in New Window", "Add Workspace...", "Forget").
 - Add dialog: destination directory (default sibling `<repo>-<name>`), name (default dir name), parent revision (default current @-? jj default: new commit on the same parent as the current working copy - expose `-r` picker using the existing CommitPickerPanel), sparse patterns (skip v1), "Open after creating" -> `ProjectUtil.openOrImport(path, OpenProjectTask)` (pattern in clone/JujutsuCloneComponent.kt:4,65).
 - Forget: confirm dialog stating files remain on disk; offer "Also delete directory" unchecked by default (never default-destructive).
 - Opening a workspace dir as a project: IntelliJ's VCS root detection (JujutsuRootChecker, tests vcs/JujutsuRootCheckerTest.kt) must accept a dir with `.jj/repo` as FILE - already handled for state watch; verify root checker covers it (add test).
Phase 3 - workspace-scoped config (comment): `jj config set --workspace <key> <value>` (and `jj config get`/`list --workspace`) - plugin config surface: the "user config needed" notification (JujutsuNotifications.notifyUserConfigNeeded :427) currently sets user.name/email at repo or user scope; add a scope choice "This workspace" (only offered when current repo is a secondary workspace or user opts). Gate by `JjFeature.WORKSPACE_CONFIG` if the flag needs > MINIMUM (verify: `--workspace` scope introduced in 0.2x; if present at 0.37 no gate).
Interplay: vwxu (stale workspaces) - independent; `jj-parallel-lanes` skill workflows use exactly these workspaces (add/forget/update-stale) - use it as the manual test scenario.
Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Where does workspace UI live? Rec: extend the existing status-bar/repo switcher popup + a dialog; a full tool-window tab is overkill for list-of-names. Reverse: dedicated tab later.
2. Q: Sparse patterns / `--sparse-patterns`? Rec: out of scope v1.
3. Q: Forget also deletes directory? Rec: optional checkbox, default off.
4. Q: Phase order? Rec: 1 -> 2 -> 3; 3 is independently shippable.
Scale: O(#workspaces) per refresh, one `workspace list` call per op change (cached); trivial. Operation-count test: refresh with 50 workspaces = 1 list call.
Testing: args builder tests; parser tests (names with spaces/unicode, stale ones); contract test with real jj: add -> list contains it -> forget -> gone (temp dirs); dialog default-value tests; manual: new MT section "Workspaces" (add, open in new window, stale interplay, forget with/without delete) + MT-WORKINGCOPY (switcher). Regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-CROSS (multi-root/workspace detection), MT-SETTINGS (config scope).
acceptance_criteria: Phase 1-3 delivered: add/list/forget/rename via jj, UI in switcher + dialog with open-in-new-window, workspace-scoped user config option, contract + parser tests, new MT 'Workspaces' section.

title: Consolidate LayoutCalculatorTest and CommitGraphBuilderTest
description: These two tests have similar aims, but they overlap. Consolidate them where possible.
design:
PLAN: consolidate overlapping tests - a refactor of tests only; no production change. Needs a human glance at deletions (label for-human) but the audit and mechanical merge can be prepared.
Facts: ui/log/graph/LayoutCalculatorTest.kt (664 lines, @Nested classes numbered 1-11: Linear History ... Parent Lane Selection, Bug jj-idea-1f2) tests the generic layout engine `LayoutCalculatorImpl` (ui/log/graph/); ui/log/CommitGraphBuilderTest.kt (728 lines) tests `CommitGraphBuilder` which is "a concrete wrapper around the fully generic LayoutCalculatorImpl" (RebaseSimulator KDoc) and likely repeats the same topologies through the wrapper (lane assertions per topology).
Steps:
1. Audit matrix (spreadsheet in notes): for every test method in both files record (topology, asserted facts: lane numbers / passthrough / children / merge lanes / ParentState / filtered-graph behaviour). `rg -n 'fun `' both files`, then group by topology. Expected: identical topologies asserted at both levels.
2. Decide the layering rule (documented in a KDoc at the top of each test class): LayoutCalculatorTest owns pure lane-assignment/geometry semantics on the generic DAG (no LogEntry, no ChangeKey); CommitGraphBuilderTest owns only what the wrapper adds: mapping LogEntry<->GraphNode, ChangeKey identity (multi-repo same change id), parent-state classification (HIDDEN vs NOT_LOADED via (entries, allEntries) overload), `appendGraph` incrementality, filtered-graph inputs. Duplicated pure-layout cases are deleted from CommitGraphBuilderTest (keep ONE smoke per topology family through the wrapper to prove wiring).
3. Mechanical safety: before deleting, run coverage (`./gradlew test jacocoTestReport` if configured, else mutation-style sanity by temporarily breaking `LayoutCalculatorImpl` lane choice and confirming a LayoutCalculatorTest failure for each deleted case's behaviour) - rule: a deleted test's behaviour must still fail at least one remaining test when broken.
4. Tests that stay: IncrementalLayoutEquivalenceTest, GraphLayoutScaleTest, IncrementalLayoutScaleTest untouched. Cross-check jj-idea-2k2b (new FilteredGraphLayoutTest) and jj-idea-hlu3 tests so the three don't re-grow duplicates - mention the layering rule in 2k2b's test KDoc.
5. Extract shared fixtures (`GraphFixtures.kt` in test support: builders like `linear(n)`, `merge(...)`) only if both remaining files use them; otherwise leave.
Decisions made without the user: Q: delete duplicates or just move? Rec: delete after the break-it check; keep a short note listing removed cases in the commit message. Q: rename numbered nested classes? Rec: no (stable references from bug ids like jj-idea-1f2).
Scale: test suite runtime only (should drop). Manual: none. Acceptance: ./gradlew check green; test count delta documented; no remaining duplicate topology between the two files except the one-smoke-per-family rule.

title: Optimize lane assignment to minimize diagonal crossings
description: When assigning lanes for pure merge passthroughs, minimize the number of lanes each diagonal line crosses. Currently using simple 'next available lane' approach. This is a future optimization.
design:
PLAN: lane choice for pure-merge passthroughs that minimises how many lanes each diagonal crosses; prove with a crossing-count metric and a randomised comparison, adopt only if it is a strict improvement and keeps invariants.
Facts: lane allocation is greedy "first free lane" (`firstFreeLane`, `firstFreeLanePreferring`, ui/log/graph/IncrementalLayout.kt:~280-350; full-layout twin in ui/log/graph/LayoutCalculator.kt; doc docs/LOG_GRAPH_ALGORITHM.md "Lane Allocation Algorithm" Step 1/4: pure merge -> NEW lane reserved for the parent = lowest free lane). A diagonal is drawn at the child's row from the child's lane to the new passthrough lane; with the lowest-free choice the passthrough lane may sit far left of the child, so the diagonal sweeps across other active lanes (crossing their vertical lines).
Metric (step 0, makes the bead testable): `crossings(layout) = sum over rows, over each diagonal segment (lane a -> lane b), of the number of OTHER passthrough/node lanes strictly between min(a,b) and max(a,b) that are active in that row`. Add as a pure function `GraphLayoutMetrics.diagonalCrossings(layout)` in test support (or main under ui/log/graph for reuse by the 2k2b invariant checker).
Design of the heuristic (step 1): when a pure-merge passthrough needs a NEW lane for the parent, choose among free lanes (not occupied in ANY row from the child's row down to the parent's row - note the current "lowest currently free" ignores future occupancy, which can later force the lane to be reassigned; the doc's "reserved for the parent" lane stays reserved until the parent) the candidate minimising the diagonal span |lane - childLane| (i.e. the nearest free lane to the child's lane, preferring the right of the child on ties so graphs grow rightward consistently with existing behaviour), instead of the lowest index. Expected effect: diagonals become short (adjacent lane), crossings drop; width may grow by <=1 lane in rare cases - guard: never exceed the width the baseline algorithm would use + 0 (monotone; test).
Compatibility constraints (hard): (a) full layout and incremental `IncrementalLayout.appendGraph` must stay EQUIVALENT (IncrementalLayoutEquivalenceTest) - implement the heuristic in the one shared helper both call (`chooseMergeLane(childLane, occupied)`), (b) existing LayoutCalculatorTest/CommitGraphBuilderTest expectations that pin specific lane numbers will change for pure merges - update expectations deliberately, listing each changed test in the PR (the "10 Parent Lane Selection" nested tests are about parent lane reassignment, unaffected), (c) GraphEdgeIndex/long-edge/hover/render math reads lanes only (no change), (d) persisted UI state doesn't store lanes.
Evaluation (step 2, before merging): run baseline vs heuristic over (i) FX-STRESS-shaped DAG generator (jj-idea-2k2b's `branchyHistory`), (ii) 200 seeded random DAGs, (iii) this repo's own `jj log` graph (export parent links via template in a test-only script, not committed) reporting total crossings and max lane; adopt only if crossings strictly decrease on aggregate and max lane never increases beyond +1 on any DAG; otherwise record the numbers in the bead and close as not worthwhile.
Decisions made without the user: Q: nearest-free vs "leftmost free" (today)? Rec: nearest-free-to-child (above), data-gated by step 2. Q: scope creep into fork-merge classification? Rec: no.
Scale: lane choice is O(#active lanes) per pure-merge passthrough (same order as `firstFreeLane`'s scan); layout stays O(n + e) (GraphLayoutScaleTest operation-count assertions must still pass - extend with a count of lane-probe steps).
Testing: unit tests with hand-made DAGs showing a reduced crossing count (expected lanes listed), property tests (no two active items on one lane/row; each parent's lane == the lane reserved for it; incremental == full), the metric function tests. Manual: MT-LOG-GRAPH (stress fixture: merges render with short diagonals; no overlapping lines). Regression scope: MT-LOG-GRAPH, MT-LOG-FILTER (filtered graph), MT-DND (edge hit-testing relies on lanes).
Related: jj-idea-66rr (long-edge collapse also touches lanes - sequence this first; both touch the lane helper), jj-idea-2k2b invariants.
acceptance_criteria: Crossing metric implemented; heuristic adopted only if aggregate crossings strictly decrease without width regression (numbers recorded); full/incremental equivalence preserved; changed test expectations listed; MT-LOG-GRAPH re-run.

title: Add graph line style configuration (straight vs curved)
design:
PLAN: graph line style option (diagonal vs curved) as a paint-only change in the row renderer, persisted in settings, with a shared geometry helper so hover/hit-testing stays correct. Kevin's comment (2026-03-01) names the spot: `JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.GraphAndDescriptionPanel.drawLinesToParents` - "draw horizontal lines and arcs instead of diagonal lines".
Facts: each row paints independently: incoming connectors from the row's top edge (connectionX, y=0) to the commit circle (commitX, commitY) and outgoing from the circle to the bottom edge (targetX, y=height) (`drawLinesToParents`, JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.kt:423-443, reading `GraphEdgeIndex.incomingEdges/outgoingEdges`), passthroughs are vertical lines (`drawPassThroughLines` :~385), all drawn via `drawLaneLine(g2d, edge, color, x1,y1,x2,y2)` (:335, applies the hover stroke). Lane geometry: LANE_WIDTH=16 (JBValue, HiDPI-aware, :41), ROW_HEIGHT=22. Currently a lane change between adjacent rows = a straight diagonal spanning one row height.
Design:
1. Setting: `graphLineStyle: String = "DIAGONAL"` (enum `GraphLineStyle { DIAGONAL, CURVED }` stored by name like `defaultPushScope`, JujutsuSettingsState.kt) in the per-log-window `LogWindowConfig` or global? Rec: global project setting in Settings > Version Control > Jujutsu > Log (radio) and also a toggle in the log toolbar "Graph" popup next to column toggles; read live by the renderer via the settings service (read once per paint pass, not per segment).
2. Geometry helper `GraphSegmentShape.path(style, x1, y1, x2, y2): Shape` (pure, in ui/log/graph/ or ui/log/): DIAGONAL -> `Line2D` as today; CURVED -> `Path2D` with a smooth S-curve: vertical tangents at both ends, i.e. cubic Bezier from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2) with control points (x1, y1 + dy/2) and (x2, y2 - dy/2) - the lane-shift "swoosh" used by GitHub/IntelliJ (IntelliJ vcs-log draws "curve" style in its own `SimpleGraphCellPainter`/`GraphCellPainter`, option `vcs.log.curved.graph` - check platform/vcs-log/impl for the exact shape to match user expectations). Endpoints are unchanged (same x,y as the diagonal), so neighbouring rows' segments still join continuously (a segment ends at the row edge at the lane centre in both styles; with vertical tangents at the endpoints the curve meets the vertical passthrough line of the next row smoothly - this is the property that makes per-row independent painting valid).
3. Renderer: `drawLaneLine` takes a `Shape` via the helper when the segment isn't vertical (x1 != x2); vertical segments unchanged. Anti-aliasing: ensure `RenderingHints.KEY_ANTIALIASING` is on for curves (check how circles are drawn; diagonals currently rely on default aliasing? set hint locally and restore). Hover thickening (sc8m) just changes the stroke - unchanged.
4. Hit-testing: `GraphEdgeIndex` works on (row, lane) cells, not pixels, so curved vs diagonal doesn't matter for long-edge hover/click (unless hit-testing uses the line geometry: check `graphEdgeHoverAt` in JujutsuLogTable - if it tests pixel distance to the diagonal, update to the same helper; Rec: verify).
5. Interactions: DnD drop-row highlight unaffected; stubs (HIDDEN wiggle/NOT_LOADED faded) unchanged; hlu3 elided dashed edges use the same helper (dash stroke on a curve works).
Decisions made without the user: Q: default? Rec DIAGONAL (no behaviour change). Q: per-window or global? Rec global (log windows share the look). Q: also straight horizontal-then-vertical "metro" style? Rec no (YAGNI).
Scale: paint cost O(visible rows x lanes touched) - unchanged order; a Bezier path per non-vertical segment (allocation per segment per paint: reuse a `Path2D.Float` instance per panel to avoid garbage; measure with the g7to repaint benchmark if added). No layout/data change.
Testing: pure geometry tests (endpoints equal inputs; tangents vertical at ends: sample derivative near ends; symmetric); renderer snapshot-ish test using BufferedImage painting one row in both styles and asserting pixel at the lane centre at row top/bottom is drawn (continuity) and mid-row pixel differs from the diagonal; settings round-trip test (ajd0 reflective guard picks it up). Manual: MT-LOG-GRAPH (switch style: lines join continuously across rows at multiple zoom levels 100%/200%, dark/light; hover thickening; stress fixture merges). Regression scope: MT-LOG-GRAPH, MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-SETTINGS.
acceptance_criteria: Settings option Diagonal/Curved changes connector shape without breaking row-to-row continuity or hover/click; default unchanged; geometry + paint tests; MT-LOG-GRAPH rows.

title: Add graph node collapsing/expanding support
design:
PLAN (pass-2 / needs-your-review: empty bead from the original custom-log epic, 2025-12): "graph node collapsing/expanding" most plausibly means IntelliJ VCS log's "Collapse Linear Branches": runs of single-parent/single-child commits fold into one placeholder row that can be expanded. IntelliJ reference: platform/vcs-log/graph (`CollapsedActionManager`, `LinearGraph` "collapsed" controller: `GraphAction.Type.COLLAPSE/EXPAND`, `FragmentGenerator`). Related existing beads: jj-idea-66rr (long-EDGE collapsing, paint only) and jj-idea-hlu3 (elided edges); this one is about collapsing NODES (rows).
Recommendation: DEFER and decide scope; if pursued, implement as a data-layer view transform, not a renderer hack:
1. Definition: a "linear run" = >= K (default 5) consecutive loaded entries where each has exactly one parent in the loaded set, that parent has exactly one child, none is the working copy, none carries a bookmark/tag/@/immutable boundary/selection/filter match/conflict/divergent flag (anything the user cares about stays visible - mirrors IntelliJ's rule that refs and merge points are never collapsed).
2. Model: `CollapsedRun(entries)` pseudo-row (like the existing `LogEntry.pending` pseudo-entries) produced by a pure transform `collapseLinearRuns(entries): List<RowItem>` run in `refreshDisplayedGraph()` (UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.kt:212) before `buildGraph`; the graph builder sees ONE node standing for the run (parents = run's last parent; children = run's first child) so layout/edge index/long-edge code keep working unchanged on the reduced entry list. The table model must then map rows -> RowItem (many places assume `getEntry(row)` returns LogEntry: selection, details pane, DnD, tooltips, context menu, search) - this is the real cost: ~everything keyed by row needs a collapsed-row case. Expand: click the placeholder (or a "+" glyph in the graph gutter) -> remember expanded run ids (by first/last change id) in the panel and recompute.
3. Interaction rules: selecting/searching/filtering a commit inside a collapsed run auto-expands it (otherwise "not found" confusion); DnD onto a collapsed run is disabled; paging (jj-idea-2c8k): runs are computed over the loaded window and may change as pages load (stable ids by endpoints, recomputed on each data change).
Decisions made without the user (please review):
 1. Q: Is node collapsing wanted at all? Rec: low value for jj - jj histories are short stacks + trunk; long linear trunk runs are the main beneficiary and paged loading already limits them; 66rr (arrows for long edges) + filtering/revsets (`trunk()..@`) give most of the benefit. Rec: keep P3-> consider moving to P4/backlog; do not start without a concrete user ask.
 2. Q: if built, per-window toggle default off? Rec yes.
Scale: transform O(n) per data change; no jj calls. Testing (if built): pure-function tests (runs broken by refs/merges/WC/selection; K threshold; idempotence; stable ids), layout equivalence on collapsed lists (LayoutCalculatorTest property), table-model row-mapping tests; manual: MT-LOG-GRAPH/MT-LOG-TABLE/MT-DND full pass (shared surface).
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded (defer/close vs build); if built, linear-run collapsing as a data-layer transform with auto-expand on select/search and full MT-LOG pass.

title: Add sorting support to custom log
design:
PLAN (pass-2 / needs-your-review: the bead has no description; the design choices below are recommendations to reverse).
Facts: the log table has NO row sorter (grep for RowSorter/SortOrder: none) - row order is jj's (`jj log` default topological order with a graph) and the graph layout (docs/LOG_GRAPH_ALGORITHM.md, ui/log/graph/LayoutCalculatorImpl) REQUIRES rows in topological order (parents after children; passthrough/lane math assumes it). Any column sort that breaks topo order invalidates the graph. IntelliJ's own VCS log does not offer per-column sorting either: it offers an ordering choice (Topological / "By date") that keeps the graph valid.
Recommendation: implement SORT as an ORDER MODE of the data, not a Swing row sorter, in two steps:
1. Order options (Rec v1): `Topological` (today: jj's order) and `By commit date` (newest first; still a valid topological order: a "date-ordered topological sort" as git does with `--date-order`, i.e. a parent never precedes its child even if its timestamp is newer; implemented client-side by the existing `topologicalSort` used for the merged snapshot (UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader mergeAndNotify / ui/log topologicalSort, jj-idea-ix4v notes its O(n log n) cost - priority-queue keyed by committerTimestamp) - so graph and `appendGraph` incremental paths stay valid). Exposed as a toggle in the log toolbar overflow/"View" menu (next to column visibility toggles in JujutsuColumnManager popup) and persisted in `LogWindowConfig` (per window).
   jj itself can order: `jj log` has `--reversed` and revset ordering is fixed by jj, so date-ordering is done in the plugin (the loader already sorts when merging multi-repo/paged results).
2. Per-column sorting (author, date asc/desc) - NOT recommended with the graph: sorting breaks topology. If the graph column is hidden (the column manager lets description-only layouts; `showDecorations`/graph is always on?) a flat sort could be allowed, but this adds a second layout mode (flat rows) with its own selection/DnD/hover consequences. Reject for v1; revisit as "flat list mode" (graph off) in its own bead if requested. Document that decision here.
Paging interaction (jj-idea-2c8k): paged loading walks the frontier in jj's order; a client-side date reorder only reorders loaded rows - the loaded set is the same, so "By date" is a display order of the loaded window. Acceptable; label the option "Order loaded changes by date".
Decisions made without the user
1. Q: Per-column sort vs ordering modes? Rec: ordering modes only (graph validity).
2. Q: Default? Rec: Topological (unchanged).
3. Q: Include "Reverse (oldest first)"? Rec: no (graph direction assumptions throughout).
Scale: date ordering = one O(n log n) sort of loaded entries per data change (same cost class as the existing merge sort; at the 100k-entry scale envelope the loaded window is bounded by paging); no per-paint cost. Operation-count test: order toggle triggers exactly one sort + one layout build; appends keep incremental equivalence (IncrementalLayoutEquivalenceTest extended with date order).
Testing: topological-date-order unit tests (diamond with newer parent; merges; equal timestamps stable by original index), property test: output is always a valid topological order; layout validity via the invariant checker from jj-idea-2k2b; settings round-trip (LogWindowConfig); manual: MT-LOG-TABLE (toggle order; graph stays correct; persists across restart), MT-LOG-GRAPH. Regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-GRAPH, MT-LOG-FILTER (filtered graph with date order).
acceptance_criteria: Log can be ordered Topological (default) or By commit date as a validity-preserving topological order, persisted per log window; graph stays correct; per-column sorting explicitly declined (documented); tests + MT rows.

design:

title: Add 'Show in Jujutsu Log' action from file history
design:
PLAN: "Show in Jujutsu Log" action from the file history panel (and, cheaply, other places that hold a log entry).
Facts: file history is `ui/history/JujutsuFileHistoryPanel.kt` (extends CommitTablePanel with toolbar id "JujutsuFileHistoryToolbar"); its rows are LogEntry; `AnActionEvent.fileRevision` (actions/ActionEventExtensions.kt:141) gives `JujutsuFileRevision` (changeId + repo) for platform file-history contexts; the log navigation primitive already exists: `project.stateModel.changeSelection.notify(ChangeKey(repo, changeId))` (used by LogClickTarget.kt:225 `ChangeNavigationClick`), consumed by UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel.kt:150 -> `logTable.requestSelection(key)` with the pending-selection + `loadExpanding` machinery for revisions not in the loaded window (:157-162, abandoned-since-render handled via onMissing - GitHub #76).
Design:
1. Action `Jujutsu.ShowInLog` (`actions/log/ShowInLogAction.kt`, DumbAwareAction, BGT update): resolves a target `ChangeKey` from, in order: `e.logEntry` (LOG_ENTRY data key, set by the history/log tables), `e.fileRevision` (platform VCS_FILE_REVISION), else disabled. Enabled only for exactly one entry. `actionPerformed`: `project.stateModel.changeSelection.notify(key)` then activate the Jujutsu log tool window tab (ToolWindowManager "Jujutsu"/whatever id JujutsuUiEnabler registers - find via `grep ToolWindow` in ui/services) and select the main log tab (not file history); keep window focus behaviour consistent with LogClickTarget's navigation (does it activate? if `changeSelection` listeners already activate, don't duplicate).
2. Registration: plugin.xml `<action id="Jujutsu.ShowInLog">`; add to the file history panel's context menu and toolbar (`JujutsuFileHistoryToolbar` group is built in CommitTablePanel.createActionGroup - see jj-idea-66id/1y1j on keeping groups XML-declared; prefer adding to an XML group if one exists for the history context menu, else add to the Kotlin list next to existing items), and to the platform file history popup if the platform's `VcsHistoryProvider` panel is ever used (JujutsuHistoryProvider exists: vcs/history/JujutsuHistoryProvider.kt -> the platform "Show History" opens the platform's own history UI or ours? verify which opens and register in `Vcs.FileHistory` popup group via `<add-to-group group-id="VcsHistoryActionsGroup">` if the platform UI is used).
3. Divergent/hidden: use the row's own commit when the entry's change id is divergent (`ChangeId.full` carries the offset) - ChangeKey(repo, id) with offset already disambiguates. A hidden (rewritten-away) historical revision (file history of a hidden commit) will not be in the log; `loadExpanding` onMissing clears navigation silently -> show a balloon "Revision not in the log (hidden)" via the onMissing callback for THIS action (one-shot notification), rather than silently doing nothing.
4. Keymap: assignable (registered action), no default shortcut.
Decisions made without the user: Q: also add to the Working Copy panel/changes tree? Rec: no (out of scope; a changed-file node doesn't map to a commit). Q: balloon on missing? Rec yes.
Scale: none (O(1)); expansion uses the existing loadExpanding (one jj call). Testing: action update() tests (data-key permutations); platform test: invoking with a stub state model records `changeSelection.notify(ChangeKey)`; missing-revision balloon test. Manual: MT-CTXMENU (file history row -> Show in Jujutsu Log selects the row in the main log, scrolls to it, loads older pages if needed); regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-LOG-TABLE.
acceptance_criteria: Show in Jujutsu Log from file history selects and reveals the change in the main log (expanding the window if needed), balloon when the revision is not in the log; action registered/keymap-assignable; tests + MT-CTXMENU row.
notes: In file history context, VcsDataKeys.VCS_FILE_REVISION gives a JujutsuFileRevision (see e.fileRevision in ActionEventExtensions). That has changeId and repo. To navigate the log: fire stateModel.changeSelection with ChangeKey(repo, changeId). The log panel's pending selection pattern handles the case where the log hasn't loaded that revision yet. Register the action in the JujutsuFileHistoryPanel toolbar and/or context menu.

title: Fix hover effect to work across entire table row
description:
**Problem**: Hover effect only works on graph+description column, not entire row

**Expected**: Like Git plugin, hovering over any cell in a row should highlight the entire row

**Current**: Only the graph+description cell shows hover background

**Solution**: Need to implement row-level hover tracking that updates all cells in the hovered row

**Files**: JujutsuLogTable.kt, JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt (Author/Date renderers need hover support)
design:
PLAN: paint the hover background in every column from one shared rule driven by JujutsuLogTable.hoveredRow.
Facts: today only the graph+description panel hovers - ui/log/JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.kt:94-97 computes `isHovered = mousePos != null && table.rowAtPoint(mousePos) == row` (uses `table.mousePosition`, a per-paint AWT query) and sets `background = isHovered -> UIUtil.getListBackground(true, false)` (:~126). Other columns use ui/components/TextTableCellRenderer.kt (author/committer `UserCellRenderer`, `DateCellRenderer` in ui/log/JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt:26/41) and the root gutter (JujutsuRootGutterRenderer.kt), which never look at hover. The table already tracks `hoveredRow` (JujutsuLogTable.kt:59, updated in refreshHoverState :595 with targeted `repaintRow`), but it repaints the whole row - so the plumbing for row-wide repaint exists; only the renderers ignore it.
Design:
1. One helper on the table: `fun JujutsuLogTable.hoverBackgroundFor(row: Int, selected: Boolean): Color?` = null when selected or row != hoveredRow, else the same `UIUtil.getListBackground(true, false)` colour (single definition; the graph renderer switches to it too, replacing `mousePos`-based detection with `hoveredRow` so there is one source of truth and `table.mousePosition` calls disappear from the paint path - small perf win).
2. TextTableCellRenderer.customizeCellRenderer (TextTableCellRenderer.kt:~25): after the existing hover-link bookkeeping, `(table as? JujutsuLogTable)?.hoverBackgroundFor(row, selected)?.let { background = it }`. Verify ordering: ColoredTableCellRenderer sets background from selection BEFORE calling customizeCellRenderer (check in intellij-community `ColoredTableCellRenderer.getTableCellRendererComponent`); if not, set it in an overridden `getTableCellRendererComponent` post-super instead.
3. Also the root gutter renderer and COLUMN_TRAILING_SPACER renderer (JujutsuLogTableRenderers.kt:~340, "paints nothing but the normal selection/background") - apply the same helper so no column is left unhighlighted; check graph column cells (the graph is drawn inside the graph+description panel, covered).
4. Exit/leave: `mouseExited` must set hoveredRow = -1 and repaint the old row (check the existing mouseExited handler at JujutsuLogTable.kt:~251 does for hoveredRow, not just hoveredEdge); scroll-without-mouse-move already re-runs refreshHoverState via the viewport listener (:233-237).
5. Setting: `showLogHoverTooltip` (:271) is a tooltip toggle - unrelated, but if a hover-highlight setting exists, honour it; otherwise none.
6. Not for picker tables (Split/Squash/Rebase) that reuse the renderer classes without being a JujutsuLogTable: helper returns null there (they keep their current look); decide in review whether picker tables should also hover (out of scope).
Decisions made without the user: Q: highlight colour? Rec: reuse the existing hover colour so the look is unchanged except spanning the row (matches the git plugin as the bead asks). Selected rows keep the selection colour.
Scale: O(visible rows) per repaint, constant extra work per cell (one Int compare); no allocation (colour from UIUtil is cached by the L&F).
Testing: unit - `hoverBackgroundFor` table (hovered/not/selected/no-table); platform test rendering Author/Date/Description cells for a hovered row and asserting all three backgrounds equal; non-hovered rows equal table.background. Manual: MT-LOG-TABLE (move pointer across columns - whole row highlights; selected row unchanged; dark/light themes; scrolling with the wheel while stationary). Regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-GRAPH (graph renderer touched), MT-DND (drop-row highlight must not be confused with hover - check drag-over visuals).
acceptance_criteria: Hovering any cell highlights the entire row in all columns with the existing hover colour; selection colour unaffected; single hover rule shared with the graph renderer; renderer test + MT-LOG-TABLE row.

1. Verify (30 min): open a project with the oldest persisted state shape you still care about (settingsVersion 0/1/2/3 sample XMLs - craft from git history of JujutsuSettingsState) and assert `loadState` reaches version 4 with expected values: a `JujutsuSettingsMigrationTest` table-driven test (one case per migration v1..v4 plus chain 0->4); add cases for any later migration automatically via a documented rule.
2. Document the rule in contributing.md (already mentions loadState migrations at :134): "every persisted-state shape change bumps settingsVersion and gets a migration test case". 
3. Close the bead with reason "covered by settings migrations v1-v4 + migration test + rule".
Questions for you (decision recorded as Recommendation above):
 Q1: Was there a specific migration intended (e.g. users of an earlier plugin version with different storage - the `.idea/jujutsu.xml` location (jj-idea-44db moves it to workspace.xml: THAT migration is the current real one, see its design), or something else? Recommend: treat 44db as the live migration work.
 Q2: Keep this bead open as a placeholder for future breaking changes? Rec: no - open a bead when a breaking change is actually planned.
How to reverse: reopen the bead and add the specific migration scope.
Scale: none. Manual: none (settings test). Regression scope: MT-SETTINGS only if migration code is touched.

title: Allow user to annotate old revisions
description: Blame/annotate works on the working copy. It should also be able to work for other revisions. Enable this menu option for read-only editors on specific revisions. Ensure that JujutsuFileAnnotation.getCurrentRevision() returns the correct change id.
design:
PLAN: make Annotate correct (and available) for historical revisions; first fix the corruption reported in the 2026-05-17 comment, then enable the menu entry for read-only revision editors.
Facts: JujutsuAnnotationProvider (vcs/annotate/JujutsuAnnotationProvider.kt) has three entry points: `annotate(file)` (:122, working copy / diffbase flow), `annotate(file, revision: VcsFileRevision?)` (:~242, used by the platform's "Annotate Revision" from the annotation popup) which does `annotateInternal(file, revisionId, repo)` with `file` being the CURRENT editor's file, not the file at that revision, and `annotate(path, revision: VcsRevisionNumber)` (:~253, for VcsVirtualFile editors, builds `repo.getVirtualFile(FileAtVersion(path, locator))` correctly). `JujutsuFileAnnotation.getCurrentRevision()` returns only `workingCopyChangeId` (JujutsuFileAnnotation.kt:67) i.e. always the working copy.
Root cause of the comment's symptom (verify with a test first): in `annotate(file, revision)` the content shown in the editor is the working-copy text but the annotation lines are for the file AT the chosen older revision (`jj file annotate -r <rev>`), so the line count differs ("number of lines don't match", corrupted annotations). The platform expects annotations for the content of the editor file, with the annotated revision selection meaning "blame as of that revision, but expressed against the CURRENT lines" (git4idea's annotate-previous-revision re-annotates the file AT that revision and opens it as a read-only VcsVirtualFile / the gutter maps through `UpToDateLineNumberProvider`). For jj the clean model: Annotate Revision = open the revision's content in a VcsVirtualFile editor and annotate THAT (route through the working `annotate(path, revNumber)` overload), never annotate the working-copy file with another revision's data.
Design:
1. Characterise: platform test with a 3-commit history where line counts differ between revisions; call `annotate(file, revision=<older>)`, assert the returned annotation's line count == the document line count of `file`. Expect failure today (reproduces the comment).
2. Fix `annotate(file, revision)`: delegate to the VcsVirtualFile path: `annotate(file.filePath, revisionNumberOf(revision))` so lines match the revision's own content, which the platform then displays (the platform's AnnotateToggleAction "Annotate Revision" opens the revision's file in an editor when the annotation's file differs - confirm in intellij-community `AnnotateRevisionAction`/`AnnotateVcsVirtualFileAction`; if the action instead keeps the original editor, return null/throw UnsupportedOperation and instead supply `getAnnotatedContent()`... the exact platform contract must be read from ../intellij-community vcs-impl `AnnotateRevisionActionBase` before choosing).
3. `JujutsuFileAnnotation.getCurrentRevision()` (JujutsuFileAnnotation.kt:67): store the annotated revision's id in the annotation (constructor param `annotatedRevision: ChangeId` instead of/in addition to `workingCopyChangeId`; for working-copy flow keep `workingCopyChangeId`), return `ChangeIdRevisionNumber(annotatedRevision)` so "current revision" is the revision of the content being annotated - this is the bead's explicit requirement. Use commit ids for the revision number when wiz0 lands (hidden commits).
4. Menu enablement: bead says "enable this menu option for read-only editors on specific revisions" - the platform shows Annotate for a VcsVirtualFile iff `AnnotationProviderEx`/`AnnotationData.extractFrom` recognises it (JujutsuVirtualFile passes a `JujutsuFileRevision` for exactly this, hq4d, JujutsuVirtualFile.kt:~45-51); null for MergeParentOf (merge-parent pseudo-files stay disabled by design). Verify that Annotate appears on a revision opened from the log/file history (jj-idea-76uo closed fixed the Jujutsu submenu there); add a test and a manual row.
5. Immutable/mutable cache: annotations of immutable revisions can be cached forever (CacheableAnnotationProvider, provider's cache cleared on working-copy change :53-56) - keep caching keyed by (path, commitId); don't clear for immutable keys.
Decisions made without the user: Q: Annotate Revision semantics - open the revision's file (git4idea-like) vs annotate current editor "as of" revision? Rec: open the revision's own content (only coherent model; "as of" would need line mapping through diffs = jj-idea-a352 territory). Reverse: disable "Annotate Revision" for jj and ship only the VcsVirtualFile route.
Scale: one `jj file annotate` call per annotate (as today). Testing: platform tests above + unit for getCurrentRevision per flow. Manual: MT-DIFF/annotation rows: annotate WC, then "Annotate Revision" via popup (no warning, lines match), annotate from a historical editor opened from log; regression scope: MT-DIFFBASE (annotate vs diff base), MT-DIFF, MT-LOG-DETAILS (open-file-at-revision).
Related: jj-idea-a352 (annotate context menu actions), jj-idea-nu6d, jj-idea-bia2, jj-idea-wiz0.
acceptance_criteria: Annotate Revision no longer warns about line-count mismatch; annotation lines always match the displayed content; getCurrentRevision returns the annotated revision; Annotate available on historical read-only editors (not merge-parent pseudo-files); platform tests + manual rows.

title: Set up UI integration tests for tree expansion behavior
description:
Set up full UI integration tests for the changes tree expansion behavior.

Current state:
- Unit tests exist for change detection logic (JujutsuTreeExpansionTest)
- Full UI tests need IntelliJ Platform test fixtures

What needs to be done:
1. Enable the full `test` task with proper IntelliJ test fixtures
2. Configure testFramework(TestFrameworkType.Platform) in build.gradle.kts
3. Create integration tests that:
   - Create mock projects with VCS changes
   - Test actual tree expansion/collapse behavior
   - Verify that new files expand parent directories
   - Verify that deleted files don't affect expansion state
   - Test mouse click handling (single click preview, double click diff)
   - Test keyboard shortcuts (Enter, F4)

Benefits:
- Catch UI regressions automatically
- Verify interaction with IntelliJ Platform APIs
- Test real-world scenarios with actual tree components

Related:
- Issue jj-idea-nk3: Run fuller test suite in CI (dependencies needed)
- JujutsuTreeExpansionTest.kt: Existing unit tests for logic
design:
PLAN: the bead's infrastructure premise is obsolete (platform test infrastructure exists: jj-idea-2u2e closed; `@Tag("platform") @TestApplication @RunInEdt` tests with `projectFixture()` run in the `platformTest` task, e.g. ui/workingcopy/UnifiedWorkingCopyPanelBindingTest.kt); what remains is writing the actual expansion/interaction tests for the Working Copy changes tree. Also: the named `JujutsuTreeExpansionTest` no longer exists (grep: only bookmarks-panel tests mention expansion) - the logic now lives in `UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel` (ui/workingcopy/UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt).
Behaviour under test (code facts): after each tree rebuild `invokeAfterRefresh { ignoreExpansionEvents = true; changesTree.treeExpander.expandAll(); reapplyUserCollapses(); ... ignoreExpansionEvents = false }` (:~512-525); user collapses are tracked via a `TreeExpansionListener` (`setupTreeExpansionTracking` :389-412: collapse adds the path identifier to `userCollapsedPaths`, expand removes it, both persist through `PropertiesComponent` under `collapsedPathsKey` = prefix + project location hash, `loadCollapsedPaths`/`saveCollapsedPaths` :550-558) and re-applied by `reapplyUserCollapses()`/`collapseMatchingPaths` (:528-548); programmatic expand/collapse events are ignored while `ignoreExpansionEvents`. `getPathIdentifier(treePath)` builds a path string from node labels.
Tests to write (platform, EDT; build the panel as in UnifiedWorkingCopyPanelBindingTest with stubbed repo/state; feed changes via `panel.updateChangesView(changes)` (public, :~503) and `changesTree.invokeAfterRefresh` waits - use the existing `drainBackgroundLoads()` util and EDT dispatch flush):
 1. New files: update with changes in `a/b/new.txt` -> after refresh ALL ancestor directory nodes are expanded (`changesTree.isExpanded(path)`), including a dir that did not exist before.
 2. User collapse persists across rebuilds: collapse `a/b` via `changesTree.collapsePath` while `ignoreExpansionEvents == false` (wait for the initial refresh to finish), then `updateChangesView` with an added file elsewhere -> `a/b` stays collapsed; siblings expanded; collapse state saved in PropertiesComponent (assert stored string contains the identifier).
 3. Deleted files don't alter expansion: update with a change set minus a file in another dir -> that dir's expansion unchanged for remaining nodes; deleting the only file in `a/b` removes the node and does not leave a stale collapsed marker affecting a NEW `a/b` directory later? (decide expected: collapsed marker persists by identifier -> a re-created `a/b` comes back collapsed; assert current behaviour and document).
 4. Programmatic expansion events are not recorded as user actions: after `updateChangesView`, `userCollapsedPaths` unchanged (assert via persisted property).
 5. Mouse/keyboard (bead's last bullet): single-click -> editor-tab preview (`JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview`, covered by JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreviewTest), double-click -> full diff (`getToggleClickCount() = 2` is for expand/collapse toggling, JujutsuChangesTree.kt:179 - NOTE the bead's "double click diff" vs toggle click count: check what double-click on a FILE node does: platform `ChangesTree` double-click on a leaf triggers `Jujutsu.ShowChangesDiff`/`OpenChangeFile`; test via `changesTree.dispatchEvent(MouseEvent(clickCount=2))` and assert the diff action's `actionPerformed` invocation through a mock `ManagedActions`/ActionManager), Enter -> diff? F4 -> `Jujutsu.OpenChangeFile` (JujutsuChangesTree.kt comment re F4 ownership). Use `ActionManager` test listener (`AnActionListener`) to record invoked action ids.
Decisions made without the user: Q: Do these as headless Swing event tests or real UI robot tests? Rec headless platform tests (dispatch synthetic events) - UI-robot is out of scope. Q: close the infra part? yes - mark obsolete.
Scale: tests only (use ~20-100 changes; plus reuse UnifiedWorkingCopyPanelScaleTest for counts). Acceptance: tests 1-4 (+5 where deterministic) pass in platformTest; manual MT-WORKINGCOPY expansion bullets (if any) reduced.
acceptance_criteria: Platform tests cover tree expansion on new files, persistence of user collapses across rebuilds, deleted-file neutrality, programmatic-vs-user event separation, and key/click action routing; stale infra premise noted.
