title: Remove or replace 'Not in any branch' message in log view details
description:
**Problem:**
The log view details pane (right-hand side) shows "Not in any branch" for all commits. This is incorrect for Jujutsu, which uses bookmarks instead of branches, and the Git concept of "current branch" doesn't apply.

**Current Behavior:**
- Details pane always shows: "Not in any branch"
- Message is misleading since JJ doesn't use Git-style branches

**Expected Behavior:**
Option 1 (Simple): Remove this field entirely
Option 2 (Better): Show bookmark information if the commit has bookmarks:
  - "Bookmarks: main, feature-x" (if commit has bookmarks)
  - Remove the field entirely if no bookmarks (don't show "no bookmarks")

Option 3 (Best): Show working copy indicator:
  - "@ Working Copy" (if this is the working copy commit)
  - "Bookmarks: main, feature-x" (if commit has bookmarks)
  - Remove field if neither applies

**Implementation Notes:**
- JujutsuLogProvider likely provides this through getCurrentBranch() which returns null
- May need to customize the log details panel rendering
- Could provide bookmark info through VcsLogProvider methods

**Related:**
- Issue #30: Display bookmarks as tags in log view
- JujutsuLogEntry has isWorkingCopy property that could be used

**Priority:** MEDIUM - Cosmetic issue but misleading to users
notes:
Requires same custom VCS log UI as jj-idea-rn8.

The 'Not in any branch' message comes from the standard CommitDetailsPanel which cannot be customized independently. Solution requires implementing custom VCS log UI via CustomVcsLogUiFactoryProvider.

Should be implemented together with jj-idea-rn8 since both need custom details pane.

Priority: Lower until custom VCS log UI foundation is built.

title: Show formatted change IDs in log view details pane
description:
**Problem:**
The log view details pane (right-hand side) currently shows the commit ID but not the change ID. When viewing a commit, users need to see the change ID prominently since that's the primary identifier in Jujutsu.

**Current Behavior:**
- Right-hand pane shows "Commit: <hash>" 
- No change ID visible
- No formatting (bold/color) applied to identifiers

**Expected Behavior:**
- Show change ID prominently: "Change: qpvuntsm" with formatting
  - Short prefix ("qp") in bold with highlight color
  - Remainder ("vuntsm") in muted color
- Optionally also show full commit ID below
- Use the same formatting as elsewhere in the UI (JujutsuCommitFormatter)

**Implementation Notes:**
- Likely need to customize the log view details pane rendering
- Apply JujutsuCommitFormatter.format() and toHtml() for consistent styling
- May need to extend VcsLogProvider or customize the details panel

**Priority:** HIGH - Change IDs are the primary way users interact with Jujutsu
notes:
Requires custom VCS log UI implementation.

Finding: Details pane cannot be customized independently. Must implement:
1. CustomVcsLogUiFactoryProvider extension
2. Custom VcsLogUi extending VcsLogUiImpl  
3. Override createMainFrame() to provide custom CommitDetailsPanel
4. Custom panel to display JJ change IDs with formatting

Example: Git plugin's BranchesInGitLogUiFactoryProvider

This is significant work (multiple components). Consider lower priority until other features complete.

title: Push dialog: 'Specific tag' scope for jj git push --tag
description: Follow-up to jj-idea-k9oy: Push Tag is only in the tag context menus. Add a tag scope to GitPushDialog (jj >= 0.44, JjFeature.TAG_PUSH), reusing gitPush(tag=...).
design:
PLAN: add a "Specific tag" scope to GitPushDialog, gated on `JjFeature.TAG_PUSH` (jj >= 0.44), reusing `CommandExecutor.gitPush(tag = ...)` and the dialog's existing scope machinery.
Facts: `GitPushDialog` (actions/git/GitPushDialog.kt, 402 lines) offers scopes via `PushScope` (DEFAULT / specific BOOKMARK / ALL bookmarks / "create bookmark(s) for change(s)" CHANGE; `parsePushScope(settings.state.defaultPushScope)` persisted by name, JujutsuConfigurable.kt:1243; radio binding helper `RadioScopeBinding.kt`), returns `GitPushSpec(repo, remote, bookmark, allBookmarks, changeRevisions)`; the result is executed by `checkAndPush(spec, project, revision)` (gitRemoteActions.kt:162-199: dry-run -> confirm force/delete -> `performPush`) which calls `gitPush(remote, bookmark, allBookmarks, changeRevisions, revision, dryRun, tag)` - the executor ALREADY accepts `tag: Tag?` (CommandExecutor.kt:425-433) and `pushTagAction` (actions/tag/pushTagAction.kt) pushes a single tag from tag context menus with a confirmation (no dry-run: "jj tracks a tag automatically on first push").
Design:
1. Scope: add `PushScope.TAG` (name "TAG" persisted if chosen as default? Exclude from the default-scope setting UI: default stays among the existing ones; `parsePushScope` falls back to DEFAULT for unknown names so adding an enum constant is backward compatible) with a tag combo (`ComboBox<Tag>` filled from `project.stateModel.references.value[repo].tags` - loaded already by the state model; the dialog is constructed with preloaded data per its KDoc ("must be loaded off EDT"): extend `DialogData` with `tags: List<Tag>` in `loadDialogData` (one extra cheap read from the state model, no jj call)).
2. Gating: radio row shown always; DISABLED with the reason when `!JjFeature.TAG_PUSH.isSupportedIn(project)` (visible-but-disabled convention; `disabledReasonIn(project)` text as the tooltip); hidden when the repo has no tags? Rec: disabled with "No tags" reason rather than hidden (discoverability).
3. Spec: `GitPushSpec.tag: Tag? = null` (default keeps constructors valid); `checkAndPush`: when `spec.tag != null` skip bookmark-specific dry-run parsing paths? The dry-run (`--dry-run --tag X`) works with tags in 0.44 (verify format: tag lines in the bracketed output `tag: v1 [add to ...]` from jj-idea-spwt's parser - extend the dry-run plan parser with tag actions; until then treat dry-run output as informational: force-push detection for tags (moving an existing remote tag) matters: jj refuses non-fast-forward tag moves? verify) and then `performPush(spec,...)` passes `tag = spec.tag`.
4. Per-remote: tags push to ONE remote chosen in the dialog's remote selector (as for bookmarks) - same as pushTagAction's per-remote submenu.
5. Keep pushTagAction (context menus) - it can reuse `performPush`/`checkAndPush` later (one push path) - optional follow-up.
Decisions made without the user: Q: include in `defaultPushScope` options? Rec no. Q: multi-tag push? Rec no (`--tag` repeatable, but UI = specific tag; keep simple v1).
Scale: O(#tags) combo population (tags from state). Testing: dialog tests (scope enabled/disabled by feature; tag combo contents; spec carries tag), `checkAndPush` test with a stub executor asserting `gitPush(tag=...)` for the TAG scope, bundle keys; contract test (jj >= 0.44) push a tag to a local bare remote via the dialog's spec path; manual: MT-GIT (dialog TAG scope pushes the tag; old-jj disabled state with reason). Regression scope: MT-GIT, MT-BOOKMARK (pushBookmark uses the dialog).
acceptance_criteria: Push dialog has a feature-gated 'Specific tag' scope that pushes via gitPush(tag=...); disabled with reason on old jj/no tags; tests + MT-GIT rows.

title: Annotate: commit-number column placement (GitHub #134)
description:
Reporter (SergejSalnikov) asks for the 'Commit number' column in the annotation gutter to come first, as it is hard to parse right after the date/time. That column is the platform's HistoryIdColumn, appended after all getAspects() columns (AnnotateToggleAction.java:264-274) - same for the Git plugin - so the plugin cannot reorder it. Our ChangeIdAspect is already first (JujutsuFileAnnotation.kt getAspects). Option if wanted: provide our own numbered aspect first. Backlog pending reporter reply.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/134
design:
PLAN: the platform's "Commit number" (HistoryIdColumn) can't be moved; offer our OWN leading numbered aspect only if the reporter still wants it; otherwise close.
Facts: `JujutsuFileAnnotation.getAspects()` returns `[ChangeIdAspect, AuthorAspect, AuthorInstantAspect, DescriptionAspect]` (vcs/annotate/JujutsuFileAnnotation.kt:56-61 - the change id is ALREADY first among OUR aspects); the platform's `AnnotateToggleAction` appends its own `HistoryIdColumn` ("Commit number") AFTER all `getAspects()` columns (AnnotateToggleAction.java:264-274, per the bead; same for Git) and shows it only when `FileAnnotation.getRevisionsOrderProvider()`/`getRevisions()` give ordering (we implement `getRevisionsOrderProvider` by timestamp at :~80-85) - so the reporter's "Commit number column" is the platform column, numbering revisions by age order. Since it is platform-owned we cannot reorder it (the bead's conclusion).
Options: (1) CLOSE: the column is a platform feature common to all VCS plugins; document in contributing.md ("annotation columns: platform appends commit number"); (2) own numbered aspect FIRST: add `CommitNumberAspect` as the first element of `getAspects()` showing the same number the platform column would (rank of the line's revision in `getRevisionsOrderProvider()` order: 1 = oldest) and suppress the platform one by returning an empty/`null` `getRevisionsOrderProvider()` (the platform column appears only when the provider yields numbers) - but that provider also drives "Annotate Previous Revision"/"Show Diff" behaviours? (it is used for the revision-ordering column and for `AnnotationGutterLineConvertor`'s revision colour grouping `getRevisionsOrderProvider` -> colour scheme? verify in platform: `AnnotateToggleAction`: `if (annotation.getRevisionsOrderProvider() != null) add HistoryIdColumn`; colour ranking uses `getRevisions()` separately) - verify before relying on it.
Recommendation: (1) unless the reporter replies that they still want it (the bead is "Backlog pending reporter reply"); if (2) is wanted it depends on the spike jj-idea-i7jd (custom gutter rendering, designed) only if richer rendering is also desired; for just reordering a number, (2) needs no spike: it is a plain `LineAnnotationAspect` (platform API) whose `getValue(line)` returns the number string and `getId()` unique. Cost: small; risk: duplicate number columns if the platform one can't be suppressed (then keep both? no - hide ours by setting).
Decisions made without the user: Q: act now? Rec no - wait for the reporter (GitHub #134). If the reporter confirms: implement (2) with a setting "Show commit number first" (default on) that swaps `getRevisionsOrderProvider()` to null to avoid the duplicate, after verifying platform behaviour with a runIde experiment.
Scale: O(distinct revisions) once per annotation (sort by timestamp, already done for `getRevisionsOrderProvider`). Testing (if built): aspect value tests (numbering stable with ties by timestamp then id), `getAspects` order test, provider-null test; manual: MT-DIFF annotation rows (column order: number, change id, author, date, description; no duplicate number column). Regression scope: MT-DIFF, MT-DIFFBASE.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded: close (platform column) or implement own leading commit-number aspect with platform column suppressed after reporter confirmation.
close_reason: Reporter withdrew on GH #134 after the explanation (platform-owned HistoryIdColumn; ChangeIdAspect already first). Draft reply proposes closing the GitHub issue.

title: Select All in the commit details pane doesn't highlight chips or the author/date line (copy includes them)
description: AtomicHtmlView.modelToView returns a zero-width point for each atomic unit, so the selection highlight paints nothing over bookmark/tag chips or the author/date line, although copy now includes their text (jj-idea-5zio). Ordinary link text (issue references in descriptions) highlights fine. Unchanged by jj-idea-3as8. Fix: report the chip's real painted extent from modelToView/viewToModel (note the hit-testing/hover code in IconAwareHtmlPane relies on the zero-width behaviour - see the comment near hoveredChipElement).
design:
PLAN: make `AtomicHtmlView` report its real painted extent from `modelToView`/`viewToModel` so Swing's selection highlight paints over chips and the author/date line, without breaking the pane's own hit-testing which relies on the zero-width behaviour.
Facts: `AtomicHtmlView.modelToView(pos, a, b)` (ui/components/AtomicHtmlView.kt:212-224) returns a ZERO-width rectangle at the unit's start (shifted by `leadingGap`) or end (`r.width = 0`), and `viewToModel` (:226-235) maps the left half of the allocation to `startOffset` and the right half to `endOffset`; `IconLeafView` (:~285-310) has the same pattern. The selection highlighter (`DefaultHighlighter.LayeredHighlightPainter` -> `View.modelToView(p0, Bias.Forward, p1, Bias.Backward, shape)` -> union of the two returned shapes) therefore paints an empty rectangle for a one-position atomic element. Hit-testing consumers depend on the current mapping: `IconAwareHtmlPane.characterOffsetAt(point)` (IconAwareHtmlPane.kt:279-282) reads `viewToModel2D` + the returned `Position.Bias` (Backward => the chip ending here: `offset - 1`), `issueLinkUriAt` (:204 `modelToView2D(elem.startOffset)` left edge as the origin for `hrefAtContentX`), hover (`hoveredChipElement`, :129-135 - the comment near :134 warns "AtomicHtmlView.modelToView reports a zero-width point, not its real bounds"), right-click `refUriAt`.
Design - fix at the SELECTION level, not by changing the shared mapping contract:
Option 1 (recommended): implement the multi-position overload that the highlighter actually calls: override `View.modelToView(p0: Int, b0: Bias, p1: Int, b1: Bias, a: Shape): Shape` in `AtomicHtmlView`/`IconLeafView` (and keep the single-position `modelToView` zero-width for caret + hit-testing): when `p0 == startOffset && p1 == endOffset` (the unit is fully inside the selection) return the real painted rectangle (`allocation` minus nothing: the unit's own bounds `a.bounds` with x shifted by `leadingGap` and width = content width `pieces.sumOf{width}`); when only a part is selected (caret inside a one-position unit cannot happen: p0/p1 are start/end) fall back to the zero-width shape. This leaves `viewToModel` and the single-offset `modelToView` untouched so hover/click code is unaffected.
Option 2 (rejected): return the real extent from single-offset `modelToView` - would change caret geometry and break the offset arithmetic documented in `IconAwareHtmlPane.characterOffsetAt` and `issueLinkUriAt` (left edge origin assumption).
Verify first: confirm which `modelToView` overload `LayeredHighlightPainter` calls in the target platform's JDK (JBR 21): `javax.swing.text.DefaultHighlighter.LayeredHighlightPainter.paintLayer` calls `view.modelToView(p0, Position.Bias.Forward, p1, Position.Bias.Backward, shape)` for multi-view ranges, and for a single `View` spanning the range it calls that same 5-arg method on the PARENT view (the paragraph/inline view), which then delegates to children by positions: for a range covering a whole atomic child, `CompositeView/ParagraphView.modelToView(p0,b0,p1,b1,a)` computes the union via child `modelToView` (single-offset) calls for the start/end - which yields zero width. So the override must be on the CHILD in a way the parent calls: parent calls `child.modelToView(pos, a, b)` single-offset for p0 and p1 and unions; if both are the same unit's start and end (distinct positions startOffset vs endOffset) the union of (startX, 0 width) and (endX, 0 width) = the real width - which would already highlight!... yet the bead observes nothing painted: because within a ParagraphView/InlineView layout the highlighter's range for ONE element covers [start,end) and `modelToView(start)` and `modelToView(end)` come back with the SAME x only if `endOffset` branch `r.x += r.width` is applied - it IS applied for `pos == endOffset` (line ~220-221), so the union should be non-empty... Therefore step 0 of this fix is a 30-minute DIAGNOSTIC: log the shapes `LayeredHighlightPainter` receives for a selected chip (use a debug `ComponentUI`/subclass `DefaultHighlighter.DefaultHighlightPainter` override `paintLayer` printing the shape) before changing code - the cause may instead be that the highlight is painted BEFORE (under) the opaque custom `paint` of AtomicHtmlView (view paints text/icons over its own background?) or that selection of whole-unit ranges isn't registered as `p1` beyond `endOffset` (range end is exclusive: p1 == endOffset of the LAST unit leaves its `Bias.Backward` mapping at `endOffset` -> `r.x += r.width` then width=0 -> union start..end non-empty only when p0=startOffset... decide from the diagnostic). Possible actual fix: in `paint`, draw the selection background yourself: `if (container is JTextComponent && selection covers [startOffset,endOffset)) { g.color = selectionColor; g.fillRect(rect...) }` using `container.selectionStart/End` + `container.selectionColor` before painting the pieces, and paint text pieces with `selectedTextColor`. This is robust regardless of highlighter geometry and independent of hit-testing; Rec as the implementation if the diagnostic confirms the highlighter yields nothing.
Decisions made without the user: Q: approach (own selection painting vs mapping)? Rec own selection painting in `paint` (zero impact on hit-testing); fall back to Option 1 only if the diagnostic shows the highlighter gets the right shapes and just paints under our content.
Scale: O(1) per painted unit. Testing: platform test using `IconAwareHtmlPaneChipHoverTest`-style harness: render a pane with a chip, `selectAll()`, paint to BufferedImage and assert selection-colour pixels inside the chip's bounds (same pixel-assertion technique as IconZoomRenderingTest, with real icons via IconLoader.activate()); regression tests: existing IconAwareHtmlPane hover/hit/refUriAt tests must pass unchanged; copy text unchanged (jj-idea-5zio). Manual: MT-LOG-DETAILS (Select All: chips and author/date highlighted; partial drag selection through a chip; dark/light; copy contents unchanged; hover/right-click on chips still work). Regression scope: MT-LOG-DETAILS, MT-LOG-TABLE (tooltips share the pane), MT-BOOKMARK.
acceptance_criteria: Select All highlights chips and the author/date line in the details pane; hover, right-click and issue-link hit-testing unchanged; copy unchanged; pixel test; diagnostic findings recorded.

title: Commit details pane doesn't auto-scroll when drag-selecting past its edge
description: Dragging to select text in the details pane (IconAwareHtmlPane in JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel) past the visible edge doesn't scroll, so text further down can't be selected by dragging (Select All works). Pre-existing; noticed during jj-idea-5zio manual testing. Likely needs Autoscroller / JComponent.setAutoscrolls(true) on the pane.
design:
PLAN: enable drag-selection autoscroll for the details pane.
Facts: the details pane is `metadataPane = IconAwareHtmlPane(project)` (ui/log/JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt:79) inside `metadataPanel` (BorderLayout) hosted in a scroll pane/splitter; Swing's drag-selection autoscroll works when (a) the component's `autoscrolls` property is true so `BasicCaret`/`BasicTextUI` mouse-drag handlers call `scrollRectToVisible` through `JComponent.processMouseMotionEvent` ("if (autoscrolls && e.getID() == MOUSE_DRAGGED) { scrollRectToVisible(new Rectangle(e.getX(), e.getY(), 1, 1)) }" - the `JComponent.autoscrolls` mechanism uses a Timer for the synthetic mouse-drag events outside the viewport), and (b) the component is inside a `JViewport` whose view is that component (so `scrollRectToVisible` propagates). For `JEditorPane` the default `autoscrolls` is TRUE in `JTextComponent`'s constructor? (`JTextComponent` calls `setAutoscrolls(true)` in its constructor in JDK; but `IconAwareHtmlPane` extends JBHtmlPane which may disable it, or the pane's PARENT is not a viewport (the pane may be wrapped in a panel inside the scroll pane: `scrollRectToVisible` then bubbles up to the panel -> viewport OK) - verify with a quick experiment before changing).
Steps:
 1. Diagnostic (15 min): in runIde, select text in the pane dragging below the edge; check `metadataPane.autoscrolls`, the parent chain (`SwingUtilities.getAncestorOfClass(JViewport)`), and whether `Scrollable` size hints (getScrollableTracksViewportHeight == true would make the pane always exactly viewport height - then it never scrolls internally and the OUTER scroll container (if any) is where scrolling must occur).
 2. Fix candidates: (a) `metadataPane.autoscrolls = true` (+ ensure the pane is the viewport view or `metadataPanel` is in a `ScrollPaneFactory.createScrollPane(metadataPanel)` - code probably already); (b) if JBHtmlPane overrides `scrollRectToVisible` or the surrounding `JBScrollPane` has `setWheelScrollingEnabled` quirks: install the platform's `com.intellij.util.ui.UIUtil.addAutoScroller`-like helper or `SmoothAutoScroller`/`Autoscroller` (java.swing.Autoscroller is package-private; IntelliJ offers `com.intellij.ide.dnd.SmoothAutoScroller` for DnD only, not text selection); (c) last resort: a `MouseMotionListener` on the pane that, on `mouseDragged` with `e.y` outside `visibleRect`, calls `scrollRectToVisible(Rectangle(e.x, e.y, 1, 1))` plus a Swing `Timer` (40ms) to keep scrolling while the button is held and the pointer is outside, stopping on mouseReleased - small self-contained helper `DragAutoScroller` (ui/components/).
 3. Same defect probably exists in other `IconAwareHtmlPane` hosts (tooltips n/a; dialogs' source panels); apply the fix in `IconAwareHtmlPane`'s init rather than per host if (a)/(c) work generically.
Decisions made without the user: none. Scale: none. Testing: headless test constructing the pane inside a `JBScrollPane` sized small with long content, dispatching MOUSE_PRESSED at top then MOUSE_DRAGGED events with y beyond the viewport bottom (via `dispatchEvent` + timer tick pumping through `UIUtil.dispatchAllInvocationEvents`) and asserting `viewport.viewPosition.y` increased and `selectionEnd` grew; manual: MT-LOG-DETAILS (drag-select past bottom/top edges of a long multi-commit selection; scroll speed reasonable; no regression to chip hover/right-click). Regression scope: MT-LOG-DETAILS.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging a text selection past the details pane's edge autoscrolls and extends the selection; no regressions to hover/click; headless drag test; MT-LOG-DETAILS row.

title: Row tooltip dismisses on any key press and on drag from its corners, so its text is hard to select/copy
description: IconAwareTooltip (jj-idea-wp12): selecting tooltip text from the top-left or bottom-right corner closes it (IdeTooltipManager's pointer-vector heuristic), and pressing any key (e.g. Cmd+A) closes it. Cmd+C after a mid-tooltip mouse selection does copy (including chip text) and then the tooltip closes. Consider sparing the tooltip while a selection exists, or on Cmd/Ctrl+A/C. Pre-existing; found during jj-idea-5zio manual testing.
design:
PLAN: stop the row tooltip from dismissing while the user is interacting with its text (selection/copy) - make auto-hide conditional on "no selection and no modifier-copy shortcut".
Facts: tooltips come from `installIconAwareTooltip(owner, ...)` (ui/components/IconAwareTooltip.kt) which installs a custom `IdeTooltip` through `IdeTooltipManager.setCustomTooltip` (:90-98); auto-hide gating is `tooltipShouldAutohide(event: TooltipEvent): Boolean = !event.isIsEventInsideBalloon` (:116-123, mirrors `TooltipWithClickableLinks`: spare while the pointer is inside/moving toward the balloon) and the platform's own heuristics hide it on key presses and on the "pointer-vector" test when a drag starts at a corner (IdeTooltipManager's pointer-vector heuristic - the bead's observation). The pane inside the tooltip is `IconAwareHtmlPane` (selectable text, copy handler `IconAwareHtmlPaneCopyWiringTest`).
Design:
1. Selection-aware auto-hide: extend `tooltipShouldAutohide(event)` to also return false while the tooltip pane has a non-empty selection (`pane.selectionStart != pane.selectionEnd`) OR a mouse button is held down inside the balloon (`pane.isMouseDown`): track via a small `MouseListener` on the pane (pressed/released) and `CaretListener`. The function currently takes only `TooltipEvent` (a seam for tests): add a second parameter `interaction: TooltipInteraction` (`hasSelection`, `mouseDown`) provided by the tooltip instance holding the pane reference.
2. Key presses: `IdeTooltipManager` hides on `KeyEvent` (via `IdeEventQueue` dispatcher -> `hideCurrent`)? Verify which path (`IdeTooltipManager.eventDispatcher`: `onKeyEvent`?). If the manager exposes `IdeTooltip.canAutohideOn(TooltipEvent)` for key events (TooltipEvent wraps the InputEvent: `event.inputEvent is KeyEvent`), then returning false when the key is Cmd/Ctrl+C/A (or while a selection exists) keeps it open; our override `canAutohideOn` (protected on IdeTooltip, reachable in our subclass inside IconAwareTooltip.kt) delegates to the extracted function: pass `event.inputEvent` into the function (extend `TooltipEvent` seam with `isKeyEvent`/`keyCode`/`modifiers`).
3. Policy: Cmd/Ctrl+A and Cmd/Ctrl+C never hide it; Escape always hides (explicit dismiss); any other key hides unless a selection exists. After Cmd+C with a selection, hide shortly after (the bead: "copy then closes" is acceptable) - keep current behaviour for that.
4. Corner-drag case (pointer-vector heuristic): when mouse is pressed inside the balloon the manager's `isEventInsideBalloon` is true so autohide is refused already; the failure is the press at the exact corner being judged outside by the heuristic: add `mouseDown` check to force false while pressed anywhere within `pane.bounds` expanded by 2px.
Decisions made without the user: Q: spare while selection exists even for other keys? Rec yes (the bead's suggestion). Reverse: Esc/any-key always hides.
Scale: none. Testing: `tooltipShouldAutohide` table tests (inside balloon, selection, mouseDown, Esc, Cmd+A, Cmd+C, plain key) extending IconAwareTooltipBehaviourTest; manual: MT-LOG-TABLE (hover a row until the tooltip shows, move into it, drag-select from the top-left/bottom-right corners, Cmd+A, Cmd+C -> pastes full text incl. chips; Esc closes; moving away closes). Regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-BOOKMARK (panel tooltips share the installer).
acceptance_criteria: Row tooltip stays open while text is selected or mouse is down, and for Cmd/Ctrl+A/C; Esc still closes; extracted-function tests; MT-LOG-TABLE row.

title: Show exact moved-commit count in the drag chip, not just a fixed scope badge
description: jj-idea-d3u5 added a fixed tree/branch icon to the drag chip when the drag scope is -s/-b (ui/log/JujutsuLogTableDnD.kt's dragImage/dragScopeBadge), deliberately deferring the exact count shown in the drop tooltip (sourceScopeLabel) since computing it needs the same RebaseSimulator.excludedDestinationIds pass DragContext.forDrag already pays for once per gesture - duplicating that just for the drag chip wasn't worth it in the same PR. This bead: thread the moved count (or the already-built DragContext) into setImageProvider so the chip can say e.g. '+3 descendants' or the branch name, matching the tooltip.
design:
PLAN: pass the per-gesture `DragContext` (already computed once) into the drag-image provider and show the exact moved count/branch in the chip.
Facts: `dragImage(payload, scopeBadge)` (ui/log/JujutsuLogTableDnD.kt:411-461) builds the chip: `scopeBadge` icon (`dragScopeBadge()`: tree icon for SOURCE `-s`, branch icon for BRANCH `-b`, none for `-r`, :464-469) + the commit summary or "N commits"; the platform asks for the image via `setImageProvider { info -> dragPayloadAt(info.point)?.let { dragImage(it) } }` (:~129-133) BEFORE/around drag start, and `DragContextHolder.forPayload(payload, sourceMode, onNewContext, allEntries)` memoises a `DragContext` per payload identity (ui/dnd/DragContextHolder.kt:22-50; `DragContext.forDrag(allEntries, payload, sourceMode)` runs `RebaseSimulator.excludedDestinationIds`, the expensive pass, once per gesture). The drop tooltip's `sourceScopeLabel` already prints the exact count from that context (bead text).
Design:
1. `setImageProvider` receives the holder: `.setImageProvider { info -> dragPayloadAt(info.point)?.let { payload -> dragImage(payload, dragContextHolder.peek(payload)) } }` where `peek(payload)` returns the memoised context only if it exists (cheap) else null, so the image NEVER triggers the expensive pass itself. The image is requested at drag start; at that moment the context may not exist yet (it is created lazily by the first `targetChecker` tick). Options: (a) compute the context eagerly in `setBeanProvider` (drag start) - `forPayload(...)` there is one pass per gesture, the same cost the first targetChecker tick would pay moments later (so no extra cost, just earlier) - then the image provider can read it; the bean provider is invoked once per drag start (:123-134). Rec (a).
2. Chip text: for SOURCE/BRANCH modes with moved count k > 1: `"+<k-1> descendants"` (SOURCE) or the branch size `"branch (k commits)"` (BRANCH) next to the badge; REVISION mode unchanged. Count = `context.movedIds.size` (check the field name on `DragContext`: sourceIds/movedIds from `collectMovedIds`, ui/rebase/RebaseSimulator.kt:70).
3. Edge: platform may call the image provider more than once during a drag (pointer moves/DnDImage refresh): memoised context makes repeated calls O(1).
Decisions made without the user: Q: wording? Rec "+3 descendants" / "branch (5 commits)" matching `sourceScopeLabel` strings (reuse the same bundle keys so tooltip and chip agree). Q: eager context at drag start? Rec yes.
Scale: no additional passes (same single `forDrag` per gesture, moved earlier); chip rendering O(1). Operation-count test: N image requests during one gesture => `DragContext.forDrag` called once (extend DragContextHolderScaleTest). Testing: `dragImage` test with a stub context (count text for -s/-b, unchanged for -r, multi-commit payload); manual: MT-DND (set scope to -s/-b; chip shows count; matches the drop tooltip). Regression scope: MT-DND.
acceptance_criteria: Drag chip shows exact moved count/branch size for -s/-b scopes using the memoised DragContext (no extra simulator pass); text matches the drop tooltip; operation-count test; MT-DND row.

title: Distinctive folder icons: Tags bunch + Unbookmarked heads
description:
The 'Tags' and 'Unbookmarked heads' categories currently render with the same generic AllIcons.Nodes.Folder icon as every other bookmarks-panel folder (Local, each remote). Give each something kind-specific.

Deferred from jj-idea-uyu9's tooltip redesign (2026-09-23), alongside jj-idea-emnu (per-remote icon) - linked here, not merged into one bead, since this one is a much smaller, independent scope (static icon swaps, no new colour-assignment infrastructure).

Tags folder - two options, left as a design call:
1. Zero-asset: reuse the platform's com.intellij.icons.AllIcons.Nodes.Tag (singular tag glyph, already the icon used for individual tag chips elsewhere in this codebase) instead of the folder icon. Ships immediately, not literally a 'bunch'.
2. Custom icons/tagGroup.svg (e.g. two overlapping tag shapes) + a new JujutsuIcons entry, closer to a literal 'bunch of tags' look but more asset work for a cosmetic nicety.

Unbookmarked heads folder (added 2026-09-23, user follow-up feedback): give this category its own folder icon too, distinguishing it from Local/a remote/Tags. The row-level leaves already got JujutsuIcons.BookmarkNone (the slashed-bookmark glyph, matching the log table's own dangling-head marker in JujutsuLogTableRenderers.appendDanglingHeadMarker) as of this same follow-up - the open question here is specifically the *folder* icon for the category header itself, not its children. Candidate: a folder-shaped variant carrying the same slash motif, or simply keep AllIcons.Nodes.Folder for this one specifically if a bespoke folder+slash glyph looks too busy - human call.

Wire into JujutsuBookmarksPanel.BookmarkNodeRenderer's WithRefKind branch (icon = AllIcons.Nodes.Folder today, gated on refKind==RefKind.TAG for the tags case) and the isDanglingHeadsGroup branch (BookmarkNode.Category.isDanglingHeadsGroup) for the unbookmarked-heads case, plus BookmarkNodeTooltip.kt's appendGroupBracket / the isDanglingHeadsGroup branch in bookmarkNodeTooltip.
design:
PLAN (design calls pre-answered; static icon swaps, no new infrastructure): kind-specific folder icons for the 'Tags' and 'Unbookmarked heads' categories in the bookmarks panel and tooltip.
Facts: category rendering = `BookmarkNodeRenderer`'s `is BookmarkNode.WithRefKind` branch (ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:~633-645: `icon = AllIcons.Nodes.Folder` for every Category/Prefix); category identity: `BookmarkNode.Category(repo, displayName, refKind: RefKind, children, rollup, isDanglingHeadsGroup)` (ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkTreeModel.kt:~120-139; `RefKind` BOOKMARK/TAG, `isDanglingHeadsGroup` flag); tooltip group bracket `appendGroupBracket` + `isDanglingHeadsGroup` branch in `bookmarkNodeTooltip` (ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkNodeTooltip.kt). Existing glyphs: `JujutsuIcons.BookmarkNone` (slashed bookmark - used on dangling-head LEAVES and the log's dangling marker), `AllIcons.Nodes.Tag` (used for individual tag chips elsewhere in the codebase - verify in JujutsuIcons/LogEntryText `appendTagChip` which icon it uses: `JujutsuIcons.Tag`, icons/tag.svg exists), `AllIcons.Nodes.Folder`.
Recommendation (answers the bead's design calls):
 - Tags category: use the plugin's own `JujutsuIcons.Tag` (icons/tag.svg, the same glyph tag CHIPS use) - zero new assets, consistent colour (tag colour `RefKind.TAG.color`); a literal 'bunch' glyph (tagGroup.svg) is cosmetic polish: skip unless you want art.
 - Unbookmarked heads category: use `JujutsuIcons.BookmarkNone` (slashed bookmark) - already the glyph for its leaves and the log marker, so the category header and its children read as one concept; a folder+slash hybrid is busier and needs custom art - skip. If you prefer the folder metaphor retained for structure (all categories being folders), keep `AllIcons.Nodes.Folder` for Local/remotes and use the specific glyphs only for these two (that is the recommendation: Local = folder, each remote = remote icon (jj-idea-emnu), Tags = tag, Unbookmarked heads = slashed bookmark).
Wiring: in the Category branch: `icon = when { node.isDanglingHeadsGroup -> JujutsuIcons.BookmarkNone; node.refKind == RefKind.TAG -> JujutsuIcons.Tag; else -> AllIcons.Nodes.Folder }` (Prefix nodes under Tags keep the plain folder: only the top-level Category gets the glyph); the same `when` in `appendGroupBracket` (extract `categoryIconFor(node)` into one function used by both sites + emnu's remote case - coordinate: whichever of p1p7/emnu lands first introduces `categoryIconFor`). Colour: the glyphs are already themed via JujutsuIcons recolouring; the tag icon takes the tag colour automatically? (check `JujutsuIcons.Tag` accent) - match the existing chip colours.
Decisions made without the user: Q1 Tags icon: plugin tag glyph (zero-asset). Q2 Unbookmarked heads: slashed bookmark. Reverse: swap the `when` branches. 
Scale: none. Testing: pure function test for `categoryIconFor` (dangling -> BookmarkNone, TAG -> Tag, remote/local -> folder; prefix nodes -> folder); renderer smoke test (icon identity); manual: MT-BOOKMARK (panel + tooltip show the glyphs; light/dark). Regression scope: MT-BOOKMARK.
acceptance_criteria: Tags category uses the tag glyph and Unbookmarked heads the slashed-bookmark glyph in panel and tooltip via one shared icon function; tests + MT-BOOKMARK row.

title: Per-remote icon in the bookmarks panel + tooltip
description:
Give each remote category (origin, github, etc.) a distinct, stably-recolored icon in both the bookmarks-panel tree and its hover tooltip, mirroring RepositoryIcons/RepositoryColors (ui/common/RepositoryIcons.kt, ui/log/RepositoryColors.kt) but keyed by remote name instead of repo directory path.

Deferred from jj-idea-uyu9's tooltip redesign (2026-09-23): the platform has no usable 'remote' icon (checked AllIcons.* and git4idea's DvcsImplIcons - neither has a generic remote/cloud glyph), so this needs a new custom SVG.

Design sketch:
- New icons/remote.svg in the repo.svg mould: fixed chrome in .primary/.contrast-fill classes, a tintable core in .accent/.accent-fill (repo.svg's own network-dots motif could be adapted, or a small cloud/antenna shape - human call on the actual art).
- New JujutsuIcons.Remote = strokeIcon/strokeFillIcon("/icons/remote.svg", ...) alongside the other JujutsuIcons entries.
- New RemoteIcons/RemoteColors pair (ui/common/ or ui/log/), keyed by remote name (String) rather than a repo path. Suggest a hash-based stable index (remote ordering is already deterministic/sorted in BookmarkTreeModel.buildRepoNodes) rather than RepositoryColors' session-order round-robin, since a remote name doesn't change across rebuilds the way first-seen order can.
- Wire into JujutsuBookmarksPanel.BookmarkNodeRenderer's WithRefKind branch (currently AllIcons.Nodes.Folder for every Category/Prefix regardless of kind) and into BookmarkNodeTooltip.kt's appendGroupBracket (currently also AllIcons.Nodes.Folder unconditionally).
design:
PLAN: distinct, stably-coloured per-remote icon in the bookmarks panel and its tooltip; new `remote.svg` + a `RemoteIcons/RemoteColors` pair keyed by remote NAME with a hash-based stable colour index (the bead's own sketch is sound; this makes it executable).
Facts: remote Category nodes render with `AllIcons.Nodes.Folder` regardless of kind (`BookmarkNodeRenderer` WithRefKind branch, ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:~633-645 `icon = AllIcons.Nodes.Folder`) and the tooltip's group bracket (`appendGroupBracket`, ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkNodeTooltip.kt, per the bead) also uses the folder icon; repos already get a coloured icon via `RepositoryIcons[repo]` (ui/common/RepositoryIcons.kt: path-keyed cache of `icon(JujutsuIcons::Repo).copy(fillColor = RepositoryColors.getColor(repo))`) and `RepositoryColors` (ui/log/RepositoryColors.kt: palette + round-robin by first-seen order + `getColorForIndex`). Remote categories are produced in sorted order (BookmarkTreeModel.buildRepoNodes remoteNames sorted, :~315-320) and the pseudo-remote `git` is hidden (j0zv). Existing icon recolouring: `JujutsuIcons.strokeIcon/fillIcon/strokeFillIcon` (ui/common/JujutsuIcons.kt:51-76), SVG class convention (.primary/.contrast-fill/.accent/.accent-fill per repo.svg).
Design:
1. Art: `icons/remote.svg` (16x16; not a platform glyph - bead checked AllIcons and DvcsImplIcons): a small cloud (or server-tower) outline in `.primary` with a tintable core dot cluster in `.accent-fill` (like repo.svg's network-dots motif; I can author a first draft of the SVG for your review). `JujutsuIcons.Remote = strokeFillIcon("/icons/remote.svg", ...)`.
2. `RemoteColors.getColor(name: String): JBColor` = `RepositoryColors.getColorForIndex(stableIndex(name))` with `stableIndex = (name.lowercase().hashCode() and Int.MAX_VALUE) % PALETTE_SIZE` so the same remote name always gets the same colour across sessions/projects (RepositoryColors' first-seen order is session-dependent); special-case common names for recognisability? `origin` fixed to palette[0] (blue), `upstream` palette[1] - small override map; others hashed (collisions acceptable; two remotes in one repo colliding is possible - detect within a rebuild and bump the later one to the next free index: deterministic because remotes are sorted).
3. `RemoteIcons[name]`: cache `ConcurrentHashMap<String, Icon>` keyed by lowercase name (application object -> NOT keyed by repo/project: avoids the LeakHunter issue documented at RepositoryIcons.kt:11-16), resolved via `IconResolver.resolveIcon(icon(JujutsuIcons::Remote).copy(fillColor = color).qualified)` like RepositoryIcons.
4. Wiring: panel renderer Category branch: `icon = if (node.refKind == REMOTE) RemoteIcons[node.displayName] else AllIcons.Nodes.Folder` (needs a distinction between Local/Tags/remote categories: `BookmarkNode.Category` has `refKind`? Local vs remote category: add `isRemote: Boolean`/`remoteName: String?` to Category (BookmarkTreeModel.kt:~120-139) set at construction (:~328)); tooltip `appendGroupBracket` uses the same lookup. Local/Tags categories keep folder (see jj-idea-p1p7 for their distinctive icons - coordinate: same renderer branch).
5. Accessibility/contrast: colours must be distinguishable in dark/light (reuse the vetted RepositoryColors palette: JujutsuColorsContrastTest exists).
Decisions made without the user: Q: who draws the SVG? Rec: I draft, you adjust. Q: hash vs round-robin? Rec hash (stable across sessions) + collision bump.
Scale: O(1) per render with cache. Testing: `RemoteColors` determinism tests (same name -> same colour; sorted collision bump; origin/upstream fixed), `RemoteIcons` cache test (no Project keys), renderer test (remote category icon != folder; local/tags unchanged), resource test; manual: MT-BOOKMARK (multi-remote repo: each remote category has its own coloured icon matching the tooltip; light/dark/zoom). Regression scope: MT-BOOKMARK.
acceptance_criteria: Remote categories show a distinct stably-coloured remote icon in panel and tooltip (hash-based, no Project keys); art reviewed; tests + MT-BOOKMARK row.

title: JJ directory mapping drop may persist across restart (jj-idea-3zk1 follow-up)
description: jj-idea-3zk1 fixed in-session recovery when the platform's ModuleVcsDetector drops a JJ VcsDirectoryMapping during the post-cache-load workspace resync. But if that drop also persists to vcs.xml, the project has no JJ mapping at all from the start of the *next* open, before JujutsuVcsRootRecovery's in-memory knownJujutsuRootPaths has ever seen it - so the in-session self-heal can't help. Needs investigation: does the drop actually reach vcs.xml, and if so, what's a safe way to recover it at startup without fighting a deliberate user removal via Settings > Version Control > Directory Mappings (which also produces a project with no mapping at startup - the two cases are currently indistinguishable without a persisted 'this diff was user-intentional' marker).
design:
Root cause found via dogfooding stack-trace evidence (2026-09-12/13, jj-stress-test idea.log,
NewMappings debug category): this is a JetBrains platform bug, not a jj-idea bug.

Call chain (captured in full from a live "roots removed" event):

  NewMappings.removeDirectoryMapping
    <- ProjectLevelVcsManagerImpl.removeDirectoryMapping
    <- ModuleVcsDetector.scheduleScanForNewContentRoots        (roots removed[...])
    <- DefaultVcsRootPolicy.scheduleRootsChangeProcessing
    <- ModuleDefaultVcsRootPolicy$MyModulesListener.contentRootsChanged
    <- ContentRootChangeListener.changed
    <- WorkspaceModelImpl.onChanged / replaceProjectModel
    <- JpsProjectModelSynchronizer.applyLoadedEntities$applyLoadedChanges   <- the cache-to-disk resync
    <- JpsProjectModelSynchronizer.applyLoadedEntities$applyChangesWithRetry

On project open, when the workspace model was loaded from a cache,
ProjectSynchronizerUtilImpl.applyJpsModelToProjectModel() re-parses the real .idea/*.xml + .iml
files fresh from disk and diffs them against the cached entities via
EntityStorage.replaceBySource. For a single-module, single-content-root project (project root ==
module root - matches jj-stress-test and most colocated/simple JJ repos), that diff intermittently
(~8/34 opens, ~24%, in our logs) reports the project's own ContentRootEntity as removed with no
correlated add ever reaching ContentRootChangeListener, even though the root is provably still
there moments later (a later VcsRootDetectorImpl scan still lists it).
ModuleDefaultVcsRootPolicy's listener reacts unconditionally to any reported removal by deleting
the VCS mapping - for any VCS, not just JJ's. This is VCS-agnostic platform behavior; nothing
JJ-specific appears in the chain above until the final "remove this mapping" call.

Consequence for THIS bead's original question (does the drop persist to vcs.xml across a
restart?): most of the time no - a separate ~40s-cadence VcsRootDetectorImpl scan notices the
mapping is gone and silently restores it before the user closes the IDE, so vcs.xml on disk stays
correct. It only stays gone across a restart if the IDE is closed inside that ~40s window, or if a
second VCS mapping exists for the project (gates off that scan's own re-registration path too -
see jj-idea-3zk1's original design notes). Narrow enough that a startup-time self-heal isn't worth
building preemptively; revisit only if it's reported as actually hit in practice.

Since this is upstream platform behavior we cannot prevent or intercept from a plugin (no
extension point exists before EntityStorage.replaceBySource runs or before
ProjectLevelVcsManager.removeDirectoryMapping is called), the next real step is reporting it to
JetBrains via YouTrack with a plugin-free minimal repro (plain Git mapping, no jj-idea installed,
to prove it's not plugin-specific) - not further plugin-side work. That repro + report draft was
scoped as a plan during this session but not yet built (session ended before execution) - see
/Users/kevin/.claude/plans/fix-jj-idea-3zk1-compiled-balloon.md for the repro recipe and report
outline if resuming this.

The already-shipped in-session self-heal (JujutsuVcsRootRecovery, jj-idea-3zk1) remains the
correct mitigation on the plugin side regardless of the upstream report's outcome.

Branch with the jj-idea-3zk1 fix + its tests, pushed for reference:
jj-idea-3zk1-vcs-mapping-self-heal on origin (not yet merged to master's pushed state - master
locally already points at the same commit, ab3f8008, pending a separate push decision).

title: Optional jj-CLI bookmark notation (bookmark*/bookmark??) in the panel
description:
Reporter's secondary ask in GitHub #110, beyond the two disappearing-state bugs tracked separately (jj-idea-5r0g, jj-idea-we1n) and the tooltip ask (delivered by jj-idea-uyu9): optionally use jj's own textual notation alongside/instead of icons in the bookmarks panel - local ahead of remote as 'bookmark*', conflicted as 'bookmark??'.

Icons should probably stay the default (survive a narrow panel better); the CLI notation would be a setting for people who want jj's exact vocabulary.

Re-scoped 2026-09-22: the tooltip half of this bead's original ask shipped as jj-idea-uyu9 (every bookmarks-panel row now explains its own state on hover). What remains here is only the optional jj-CLI-notation setting. Dropped to P4 - its utility beyond what the tooltip now covers is unproven; no GitHub follow-up has asked for it since the tooltip landed.
design:
PLAN: optional jj-CLI textual notation (`bookmark*`, `bookmark??`) in the bookmarks panel - a rendering setting; defaults unchanged. (Tooltip half already shipped as jj-idea-uyu9 - BookmarkNodeTooltip.kt.)
Notation semantics (jj CLI `jj bookmark list`/log): a trailing `*` means the local bookmark has unpushed changes / differs from its remote ("ahead" - bookmark is out of sync with its tracked remote: local target != remote target); `??` marks a CONFLICTED bookmark (multiple targets). Mapping from our model: `Bookmark.conflict` -> `??`; `Bookmark.isDiverged || aheadCount > 0 || behindCount > 0` for a local bookmark with a tracked remote -> `*` (jj prints `*` when the local differs from the remote-tracking target in any direction: verify with real jj: `jj log -T bookmarks` output for ahead, behind, and diverged cases to decide whether behind also yields `*` - probe in a scratch repo before coding; record results in the bead).
Design:
1. Setting: application-level `JujutsuApplicationSettings.bookmarkNotation: BookmarkNotation { ICONS (default), JJ, BOTH }` next to `showBookmarkDivergence` (settings/JujutsuApplicationSettings.kt:61, toggled from the log toolbar View Options in CommitTablePanel.kt:~626-629) - expose in the same View Options popup ("Bookmark notation: Icons / jj / Both") and Settings.
2. Rendering: in `appendBookmarkChip(bookmark, label)` (ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:140-153) the label is followed by `divergenceText` (↑n↓m) in DIVERGENT colour; add `jjSuffix(bookmark)` = `??` (conflict) or `*` (differs from tracked remote) appended directly to the label text (`label + suffix`, no space, jj style) when notation is JJ or BOTH; in JJ mode suppress the status icon (`bookmarkIcon(bookmark)`) and arrows to realise "instead of"; BOTH keeps icon + arrows + suffix. The panel and the log table both go through `appendBookmarkChip`, so one change covers both; limit to the PANEL only? The bead says "in the panel" - Rec: apply to the panel (BookmarkNodeRenderer) and the log table chips consistently (one code path; surprising otherwise), behind the single setting.
3. Narrow-panel behaviour: suffix chars are narrower than icon+arrows, so JJ mode helps narrow panels (opposite of the bead's "icons survive narrow panel better" - note both).
4. Tooltip: unchanged (explains state).
Decisions made without the user: Q: panel-only or panel+log? Rec both via shared function. Q: low priority/unproven utility (bead's own note) - Rec: implement only if requested again; the plan is ready.
Scale: O(1) per chip. Testing: `appendBookmarkChip` canvas tests for each notation x state (clean, ahead, behind, diverged, conflict, deleted, remote-only); settings round-trip; manual: MT-BOOKMARK (switch notation: panel and log chips follow; matches `jj bookmark list` output for the same repo). Regression scope: MT-BOOKMARK, MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-DETAILS.
acceptance_criteria: Notation setting (icons/jj/both) renders bookmark*/bookmark?? per jj semantics in panel and log chips; verified against real jj output; tests + MT rows.
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/110.

title: Run IDE code cleanup over a range of changesets (GitHub #98 follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to jj-idea-ob0t (manual "run cleanup on the working copy" button, GitHub #98).
Already flagged in ob0t's notes as "track separately if pursued, NOT in scope for [ob0t]" —
the reporter (CaptaiNiveau) raised it a second time on 2026-09-06, pointing at `jj run` as a
conceptual model: it accepts a range of commits and is intended for exactly this kind of
code-cleanup-with-linters workflow.

Important constraint from that exchange: Rider's code-cleanup action can't be invoked as an
external program, so the plugin cannot delegate to `jj run` directly — it would have to walk
the range itself (edit each change, run cleanup, move to the next, return). `jj run`'s
semantics (a range, applied per-commit) are a useful guide rail for what the UI should promise,
not an implementation shortcut.

Goal: every changeset in a range has passed through cleanup, not just the working copy — a
button in the log to run cleanup on one changeset or a range, auto-editing each in turn.

Depends conceptually on jj-idea-ob0t landing first (reuses its SilentCodeCleanup /
profile-selection-config decisions from the reporter's answers).
design:
PLAN: record the DESIGN DECISION for how a multi-changeset cleanup walk is driven (the bead's acceptance is a recorded decision), reusing jj-idea-ob0t's cleanup invocation + profile decisions.
Constraints (from the bead + code): (1) Rider's cleanup can't run as an external program, so `jj run` cannot do it. `jj run` (jj 0.44: "Run a command across a set of revisions. Checks out each revision in an isolated working copy, runs the command, then amends the revision with the resulting working copy; descendants rebased by default; env JJ_CHANGE_ID, JJ_COMMIT_ID, JJ_WORKSPACE_ROOT") is a useful MODEL of the semantics to promise, not a mechanism (in-IDE cleanup needs the IDE's PSI/inspection engine on files that are open in THIS IDE's project directory). (2) ob0t's layer 1 invokes the IDE's `SilentCodeCleanup` action by id with a DataContext carrying `VIRTUAL_FILE_ARRAY` for the working copy's changed files (see ob0t design).
Candidate drivers:
 A. Sequential edit-walk in the user's workspace (the bead's own sketch): for each change C in the range (oldest first): `jj edit C` -> the working directory now holds C's tree -> run cleanup over C's changed files (changed files known from `jj diff --summary -r C`) -> `jj` snapshots automatically on the next command, amending C and rebasing descendants (conflicts possible if cleanup edits collide with descendants' changes) -> next; finally `jj edit` back to the original @ (or `jj new` if @ was the tip...). Cost: touches the user's working copy and files-on-disk N times; editors reload; the IDE VFS must refresh after each `edit` (existing `invalidate(vfsChanged = true)`); cleanup is async inside the IDE (Silent action returns before fixes apply? `codeCleanup(..., postRunnable)` runs under a progress task; we need a completion signal => use the action's post-runnable via our own invocation (layer 2 of ob0t uses `GlobalInspectionContextBase.codeCleanup(scope, profile, title, postRunnable, false)` which provides `postRunnable`)); the walk must WAIT for completion before the next `jj edit` (document saved + snapshot).
 B. Isolated workspace walk (closer to `jj run`): `jj workspace add <tmp>` per range, open as a second IDE project?? Not feasible (cleanup needs the IDE project model for those files, language levels, SDKs...). Rejected.
 C. Patch-based: compute the cleanup fixes in the user's working copy once and attempt to apply per-change via `jj absorb`/restore: lossy and unsafe. Rejected.
Decision (recommended): A, with guardrails: (1) Preconditions: working copy clean or described? Require that `@` is empty OR confirm ("Cleanup will edit N changes in turn; your current working copy changes will be moved into a snapshot first": jj handles @ naturally - `jj edit` away from a dirty @ snapshots it; returning via `jj edit <orig @ change id>` restores it), no conflicts in the range (abort on first conflict with a notification and the remaining range untouched), no immutable changes in the range (jj refuses edit - skip with a note); (2) every step wrapped via undo tracking and ONE group balloon "Cleaned N changes - Undo" using the Stage-1 undo machinery storing the list of OperationIds (see x30x/aii0 notes) - Undo reverts newest-first; (3) cancellable progress dialog (`Task.Modal` with cancel between changes; never mid-change); (4) state restore in `finally`: always `jj edit <original @>` (or `jj new <orig>` when the original was an empty @ that jj abandoned by edit-away - jj abandons an empty working-copy commit when moving away, so record `isEmpty` and recreate via `jj new <parent>` afterwards); (5) range semantics: single selected change, or a contiguous selection in the log, or revset `trunk()..@` via a small dialog; process in topological order oldest-first so descendants (already rebased automatically by jj after each amend) are cleaned once.
Why edit-walk is acceptable: it is exactly what a human would do; jj's automatic descendant rebase makes it safe/idempotent; cleanup being idempotent means re-running is harmless.
Open questions for you (recommendations): Q1 prompt before running on > 3 changes? Rec yes (one confirmation naming the count and the abort-on-conflict rule). Q2 allow `--restore-descendants`-style "don't propagate"? Rec no (default propagate; amending a change changes descendants' parents' content, propagate keeps them consistent). Q3 entry points? Rec: log context menu "Run Code Cleanup on Selected Changes" (single/contiguous multi-select), disabled when any immutable/conflicted.
Scale: per change: 1 `jj edit` + cleanup over that change's changed files (O(files)) + snapshot; no per-commit loop over the whole repo; range size is user-selected (cap 50 with a warning). Testing: driver unit tests with a stub executor + fake cleanup runner (ordering, abort on conflict, restore of original @ incl. empty-@ case, cancel between steps, undo group list), no UI; manual (IDEA): range of 3 changes with fixable warnings: each cleaned, @ restored, one Undo reverts all; conflict mid-range aborts cleanly. Regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-CTXMENU, MT-LOG-REFRESH.
acceptance_criteria: Design decision recorded: sequential edit-walk with preconditions, abort-on-conflict, original-@ restore, grouped undo; reuses ob0t's cleanup invocation; driver unit-test plan.
notes: Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/98 (comment 2026-09-06). relates_to jj-idea-ob0t.

title: Determine whether a defensible 'primary remote' notion exists for the bookmarks panel
description:
## Summary
Parked from jj-idea-d65h's spike (jj-idea-3sac's design field, Finding
2), GitHub #48. jj-idea-a7a7 (collapse remote categories + roll-up) solves the reporter's noise
complaint without needing to rank or promote any remote — collapsed-by-default with persisted
per-user expansion state. This issue is only for the separate, lower-priority question of whether
remote *ordering* (not promotion/hiding) could ever be derived rather than alphabetical, e.g. for
sorting remote categories so a "more relevant" one appears first when expanded.

Signals available, none currently read by the plugin (jj/cli/Config.kt's Key enum has only
USER_NAME/USER_EMAIL):
- `git.push` config (jj/cli/Config.kt) — a single remote; unset in most repos observed.
- `git.fetch` config — defaults to the glob "origin"; also commonly unset.
- The built-in `trunk()` revset alias's origin-then-upstream preference order.
- Single-remote repos, where the "primary" question is trivially answered by having only one.

## Explicitly out of scope
This is not a prerequisite for jj-idea-a7a7 or jj-idea-j0zv. Only revisit if there's actual
demand for remote *ordering* beyond alphabetical, or a future feature (e.g. a "push" quick-action)
needs to guess a default remote.
design:
PLAN: this bead's deliverable is a WRITTEN RECOMMENDATION (no code); here it is, with the evidence gathered.
Question: can a defensible "primary remote" (for ordering remote categories in the bookmarks panel, or choosing a default remote for a quick action) be DERIVED?
Evidence:
 - jj's own default `trunk()` alias (verified `jj config list --include-defaults`): `remote_bookmarks(exact:"trunk", exact:"origin") | remote_bookmarks(exact:"trunk", exact:"upstream") | ...` - jj hard-codes a PREFERENCE ORDER `origin` then `upstream` for finding trunk, i.e. jj's own convention treats `origin` as the primary and `upstream` as the secondary (the fork-workflow pair).
 - `git.push` config (a single remote name) and `git.fetch` (default glob "origin"): present in the repo config only if the user set them; unset in most repos (bead observation). `git.push` unset => `jj git push` pushes to `origin` if it exists, else the only remote, else errors asking for `--remote` (jj behaviour) - again "origin" by convention.
 - Single-remote repos: trivially primary.
 - `jj git remote list` order is lexicographic by name (jj stores remotes sorted) - no "first added" signal.
 - The plugin currently reads only user.name/user.email from jj config (jj/cli/Config.kt `Key` enum), so reading `git.push`/`git.fetch` needs two enum entries + `Config.get` (already generic) - cheap if ever wanted.
Recommendation: a defensible, deterministic derivation exists and is cheap: primary = (1) `git.push` if set and it names an existing remote; else (2) `origin` if present; else (3) `upstream` if present (jj's own trunk() preference); else (4) the alphabetically first remote. Use it ONLY for tie-breaking/ordering (order remote categories primary-first, then alphabetical) and as the default-remote guess for future quick actions - NEVER to hide or demote remotes (jj-idea-a7a7 already solved noise by collapsing; keep that). Because no user demand exists beyond alphabetical today, the recommendation is: DO NOT implement now; if implemented later, it is ~30 lines (Config keys + a pure `primaryRemote(remotes, config)` function with tests) and low risk.
Decisions made without the user: Q: implement? Rec no until a feature needs a default remote (e.g. periodic fetch jj-idea-crik chooses `jj git fetch` default = jj's own selection, so even that doesn't need it). Q: close? Rec close with this recommendation recorded (acceptance says no code change required to close).
Testing/Scale/Manual: n/a (documentation). Related: jj-idea-3sac epic design, jj-idea-spt6 (per-remote notation), jj-idea-emnu (remote icons).
acceptance_criteria: Written recommendation recorded (derivation order and 'do not implement yet'); bead can be closed.

title: Investigate DevKit NPE indexing JujutsuBundle.properties (GitHub #100 stack trace)
description:
## Summary
A user posted a stack trace on GitHub #100 (comment 2026-09-04T08:49:24Z) while investigating the (separate, already-fixed) widget-visibility bug. This stack trace is unrelated:

java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Argument for @NotNull parameter 's' of com/intellij/openapi/util/TextRange.allOf must not be null
  at org.jetbrains.idea.devkit.references.MessageBundleReferenceContributor$PluginIdReference.<init>
  ... (during PSI reference resolution while indexing JujutsuBundle.properties)

This is JetBrains DevKit plugin code (MessageBundleReferenceContributor, in org.jetbrains.idea.devkit.references) throwing while building a PSI reference over our properties file — not our plugin's code, and not caused by the widget-visibility bug (jj-idea-0hw4, already fixed in commit b4036dc18).

## Investigation
Confirm whether any of our JujutsuBundle.properties keys have a shape (missing plugin id association, malformed key, etc.) that triggers this DevKit code path, or whether it is purely a DevKit-side defect independent of our file. If it's DevKit-side only, this reduces to reporting it upstream (YouTrack) rather than a plugin fix.

Do NOT reopen jj-idea-0hw4 for this — they are unrelated defects that happened to surface in the same comment.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/100 (comment 2026-09-04T08:49:24Z)
design:
PLAN: ROOT CAUSE FOUND by reading DevKit source (../intellij-community/plugins/devkit/devkit-core/src/references/MessageBundleReferenceContributor.java) - it is triggered by one of OUR keys, and is also a DevKit null-safety defect. Fix on our side (one-line rename) and optionally report upstream.
Evidence: the contributor treats any bundle key that STARTS WITH `plugin.` and ENDS WITH `.description` as a plugin-localisation key of the form `plugin.<pluginId>.description` (constants PLUGIN = "plugin.", DESCRIPTION = ".description", :69/:78; `isPluginDescriptionKey`, :174-175) and builds `new PluginIdReference(element, id)` with `id = StringUtil.substringAfter(StringUtil.notNullize(StringUtil.substringBefore(text, ".description")), "plugin.")` (:134-138). Our bundle (src/main/resources/messages/JujutsuBundle.properties:16-17) has `plugin.name=...` and `plugin.description=Native integration with Jujutsu ...`. For `plugin.description`: `substringBefore("plugin.description", ".description")` = "plugin"; `substringAfter("plugin", "plugin.")` = null (no "plugin." prefix left) -> `PluginIdReference(element, null)` -> `TextRange.allOf(null)` -> exactly the reported "Argument for @NotNull parameter 's' of TextRange.allOf must not be null" (PluginIdReference.<init> at :185-187). So the trigger is our key shape matching DevKit's `plugin.<id>.description` pattern without an id segment (DevKit should null-check `id`, but we can avoid it).
Usage check: `grep -rn "plugin.description\|plugin.name" src/main` finds NO Kotlin/XML references - both keys appear unused (the plugin name/description come from plugin.xml `<name>`/`<description>`; the keys look like leftovers from the original bundle - `plugin.name` is harmless to DevKit (not ending in .description) but unused too).
Fix:
1. Remove the two unused keys (preferred), or if they are intended for the platform's plugin-description localisation (JetBrains convention `plugin.<pluginId>.description` with the id `in.kkkev.jj-idea`: `plugin.in.kkkev.jj-idea.description=...` + `plugin.in.kkkev.jj-idea.name=...` are the REAL localisation keys used when plugin.xml has `<resource-bundle>` and the IDE shows localised plugin metadata) - then rename to the conformant form, which ALSO gives DevKit a valid id to resolve. Rec: rename to the conformant keys: gives future i18n of the marketplace description (jj-idea-ysew's scope: extract hardcoded plugin.xml text) while eliminating the NPE.
2. Verify in the sandbox IDE with the DevKit plugin installed (it is bundled in IDEA Ultimate/Community dev installs): open the properties file, trigger indexing/"Find Usages"; no exception. Add a guard test: bundle keys must not start with `plugin.` and end with `.description` unless of the form `plugin.<non-empty id>.description` (pure JVM test reading the properties file) - prevents reintroduction.
3. Upstream: DevKit should guard null `id` - file a YouTrack issue (IJPL/IDEA DevKit component): title "NPE in MessageBundleReferenceContributor.PluginIdReference for key 'plugin.description'", with the exact stack and the 3-line explanation above; draft text kept here (posting is outward-facing -> user posts/approves): link back to GitHub #100 comment.
4. GitHub #100: reply (draft, not posted): "That stack trace is DevKit choking on our `plugin.description` key name; renamed in <version>".
Decisions made without the user: Q: delete vs rename the keys? Rec rename to `plugin.in.kkkev.jj-idea.name/description` (conformant, ready for localisation) - verify the plugin id exactly (`<id>in.kkkev.jj-idea</id>`, plugin.xml:2). Reverse: delete both keys.
Scale: none. Testing: the guard test; manual: MT-SETTINGS? none (no UI); verify DevKit behaviour once in runIde. Acceptance: no NPE with DevKit; keys conformant or removed; guard test; upstream report drafted.
acceptance_criteria: plugin.description key shape no longer triggers DevKit NPE (renamed to plugin.<id>.description or removed); guard test; upstream YouTrack report + GH #100 reply drafted for user approval.
close_reason: Renamed plugin.* bundle keys to plugin.<id>.*; guard test BundleKeyShapeTest added. Upstream YouTrack report and GH #100 reply still need posting (drafts in bead design).

title: Feature Request: Integration with IntelliJ Tasks (vcs.taskHandler) (GitHub #102)
description:
## Summary
IntelliJ Tasks lets a user switch between tasks, restoring per-task context (open files, breakpoints, bookmarks). VCS plugins participate via the vcs.taskHandler extension point (VcsTaskHandler, platform/vcs-api/src/com/intellij/openapi/vcs/VcsTaskHandler.java), implemented by git4idea.GitTaskHandler and hg4idea's equivalent. Confirmed the EP exists and is branch-shaped (TaskInfo, startNewTask, switchToTask, closeTask).

jj has no branch concept — the natural analogue is bookmarks. Two candidate mappings to evaluate:
1. Bookmark-per-task: starting a task creates/advances a bookmark named for the task; switching moves @ to that bookmark.
2. Change-per-task: starting a task creates a new change; switching edits that change (jj edit).

Follow-up from reporter: the issue-tracker bookmark could also be attached to the working copy context, separate from branch-equivalent state.

This is backlog-grade exploration, not scheduled — record the mapping options here before any implementation.

Reported: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/102
design:
PLAN (decision bead - recommendation; implement only on demand): record the mapping decision for IntelliJ Tasks (`vcs.taskHandler` EP -> `VcsTaskHandler`, platform/vcs-api/.../VcsTaskHandler.java; implemented by git4idea `GitTaskHandler`).
EP shape (verified in ../intellij-community): abstract class `VcsTaskHandler` with a branch-shaped contract: `TaskInfo(branch name, repositories, remote?)`, `startNewTask(taskName)` (create+switch), `switchToTask(taskInfo, runnable)`, `closeTask(taskInfo, original)`, `isSyncEnabled`, `getCurrentTasks()`, `getAllExistingTasks()`; Tasks core calls it when the user opens/switches/closes a task to create/switch a branch and restore context (open files, breakpoints).
Candidate mappings:
 1. Bookmark-per-task: `startNewTask(name)` = `jj new <trunk or current @-> -m <name>` + `jj bookmark create <slug(name)> -r @`; `switchToTask(task)` = `jj edit <bookmark>` (or `jj new <bookmark>` when the target is immutable/pushed: reuse the plugin's edit-vs-new confirmation, chooseSwitchMode in ui/statusbar/JujutsuWorkingCopySwitcher.kt:~38-62); `closeTask` = optionally `jj bookmark delete` (+ forget) and abandon if empty; `getAllExistingTasks` = local bookmarks (+ remote-only as `isRemote` like git's remote branches); `getCurrentTasks` = bookmarks at/ancestor of @ (the plugin already computes "closest bookmarks to @": `closestBookmarks`, jj/ClosestBookmarks.kt / JujutsuStateModel). Fits publish-via-bookmark workflows (GitHub/GitLab PR branches) and survives rewrites (bookmarks follow rewritten commits).
 2. Change-per-task: task id = change id (stable across rewrites; jj's native unit of work); `startNewTask` = `jj new -m <name>`; `switchToTask` = `jj edit <change>`; task name <-> change description first line; `getAllExistingTasks` = mutable changes with non-empty descriptions in the user's stack (`mutable() & author(me)` revset); no bookmark needed until pushing. Closer to jj's model ("describe-first" - contributing.md's key differentiator) but `TaskInfo.branch` is a free string: store `<changeId>` or `<description>` ambiguity: descriptions are not unique/stable (renames), so the key must be the change id and the display name the description - Tasks UI shows `getName()`; mapping names to ids needs a persisted map.
 3. Hybrid (recommended if built): task = change; a bookmark is created lazily only when the user publishes/pushes (jj needs a bookmark to push anyway): `startNewTask` creates the change with the task name as description (no bookmark); `TaskInfo.branch` = the bookmark if one exists else the change id short + description; `switchToTask` = `jj edit`; the issue-tracker id from the Task (e.g. `PROJ-123`) is embedded in the DESCRIPTION prefix (matches the plugin's issue-navigation linkification) AND in the bookmark name when created (`proj-123-<slug>`); follow-up from the reporter (bookmark attached to working copy context) = the same bookmark.
Decision (recommended): do NOT implement now; if/when demanded, implement the HYBRID (change-per-task with lazy bookmark) because it matches jj's describe-first workflow and avoids bookmark clutter, with these rules: slug = lowercase task id + title words, max 40 chars; collision -> suffix; switching to a task whose change is immutable -> `jj new` on top; dirty @ -> jj snapshots automatically (no stash needed - an advantage over git: switching tasks never needs shelving; document it).
Registration if built: `<vcs.taskHandler implementation="in.kkkev.jjidea.vcs.JujutsuTaskHandler"/>`; requires the Tasks plugin (`com.intellij.tasks`) as an OPTIONAL dependency (`<depends optional="true" config-file="jj-tasks.xml">com.intellij.tasks</depends>`) so the plugin loads without it - verify the EP is `com.intellij.vcs.taskHandler`... (EP name `Vcs.taskHandler`? read VcsExtensionPoints.xml) and platform since-build 251 availability.
Decisions made without the user: Q: bookmark vs change vs hybrid? Rec hybrid. Q: build now? Rec no (backlog, single request, #102). Scale: none. Testing (if built): handler unit tests with a stub executor (start/switch/close/list mappings), optional-dependency load test (plugin descriptor loads without tasks plugin); manual: Tasks open/switch/close flow; regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-BOOKMARK. Acceptance of THIS bead: the decision above recorded (done once reviewed).
acceptance_criteria: Mapping decision recorded (hybrid change-per-task with lazy bookmark; not scheduled); implementation notes retained.
notes: Implemented 2026-10-05: bookmark-per-task (chosen over the hybrid: Tasks persists/shows the TaskInfo name as a branch name, so the bookmark name is the only key that matches the dialog, the persisted key and the push target). Close = switch back only. Switch = newest mutable head of the bookmark's stack (jj new on top if immutable). Task commit message from default changelist comment becomes the change description. Code: vcs/JujutsuTaskHandler.kt; tests JujutsuTaskHandlerTest; manual MT-TASKS. ./gradlework check green. TODO before close: runIde smoke of MT-TASKS.
close_reason: Implemented bookmark-per-task Tasks integration (JujutsuTaskHandler); check green; smoke-tested in runIde

title: Live graph preview during a drag
description: jj-idea-6oeg design doc section 9 (Performance). v1 ships zone-highlight + setDropPossible tooltip feedback only (both O(1) per pointer move). This bead adds a live simulated-graph preview using RebaseSimulator.simulate, memoised on (payload, targetId, position) so it runs once per zone change rather than once per pixel of pointer movement - required given DnDTargetChecker.update fires on every mouse move and the log's ~100k-commit scale envelope. Per contributing.md's performance rule, this must ship an operation-count test, not a wall-clock benchmark (see ui/log/graph/GraphLayoutScaleTest.kt, jj/RepoLogCacheScaleTest.kt for the pattern).
design:
PLAN: live simulated-graph preview while dragging a commit, rendered in a small floating panel next to the pointer (NOT by rewriting the real table's rows), memoised per (payload, target, destination mode).
Facts: DnD wiring = `installDragAndDrop` in ui/log/JujutsuLogTableDnD.kt (`DnDSupport.createBuilder(this).setTargetChecker { event -> ... resolveLive(event, hysteresis, dragContextHolder) { savedGraphNodes = it } ...}`, :123-175; it already stores `savedGraphNodes` so a drag can temporarily swap the table's graph (restored in `cleanUp`, :115-121) - so the table-graph-swap mechanism exists for the highlight; `DropHint` (ui/dnd/DropHint.kt) is the existing pointer-adjacent HTML popup (an `IconAwareHtmlPane` in a layered pane, never intercepting DnD), `RejectOverlay`/zone highlight for the row; `ZoneHysteresis` stabilises zones (jitter); drop zones map to `RebaseDestinationMode` (ONTO/INSERT_AFTER/INSERT_BEFORE: DropZones.kt, DropZoneToDestinationModeTest). `RebaseSimulator.simulate(allEntries, sourceEntries, destinationIds, sourceMode, destinationMode)` (ui/rebase/RebaseSimulator.kt:35-65) scopes the result to relevant entries (`scopeToRelevant`, :285: for > 20 entries keeps only ancestors/descendants of sources+destinations plus a bounded context) and returns `RebaseSimulation(entries, sourceIds, destinationIds, reparentedIds)`; `RebasePreviewPanel(project).update(...)` renders it (ui/rebase/RebasePreviewPanel.kt:29-101).
Design:
1. Memo key `DragPreviewKey(payloadKey, targetChangeKey, destinationMode, sourceMode)`; `DragPreviewController` (ui/dnd/) holds `lastKey`/`lastSimulation`; on each `targetChecker` tick the zone-hysteresis output yields a resolution with (row, zone); compute the key (O(1)); if equal to `lastKey` do NOTHING (no simulate, no repaint) - the "memoised, not per pixel" acceptance. Only when the key changes: run `simulate` OFF the EDT? Simulation cost: `scopeToRelevant` + `topologicalSort` over the loaded window (<=~10k entries typical; the existing rebase dialog runs it on the EDT per selection change at picker scale); at 100k entries it is O(n) per zone change (~tens of ms) - run on a pooled thread with cancel-previous semantics (generation counter; stale results dropped) and update the preview on EDT when ready; show the previous preview (dimmed) meanwhile.
2. Rendering: a `DragGraphPreview` floating panel (like `DropHint`: JLayeredPane child, `isOpaque`, drop-target-transparent via `setDropTarget(null)`), containing a compact `RebasePreviewPanel`-style graph limited to the scoped entries (cap rows at ~12: scoped list can be longer - clip to rows around source+destination with ellipsis row), positioned beside the table (right edge or opposite side of the pointer to avoid covering the target row). Reuses `RebasePreviewPanel` internals via the shared render function extracted for jj-idea-uuy9 (`setSimulation(...)`), so source/destination highlight colours match.
3. Interaction with existing feedback: keep zone highlight + DropHint text (O(1) feedback is unchanged and shown immediately); the graph preview appears after the first computed simulation (<=100 ms typical), hides on reject/leave/drop (`cleanUp` extended).
4. Settings/gating: DnD is graduating out of preview (jj-idea-jxii); ship this behind a registry key/setting `showDragGraphPreview` default ON? Rec default ON for >=2 rows of change, with a quick off-switch in the View options (it is purely visual).
5. Payload types: only Commit payloads onto commits (rebase/duplicate/…): the simulator exists for rebase modes; for Duplicate (jj-idea-77i5 DuplicateSimulator) and bookmark/tag moves (no graph change) show nothing; ties to 77i5 for the duplicate preview.
Decisions made without the user: Q: floating panel vs swapping the table's rows? Rec floating panel (row swapping would shift rows under the pointer and break hit-testing/hysteresis). Q: simulate on pooled thread? Rec yes with generation cancel. Q: default on? Rec on.
Scale: per ZONE CHANGE (not per pixel): one `simulate` O(n) over loaded entries (scoped output small); rendering O(<=12 rows). Operation-count test (required by the bead): drive `targetChecker` 10,000 times with 5 distinct (target, zone) keys -> `simulate` invoked exactly 5 times, repaints <= 5; same key repeated -> 0 calls; cancel semantics: key change during an in-flight simulation drops the stale result (assert only latest result applied).
Testing: DragPreviewController unit tests with a counting `Simulator` seam + fake executor; render test of the floating panel with a stub simulation (rows <= 12, highlight colours); DnD integration test using the existing `DropOperationDispatchTest`/`DragContextScaleTest` patterns; manual: MT-DND (drag a commit across rows: preview updates only when the zone changes, matches the result after drop; no flicker; large repo smoothness (stress fixture SCALE=6); hides on cancel/reject). Regression scope: MT-DND (full), MT-LOG-GRAPH, MT-LOG-TABLE.
acceptance_criteria: Floating live graph preview during commit drags, simulation memoised per (payload,target,mode) and run off-EDT with stale-result cancellation; operation-count test proves no per-pixel work; tests + MT-DND rows.
notes:
Depends on jj-idea-6jvh (core) and jj-idea-8fxs (rebase-drop) having shipped first. Deliberately deferred out of v1 on performance grounds.
See docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md for batch scope, sequencing, and the preview-gating design. Find your batch's siblings with: bd list --label dnd-batch-N

title: Adaptive drop zones (speed/reversal-weighted bands)
description: jj-idea-6oeg design doc section 4. Research surveyed: Bubble Cursor (Grossman & Balakrishnan 2005) reduces to the static split in 1-D and adds nothing; DynaSpot (Chapuis et al. 2009, speed-dependent area cursor) is the closest published match - grow the nearer edge band toward ~JBUI.scale(10) when pointer speed drops or direction reverses near a boundary, composed with hysteresis so it can't oscillate; semantic pointing was rejected as unsuitable (its mechanism is invisibility, which conflicts with the always-visible drop indicator here). Deliberately deferred until the static-zone gesture (jj-idea-8fxs) has shipped and been validated.
design:
PLAN: a pure, deterministic zone-resolver that widens the nearer edge band on slow/reversing pointers (DynaSpot-style), composed with the existing hysteresis - specified entirely over synthetic (t, y) samples so it unit-tests with no UI.
