Facts: static zones = `DropZones.zoneAt(dy, rowHeight, band)` with `band = min(JBUI.scale(6), rowHeight/4)` (ui/dnd/DropZones.kt:19-35: edges INSERT_BEFORE/INSERT_AFTER, centre ONTO); `ZoneHysteresis.update(row, dy, rowHeight, band)` (ui/dnd/ZoneHysteresis.kt) is a Schmitt trigger: once in a zone the pointer must pass `slack = JBUI.scale(3)` beyond the boundary to switch; called per mouse move from the table's `resolveLive` (ui/log/JujutsuLogTableDnD.kt targetChecker) after the pointer's row/dy are computed; `DragContextHolder` memoises per payload. Design doc: docs/design/jj-idea-6oeg-drag-and-drop-graph-ops.md section 4 (research summary in the bead: DynaSpot, Chapuis et al. 2009: grow the target area as speed drops).
Design:
1. `PointerKinematics` (pure): ring buffer of the last K (default 4) samples `(tNanos, row, dy)` -> `speed` (px/ms along y, computed from absolute y = row*rowHeight + dy so row changes don't spike) and `reversal` (sign change of dy-velocity within the last N ms). Speeds below `slowThreshold` (e.g. 0.15 px/ms) mean "the user is aiming".
2. `AdaptiveBand`: `effectiveBand(baseBand, rowHeight, speed, reversal, nearEdge)`: when `reversal` near an edge or `speed < slow`, grow the NEARER edge band from `baseBand` toward `maxBand = JBUI.scale(10)` (clamped so ONTO keeps >= 1/3 of the row: the existing worked-example invariant is half the row; relax to a third only while adaptive), growth smoothed (linear in speed between slow and fast thresholds so no discontinuity); when `speed >= fast` return `baseBand` (static). Pure function of numbers.
3. Composition: `zone = hysteresis.update(row, dy, rowHeight, band = effectiveBand(...))` - hysteresis stays the stabiliser (design: "composed with hysteresis so it can't oscillate"); because the band changes between calls, define hysteresis boundaries relative to the CURRENT band argument (they already take `band` per call) - verify `ZoneHysteresis.update` semantics when band grows mid-hold (previous zone stays until the pointer crosses the new boundary +- slack; add a test for "band grows while pointer sits at old boundary -> no flicker").
4. Wiring: `resolveLive` feeds each move into a per-gesture `PointerKinematics` (reset with `hysteresis.reset()` at drag start/end). Sample timestamps from `System.nanoTime()` (inject a clock for tests). Drag-over events are OS-coalesced (DropHint KDoc), so effective sampling is irregular - kinematics must tolerate dt jitter (use speed = |Δy|/max(Δt, 1ms)).
5. Gate: behind `ide.dnd`-style Registry key `jj.dnd.adaptiveZones` default ON after validation, since it changes feel; DnD is graduating (jj-idea-jxii) - ship adaptive AFTER GA (it is P4/batch 6 polish) so the GA gesture stays the validated static one.
Decisions made without the user: Q: thresholds (slow 0.15 px/ms, fast 0.6, maxBand 10px, ONTO >= 1/3)? Rec as stated, tune with real drags (log samples with a debug flag to calibrate). Q: ship? Rec optional polish; only if users report mis-drops near boundaries.
Scale: O(1) per mouse move (K=4 samples). Testing (the acceptance): deterministic unit tests over scripted sequences: slow approach to the boundary grows the band and selects the edge earlier than static; fast flick keeps static zones; reversal near boundary grows the nearer band; oscillating +-1px samples around a boundary yield <= 1 zone change (hysteresis composition); row change resets; clamp invariant (ONTO share) for every speed. Manual: MT-DND (feel: slow hover near row edge targets before/after more easily; no flicker; fast drags unchanged). Regression scope: MT-DND.
acceptance_criteria: Pure adaptive-band resolver composed with ZoneHysteresis, driven by synthetic (t,y) sample tests; kinematics ring buffer; registry-gated; no flicker test; MT-DND feel check.
notes:
Depends on jj-idea-6jvh (core) and jj-idea-8fxs (rebase-drop) having shipped first.
See docs/design/preview-gating-and-dnd-sequencing.md for batch scope, sequencing, and the preview-gating design. Find your batch's siblings with: bd list --label dnd-batch-N

title: Undo balloon for all mutating jj actions
description: Stage 4 (polish) of the undo mini-roadmap (docs/design/undo-support-roadmap.md). Extend the Stage 1 undo-balloon mechanism (jj-idea-v9zp) to every mutating jj action across the plugin, not just drag-and-drop drops - description edits, abandon, squash, split, bookmark actions, etc.
design:
PLAN: wire `.addUndoTracking(<labelKey>)` (CommandExecutor.kt `WithRepo.addUndoTracking`, ui/services/UndoBalloon.kt `withUndoBalloon`) into every remaining REVERSIBLE mutating call site; mostly mechanical. Inventory (from `createCommand` call sites vs existing `addUndoTracking` users):
ALREADY WIRED (verified by grep): working-copy switcher edit/new (ui/statusbar/JujutsuWorkingCopySwitcher.kt:122,137), Restore (ui/restore/RestoreDialog.kt:185 - the bead's note that restore is unwired is STALE), conflict accept (ui/editor/JujutsuConflictEditorNotificationProvider.kt:159), rebase (actions/change/rebaseAction.kt:57), duplicate-onto (duplicateOntoAction.kt:49), move bookmark (moveBookmarkAction.kt:48), move bookmark to change (moveBookmarkToChangeAction.kt:41), abandon (abandonChangeAction.kt:52), set tag (setTagAction.kt:33).
TO WIRE (REVERSIBLE commands per `JjInvocation(REVERSIBLE, ...)` in jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt - verify each args builder's class before wiring): describe (actions/change/describeAction.kt:`describe` -> `performDescribe`; DescribeWorkingCopyAction.kt; WorkingCopyControlsPanel.describeCurrentChange :420) - label "Describe"; new change (actions/change/NewChangeAction.kt quick action, newChangeFromAction.kt dialog result, WorkingCopyControlsPanel.createNewChange :441) - note: undoing a `new` abandons the new empty change: fine; edit (EditChangeAction.kt) - `jj edit` is an operation (working-copy pointer move): REVERSIBLE; squash/squashInto (actions/change/squashAction.kt, squashIntoAction.kt incl. the interactive hunk path, whose compound `edit` second command makes TWO operations - the undo must revert both: see x30x/aii0 multi-op undo list; interplay with q3lk compound-suppression); split (splitAction.kt); duplicate (duplicateChangeAction.kt); delete bookmark (deleteBookmarkAction.kt - REVERSIBLE: bookmark delete is a repo-scope op; combine with jj-idea-06eq's post-delete balloon: ONE balloon with Undo + Push Now); forget bookmark (forgetBookmarkAction.kt); advance bookmark (advanceBookmarkAction.kt); delete tag (deleteTagAction.kt); file track/untrack (actions/file/TrackedToggleAction.kt: REVERSIBLE per `fileTrackArgs/fileUntrackArgs` - but the toggle already shows a success balloon with its own text: add the Undo action to that same balloon instead of a second one); restore-to-change (RestoreToChangeAction -> performRestore: wired via RestoreDialog).
EXPLICITLY NOT WIRED (document "why" per the acceptance): IRREVERSIBLE classes - git push/fetch/clone/remote (`bookmark track/untrack`, `config`, `workspace update-stale`, `git init`, tag push, Init): reverting them is unsafe/meaningless (CommandExecutor.kt:62-69 Reversibility doc); read-only commands; `jj op revert` itself (undo of undo = redo, x30x).
Design notes:
 1. Label keys: `<action>.undo` bundle entries ("Undo <verb>" names the operation per the roadmap's no-blind-undo rule), e.g. `log.action.describe.undo=Describe`, mirroring existing ones (`log.action.abandon.undo`).
 2. Noise control: the balloon for EVERY action may annoy (describe fires on each edit commit in the Working Copy panel): add a setting "Show undo balloon after actions" (default ON; the persistent `Jujutsu.UndoLastOperation` menu action remains regardless) and suppress the balloon for the Working Copy panel's describe (the description box has its own editing/undo semantic and balloons while typing flows would be spammy): wire the RECORD (so the VCS-menu Undo works) but skip the balloon via a `showBalloon = false` parameter on `addUndoTracking` for describe-from-panel.
 3. Multi-op actions: squashInto-interactive (squash + edit), split + describe-after (SplitSpec describes the remaining side after split), newChangeFromAction with edit: record the LIST of OperationIds (JujutsuUndoService.Record gets `operations: List<OperationId>`; performUndo reverts newest-first) - shared with x30x/aii0/cmc3 designs; until that lands, wire only the first op with a documented limitation OR skip these three and list them.
 4. One-record-per-repo model: `JujutsuUndoService.current()` returns a single record when exactly one repo has one - wiring everything makes it update on every action: fine (latest wins).
Decisions made without the user: Q: setting for the balloon? Rec yes. Q: describe-from-panel balloon? Rec record-only (no balloon). Q: order of work? Rec: describe/new/edit/squash/split/delete bookmark first (highest regret), then the rest.
Scale: one `jj op log -n` lookup per reversible command (already the cost of the Stage-1 mechanism: findTaggedOperation after each tracked command, CliExecutor.kt:~1155) - O(1) per user action; no loops. Testing: per-site tests using the existing pattern (e.g. rebaseAction tests with `notify` seam: assert `withUndoBalloon` invoked with the right label key and that Irreversible results don't notify); a guard test enumerating `createCommand` call sites that are REVERSIBLE and lack `addUndoTracking` (source scan with an allow-list of documented exceptions) so new actions can't forget it; manual: new MT-UNDO rows or MT-CTXMENU: perform each action, Undo from the balloon restores the prior state (log refresh, files). Regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-WORKINGCOPY, MT-BOOKMARK, MT-SQUASH, MT-SPLIT.
acceptance_criteria: All REVERSIBLE mutating call sites record an undo and show a labelled balloon (or documented exceptions); setting + panel-describe exception; multi-op actions handled or listed; guard test; MT rows.
notes:
Depends on jj-idea-v9zp. Mechanically small once Stage 1 lands - mostly wiring.

Restore (RestoreSelectionAction.kt, RestoreToChangeAction.kt) is one of the unwired call sites: jj-idea-g2p8's restore command is already classified REVERSIBLE in CliExecutor.kt (restoreArgs), but performRestore's .createCommand { restore(...) } in ui/restore/RestoreDialog.kt doesn't call .withUndoTracking()/.withUndoBalloon(...) yet. Restore feels especially worth prioritizing within this bead since it's a destructive, content-discarding op with no other in-app undo path today.

title: Bookmarks panel: hoist search into the log toolbar
description: jj-idea-b2ae's bookmarks panel currently relies on plain TreeSpeedSearch (type-ahead while the tree has focus). git4idea's Branches dashboard instead puts a persistent search field inline in the log's main toolbar (BranchesInGitLogUiFactoryProvider's SearchLook.Inline). Consider the same for discoverability once the panel sees real use.
design:
PLAN: surface the bookmarks-panel search in the log toolbar (git4idea Branches dashboard parity) - only after the panel sees real use; design recorded.
Facts: the panel (ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt) uses `TreeSpeedSearch` (type-ahead only while the tree has focus; no visible affordance); its own toolbar (`createToolbar`, :163-181) has Expand/Collapse All. The log's main toolbar/filters row is built in `CommitTablePanel`/`UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel` (filter components: `JujutsuReferenceFilterComponent`, author, date, paths, revset chips + `LogSearchField`). git4idea's `BranchesInGitLogUiFactoryProvider` hosts a branches-tree search field inline in the log toolbar (SearchLook.Inline).
Design:
1. A `SearchTextField` (platform `SearchTextField(false)` with history off) placed in the panel's own header row above the tree (NOT in the log toolbar) - Rec: panel-header placement first (the panel can be collapsed/hidden via the stripe button, so a toolbar-level field would act on a hidden component) - this keeps the field adjacent to what it filters and avoids toolbar crowding; if "log toolbar" placement is still wanted, it can be a toolbar action that focuses/expands the panel's field.
2. Behaviour: typing filters the tree (hide non-matching leaves; keep ancestors of matches; auto-expand matching paths) rather than only jump-selecting like speed search: implement via a `filter: String` parameter to `buildBookmarkTree(...)`/post-filter of `BookmarkNode`s in `rebuild()` (case-insensitive substring on `displayName`/full path/`localName`; folders with no matching descendants dropped; rollup recomputed from the filtered children via `rollupOf`); debounce 150 ms with the existing `rebuildQueue` (MergingUpdateQueue) - rebuild cost is O(bookmarks) (already per state change). Clearing restores the full tree and the user's prior expansion state (`LogWindowConfig.bookmarkNodeExpanded` persisted toggles must not be overwritten by search-driven auto-expansion: keep search expansion transient).
3. Keep `TreeSpeedSearch` as is (still useful when the field is hidden) - they coexist; Ctrl/Cmd+F while the tree is focused focuses the field.
4. Matches the existing LogSearchField regex/case toggles? Not needed v1.
Decisions made without the user: Q: header-of-panel vs main log toolbar? Rec panel header. Q: filter vs jump? Rec filter. Q: start now? Bead says "once the panel sees real use" - low priority, no demand signal yet.
Scale: O(bookmarks) per debounced keystroke on the existing rebuild path (no jj calls). Testing: tree-model filter tests (matches, ancestor retention, rollups, empty result, case-insensitive, multi-repo), debounce test, expansion-state isolation test; manual: MT-BOOKMARK (type: tree filters; clear: restores incl. manual collapses; Cmd+F focus). Regression scope: MT-BOOKMARK.
acceptance_criteria: Panel header search field filters the bookmark tree (ancestors kept, transient expansion), speed search retained; model-level filter tests; MT-BOOKMARK rows.

title: Bookmarks panel: favourites/starred bookmarks
description: git4idea's Branches dashboard lets you star a branch so it sorts first within its group. jj-idea-b2ae's bookmarks panel (ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkTreeModel.kt) has no equivalent yet. Would need per-project persisted favourite names and a sort-favourites-first tweak in buildPrefixTree.
design:
PLAN: starred (favourite) bookmarks that sort first within their group, persisted per project.
Facts: tree built by `buildBookmarkTree(...)`/`buildPrefixTree(...)` (ui/log/bookmarks/BookmarkTreeModel.kt:217-250, :432-459) whose final ordering is `(prefixNodes + leaves).sortedWith(compareBy({ it !is BookmarkNode.Prefix }, { it.displayName.lowercase() }))` (:457-458: folders first, then alphabetical, case-insensitive); leaves are `BookmarkNode.Local/Remote/Tag` carrying `item.bookmark.localName`; the panel's context menu is built per node in `actionGroupFor(node)` (ui/log/bookmarks/JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:~506-560); persisted UI state precedent: per-window `LogWindowConfig` (e.g. `bookmarksPanelVisible`) and project `JujutsuSettingsState`. git4idea's Branches dashboard star: favourites sort first within their group and show a star icon.
Design:
1. State: `JujutsuSettingsState.favouriteBookmarks: MutableSet<String>` keyed by `"<repoPath>::<localName>"` (repo-qualified so multi-root projects don't share stars; local name without remote so a star applies to the local bookmark and its `@remote` rows). Persisted with the project (xmlb set of strings; the ajd0 reflective round-trip guard covers it). Stale names (deleted bookmarks) are ignored at read time and pruned lazily when the set is written (cap 500 entries).
2. Tree ordering: `buildPrefixTree` gets a `isFavourite: (BookmarkNode) -> Boolean` (default none) -> sort key `compareBy({ it !is Prefix }, { !isFavourite(it) }, { name })` so within a group: folders, then starred leaves, then the rest. A starred bookmark inside a `feature/x` prefix folder sorts first WITHIN that folder (group-local, matching git4idea); optionally also surface a "Favourites" pseudo-category at the top of the repo node with the starred bookmarks (Rec: NOT in v1 - the bead asks only for sort-first). Folder rollup: a folder containing a favourite could carry a small star badge (rollupOf extension) - skip v1.
3. UI: context menu item `Jujutsu.Bookmark.ToggleFavourite` (registered action, keymap-assignable: reads `BOOKMARK_TARGET` like Delete/Rename; text "Add to Favourites"/"Remove from Favourites" via update(), icon AllIcons.Nodes.Favorite / `AllIcons.Nodes.NotFavoriteOnHover`); starred rows render a leading small star (`AllIcons.Nodes.Favorite`) in `BookmarkNodeRenderer` (JujutsuBookmarksPanel.kt:~590-700) for Local leaves only; the log table's bookmark chips unchanged. Toggle -> settings write + `queueRebuild()`.
4. Persistence of expansion/selection across rebuild is existing behaviour (expandAll on rebuild; selection restore: check `restoreSelection` if present - starring reorders rows, selection should follow the node).
Decisions made without the user: Q: favourites pseudo-category? Rec no (sort-first as asked). Q: key by local name across remotes? Rec yes. Q: project vs application scope? Rec project (bookmark names are project-specific).
Scale: O(#favourites) set lookups during an O(B log B) sort already performed; no jj calls. Testing: tree-model tests (favourites sort first within folder and at top level; folders still first; case-insensitive; multi-repo keys isolated; stale names ignored), action update() tests (text toggles), settings round-trip; manual: MT-BOOKMARK (star/unstar via context menu, order changes, persists across restart, multi-root). Regression scope: MT-BOOKMARK, MT-SETTINGS (persistence).
acceptance_criteria: Bookmarks can be starred via context action; starred leaves sort first within their group with a star marker; persisted per project (repo-qualified); tests + MT-BOOKMARK rows.

title: Jujutsu context menu extensibility for third-party plugins
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/68

SergejSalnikov asked for the ability to add custom actions into the jj context menus from a
third-party plugin, the way the platform's own Vcs.Log.ContextMenu group works: declare a
group in plugin.xml, add-to-group it, done.

Today every jj context menu is assembled programmatically rather than declared: the log
context menu is built in ui/log/JujutsuLogContextMenuActions.kt:67-87 (a BackgroundActionGroup
populated by pulling individual actions out of ActionManager.getInstance().getAction("Jujutsu.…")),
and the working copy toolbar/context menu is built the same way in
ui/workingcopy/UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt:159-191. plugin.xml registers only five <group id=…>
entries (Jujutsu.OpenFileInRemote, Jujutsu.EditorGroup, Jujutsu.OpenInRemoteFromEditor,
Jujutsu.DiffEditorOpenInGroup, Jujutsu.OpenInRemoteFromHistory) — none of which covers the log
or working-copy context menu, so a third party has nowhere to add-to-group into.

Deliberately backlogged at P4: this is internal extensibility that benefits plugin authors,
not an external feature that benefits all users, so it comes after user-facing work. It is
also an API-stability commitment once shipped (a public extension point has to keep working
across releases), which is a further reason not to rush it.
design:
Declare stable, documented group ids in plugin.xml (e.g. Jujutsu.Log.ContextMenu,
Jujutsu.WorkingCopy.ContextMenu) and have the programmatic builders in
JujutsuLogContextMenuActions.kt and UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt include those groups rather
than replacing them, so contributed actions appear alongside the built-ins.

Open design question, to decide separately from the group ids: whether to also expose public
base action classes carrying the jj command executor (the requester's "bonus" ask), since that
is a bigger API-stability commitment than a couple of group ids.
acceptance_criteria: Declared, documented group ids in plugin.xml for log/working-copy/file-change context menus; AND decision recorded on whether LazyActionById / primaryActions lazy-resolution is still needed (retire or narrow, per notes).
notes:
2026-09-01: jj-idea-4lfi added Annotate to actions/filechange/FileChangeActionGroup.kt's programmatic builder (shared by the Working Copy panel and the log's commit details pane) - a third hardcoded-list builder alongside JujutsuLogContextMenuActions.kt and UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt already named in DESIGN. Widen this bead's scope to include it: a Jujutsu.FileChange.ContextMenu group id candidate, so the working-copy/commit-details file-change menu is also declared rather than assembled by hand once this refactor happens. No priority change - still P4, deliberately backlogged.
2026-10-04: Merged jj-idea-1y1j (LazyActionById revisit) into this bead as a post-refactor verification step. After the XML-declared groups land: (1) verify with the jj-idea-8awj unload harness (install-over-running-IDE, -Dide.plugins.snapshot.on.unload.fail=true, log tab open) that there is no ClassCastException and no leaked old action instances - XML groups are mutated in place by the platform on dynamic load/unload, so toolbar staleness should disappear; (2) check for any remaining Kotlin-constructed/captured action whose update() touches Project.stateModel/isJujutsu; (3) primaryActions() four actions (NewChange/EditChange/RebaseChangeToolbar/DescribeChangeToolbar): moot once in an XML group, else wrap in LazyActionById for structural safety. Default outcome: RETIRE LazyActionById only if (1) passes and (2) finds nothing; otherwise narrow it to remaining sites and document the rule in its KDoc ('any action captured outside an XML group must be resolved lazily'). Record decision here and update contributing.md Architecture/Threading. Regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-LOG-TABLE (toolbar), MT-CROSS (dynamic update). Related: jj-idea-wdqg (GH #135) lands first and establishes Jujutsu.GitFetch/GitPush ids as a stable contract; not a blocker.

title: Consider capability probing instead of version compare for JjFeature
description: JjFeature currently gates by comparing JjVersion against a minimum. For forks/distro builds (JjVersion.parse already handles 'jj companyname-0.39.0-abc123'), a probe (e.g. 'jj bookmark advance --help' exit code) might be more robust than version numbers. Version compare is adequate for now; revisit if a fork/distro mismatch is reported.
design:
PLAN: record the decision (defer; capability probing only as a documented fallback) and sketch the probe design for when a fork/distro mismatch is reported.
Facts: `JjFeature` (jj/JjFeature.kt:15-24) gates by `JjVersion >= minVersion` (`BOOKMARK_ADVANCE(0.39)`, `TAG_PUSH(0.44)`; further candidates from beads: FETCH_TAG(0.38) (2y4s), REBASE_SIMPLIFY_PARENTS(0.39) (7y2o)); `JjVersion.parse` (jj/JjVersion.kt, used by JjExecutableFinder.kt:211) already tolerates 'jj companyname-0.39.0-abc123'-style strings, so the version compare works for common distro/fork naming. A mismatch occurs when a fork reports an OLDER base version number but backports a feature, or reports a newer number without it.
Design (when needed): optional capability probes per feature: `JjFeature(minVersion, nameKey, probe: JjProbe? = null)` where `JjProbe` = a cheap read-only command whose exit code/stdout proves support: e.g. BOOKMARK_ADVANCE -> `jj bookmark advance --help` exit 0 (unknown subcommand exits 2); TAG_PUSH -> `jj git push --help` output contains `--tag`; FETCH_TAG -> `jj git fetch --help` contains `--tag`; REBASE_SIMPLIFY_PARENTS -> `jj rebase --help` contains `--simplify-parents`. Evaluate lazily on first use per (executable path, feature), cached in `JjAvailabilityChecker`'s result (jj/JjAvailabilityChecker.kt) and invalidated with it on exe path change; `supports(feature)` = `probeResult ?: (version >= min)` - probe wins when available, version is the fallback when the probe can't run (timeout/failure). Cost: one subprocess per probed feature at first use (<100 ms each, run on the pooled thread when the availability check runs, batched into one `jj --help`-style pass? separate calls are fine for <=5 features).
Why not now: version compare is deterministic, free (no subprocess), testable via fake versions (the existing `FeatureAvailabilityTest`), and no mismatch has been reported. Probing adds process spawns, parsing of help text (format may change between jj versions - itself a drift risk like jj-idea-spwt's), and complicates the Settings "features unavailable" list (et35 = version-based text).
Decisions made without the user: Q: implement now? Rec NO - keep as documented backlog until a real fork/distro report arrives; add a one-line escape hatch instead: a hidden Registry key `jj.feature.override=<comma list of enabled FEATURES>` letting such a user force-enable a feature (support burden minimal, no probing machinery). Reverse: build the probes.
Scale: none. Testing (if the registry override is added): `supports()` with/without override; manual: none. Related: jj-idea-gv1k (policy for retiring gates via MINIMUM bumps), jj-idea-et35.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded (defer probing; optional registry override); probe design retained for later.

title: Settings: list features unavailable with current jj version
description: Once there is more than one JjFeature gate (see jj-idea-asap), consider a Settings panel section enumerating gated features the user can't use yet and why. Not worth it for a single gate.
design:
PLAN: effectively DONE - recommend closing after a quick verification.
Evidence: Settings > Installation Help already lists gated features unavailable with the current jj: `JujutsuConfigurable` renders `featureLine(feature)` per unsupported `JjFeature` inside the Installation Help group (settings/JujutsuConfigurable.kt:~818-850, `featureLine` :892; comment at :818 "jj-idea-258c: folded in from the former standalone 'Feature Availability' group"), driven by `unsupportedFeatures(status)` (jj/JjFeature.kt:36-47) so it is automatically correct as gates are added. The bead's condition ("once there is more than one JjFeature gate") is met (BOOKMARK_ADVANCE 0.39, TAG_PUSH 0.44; further gates planned in 2y4s/7y2o) and the one-time nudge balloon exists (jj-idea-sov0 `notifyFeaturesGatedByVersion`).
Verification steps before closing: (1) run with a pinned old jj (scripts/jj-install-version.sh 0.37.0, set the executable path in Settings per contributing.md "Testing against multiple jj versions") and confirm the list shows both gated features with "(needs jj X)" text; (2) with current jj the group's feature list is empty/hidden; (3) when jj-idea-2y4s/7y2o add gates, their `displayName` bundle keys appear automatically (feature.<id>.name).
Decisions made without the user: Q: close? Rec yes (not closed by this pass). If you wanted a separate always-visible "Features" panel (not buried in Installation Help), that is a different request - say so.
Scale/Testing: existing `FeatureAvailabilityTest` (settings/) covers unsupportedFeatures; add one assertion that every `JjFeature` has a non-blank `displayName` bundle key (guard for new gates).
acceptance_criteria: Verified (old-jj run) that gated features are listed in Settings; bead closed as done; guard test for displayName keys.
close_reason: Done: Settings Installation Help already lists unavailable gated features (jj-idea-258c)

title: Decide policy for retiring JjFeature gates via JjVersion.MINIMUM
description: As JjVersion.MINIMUM is raised over time, some JjFeature gates become permanently satisfied and their checks/disabled-branches become dead code. Decide a policy: how far back to support, and a process for pruning satisfied gates.
design:
PLAN (policy bead - proposed policy; ratify or adjust).
Facts: `JjVersion.MINIMUM = 0.37.0` ("Required for change_offset feature", jj/JjVersion.kt:28); gates: `JjFeature` enum (jj/JjFeature.kt:15-24) BOOKMARK_ADVANCE 0.39, TAG_PUSH 0.44 (+ planned FETCH_TAG 0.38 (2y4s), REBASE_SIMPLIFY_PARENTS 0.39 (7y2o)); gating contract: visible-but-disabled with reason, never emulated (jj/JjFeature.kt KDoc, contributing.md); CI/dev test matrix: min + current jj (contributing.md "Testing against multiple jj versions", scripts/jj-install-version.sh).
Proposed policy:
1. Support window: MINIMUM = the jj release that is ~12 months old at the time of each plugin MINOR release, but never raised in a PATCH release; documented in contributing.md and CHANGELOG ("Requires jj X.Y or newer") with the release date of that jj version (jj ships roughly monthly; 12 months = ~12 minor versions: today 0.44 -> floor ~0.32-0.33; the current floor 0.37 is ~7 months behind 0.44 - consistent). Rationale: Linux distro packages and Homebrew/Scoop lag, enterprise/Piper users lag more; a 12-month window avoids stranding them while bounding the gate/compat burden.
2. Raising MINIMUM: a deliberate decision per plugin minor release, announced in the changelog one release ahead ("jj < X will stop being supported in the next release") and via the existing version-too-old notification (`notifyJjUnavailable`, JujutsuNotifications.kt:269) which already explains upgrade paths.
3. Pruning satisfied gates: when MINIMUM >= a feature's minVersion the gate is dead code: in the same PR that raises MINIMUM, delete the enum constant, its `isSupportedIn` checks and disabled-branch UI, bundle keys (`feature.<x>.name`, `action.disabled.requires.jj.version` uses) and tests; a unit test `no JjFeature gate has minVersion <= MINIMUM` (pure JVM over `JjFeature.entries`) fails the build if someone forgets - this is the process guard.
4. New gate vs raising floor: add a gate only for features that are clearly additive (menu entry/flag); if more than ~3 gates accumulate within 2 minor jj versions of the floor, consider raising MINIMUM instead.
5. Contract tests: keep Cli variants runnable against MINIMUM (JJ path override) and "current"; the multi-version CI job (blkg) pins both.
6. Interaction with jj-idea-cphn (capability probing): out of scope; version compare remains the mechanism.
Decisions made without the user (please ratify): window 12 months (vs 6/18/24); announce-one-release-ahead rule; the guard test. Reverse: adjust the window constant in contributing.md.
Scale/Testing: the guard test only; manual none. Acceptance: policy documented in contributing.md (new "jj version support policy" subsection) + guard test.
acceptance_criteria: Policy documented in contributing.md (support window, announce-ahead, prune-with-raise rule) and enforced by a guard test that no gate is <= MINIMUM.

title: Decide: one-time gated-feature nudge balloon
description: Deferred from bookmark-advance work (jj-idea-l7wd). Should we show a one-time-per-session balloon the first time a user hits any version-gated feature, or is the disabled action's tooltip enough? Needs real usage data before deciding.
design:
PLAN (decision bead - recommendation: NO additional balloon; keep disabled-with-tooltip, plus the existing one-time upgrade nudge).
Current mechanisms (verified): (1) version-gated actions are VISIBLE but DISABLED with the reason as description (`JjFeature.disabledReasonIn(project)`: "requires jj X.Y.Z (you have A.B.C)" - jj/JjFeature.kt, contract in its KDoc: "never hidden, never emulated"); (2) a one-time-per-install upgrade nudge balloon already exists: `FeatureUpgradeNudge` -> `JujutsuNotifications.notifyFeaturesGatedByVersion(project, version, gatedFeatures)` (ui/services/JujutsuNotifications.kt:458-483) listing ALL gated features once with an "Update jj..." action (jj-idea-sov0; guarded by a persisted shown-key); (3) Settings > Installation Help lists unavailable features (jj-idea-258c).
The question: ALSO show a balloon the first time the user actually USES (clicks) a gated entry in a session? Analysis: a disabled action cannot be "hit" (clicking does nothing; the tooltip is the explanation), so a hit-balloon would require making the action enabled-but-failing or intercepting clicks on disabled items (impossible in Swing menus). The nudge at project open already informs once; per-use balloons would nag and need a usage signal that doesn't exist.
Recommendation: close as "no": the combination (disabled+reason tooltip, one-time nudge, Settings list) covers discoverability; revisit only if user reports show confusion about greyed-out items despite the nudge (e.g. after raising MINIMUM and gating more features). If revisited: show the SAME nudge again after a plugin version bump that adds a gate (key the persisted shown-state by the set of gated features, so only NEW gates re-notify) - cheap and targeted: compare the stored feature-name set with the current gated set at project open.
Decisions made without the user: close as won't-do? Rec yes, with the "re-notify on newly added gate" idea recorded as the only enhancement worth doing. Reverse: reopen with usage data.
Scale/Testing: n/a for closure; for the enhancement: `FeatureUpgradeNudge` unit test (shown-set persisted, new gate triggers, same set silent). Manual: MT-SETTINGS/MT-WORKINGCOPY nudge row. Regression scope: none for closure.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded (no per-use balloon; optional re-notify for newly added gates); bead closable.

title: git blame fast path for colocated repos (backlog, conditional)
description:
GitHub #64 originally asked for a git-blame fallback when jj file annotate is slow. Initial reply rejected this outright; the OP's follow-up numbers (2M commits, colocated, jj annotate ~100s vs git blame ~1s, i.e. ~100x vs the ~5x reported in jj-vcs/jj#4878) make the case more compelling than first assessed, so this is recorded as a real backlog item rather than a closed door - but it stays low priority.

Why more plausible than first assessed: in a colocated repo, you could blame with git then batch-map hashes to change ids with a single `jj log -r <hashes>` call. That produces the same change-id substrate the annotation UI needs end-to-end, so it need not be a lower-fidelity second model. The commits that genuinely don't map (un-exported working copy, divergent changes) are recent lines, which the plugin already leaves unannotated today since it annotates at @- (JujutsuAnnotationProvider.kt:57-60).

Why it stays P4: scoping this to "just Code Vision hints" doesn't reduce the work. VcsCodeVisionProvider reads through CacheableAnnotationProvider and consumes the same FileAnnotation the gutter uses (JujutsuAnnotationProvider.kt:34-36) - there's no seam where hints alone get a different backend. A real implementation means a second parser, a second set of contract tests, and either duplicating or degrading per-change colors / Show Diff / Annotate Previous Revision for the git-blame path.
design: Gated feature, not scheduled: (1) colocated repos only, (2) blocked on jj-vcs/jj#4878 not being fixed upstream, (3) blocked on the OP posting their 100x numbers to jj-vcs/jj#4878 first - that's the direct ask back to them. If #4878 lands, this issue can likely be closed as moot.
acceptance_criteria: No acceptance criteria yet - this is a recorded, gated backlog decision, not scheduled work.
notes: Update: OP has already posted the 100s/1s numbers on jj-vcs/jj#4878. That thread also surfaced a likely root cause from mernen — remove_transitive_edges()/consume_to() in the revset graph walk tests every commit in ..@ against the file predicate, even for files only a couple commits deep — which suggests this may be an algorithmic fix upstream rather than a fundamental limit. Gate (3) from the original description ("blocked on OP posting numbers upstream") is satisfied; remaining gates are (1) colocated-only and (2) blocked on jj-vcs/jj#4878 progress.

title: Support jj bookmark advance
description: jj 0.39 added the 'jj bookmark advance' command for moving a bookmark forward along its own history. The plugin has bookmarkSetArgs/bookmarkCreateArgs/etc (CliExecutor.kt) but no advance support. Low-priority feature opportunity from the 0.38-0.43 changelog sweep; would need UI/UX design for how it surfaces in the bookmark widget.

title: Support jj show --reversed
description: jj 0.43 added '--reversed' to 'jj show', reversing diff/hunk ordering. Could be exposed in commit detail/diff views. Low-priority feature opportunity from the 0.38-0.43 changelog sweep.
design:
PLAN: recommend closing as not applicable; the premise is mistaken.
Verified with jj 0.44 (`jj show --help`): `--reversed` = "Show revisions in the opposite order (older revisions first)" - it reverses the ORDER OF REVISIONS when `jj show` is given multiple revisions, not "diff/hunk ordering" as the bead states. The plugin does not render `jj show` output: file content/diffs come from `file show`/`diff --git`/`--summary` (CommandExecutor.show(filePath, revision) is `jj file show`, jj/CommandExecutor.kt:161; diffs via IDE viewers), and multi-commit details ordering is the plugin's own (details pane stacks selected entries in selection order with `MAX_DISPLAYED_COMMITS = 20`, ui/log/JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt:293-330, combined diff oldest-first via `ChangeService.loadChanges(entries)`, jj/ChangeService.kt:17-24). There is no consumer for a `--reversed` flag, and if the details pane ever wanted a "newest/oldest first" toggle it would reorder client-side with no jj call.
Recommendation: close (not closed by this pass). If a "reverse order" toggle for multi-commit details is desired: tiny client-side feature (selection order vs oldest-first) - file separately with that title.
Scale/Testing/Manual: n/a.
acceptance_criteria: Closed as not applicable (flag reverses revision order, plugin has no jj show consumer) or re-scoped to a client-side order toggle.

title: Truncation ellipsis can land just outside the visible description cell edge
description: When the graph+description column is sized fractionally past the viewport edge, Swing clips the entire cell. The truncation budget in TruncatingLeftRightLayout.configure is availableForLeft = cellWidth - rightWidth, and FragmentLayout.truncateToFit computes the ellipsis to fit cellWidth — so the trailing '...' can be positioned just past the visible area and not be seen. Purely cosmetic: no scrollbar, no data loss. Possible fix: compute the truncation budget against the visible/clipped width rather than the nominal cellWidth, or reserve a few px of right padding so the ellipsis is always inside the visible region. Split out from jj-idea-8gli, whose wide-scroll claim was invalid.
design:
PLAN: reserve a small right inset in the truncation budget so the ellipsis always lands inside the visible cell (cosmetic fix).
Facts: `TruncatingLeftRightLayout.configure(leftCanvas, rightCanvas, cellWidth, background, rightHighlightTarget)` (ui/components/TruncatingLeftRightLayout.kt:143-166): `availableForLeft = (cellWidth - rightWidth).toDouble()` then `FragmentLayout.truncateToFit(leftCanvas.fragments, truncateRange, availableForLeft, font, frc)`; callers pass `cellWidth = columnWidth - textStart` (JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.configureTextPanel :~232 `cellWidth = columnWidth - textStart`). When the column's nominal width extends fractionally past the viewport (fit-to-width flex column, jj-idea-lzq7, or a sub-pixel scroll), Swing clips the cell, so an ellipsis positioned at the nominal edge is not visible.
Fix options: (1) simple: subtract a constant right inset in the budget: `availableForLeft = cellWidth - rightWidth - TRAILING_INSET` with `TRAILING_INSET = JBUI.scale(4)` (also gives the ellipsis a hair of breathing room like platform tables' cell padding); (2) precise: use the visible width: in the renderer, `val visibleRight = (table.parent as? JViewport)?.let { viewport -> min(columnRight, viewport.viewPosition.x + viewport.width) }` and compute `cellWidth = visibleRight - cellLeft - textStart` - correct but couples the cell content to scroll position: truncation would change while scrolling horizontally (re-layout per scroll tick; bad for the LaidOutCell caching planned in g7to and visually jumpy) -> rejected. Recommend (1).
Where: keep the inset inside `TruncatingLeftRightLayout.configure` (one place, covers the log table, file history and picker tables that share the layout); ensure the RIGHT panel's own width isn't reduced (the inset applies only to the left budget). Check `FragmentLayout.truncateToFit` KDoc for how it accounts the ellipsis width (the ellipsis itself must fit within `availableForLeft`).
Decisions made without the user: Q: inset size? Rec 4 scaled px. Reverse: tweak the constant.
Scale: none. Testing: layout unit test: for `cellWidth = W`, truncated left fragments' total painted width + ellipsis <= W - rightWidth - inset (assert via `FragmentLayout` measurement helpers in FragmentLayoutTest); existing truncation tests adjust expected widths by the inset; manual: MT-LOG-TABLE (resize columns / enable fit-to-width with the window narrower than the sum; ellipsis visible in long descriptions; no scrollbar change). Regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-GRAPH.
acceptance_criteria: Truncation budget reserves a trailing inset so the ellipsis is always visible; layout test; MT-LOG-TABLE check.

title: Wall-clock budget tests via IntelliJ platform Benchmark utilities
description:
Order-of-magnitude backstop complementing the deterministic operation-count tests. Use the platform's benchmark support — com.intellij.tools.ide.metrics.benchmark.Benchmark / PlatformTestUtil.assertTiming (see ../intellij-community) — which has attempt-retry logic to absorb machine noise. These can ride the existing platformTest task configuration (see build.gradle.kts platformTest setup and its coroutines-classpath filtering).

- Tag @Tag("perf"); excluded from the default PR gate, run locally on demand and by the nightly CI job (jj-idea-edjs.5).
- Generous budgets only (e.g. 10k-file ignore scan < 2s; 10k-entry log parse+layout < 1s) — these catch 10x regressions like GitHub #35, not 20% drift (the trend job handles drift).
design:
PLAN: perf-tagged budget tests with a dedicated Gradle task, generous order-of-magnitude budgets, built on the platform benchmark helpers.
Platform API facts (verify in ../intellij-community before coding): `com.intellij.tools.ide.metrics.benchmark.Benchmark` (platform/testFramework/... `Benchmark.newBenchmark(name) { block }.warmupIterations(n).attempts(k).start()`) and the older `PlatformTestUtil.newPerformanceTest(name, block).attempts(n).warmupIteration(m).start()` / `assertTiming`; both retry attempts to absorb noise and (in some versions) scale expectations by machine speed via `PlatformTestUtil.getUsefulTestCaseTimeScale`. Check which are available/stable for sinceBuild 251..262 test classpaths (build.gradle.kts platformTest uses the IJPGP original classpath, :393-440); prefer the newer `Benchmark` if present on the 2025.2 test framework jar, else a tiny in-repo `timeBudget(name, budgetMs, attempts = 3) { }` helper (run block, take best-of-N wall-clock with `System.nanoTime`, assert <= budget) - simple, dependency-free, and enough for 10x-regression detection. Rec: start with the in-repo helper (no API-compat risk across the IDE matrix), document the platform Benchmark as an upgrade path.
Design:
1. Tag `@Tag("perf")`; exclude from `test`, `platformTest`, `contractTest` (build.gradle.kts `excludeTags("platform","contract")` pattern at :154-156 and :393-ish includeTags) and from `check`; new task `perfTest` (`useJUnitPlatform { includeTags("perf") }`, same classpath/JVM args as platformTest - copy the config block rather than inheriting to keep exclusions explicit).
2. Tests (pure JVM unless noted): (a) ignore scan: `GitignoreCache.collectIgnored` over an in-memory `IgnoreScanNode` tree (the abstraction used by GitignoreScanTest: tests already build in-memory trees) of 10k tracked + 50k ignored entries with 5 nested .gitignore files: budget < 2 s (bead's number) - also a REAL-FS variant on a temp dir (10k files) for I/O realism; (b) log load+layout: parse a synthetic 10k-entry log output through `CliLogService.parse` + `topologicalSort` + `CommitGraphBuilder.buildGraph` + `GraphEdgeIndex.build`: budget < 1 s; (c) working-copy tree rebuild for 1k changes (`JujutsuChangesTree.buildTreeModel`, platform test) < 2 s; (d) paged window ops (`PagedLogWindow` + `LayoutCalculator.appendGraph`) for 100 pages < 1 s. Budgets are 10x typical to catch regressions like GitHub #35 only.
3. Output: each test prints `perf-budget: <name> best=<ms> budget=<ms>` (greppable) and writes a JSON line to `build/reports/perf/results.json` (name, bestMs, budgetMs, timestamp) for the nightly trend job (edjs.5).
4. Docs: contributing.md Performance & Scale: "run `./gradlew perfTest` before merging changes to refresh paths; not part of check".
Decisions made without the user: Q: in-repo helper vs platform Benchmark? Rec in-repo helper first. Q: run in PR CI? No (advisory only - the epic principle).
Scale: tests themselves are the scale artifacts. Testing: self-test the helper (fails when a block sleeps beyond budget; passes with retries on a noisy first attempt). Acceptance as bead: budget tests for ignore scan and log load/layout, excluded from default tasks, dedicated Gradle task, documented.
acceptance_criteria: Perf-tagged budget tests exist for ignore scan and log load/layout. Excluded from default test/check tasks; runnable via a dedicated Gradle task. Documented in contributing.md.

title: Nightly CI perf job with trend tracking (advisory, never PR-blocking)
description:
GitHub Actions scheduled (nightly/weekly) job that:
1. Generates the stress repo (jj-idea-edjs.4).
2. Runs the perf-tagged wall-clock suite (jj-idea-edjs.6) against it.
3. Records timings and tracks trend — e.g. benchmark-action/github-action-benchmark storing results on a branch, alerting/failing the nightly run when a result exceeds ~150% of baseline.

Strictly advisory: the PR gate runs only the deterministic operation-count tests (jj-idea-edjs.2). Wall-clock results never block PRs, so noisy timings cannot train contributors to ignore red builds. Failures open visibility (issue comment / workflow failure on the scheduled run) rather than blocking merges.
design:
PLAN: scheduled GitHub Actions workflow running `perfTest` (edjs.6) on a generated fixture (edjs.4 SMALL preset), recording trend with `benchmark-action/github-action-benchmark`, alert-only.
Facts: existing CI is `.github/workflows/build.yml` (jobs `changelog-check`, `compat`, `verify`, `build`; triggers push/PR/workflow_dispatch; no `schedule`); contractTest/stubTest are not run there yet (jj-idea-blkg). Runner variance on shared GitHub runners is large (20-50%): hence advisory + 150% alert threshold + trend rather than gating.
Design:
1. New file `.github/workflows/perf-nightly.yml`: `on: schedule: cron '17 3 * * *'` + `workflow_dispatch`; `permissions: contents: write` (to push the results branch) and `issues: write` if commenting; single job on `ubuntu-latest` (macOS runners cost 10x; document that absolute numbers are Linux-runner numbers); steps: checkout, setup-java 21 (same action/version as build.yml), Gradle cache (`gradle/actions/setup-gradle`), install jj (use the repo's `scripts/jj-install-version.sh 0.44.0` pinned or the latest release for the fixture generator), run `scripts/fixtures/fx-scale.sh` with `SMALL=1` into `build/fixtures`, run `./gradlew perfTest` (edjs.6) with `-Pperf.fixture=...` if tests use the real fixture, convert `build/reports/perf/results.json` to the action's `customSmallerIsBetter` JSON shape (a 10-line jq step), then `benchmark-action/github-action-benchmark@v1` with `tool: customSmallerIsBetter`, `gh-pages` or a dedicated `perf-results` branch (`gh-pages-branch: perf-data`, `benchmark-data-dir-path: dev/bench`), `alert-threshold: '150%'`, `comment-on-alert: true`, `fail-on-alert: true` (fails the NIGHTLY run only - no branch protection depends on it), `auto-push: true` on master only.
2. "Baseline stored; deliberately introduced 2x slowdown trips the alert": verification procedure documented in the PR: temporarily add `Thread.sleep` doubling in `GitignoreCache.collectIgnored` on a branch, `workflow_dispatch` the job on that branch with `auto-push: false`, confirm failure + comment, revert (record the run URL in the bead).
3. Trend visibility: README/contributing.md note linking the GitHub Pages chart (`https://<owner>.github.io/jj-idea/dev/bench/`) - enable Pages for the data branch (repo setting - needs the maintainer; flagged as a manual step).
4. Cost control: skip when no commits since last run (`if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.sha != cache of last tested sha` via actions/cache key) - minor; runtime target < 15 min.
5. Release hygiene: the workflow must not run on forks (`if: github.repository == 'kkkev/jj-idea'`) and must not use the publishing token/secrets.
Decisions made without the user: Q: Linux runner only? Rec yes. Q: fail-on-alert true (nightly only)? Rec yes (visibility). Q: Pages vs plain artifact? Rec the action's Pages chart (the bead asks for trend tracking) - requires enabling Pages; fallback = upload `results.json` as an artifact (history via artifacts retention 90 days).
Scale: CI-only. Blocked by edjs.4 and edjs.6 (as listed) - sequence .6 -> .4 -> .5. Testing: the verification procedure above; `actionlint` locally on the YAML. Manual: maintainer enables Pages / reviews first run.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduled workflow exists and passes on master. Baseline stored; a deliberately introduced 2x slowdown in a hot path trips the alert. README/contributing.md notes where to find trend data.

title: Stress-repo generator script/Gradle task for manual perf verification
description:
Formalize the informal stress-test repo (referenced in jj-idea-7jn1) into a reproducible generator: a script or Gradle task (e.g. ./gradlew generateStressRepo) producing a jj repo with parametric scale:
- ~100k tracked files in a realistic directory tree
- a ~500k-file node_modules-style ignored tree (plus nested .gitignore files exercising negation/anchoring)
- ~10k commits with branching/merging for graph layout stress
- a ~1k-file working set (modified + added + renamed)
- variants: colocated and non-colocated; optionally multi-root

Document in contributing.md as the required runIde smoke target for any change touching refresh paths, listeners, or traversals (ties into the CLAUDE.md rules bead). Also useful to give GitHub issue reporters a reproducible baseline.

Generation must be fast enough to run locally (minutes, cached output dir).
design:
PLAN: extend `scripts/fixtures/` with a deterministic large-FILE-tree generator `fx-scale.sh` (new) and a thin Gradle wrapper; reuse fx-stress.sh for the commit-graph dimension rather than duplicating it.
Existing: `scripts/fixtures/fx-stress.sh` (~1,084 commits, ~26 heads; `SCALE=<n>` multiplies commit counts, `WITH_REMOTE=1` pushes to a bare repo; header documents shape) covers the "~10k commits with branching/merging" bullet (SCALE=10) - the bead's other bullets (100k tracked files, 500k-file ignored node_modules tree, 1k-file working set, colocated/non-colocated/multi-root) are NOT covered.
Design:
1. `fx-scale.sh [target-dir]` with env knobs (all seeded via a `SEED` for deterministic names/content): `TRACKED_FILES=100000` (realistic tree: depth 4-6, 20-200 files/dir, mixed extensions; content = short seeded text so files are tiny and generation is I/O-bound), `IGNORED_FILES=500000` (node_modules-style: deep tree of many tiny files under `node_modules/`, `build/`, `.gradle/` + a nested `.gitignore` set exercising negation/anchoring/`**`/dir-only, mirroring the golden cases planned in jj-idea-2poe), `WORKING_SET=1000` (after the initial commit: modify 600, add 300, rename 100 via `git mv`-equivalent shell moves), `COMMITS=1` (or call fx-stress for graph scale via `WITH_GRAPH=1` sourcing it), `COLOCATE=1|0` (`jj git init --colocate` vs `jj git init`), `ROOTS=1..N` (multi-root: N sibling repos under target-dir).
   Speed: generate with `xargs -P`/a single awk/python helper creating files in bulk (500k files: use python3 `os.makedirs` + `open(...).write` in a tight loop ~ 60-90s on SSD; document expected timing); cache: skip generation if `target-dir/.fx-scale-stamp` records identical knob values + script hash; `--force` to rebuild.
2. Gradle: `tasks.register<Exec>("generateStressRepo")` (build.gradle.kts, group "verification") invoking the script with `-Pscale.dir=build/fixtures/scale` default dir and passing knobs via `-P` properties; NOT part of check/test.
3. Docs: contributing.md (Performance & Scale section, ~:530-610) gets "Required runIde smoke target for changes touching refresh paths, listeners or traversals" with the one command and expected baselines recorded from a first run on the maintainer's machine (e.g. "working-copy changes visible < Ns after open; ignored-scan completes in <Ns, UI never blocks"); docs/manual-tests.md Fixtures table gains the FX-SCALE row (the table at ~:59 lists FX-STRESS etc.).
4. Determinism check: run twice into two dirs and compare `find ... | sort | sha1sum` of the tree listing + `jj log` commit-id lists (commit ids vary with timestamps: set `JJ_TIMESTAMP`/`JJ_OP_TIMESTAMP`/`JJ_USER`/`JJ_EMAIL` env for reproducible ids) - acceptance "deterministically (seeded)".
5. Reporter baseline use: `scripts/fixtures/README` line for issue reporters: "run `./gradlew generateStressRepo -Pscale.files=...` and open it" to produce comparable reports.
Decisions made without the user: Q: Gradle task vs script only? Rec both (script is the implementation; task = discoverability). Q: default sizes at the bead's full scale (100k/500k)? Rec yes default FULL, with `SMALL=1` preset (10k/50k) for quick local runs and for CI smoke.
Scale: generation-time only (disk: ~1.5 GB at full scale with 4KB blocks - note in docs; gitignored output dir `build/fixtures`). Testing: script self-check mode (`--verify`: counts files/commits/working-set via jj and fails if off); CI uses SMALL preset; manual: run + open in runIde per the new docs. Acceptance as in the bead plus docs/manual-tests fixture row.
acceptance_criteria: One command produces the repo deterministically (seeded). Documented in contributing.md with expected baseline behavior (e.g. working-copy changes appear <Ns). Used by the nightly CI perf job (jj-idea-edjs sibling).

title: Performance guardrails: prevent latency/scale regressions
description:
Follow-up to GitHub #35 (ignore-scan regression, jj-idea-2570.1). That bug was an algorithmic/scale regression — O(repo-size) work on the refresh path — shipped because dev/test repos are small, nothing logged work counts, and no test asserted traversal scale. This epic builds layered guardrails so the next one is caught at design time, test time, or in user logs:

1. Instrumentation: timers AND work counters on hot paths, WARN above thresholds (counters are the robust detector — 'visited 1.8M entries' is a red flag on any hardware).
2. Operation-count scale tests: deterministic, PR-blocking assertions on work done, not wall-clock.
3. Docs + agent instructions: stated scale envelope and refresh-path rules in CLAUDE.md/contributing.md.
4. Stress-repo generator for manual runIde verification.
5. Nightly CI perf job with trend tracking (advisory, never PR-blocking).
6. Wall-clock budget tests via IntelliJ platform Benchmark utilities (order-of-magnitude backstop).
7. Runtime escape hatches: scan watchdog + setting to disable.

Principle: PR-blocking checks must be deterministic (operation counts); wall-clock is advisory/nightly only, so flaky timings never train contributors to ignore red builds.
design:
PLAN: epic is 5/8 complete; the remaining three children (edjs.4 generator, edjs.5 nightly job, edjs.6 wall-clock tests) are all P4 and chain in the order .6 + .4 -> .5. This pass wrote their designs (see each). Epic-level notes:
1. Existing assets to build on (verified): perf instrumentation `Logger.measurePerf("name", key) { report -> report.count(...) }` (util/Perf.kt:36-44) with WARN thresholds (edjs.1 done); deterministic operation-count scale tests (edjs.2, f21f done); Performance & Scale rules in contributing.md:530-610 (edjs.3 done); runtime escape hatches (edjs.7 done); informal fixtures ALREADY scripted: `scripts/fixtures/fx-stress.sh` (log graph/filter stress; `SCALE=<n>`, `WITH_REMOTE=1`), fx-stack.sh, fx-conflict.sh, fx-md-conflict.sh. edjs.4 therefore EXTENDS the fixtures family (a large-FILE-tree generator for ignore-scan/working-copy scale) rather than starting from nothing.
2. The GitHub #113 freeze investigation recorded in this epic's notes concluded platform-caused (HelpTooltip/Metal layer) - nothing to do here; keep the "stack-sample analysis" tip for future freeze reports: ask for thread dumps and check whether in.kkkev.jjidea frames are on the EDT first.
3. Epic closure criterion: all three children done OR explicitly deferred; recommend closing the epic after .4/.6 (local tooling) and leaving .5 (CI trend) until there is evidence of drift problems - it is advisory anyway.
Decisions made without the user: Q: keep P4 for the trio? Rec yes - the deterministic guardrails (the blocking ones) are done; these are nice-to-haves.
notes:
2026-09-17 update: toddjonker (GitHub #113, 2026-09-15) reports daily multi-minute IDE freezes that never self-recover - has to force-quit every time. This means IntelliJ's own ~5s freeze report is never written (it fires only once the EDT becomes responsive again), so the maintainer's earlier advice ("wait for it to end, then Help -> Collect Logs and Diagnostic Data") doesn't apply to this reporter's freezes. Distinct from the stack trace fixed in 0.8.16 (NewChangeAction -> invalidate() -> VfsUtil.markDirtyAndRefresh on EDT, GitHub #113's originally-reported error) - toddjonker's freezes are unattributed beyond correlation with starting to use the plugin.

2026-09-18 update: toddjonker caught one (2026-09-17 comment, threadDumps-freeze-20260917-163646 zip attached) - a 40s EDT freeze that survived long enough for IntelliJ's own freeze reporter to fire after all. Downloaded and inspected all 8 thread-dump samples plus report.txt/.throwable: every sample is stuck in the identical native stack - HelpTooltip.scheduleShow -> AbstractPopup.show -> ... -> CPlatformView.createMTLLayer -> sun.java2d.metal.MTLLayer.nativeCreateLayer (macOS Metal layer allocation for a tooltip popup). No in.kkkev.jjidea frames are executing anywhere in the dump (only idle coroutine-scope bookkeeping entries with no stack). Conclusion: this specific freeze is a JetBrains/macOS platform bug (native tooltip-layer creation hang), not caused by this plugin - consistent with IDEA 2026.2.3's release notes citing freeze fixes. Closing out this line of investigation for #113 rather than pursuing further; reply drafted asking the reporter to upgrade and report back only if freezes persist after 2026.2.3.

title: [perf] Graph layout LayoutCalculatorImpl becomes wide with many concurrent branches — O(n×lanes) rendering
description:
With the stress-test repo's 20 short feature branches + 5 long branches + octopus merge all visible simultaneously in the log, LayoutCalculatorImpl will assign up to 26+ concurrent lanes. JujutsuCommitGraph.paintComponent() draws all lane lines for every row regardless of whether they are visible in the viewport. With 1080 rows × 26 lanes × 2 (passthrough + connector lines), the paint loop is ~56k draw calls per full repaint.

TableCellRenderers are called once per visible row, but JujutsuCommitGraph paints all rows. JujutsuLogTable likely delegates to standard JTable painting which only paints visible rows, but the graph's graphNodes map (ChangeId → GraphNode) is constructed for all rows at load time including all lane data.

Fix: verify the graph renderer only paints visible rows (clip rectangle check); profile paintComponent on the stress-test repo.
notes: 2026-10-03: the O(sum of edge spans) build this bead accepted is now the dominant UI freeze on wide graphs (5-6 s on the EDT per page at ~47k rows in git/git) - tracked in jj-idea-2570.6.
close_reason: Bead's premise was stale (JujutsuCommitGraph.paintComponent() it targeted no longer exists - painting is a plain TableCellRenderer, Swing already clips to visible rows). Found and fixed the real quadratic: JujutsuGraphAndDescriptionRenderer.drawLinesToParents scanned every row above the one painting (O(visible rows x total rows) per repaint - the further down you scroll, the slower), and sc8m's hover path (graphTextStartX) rebuilt the whole GraphEdgeIndex on every mouse-move/scroll tick, bypassing its own cache. Fixed by extending GraphEdgeIndex with incomingEdges/outgoingEdges/stubEdgeAt (built once, O(rows + edge spans)) and routing graphTextStartX through the shared cached index; repaint cost is now O(visible rows x lanes), hover/scroll is O(1) per event. Also merged the renderer's and table's duplicate edge-index caches into one, and derived GraphNode.color from lane instead of a second copy of the palette. New tests: GraphEdgeIndexTest brute-force equivalence (6 DAG shapes) pins the rewrite as a pure refactor; GraphEdgeIndexScaleTest's new 'per-row paint work is independent of row offset' test pins the complexity fix (would have caught the original bug). ./gradlew check green. Filed jj-idea-jnqi (mergeAndNotify full relayout per refresh) and jj-idea-g7to (LaidOutCell per-paint layout, no cache) as separate follow-ups - both bounded, out of scope here. Manual runIde confirmation on the fx-stress fixture (and re-verifying jj-idea-06t5's hang) still needed - flagged to the user, not run in this session (no GUI driving available).

title: [perf] topologicalSort priority queue is O(n log n) on every log load — no incremental path
description:
topologicalSort() (ui/log/UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt:186-234) uses Kahn's algorithm with a PriorityQueue, which is O(n log n). With 1080 commits this is fine, but it runs on every log refresh (file save, VCS op, focus change triggers 300ms debounce). The sort is also called in loadExpanding() where it re-sorts the entire set including already-sorted entries.

loadExpanding() additionally calls repositories().flatMap { r -> r.logCache.all + expansionEntriesByRepo[r] } — with 1080 cached entries + expansion, this creates 1000+ intermediate list objects on every navigation press.

Fix: cache the sort order between refreshes; only re-sort when the entry set actually changes (use a content hash or version counter to detect no-op refreshes).
notes:
2026-09-26 - GitHub #69 retest on 0.8.17 confirms jj's own 'jj log -r "all()"' walk (~3s on ~7k commits) dominates end-to-end latency, not the plugin's Kotlin-side re-sort. Graduating paged log loading out of preview (jj-idea-2570.4) is the real fix; this bead's topologicalSort optimization stays P4 since it can't close that gap on its own.
2026-10-07: largely superseded. jj-idea-2570.7 moved the main-log hot path to logOrder() (O(n) position-based Kahn per repo + timestamp merge, UnifiedJujutsuLogDataLoader.kt). O(n log n) topologicalSort now only on cold LogCache.fetch and CommitPickerPanel. Remaining (optional, P4): skip re-ordering when the entry set is unchanged (logOrder call sites ~:191/:441); consider logOrder in LogCache.fetch.

title: Add icon for conflict action
design:
PLAN: give the Resolve Conflicts actions a consistent icon. Inventory first: three actions, only one has an icon today.
Facts: `ResolveAllConflictsAction` (actions/file/ResolveAllConflictsAction.kt:22-26) uses `AllIcons.Vcs.Merge`; `ResolveSelectedConflictsAction` (actions/file/ResolveSelectedConflictsAction.kt:35-39) passes `null` icon; the log context-menu factory `resolveConflictsAction(project, entry)` (actions/change/resolveConflictsAction.kt:15-20) - check its icon argument (likely none); Accept-side actions (`AcceptConflictCurrentSideAction`/`LastSide`, plugin.xml:~145-150) have none; the plugin's own conflict glyph is `JujutsuIcons.Conflict` (red fill, JujutsuIcons.kt:51) used in status brackets and `BookmarkConflict` for bookmarks; the 'Jujutsu' actions elsewhere use plugin icons (Squash, Split, Describe, NewChange...).
Recommendation: use `AllIcons.Vcs.Merge` (platform's merge/resolve glyph, already on Resolve All and familiar from the IDE's own "Resolve Conflicts" entries) for the three RESOLVE actions (all / selected / log row) for consistency with the IntelliJ-native tenet (UX priority: IntelliJ-native > jj-native > bespoke, jj-idea-2ffd), and `JujutsuIcons.Conflict` only for STATUS indicators (it means "this has a conflict", not "resolve it"); Accept-side actions: no icon (they're sub-items, labelled "Accept Side #1/#2") - or a check/arrow glyph if you want parity: leave unchanged.
Where: pass `AllIcons.Vcs.Merge` as the icon in `ResolveSelectedConflictsAction`'s constructor (:38 `null` -> icon) and in `resolveConflictsAction(...)` (:15-20), keep Resolve All. The conflict EDITOR banner (JujutsuConflictEditorNotificationProvider) actions: check for icons too (S1 banner "Open Merge Tool" etc.) - leave.
Decisions made without the user: Q: platform glyph vs custom 'conflict action' SVG (the bead title 'Add icon for conflict action')? Rec platform Merge glyph (zero art, consistent, theme-safe). Reverse: draw `resolveConflict.svg` later and swap the three references.
Scale: none. Testing: action presentation tests asserting `templatePresentation.icon` non-null and identical across the three; manual: MT-CONFLICT/MT-CTXMENU menus (icons present in log menu, changes tree menu, editor group). Regression scope: MT-CONFLICT, MT-CTXMENU.
acceptance_criteria: All three Resolve Conflicts actions carry AllIcons.Vcs.Merge; status indicators keep JujutsuIcons.Conflict; presentation test; MT-CONFLICT/CTXMENU check.

title: Add icon for divergent commits
design:
PLAN (bead has no description): add a dedicated icon for DIVERGENT commits (a change id with more than one visible commit) and use it where divergence is currently text-only.
Facts: divergence is detected via `LogEntry.isDivergent` (the change id carries an offset, `ChangeId.divergent` = `offset != null`, jj/ChangeId.kt:28) and rendered only as the coloured text tag `status.divergent` in the status bracket (`appendSummaryAndStatuses`, ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:469-471: `colored(JujutsuColors.DIVERGENT) { append(message("status.divergent")) }`, no icon); the change id text shows the `/<offset>` suffix (`ChangeId.short`, ChangeId.kt:26). Other statuses have icons: `JujutsuIcons.Conflict` (red fill), `Immutable` (LogEntryText.kt:~460-478), working copy `@`.
Design:
1. Icon concept: a "fork" motif - one node splitting into two diverging arrows/dots (distinct from the branch icon `AllIcons.Vcs.Branch` and from conflict's cross/!) in the DIVERGENT colour (`JujutsuColors.DIVERGENT`, already themed); `icons/divergent.svg` single-colour, `JujutsuIcons.Divergent = fillIcon("/icons/divergent.svg", JujutsuColors.DIVERGENT-equivalent)` (JujutsuIcons.kt:51-76 pattern; conflict uses `fillIcon(..., RED)`).
2. Use: (a) status bracket: `colored(DIVERGENT) { append(icon(JujutsuIcons::Divergent)); space(); append(message("status.divergent")) }` mirroring the conflict part (:462-467); (b) log row text path: `appendStatusIndicators(entry)` in LaidOutCell (ui/log/LaidOutCell.kt) when `columnManager.showStatus` - check whether divergence has an indicator there today (conflict/@ do) and add the icon in the same place so rows with divergent ids stand out without opening the details; (c) tooltip/details via the shared function; (d) bookmarks panel conflicted-bookmark rows have their own icon (`BookmarkConflict`) - unrelated.
3. Accessibility: icon + text label retained in details (colour alone insufficient).
Decisions made without the user: Q: who draws? Rec I draft the SVG; you review (same as kcgf/bk7s/pr39). Q: where to show in the table? Rec: same slot as the conflict icon.
Scale: none. Testing: resource-exists test; canvas test (status bracket contains the icon for divergent entries only); manual: MT-LOG-TABLE/MT-LOG-DETAILS with a divergent change (make one with `jj describe --at-op` trick or fx-conflict-like fixture script: add `scripts/fixtures/fx-divergent.sh` creating a divergent change via `jj new @- -m x; jj describe` twice with `--at-op`... simplest: `jj bookmark`-less approach: `jj describe -r X --at-op=@-` creates divergence) - include the fixture script in the PR. Regression scope: MT-LOG-TABLE, MT-LOG-DETAILS.
acceptance_criteria: Divergent commits show a dedicated themed icon in the status bracket and row status indicators (text label retained); fixture + tests.

title: Select changes for PR
description: When reviewing a PR, it would be really helpful to be able to filter the log by commits (and their parents) for a specific PR, select commits on the PR, and to include/exclude merge commits and commits merged from other branches, to distinguish actual changes from merges.
design:
PLAN: "Select changes for PR" = filter the log to a PR's commits with merge/side-branch toggles. Build it from existing filter machinery plus two small additions; real GitHub PR integration (jj-idea-osyk) is out of scope here but can feed it later.
Existing building blocks: the log supports a client-side REVSET filter chip (`JujutsuRevsetFilterComponent`, ui/log/JujutsuRevsetFilterComponent.kt: resolves the typed revset to a `ChangeKey` set via one ids-only `jj log` per repo, intersected with the other chips in `JujutsuLogTableModel`'s filter pipeline), the Reference filter (bookmark/tag -> ancestors? `JujutsuReferenceFilterComponent`), and the table's multi-selection + combined diff in the details pane. A PR's commits in jj terms = `<base>..<head>` (e.g. `main..feature` = `ancestors(feature) ~ ancestors(main)`), where base is the target branch bookmark and head the PR bookmark/change.
Design (three small pieces):
1. Quick action "Filter Log to Commits Not in <base>" on a bookmark/change (log + bookmarks panel context menus): sets the revset chip to `<base>..<head>` where `head` = the clicked bookmark/change id and `base` = `trunk()` by default (jj's built-in alias; exact `main@origin` when the user picks via a small popup of remote bookmarks/trunk()). Implementation = `revsetFilterComponent.setRevset("trunk()..<head>")` via `stateModel`/panel API (the chip exposes `currentRevset`; add `setRevsetFromAction(revset)` + `reresolve()` call) - no new filter machinery.
2. Merge handling toggle: a second revset-chip preset toggle "Exclude merge commits" that ANDs `~merges()` into the active revset expression: do this as a model-level predicate rather than text surgery: `JujutsuLogTableModel` gets `hideMergeCommits: Boolean` (entry.parentIds.size > 1) applied in the same pipeline (cheap, no jj call; entries are loaded) - since the revset resolves to a key set, merges inside the set are dropped by the predicate; "commits merged from other branches" = side-branch commits brought in by merges: for a PR branch that merged `main` in, `trunk()..head` already EXCLUDES trunk's commits (that's the point of the range), so the remaining noise is the merge commits themselves -> the toggle covers it. The "include/exclude merge commits and commits merged from other branches" bullet is thereby satisfied; a stricter "first-parent only" option (`first_ancestors(head)` revset) can be a variant: toggle "First-parent only" -> `first_ancestors(<head>) ~ ::<base>`.
3. Selection helper: "Select All Commits Shown" (Ctrl+A in the table already selects rows; with the filter active it selects exactly the PR's commits) -> details pane shows the combined diff of all selected (existing multi-select behaviour: `ChangeService.loadChanges(entries)` zips changes oldest-first); add a title line in the details pane "N changes, combined diff" when multiple (check existing).
4. Out of scope: fetching PR metadata from GitHub (osyk); naming the PR; `jj git push --change`.
Decisions made without the user: Q: where is the base from? Rec `trunk()` default + popup to override; remember last base per repo in `LogWindowConfig`. Q: implement as chip presets vs new dialog? Rec presets/actions (reuse). Q: first-parent variant in v1? Rec yes as the second toggle (cheap).
Scale: one revset resolution (ids-only `jj log`, existing path) per filter change; merge toggle O(loaded rows) client-side; no per-commit calls. Testing: unit tests for revset construction (trunk base, bookmark head, remote head, first-parent variant) and the merge predicate in `JujutsuLogTableModelFilterTest` style; action update tests; manual: MT-LOG-FILTER (right-click bookmark `feature` -> Filter Log to Commits Not in trunk(): only PR commits; toggle merges off; select all -> combined diff). Regression scope: MT-LOG-FILTER, MT-BOOKMARK.
acceptance_criteria: Context action filters the log to <base>..<head> via the revset chip; hide-merges and first-parent-only toggles; combined diff of all selected via existing multi-select; tests + MT-LOG-FILTER rows.

title: Spike: custom annotation gutter rendering via LineMarkerRendererEx
description: Explore using LineMarkerRendererEx with Position.CUSTOM to render annotations with full TextCanvas-style rich rendering (multiple styled segments per line) instead of the standard single-string-per-column API.
design:
## Research Summary (April 2026)

### Standard API Limitation
TextAnnotationGutterProvider (editor-ui-api) supports only single-string, single-color, single-font per line per column. EditorGutterComponentImpl.paintAnnotationLine() does one g.drawString() call with no hooks or overrides. This is the only supported rendering path for annotation gutters.

### LineMarkerRendererEx Approach
LineMarkerRendererEx (platform-impl, NOT public API) with Position.CUSTOM receives a paint rectangle spanning x=0, w=getWidth() — the entire gutter. Paint order: paintAnnotations() (line 446) then paintLineMarkers() (line 466), so LineMarkerRenderer paints OVER annotations.

**Implementation plan:**
1. Register a filler TextAnnotationGutterProvider that reserves column width but renders empty strings
2. Register a RangeHighlighter spanning the annotated lines with a LineMarkerRendererEx(Position.CUSTOM)
3. In paint(), use EditorGutterComponentEx.getAnnotationsAreaOffset() and getAnnotationsAreaWidth() to position painting
4. Draw rich content with Graphics2D — multiple styled text segments per line (change ID in change ID color, author in author color, etc.)
5. Reimplement mouse handling: clicks, hover, tooltips — the gutter's internal event dispatch doesn't know about painted-over content

**Key files in intellij-community:**
- LineMarkerRendererEx: platform/platform-impl/src/com/intellij/openapi/editor/markup/LineMarkerRendererEx.java
- EditorGutterComponentEx: platform/platform-impl/src/com/intellij/openapi/editor/ex/EditorGutterComponentEx.java (has getAnnotationsAreaOffset/Width)
- EditorGutterComponentImpl paint order: platform/platform-impl/src/com/intellij/openapi/editor/impl/EditorGutterComponentImpl.java lines 440-466
- DiffLineSeparatorRenderer uses Position.CUSTOM: platform/diff-impl/src/com/intellij/diff/util/DiffLineSeparatorRenderer.java

**Risks:**
- LineMarkerRendererEx is in platform-impl, not the public API — can change without notice (no @ApiStatus.Internal but no stability guarantee)
- EditorGutterComponentEx.getAnnotationsAreaOffset/Width are also platform-impl
- Paint order (annotations before line markers) is an implementation detail
- Must reimplement event handling (click dispatch, tooltips, hover) — the gutter's internal systems won't know about painted-over content
- Filler provider must request enough width, but actual column widths are computed internally by EditorGutterLayout

**Mitigating factors:**
- LineMarkerRendererEx has been stable since 2015
- DiffLineSeparatorRenderer (platform's own diff system) uses Position.CUSTOM, suggesting some stability
- No existing plugin uses this for annotation rendering, so it's uncharted territory

**Spike should verify:**
1. Can we actually paint styled text segments over the annotation area?
2. Does click dispatch work or do we need to handle all mouse events ourselves?
3. Does tooltip rendering work or do we need manual tooltip logic?
4. How does the filler provider's width calculation interact with the actual painting?
5. Does this work in both classic and new UI?

title: Open in Remote: support self-hosted GitHub Enterprise and GitLab instances
description: Extend remote URL detection beyond github.com and gitlab.com to support self-hosted instances. The IntelliJ git plugin does this by probing /api/v3/meta (GitHub Enterprise) and /api/v4/metadata (GitLab) endpoints. For our plugin, a simpler approach might be to let users configure known self-hosted remotes in plugin settings. Prerequisite: jj-idea-4kg.8 (commit view must be working first).
design:
PLAN: user-configured self-hosted hosts (GitHub Enterprise, self-hosted GitLab, Forgejo/Gitea) classified by host name; NO network probing in v1. Shared with the remote-provider work in jj-idea-06tq.3.
Facts: `RemoteUrlBuilder.parseBaseUrl(remoteUrl)` (actions/git/RemoteUrlBuilder.kt:~96-122) accepts SSH `git@host:path(.git)` and HTTPS `https://host/path(.git)`, then `hostKind(host)` returns GITHUB for exactly `github.com`, GITLAB for `gitlab.com`, else null (:~124-128), so any other host yields no "Open in Remote" entries. `RemoteKind` enum (GITHUB, GITLAB) carries label+icon (:11-14); URL shapes differ per kind (`/commit/<hash>`, GitLab `/-/commit/<hash>`, file URLs `/blob/...` vs `/-/blob/...` with different line-fragment forms, :~65-90). Forgejo/Gitea (GH #92) URL shapes: `/commit/<hash>`, `/src/commit/<hash>/<path>` for files with `#L10-L12` fragments (verify against a Forgejo instance docs: file URL = `<base>/src/commit/<sha>/<path>#L<n>`), and an icon (none in AllIcons: add `forgejo.svg` like `gitlab.svg`, or reuse a generic repo icon).
Design:
1. Settings: application-level list `JujutsuApplicationSettings.selfHostedRemotes: MutableList<SelfHostedHost(host: String, kind: RemoteKind)>` (e.g. `git.example.com` -> GITHUB_ENTERPRISE/GITLAB/FORGEJO), edited in Settings > Version Control > Jujutsu > "Open in Remote": a small table (Host, Type) with Add/Remove + validation (hostname chars only, no scheme/path). Application-level (hosts apply across projects) - Rec; per-project override out of scope.
2. `RemoteKind` gains `FORGEJO` (and `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE` can reuse GITHUB URL shapes: same paths as github.com - treat as kind GITHUB with a custom host); `hostKind(host)` consults `builtin[host] ?: settings.selfHostedRemotes.firstOrNull { it.host.equals(host, ignoreCase = true) }?.kind`; `parseBaseUrl` also handles `ssh://git@host:port/path.git` and `https://host:port/...` (ports - common on self-hosted: strip the SSH port, keep an HTTPS port in base) - add cases.
3. IntelliJ's own approach (probing `/api/v3/meta` / `/api/v4/metadata`) is rejected for v1: network calls from a context-menu update path (must be instant), auth-gated instances return 401/redirects, and the settings list is explicit and predictable. Optional follow-up: a one-time "Detect host type" button in the settings row that probes the two endpoints on demand (user-initiated, with progress) to prefill the type - nice-to-have.
4. UI: kind label/icon in menus (`RemoteKind.label` "Forgejo", icon); the 0/1/2+ remote visibility logic (`applyRemoteVisibility`) unchanged.
5. Unrecognised host hint: when a remote URL has an unknown host, the Open-in-Remote group stays hidden today (silent). Add, only in the editor/log "Open in Remote" popup when ALL remotes are unrecognised, a disabled entry "Unknown host '<host>' - add it in Settings" linking to the settings page (discoverability) - small.
Decisions made without the user: Q: probing vs configuration? Rec configuration (+ optional detect button later). Q: kinds? Rec GITHUB (covers GHE), GITLAB, FORGEJO (covers Gitea/Codeberg - same URL scheme; verify Gitea compat). Q: ports? Rec handle.
