Scale: O(#configured hosts) per URL classification (tens). Testing: `RemoteUrlBuilderTest` additions: self-hosted GHE/GitLab/Forgejo hosts with/without ports in ssh/https forms, commit and file URLs with line ranges per kind, case-insensitive host, unknown host null; settings round-trip; manual: MT-GIT/MT-DIFF Open in Remote (configure a host, open commit/file URLs correct). Regression scope: MT-DIFF (editor Open in Remote), MT-CTXMENU (log), MT-SETTINGS. Related: jj-idea-06tq.3 (provider classification) should reuse this function.
acceptance_criteria: Configured self-hosted hosts (GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, Forgejo) produce correct commit/file URLs incl. ports; settings table; unknown-host hint; tests.
notes: GitHub #92 (CaptaiNiveau, 2026-08-26): add Forgejo to the self-hosted-instance detection list alongside GitHub Enterprise and self-hosted GitLab.

title: GitHub/GitLab PR/MR integration
description: Create, view, and list pull requests and merge requests from within the IDE. Future epic for deep forge integration.
design:
PLAN (epic-scale, backlog; this is the architecture decision + phase plan so children can be cut when it is prioritised). GitHub #92 (Forgejo) and #68/jj-idea-66id (pluggable SPI, in-house 'send for review' tooling) shape it.
Principles: (1) a FORGE SPI, not per-provider branches; (2) authentication delegated to the IDE's existing GitHub/GitLab accounts where possible, never a plugin-owned token store (same stance as jj-idea-06tq); (3) read-only listing first; creation flows after.
Architecture:
 - SPI: `interface ForgeProvider { val kind: ForgeKind; fun matches(remote: GitRemote): ForgeRepoRef?; suspend fun listChangeRequests(ref, filter): List<ChangeRequest>; suspend fun get(ref, id): ChangeRequest; suspend fun create(ref, spec): ChangeRequest; fun webUrl(...) }` with data model `ChangeRequest(id, title, state, sourceBranch/bookmark, targetBranch, author, url, checks?)`. Registered through an application-level EP `in.kkkev.jj-idea.forgeProvider` (dynamic) so third parties can contribute (Sergej's in-house tooling = a provider that implements only `create`/`web`). Built-in providers: GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo (Forgejo/Gitea API is GitHub-like `/api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`).
 - Host classification reuses the URL/kind machinery being extended in jj-idea-ecyd (self-hosted hosts config) and 06tq.3: `RemoteUrlBuilder.parseBaseUrl` -> `ForgeRepoRef(baseUrl, owner, repo, kind)`.
 - Authentication: for GitHub/GitLab use the IDE's bundled accounts when available (`org.jetbrains.plugins.github` / `org.jetbrains.plugins.gitlab` expose `GHAccountManager`/`GitLabAccountManager` - optional dependencies, internal-ish APIs: REVIEW stability before depending; fallback = personal-access-token entry stored in `PasswordSafe` (platform API, per-forge-host), with scopes help text); Forgejo: token in PasswordSafe only.
 - jj mapping: a PR is a (source bookmark -> target bookmark) pair: the plugin already knows bookmarks, remotes, push state (`pushAvailability`, `hasPushedAncestor`); "Create PR" = ensure the bookmark is pushed (reuse `checkAndPush`), then API create with head = bookmark, base = trunk bookmark; show PR state chips on bookmark rows (bookmarks panel leaf: `#123 open`) and a "Pull Requests" tool-window tab listing PRs with checkout (= `jj new <bookmark>@origin`) and "Show in log" (= filter to `<base>..<head>` per jj-idea-8lyd).
Phases: P1 provider SPI + GitHub read-only list/open-in-browser (no auth for public repos; token for private); P2 PR chips on bookmarks + "Filter log to PR" (8lyd); P3 create PR (push + API); P4 GitLab MR + Forgejo; P5 comments/checks (out of scope).
Risks: API rate limits (cache with ETag, fetch on demand + manual refresh, never on the VCS refresh path - scale rule), GitHub Enterprise hosts (config from ecyd), token storage review, maintenance burden of provider APIs (keep the SPI minimal), conflicts with the IDE's own GitHub plugin (users may prefer it: detect and offer to defer).
Decisions made without the user: Q: build on the IDE GitHub/GitLab plugins' accounts vs own token store? Rec: PasswordSafe token store v1 (simple, no internal-API coupling) with optional account import later. Q: scope for first release? Rec P1+P2 only. Q: SPI public? Rec yes (EP dynamic) - serves #68/Sergej.
Scale: network calls on demand, cached; nothing on the refresh path. Testing: provider contract tests against recorded fixtures (WireMock-style JSON files), URL/ref parsing tests, SPI registration test; manual MT sections per phase. Not scheduled - needs the user's go-ahead on the phase plan.
acceptance_criteria: Phase plan and SPI decisions approved; children cut per phase when prioritised.
notes: GitHub #92 (CaptaiNiveau, 2026-08-26): please also support Forgejo when forge integration lands, alongside GitHub/GitLab. Tied to #68 (jj-idea-66id): the forge layer should be a pluggable SPI rather than hard-coded per-provider branches, since SergejSalnikov independently wants to plug in their own in-house 'send for review'/'submit' tooling on #68 — a proper forge SPI would let Forgejo (and custom forges) be one implementation rather than a special case.

title: Provider-integrated clone
description: Specify GitHub/GitLab credentials, list remotes, and clone repositories without copy-pasting URLs. Includes authentication management for different providers.
design:
PLAN: provider-integrated clone as an extension of the existing clone dialog tab; reuse the IDE's own GitHub/GitLab account infrastructure rather than building credential management (same principle as jj-idea-06tq's "no plugin-owned tokens").
Facts: the plugin already contributes a clone tab: `JujutsuCloneExtension : VcsCloneDialogExtension` (clone/JujutsuCloneExtension.kt) creating `JujutsuCloneComponent` (clone/JujutsuCloneComponent.kt: URL `TextFieldWithHistory`, directory field, "colocate" checkbox; validation via `CloneDvcsValidationUtils`; clone runs `CommandExecutor.gitClone` under `Task.Backgroundable`, then opens the project with `ProjectUtil`). The IDE's clone dialog (Welcome > Get from VCS) also hosts provider tabs from the GitHub/GitLab plugins ("GitHub" / "GitLab" account-based repo lists) which clone via the IDE's GIT checkout provider, not jj - so a user cloning from those tabs gets a Git repository, not a jj repo.
Design (phased; only the cheap, token-free parts first):
 1. Phase 1 - repo URL helper without credentials: in the Jujutsu clone tab add a "Browse accounts..." affordance? That needs the account APIs. Cheaper: "Paste URL" quality-of-life: normalise GitHub/GitLab web URLs (`https://github.com/org/repo`, `.../tree/main`, `git clone ...` pasted text) to clone URLs; detect SSH vs HTTPS suggestions; Clone via HTTPS uses git credential helper (jj shells to libgit2/git transport: auth via the user's configured credential helper/ssh-agent). Show a hint "Authentication uses your Git credential helper or SSH agent".
 2. Phase 2 - account-backed repo list: OPTIONAL dependency on the IDE's GitHub plugin (`org.jetbrains.plugins.github`) and GitLab plugin: list repositories for accounts already signed in via Settings > Version Control > GitHub, using their `GHAccountManager` + `GHGQLRequests`/REST helpers or the shared `com.intellij.openapi.vcs.ui.cloneDialog.RepositoryUrlCloneDialogExtension`/`VcsCloneComponent` base used by git4idea's GithubCloneDialogExtension (`GHCloneDialogExtension`) - subclass-style reuse is not available (internal to those plugins); the stable surface is the platform's `RepositoryUrlCloneDialogExtension` (`com.intellij.openapi.vcs.ui.cloneDialog.RepositoryUrlCloneDialogExtension`, check @ApiStatus) which provides a list+search UI over `RepositoryUrlCloneDialogExtension.RepositoryListItem`s: implement a `JujutsuGitHubCloneExtension` that fetches items from the GitHub plugin's API (reflection-free via optional `<depends optional=true config-file="jj-github.xml">org.jetbrains.plugins.github</depends>` with a separate descriptor so the plugin loads without it). Needs verification of public API stability in the GitHub plugin (their classes are not API: risk of breakage per IDE version) - decide after reading ../intellij-community/plugins/github.
 3. Authentication management: NOT built - sign-in lives in the IDE accounts UI (link to Settings > Version Control > GitHub); for hosts without IDE account support (self-hosted Forgejo) the URL field remains.
 4. After clone: initialise as jj repo (done by `jj git clone`), open project (existing).
Decisions made without the user: Q: how far? Rec Phase 1 now (cheap polish), Phase 2 only if GitHub plugin API proves stable enough (spike), Phase 3 never (no token store). Q: relation to 06tq 'clone to create project': same feature - link beads.
Scale: network list calls on demand with paging (provider's own); nothing on refresh paths. Testing: URL normaliser unit tests (web URL, tree/blob URLs, `git@` forms, trailing `.git`, whitespace, `git clone` prefix), validation tests; Phase 2: fake provider seam tests; manual: MT-CLONE? (add section) - Get from VCS > Jujutsu: paste web URL, colocate option, clone, project opens; with GitHub plugin account (phase 2). Regression scope: MT-CROSS, new clone rows.
acceptance_criteria: Phase 1 URL normaliser + auth hint in the Jujutsu clone tab; phase 2 account-backed list gated on API stability spike; no plugin-owned credential store; tests.

title: Tidy display of parents
description: Find a more compact UX for displaying the parents. They can still be displayed in a smaller font, but maybe to the right of the current change id (rather than below) and with some kind of symbol (colon? arrow?) indicating that the change id represents a parent, or that the working copy inherits from or extends those parents. Find an appropriate UX here.
design:
PLAN (label for-human - UX taste call; options + recommendation so you can pick quickly).
Current rendering: `TextCanvas.appendParents(entry)` (ui/components/LogEntryText.kt:335-342) = `smaller { "Parents:" + each parent key (change id) separated by spaces }` or `details.parents.none`; used in the details pane (ui/log/JujutsuCommitDetailsPanel.kt:301, a separate line under the summary/status bracket) and the Working Copy panel's current-change label (ui/workingcopy/WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt:468). Parent ids are styled change ids (bold shortest prefix + grey remainder) and are links that navigate the log (ChangeNavigationClick).
Options (visual sketches):
 A. Inline after the id, small grey, with an arrow glyph - `qpvuntsm  ← rsyxzmkp  ← ... [@]`: id then "◂ parents" arrow chip: compact, one line saved; arrow direction convention: jj's graph shows parents BELOW children, so "↓ rsyxzmkp" (down-arrow = parent) matches the log's vertical direction; for merges `↓ rsyxzmkp, tzkvwuxn`.
 B. Parenthesised suffix on the status bracket line: `[@ working copy, empty] (parent: rsyxzmkp)` - reuses the existing `appendBracket` status line (LogEntryText.kt:~480) to avoid a new line; long for merges.
 C. Keep a separate line but with a leading glyph instead of the word "Parents:" (`↓ rsyxzmkp tzkvwuxn`) and a tooltip "Parent changes" - minimal change, still own line.
 D. Show parents only on hover/expand (progressive disclosure): collapsed `↓ 2` badge for merges, expands on click - good for octopus merges, adds interaction cost.
Recommendation: A for the details pane header row (id + parents on one line; wraps naturally via the existing unbreakable-chip machinery: each parent id as an unbreakable unit), C for the narrow Working Copy panel label (space-constrained). Merges (2+ parents) use `↓ a, b` with first-parent-first order (jj order; consistent with graph fix jj-idea-fdux). Root commit: show nothing (not "no parents" text).
Implementation sketch: change `appendParents` to `appendParentsInline(entry)` returning an unbreakable run `appendUnbreakable { grey { "↓" } ids... }` with the arrow glyph from a bundle key (`details.parents.arrow=↓`) so locale/font fallback is controlled (check glyph availability in JB Mono/Inter at 85-200% zoom - jj-idea-3as8 showed scaling pitfalls; if the arrow glyph is missing use an SVG icon from the icon set); keep tooltip text "Parent change(s)" on the arrow chip (chip tooltip path); keep each id a `ChangeNavigationClick` link.
Decisions made without the user (please pick): Q: A vs C vs D? Rec A (details) + C (working copy). Q: arrow glyph vs word? Rec glyph + tooltip (language-neutral, compact). Q: show for root? Rec nothing.
Scale: none. Testing: `LogEntryText` canvas tests (0, 1, 2, 3 parents; unbreakable runs; link tags retained), details-pane render test at 3 widths for wrapping behaviour, bundle key; manual: MT-LOG-DETAILS (single/merge/octopus/root; zoom 85/100/200%; narrow pane wraps without clipping - note jj-idea-kxcu's clipping issue interacts: unbreakable parent runs must be allowed to wrap between parents), MT-WORKINGCOPY (label). Regression scope: MT-LOG-DETAILS, MT-WORKINGCOPY.
acceptance_criteria: Parents shown compactly (arrow glyph + styled ids, inline in the details header; separate-line glyph variant in the working copy label), links preserved, wraps cleanly; tests + MT rows.
notes: Sibling: jj-idea-fdux is the graph-rendering half of merge-parent display (parent order/colours in the graph itself, GitHub #51 point 2). This bead (4afk) is about the detail-panel's parent list presentation, not the graph.

title: Extract hardcoded text/description in plugin.xml to resource bundle for i18n
description: IDE inspections report 'Extract text/description for i18n' warnings in plugin.xml. Several action registrations use hardcoded text= attributes (e.g. text="Jujutsu" on EditorGroup) instead of resource bundle keys. Move all hardcoded strings to JujutsuBundle.properties using the standard action.<id>.text / action.<id>.description key pattern.
design:
PLAN: convert the remaining hard-coded `text=`/`description=` strings in plugin.xml to bundle keys; one pass plus a guard test.
Inventory (grep of `text="` in src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.xml): `Jujutsu.RenameLogTab` `text="Rename…"` (plugin.xml:~309), group `Jujutsu.MainMenuGroup` `text="Jujutsu"` (:200), group `Jujutsu.EditorGroup` `text="Jujutsu"` (:341), group `Jujutsu.DiffEditorOpenInGroup` `text="Open In"` (:385); plus the tool window / other `<toolWindow ... >` attributes (`id`, `factoryClass`; title comes from `toolwindow.title`), `<notificationGroup id="Jujutsu">` and `id="Jujutsu Onboarding"` (:70-71: notification group `displayName`/`key` attributes should use `bundle`+`key` for localisation), `<vcs name="Jujutsu" ...>` (display name via the registered `vcs` EP `displayName`), the `<description>` CDATA (:8-48, the Marketplace text - localisable via the `plugin.<id>.description` key convention, careful with jj-idea-18ju's constraint) and `<name>`. Action registrations whose text is set in the class constructor (comment at :189) are already bundle-driven.
Convention (platform): for an `<action id="X">` the IDE reads `action.X.text` / `action.X.description` from the plugin's `<resource-bundle>`; for groups `group.X.text`; `override-text place=...` uses `action.X.<place>.text` (existing example: key `action.Jujutsu.Init.Vcs.Toolbar.Widget.text` at JujutsuBundle.properties:230). So the work = delete the `text="..."` attributes and add keys: `action.Jujutsu.RenameLogTab.text=Rename…`, `group.Jujutsu.MainMenuGroup.text=Jujutsu`, `group.Jujutsu.EditorGroup.text=Jujutsu`, `group.Jujutsu.DiffEditorOpenInGroup.text=Open In` (+ `.description` where the group class doesn't set one). Caveat: `JujutsuMainMenuGroup`/`JujutsuEditorActionGroup` are `class=` groups that may set their own template presentation text in code - check so the bundle key doesn't get overridden or duplicated; the platform prefers the bundle key over the `text` attribute.
Notification groups: `<notificationGroup id="Jujutsu" displayType="BALLOON" bundle="messages.JujutsuBundle" key="notification.group.jujutsu"/>` (display name shown in Settings > Notifications) - add keys `notification.group.jujutsu=Jujutsu`, `notification.group.jujutsu.onboarding=Jujutsu Onboarding`; keep ids unchanged (they're API: saved user notification settings key on id).
Interplay: jj-idea-rech's naming guard must allow `group.*` and `action.<id>.*` forms and `notification.group.*`; jj-idea-18ju's `plugin.description` rename (conformant `plugin.<id>.description`) - do these three beads' bundle edits together or in order 18ju -> ysew -> rech to avoid merge churn on the properties file.
Verification: IDE inspection "Extract text/description for i18n" (DevKit plugin.xml inspection) shows no warnings; a unit test parsing plugin.xml (DOM) asserting no `<action>`/`<group>` has a non-empty `text=`/`description=` attribute and every `<notificationGroup>` has `key`; manual: menus/groups render the same English text (Vcs menu 'Jujutsu', editor popup 'Jujutsu', Open In, tab 'Rename…').
Decisions made without the user: Q: localise the marketplace `<description>` now? Rec no (needs a localisation strategy; leave CDATA). Scale: none. Regression scope: MT-CTXMENU (menu texts), MT-CROSS (VCS menu).
acceptance_criteria: No hard-coded text/description attributes on actions/groups in plugin.xml (keys in bundle, same English text); notification groups keyed; plugin.xml guard test; DevKit inspection clean.

title: Rebase option icons
description: Add icons to represent the various rebase options visually. Use the jj rebase command line documentation as inspiration.
acceptance_criteria: Six rebase option icons (-r/-s/-b/-d/-A/-B) shown in the Rebase dialog (and DnD hints), theme-aware; resource tests; visual review.

title: Reorder resources
description: The resource file is currently in a chaotic order, and there is no naming convention for properties. Make the property names consistent (e.g. actions starting with action.), group consistently, and reorder vaguely alphabetically.
design:
PLAN (label for-human: touches ~1,000 keys; low-risk MECHANICAL plan with guard rails; decisions flagged).
Facts: `messages/JujutsuBundle.properties` = 1,013 lines with 36 `# Section` headers in no systematic order (e.g. "Actions" at :34-135 then Bookmarks panel, tooltips, dangling heads, then ~170 lines later "Version-gated features", "Context Menu & Diff", "Dialog Messages", "Settings" ...; per-feature sections added at the end over time). Key prefixes by count: `action.*` 236, `dialog.*` 182, `log.*` 170, `settings.*` 88, `notification.*` 62, `bookmarks.*` 27, `statusbar.*` 14, `details.*` 13, `workingcopy.*` 12, `clone.*` 12, `diff.*` 11, `panel.*`/`vcs.*`/`merge.*`/`annotation.*` 7-9 each, then small groups (status, preview, button, toolwindow, progress, gutter, changes, history, plugin, feature). So a prefix convention largely exists; inconsistency is mostly ORDER/grouping and some stragglers (e.g. `log.action.*` actions living under `log.` instead of `action.log.*`; `dialog.*` keys describing actions).
Risks to manage: (1) keys are referenced from Kotlin (`JujutsuBundle.message("...")`, many via computed prefixes: `"$resourceKeyPrefix.title"` in actions/Inputs.kt:20-21, `"preview.$id.name"` (PreviewFeature.kt), `"action.Jujutsu.<Id>.text/description"` bound by action id from plugin.xml (platform convention: renaming these BREAKS action text), `"feature.<x>.name"`): a RENAME of keys requires finding dynamic constructions; (2) plugin.xml `<resource-bundle>` + `key=` attributes; (3) DevKit conventions (`action.<id>.text`, `group.<id>.text` are fixed by the platform and must stay: jj-idea-18ju also constrains `plugin.*` keys).
Plan - three tiers, each independently shippable:
 1. REORDER ONLY (zero risk to behaviour): a script `scripts/sort-bundle.py` that parses the file into (comment-block + key=value (with continuation lines)) entries, groups entries by their first key segment in a fixed section order (VCS/Plugin/Tool window/Buttons/Actions (`action.*`, `group.*`)/Dialogs (`dialog.*`)/Settings/Log (`log.*`)/Bookmarks/Details/Working copy/Notifications/Status/Misc), keeps existing section comments (merged with their feature references like jj-idea-xxxx), sorts keys alphabetically WITHIN each group, preserves multi-line values and `\u` escapes byte-for-byte; idempotent. Verify with a test that loads the properties before/after through `java.util.Properties` and asserts identical key->value maps (no key lost/changed).
 2. NAMING GUARD: a unit test enforcing the convention going forward: every key starts with one of an allow-listed set of prefixes (the list above), `action.*` keys of the form `action.<id>.text|description` are checked against plugin.xml action ids (platform convention), no duplicate keys, no unused keys (optional: scan src/main for literal references; dynamic prefixes whitelisted) and no key whose prefix is not allow-listed (new prefixes require adding to the list: documented in contributing.md "Resource bundle conventions").
 3. RENAMES (optional, only where valuable): move `log.action.*` -> `action.log.*`? ~40 keys; each rename = update all Kotlin references (compiler can't check string keys: add the "all referenced keys exist" test first (step 2) so missing keys are caught); do via a rename map file + sed + the test; skip entirely if the value isn't compelling (naming consistency for translators is the main benefit; no locale bundles exist yet, so the urgency is low).
Decisions made without the user: Q: how far? Rec tiers 1+2 now (reorder + guard), tier 3 only if you want strict naming. Q: alphabetical within groups vs by feature? Rec alphabetical within group (the bead says "vaguely alphabetical"); keep the feature-reference comments attached to their first key.
Scale: none. Testing: the before/after equality test, idempotence test (running the script twice yields the same file), the naming/dup guard test. Manual: smoke the IDE once (a few dialogs/menus) to catch any dynamic-key mishap - tier 1 doesn't change keys so risk is nil. Regression scope: none expected (reorder only); run `./gradlew check`.
acceptance_criteria: Bundle reordered by script (key/values identical per test), naming/duplicate guard test added, conventions documented; renames only if approved.

title: File history: Navigate directly to file diff from history entry
description: When viewing file history (Show History), clicking a revision should open the diff for that specific file directly, rather than requiring navigation through the changes pane to re-select the file. This would streamline the workflow: file history entry → file diff in one step.
design:
PLAN: opening a file-history row (Enter/double-click/Show Diff) should open THAT file's diff at that revision directly, instead of the commit's file list.
Facts: `JujutsuFileHistoryPanel` (ui/history/JujutsuFileHistoryPanel.kt) = `CommitTablePanel<List<LogEntry>>` for one `filePath`; Enter/double-click on a row go through `invokeEnterBoundAction` (ui/log/JujutsuLogTable.kt:356-369 DoubleClickListener -> actions/EnterBoundAction.kt) -> `Jujutsu.ShowChangesDiff` = `ShowDiffAction` (actions/filechange/ShowDiffAction.kt: uses `DiffDataKeys.EDITOR_TAB_DIFF_PREVIEW` if present, else `e.changes`/`e.fileList` and `buildDiffRequests(project, changes, files)` in a background thread; enabled when changes, a LOG_ENTRY or a repo exists). In the history panel the data context carries the selected row's `LOG_ENTRY` (set by CommitTablePanel for the table selection) but NOT the file's `Change`, so the action has nothing file-specific to diff (it may open the whole commit via the details pane's tree, i.e. "navigate through the changes pane to re-select the file" as the bead describes).
Design:
1. Publish the file-scoped change: override `uiDataSnapshot(sink)` in `JujutsuFileHistoryPanel` (or its table via `JujutsuLogTable`'s snapshot) to add `VcsDataKeys.CHANGES = arrayOf(change)` (lazily: `sink.lazy(VcsDataKeys.CHANGES) { ... }`) where `change` = the platform `Change` for `filePath` in the selected entry: build from `repo.logService.getFileChanges(entry, filePath)` (jj/cli/CliLogService.kt: `getFileChanges(entry, filePath): Result<List<FileChange>>` filters to the path; used in the annotation provider) -> `FileChange` -> platform `Change` via the existing converter used by `ChangeService.loadChanges(entry)` (jj/ChangeService.kt:36-60) with the entry's before/after content revisions (so renamed files across history diff correctly - ties to jj-idea-i2e2's per-row path: use the row's `pathAtRevision`). Cache per (commitId, path) in a tiny map in the panel (immutable per commit id) so repeated Enter/selection is instant; a cold load runs off the EDT: `sink.lazy` is evaluated on BGT in `update()`/`actionPerformed` snapshots (platform guarantees BGT for lazy providers) - but a `jj` call must not run under a read action: use the pre-fetched cache populated on selection change (`logTable.selectionModel` listener -> `runInBackground { cache[commitId] = loadFileChange(...) }`), and have the lazy provider read ONLY the cache (null until loaded -> action disabled for a few ms; first Enter right after selecting may no-op: mitigate by also kicking the load on Enter via `ShowDiffAction` fallback: when `changes` empty and `e.logEntry != null` and the panel is a file-history panel (data key `JujutsuDataKeys.HISTORY_FILE_PATH`), run the load then show the diff).
2. Alternative minimal approach (preferred if the above proves heavy): add `JujutsuDataKeys.HISTORY_FILE_PATH` (the panel's `filePath`) to the data context and teach `ShowDiffAction` to use it: `if (entry != null && historyFile != null) -> diff only that file`: `buildDiffRequests(project, changes = emptyList, files = [VirtualFile at revision])` using `repo.getVirtualFile(FileAtVersion(path, entry.commitId-or-id))` pairs (before = parent revision of entry, after = entry) via the existing `createDiffSideFor(file.filePath.fileAt(...))`/`DiffRequestBuilder` (actions/filechange/DiffRequestBuilder.kt) - no Change objects needed, one background resolution of parent locators (`entry.parentIds.first()` / MergeParentOf for merges, as `compareBeforeWithRevision` does). Rec this one: smaller, no cache, reuses DiffRequestBuilder.
3. Interaction: single click selects (details pane shows the commit's tree as today); Enter/double-click = diff for the file; the details pane tree remains for browsing other files of the commit. Editor-tab preview (`JujutsuEditorTabDiffPreview`, used by the details tree) is NOT used for this path (history panel has no EDITOR_TAB_DIFF_PREVIEW key): opens a diff window/tab via DiffManager like the current fallback.
4. Rename/merge/delete edge cases: file deleted in that commit -> after side = empty content ("deleted" label); added -> before empty; merge commit -> diff vs auto-merged parent (MergeParentOf locator, `JujutsuContentRevisions`/annotation uses it) - reuse; renamed (needs i2e2's per-row path).
Decisions made without the user: Q: approach 2 (history file key + builder) vs approach 1 (publish Change)? Rec 2. Q: keep double-click = same as Enter (jj-idea-th9h rule: one action for both)? Yes - automatically.
Scale: one jj call (or two content fetches) per opened diff; none per row. Testing: `ShowDiffAction` test with HISTORY_FILE_PATH data -> exactly one diff request for that path (stub repo/executor), edge cases (added/deleted/merge); panel data-context test (key published); manual: MT-DIFF/file-history rows (Show History -> Enter on a row opens the diff of that file at that revision; deleted/added/renamed/merge rows; double-click equals Enter; details pane unaffected). Regression scope: MT-DIFF, MT-CTXMENU (ShowDiff in other contexts unchanged: editor, log, working copy).
acceptance_criteria: Enter/double-click on a file-history row opens that file's diff at that revision directly (added/deleted/merge handled); other ShowDiff contexts unchanged; tests + MT-DIFF rows.

title: Allow abandon on multiple changes
description: It is possible to abandon a single change from the log. It would be great to be able to multi-select log entries and abandon them all. This should be possible only if all selected changes are mutable.
design:
PLAN: multi-select abandon from the log (mutable changes only), one `jj abandon` invocation, one confirmation, one undo.
Facts: single-target factory `abandonChangeAction(project, entry)` (actions/change/abandonChangeAction.kt:20-56): confirmation only when risk (files/description/local bookmarks: `abandonConfirmMessage(entry)` :~60-90, lists reasons, bookmarks that will be deleted), then `repo.createCommand { abandon(target.id) }.onSuccess { invalidate(select = selectAfter, vfsChanged = true) }.addUndoTracking("log.action.abandon.undo")`; executor `abandon(revision)` / `abandonArgs(revision) = JjInvocation(REVERSIBLE, "abandon", "-r", revision)` (jj/cli/CliExecutor.kt:92). The log menu passes `entry?.takeIf { !it.immutable }` (single selection only: JujutsuLogContextMenuActions `abandonChangeAction(project, entry?.takeIf { !it.immutable })`, with a TODO "Allow abandon on multiple if all entries are immutable" - sic: meant mutable). jj facts: `jj abandon [REVSETS]...` accepts multiple revisions; abandoning a set rebases descendants once, deletes local bookmarks on the abandoned commits.
Design:
1. Executor: `abandon(revisions: List<Revision>)` (keep the single-arg overload delegating): `abandonArgs(revisions)` = `abandon -r a -r b ...` (repeated `-r`, REVERSIBLE; one operation => one undo). Add to CommandExecutor.kt + CliExecutor + StubCommandExecutor; args test in CliExecutor*Test.
2. Action: `abandonChangesAction(project, entries)`: enabled when `entries.isNotEmpty()`, all MUTABLE (`!immutable`), all in ONE repo (`entries.uniqueRepo`, else disabled with reason) and the set may include the working copy (jj creates a new empty @ automatically; `selectAfter` = WorkingCopy if the WC is among them else the first surviving parent of the topmost/oldest abandoned commit). Keep the single-entry factory as the N=1 case so tooltips/ids/text stay ("Abandon" vs "Abandon N Changes" via `log.action.abandon.plural`).
3. Confirmation: aggregate across entries: reasons per category with counts ("3 changes have file modifications, 2 have descriptions; bookmarks main, feature/x will be deleted") via `abandonConfirmMessage(entries)` generalisation (pure function, easily tested); skip the confirmation only if EVERY entry is empty/undescribed/unbookmarked (same rule as today); for N >= 10 always confirm (bulk destructive).
4. Descendant effects: abandoning a middle change rebases its children onto its parents (jj semantic) - mention in the confirm text only when some abandoned change has non-selected descendants ("N descendant changes will be rebased"): compute from loaded entries (children map) - best effort, skip when unknown.
5. Undo: single `addUndoTracking("log.action.abandon.undo")` (one op) - label plural "Abandon N changes" via a parameterised message.
6. Registration: replace the menu entry in `JujutsuLogContextMenuActions` (live selection and link-menu paths) with the multi version; the toolbar/keymap: no id currently (factory) - candidate for a registered id `Jujutsu.Abandon` later (jj-idea-plpa/66id).
Decisions made without the user: Q: allow WC in the set? Rec yes (jj handles). Q: mixed immutable -> disabled with reason "N selected changes are immutable". Q: always confirm for N>=10? Rec yes.
Scale: O(selection) for the confirm text; one jj call. Operation-count test: abandoning 50 selected = 1 executor call. Testing: args test (multiple -r), `abandonConfirmMessage` list tests (counts, bookmarks union, empty set -> null, N>=10 forced), action enablement tests (immutable/mixed repos/empty), selectAfter selection logic tests, contract test (real jj abandons a chain, descendants rebased, bookmarks deleted); manual: MT-CTXMENU (multi-select 3 changes -> Abandon: confirm lists reasons; Undo restores all; immutable in the set -> disabled). Regression scope: MT-CTXMENU, MT-LOG-TABLE (selection after abandon), MT-BOOKMARK.
acceptance_criteria: Multi-select abandon (mutable, single-repo) via one jj invocation with aggregated confirmation and a single undo; selection after abandon sensible; args/confirm/enablement/contract tests; MT-CTXMENU rows.

title: Add configuration to choose custom vs standard log
design:
PLAN: OBSOLETE - recommend closing. The bead ("Add configuration to choose custom vs standard log", no description, from the original custom-log epic gyo) was explicitly de-prioritised by its owner on 2026-02-10 ("becoming less important now that the custom log has most of the features of the standard log"), and the code has since moved decisively: JujutsuUiEnabler suppresses the standard VCS log tab for jj roots (ui/services/JujutsuUiEnabler.kt:~140 "prevents the standard log from reappearing after we close it"), the plugin registers no VcsLogProvider (grep: none; the platform log integration was removed - see also jj-idea-i2e2/yki9's stale JujutsuLogFileHistoryHandler references), and the custom log is the only implementation (UnifiedJujutsuLogPanel). Offering a toggle would need to resurrect and maintain a second log implementation.
Recommendation: close as won't-do (not closed by this pass; needs your OK). If the underlying wish is "let users reach the IDE's standard log for Git roots in mixed projects": that is the platform's own Git log and already works untouched for Git roots.
Reverse: keep open as a placeholder; no work is implied.
acceptance_criteria: Closed as won't-do/obsolete (user confirmation).

title: Size the description text box
description: In the working copy tool window, allow the description text box to grow until it (and the buttons below it) take up half of the height of the tool window OR stretch as far as possible without the change tree needing to have scroll bars, whichever is greater.
design:
PLAN: size the Working Copy panel's description area dynamically via the existing vertical splitter's proportion (no new layout engine).
Facts: `UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel` lays out a vertical `Splitter(true, 0.6f)` (ui/workingcopy/UnifiedWorkingCopyPanel.kt:143-158): first = changes toolbar + `ScrollPaneFactory.createScrollPane(changesTree)`, second = `WorkingCopyControlsPanel` (description editor, Describe/Revert buttons, current-change label; `descriptionEditor.component.preferredSize = JBUI.size(400, 90)`, minimum 70px, WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt:~95-100). The user can already drag the divider; the default is a fixed 0.6/0.4 split, so the description box never grows by itself and the tree may waste space (few changes) or need scrolling (many).
Rule from the bead (the "greater of" two criteria): give the controls area = max(50% of the tool-window height, the space left after the tree's content height (so the tree needs no scrollbar)).
Design:
1. Compute on layout/changes: `treeContentHeight = changesTree.preferredSize.height + toolbarHeight` (JTree preferred height reflects expanded rows; with 1k changes it's huge - cap by the available height); `available = splitter.height - dividerWidth`; `controlsMin = controlsPanel.minimumSize.height`; `controlsWanted = max(available * 0.5, available - treeContentHeight)`; clamp so controls >= minimum and the tree area >= a minimum (e.g. 4 rows); `splitter.proportion = (available - controlsWanted) / available`.
2. When to apply: (a) once on first show/size, (b) when the tree's row count changes by a rebuild (`updateChangesView`), (c) NOT while the user has dragged the divider manually: keep a flag `userAdjustedDivider` set on divider drag (listen to `splitter.addPropertyChangeListener("proportion")` filtered to non-programmatic updates via a `programmaticProportion` guard) and persist the user's proportion via `PropertiesComponent` (precedent: collapsed-paths persistence in the same class :550-558); auto-sizing is a DEFAULT only until the user resizes.
3. Description editor growth: the editor must actually fill the extra height: `descriptionEditor.component` is added to `topPanel` with GridBag constraints (WorkingCopyControlsPanel.kt:~157 `topPanel.add(descriptionEditor.component, gbc)`): ensure `gbc.weighty = 1.0, fill = BOTH` for that row so it expands while the buttons keep their height; check the current constraints.
4. Edge cases: collapsed tool window height tiny -> clamp; multi-repo "other repositories" nodes inflate tree height (they're part of preferredSize - fine); repeated rebuilds during bursts: apply through the existing debounced `rebuildQueue` completion hook to avoid flicker.
Decisions made without the user: Q: auto-size vs just a better static default (e.g. 0.5)? Rec dynamic as the bead asks, gated by the user-adjusted flag. Q: persist user divider position? Rec yes per project.
Scale: O(1) per rebuild (preferredSize of the JTree is O(visible rows) already computed by Swing; guard against huge row counts by capping at `available`). Testing: pure function `desiredControlsHeight(available, treeContent, controlsMin)` table tests (few changes -> half; many changes -> half (greater of); no tree -> all but min tree; tiny window clamps); panel test setting sizes and asserting splitter proportion; user-adjust flag test; manual: MT-WORKINGCOPY (few vs many changes, resize window, drag divider then add changes: stays put, restart: persisted). Regression scope: MT-WORKINGCOPY.
acceptance_criteria: Description area defaults to max(50% height, space not needed by the tree) via splitter proportion; manual divider adjustments persist and are respected; pure sizing function tests; MT-WORKINGCOPY rows.

title: New change command with options
description:
**Priority**: HIGH (Phase 2 - Simple write operations)
**Effort**: 1-2 days

## Description
Enhance "New Change" button to support creating change with description and options.

## Current Status
- ✅ "New" button exists
- ⚠️ Creates empty change, no description option

## User Experience
- Dialog: "Create new change"
- Optional description field
- Option: Create after current change vs. after parent
- Success notification with new change ID

## Implementation
```kotlin
fun createNewChange(description: String?, after: String?) {
    val args = mutableListOf("new")
    if (description != null) args.addAll(listOf("-m", description))
    if (after != null) args.addAll(listOf("-A", after))
    vcs.commandExecutor.execute(args)
}
```

## Commands
- `jj new` - Create new change after @
- `jj new -m "desc"` - Create with description
- `jj new -A <change-id>` - Create after specific change

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dialog for new change options
- [ ] Optional description field
- [ ] Optional "after" change selection
- [ ] Success notification
- [ ] Refreshes changes view
- [ ] Updates current change display

## References
See ROADMAP.md Phase 2 - Simple Write Operations
